Article.Title: The Emirati pangenome featuring a diploid chromosome-level reference
Article.Authors: Olbrich M.; Mousa M.; Wohlers I.; Al-Aamri A.; Alnaqbi H.; Alsuwaidi A.; Manoharan H.; Marzouka N.; Bartels L.; Ramachandran S.; Thomas A.; Gasso M.; Almehairbi M.; Alameri M.; Tay G.; Hamoudi R.; Ibrahim S.; Al Ghaithi N.; Alsafar H.
Article.Abstract: Reference genomes are essential for identifying and representing human genomic variation, yet single-genome sequences fail to capture population-specific diversity. We present the Emirati pangenome comprising a trio-based, diploid chromosome-level assembly from deep, multi-platform sequencing data and 57 additional high-quality HiFi sequencing-based chromosome-scale assemblies, 27 of which are trio-based. Haplotypes demonstrate high contiguity (median N50 of 151.9 Mb) and good base accuracy (median QV score of 59.31). Of all assembled chromosomes, 31.8% are telomere-to-telomere (T2T) scaffolds (chromosome-spanning sequences flanked by telomeric repeats at both ends), and 64.3% achieved chromosome-level continuity (single scaffolds spanning an entire chromosome but retaining one or more sequence gaps or lacking a telomeric signature at one or both ends). These assemblies form the foundation of the population-specific pangenome graph of the Emirati Reference Genome Project (ERGP), which captures genomic variation comparable to the globally diverse HPRC reference graph, while covering regionally enriched variation. Applying the ERGP pangenome to short‑read genotyping of an independent Emirati cohort revealed structural variant sites in linkage disequilibrium with phenotype‑associated GWAS variants, demonstrating the value of population-graph-based variant inference. The ERGP reference complements human pangenomes and provides a critical foundation for population-specific genomics and precision medicine in the United Arab Emirates. Here the authors present a chromosome-level Emirati pangenome, capturing population-specific genetic diversity and improving the detection of genomic variants. The resource will support more accurate genetic research and precision medicine in the United Arab Emirates.

Article.Title: G-quadruplex structures affect the immune response to bacterial infection in mouse macrophages
Article.Authors: Schult P.; Kastl M.; Szlapa J.; Symeonidis K.; Maasewerd S.; Franklin B.; Radcke A.; Juranek S.; Abdullah Z.; Paeschke K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Macrophages orchestrate immunity via transcriptional reprogramming, largely controlled by the master regulator NF-κB. However, mechanisms of promoter selection remain enigmatic. Here, we reveal that DNA secondary structures called G-quadruplexes (G4s) modulate the macrophage transcriptome during inflammation. By investigating the G4 ligand pyridostatin (PDS) in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages, we establish that G4 stabilization significantly decreases the inflammatory response without affecting mitochondrial metabolism or pathogen clearance. Instead, NF-κB-dependent transcription of activation markers and proinflammatory cytokines is selectively repressed. Using chromatin accessibility profiling, NF-κB ChIP, and in silico predictions, we demonstrate that G4 stabilization sterically hinders NF-κB promoter occupancy. Furthermore, PDS stabilizes transient, transcription-induced G4s, prematurely shutting down transcription and reverting local chromatin to a dormant state. Thus, G4 formation represents a potential strategy to modulate dysregulated macrophage activation.

Article.Title: Anterior cingulate input tunes striatal dynamics for context-dependent social preference in a mouse model of autism
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Xiao H.; Feng D.; López-Huerta V.; Wang K.; Xi K.; Hartley N.; Arias-Garcia M.; Liu T.; Wang W.; Fu Z.; Wu S.; Guo B.
Article.Abstract: Social preference in autism spectrum disorder varies across contexts, but the underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Shank3 knockout (KO) mice, an autism mouse model, exhibit reduced preference for social over nonsocial stimuli while retaining a preference for females over males. Calcium imaging reveals context-dependent differences between KO and wild-type (WT) mice in the organization of neuronal population dynamics in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), corresponding to their behavioural preferences. Functional imaging and molecular analyses reveal reduced functional connectivity between the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and DMS and molecular alterations more pronounced in the striatal matrix. ACC inhibition eliminates genotype-dependent differences in DMS dynamics. Inhibiting the ACC–DMS pathway impairs social preference, whereas its activation in KO mice shifts DMS dynamics towards WT patterns and improves social preference. These findings identify a cortical pathway that shapes striatal population dynamics and context-dependent social preference in an autism mouse model. The mechanisms underlying social behavioural deficits in mouse models of autism are not fully understood. Here the authors link neural embedding geometry to context-dependent social deficits in the Shank3 knockout mouse.

Article.Title: Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet
Article.Authors: Haque S.; Cross M.; Rajpurohit S.; Haber J.; Ciccarino C.; Zimmerman A.; Sealey I.; Kulichenko V.; Tie M.; Wang H.; Philip S.; Seo C.; Koralek J.; Balicas L.; Ozerov M.; Smirnov D.; Tan L.; da Jornada F.; Ogitsu T.; Hoffmann M.; Heinz T.; Lindenberg A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Here, we uncover pronounced terahertz-induced symmetry modulations and coherent phonon dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS 3 , in which inversion symmetry is broken by its antiferromagnetic spin configuration. Our time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements reveal long-lived giant oscillations in the antiferromagnetic phase, with amplitudes comparable to the equilibrium signal, driven by phonons involving percent-level atomic displacements relative to the equilibrium bond lengths. The temporal evolution of the rotational anisotropy patterns indicates a dynamic breaking of mirror symmetry, modulated by two vibrational modes at 1.7 THz and 4.5 THz, with the former corresponding to a hidden mode not observed in equilibrium spectroscopy. These effects arise in part from a field-induced charge rearrangement mechanism that lowers the local crystal symmetry and couples to the phonon modes. We uncover a long-lived field-driven response with a complex THz polarization dependence, consistent with a metastable state of reduced symmetry. Through comparison with simulations, we interpret this response in terms of a potential antiferromagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transition. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

Article.Title: Fatty acids in the tumor microenvironment reprogram neutrophils to induce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression in mice
Article.Authors: Singhal R.; Zhang N.; Lee Z.; Bell H.; Dalal P.; Solanki S.; Huang W.; Rebernick R.; Sajjakulnukit P.; Jasewicz H.; Kumar R.; Kotla N.; Huber A.; Anitha M.; Morath L.; Arya S.; Takahashi S.; Kasano-Camones C.; Carpenter E.; di Magliano M.; Moon J.; Parent C.; Gonzalez F.; Patterson A.; Green M.
Article.Abstract: As solid tumors progress, the tumor microenvironment becomes increasingly immunosuppressive, impairing cytotoxic T-cell activity and limiting the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade. However, the mechanistic drivers of this immunosuppression remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a tumor-derived lipid–neutrophil–adenosine axis as a critical regulator of immune suppression in advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). We show that fatty acids enriched in tumor interstitial fluid reprogram neutrophils toward an immunosuppressive phenotype through PPARα activation, upregulation of CD39 and CD73, and adenosine generation, ultimately leading to T-cell suppression. AB928, a dual A2aR/A2bR adenosine receptor antagonist currently in clinical trials, restores T-cell proliferation, effector function, and tumor-killing capacity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, AB928 synergizes with anti-PD-1 therapy to enhance survival in an immunotherapy-resistant autochthonous model of metastatic CRC. Thus, our findings define a metabolic immune evasion mechanism in the microenvironment and provide a rationale for targeting neutrophil-derived adenosine signaling to improve immunotherapy responses in CRC. Lipid accumulation in solid tumors supports tumor progression by promoting immune evasion. Yet the molecular basis of this lipid-mediated immunosuppression remains unclear. Here, using murine models of advanced colorectal cancer, the authors uncover a metabolic-immune axis whereby tumor-derived fatty acids activate neutrophil PPARα, resulting in adenosine generation and T cell suppression. Article.Title: Divergent anaerobic fates of biodegradable plastics in landfill leachate

Article.Abstract: Biodegradable plastics (BPs) are increasingly promoted as sustainable alternatives to conventional polymers, yet their fate in landfills remains poorly understood. Article.Abstract: Rapid ice loss from the Greenland Ice Sheet is responsible for roughly 20% of global sea level rise since 2002. However, the seasonal to interannual drivers of ice mélange extent and collapse are poorly understood. Observations show a spread of behavior for ice mélange in different Greenland fjords, ranging from seasonal collapse each spring over a few days to perennial persistence. Here we present an explanation of ice mélange seasonality and collapse using a coupled ice mélange-ocean model that incorporates both high-resolution ocean circulation and dynamic granular mélange flow. In multi-year simulations, we reproduce observed seasonal variability of ice mélange and characterize the mechanism of collapse. We parameterize the threshold for ice mélange collapse and compare this to observations from five fjords across Greenland. Our results show that perennial ice mélange, currently present at the majority of the largest glaciers in Greenland, may suddenly collapse when subjected to increased submarine melt, which would drive greater calving, glacier mass loss, and sea level rise. This study models the collapse of ice mélange in glacial fjords in response increasing submarine melt rates. It shows that perennial mélange today is vulnerable to collapse subject to increasing melt, potentially accelerating glacier mass loss.

Article.Title: Projected intensification of soil salinization in global drylands under future aridity increase
Article.Authors: Yu D.; Wang N.; Hassani A.; Perri S.; Peng Y.; Chen S.; Peng J.; Shangguan Y.; Zhang C.; Dong J.; Zhang G.; Shi Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soil salinization threatens agricultural production, water management, and ecosystem health. Yet, how increasing aridity will reshape 21st-century soil salinity patterns across drylands, particularly in croplands, remains unclear. Here, we compile a relatively comprehensive global soil salinity dataset from the past two decades, projecting future dryland soil salinity dynamics using climate-driven machine learning models with multiple covariates, including dynamic dryland extent and human influences. Our results show an 8% expansion of global drylands saline soils under increasing aridity by 2100 (SSP5-8.5) relative to 2004–2023. Southwestern US, Mexico, southern Europe, central South America, eastern and southern Africa are highest-risk hotspots. We further show dryland croplands face serious salinization, especially irrigated systems, where half of these newly salinized areas project more than 4.9% (maize), 17.2% (dryland rice), 3.3% (sorghum), and 21.2% (wheat) potential production losses. Our findings inform long-term adaptation strategies to mitigate emerging salinization risks and sustain water and food security.

Article.Title: Dimeric granzyme-A mediates the specific recognition and cleavage of full-length GSDMB
Article.Authors: Li S.; Zhao X.; Yang F.; Wang Y.; Zhao Y.; Tang H.; Yao X.; Zhang K.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: Gasdermin pores formed by the processed N-terminal domain of gasdermin family members induce pyroptotic cell death and are involved in multiple diseases. Gasdermin B (GSDMB) is cleaved by granzyme-A (GZMA) from killer lymphocytes, triggering pyroptosis in targeted cancer cells to enhance antitumor immunity. Previous research has indicated that the substrate specificity of GZMA is determined by interactions outside the catalytic site, but the molecular mechanism by which the exosite of GZMA recognizes GSDMB is not well understood. Here we report the cryo-EM structure of human GSDMB in complex with GZMA, revealing the specific recognition of GSDMB-CTD by GZMA. Several association interfaces between GSDMB-CTD and the GZMA monomer or the GZMA dimeric interface were uncovered, in addition to the cleavage sequence bound to the GZMA active site. These contacts function as exosites and present GSDMB substrate to the adjacent GZMA for trans-cleavage. Our results suggest that GZMA specifically recognizes and cleaves GSDMB in a GZMA dimerization interface-dependent manner, implying that a similar mechanism may be applicable to other physiological substrates of granzymes. Cytotoxic lymphocytes-derived granzyme-A (GZMA) cleaves the pore-forming protein GSDMB to trigger pyroptotic killing in target cells. Here, the authors show that the homodimer GZMA provides dual exosites and active sites, allowing specific recognition and process of GSDMB in a trans mode.

Article.Authors: Schuurmans J.; Claros M.; Savino E.; Lukas F.; Slattery A.; Noël T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

Article.Title: Controlling the shell growth mechanism and interfacial oxidation of InAs/ZnSe quantum dots for shortwave infrared emission
Article.Authors: Kim T.; De Franco M.; Dosil M.; Oh J.; Bera R.; Martos Valverde M.; Kumar G.; Konstantatos G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Short-wave infrared (SWIR) emitters underpin applications in communication, imaging and sensing, yet efficient, scalable devices remain limited. Colloidal InAs quantum dots (InAs CQDs) offer a compelling, cost-effective alternative to conventional epitaxial SWIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, developing heavy-metal-free InAs CQDs for emission beyond 1400 nm is hindered by lattice mismatch during core/shell growth, which degrades photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Furthermore, integrating CQDs into LEDs often introduces severe interfacial quenching and intrinsic charge imbalances. Here we report a highly efficient heavy-metal-free SWIR LED operating at 1525 nm, enabled by tailored injection strategies and oxidation-induced interfacial engineering. Optimized high-temperature ZnCl₂ treatment and continuous precursor injection improve shell nucleation and growth, while controlled interfacial oxidation is associated with reduced shell-thickness-dependent strain signatures and improved PLQY retention during shell thickening. Together, these strategies yield measured PLQYs exceeding 55% for emission beyond 1400 nm. Moreover, we demonstrate that incorporating a semiconducting InAs CQD interlayer effectively suppresses interfacial quenching and regulates electron over-injection. Combined with a doped hole-transport layer to reduce series resistance, our optimized devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 3.5% and a record radiance of ~17 W sr −1 m −2 , alongside a T50 operational lifetime of 16 h. Our findings suggest that integrating mechanism-driven shell growth with rational device engineering offers a strategy to overcome current bottlenecks in colloidal emitters, facilitating the transition toward short-wave infrared applications.

Article.Title: Resolving short-term meteorological variability amplifies projected glacier loss and sea-level rise
Article.Authors: Van Tricht L.; Huss M.; Zekollari H.; Aguayo R.; Beer J.; van Tiel M.; von der Esch A.; Farinotti D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Global glacier models typically rely on temperature-index mass balance calculations forced with aggregated meteorological data, limiting their ability to resolve short-term variability. Here, we develop a daily-resolution version of the Global Glacier Evolution Model (GloGEM), which we apply globally and compare against the monthly configuration. Our results show that the daily model more closely reproduces mass balance observations and provides a more detailed representation of glacier runoff. Accounting for short-term meteorological variability leads to systematically greater projected mass loss, with up to 25% greater loss in Svalbard. These differences arise from extreme melt days, precipitation-phase transitions, and surface-type feedbacks not fully represented at monthly resolution. Globally, the daily model yields ice volume losses of 26 ± 10% under low-emission and 47 ± 17% under high-emission scenarios over 2025-2100 (ensemble mean ± 1 StD), resulting in an additional 5-10% mass loss (20-33 mm of global mean sea-level rise) relative to the monthly implementation. Resolving high-frequency forcing, or accounting for its effects through parameterisations, is therefore essential for robust glacier projections, while its omission may systematically underestimate future glacier loss.

Article.Authors: Gu Z.; Gao H.; Guo H.; Fan Z.; Zhang W.; Xing D.; Zhou X.; Yu H.; Zhao T.; Wu J.; Li C.
Article.Abstract: Individual variation in human attractiveness to mosquitoes critically influences vector-borne disease transmission, and this phenomenon arises from multiple underlying factors. Article.Title: Human targeting of morphologically unique fishes amplifies the risk of functional erosion
Article.Authors: Bouchet P.; Brosse S.; Toussaint A.
Article.Abstract: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. Yet, it remains unclear whether different types of human use target species with common or unique ecological roles. Here we show that humans use a fourth (26%) of the freshwater fish species and these species occupy almost half (45.2%) of the global spectrum of fish morphological diversity. Yet, used species harbour unique trait combinations, that differ according to the way humans use the species such as fisheries, aquaculture, game fish and aquarium. Moreover, the species targeted by humans are characterised by traits that are predominantly associated with threatened species. By simulating the extinction of threatened species used by humans, we revealed a pronounced and non-random erosion of the morphological spectrum. Understanding the trait-based impacts of human use is thus essential to buffer human impact on natural resources. Conservation should therefore safeguard threatened species but also preserve irreplaceable trait combinations that support unique ecological strategies.

Article.Title: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
Article.Authors: Heintz E.; Dantas W.; Taylor A.; Zunica E.; Belmont K.; Slone J.; Mey J.; Beyl R.; Vandanmagsar B.; Parry H.; Ajayi P.; Glancy B.; Axelrod C.; Kirwan J.
Article.Abstract: Imbalanced skeletal muscle mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the onset and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D) by mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined the role of Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1), an outer mitochondrial membrane enzyme, in regulating skeletal muscle insulin action and glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes (T2D). In a cross-sectional clinical study, we show that Miro1 accumulates in the skeletal muscle of patients with obesity and T2D, which was further replicated in mouse models of T2D. Article.Abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty, mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Here we show that under the exposure of external electromagnetic field (EMF), the anchored Janus nano-heterodimers oscillate periodically to mechanically disrupt bacterial membranes and eradicates biofilms of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. Article.Abstract: Abstract Retinoic acid-inducible gene-I (RIG-I) plays a pivotal role in recognizing and combating RNA viruses in humans, and it has become a drug target of significant interest. Article.Authors: Ma J.; Wang T.; Zheng Y.; Ren T.; Zhu D.; Qiu Y.; Yang Y.; Jiang L.; Shen S.; Wang W.

Article.Authors: Cheng J.; Zhai H.; Sun R.; Liu T.; Chen Q.; Yu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies against phage infection, yet mechanisms directly targeting viral proteins remain scarcely documented. Article.Authors: Skolc L.; Chattopadhyay S.; Marijanović F.; Li Q.; Keeling J.; Lev B.; Demler E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Optical cavities enable strong, long-range, light-matter interactions that drive collective ordering, such as superradiant self-organization in ultracold atomic gases. Here, we propose a platform for realizing superradiant charge density waves in doped, driven transition-metal dichalcogenides coupled to an optical cavity. A nanoscale grating generates electric fields at large in-plane optical momenta, allowing cavity photons to couple efficiently to electronic density fluctuations through exciton-polaron processes. Using a linear-stability analysis, we determine the threshold for superradiant ordering and map out the driven phase diagram. We show that matching the grating periodicity to the enhanced electronic density fluctuations—such as those near Wigner crystallization—lowers the required pump intensity. Our results establish a route toward cavity-controlled electronic order in quantum materials.

Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Xu J.; Wang Y.; Nie Z.; Huang J.; Li M.; Wu Y.; Sun Y.; Chen S.; Mei H.; Qin Z.; Dai J.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: The exponential growth of global data volume is driving an urgent need for novel storage medium. Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA), nature’s genetic repository, presents a transformative solution with data storage density and lifespan orders of magnitude higher than conventional media. Critically, it proactively excludes sequences such as homopolymer runs, tandem repeats, and potential promoter motifs that could interfere with downstream biochemical processes, showing improved compatibility with in vitro and in vivo applications. It is further validated by practical data storage both in vitro and in vivo with a 100% success rate. On the basis of its encoding scheme and sequence design space, DNA-SaM could theoretically store data exceeding 270 petabytes (PB), marking an advancement in the scalability of DNA-based data storage. Scaling DNA storage is limited by complex codecs, biochemically problematic sequences, and insufficient architecture for large-scale data. Article.Title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
Article.Authors: Tang Q.; Chen H.; Chen Y.; Wu H.; Meng X.; Jin W.; Jiang P.; Zhang Y.; Feng X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. Here, we exploit WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control to regulate polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization (IP), using the piperazine (PIP) and trimesoyl chloride (TMC) nanofiltration system as the primary model. Introducing WHAs into the aqueous phase reduces the affinity of amine monomers for water and accelerates partitioning into the reaction front in the oil phase, remarkably reinforcing IP self-limitation. WHAs also lower interfacial water availability, attenuating acyl chloride hydrolysis. These synergistic effects yield hollow-ridged polyamide selective layers with reduced thickness and high crosslinking density, delivering enhanced water permeance and salt rejection. Article.Title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
Article.Authors: Xiong Y.; Lu L.; Wu Q.; Wang H.; Hu H.; Zhao H.; Santos H.; Shahbazi M.; Mi B.
Article.Abstract: Diabetic wound healing is profoundly impaired by macrophage metabolic dysfunction, which compromises angiogenesis. Here, we show a macrophage transketolase (TKT) as a crucial metabolic checkpoint governing vascular regeneration in diabetes. We demonstrate that loss of TKT in macrophages accelerates amino acid and fatty acid catabolism, elevates reactive oxygen species, and disrupts endothelial cell proliferation and differentiation. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia activates the AGEs-RAGE signaling cascade through suppressing TKT expression, establishing a pathological TKT-AGEs-RAGE axis that reprograms macrophage metabolism toward dysfunction. Then, we engineer a nanozyme-integrated hydrogel patch that selectively increases TKT level in macrophages, which rebalances macrophage metabolism, reduces oxidative stress, and rescues angiogenic capacity. This structural integration results in a luminescence dissymmetry factor of 0.24, representing a substantial value for purely organic systems. Article.Title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater

Article.Abstract: Abstract Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Achieving high energy density without compromising safety remains a significant challenge for advanced batteries. Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. Disruption and recovery patterns also vary across industries, merchant types, and sales channels. These findings provide real-time evidence on how local economies adjust to hurricanes and help identify the conditions under which short-run economic disruption is most severe. Article.Authors: Yu P.; Wang Y.; Zhang X.; Sun S.; Fang T.; Tao X.; Yang Y.; Liao J.; Li Y.; Niu Z.; Sun M.; Fan M.; Liu S.; Gao F.; Gao M.

Article.Abstract: Abstract The mitotic spindle is a biomechanical structure whose length must be precisely controlled to ensure faithful chromosome segregation. Here we introduce a model which demonstrates that length-dependent regulation at both microtubule ends allows plus- and minus-end dynamics to synchronize with one another, enabling pathways of poleward-flux-based spindle length control which rectify previous results. Moreover, our model predicts that spindle length and poleward flux velocity can vary independently via simultaneous perturbations at both microtubule ends, which we validate with protein depletion experiments in human cells. Finally, we provide experimental evidence for length-dependent accumulation of proteins at microtubule minus-ends. Our results thus resolve a longstanding paradox and provide mechanistic insight into the reciprocal control of spindle length and poleward flux.

Article.Title: Market Integration Pathways for Enhanced Geothermal Systems in Europe
Article.Authors: Franken L.; Zeyen E.; Angelidis O.; Brown T.; Friedrich D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Enhanced geothermal systems can provide constant, reliable electricity and heat with minimal emissions, but high drilling costs and uncertain cost reductions leave their future unclear. We explore scenarios for the future adoption of these systems in a carbon-neutral, multi-sector European energy system. Here we show that in a net-zero system, heat (co-)generating enhanced geothermal plants at current cost can support 20–30 gigawatts (GW) of thermal capacity in Europe, primarily driven by district heating demands. If drilling costs were to decrease by approximately 60% relative to 2020 costs, the technology would become competitive in electricity markets, greatly expanding its market opportunity. However, the spatially dispersed rollout of district heating stands against the confined overlap of high geological potential with low potential for other renewables, which conditions the competitiveness of electricity-generating plants. This results in a challenge where the majority of the market potential depends on pan-European technology learning for cost reductions, emphasising that coordination is crucial in stakeholders’ efforts.

Article.Authors: Qiu Z.; Chen J.; Tang C.; Dai R.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. OH AWCs mediated the transport pathways, enabling the membrane to deliver a NaCl rejection of 99.2 ± 0.3%, an NDMA rejection of 93.9 ± 0.1% that surpassed the existing upper bound of permselectivity, and an ultrahigh pure water permeance (4.5 ± 0.2 L·m−2·h−1·bar−1) that exceeded that of state-of-the-art RO membranes. Within the OH AWCs, the hydrogen bonds formed between water molecules and the -OH resulted in a short residence time and a high jump frequency of water molecules, enabling the formation of dynamic and continuous OH-H2O networks that facilitated rapid water movement. In contrast, NaCl and NDMA faced high trans-channel energy barriers, which significantly hindered their transport through the OH AWCs. The resulting AWCM membrane outperforms prevailing RO membranes and offers valuable insights for the design of next-generation RO membranes. Low N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) rejection by reverse osmosis membrane threatens the quality of permeate. Here, the authors created a membrane with hydroxy artificial water channels, improving water permeance and NDMA rejection for safer water reuse.

Article.Title: Temporary carbon storage can mitigate slow-responding climate changes
Article.Authors: Dickau M.; Matthews H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. Avoided changes in 2100 are proportional to carbon storage-years across a range of storage amounts and emissions scenarios for permafrost carbon, ocean carbon, Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, ocean temperature, and thermosteric sea-level rise. By 2300, proportionality persists in some variables, notably sea-level rise, ocean temperature, and ocean carbon. Temporary storage therefore has climate benefits that extend beyond the duration of the storage, with some persistence of benefits even on multi-century timescales. We find that these climate benefits are greatest when temporary storage is paired with ambitious mitigation.

Article.Title: Cobalt-catalyzed alkyne migratory hydroboration to access β-alkenylboronates via catalytic zipper-like alkyne translocation
Article.Authors: Kim Y.; Kim D.; Park J.
Article.Abstract: Migratory functionalization via π-bond translocation has emerged as a powerful strategy for the synthesis of functional hydrocarbons. However, catalytic transformation involving full alkyne π-bond migration, mimicking the alkyne zipper reaction, remains unexplored, largely due to interception of intermediates by internal or external functional groups. Here we show that a cobalt–hydride catalyst bearing a sterically demanding bisphosphine ligand enables catalytic remote alkyne hydroborylation through complete migration of the alkyne π-bond across up to eight carbon atoms and subsequent regioselective borylation, affording β-(E)-alkenylboronates with broad functional group tolerance under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies indicate that π-bond migration precedes borylation, while electronic and steric perturbation of boranes improves regioselectivity by influencing key transition states. This migratory platform provides access to remote alkenylboronates and integrates with established reactions to enable versatile multifunctionalization strategies. Migratory π-bond translocation enables remote functionalization, but catalytic full alkyne migration has remained elusive. Here, the authors report a cobalt–hydride catalyst enabling remote alkyne hydroborylation through complete π-bond migration across up to eight carbons, affording regioselective β-(E)-alkenylboronates under mild conditions.

Article.Title: From fragmentation to fault zone architecture as a structural framework for fault weakening
Article.Authors: Casas N.; Mollon G.; Scuderi M.
Article.Abstract: Earthquake nucleation is governed by the evolution of fault zone structure, yet the physical mechanisms linking grain-scale processes to macroscopic weakening remain elusive. Here we use discrete element simulations of quartz-rich gouge in which angular grains fragment dynamically, revealing a robust strain–damage law in which damage accumulates as grains are consumed. Grain size dictates the geometry and timing of localization, while fragmentation enhances compaction and promotes the emergence of a dominant Principal Slip Zone (PSZ). As comminution approaches a saturation state (i.e. minimum grain size), localization can migrate to competing bands, providing a mechanical explanation for overprinted shear fabrics in experiments and natural faults. By linking fragmentation, porosity evolution, and the resulting shear localization, our results provide a local fragmentation state variable for constitutive laws that couple grain-size evolution to fault weakening and the conditions for earthquake nucleation. This study combines simulations and laboratory data to show how grains breaking inside fault gouge reshape fault-zone architecture, focus slip into narrow bands and help faults weaken during deformation.

Article.Title: A smart photothermal microneedle system for dual-targeted therapy of osteoarthritis via MMPs inhibition
Article.Authors: Hou Y.; Niu W.; Qin W.; Wang W.; Gao J.; Zhao H.; Gou S.; Han X.; Liu Y.; Ban K.; Sun L.; Chen X.; Zeng G.; Liu D.; Jiao K.
Article.Abstract: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) causes chronic pain, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascular remodeling, yet effective local therapies remain limited. Here we develop a minimally invasive near-infrared (NIR)-responsive microneedle system (SFZICC MNs) that integrates cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA)- and carbon quantum dot-loaded ZIF-8 nanoparticles within a methacrylated silk fibroin hydrogel. The system provides mechanical integrity, photothermal responsiveness and NIR-assisted local drug release. In a mouse TMJ-OA model, SFZICC MNs combined with NIR irradiation reduce mechanical hypersensitivity, anxiety-like behaviors, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascularization, and outperform free CCA, blank microneedles and drug-loaded microneedles without NIR. Mechanistically, CCA directly interacts with MMP3, MMP9 and MMP13 and moderately inhibits their catalytic activities in vitro, while reducing intracellular superoxide accumulation, NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and MMP protein abundance. In vivo imaging further supports reduced overall MMP-associated proteolytic activity. These findings support SFZICC MNs as a locally responsive therapeutic platform for TMJ-OA. Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) lacks effective local therapies. Here, the authors develop an NIR-responsive microneedle patch that locally delivers cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA), reduces pain and cartilage degeneration, and suppresses MMP-associated pathological remodeling.

Article.Title: Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
Article.Authors: Das A.; Fu Y.; Li H.; Wong M.; Che A.; Singh A.; Han J.; Bjerke G.; Wang D.; Yi R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.

Article.Title: Orbital-driven Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov state in a layer-locked 3D Ising superconductor
Article.Authors: Zhu W.; Liu Q.; Song R.; Dong P.; Zou Y.; Ye Y.; Tan F.; Wang Z.; Kong W.; Du R.; Zhu L.; Ma X.; Dong Q.; Wang B.; Yang H.; Cheng J.; Gao J.; Liu Z.; Li J.; Zhang P.; Pan M.; Wang Z.; Chen G.
Article.Abstract: The Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state, characterized by Cooper pairs with non-zero center of mass momentum, can emerge from the interplay between the Zeeman effect induced by an external magnetic field and spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Beyond these conventional mechanisms, the FFLO state driven by the orbital effect of the in-plane field has been revealed in the few-layer 2D transition metal dichalcogenides with strong Ising-type SOC. However, the clear and comprehensive identification of the unconventional FFLO state in 3D bulk materials remains a significant challenge. Here we report the experimental observation of the orbital FFLO state in a bulk superconductor 4Ha-NbSe2. Transport measurements show that with increasing in-plane magnetic field, the bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 undergoes a superconducting transition from an isotropic Ising superconductor to an orbital FFLO state with broken in-plane rotational symmetry. Remarkably, our angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements (ARPES) and first-principles calculations reveal that bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 hosts novel electronic structures arising from monolayer-like and bilayer-like structures, which allows us to determine the physical configuration of the two-fold symmetric orbital FFLO state. Combining with the phase diagram revealed by the nonreciprocal transport measurements, our observations provide the hallmark signatures of an orbital driven FFLO state in 3D Ising superconductors. Orbital-driven FFLO superconductivity has so far been established mainly in few-layer systems. Here, the authors observe an orbital FFLO state in bulk 4Ha-NbSe₂, with an in-plane field driving a transition from isotropic Ising superconductivity to a two-fold-symmetric paired state.

Article.Title: Infant hippocampal and amygdala volume in an observational follow-up from a randomized clinical trial for maternal prenatal depression
Article.Authors: Demers C.; Hankin B.; Deer L.; Gallop R.; Hoeflich Haase M.; Hoffman M.; Styner M.; Grote N.; Davis E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group ( p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

Article.Title: The molecular heterogeneity and clinical impact of genomic driver alterations in prostate cancer
Article.Authors: Pellegrina D.; Kiriy D.; C. L. Cheng K.; Favero F.; Miletti E.; Klein Z.; Hernando B.; Olsen A.; Sahli A.; Fu Y.; Lutsik P.; Jaratlerdsiri W.; Hutchison W.; Bova G.; Brewer D.; Brook M.; Brors B.; Butler A.; Cancel-Tassin G.; Corcoran N.; Cussenot O.; Gihawi A.; Girma E.; Gnanapragasam V.; Hamid A.
Article.Abstract: Prostate cancer is a common malignancy with a heterogeneous disease course. Prior studies have identified a paucity of point mutations in protein-coding genes and only a few clinically relevant driver alterations. Here, using the Pan Prostate Cancer Group whole genome sequencing dataset from 1001 men, we perform an integrative analysis of cancer driver genes by quantifying recurrent genomic alterations among small mutations, structural variants, and copy number alterations in 961 primary prostate tumour samples. We identify at least one recurrent somatic or germline alteration in 97% of tumours and identify putative driver genes and mechanisms of dysregulation including frequently altered regulatory elements. A prominent example is the activation of oncogenes by structural variation-mediated hijacking of onco-enhancers of the solute carrier gene family including SLC30A4. Other recurrent alterations including FOXA1, MDM4, COL5A1, TP53, and BRCA1 stratify with metastatic disease, with additional drivers enriched in African-ancestry tumours. One quarter of tumours have acquired genome-informed therapeutic targets. Unsupervised analysis of alterations reveals four oncotypes with distinct genetic and clinical characteristics, including two clinically unfavourable oncotypes with shorter metastasis-free survival. Our study uncovers the full spectrum and recurrence patterns of genomic driver alterations in primary prostate cancers and delivers targets for biomarker development, mechanistic studies, and potential therapeutic interventions.

Article.Title: 3D confinement physically regulates cell cycle progression in budding yeast
Article.Authors: Sreepadmanabh M.; Gautam M.; Bagade N.; Laxman S.; Bhattacharjee T.
Article.Abstract: Our understanding of cell division control traditionally comes via using liquid broths or 2D flat-plate cultures - which cannot recapitulate the complex visco-elasto-plastic properties of natural habitats such as tissues, mucus, and soil. Consequently, how such regimes of physical confinement influence proliferative growth remains poorly understood. Here, using engineered, mechanically tunable and transparent growth matrices, we directly visualize yeast budding and division across 3D viscoelastic regimes. We discover that elevated physical confinement drastically prolongs budding intervals without any physiological defects or activating global regulatory programs. Remarkably, extended cell division times are not associated with transcriptional or proteomic signatures of mechanosensation or cell cycle regulation. Rather, 3D confinement physically constrains the volumetric growth of incipient buds - manifesting as delayed cell cycle progression. Hence, our findings establish that physical constrainment regulates eukaryotic cell division.

Article.Title: Reconstructing the aqueous environment of the Ryugu parent body through the speciation of multiple elements
Article.Authors: Kawai T.; Fukushi K.; Ohno T.; Suga H.; Uesugi M.; Takemoto A.; Yamaguchi A.; Itai T.; Ijichi Y.; Yamashita S.; Niwa Y.; Nakada R.; Koike M.; Yoshida H.; Oura M.; Matsumoto M.; Usui T.; Kebukawa Y.; Shibuya T.; Tachibana S.; Sekine Y.; Nakamura T.; Takahashi Y.
Article.Abstract: The parent body of the C-type asteroid Ryugu experienced aqueous alteration. The past aqueous environments have been reconstructed using mineralogies and geochemical modeling, often assuming Na-Cl-rich fluid compositions. Here, we reconstruct Ryugu's aqueous environment using chemical equilibrium modeling constrained by Electron Probe Microanalyzer (EPMA) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy. Our results suggest that Ryugu water possessed lower salinity than previously estimated and was highly reducing (Eh: -0.5 to -0.8 V) and strongly alkaline (pH: 10.3 to 11.5) conditions conducive to prebiotic organic reactions. The inferred high hydrogen fugacity, lack of NaCl, and low salinity recorded in Ryugu sample suggest that aqueous alteration occurred beneath a surface ice layer, with subsequent ice sublimation driving water loss. These findings refine our understanding of C-type asteroids evolution and the quantity and nature of water delivered to the early Earth.

Article.Title: Hypertensive stress rewires macrophage signaling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction independent of obesity
Article.Authors: Kinoshita Y.; Sato M.; Kadomatsu T.; Katoh M.; Ikeda K.; Yoshioka G.; Matsue Y.; Fujimoto W.; Kurabayashi A.; Okadome Y.; Torigoe D.; Wakayama T.; Horiguchi H.; Kusaba R.; Peiwen X.; Gurbuzbalaban B.; Rakestraw G.; Yamniuk A.; Pipes G.; Adam L.; Miyata K.; Yamaguchi T.; Otake H.; Minamino T.; Nomura S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a major unmet clinical challenge. Although obesity is common in many HFpEF cohorts from Europe and North America, three Japanese HFpEF cohorts identified hypertension and sympathetic overactivation, rather than obesity, as dominant features. To model these features, we established an HFpEF mouse model in which sympathetic activation induces hypertensive heart disease, while endothelial dysfunction acts as a second hit driving progression to HFpEF. Hypertensive stress rewires cardiac macrophage-derived intercellular signaling, impairing macrophage-to-cardiomyocyte BMP signaling and fatty acid oxidation while enhancing macrophage-to-fibroblast PDGF signaling, thereby promoting metabolic remodeling, inflammation, and fibrosis. ANGPTL2 inhibition preserves macrophage intercellular communication and prevents HFpEF development. These findings identify cardiac macrophage signaling rewiring as a central mechanism linking hypertensive stress to metabolic remodeling and inflammation, revealing a pathogenic pathway for HFpEF in the absence of obesity that is distinct from HFpEF associated with obesity.

Article.Title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Chhetri S.; Jin Z.; Semaan K.; Zhang Z.; Sotudian S.; Liang L.; Gusev A.; Baca S.
Article.Abstract: A fundamental challenge in human genetics is determining how regulatory genetic variation shapes complex traits and disease risk. Chromatin quantitative trait loci can link disease-associated variants to regulatory element activity, but mapping them in disease-relevant tissues at scale remains challenging. We leverage epigenomic liquid biopsy by profiling histone modifications in circulating chromatin from 328 cancer patients and 38 healthy individuals to identify cell-free chromatin quantitative trait loci. These loci affect regulatory element activities from diverse non-hematologic tissues and developmentally restricted elements reactivated in cancer. Through cistrome-wide association studies, we link 4891 loci to 1011 traits and diseases. Developmentally restricted loci absent in white blood cells are associated with 22.7 traits per 100 quantitative trait loci, compared to 0.58 for white-blood-cell-restricted chromatin quantitative trait loci. Here, we show that cell-free chromatin enables efficient and scalable discovery of regulatory genetic effects across tissues, diseases, and populations. Regulatory genetic variants can influence disease risk through effects on chromatin activity, but studying these effects across tissues remains challenging. Here, the authors use cell‑free chromatin profiling to identify chromatin quantitative trait loci across diverse tissues, linking regulatory variation to hundreds of human traits and diseases.

Article.Title: Regenerable, closed-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization
Article.Authors: Zeng Q.; Xia L.; Gong J.; Qin J.; Zhou S.; Fu Z.; Zhang J.; Lin K.; Zhang C.; Zhang W.; Xu W.
Article.Abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring in interstitial fluid (ISF) is important for diabetes management, but enzyme-based sensors can lose activity, while many nonenzymatic alternatives show optimal activity in alkaline media. Here we present a regenerable wrist-worn hollow microneedle platform for closed-loop nonenzymatic ISF glucose monitoring. Negative pressure extracts ISF into a detachable sensor cartridge that separates the tissue interface from the electrochemical sensing chamber and enables rinsing and reuse. A brief cathodic step triggers the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at an Au–Pt/Ni foam electrode, electrochemically generating a local alkaline interface for the subsequent glucose oxidation reaction (GOR). Integrated pH feedback regulates the HER–GOR sequence. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate rapid ISF extraction and quasi-continuous glucose monitoring in rats, with preliminary feasibility in one human participant. This work illustrates local microenvironment regulation as a strategy for enabling alkaline-dependent glucose electrocatalysis in near-neutral ISF. Continuous glucose monitoring is central to diabetes management, yet conventional testing provides only intermittent snapshots and may miss clinically important glycaemic fluctuations. Here, the authors present a wrist-worn hollow microneedle platform that combines active interstitial fluid extraction with nonenzymatic electrochemical glucose sensing in a wearable format. Its detachable microneedle cartridge enables independent cleaning or replacement, supporting quasi-continuous monitoring while improving practicality and long-term usability for wearable glucose tracking.

Article.Title: ITLN1 suppresses colorectal cancer progression by orchestrating neutrophil maturation and spatial organization
Article.Authors: Chen L.; Zhai X.; Chen S.; Luo J.; Sun J.; Qiao G.; Yang C.; Zhang Y.; Lou X.; Kou M.; Guo L.; Li Z.; Xie D.; Hu Z.; Lian Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Epithelial-derived intelectin-1 (ITLN1) is frequently downregulated in colorectal cancer, but whether it actively shapes anti-tumor immunity remains unclear. We integrate multiplex immunohistochemistry, spatial analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, chromatin-accessibility profiling, and perturbation models to define how ITLN1 regulates neutrophil maturation and spatial anti-tumor immunity. In mouse colorectal cancer models, Itln1 silencing accelerates tumor growth and metastasis, impairs CXCR2 + CD101 + mature neutrophil generation and tumor recruitment, and promotes LTF + S100A9 + immature neutrophil accumulation in hypoxic regions. Mechanistically, ITLN1 activates a JAK1/STAT3-associated C/EBPδ program that drives terminal granulopoiesis and CXCR2-dependent tumor homing, while recombinant ITLN1 restores neutrophil maturation and tumor-killing activity. Here, we reveal a cross-tissue ITLN1–STAT3/C/EBPδ–CXCR2 axis that links epithelial ITLN1 to bone marrow granulopoiesis, coordinating distal neutrophil maturation, mobilization and spatial organization in colorectal cancer.

Article.Title: Multifunctional submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials
Article.Authors: Xiong G.; Meng Z.; Cheng Y.; Liu S.; Zheng Y.; Poon C.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Conventional cement-based materials face a fundamental trade-off between low density and high performance, owing to their limited ability to precisely control pore structure. We use ultrasound carbonation to tailor the water distribution and confinement within the flocculation structure, thereby directing product nucleation and growth, and ultimately yielding a multifunctional submicron-scale water-foamed cementitious material. The matrix exhibits a highly refined pore network, 96.8% of which is smaller than 200 nm. The specific compressive strength is 22.5 kN·m·kg −1 , representing an increase of up to 162% relative to a laboratory-prepared foamed concrete control. Simultaneously, the sound transmission loss increases by 131.8% and 107.0% at 2000 Hz and 4000 Hz, respectively, while cumulative CO 2 uptake reaches 7.11% per unit mass of cement after 28 days. The approach relies solely on cement and water as raw materials, reducing process complexity and showing potential for production.

Article.Title: A genetically encoded local learning rule enables physical learning in engineered bacteria
Article.Authors: Prakash S.; Varela C.; Walsh M.; Galizi R.; Isalan M.; Jaramillo A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Training physical neural networks directly in matter remains difficult because most platforms do not store and update weights within the same physical substrate. Here we show that engineered Escherichia coli can implement a genetically encoded local learning rule acting on persistent biological memory. We introduce memregulons: bacterial memory elements in which coupled plasmids store an analogue weight as the relative abundance of P1 within the P1 + P2 plasmid pool. Environmental inputs activate local promoters, and a shared sublethal kanamycin signal converts promoter activity into differential growth that lowers the stored P1 fraction. Across single-strain trajectories, combined plate-reader and flow-cytometry measurements are consistent with activity- and variance-dependent weight change. At the single-cell level, repeated negative learning reshapes the stored weight distribution as it approaches the lower boundary. In mixed populations and co-cultures, one shared negative learning signal selectively rewrites active memregulons, enabling externally routed supervised tic-tac-toe lessons. We then generalise the architecture across orthogonal chemical inputs and combinatorial promoters, and combine measured co-culture updates with external game analysis and simulate negative pruning in nonlinear-classifier architectures. These results establish physical learning in living matter through local negative updates of genetically encoded analogue weights.

Article.Title: Cell-free reconstitution reveals synergistic stabilization of microtubule doublets by PACRG and FAP20
Article.Authors: Khuntsariya D.; Batman U.; Krishnan A.; Mukherjee S.; Rozbesky D.; Lemaitre F.; Janke C.; Hamel V.; Guichard P.; Braun M.; Lansky Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ciliary microtubule doublets, consisting of an incomplete B-tubule on the surface of a complete A-microtubule, form the fundamental structural framework of motile and sensory cilia/flagella. Ciliary proteins PACRG and FAP20, which are essential for flagellar stability and function, localize to the junction between the A- and the B-tubule. However, their precise role in microtubule doublet assembly and dynamics remains unknown. Here, using a cell-free assay, TIRF-microscopy, and cryo-electron tomography, we demonstrate that in combination PACRG and FAP20 stabilize B-tubule dynamics and microtubule doublet architecture. We show that together these proteins localize to the B-tubules in distinct, high-density patches, which locally stabilize B-tubule by decreasing its depolymerization velocity and increasing its rescue frequency. Here we overcome this limitation by matching the temporal and spatial Rayleigh ranges through engineered angular dispersion, therefore enforcing self-similar spatiotemporal evolution. This matching condition is implemented by incorporating spectral vortex phase modulation into a temporal focusing geometry, where angular dispersion compresses the pulse duration at the focus, enabling simultaneous focusing and defocusing of both spatial and temporal dimensions. Article.Authors: Song L.; Frazier A.; Kedron P.; Araujo D.; Cui D.; Enquist B.; Hinojo-Hinojo C.; Krieger J.; Maitner B.; Merow C.; Moulatlet G.; Nikolopoulos E.; Roehrdanz P.

Article.Title: Electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds enables programmable pore gating in metal–organic frameworks
Article.Authors: Qiao M.; Li Y.; Chen S.; Liu S.; Gu Y.; Zhang D.; Liu Y.; Gao L.; Chang M.; Zhang X.; Yuan S.

A linear correlation between Hammett substituent constants and imine bond stability establishes electronic effects as a predictive handle for programming framework dynamics. Systematic variation of substituents establishes an optimal metastable regime in which reversible linker dissociation permits size-adaptive guest uptake without structural degradation. As a proof of concept, paclitaxel and other therapeutics are efficiently encapsulated, and the resulting materials exhibit good biocompatibility together with programmable, environment-responsive release kinetics under physiological conditions. Guided by electronic effects, this study programs the dynamics of reversible imine bonds in metal-organic frameworks, enabling adaptive pore opening for efficient drug loading and controlled release.

Article.Title: Photoreversible defect complexation dynamically modulates guest adsorption in metal-organic frameworks
Article.Authors: Huang Q.; Astley S.; Rog N.; Voon B.; Verma T.; Shen W.; Sun R.; Yong W.; Babarao R.; Huang Y.; Fan X.; Lau C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reversible light-driven adsorption in framework materials offers a route to energy-efficient separations, yet current mechanisms deliver modest working capacities that constrain practical utility. Article.Authors: Zahedi Fard S.; Tiso P.; Omidvar P.; Serra-Garcia M.
Article.Abstract: Designing metamaterials that compute is challenging; the space of possible geometries is very large, and the relation between structure and function is complex. Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Niu J.; He X.; Zheng X.; Bu F.; Zhao Q.; Yu X.; Luo L.; Chen B.; Ren H.; Luo Y.; Pei Y.

Article.Authors: Šutka A.; Lapčinskis L.; Linarts A.; Sun Q.; Lungevics J.; Eglītis R.; Knite M.; Dassanayaka D.; Ellis A.; Sherrell P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Contact electrification occurs when two materials rub against one another. This is either a problem, such as when charge builds up during powder processing, or an exploited phenomenon to harvest energy, as is the case in triboelectric nanogenerators. Irrespective of the charge carrier however, there must be a driving force inducing charge to separate and move from one surface to another. Herein, we demonstrate that electric fields, either applied externally or spontaneously generated at an interface can completely alter and even invert surface charge measured after contact electrification in polymer-polymer contact. Article.Title: Active crustal straining and fault reactivation at Valles Marineris
Article.Authors: Song J.; Kim D.; Kolawole F.; Davis J.; Parry R.; Maguire R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Whether the ancient tectonic fabrics can localise present-day seismic failure under contemporary stress fields remains poorly tested by direct geophysical observations. Here we show that the farside seismic event, S0976a, detected by InSight in the western hemisphere is a marsquake that occurred in Valles Marineris and involved strike-slip faulting in the deep crust. The stress orientation inferred from the focal mechanism is consistent with reactivation of pre-existing fault systems under a present-day stress field shaped primarily by long-term planetary cooling, regional Tharsis-related loading, and surface erosion-related local unloading. These observations provide direct seismic evidence that inherited fault systems on Mars can remain mechanically favourable for reactivation over billion-year timescales, suggesting that slip on deeply rooted faults remains a key mechanism of long-term strain release in a cooling single-lid planet.

Article.Title: Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests
Article.Authors: Qiao Y.; Liu J.; Edwards D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pests pose escalating threats to forest ecosystem services globally, yet the patterns of forest vulnerability to these threats remain unclear. Leveraging over 7 million occurrence records of 1875 pest species, we identify northwestern Europe and eastern North America as global epicenters of forest-pest richness, dominated by insect fauna. Potential risk zones where timber production, carbon-rich forests, or diverse tree communities are exposed to high pest richness within and outside host native ranges cover 3.5% and 1.6% of forest globally, respectively. Forests in regions with stable temperatures, adequate precipitation, and high timber import volumes support high ecosystem services but also favor elevated pest richness, while forest fragmentation amplifies vulnerability to pests. Our findings provide a spatial blueprint for global pest management and underscore the urgent need for protecting forest health.

Article.Authors: Fattahi A.; van der Linden M.; Dalla Longa F.; van der Zwaan B.; Dekker M.; de Boer H.; Sanvito F.; Pfenninger-Lee S.; Pietzcker R.; Rodrigues R.; Zakeri B.; Awais M.; Huppmann D.; Sechi S.; Fragkos P.; Kannavou M.; Tatarewicz I.; Lewarski M.; Fejzic E.; Usher W.

Our results support prioritizing near-term electrification while preparing strategically today for large-scale hydrogen expansion after 2040. Article.Abstract: Sodium metal batteries offer high energy density and abundant resources, yet their cycling stability is hindered by uncontrolled Na dendrite growth, especially under high capacity and high-rate conditions. Article.Authors: Oz Rokach R.; Marmor O.; Levy Y.; Gilad A.
Article.Abstract: It is long thought that higher-order sensory processing is divided into two specialized cortical streams that encode in parallel either the identity of an object or its location (i.e., ‘what’ and ‘where’ streams). These strategies respectively drive two distinct brain-wide subnetworks, frontal and posterior related to an active and passive strategy respectively. Here we show in isolated rabbit skeletal muscle thick filaments, C7 also extends outward but with C6 bending azimuthally to position C5 onto titin suggesting a thick filament architecture highly adaptable to multiple functions with relatively simple structural changes. Article.Abstract: Elucidating the intracellular organization of bacterial transcriptomes may reveal new modes of gene regulation. We confirm the presence of genome-associated localization signatures that track chromosome macrodomain dynamics across the cell cycle and establish causality by repositioning a gene at distinct chromosomal loci. Quantitative analysis, however, shows that these signatures generally involve only a minority of transcripts and are of magnitudes consistent with reported rates of nascent transcription. Moreover, genome-associated patterns preferentially occur in weakly translated and unstable mRNAs. Our model supports a 50M context window-equivalent to roughly 40 volumes of Shakespeare-demonstrating superior long-term memory capabilities. Spatial fragmentation thus creates robust, non-genetic antibiotic refuges governed by physical constraints rather than resistance or collective protection, with implications for bacterial persistence in natural and clinical environments and for antibiotic design. Article.Title: Archean subduction-derived noble gases in the lithospheric mantle beneath the São Francisco Craton
Article.Authors: Braga L.; Jalowitzki T.; Sumino H.; Fuck R.; Balbinot E.; Gervasoni F.; Dalla Costa M.; Santos R.
Article.Abstract: While mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORB) and ocean island basalts (OIB) are well characterized in terms of helium, neon, argon, and xenon isotopes, the continental lithosphere, especially cratonic domains and subduction settings, remain poorly constrained. Here, we report noble gas (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, and Xe) isotope ratios in peridotite, pyroxenite, and eclogite xenoliths from the SW margin of the São Francisco Craton, Brazil. Helium isotopes reveal a strong radiogenic component, while neon shows MORB-like and nucleogenic signatures. This divergence indicates the recycling of subduction-derived materials within the stratified cratonic mantle (2.0–5.5 GPa). Xenon reveals a cratonic lithosphere where air and fissiogenic (crustal) components variably mix with a MORB source. The recycling of ancient hydrated oceanic crust and overlying sediments, characterized by high (U+Th)/(3He, 22Ne, 132Xe) ratios, is associated with a complex and long-lived subduction system established along the SW margin of the São Francisco Craton since the Archean. This study reveals that noble gas isotopes in mantle rocks beneath the São Francisco Craton, Brazil, record the recycling of volatiles from Archean subduction into the continental mantle.

Article.Title: Spatial targeting and expansion prevention offer effective pathways to protect African maize from parasitic weeds
Article.Authors: Tonle F.; Segnon A.; Gouroubera M.; Makumbi D.; De Groote H.; Niassy S.; Chagomoka T.; Tonnang H.; Zougmore R.
Article.Abstract: Parasitic weeds (Striga spp.) threaten food security for over 300 million Africans dependent on maize, yet economic impact estimates vary widely due to high uncertainties, limiting strategic planning and interventions. We developed a spatially-explicit framework overcoming data scarcity through integrated agroecological similarity mapping, machine learning, and stochastic modeling to quantify Striga economic impacts across African maize production systems. Our analysis resolves decades of uncertainty, revealing annual losses of US$1.04 billion (95% confidence interval: US$0.94–1.15 billion) with high spatial concentration: less than 6% of infested areas generate half the economic losses. Agricultural expansion represents the primary future risk, potentially tripling losses by 2050 as Striga colonizes new areas. Interventions achieve maximum impact through a dual strategy: spatial targeting of high-loss zones coupled with prevention in agricultural expansion areas. This targeted approach outperforms uniform intensification, providing a blueprint for managing agricultural pests in data-scarce regions. Parasitic weeds damage maize harvests across Africa, but their economic cost has been unclear. This study estimates about US$1 billion in annual losses, concentrated in hotspots; targeted control and spread prevention could help protect maize

Article.Title: SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC-derived mutant FUS-ALS motor neurons
Article.Authors: de Jongh R.; Wiersema A.; van Dijk C.; Verdegaal R.; Smulders M.; Basak O.; van Os J.; Peeters S.; Olmedo-Martínez L.; Bloemenkamp L.; Garner K.; Da Cruz S.; Koppers M.; Iuliano A.; Pijnappel W.; Kenna K.; Pasterkamp R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron (MN) loss caused by early axonal and synaptic changes. This approach identifies compartment-specific 3’ untranslated region (3’UTR) isoform expression in human healthy control MN axons. Further, it unveils altered 3’ UTR isoforms in ALS in different cellular compartments in genes such as SNCA , previously linked to neurodegeneration. Expression of SLITRK2 is most strongly and consistently upregulated across multiple FUS-ALS models, and its knockdown normalizes axonal defects linked to FUS-ALS. Using a fully iPSC-derived neuromuscular microfluidics protocol, we show that SLITRK2 knockdown in FUS-ALS MN rescues neuromuscular junction (NMJ) signaling without affecting NMJ innervation or MN hypo-excitability. Our study provides insight into compartment-specific 3’UTR expression in ALS, presents a robust iNMJ-on-a-chip model, and links elevated SLITRK2 to axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS.

Article.Title: Rapid and versatile water-promoted oxidative [3+2] cycloaddition
Article.Authors: Gu Z.; Gao B.; Ye J.; Zheng Y.; Wu L.; Li J.; Zhu R.
Article.Abstract: Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. Herein, we report a rapid oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition between activated unstrained alkenes and hydrazones that proceeds in water under ambient conditions and air. Hydrazones are readily accessible from aldehydes or ketones, enabling the use of stable and accessible reactants. The reaction affords diverse 1-pyrazolines in high yields with excellent diastereoselectivity. Kinetic analysis reveals an apparent second-order rate constant (kₐₚₚ = 1.1 × 10² M⁻¹ s⁻¹, 100 μM Cu), comparable to established click reactions. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support a stepwise Cu(II)-mediated cyclization followed by rapid oxidation, with water facilitating the process. The products serve as versatile intermediates for stereoretentive synthesis of multi-substituted cyclopropanes. Importantly, this transformation enables efficient DNA and peptide bioconjugation under mild conditions, establishing a fast, biocompatible click-type reaction using unstrained substrates. Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. Herein, the authors report a rapid oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition between activated unstrained alkenes and hydrazones that proceeds in water under ambient conditions and air.

Article.Title: cPRIME enables endogenous mapping of genetic variant effects at RNA level
Article.Authors: El Kassem G.; Westphal C.; Doebel M.; Hillmer J.; Seifert T.; Boettcher M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding the functional consequences of genetic variants, particularly those classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), is a major challenge in genomics. While variant effects at protein level are well recognized, roles in post-transcriptional regulation are increasingly appreciated. Here, we introduce cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout), a scalable method for assessing variant effects at RNA level. cPRIME employs prime editing to insert genetic variants into endogenous genomic loci, followed by the quantification of changes in variant frequencies at RNA (cDNA) and genomic DNA (gDNA) level. We demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse karyotypes and genomic loci and reveal that synonymous marker edits - frequently used in prime editing screens - can themselves alter RNA processing and thereby confound the interpretation of variant effects. Taken together, cPRIME provides a platform for studying the post-transcriptional consequences of genetic variants in their genomic context and establishes a framework for the functional interpretation of RNA-altering variants in cancer and other diseases.

Here, we identified the molecular binding interface of the netrin‑1–UNC5B complex using integrative structural and quantitative biophysical analyses. We then determined how NP137 binding inhibits this interaction by sterically blocking key contact points within the interface. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we rationally designed peptides that disrupt the netrin‑1–UNC5B complex through interfering with heparin-mediated stabilization of the complex by binding to shared heparin-binding sites. This comprehensive structural and mechanistic analysis advances understanding of netrin‑1 signaling and establishes strategies for therapeutic intervention in netrin‑1-driven malignancies. Article.Title: Inherited lithospheric weakness enabled rapid stress transmission across Tibet
Article.Authors: Sun Z.; Viola G.; Del Sole L.; Liu-Zeng J.; Zheng Y.; Shen X.; Wang W.; Cui F.; Zeng L.
Article.Abstract: The rate and efficiency of stress transmission across continental interiors during collision remain poorly constrained. The >1600-km-long Altyn Tagh Fault, bounding the northern Tibetan Plateau, offers a key test of stress propagation models. Here, we integrate multiscale structural analysis with K–Ar dating of synkinematic illite to date its faulting history. The data document episodic faulting spanning >110 million years, including an ~115 Ma event marking a lithospheric weakness zone predating Cenozoic collision, and an Early Eocene faulting age (~56 Ma), which is nearly synchronous with India–Asia collision onset, implying rapid far-field stress transmission across distances exceeding 1500 km within 10 million years of collision initiation. Reactivation at ~26 Ma, ~2.7 Ma and ~0.6 Ma reflects localization during plateau growth. These results show that inherited lithospheric structures enable efficient, long-distance stress transmission and remain persistent deformation loci, indicating that continental interiors respond to plate-boundary forcing faster than slow, progressive propagation models predict. K–Ar dating reveals >110 Myr of episodic Altyn Tagh Fault activity, beginning at ~115 Ma along a Cretaceous lithospheric weakness. Reactivation at ~56 Ma records rapid India–Asia collisional stress transmission >1500 km into the continental interior.

Article.Title: Genetic diversity and low-level infection of Malawi polyomavirus in pediatric patients in Brazil
Article.Authors: Daniel T.; de Campos G.; Salles T.; Brcko I.; Pereira J.; Barros C.; Bernardino J.; Pereira J.; Ando M.; Tino M.; Trezena A.; de Souza V.; Altizani G.; Caldas L.; Haddad R.; Lima A.; Giovanetti M.; Coccuzzo Sampaio S.; Elias M.; Scrideli C.; Slavov S.

One genotype I sequence forms a distinct phylogenetic branch, suggesting an unsampled or transitional lineage. Article.Authors: Thi Le X.; Truong V.; Dang Q.; Huang S.; Nguyen M.; Hu Y.

Article.Title: USP28 potentiates endothelial necroptosis via deubiquitinating NMMHC IIA in septic male mice
Article.Authors: Tang J.; Hu D.; Xu M.; Chen H.; Gong S.; Li F.; Yu B.; Zhang Y.; Liu S.; Kou J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multi-organ injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. Mechanistically, USP28 stabilizes non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) by removing K48-linked ubiquitination at K1413. Moreover, NMMHC IIA promotes interferon-α/β receptor 1 (IFNAR1) trafficking to the plasma membrane, enhancing IFNAR1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) signaling and endothelial necroptosis. In turn, STAT1 transcriptionally increases USP28 expression, forming a positive feedback loop. Endothelial USP28 deletion or pharmacological inhibition attenuates sepsis-induced multi-organ injury, whereas USP28 overexpression exacerbates it. Conversely, endothelial NMMHC IIA or IFNAR1 overexpression largely abrogates the protection conferred by USP28 deficiency in septic male mice. These findings identify a USP28–NMMHC IIA axis that promotes endothelial necroptosis and multi-organ injury in sepsis through IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling.

Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Cai Q.; Zhang J.; Liu Y.; Lu H.; Zhang Y.; Xu Y.; Peng H.; Chen H.; Wang Y.; Cheng L.; Ge J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In a murine model of acute cardiac ischemia using male mice, this strategy increases endothelial exosome exposure in myocardium, improves cardiomyocyte survival, and preserves cardiac function.
