Article.Title: Global rise of a wheat pathogen through two-stage evolutionary emergence coupled with aerial dispersal
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Li Y.; Zhan G.; Zhao J.; Zhang Z.; Liu H.; Basu U.; Kanyuka K.; Davis H.; Qucuo Z.; Tao F.; Gao H.; Li G.; Ma J.; Yao Q.; Jia Q.; Cao S.; Hu Y.; Li Y.; Huang W.; Bai Y.; Tadesse W.; Jonas-Levi A.; Song W.; Huang L.
Article.Abstract: The rise of plant pathogens following crop domestication and their subsequent global spread pose persistent threats to food security, yet the mechanisms underlying host jumps and rapid adaptation in obligate biotrophs remain unclear. Using 319 Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst) genomes and virulence phenotypes of 234 isolates across six continents, we construct its origin and global dissemination. Our analyses support a two-stage emergence model: P. striiformis sensu stricto originated and diversified in the Himalayan region, subsequently a P. striiformis s. str. lineage jumped to domesticated wheat in the Fertile Crescent, giving rise to epidemic lineage (Pst) and spreading worldwide with wheat cultivation. This host jump triggered demographic expansion and selective sweeps, while GWAS identified region-specific virulence loci shaped by resistant cultivars. Overlay of air trajectory and dispersal simulations identified atmospheric corridors consistent with genomic migration patterns, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport in the pathogen’s global spread. Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici, an obligate fungal pathogen, threatens wheat production worldwide. Using 319 genomes and virulence data from 234 isolates globally, this study constructs its two-stage emergence and global dissemination, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport.

Article.Title: Serine-65 phosphorylated ubiquitin associates with soluble tau and seeding activity in Alzheimer’s disease
Article.Authors: Yan T.; Hou X.; Watzlawik J.; Dickson D.; Fiesel F.; Springer W.
Article.Abstract: Tau propagation is a key driver of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet selective markers of seeding-competent tau remain elusive. Ubiquitin phosphorylated at Serine-65 (pS65-Ub) is a PINK1-derived cellular stress signal that accumulates in AD with elevated tau pathology, but its relationship to tau seeding is unknown. Here, using postmortem brain tissue from female and male donors, we show that a subset of tau is covalently modified by pS65-Ub in AD brain. The pS65-Ub-associated tau population is elevated in AD and is enriched in soluble, high-molecular-weight, oligomeric, and hyperphosphorylated tau species. Across AD cases, soluble pS65-Ub-associated tau levels strongly correlate with tau seeding activity. Tau species isolated with pS65-Ub antibodies exhibit seeding activity, whereas removal of pS65-Ub-associated material markedly reduces seeding from AD brain extracts. Together, these findings identify pS65-Ub as a disease-enriched molecular feature of a seed-competent tau population and link cellular stress signaling with pathological tau propagation in AD. Not all selective markers of seeding-competent Tau are known. Here, the authors identify pS65-Ub-associated tau linked to pathological Tau spreading and elevated in Alzheimer’s disease. Removal of pS65-Ub reduces tau seeding activity.

Article.Title: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
Article.Authors: Mazumder A.; Cooper J.; Goksal C.; Brockhausen R.; Schauß J.; Khanduja J.; Joh R.; Amine A.; Groos J.; Kanoh J.; Motamedi M.; Finkelstein I.; Al-Sady B.; Braun S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.

Article.Title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Chen P.; Jamet C.; Zhang S.; Shi K.; Pan D.
Article.Abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. While the chlorophyll-increase phase has lengthened by 2.3–5.5 days, the post-peak chlorophyll-decline phase has extended disproportionately by 5.7–6.2 days. Environmental sensitivity analyses reveal distinct hemispheric patterns in the statistical associations between phenological variability and multiple co-varying physical and biogeochemical factors, consistent with contrasting nutrient regimes between the Northern and Southern high-latitude oceans. We further show that these shifts are associated with spatially heterogeneous changes in marine chlorophyll accumulation patterns. Our results identify bloom asymmetry as an important dimension of marine phenological change, providing an observational baseline for evaluating future links between chlorophyll phenology, ecosystem timing, and polar biogeochemical processes under climate change. This study shows that unequal changes in bloom duration between hemispheres contribute to contrasting high-latitude ocean chlorophyll trends, linking asymmetric phytoplankton phenology to marine ecosystem changes under climate warming.

Article.Title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Ren Z.; Gao Y.; Li H.; Xiao H.; Liu Q.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. Oleylamine ligands adsorbed on NiMoO4 sub-nanowires act as mild reductants, selectively reducing Ni2+ to spatially confined metallic Ni domains and forming coherent Ni/NiMoO4 heterointerfaces. Experimental and theoretical analyses suggest that the Ni/NiMoO4 interfaces modify the local electronic structure and facilitate the adsorption and activation of hydrogen evolution intermediates. The resulting catalyst requires an overpotential of 14.4 ± 2.9 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and delivers 2 A cm−2 at 1.62 V in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer at 80 oC, with stable operation over 2200 h at 25 °C. These findings provide insights into the construction and interfacial regulation of sub-nanometer heterostructures through in situ reduction. Sub-nanometer heterostructures offer opportunities to tune interfacial reactivity, but their precise construction remains challenging. Here, the authors report alternating Ni/NiMoO₄ heterostructures that promote hydrogen evolution and sustain durable high-current electrolysis.

Article.Title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
Article.Authors: Adamczyk S.; Adamczyk B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

Article.Title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
Article.Authors: Sebastianelli Arbelaez M.; Enbody E.; Rubin C.; Valle C.; Keller L.; Grant B.; Grant P.; Andersson L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin’s finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03 , a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -( G03 )- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin’s finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity.

Article.Title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
Article.Authors: Sabbatini C.; Le Strat Y.; Bonaldi C.; Brouard C.; Audran M.; Saboni L.; Richard J.; David A.; Gaudy-Graffin C.; Chevaliez S.; Barin F.; Stefic K.; Jauffret-Roustide M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions.

Article.Title: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
Article.Authors: Minet G.; Ray A.; Pennacchietti F.; Coceano G.; Jug F.; Testa I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation.

Article.Title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
Article.Authors: Zheng Y.; Zhai X.; Stevens D.; Wu W.; Gong W.; Du Y.
Article.Abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. We further show that these trends in Atlantic NICs are primarily driven by changes in near-inertial wind forcing, particularly those associated with mesoscale weather systems, while variations in mixed-layer depth playing a minor role. This observed intensification of Atlantic NICs may have important implications for ocean transport and mixing, and needs to be properly represented in the current generation of climate models. Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems.

Article.Title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Liu L.; Sun X.; Wu H.; Fu S.; Jin J.; Zhang Y.; Zhang X.; Zeng Z.; Tao Z.; Chen N.; Wang X.; Lv J.; Luo P.; Hu D.; Gao H.; Keasling J.; Luo X.
Article.Abstract: Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)—an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning—directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. We apply OSAR to 34 low- to medium-GC bacterial NRPS clusters (7–78 kb) and successfully assemble 31. Expression in Bacillus subtilis yields 29 peptides from 10 clusters. Several products arose from cryptic biosynthetic behaviors such as potential module skipping and premature release. OSAR provides a practical workflow for assembly and refactoring of NRPS clusters and may facilitate the translation of sequence information into natural products. Existing approaches for biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) discovery are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that an automated platform for one-step assembly and refactoring of BGCs facilitates facile novel product discovery.

Article.Title: ETSAM: effectively segmenting cell membranes in cryo-electron tomograms
Article.Authors: Selvaraj J.; Cheng J.
Article.Abstract: Cryogenic Electron Tomography (cryo-ET) is an emerging experimental technique used to visualize cell structures and macromolecules in their native cellular environment. Accurate segmentation of cell structures in cryo-ET tomograms, such as cell membranes, supports the study of cellular organization and function. However, several inherent limitations in cryo-ET, including the very low signal-to-noise ratio, missing wedge artifacts from limited tilt angles, and other noise artifacts, collectively hinder the reliable identification and delineation of these structures. In this study, we present ETSAM, a two-stage Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2)-based fine-tuned AI method that effectively segments cell membranes in tomograms. It is trained on a diverse dataset comprising 83 experimental tomograms from the CryoET Data Portal (CDP) database and 28 simulated tomograms generated using PolNet. On an independent test set of 17 experimental tomograms for which ground-truth annotations are available, ETSAM outperforms other deep learning based methods by robustly identifying cell membranes with high sensitivity while also maintaining better precision. Cell membranes are hard to distinguish in the noisy 3D volumes from cryo-electron tomography. Here, authors adapt a video segmentation foundation model to the task, segmenting membranes across diverse organisms more accurately than existing tools.

Article.Title: Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys
Article.Authors: Ma Y.; Wang Z.; Zhang J.; Xu N.; Duan Z.; Li D.; Wu Z.; Chang X.; Shao R.; Huang T.; Wang X.; Sun Z.; Wang C.; An Z.; Yang C.; Zhang J.; Liao X.; Wang L.; Han X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe 48 Mn 32 Co 10 Cr 10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation.

Article.Title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model
Article.Authors: Wu X.; Zhao Z.; Ouyang S.; Hao X.; Li J.; Zhu W.; Zhang T.; Lu S.; Dong T.; Jiang N.; Yang X.; Guo H.; Li J.; Tian T.; Yang R.
Article.Abstract: Dynamic remodeling of immune cell-surface glycans reflects cellular state and immune activity. Despite advances in single-cell glyco-profiling, current methods primarily capture pre-existing glycan epitopes, providing limited information on dynamic sialoglycans. Here, we present GlycoStamp-seq, a method to profile nascent sialoglycan dynamics by coupling Ac₄ManNAz-based metabolic glycoengineering with single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) and scDyna-seq. We apply GlycoStamp-seq by injecting Ac₄ManNAz into oxaliplatin-treated mice with subcutaneous bladder tumors, days before extracting tumor-derived single-cell suspensions for sequencing. Following oxaliplatin treatment, a subset of CD8⁺ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment exhibits elevated nascent sialoglycan activity, enhanced effector programs, and increased clonal expansion. Furthermore, elevated nascent sialoglycan levels mark antigen-reactive CD8⁺ T cells with increased anti-tumor efficacy in vitro and in vivo. GlycoStamp-seq may thus serve as a versatile platform for profiling nascent sialoglycan dynamics in complex tissues, thereby expanding the single-cell multi-omics toolkit and providing insights into sialoglycan dynamics during therapeutic response. Glycosylation is critical for an effective immune response, but immune cell glycan dynamics are not fully understood. Here, the authors present GlycoStamp-seq to track sialoglycan dynamics, and apply GlycoStamp-seq in an oxaliplatin-treated subcutaneous bladder cancer mouse model.

Article.Title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
Article.Authors: Zhong H.; Kochan D.; Žutić I.; Wu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe 2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1 ∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits.

Article.Title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing
Article.Authors: Xu X.; Wang X.; Cui Y.; Liu Q.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Piezoelectric electronic skin (PE-skin) offers a significant advantage in detecting minute forces, making it highly promising for human-computer interaction in health management and medical rehabilitation. However, PE-skin often faces challenges in real-time, wireless transmission of sensing data, which can compromise both data accuracy and user comfort. Here, we report the synthesis of an inorganic piezoelectric polyoxometalate-based subnanowire, ZnBiPMo12, which possesses intrinsic flexibility and chirality, a piezoelectric coefficient of 24.9 pC/N, and notable ferroelectricity. Leveraging its piezoelectric response, ZnBiPMo12-based PE-skin (1) demonstrates high elasticity and sensitivity to tiny pressures in the range of 0.045-0.319 N. Building on this, a wireless, wearable bioelectronic (WBE) device (1A) is fabricated through multi-level assembly, enabling non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals, including subtle muscle contractions, blinking, breathing, and all-day heart rate. By integrating a machine learning system, a 1-based facial-computer interface (1B) can accurately recognize nine emotional expressions and twelve spoken words. This work not only introduces a typical inorganic piezoelectric material with intrinsic flexibility but also demonstrates scalable manufacturing from subnanomaterials to wireless WBEs, paving the way for non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals and advanced human-computer interaction. Piezoelectric materials enable bioelectronic sensing by converting mechanical stimuli into electrical signals. Xu et al. introduce intrinsically flexible polyoxometalate-based subnanowires and demonstrate their scalable integration into wireless wearable systems for human physiological monitoring.

Article.Title: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
Article.Authors: Jiao A.; Maghrouni A.; Gutierrez A.; Annett A.; Manokaran C.; Wen T.; Grassl N.; Chan J.; Nguyen S.; Bou-Tayeh B.; Jawhar W.; Le Dily F.; Kleinman C.; Di Croce L.; Jabado N.; Shi Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) drive aggressive diffuse midline gliomas by blocking differentiation of radial glial progenitor cells committed to oligodendrogenesis. We establish prolonged differentiation as a powerful tool to uncover regulators of glioma cell states and demonstrate that the pioneer transcription factor (TF) ASCL1 is a key mediator of H3K27M-driven plasticity and tumorigenesis. H3K27M prevents Polycomb silencing of ASCL1 , co-opting this TF to maintain oligodendroglial progenitor states. Consistently, ASCL1 loss drastically impairs tumor formation in vivo. Mechanistically, ASCL1 synergizes with H3K27M to redistribute the chromatin remodeler BRG1 to regulatory elements co-enriched for ASCL1 and SOX motifs, promoting expression of stem and neural progenitor genes at the expense of mesenchymal genes in DMGs. ASCL1 loss acts as a “fire exit”, enabling alternative differentiation despite H3K27M, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting stalled differentiation and tumor plasticity in histone-mutant gliomas and cancers with a stem cell hierarchy.

Article.Title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
Article.Authors: Funston G.; Dudgeon T.; Simon D.; Dufault D.; Boyd C.; Fowler D.; Currie P.; Evans D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi —the first for the clade—reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit—which shaped early Cenozoic flora—remains unclear.

Article.Title: Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
Article.Authors: Kamšek A.; Ruiz-Zepeda F.; Tabernik D.; Vidergar J.; Logar A.; Kregar A.; Skočaj D.; Dražić G.; Hodnik N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale.

Article.Title: Quantum-sensing-based super-resolution live cell microenvironment imaging
Article.Authors: Lu Y.; Yang Y.; Xu K.; Mao Z.; Yin L.; Xu Y.; Zhou Z.; Wang X.; Zhang C.; Zhu W.; Feng J.
Article.Abstract: Direct monitoring the multifaceted intracellular microenvironment is fundamental for deciphering localized cellular behavior and function. However, performing nanoscale spatiotemporal sensing of the dynamic physiochemical environment within a live cell has remained challenging, mainly limited by the lack of robust, biocompatible method which satisfies the requirements for spatiotemporal resolution, sensitivity, multi-physical sensing capability and long-term viability. Here we present a super-resolution-based quantum biosensing approach, namely Super-resolution Multi-physical field Imaging with Deconvolution, implemented in our custom-built setup which integrates nitrogen vacancy center-based quantum sensing with structured illumination microscopy. This enables quantitative, super-resolved, and long-term tracking of intracellular physical fields, featuring spatial resolution of 136 nm, temporal resolution of 150 ms, and field of view of 180×180 μm2. We further perform super-resolution multimodal imaging in a live cell, revealing the spatially heterogeneous reactive oxygen species dynamics under external stimulation. Our work enables the dynamic assessment of localized physiochemical dynamics under super-resolution quantum biosensing. This work presents a super-resolution quantum biosensing approach by integrating nitrogen vacancy (NV) center-based quantum nanodiamond sensors with structured illumination microscopy, which achieves super-resolution multi-physical imaging within live cells.

Article.Title: A dual-attribution framework reveals how foreign investment and trade redistribute cobalt availability
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Zhang L.; Jiang S.; Li Y.; Li R.; Mei Z.; Yuan Z.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Global resource allocation is increasingly shaped by foreign direct investment (FDI) and international trade, yet their combined effects on distribution of critical mineral availability across countries remain poorly quantified. Here, we develop a dual-attribution framework covering 193 countries and 36 territories that attributes primary cobalt availability according to corporate ownership and secondary availability according to international trade. We compare these estimates with a combined baseline scenario using geographic-production and pre-trade perspectives to assess how ownership and trade reshape country-level cobalt availability. Relative to this baseline, total cobalt availability is higher in 63.6% of countries, while 72.7% show a positive composite change when primary and secondary availability are equally weighted. Although these mechanisms do not alter the global total amount of cobalt available, they reduce its concentration across countries. Our findings highlight how FDI and trade reshape cobalt distribution and support resource-governance policies that account for both host and exporting countries. This study shows how foreign investment and international trade reshape global cobalt availability. A dual-attribution framework reveals higher attributed availability in most countries while reducing country-level concentration.

Article.Title: PRPF19 drives hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis via PKM2-mediated glycolytic reprogramming
Article.Authors: Zhang G.; Zi S.; Ye B.; Ma Y.; Chen J.; Zhu J.; Liu T.; Yin J.; Shen X.; Yu X.; Dong L.
Article.Abstract: Activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) is a pivotal event driving fibrogenic remodeling of the injured liver. However, the upstream regulators that integrate post-translational signaling with metabolic reprogramming during HSC activation remain poorly defined. Here, we identify pre-mRNA processing factor 19 (PRPF19) as a ubiquitination-linked metabolic regulator that promotes HSC activation. PRPF19 expression was elevated in human and murine fibrotic livers, enriched in activated HSCs, and positively correlated with fibrosis severity. Conditional deletion of Prpf19 in HSCs (Prpf19flox/flox;Lrat-CreERT2), but not in hepatocytes (Prpf19flox/flox;Alb-CreERT2), attenuated HSC activation and liver fibrosis in vivo. Integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses indicated that PRPF19 sustains glycolytic flux and transcriptional programs associated with HSC activation. Mechanistically, PRPF19 promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2), facilitating its nuclear translocation and hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α)-dependent transcription of glycolytic and fibrogenic genes. These findings support a role for the PRPF19-PKM2 pathway in metabolic regulation during HSC activation and liver fibrosis. Zhang et al. show that PRPF19 promotes hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis by driving PKM2-dependent glycolytic reprogramming, identifying a potential metabolic target in chronic liver disease.

Article.Title: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis is concomitant with reduced metacognitive efficiency and sensitivity across multiple cohorts and modalities
Article.Authors: Barnby J.; Dean R.; Burgess H.; Dayan P.; Richards L.
Article.Abstract: The corpus callosum is the largest commissure in the mammalian brain and has been implicated in supporting cognitive processes required for adapting to complex environments. Individuals born with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis, characterized by malformations of the corpus callosum, commonly exhibit deficits in social navigation, abstract problem-solving, decision-making, and self-awareness. Metacognition is a key cognitive process that supports these functions; however, it has yet to be tested comprehensively in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis. Over three experiments, and three Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis cohorts, we examine perceptual accuracy, confidence judgments, and metacognitive efficiency in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis using two variants of a Random Dot Kinematogram task within lab, online, and virtual reality conditions. We find that individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis typically display normal perceptual accuracy but fail to adjust their confidence judgments in line with task difficulty. Computational modeling reveal that this difference is characterized by lower metacognitive efficiency concomitant with lower metacognitive sensitivity. Together, these results provide evidence that the corpus callosum is consistently associated with reduced metacognitive efficiency. Corpus collosum dysgenesis is an umbrella term for all congenital malformations of the corpus callosum. Here, the authors show that corpus callosum dysgenesis is associated with intact visual perception but impaired metacognition.

Article.Title: A self-limiting mechanotransduction feedback loop ensures robust organ formation
Article.Authors: Mori Y.; Robin P.; Briggs A.; Levic D.; Wang J.; Jain-Sharma V.; Heikes K.; Bagnat M.; Hannezo E.; Munjal A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Organ morphogenesis uses mechanotransduction feedback loops to convert forces into gene expression changes that regulate cell mechanics. How these loops integrate with developmental programs to ensure robust outcomes remains unclear. We show Yap mechanotransduction establishes a self-limiting positive feedback loop for semicircular canal formation in zebrafish. Canal development proceeds through bud initiation, extension, and fusion within the otic epithelium. Local swelling of hyaluronan-rich extracellular matrix (ECM) in the bud activates Yap in a spatial pattern. Yap induces its target ccn1l1 , promoting further ECM expansion to sustain bud extension. This feedback loop confers developmental robustness: graded knockdown of ccn1l1 reduces extension rate, yet canal formation persists and fails only with strong disruption. Critically, the loop contains its own termination mechanism. During bud fusion, PKA-CREB signaling, activated by an adhesion GPCR, gpr126, suppresses ccn1l1 , ending the loop. These findings reveal how mechanotransduction loops with built-in termination provide developmental control by integrating mechanical forces, transcriptional responses, and morphogenetic outcomes.

Article.Authors: Zheng T.; Keidel I.; Omer H.; Joshipura A.; Cenier A.; Atay E.; Tan Y.; Wetzel D.; Gacesa R.; Zhao S.; Mengoni C.; Jin S.; Co K.; Peters C.; Segata N.; Ley R.; Yabal M.; Weersma R.; Haller D.; Schirmer M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Desulfovibrio spp. are associated with inflammatory diseases and human health, yet limited representative genomes and isolates hinder our understanding of their role in disease. Here, we assembled a comprehensive database of 2658 Desulfovibrio genomes across 90 diseases and 32 countries, including 24 human isolates. Genomic analyses showed extensive species diversity and revealed disease-associated functional traits, including flagellin and adaptation-associated genes (i.e., ureases). Flagellin-mediated Toll-like receptor 5 activation was species-specific and D. desulfuricans flagellin downregulated TGF-beta signalling in murine small intestinal organoids, suggesting impaired immune tolerance. Additionally, we investigated genomic capacity for hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) production, a main Desulfovibrio metabolite. While health- and disease-associated Desulfovibrio spp. mainly encoded dissimilatory sulfate reduction, tetrathionate metabolism-encoding bacteria were exclusively detected in inflammatory bowel diseases, including Proteus mirabilis and Morganella morganii . Overall, our study provides a comprehensive genomic Desulfovibrio resource and identifies new links associating strain variation, functional traits and H 2 S-production with inflammatory diseases.

Article.Title: Disability related disparities in diagnosis and survival of digestive system cancers in Northern Italy
Article.Authors: Pennisi F.; Buzzoni C.; Gervasi F.; Greco M.; Signorelli C.; Russo A.; Renzi C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Individuals with disabilities may experience disparities in cancer diagnosis, but population-based evidence remains limited. We conduct a population-based cohort study using linked cancer registry and administrative healthcare data for digestive system cancers diagnosed between 2018 and 2021 in Northern Italy, examining diagnostic routes and one-year survival according to pre-existing impairments. Individuals with impairments are more likely to be diagnosed following emergency presentation compared with those without impairments (51.8% compared with 37.9%; adjusted odds ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval 1.23–1.61), particularly those with impairments of mental and neuromusculoskeletal functions. They also have higher one-year mortality (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.26–1.46), independent of socio-demographic and clinical factors. Here, we show that disability-related disparities in emergency cancer diagnosis and survival persist across multiple impairment categories, providing population-based evidence from a European setting on differences in diagnostic pathways across heterogeneous disability groups.

Article.Title: Transposable element-mediated structural variations shape gene expression and agronomic trait diversity in Brassica napus
Article.Authors: Tan Z.; Zheng Y.; Guan Z.; Zhong R.; Zhang M.; Wang X.; Yang J.; Zong Z.; Song Y.; Yang Q.; Guo L.; Song J.; Liu K.; Zhao H.
Article.Abstract: Brassica napus is a globally important allotetraploid oilseed crop with a complex genome and extensive structural diversity that remains incompletely characterized. Here, we present gap-free reference genome assemblies for Zhongshuang 11 (ZS11) and Westar, and assemble six additional accessions. We harmonize gene annotations across 22 genomes and develop BnaScope (https://rgmi.hzau.edu.cn/bnascope), a gene-centric functional genomics platform. Gene-based and graph-based pan-genomes identify 123,107 non-redundant gene clusters and 188,218 structural variants, including 112,417 transposable element-mediated structural variants (TEMSVs). TEMSVs show asymmetric distributions between An and Cn subgenomes and are associated with increased homoeolog expression imbalance, particularly for CDS-TEMSVs. SV-based genome-wide association analyses identify candidate genes underlying seed quality traits, and functional analyses demonstrate that BnaPYRDs negatively regulate seed glucosinolate content. These findings establish structural variation as an important contributor to homoeolog regulation and seed-quality variation in B. napus. This study develops a comprehensive pan-genome resource for Brassica napus and reveals how structural variations shape gene regulation and seed quality traits. The findings provide insights into genome diversity and crop improvement.

Article.Title: Long-term nitrous acid evolution modulates ozone and secondary aerosol variations in global megacities
Article.Authors: Li X.; Ye C.; Dong H.; Xu X.; Wang H.; Chen X.; Tan Z.; Ma X.; Chen S.; Lu K.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is a crucial urban source of HOx radicals, promoting surface ozone (O3) and secondary fine particle (PM2.5) formation, yet its long-term evolution and air-quality impacts remain poorly constrained. Here, using a deep neural network established on worldwide field campaigns, we reconstruct global surface HONO distributions. Typical megacities exhibited contrasting trends in 2005–2021, marked by a sharp decline in Beijing (−47.4% in 2013–2021), an increase in Delhi (+10.0% in 2005–2018), and slight decreases in London, New York and Los Angeles. These HONO changes are identified as major driver of O3 and particulate nitrate variations, outweighing contributions of conventional NOx and volatile organic compounds abatement in Beijing and Delhi, while showing comparable impacts in the remaining cities. A fused data-driven framework further uncovers regime-dependent HONO reduction strategies, prioritizing NOx control in summer and co-reduction of NOx, PM2.5 and direct combustion emissions in winter, to accelerate O3 and PM2.5 joint mitigation. Deep learning reveals a sharp decline of HONO in China, modest drops in EU and US but an increase in India. HONO changes drive O3 and PM2.5 variations, outweighing traditional NOx and VOC control, calling for HONO-targeted air quality management.

Article.Title: Giant step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Liu D.; Zhang X.; Chen X.; Pei F.; Zhang Y.; Yan P.; Ai Y.; Chen G.; Wu Y.; Qiu Z.; Zhu Z.; Yang M.; Li Q.
Article.Abstract: Control of magnetization reversal is crucial for spintronic memory and logic devices. Previous studies on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnets have largely treated magnetic regions in isolation, leaving the roles of step boundaries comparatively unexplored. Here, we investigate step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped Fe3GaTe2 using Kerr microscopy, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy, and micromagnetic simulations. Our results indicate that step boundaries can serve as preferential sites for premature nucleation, giving rise to two distinct regimes. In Type I, reversal initiated in a thicker region propagates rapidly across the step boundary, reducing the coercivity of an adjacent thinner region by up to 59.3%. In Type II, stripe domains originating from the thicker region progressively enter the thinner region, shifting its critical switching field polarity and transforming its hysteresis loop from square to slanted, accompanied by a transition in the dominant reversal mode from rapid domain-wall motion to stripe domain growth. Similar behavior in Fe3GeTe2 suggests that step-boundary-mediated modulation may occur more broadly in layered van der Waals ferromagnets. Our findings highlight step engineering as a potential non-invasive strategy for designing efficient and thermally stable vdW spintronic devices. Boundaries can serve as nucleation points for magnetic domains, influencing the switching behavior. Here, Chen, Liu, Zhang, Chen and co-authors study magnetization reversal from stepped boundaries in van der Waals magnets, finding two distinct regimes of switching.

Article.Title: Fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography using explicit neural fields
Article.Authors: He R.; Li Y.; Chen J.; Dinh T.; Stevens C.; Gilchrist A.; Xue Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multimodal fluorescence and phase imaging provides complementary information about biological samples. However, existing simultaneous fluorescence-phase techniques primarily operate in transmission mode and are limited to thin specimens, restricting their use in thick tissues and in vivo applications. Although multiphoton microscopy enables deep-tissue fluorescence imaging, combining it with three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) imaging remains challenging because few methods can reconstruct the RI of bulky, label-free tissues in reflection mode at subcellular resolution. Here, we introduce fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography (FDT), which reconstructs the 3D RI of label-free and fluorescence-labeled objects from diffracted fluorescence images acquired in reflection mode under two-photon excitation. FDT uses the transport of intensity equation and a self-supervised neural network based on explicit neural fields. Compared with state-of-the-art implicit neural fields, this approach improves computational speed, reconstruction accuracy, and interpretability. We demonstrate FDT in two experimental regimes: reconstructing the 3D RI of label-free tissues up to 300 μ m thick placed on a fluorescent substrate, and reconstructing the 3D RI of fluorescence-labeled, 3D-cultured cells without transmission-side access using fluorescence emitted by the cells themselves. FDT establishes a foundation for accessible reflection-mode multimodal fluorescence-phase imaging in complex biological systems.

Article.Title: Structural basis of ammonium transport and coordinated regulation of AMT1;1 in Arabidopsis thaliana
Article.Authors: He B.; Bai T.; Wang L.; Zhang S.; Ying W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient ammonium uptake is essential for plant growth and nitrogen-use efficiency, yet the structural basis of ammonium transport and regulation in plant AMTs remains unclear. Here, we determined multiple cryo-electron microscopy structures of the Arabidopsis thaliana ammonium transporter AMT1;1 in apo, ammonium-bound, methylammonium-bound, low-pH and phosphomimetic states. These structures reveal a conserved ammonium conduction pathway comprising an aromatic recruitment vestibule, a Phe-gate/Twin-His-containing pore, and a polar intracellular exit region. We further identified a conserved extracellular N-terminal disulfide bond required for oligomer stability and transport activity, suggesting potential redox-dependent regulation. On the cytoplasmic side, phosphorylation modulates C-terminal interactions with intracellular loops, revealing an allosteric regulatory mechanism. Comparison with the bacterial ammonium-sensing protein Sd -Amt1 uncovers a conserved ammonium-recognition region in At AMT1;1 that contributes to transport activity but lacks the signaling module and ligand-dependent conformational switching observed in Sd -Amt1. Together, these findings provide structural insight into ammonium transport and coordinated regulation in plant AMT transporters.

Article.Title: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus
Article.Authors: Nam A.; Shin J.; Tenney M.; Zhang B.; Hong Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sensory inputs reach cortical and subcortical areas in parallel, but how they coordinate to guide decisions remains unknown. While inactivating S1 contralateral to the stimulus increased detection threshold, inactivating ipsilateral S1 decreased it. These opposing effects reflected shifts in choice bias rather than sensitivity. Unilateral SC inactivation produced similar directional effects, whereas bilateral inactivation of either S1 or SC neutralized bias. Furthermore, SC lesions impaired detection performance, and combined S1 inactivation caused no further impairment, indicating that S1-mediated shifts in bias were SC-dependent. S1 inactivation also decreased sensory-evoked neural activity in SC, and choice decoding revealed that behavioral impairment was more closely associated with changes in SC population activity than with loss of sensory encoding in S1. Thus, S1 shapes perceptual bias by modulating SC-dependent circuits that transform sensory evidence into perceptual decisions.

Article.Title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
Article.Authors: Hsieh Y.; Konovalov A.; Su Z.; Vogel T.; Manohar S.; Apps M.; Husain M.; Ruff C.; Lockwood P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

Article.Title: CREST functions as a molecular bridge between neuron-specific enhancers and epigenetic regulators in mature motor neurons
Article.Authors: Montanera K.; Lee A.; Yun W.; Ialongo Del Prete A.; Yeh S.; Jung I.; Rhee H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Motor neuron development requires precise transcriptional regulation mediated in part by BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factor) chromatin remodeling complexes. The neuron-specific BAF subunit CREST is critical for neuronal function and is mutated in some cases of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet its underlying genomic mechanisms remain unclear. Mechanistically, CREST interacts with the neuronal transcription factors ONECUT1 and NGN2, and the BRM ATPase to target pre-existing accessible enhancers of neuronal genes. CREST deletion selectively prevents CBP histone acetyltransferase recruitment, reducing histone H3K27 acetylation at these enhancers and downregulating target gene expression, without disrupting BRM binding, enhancer accessibility, or long-range chromatin architecture. Overall, our findings identify CREST as a crucial epigenetic mediator bridging lineage-specific transcription factors, BAF complexes, and CBP to activate enhancers and promote proper motor neuron development.

Article.Title: P450-catalyzed enantiodivergent kinetic oxidation to access chiral haloalcohols
Article.Authors: Ma T.; Cui H.; Zhang X.; Liu D.; Yang Y.; Ran X.; Wan H.; Tang Z.; Yang J.; Lv Y.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Chiral recognition constitutes the central element of asymmetric catalysis. The control over stereoselectivity becomes more precise with the greater diversity of substituent groups introduced. Distinguishing between high similarity substituents has been a challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Herein, we report an enzymatic approach enabling kinetically enantioselective hydroxylation of (2-chloropropyl)benzene derivatives with excellent stereoselectivity, though the difference of substituent radius between methyl and chloro substituents is 0.07 Å. The cytochrome P450 enzyme P450PL2 is engineered through multiple mutagenesis strategies to enhance both its substrate selectivity and stereoselectivity, thereby enabling the enantiodivergent synthesis of haloalcohols with two stereocenters. Molecular dynamic simulations and DFT calculations infer that the engineered P450PL2 exhibits steric discrimination capability, which enables host-guest interaction with a chiral center bearing methyl and chloro substituents. The biocatalytic system provides efficient access to the 2-chloro-benzyl alcohol derivatives with up to 99:1 enantiomeric ratio and >99:1 diastereomeric ratio. Differentiation between highly similar substituents is a challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Here, the authors report an enzymatic approach enabling kinetically enantioselective hydroxylation of (2- chloropropyl)benzene derivatives using engineered P450PL2 to obtain the 2-chloro-benzyl alcohol derivatives with up to 99:1 enantiomeric ratio and >99:1 diastereomeric ratio.

Article.Authors: Dai A.; Zheng Z.; Wu R.; Ma D.; Xu J.; Mo Y.; Duan L.; Tan W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Strigolactone (SL) signaling is an important agricultural target for controlling plant branching and parasitic weeds. We demonstrate CMCS-DK6 strongly inhibits germination of parasitic weeds, especially Striga asiatica (IC 50 = 1.80 μM), while promoting rice tillering, reducing height, and increasing dry weight. Molecular simulations, along with microscale thermophoresis results, suggest that DK6 binds stably to SL receptors. This work offers a hydrogel delivery strategy and some potential mechanistic implications for improving crop architecture and weed control.

Article.Title: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics reveals fibroblast and neuroimmune microenvironments in endometriosis lesions
Article.Authors: Haney C.; Alizadeh E.; Lee J.; Sullivan M.; Kuljancic J.; Flynn W.; Robson P.; White B.; Luciano D.; Courtois E.
Article.Abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic, systemic, inflammatory disease characterized by the presence of endometrium-like tissue growing outside of the uterus. Affecting one in ten individuals assigned female at birth, it causes chronic pain and inflammation that significantly impairs quality of life. Yet the mechanisms that drive pain and disease progression remain poorly defined. This study establishes the precise spatial transcriptomic cartography of human ovarian and peritoneal lesions, two of the most commonly found lesions. We identify shared spatial features across lesion types, including immune cell infiltration, fibroblast compartments surrounding epithelial glands, and distinct distributions of neuronal and macrophage subsets. We precisely defined sensory neuronal subtypes and mapped their spatial location relative to immune cells. We further validate the epithelial-neuronal interactome, using an in vitro 3D model of peripheral sensory brain organoids co-cultured with human endometriosis epithelial and fibroblast cells. By mapping spatial cellular interactions and conserved features across lesion types linked to pain, our study advances understanding of endometriosis pathophysiology and informs targeted therapeutic development. Article.Abstract: Mycobacterial-derived lipid-linked galactan (LLG) is an essential component of the Mycobacterial tuberculosis (Mtb) cell wall core arabinogalactan (AG), a well-established virulence factor and target of anti-tubercular drugs. Here we present cryo-EM structures of WzmWztMtb to uncover critical steps of Mtb LLG translocation. Notably, densities suggestive of the mycobacterial-derived LLG substrates were observed in the structure of WzmWztMtb, indicating that the substrate may bind through two Wzm and two Wzt subunits. This proposed LLG binding is fulfilled by a fully upward extension of the Wzt gate helix, which serves as a critical step to prime Wzt for dimerization. The ATP-bound structure revealed a remarkable downward movement of the gate helix, together with the Wzt dimerization. The third, DDM/ATP-bound structure captured WztWzmMtb in an intermediate state with two DDM molecules in the Wzm central cavity. Using two conditional mycobacterial mutants for functional analyses, we have identified residues on the Wzm N-terminal interface helix (IFN) and on the Wzt helical domain are essential for LLG recognition and translocation in vivo. Article.Title: Bias-reconfigurable barrier photodetectors for integrated broadband sensing and neuromorphic vision
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Yang F.; Zhao W.; Lang S.; Chen Z.; Wang Y.; Yang Y.; Zhang X.; Wan D.; Song J.; Liu Y.; Li Y.; Yu Y.; Ju X.; Wu J.; Ni Z.; Lu J.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Intelligent vision systems demand photodetectors with reconfigurable response to support diverse modalities like high-speed sensing and neuromorphic processing. Here we show a bias-reconfigurable barrier photodetector that enables continuous modulation of response time across 7 orders of magnitude, from 614 ns to 8.28 s. This wide-range tunability is achieved by electrically modulating the interfacial barrier height, which switches the dominant carrier transport mechanism from direct tunneling to barrier-limited thermal excitation and trap-assisted processes. Under low bias, the device functions as a high-speed photodetector, whereas elevated biases extend the response to synaptic timescales, enabling in-sensor neuromorphic computing as a physical reservoir. Notably, the device exhibits a broadband photoresponse from visible to mid-infrared. High accuracy was achieved in complex recognition tasks, such as classifying vehicle acceleration or deceleration. This integration of fast photodetection and neuromorphic computation establishes hardware-efficient paradigms for integrated machine vision, adaptive multispectral sensing, and energy-efficient edge intelligence. Intelligent vision systems require diverse functionalities, ranging from high-speed sensing to neuromorphic processing. Article.Authors: Ru K.; Zhao L.; Li X.; Liu Y.; Yan Q.; Yang H.; Zhang Y.; Li Z.; Xing J.; Liu S.; Tian Y.; Deng X.; Luo Q.; Zhu C.; Sun J.; Peng Y.; Wang Y.; Yang T.; Xu X.; Chen Z.; Qian A.

The equilibrium has been studied by variable-temperature nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in benzene-d6 solution, affording a modest driving force for dimerization (ΔHΘ = 16.26( ± 0.83) kcal mol−1 and ΔSΘ = 3.98( ± 0.26) × 10−2 kcal mol−1 K−1) through van’t Hoff analysis. Both the dimer and the weakly coordinated monomer function as phosphagermylenylidene synthons, enabling C ≡ C and Si–H bond activation. These findings demonstrate that weak coordination combined with steric control provides a general strategy for accessing reactive heavier isonitrile analogues while preserving their intrinsic reactivity. Article.Abstract: During replication-coupled DNA interstrand cross-link (ICL) repair, fork reversal is thought to enable the Fanconi anemia (FA) pathway to resolve the ICL through nucleolytic incisions. Taken together, this work identifies reversed forks as substrates for ATM activation and reveals a phospho-regulatory circuit that controls reversed fork processing. Replication stress often induces fork reversal, which protects stalled replication intermediates until replication can resume. Article.Authors: Lin J.; Mu A.; Tang W.; Li F.; Zhu Y.; Li M.; Yeerella R.; Potts C.; Cai S.; Mu L.; Muldoon J.; Chen Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Today’s lithium‑ion battery manufacturing heavily relies on polyvinylidene fluoride binder and N‑methyl‑2‑pyrrolidone solvent-based processing, which incurs high cost and hinders environmental sustainability. The network integrates hydrogen, covalent, and ionic bonding among binder chains, active particles, and current collectors, providing strong adhesion as well as good oxidative stability and thermal stability. Importantly, the fluorine‑free binder further facilitates sustainable direct recycling, demonstrating full recovery of spent positive and negative electrodes to achieve the same level of performance with pristine materials without generating fluorinated residue. Life-cycle analysis shows significant reductions in energy cost and emissions compared with recycling polyvinylidene fluoride-based batteries. This binder strategy endows high performance with circularity, offering a scalable route to sustainable battery manufacturing technologies.

Article.Authors: Gairin E.; Miura S.; Chamot Z.; Sautereau C.; Zwahlen J.; Takamiyagi H.; Gibert Y.; Herrera M.; Laudet V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban zones are rapidly expanding worldwide, exposing organisms to complex and multidimensional stressors. Article.Authors: Rogers T.; Stock J.; Schulz N.; Yalçin G.; Rencken S.; Weissenbacher A.; Clarence T.; Schultz D.; Ragsdale C.; Albertin C.; Simakov O.

We propose that differential evolutionary constraints across the coleoid 3D genome allow macroevolutionary processes to shape genome topology in distinct ways, facilitating the emergence of novel regulatory entanglements and ultimately contributing to the evolution and maintenance of complex traits in the coleoids.

Article.Authors: Doratt B.; Wagner S.; Keen K.; Avila U.; Varlamov O.; Messaoudi I.

Investigations into fetal immune ontogeny across compartments are constrained by tissue inaccessibility during pregnancy. Article.Title: Fast-charging and durable all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries enabled by pre-embedded solid-solid redox mediator
Article.Authors: Song H.; Zhang R.; Zheng C.; Münch K.; Shen K.; Liu F.; Hong X.; Wang H.; Meng J.; Yan Y.; Shi W.; He M.; Ma Y.; Li Y.; Xiao Z.; Shafqat M.; Gao X.; Wu J.; Luo M.; Song T.; Ma C.; Zheng L.; Gao P.; Safari M.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: All-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries promise high specific energy and low cost. However, they are challenged by poor rate capability and cycling stability owing to the slow solid-solid sulfur redox reactions. Here, we present fast-charging and durable all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries enabled by a pre-embedded solid-solid redox mediator using an amorphous sulfur/iodine nano-eutectic positive electrode. The iodine, intimately homogenized with sulfur owing to carbon mesopore encapsulation, undergoes rapid I2/I− redox reaction, mediating solid-solid sulfur reactions by promoting electron transfer across the boundaries. The iodine within the carbon and on its surface reacts in situ with the sulfide catholyte to form a globally distributed I2/I− nano-network throughout the positive electrode, thereby enabling fast charging. The cell exhibits a specific capacity of 851.9 mA h g−1S/I when charged at 10 C, and 474.7 mA h g−1S/I at a charging rate of 24 C (1 C is defined as 945 mA g−1S/I). The high reversibility of the redox-mediated reaction enables durable cycling for 9,000 cycles over 9 months at 2 C and 2,800 cycles over 17 months at 0.5 C. This strategy represents a perspective for developing solid-state conversion electrodes that are plagued by sluggish reactions. All-solid-state lithium sulfur batteries suffer from sluggish solid-solid sulfur redox reactions. Here, the authors report fast charging and durable all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries enabled by a pre-embedded solid-solid redox mediator in an amorphous sulfur/iodine nano-eutectic positive electrode.

Article.Title: Environmentally Relevant Concentrations of Nanomaterials Drive Photochemical Production of Reactive Species and Pollutant Degradation in Surface Waters
Article.Authors: Quinn J.; McClure A.; Herckes P.; Westerhoff P.
Article.Abstract: Reactive intermediates in surface waters are widely attributed to dissolved organic matter (DOM). Natural, incidental, or engineered nanomaterials simultaneously occur at parts per billion and can function as photocatalysts, yet the photochemical role of nanomaterials at environmentally relevant concentrations remains overlooked in surface water photochemistry. Here, we quantify reactive intermediates from TiO2 nanomaterials (1–100 μg L−1) and DOM (1–5 mgC L−1) under 222, 265, and 365 nm. Despite lower concentrations relative to DOM, TiO2 produces hydroxyl radical (HO•) rates 10× to 100× higher per unit mass, resulting in comparable HO• formation. DOM plus nanomaterial mixtures shows synergistic behavior, with HO• formation 16-21% above additive predictions. DOM has limited impact in the degradation of 6PPD-quinone whereas nanomaterials enhanced its degradation due to elevated [HO•]ss. These results demonstrate nanomaterials can contribute to or exceed DOM in HO• driven micropollutant degradation in surface waters or engineered ultraviolet-light water treatment systems. Environmentally relevant nanomaterial concentrations can rival dissolved organic matter in driving pollutant transformation under sunlight or UV-based water treatment.

Article.Title: Consecutive waves of NODAL inhibition are required for epiblast patterning
Article.Authors: Wang M.; Hou T.; Villagrana J.; Kijima Y.; Dias N.; Altus R.; Brueckner M.; Aktaş T.; Sumigray K.; Kretzmer H.; Smith Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The mouse genome encodes two Lefty genes that antagonize NODAL signaling to break symmetry during gastrulation. Despite their central regulatory role, accurately describing and comparing their embryonic function remains unclear. Here, we generated high replicate powered single-cell transcriptional atlases of Lefty1 and Lefty2 mutant embryogenesis to evaluate the effects of perturbed NODAL signaling during gastrulation. We find that both mutants exhibit phenotypes beginning with the earliest primitive streak derivatives, suggesting a sequential shift from anterior Lefty1 to posterior Lefty2-based control that prevents spurious differentiation into extraembryonic and axial mesoendoderm at the cost of embryonic mesoderm and, in the case of Lefty1, rostral forebrain specification. By phasing bulk SMAD2/3 ChIP-seq data into single-cell-resolved descriptions of signal transduction, we identify distinct NODAL-responsive modules that track the context-specific use of this morphogen over gastrulation time. Collectively, our work highlights the potential of single-cell assays to decode how complex differentiation processes resolve morphogen signals in space and time.

Article.Title: Pipeline infrastructure for hydrogen transport in the United States
Article.Authors: Singh A.; Zhai H.; Holubnyak E.; Biggs C.
Article.Abstract: Pipeline infrastructure is crucial for regional hydrogen transport. However, existing pipeline models have remarkably underestimated the construction-related material and labor costs compared to U.S. historical data. To cope with this problem and establish sustainable infrastructure, we develop integrated performance, economic and life cycle emissions models to comparatively evaluate dedicated pipelines and repurposed natural gas pipelines for hydrogen transport across the country. We find that the levelized cost of hydrogen transport via dedicated pipelines varies with numerous factors, such as location, capacity, and distance; there are similar variabilities in the cost of hydrogen transport via repurposed natural gas pipelines; and although leveraging existing natural gas pipelines can substantially reduce upfront capital expenditures, it may involve tradeoffs in cost and life cycle emissions. Here, we show that the integrated pipeline models and multi-criteria analysis can better guide engineering design, planning, and investment decisions on building nationwide hydrogen transport networks. This study compares new and repurposed gas pipelines for nationwide hydrogen transport, showing how costs and life-cycle emissions vary across options and highlighting trade-offs for infrastructure planning and investment.

Article.Title: Periodontal pathogen Tannerella forsythia promotes liver fibrosis via ICAM-1⁺ neutrophil–dependent hepatic stellate cell activation
Article.Authors: Tang D.; Wei J.; Liu M.; Cui L.; Chen J.; Li H.; Lin M.; Li X.; Ou Q.; Li Q.
Article.Abstract: Periodontitis is a key driver in the development and progression of liver fibrosis. Nevertheless, how specific periodontal pathogens contribute to liver fibrosis remains elusive. Here, we identify Tannerella forsythia as the crucial mediator in the link between periodontitis and liver fibrosis, which can translocate to the gut and aggravate liver fibrosis. Mechanistically, Tannerella forsythia promotes the infiltration of ICAM-1+ neutrophils and inflammatory response in the liver via disrupting intestinal barrier integrity. ICAM-1+ neutrophils secrete TNF-α, which activates the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway in hepatic stellate cells, triggering collagen deposition and fibrogenesis. Conditional knockout of ICAM-1 in neutrophils or global deletion of TNF-α significantly attenuates inflammatory response and liver fibrosis caused by Tannerella forsythia. Taken together, this study identifies an oral-gut-liver axis driven by Tannerella forsythia and provides a prospective therapeutic target for periodontitis-related liver fibrosis. Peridontitis has been linked in the development and progression of liver fibrosis. Here the authors suggest that Tannerella forsythia is linked to the promotion of liver fibrosis by ICAM-1+ neutrophils activating hepatic stellate cells.

Article.Title: A cross-layer 2D photodetection framework for standardized readout and signal fusion
Article.Authors: Sun X.; Liu X.; Liu J.; Wang Y.; Lu X.; Wang P.; Zhao M.; Xu Y.; Wu H.; Peng D.; Wang L.; Tan C.; Hu G.; Cui H.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Beyond improving device responsivity, a central challenge in photodetectors based on two-dimensional (2D) materials is to resolve the information-interface mismatch and delayed system translation caused by trap-governed persistent photoconductivity (PPC). Here we present a cross-layer engineering route oriented towards practical implementation that integrates defect-mechanism analysis, non-stationary signal definition, dynamic distortion compensation and readout-interface engineering, thereby establishing a conversion pathway from physical response to system output in 2D MoS2, WSe2 and PtSe2 photodetectors. In this context, drift, hysteresis and fatigue accumulation in time-varying photoresponses are no longer treated merely as non-ideal perturbations, but are reformulated as state-dependent information that can be defined, compensated and interfaced. Through interface restructuring and stable readout, nW-level state-dependent photocurrents are systematically mapped onto a mixed-signal readout interface. We further extend this strategy to array-level unified output and multisensor fusion, with its frequency-guided representation evaluated in a machine-vision task. Our results show that the history-dependent nonlinear response governed by PPC is not simply a local device non-ideality, but a state-encoded signal linking defect dynamics, readout pathways and system-level tasks. This work provides an engineering route for translating 2D photodetectors from device-level studies to system-level applications. Persistent photoconductivity usually complicates the readout of 2D photodetectors, limiting the stability and speed of the signal representation and processing. Here, the authors introduce a cross-layer signal engineering approach to analyse and stabilize the dynamic outputs of 2D MoS2, WSe2 and PtSe2 photodetectors, showing its extension to multi-sensor image recognition tasks.

Article.Title: Antisense oligonucleotides targeting transcription termination windows disrupt mRNA 3’ end processing and decrease gene expression
Article.Authors: Winczura K.; Joenson L.; Koller E.; Grzechnik P.; Jan Kiełpiński Ł.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) are short, synthetic nucleic acids that bind to complementary RNA sequences and alter gene expression, making them versatile therapeutic agents. Here, we identify transcription termination windows of protein-coding genes as previously unrecognized targets for ASOs. We show that ASOs can act on nascent RNA synthesised downstream of the annotated genes, leading to a pronounced decrease in the corresponding mRNA levels. These downstream-of-gene ASOs (DG-ASOs) induce RNase H1-dependent cleavage, impairing mRNA 3’ end processing, directing the unprocessed mRNAs for exosome-dependent degradation and creating early entry points in the nascent RNA for the XRN2 exonuclease termination factor. Altogether, we show that termination windows are genuine ASO targets which can be exploited to suppress gene expression. Importantly, we also reveal an underappreciated source of off-target effects which may arise from ASOs binding downstream of genes. Our findings indicate the necessity to expand ASO design and off-target assessment guidelines to include termination window sequences, thereby improving therapeutic efficacy and safety.

Article.Title: Non-sewered sanitation systems reshape microplastics into chemically complex and reactive contaminants
Article.Authors: Liu N.; Li Z.; Cheng S.; Zhang P.; He C.; Ye Z.; Ma T.; Wang S.; Liu J.; Campos L.; Guo Z.; Lynch I.
Article.Abstract: Non-sewered sanitation systems (NSSSs) are gaining global attention as decentralized solutions, yet the transformation of microplastics (MPs) within these systems remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate MP characteristics in the influent and effluent of two NSSSs using laser direct infrared spectroscopy, Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Both systems substantially reduce MP abundance (retention: 53.7–77.1%) but also alter MP characteristics. MPs exhibit fragmentation, reduced particle size, increased morphological irregularity, and surface oxidation, evidenced by decreased spectral matching scores and emerging oxygen-containing functional groups. FT-ICR MS reveals molecular-level oxidation enrichment, and over 260 candidate plastic additives are identified. LC-MS/MS confirms elevated phthalate ester concentrations, including DBP and DEHP. Statistical analyses link MP fragmentation, oxidation, and additive release as coupled processes. These findings suggest that NSSSs reshape MPs into more chemically reactive forms, highlighting the need to evaluate transformation-associated risks beyond retention efficiency. Microplastics are known to be present within non-sewered sanitation systems, but how treatment processes alter their physicochemical properties is not well understood. Here, the authors use a range of techniques to study the fate and transformation of microplastics with treatment.

Article.Title: High-throughput spatial proteomics from cellular to subcellular scales via a hanging droplet workflow
Article.Authors: Chen H.; Guzman U.; Olsen J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples are central for clinical research and spatial proteomics (SP), yet liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) remains challenging due to protein extraction losses, evaporation during decrosslinking, and inefficient sample preparation. Current methods often involve complex protocols or specialized equipment, limiting scalability, throughput, and proteome depth. We present a streamlined micro-FFPE proteomics protocol for laser-capture microdissection (LMD) that enables high-throughput processing in a 96-well format, completing the workflow from tissue lysis to LC-MS-ready tryptic peptides on Evotips in just 2-hours. By integrating whole-slide imaging, LMD, and narrow-window data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (nDIA-MS), our approach optimizes lysis, decrosslinking, and digestion within nano-wells leveraging the hanging droplet concept. This design minimizes surface adsorption, enhances sample processing efficiency, reduces preparation time by ~30% compared with reference methods, and enables parallel handling of up to 192 samples with standard equipment. This enables the quantification of >5,500 protein groups (PGs) from 50,000 µm² regions (~250 cells), with robust performance down to 1000 µm2 (~5 cells) with ~2,500 PGs identified. Application to breast cancer (BC) tissue resolves BC subtypes and microenvironments via biomarkers (TP53, HER2, PR). Even from ~60 µm² regions of single nuclei identify ~1,800 protein groups, enabling microscale spatial proteomics approaching near-organelle resolution.
