Article.Title: The Impact of the ACTN3 rs1815739 Polymorphism on Physical Performance in Youth Football Players
Article.Authors: Cerit M.; Önlü A.; Ahmetov I.; Hızarcı Ö.; Aslan B.; Dalip M.; Ulucan K.
Article.Abstract: This cross-sectional study examined ACTN3 rs1815739 (C/T; R577X) genotype distribution and its associations with physical performance and biological maturation in male youth football players. A total of 274 players (11–14 years, n = 166; 15–18 years, n = 108) from a professional club in North Macedonia completed Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery, linear sprint, and jump tests, including the drop jump, countermovement jump (CMJ), and squat jump (SJ). Genotype frequencies were compared with the 1000 Genomes European reference population (n = 503). ACTN3 CC (RR) genotype was more frequent in players than in the reference population (48.2% vs. 32.0%; OR = 1.97, 95% CI 1.46–2.67, p < 0.0001), as was the C (R) allele (OR = 1.34, 95% CI 1.08–1.66, p = 0.009). However, the player genotype distribution deviated from Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium (p < 0.001). CMJ height increased by approximately 2.3 cm per one-year increase in maturity offset (p < 0.001). In the younger cohort, TT (XX) carriers had lower Yo-Yo distance and estimated VO2max than CC and CT (RX) carriers (p = 0.007). Exploratory whole-sample models provided limited evidence that the association between maturity offset, and vertical-jump performance (CMJ, SJ) might differ by genotype; however, these interactions were not statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. No significant genotype differences were observed for sprint performance or most other jump-related outcomes. These findings indicate that ACTN3–performance associations in youth football players are modest and outcome-specific and should be interpreted cautiously given the external reference population and deviation from Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium.

Article.Title: Madeng’ai Ethyl Acetate Extract Attenuates Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Inflammation and Acute Lung Injury
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Ji W.; Cao L.; Wang Y.; Wang W.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Madeng’ai, the dried root of Potentilla freyniana Bornm., is used in Dong medicine for infections and wound care. This study examined the chemical composition and prophylactic protective effects of the ethyl acetate fraction of its ethanolic root extract (referred to as MEA) in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced acute lung injury (ALI). Ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled to Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometry detected 77 constituents, comprising 13 compounds authenticated with reference standards and 64 constituents tentatively annotated from accurate mass and tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) fragmentation. Network pharmacology prioritized six candidate compounds, 120 overlapping targets, and nine hub targets, and molecular docking explored theoretical interactions with inflammation-related proteins. MEA was evaluated in LPS-stimulated MH-S alveolar macrophages and in male C57BL/6J mice receiving oral pretreatment for seven days prior to intraperitoneal LPS challenge. In MH-S cells, MEA pretreatment reduced nitrite, interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, 2′,7′-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate (DCFH-DA)-detectable intracellular oxidative fluorescence, and Nlrp3, Pycard, Casp1, and Gsdmd mRNA levels. In mice, seven-day oral pretreatment with MEA attenuated qualitative histological lung injury, pulmonary edema, and serum cytokine elevation, accompanied by lower lung protein levels of NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3), apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD (ASC), pro-caspase-1, and the ~30 kDa N-terminal fragment of gasdermin D (GSDMD-N), together with related transcripts. These findings indicate that prophylactic MEA administration attenuates LPS-induced macrophage inflammation and experimental lung injury, accompanied by reduced intracellular oxidative stress and decreased expression of NLRP3–GSDMD pathway-associated markers.

Article.Title: Food Allergy Induces Anxiety-like Behavior and Neuroimmune Dysregulation in the Prefrontal Cortex of Mice
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Guo C.; Yu X.
Article.Abstract: Food allergy (FA) is associated with anxiety, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. An ovalbumin (OVA)-induced FA model was established in female BALB/c mice to evaluate anxiety-like behavior and characterize molecular alterations in the prefrontal cortex (PFC). We assessed the FA model by anaphylactic scores, OVA-specific IgE and IgG1 levels, serum cytokines, and intestinal histology, and evaluated anxiety-like behavior using the open field test (OFT) and elevated plus maze (EPM). Mice with OVA-induced food allergy exhibited pronounced allergic responses and intestinal mucosal injury, together with reduced center-zone exploration in the OFT and reduced open-arm exploration in the EPM. In the PFC, inflammatory and chemotactic mediators were increased, accompanied by enlarged Iba1-positive microglial soma area. Bulk RNA sequencing identified 183 differentially expressed genes, including upregulated genes involved in immune and inflammatory responses and downregulated genes associated with neuronal activity and plasticity. Western blotting further showed an increased p-Akt (Ser473)/Akt ratio. These findings reveal that OVA-induced food allergy in female BALB/c mice is associated with neuroimmune dysregulation and broader transcriptional alterations in the PFC involving immune and inflammatory responses and processes related to neuronal activity and plasticity, and suggest that altered Akt-related signaling may provide a molecular link between these changes.

Article.Title: Beyond Mutation Diversity: Common Pathogenic Mechanism for Putative Intervention Sites in Monogenic Diseases
Article.Authors: KC B.; Modha N.; Poudel P.; Panday S.; Alexov E.
Article.Abstract: Monogenic disorders present a compelling target for drug discovery due to their clear, single-gene etiology. Yet, effective therapies remain scarce, largely because diverse mutation types scattered across a protein obstruct targeted drug design. In this study, we leverage MOGEDO, a curated database of monogenic disorders, to test whether different pathogenic genotypes within a single protein converge on a common molecular mechanism. By clustering MOGEDO proteins into eight functional families and analyzing representative proteins carrying both benign and pathogenic mutations, we integrated molecular dynamics, network analysis, and side-chain entropy metrics. Our findings reveal that distinct pathogenic mutations disrupt the structural and dynamic properties of the wild-type and benign protein through common pathways. By demonstrating that diverse disease-causing mutations manifest a unified pathogenic phenotype, this work provides a framework for designing broad-spectrum therapeutics that target common putative intervention sites rather than individual mutations.

Article.Title: Genetic Architecture of Body Weight Variation and GWAS-Informed Genomic Selection in Formulated Diet-Adapted Mandarin Fish (Siniperca chuatsi)
Article.Authors: Geng C.; Song H.; Xia Y.; Zhang X.; Li S.; Liu S.; Teng J.; Zhang Y.; Hu H.
Article.Abstract: Large variation in body weight poses a major challenge to the development and industrialization of formulated-feed aquaculture in Siniperca chuatsi. Breeding varieties that combine formulated-diet adaptation, rapid growth, and uniform body weight is therefore important for improving production efficiency. However, the genetic architecture of body weight and optimal genomic selection (GS) strategies remain poorly understood. Here, whole-genome resequencing was performed on 522 formulated-diet-adapted individuals. Genome-wide association study (GWAS) identified 21 significant loci, with candidate genes associated with lipid metabolism, endocrine regulation, and neuroendocrine signaling. Genomic prediction was evaluated using genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and GWAS-prioritized SNP panels with Bayesian and machine-learning models. Prediction accuracy increased with marker number and generally plateaued at approximately 30,000 SNPs. Random forest using GWAS-prioritized markers achieved the highest accuracy, improving prediction accuracy by 4.8% over genome-wide genomic best linear unbiased prediction (GBLUP) while using fewer markers. These findings demonstrate the potential of GWAS-informed marker prioritization to reduce marker requirements and improve GS efficiency for body weight in formulated-diet-adapted S. chuatsi.

Article.Title: BZR1 and BES1: From Brassinosteroid Signaling Termini to Multifunctional Integrators of Plant Growth and Environmental Adaptation
Article.Authors: Guo F.; Ge S.; Lei M.
Article.Abstract: BZR1 (Brassinazole-resistant 1) and BES1 (bri1-EMS suppressor1) are the principal transcription factors that convert brassinosteroid (BR) perception into genome-wide transcriptional programs governing plant growth, development, and stress responses. Once regarded as end-effectors of a linear receptor-to-nucleus relay, they are now recognized as central hubs that integrate diverse endogenous and environmental cues into context-specific transcriptional outputs. We synthesize recent progress across four connected levels. Structurally, a modular architecture enables simultaneous target recognition, signal input, and output control. Mechanistically, the canonical BIN2-mediated phosphorylation switch is expanded by upstream regulators that couple membrane dynamics, carbon status, protein homeostasis, and nuclear import to BZR1/BES1, while ubiquitination, SUMOylation, redox modification, and acetylation form an interconnected post-translational network. During transcriptional execution, dephosphorylated BZR1/BES1 partition targets into activated and repressed sets through cis-element preference, corepressor recruitment, chromatin modifiers, and partnerships with factors such as PIF4 and ARF6. Physiologically, BZR1/BES1 coordinate anutrient-responsive metabolism, yield-related traits, and abiotic-stress tolerance, with marked functional divergence among crop orthologs. We highlight open questions in signal-integration specificity and discuss how BZR1/BES1 modules could be engineered for climate-resilient crops.

Article.Title: Interpretable Machine Learning of Hydrogen Production from Reactive Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Polyethylene Oxidative Gasification
Article.Authors: Truong T.; Trinh T.
Article.Abstract: Reactive molecular dynamics (ReaxFF MD) simulations of polyethylene (PE) oxidative gasification generate large trajectory datasets suited to machine learning (ML). We recast H2 production monitoring as a leakage-free forecasting task: given the simulated thermochemical state at time t, predict the time-weighted cumulative H2 production cumH2(t+h) a fixed horizon h=25 ps ahead. Data from 48 trajectories spanning six O2 loadings (1–900 molecules per 50 PE chains) and eight temperatures (1500–2900 K) yield 72,117 forecast pairs (45 simulations; three truncated trajectories excluded). Eight tabular regression models are benchmarked against persistence and physics-informed baselines under simulation-grouped nested cross-validation, a held-out test partition, temperature- and loading-holdout stress tests, and a paired ablation removing all H2-derived inputs. With the H2 history available, the best test model (random forest) attains R2=0.9999 at RMSE 121.8 molecules·ps, a 93.0% RMSE reduction relative to persistence, robust to unseen O2 loadings and largely robust to unseen temperatures. Without it, no model beats persistence in any evaluation: the best ML model (an artificial neural network) is 26.0% worse, and accuracy decreases substantially under temperature extrapolation. The ablation attributes 93.3–98.3% of the tree and kernel models’ RMSE reduction to the H2-derived features, quantifying how much forecasting skill derives from the target history rather than instantaneous observables.

Article.Title: Src Homology Phosphatase 2 Disruption in Podocytes Attenuates Markers of Aristolochic Acid 1-Induced Renal Injury, Inflammation, and Fibrosis in Mice
Article.Authors: Hsu M.; Haj F.
Article.Abstract: Aristolochic acid nephropathy (AAN) is a tubulointerstitial kidney disease caused by ingestion of aristolochic acids (AA). It is a global health concern, with no established disease-modifying therapy. Src homology phosphatase 2 (Shp2; encoded by Ptpn11) is a ubiquitously expressed protein tyrosine phosphatase that is implicated in renal development and function, but its contribution to AAN is unknown. Mice with podocyte-specific Shp2 disruption (Ptpn11fl/fl;Pod-Cre; KO) and controls (Ptpn11fl/fl) were subjected to weekly intraperitoneal injections of saline or aristolochic acid 1 (AA1, 5 mg/kg) for 4 consecutive weeks. Afterward, animals were sacrificed at 6 and 11 weeks. Renal Shp2 protein and immunofluorescence staining, including in glomeruli, were elevated following AA1 challenge. Relative to controls, KO mice exhibited attenuation of AA1-evoked changes in renal function indices, including kidney-to-body weight ratio, blood urea nitrogen, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. Additionally, AA1-induced elevation in blood pressure was reduced in KO mice. At the molecular level, Shp2 deficiency was associated with significantly lower AA1-induced renal expression of inflammatory (Ccl2, Tnf) and fibrotic (Acta2, Col1a1) markers compared with controls. Histologically, AA1-induced renal interstitial collagen deposition, evaluated by picrosirius red staining, was significantly reduced in KO mice compared with controls. These findings indicate that podocyte Shp2 deficiency confers beneficial effects and attenuates AA1-induced renal injury, inflammation, and fibrosis, and identify Shp2 as a target in AAN.

Article.Title: Volatile Anesthetic-Based Combination Strategies Against Ischemia–Reperfusion Injury: Experimental Evidence, Molecular Mechanisms, and Translational Limitations
Article.Authors: Şengel N.; Arslan M.
Article.Abstract: Ischemia–reperfusion (I/R) injury is a complex pathological process involving adenosine triphosphate (ATP) depletion, calcium overload, excessive reactive oxygen species generation, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory activation, and regulated cell death. Volatile anesthetics, including sevoflurane, desflurane, and isoflurane, may modulate several of these processes through antioxidant and prosurvival signaling, suppression of inflammatory pathways, and regulation of apoptosis. Because I/R injury involves interconnected mechanisms, combining interventions that act on different targets may offer additional protection. Experimental studies have investigated volatile anesthetics together with fullerenol C60, ischemic conditioning, and selected pharmacological interventions. Other combination strategies involving ozone conditioning and boric acid have also been evaluated in experimental models, although these have not established the effects of combining either intervention with a volatile anesthetic. This narrative review examines the molecular mechanisms and organ-specific evidence underlying these approaches, with particular attention to study design, treatment timing, and the interpretation of combined effects. While some combinations have shown greater protection than individual interventions, the findings remain heterogeneous, and formal analyses distinguishing additivity from synergy are generally lacking. Clinical evidence is limited, and further studies are needed to establish whether these experimental findings can be translated into meaningful patient outcomes.

Article.Title: PLOD3 Variably Regulates Diverse Phenotypes in Human Cancer Cells
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Zhang M.; Zhang X.; Chen K.; Wang Y.; Zeng Y.
Article.Abstract: PLOD3 (procollagen-lysine, 2-oxoglutarate 5-dioxygenase 3) is an essential enzyme that modifies collagen and contributes to collagen assembly and function. PLOD3 expression has been linked to human cancers and patient prognosis, although how PLOD3 regulates tumorigenesis is poorly understood. In this study we first examined the association between PLOD3 expression and human cancer survival and found that, in contrast to previous reports, PLOD3 expression was not significantly correlated with overall survival in cancers. We then studied how decreasing and increasing PLOD3 levels affected the phenotypes of HeLa, HT-1080, and HCT116 cells, three diverse and representative human cancer cell lines. Altering PLOD3 expression elicited a variable effect on the cell cycle and cell migration in the three cell lines. However, increased PLOD3 induced apoptosis, elevated the mitochondrial membrane potential, and reduced the reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in all three cell lines, whereas decreasing PLOD3 had the opposite effects. Subsequent global mRNA expression analyses revealed changes in biological processes and pathways that were consistent with these phenotypic changes and suggested that apoptosis and mitochondrial metabolism might be two important mechanisms by which PLOD3 regulates cell behaviors.

Article.Title: Evaluation of Bone Regeneration by Sustained Release of Bone Morphogenetic Protein from Porous Polyetheretherketone
Article.Authors: Shiotani Y.; Jo J.; Takasugi S.; Adachi T.; Yasui K.; Hashimoto Y.; Nishiura A.
Article.Abstract: Owing to its excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility, polyetheretherketone (PEEK) is a promising biomaterial in dental and medical fields. After confirming the sustained release of BMP-2 from Gel-PEEK in vitro, the bone regeneration potential of BMP-2@Gel-PEEK was evaluated using a model of critical-sized calvarial defects in rats. Micro-computed tomography and histological analyses demonstrated augmented bone regeneration by BMP-2@Gel-PEEK compared with PEEK only and Gel-PEEK without incorporating BMP-2. These findings suggest that through the sustained release of BMP-2, the porous PEEK with gelatin hydrogel is a promising platform for bone regeneration.

Article.Title: Genome-Wide Characterization of the HSF Gene Family in Paulownia fortunei and Preliminary Functional Analysis of PfHSF6 in Drought Response
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Liu C.; Wang L.; Zhao Z.; Cao Y.
Article.Abstract: Heat shock transcription factors (HSFs) act as crucial regulatory components in plant stress regulatory network and play essential roles in abiotic stress adaptation, particularly drought tolerance. Here, we identified 36 PfHSF gene family members in Paulownia fortunei through genome-wide analysis. Their chromosomal distribution, physicochemical properties, phylogenetic relationships, gene structures, conserved motifs, cis-acting elements, and post-translational modification sites were systematically characterized. Subcellular localization assays confirmed nuclear and plasma membrane localization of PfHSF6. Transient overexpression of PfHSF6 in tobacco significantly enhanced drought tolerance, as evidenced by alleviated wilting, a ~60% reduction in MDA content, ~2-fold increases in SOD and POD activities, and a ~67% reduction in electrolyte leakage relative to the control (p < 0.01); consistently, stress-responsive genes such as NbRD29A and NbLEA5 were up-regulated by ~6- and ~3-fold, respectively. This study provides a comprehensive characterization of the PfHSF family and preliminary functional evidence for PfHSF6, offering candidate genes for further functional validation and potential drought-tolerance breeding in paulownia.

Article.Title: Neurobiological Pathways Underlying Opioid Addiction and Overdose: Mechanisms, Therapeutic Targets, and Insights from Zebrafish Model
Article.Authors: Duric J.; Williams F.; Schiefer I.
Article.Abstract: The worldwide opioid epidemic continues to claim thousands of lives each year and remains one of the most urgent global public health challenges, driven by the high abuse potential and overdose risk of potent, fully synthetic μ-opioid receptor (MOR) agonists such as fentanyl. While fentanyl is highly effective in pain management, it also carries severe risks including respiratory depression, addiction, and fatal overdose. Understanding the neurobiological pathways underlying these risks is essential for developing safer analgesics and effective interventions. The MOR, a G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) that modulates neuronal excitability and synaptic transmission in important brain circuits like the ventral tegmental area (VTA), nucleus accumbens (NAc), and prefrontal cortex (PFC), is the primary receptor through which opioids exert their therapeutic effects. Dopaminergic dysregulation, transcriptional remodeling, and altered synaptic plasticity are neuroadaptations brought on by long-term opioid exposure that contribute to dependence and relapse. Life-threatening opioid toxicity is primarily driven by MOR-mediated suppression of respiratory networks, with risk shaped by dose, pharmacokinetics, receptor efficacy, and circuit sensitivity. Zebrafish (Danio rerio) provide a powerful complementary system for dissecting opioid-related neurocircuitry and screening for potential therapeutics. Zebrafish share conserved opioid-signaling components with mammals, and larval transparency facilitates in vivo imaging of neuronal activity at cellular resolution. Behavioral paradigms capture reward-related and drug-seeking phenotypes, while CRISPR-based approaches offer a means to investigate receptor-specific functions in validated models. In addition, zebrafish larvae provide an efficient platform for high-throughput screening of compounds that modulate opioid signaling and respiratory-related phenotypes. Together, insights from human, rodent, and zebrafish studies provide a more integrated understanding of opioid overdose and addiction neurobiology. This review incorporates current knowledge on the molecular and circuit-level mechanisms driving these processes and discusses how zebrafish models accelerate the discovery of safer analgesics and novel treatments for opioid use disorder and overdose.

Article.Title: Interferon-Induced Protein 6 (IFI6): Biological Functions, Molecular Mechanisms and Pathological Roles in Human Diseases
Article.Authors: Yang J.; Chen Y.; Zhang Y.; Xie Q.; Yin G.
Article.Abstract: Interferon (IFN)-induced protein 6 (IFI6) is an important member of the IFN-stimulated gene (ISG) family. It plays significant roles in anti-apoptosis, immune regulation, maintenance of mitochondrial homeostasis, antiviral defense, and tumor progression. At the molecular mechanism level, IFI6 inhibits mitochondrial membrane depolarization, cytochrome c release, and caspase activation. It also regulates the balance between B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2)/Bcl-2 interacting mediator of cell death (Bim), activates the Janus kinase (JAK)/signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-protein kinase B (PI3K-AKT) pathways, and upregulates the ferroptosis-related proteins solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11) and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), thereby enhancing cell survival and proliferation through multiple pathways. In terms of immune regulation, IFI6 is associated with immune cells (such as T/B cells, etc.) and the tumor microenvironment. IFI6 regulates mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) and mitochondrial calcium homeostasis, influencing respiratory chain assembly and metabolism. In terms of viral infection, IFI6 may inhibit the replication of multiple viruses (such as hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), SARS-CoV-2, etc.) by inhibiting flavivirus-induced endoplasmic reticulum (ER) invagination, interfering with retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like receptor signaling pathways, and inhibiting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) kinase activity. In addition, IFI6 is highly expressed in autoimmune diseases and malignant tumors and is associated with proliferation, metastasis, and poor prognosis. In this review, we aim to highlight IFI6 as a potential key target in disease diagnosis and treatment.

Article.Title: Prophylactic ALA Administration Attenuates Liver and Lung Injury in CLP-Induced Sepsis in Mice Through CSE/H2S Dependent Pathways
Article.Authors: Shahid A.; Scott-Thomas A.; Chambers S.; Miller A.; Bhatia M.
Article.Abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by a dysregulated host immune response to infection. Sepsis development usually results in organ dysfunction and multiple organ failure, including the liver and lungs. Alpha-lipoic acid (ALA) is a well-known anti-inflammatory agent. However, its effects on the endogenous cystathionine γ-lyase/hydrogen sulfide (CSE/H2S) pathway during cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced sepsis remain unclear. In this study, the protective effects of ALA in wild-type (WT) and CSE knockout (CSE−/−) mice were investigated. Mice were randomly divided into six experimental groups, including (a) WT sham (b) CSE−/− sham (c) WT CLP (d) CSE−/− CLP (e) WT CLP + ALA.P and (f) CSE−/− CLP + ALA.P (n = 8 in each group). ALA (100 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally one hour before CLP surgery. Eight hours after CLP induction, mice were euthanized, and blood, liver and lung tissues were collected. Body weight changes, proinflammatory cytokine and chemokine concentrations (including tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) and macrophage inflammatory protein-2 alpha (MIP-2α), myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity, histopathological changes, plasma H2S concentrations, and CSE expression in the liver and lung were measured. Severe liver and lung damage was characterized by markedly increased levels of MCP-1, MIP-2 α, TNF-α, and myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity, compared to WT sham control and CSE−/− groups (p < 0.0001). WT CLP-induced septic mice showed liver and lung injury as evidenced by hepatocyte swelling and ballooning degeneration with liver sinusoidal congestion, as well as pulmonary intra-alveolar and interstitial edema associated with thickening of alveolar septa and leucocyte infiltration, as compared to WT sham control and CSE−/− groups (p < 0.001). The WT-CLP group also showed a significant increase in hepatic and pulmonary expression of the H2S-producing enzyme (CSE) with elevated levels of plasma H2S concentrations, as compared to the WT sham group (p < 0.0001). Prophylactic ALA administration markedly improved these changes in the WT group. ALA also significantly decreased plasma H2S concentrations and hepatic and pulmonary CSE expression as compared to the WT CLP group (p < 0.01). However, ALA administration did not confer additional significant protective effects in CSE−/− mice, which supports the hypothesis that the effects of ALA are mediated through the modulation of the CSE/H2S pathway. In conclusion, this is the first experimental evidence showing that ALA prevents sepsis-associated organ injury at least partly by the downregulation of hepatic and pulmonary cystathionine γ-lyase expression.

These findings suggest that diosmin exerts protective effects against PTSD-like symptoms by regulating astrocytic function and immune-related pathways, with STAT1 signaling serving as a key but non-exclusive downstream mechanism underlying its therapeutic actions. Article.Title: Vitamin D in Digestive Neoplasms: Molecular Mechanisms and Clinical Evidence
Article.Authors: Treteanu A.; Stănescu A.; Constantinescu A.; Băjenaru O.; Nuță C.; Gradisteanu Pircalabioru G.; Andronic O.
Article.Abstract: Digestive neoplasms represent a major global health burden, accounting for a substantial proportion of cancer incidence and mortality. Increasing attention has been directed toward modifiable factors that may influence both the onset and progression of these malignancies. Among them, vitamin D has emerged as a potential protective factor, with deficiency frequently associated with elevated risk and unfavorable prognosis in gastrointestinal cancers. This review critically examines the current evidence regarding the role of vitamin D and its receptor (VDR) in digestive tumorigenesis. Beyond its classical function in calcium and bone homeostasis, vitamin D exerts pleiotropic effects on cellular processes fundamental to carcinogenesis, including regulation of proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, angiogenesis, immune modulation and genomic stability. Experimental studies demonstrate that adequate vitamin D status or administration of its analogues may suppress tumor growth and enhance responsiveness to conventional therapies. Epidemiological and clinical data, however, remain inconsistent across cancer subtypes, geographic populations and methods of vitamin D assessment. The analysis underscores the need for standardized evaluation of vitamin D levels, elucidation of dose–response relationships and clarification of interactions with genetic polymorphisms and environmental exposures. Future large-scale, randomized controlled trials are essential to establish causality and to define the optimal role of vitamin D in prevention and treatment strategies. Taken together, current findings support the hypothesis that vitamin D may serve not only as a biomarker of prognosis but also as a promising adjunctive approach in the management of digestive neoplasms.

Article.Title: Modeling the Prader–Willi Syndrome-Associated Growth Phases in Snord116 KO Mice
Article.Authors: Kummerfeld D.; Khanam T.; Wolters A.; Skryabin B.; Rozhdestvensky T.
Article.Abstract: Prader–Willi syndrome (PWS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by distinctive developmental transition from neonatal hypotonia and poor feeding to progressive weight gain and, later, hyperphagia and obesity. The Snord116-deficient mice exhibited a distinct three-stage growth trajectory: impaired growth until approximately P16, normalization between P17 and P21, followed by transient accelerated weight gain until approximately P30. Although growth rates subsequently normalized, the accumulated deficit was not fully compensated, and the adult Snord116KO mice remained smaller than the wild-type controls. These developmental transitions broadly parallel the early nutritional phases of human PWS, although the mice did not progress to exhibit persistent obesity-associated growth. Reactivation of the maternal Snord116 cluster partially rescued the growth phenotype, whereas activation of both parental alleles produced a modest growth advantage, which was most evident in the males. These findings identify early postnatal development as a critical window of Snord116-dependent growth regulation and provide a framework for investigating the mechanisms underlying PWS’s progression.

Article.Title: Hypothyroidism and Thyroxine-Induced Hyperthyroidism Differentially Affect Cathepsins, Mct8, and Thyroid Tissue Architecture in Male Mice
Article.Authors: Rehders M.; Kerp H.; Nica R.; Ecker R.; Führer D.; Brix K.
Article.Abstract: Adequate thyroid hormone concentrations are essential for tissue homeostasis, including in the thyroid gland. Hypothyroid tissue also exhibited markedly increased thyrocyte proliferation, while cell death rates were not altered across thyroid dysfunction. In addition, alterations in laminin indicated disbalanced extracellular matrix remodeling in hypothyroidism. Together, these findings demonstrate profound changes in thyroid architecture, proteolytic activity, and thyroid hormone transport under chronic thyroid dysfunction, particularly hypothyroidism. Further studies are needed to define the specific role of individual proteases in these processes.

Article.Title: Tumor-Centric Immune Crosstalk in Colorectal and Gastric Cancer: Molecular Mechanisms Linking Tumor Cells to Macrophages and CD8+ T Lymphocytes
Article.Authors: Pascu A.; Ianole V.; Danciu M.
Article.Abstract: Digestive malignancies remain a major cause of cancer-related mortality, with tumor progression (TP) being strongly influenced by the complex interactions between tumor cells (TCs) and their microenvironment. This review summarizes recently described mechanisms of interactions between tumor cells, macrophages and CD8+ T lymphocytes in colorectal and gastric cancer. PubMed and Web of Science were searched for studies published between 2020 and 2026, with the final search being conducted on 8 July 2026. Experimental and clinical studies, together with relevant reviews, were considered to examine these interactions and their therapeutic implications. The evidence shows a bilateral crosstalk in which tumor cells influence immune cell phenotype and function, while immune cells can further support or restrict tumor progression. These interactions involve receptor-ligand systems and paracrine signaling, followed by changes in intracellular pathways regulating proliferation, invasion, macrophage polarization and CD8+ T-cell exhaustion. Considerable methodological heterogeneity among studies limits a direct comparison of the reported mechanisms. Several therapeutic approaches targeting these interactions are currently being investigated in early-phase clinical trials. However, many components of tumor–immune crosstalk and their connections remain incompletely understood. A further characterization of these mechanisms may help identify therapeutic strategies able to interfere with the immunosuppressive microenvironment of colorectal and gastric cancers.

Article.Title: Naringenin Enhances the Inhibitory Effect of Regorafenib on HepG2 Hepatocellular Carcinoma Cell Viability with Modulation of E-Cadherin and MRP1 Gene Expression
Article.Authors: Gaballah S.; Abulsoud A.; Saleh A.; Eldesoky N.
Article.Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a life-threatening malignancy. Although regorafenib is used for HCC treatment, its clinical utility is limited by significant adverse effects. This study included seven groups of HepG2 cancer cells: an untreated control group, a naringenin-treated group (100 μM), a regorafenib-treated group (1 μM), and four groups receiving naringenin (100 μM) combined with decreasing concentrations of regorafenib (1, 0.75, 0.5, and 0.25 μM). All treatments significantly reduced cell viability compared with the control group, with greater inhibition observed in the combination-treated groups than in the monotherapy groups. Combination treatment also increased E-cadherin expression and decreased MRP1 expression. The combination of regorafenib (1 μM) and naringenin (100 μM) exhibited the greatest growth inhibition, the highest E-cadherin, and the lowest MRP1 expression levels. Notably, combining the IC50 of naringenin with one-quarter of the regorafenib IC50 significantly enhanced E-cadherin expression and reduced MRP1 expression compared with regorafenib alone. The present findings suggest that naringenin enhances the anticancer effects of regorafenib in HepG2 cells and modulates E-cadherin and MRP1 gene expression.

Article.Title: Copy-Number Alterations and Copy-Neutral Loss of Heterozygosity in Adult T-ALL: A Descriptive Study in Relation to Day +70 MRD
Article.Authors: Risinskaya N.; Starchenko S.; Abdulpatakhov A.; Chabaeva Y.; Aleshina O.; Kotova E.; Obukhova T.; Yushkova A.; Maiorova O.; Kapranov N.; Galtseva I.; Surimova V.; Kulikov S.; Sudarikov A.; Parovichnikova E.
Article.Abstract: Chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) detects copy-number alterations and copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity (cnLOH), but the CMA landscape of adult T-ALL has been described in few cohorts. Day +70 measurable residual disease (MRD) is a surrogate marker of early treatment response, available only after induction. Thirty-nine adults with Ph-negative T-ALL on a single protocol underwent diagnostic CMA. Mosaic events were catalogued per chromosome and against a 57-gene panel and described in relation to day +70 MRD status (13 MRD-positive, 25 MRD-negative). The analysis is presented as descriptive without formal inference. Mosaic alterations were present in almost all patients, so groups differed in the amount rather than the presence of genomic change. Complex profiles (≥3 affected chromosomes) were seen in 46.2% of MRD-positive and 20.0% of MRD-negative patients. Biallelic 9p21.3 deletion occurred in both groups, whereas 9p cnLOH without deletion occurred predominantly in MRD-negative patients. Total cnLOH burden did not track with copy-number burden. Copy-number and copy-neutral events are mechanistically distinct and were not interchangeable here: 9p deletion and 9p cnLOH are separable by SNP array and should be reported separately rather than pooled. No association reached significance, although the cohort was too small to detect all but very large effects.

Article.Title: Mitochondrial C1-FDX Depletion Perturbs ROS Homeostasis and Iron Metabolism in Arabidopsis
Article.Authors: Huang M.; Zhang K.; Wang T.; Li P.; Xin Y.; Chen B.
Article.Abstract: Mitochondrial complex I (CI) is a major source of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in plant cells, and iron–sulfur (Fe-S) cluster proteins are critical for maintaining CI structure and electron transport. C1-FDX, a mitochondrion-localized ferredoxin containing a [2Fe-2S] cluster, acts as a structural component and assembly factor of mitochondrial CI and complex V (CV) in Arabidopsis. In this study, we further characterized the physiological and molecular functions of C1-FDX in regulating ROS production, NADH/NAD+ homeostasis, and iron metabolism. Histochemical staining demonstrated that loss of function of C1-FDX in Arabidopsis c1-fdx mutants accumulated excessive superoxide anions (O2•−) but exhibited reduced hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) relative to the wild type (WT). Biochemical assays further confirmed that there was an elevated NADH/NAD+ ratio in mutant seedlings, which facilitated O2•− overproduction at mitochondrial CI. Loss of C1-FDX also led to Fe3+ accumulation in mutant tissues. Immunoblot and qRT-PCR results showed that the abundance of MnSOD markedly increased, while other antioxidant proteins, including FeSOD, CAT1, and GR, were downregulated in c1-fdx mutants of Arabidopsis. The enhanced MnSOD activity accelerated the conversion of O2•− into H2O2, and the subsequently accumulated Fe3+ may be derived from the Fenton reaction, which consumes H2O2, ultimately resulting in decreased H2O2 levels. Additionally, deficiency of C1-FDX disturbed the abundance of mitochondrial chaperones, proteases, and alternative respiratory pathway proteins. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that C1-FDX participates in the regulation of mitochondrial ROS balance and iron homeostasis and suggest there is a novel regulatory link between ferredoxin, the electron transport chain, and the Fenton reaction in plant mitochondria.

Article.Title: Beyond Monogenic Inheritance: Emerging Genetic Architecture of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
Article.Authors: Ramadan S.; Panza E.; Orlacchio A.
Article.Abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by marked genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity. Although pathogenic variants in major ALS genes, including C9ORF72, SOD1, TARDBP, and FUS, have provided fundamental insights into disease pathogenesis, many familial and most sporadic cases remain without a molecular diagnosis, suggesting a genetic architecture extending beyond coding variants and monogenic inheritance. Advances in genomic technologies have revealed contributions from deep-intronic and regulatory variants, structural rearrangements, repeat expansions, and other forms of genomic variation incompletely captured by standard diagnostic approaches. Evidence also indicates that combinations of rare variants with moderate or incomplete penetrance may contribute to disease susceptibility and clinical variability, supporting a multilayer model of ALS genetics. Population-specific variation and convergence of genetically diverse defects on common molecular pathways further complicate variant interpretation and disease classification. This review examines emerging components of ALS genetic architecture, including non-coding variation, structural variants, repeat expansions, oligogenic burden, ancestry-related gaps, and convergent neurodegenerative pathways. Integrating these genomic layers with functional and transcriptomic evidence may improve variant interpretation, diagnostic yield, patient stratification, and the development of mechanism-based precision therapies.

Article.Title: The Glymphatic–Meningeal Lymphatic System and Autophagy in ME/CFS and Long COVID: A Mechanistic Perspective
Article.Authors: Nemat-Gorgani M.; Jensen M.; Davis R.
Article.Abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (Long COVID) are complex multisystem disorders affecting 60–400 million individuals globally. They are considered post-infectious illnesses and share similar biological mechanisms, including immune dysregulation, orthostatic intolerance and cognitive dysfunction, highlighting a substantial overlap between the two conditions. Persistent fatigue, sleep dysfunction, post-exertional malaise and brain fog are among some of their most common and debilitating symptoms. Despite extensive research, they remain incurable, with no effective treatments, or simple diagnostic tests. They are increasingly understood as heterogeneous, multisystem diseases, involving neurological symptoms, with varying severities and diverse underlying biological abnormalities. More recently, the possibility of glymphatic dysfunction and autophagy impairment have been proposed as parts of the mechanistic features of the pathophysiology of these conditions, which are discussed more fully in the present perspective. With the glymphatic and meningeal lymphatic systems being operationally integrated, we will try to delineate how the metabolic waste removal mechanism afforded by this system may work together with autophagy to maintain brain homeostasis. We will provide some of the established mechanistic features of toxicity of misfolded proteins, explore their role in causing glymphatic dysfunction and impairing autophagy, and discuss the potential for therapeutic interventions.

Article.Title: Paeonol Attenuates UVB-Induced Premature Senescence in Human Dermal Fibroblasts to Promote Skin Longevity
Article.Authors: Lee K.; Han J.; Zhao H.; Kim Y.; Choi Y.; Ki H.; Kim J.; Choi Y.; Park H.; Jang A.; Park M.; Cho H.; Hwang J.
Article.Abstract: Skin photoaging is largely driven by ultraviolet (UV) irradiation, which contributes to chronic inflammation and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation. This study investigated the protective effects of paeonol against UVB-induced cellular senescence in human dermal fibroblasts (HDFn). Repeated UVB irradiation was used to induce premature senescence. Paeonol treatment reduced the senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) positive cells and intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. Paeonol also reduced the expression of senescence-associated cell cycle regulators, including p21 and p16 at the mRNA level and the protein level. In addition, paeonol suppressed matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP-1) production but did not significantly restore type I procollagen secretion. Paeonol also attenuated the expression and secretion of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors inter-leukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-8 (IL-8). These effects were accompanied by reduced phosphorylation of JNK and c-Jun. Furthermore, activation of JNK signaling with anisomycin partially reversed the paeonol-mediated suppression of MMP-1 mRNA expression, supporting the involvement of JNK signaling in the regulation of MMP-1. Collectively, these findings suggest that paeonol attenuates multiple features of UVB-induced cellular senescence in HDFn cells, with JNK signaling potentially contributing to its inhibitory effect on MMP-1 expression. Further studies are needed to clarify the mechanisms underlying these effects and establish their physiological relevance in UVA-based and in vivo models.

Article.Title: Isolated Rat Cardiomyocytes Differ in Their Sensitivity to the Action of Heterodimeric Phospholipase A2 from the Venom of the Viper Vipera nikolskii
Article.Authors: Galimova M.; Pimenov O.; Teplov I.; Berezhnov A.; Starkov V.; Tsetlin V.; Utkin Y.
Article.Abstract: Snake venom phospholipase A2 (PLA2) affect, among others, the cardiovascular system; however, data on their effect on isolated cardiomyocytes are practically absent. In this work, we investigated the influence of HDP-1 and HDP-2, heterodimeric PLA2s from the venom of viper Vipera nikolskii, on isolated rat cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocytes were stained with fluorescent probes and fluorescence was measured using Cell Observer fluorescent station. After PLA2 application, there was a prolonged lag phase with no changes in cell morphology or probe signal, followed by fluctuations in the cytosolic calcium level and cell hypercontracture with subsequent disruption of plasma membrane. In individual cardiomyocytes, time from the toxin addition until the hypercontracture varied by more than two-fold. In experiments with electrical stimulation, at HDP-2 application, a “pause” in contractions was observed, characterized by a decrease in the amplitude of the fluorescent response. Then, the contraction rhythm recovered, and later, hypercontracture was observed followed by cell destruction. Depending on times to these events, all cardiomyocytes studied were classified into two groups with fast and slow response to PLA2 action. The observed differences in the sensitivity of cardiomyocytes may be explained by unequal concentrations of intracellular calcium due to the different states of the cells at isolation.

Article.Title: Immunomodulatory Effects of Vitamin D Receptors and Serum Vitamin D Levels in COVID-19 Patients After Immunization: A Narrative Review
Article.Authors: Rathored J.; Shende S.
Article.Abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has caused global morbidity and mortality. Vaccination remains the most effective preventive strategy. However, variation in immune response after immunization has been observed among individuals. vitamin D plays a crucial role in immune regulation through activation of the VDR, which is expressed on various immune cells. The role of vitamin D status in post-vaccination immune responses among COVID-19 patients has gained increasing scientific interest. This narrative review evaluates the immunomodulatory roles of vitamin D receptors (VDRs) and serum vitamin D status in COVID-19 patients following vaccination, with particular emphasis on immune mechanisms, inflammatory regulation, and vaccine-induced immune responses. The relevant literature concerning vitamin D, VDR signaling, COVID-19 infection, vaccination, and immune responses was comprehensively reviewed. Emphasis was placed on studies discussing immune modulation, cytokine regulation, and antibody responses. Current evidence suggests that adequate serum vitamin D status may support both innate and adaptive immune responses following COVID-19 vaccination. Activation of the VDR regulates T-cell differentiation, modulates pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and supports humoral immune responses. Vitamin D deficiency has been associated with impaired vaccine responsiveness and persistent systemic inflammation. Vitamin D and VDR-mediated signaling pathways appear to play important roles in regulating immune responses following COVID-19 vaccination. Maintaining optimal vitamin D levels may help improve vaccine-induced immunity and reduce excessive inflammatory responses.

Article.Title: α-Halogenated Curcumins Enhance the Binding Affinity and Induced Structural Alterations to Amyloid-β Protein in Alzheimer’s Disease
Article.Authors: Khan M.; Chinnappan R.; Andole S.; Akif M.; Mir T.; Yaqinuddin A.; Pham P.; Bader M.
Article.Abstract: Amyloid-β (Aβ) aggregation and associated structural changes are central features of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology. In this study, we investigated the binding of α-halogenated curcumins, α-bromocurcumin and α-chlorocurcumin, to Aβ1-42 and examined their effects on the peptide secondary structure using fluorescence spectroscopy and circular dichroism (CD). Both α-halogenated curcumins interacted with Aβ1-42, but their binding properties differed from those of the parent curcumin. α-Chlorocurcumin exhibited a higher binding affinity for Aβ1-42 than curcumin, whereas α-bromocurcumin showed comparatively weaker binding. Temperature-dependent binding studies revealed that the association of α-halogenated curcumins with Aβ1-42 was influenced by temperature, with reduced binding affinity at higher temperatures. Thermodynamic analysis demonstrated favorable free-energy changes for the interactions and revealed that α-halogenation altered the relative enthalpic and entropic contributions to Aβ1-42 binding. CD analysis further showed that binding of the curcumin altered the secondary structure of Aβ1-42. These structural changes were more pronounced in the presence of the α-halogenated derivatives, indicating that halogen substitution influences the interaction and conformational response of Aβ1-42. Molecular docking analysis provided additional insight into the possible binding modes and predicted intermolecular contacts between the α-halogenated curcumin and Aβ1-42. Overall, the findings demonstrate that α-halogenation modulates the binding and structural effects of curcumin derivatives on Aβ1-42, with α-chlorocurcumin exhibiting particularly favorable binding characteristics. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of α-halogenated curcumins as potential modulators of Aβ-related molecular processes associated with AD.

Article.Title: Prometheus’s Fire, Part II: The Hydra of Inflammation—Multiorgan Self-Amplifying Inflammatory Loops in Obesity: Molecular Crosstalk Between Adipose Tissue, Liver, Skeletal Muscle, Pancreas and Cardiovascular System
Article.Authors: Grudniewska A.; Mrozikiewicz-Rakowska B.; Wiszniewski K.; Dudek P.; Kuryłowicz A.
Article.Abstract: Obesity should no longer be regarded as a disease confined to adipose tissue. Contemporary evidence indicates that adipose tissue dysfunction can initiate a cascade of metabolic and inflammatory responses that progressively involve multiple peripheral organs. Drawing on current molecular and translational evidence, we delineate mechanisms through which lipotoxicity, oxidative and endoplasmic reticulum stress, NLRP3 inflammasome activation and adipokine dysregulation contribute to inflammatory and metabolic dysfunction in the liver, skeletal muscle, pancreatic β-cells, vascular endothelium, perivascular adipose tissue and tumour microenvironment. Once established, organ-specific processes may become partially self-reinforcing and reciprocally amplify systemic immunometabolic dysfunction. We propose the Hydra of Inflammation as an integrative framework in which peripheral organs function not only as targets of adipose tissue-derived signals but also as secondary contributors to a progressively interconnected inflammatory network. This network-based perspective may help explain the heterogeneity of obesity-associated metabolic phenotypes and supports a shift from isolated organ-centred models towards systems-level approaches. The framework integrates the adipose tissue mechanisms discussed in Part I with the therapeutic perspectives developed in Part III of the Prometheus’s Fire series.

Article.Title: Whole-Exome Sequencing in Patients with Tooth Agenesis and Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Descriptive Case Series
Article.Authors: Calì F.; Musumeci A.; Vinci M.; L’Episcopo S.; Bartolone M.; Gloria A.; Ferri R.; Treccarichi S.; Fallea A.
Article.Abstract: Tooth agenesis (TA) is a common developmental abnormality that may occur as an isolated trait or as part of a multisystem disorder. Its genetic architecture remains incompletely characterized, particularly in individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). This descriptive case series aimed to investigate potentially relevant genetic variants in a clinically selected cohort of patients with TA using whole-exome sequencing (WES). Ten patients with TA and neurological or neurodevelopmental conditions were recruited at the IRCCS Oasi Research Institute of Troina between January 2024 and July 2026. The cohort included eight males and two females (age range: 5–50 years). The associated clinical spectrum included autism spectrum disorder (ASD), intellectual disability (ID), language impairment, behavioral abnormalities, and Down syndrome (DS). WES was performed in the examined cohort and variants were prioritized according to population frequency, predicted functional impact, inheritance pattern, and phenotypic concordance. The cohort comprised nine patients with hypodontia and one with oligodontia. Thirty variants involving 28 genes were identified. A homozygous GLI3 p.Gly727Arg variant, inherited from two heterozygous parents, was detected in an eight-year-old boy with ASD, global developmental delay, and hypodontia. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic loss-of-function variants in BCL11B were identified in two girls with ID and hypodontia. A likely pathogenic NIPBL splice-site variant was identified in a 15-year-old boy with hypodontia. His similarly affected father carried a novel FGFR1 p.Asn185His variant that was absent in the son, excluding it as the sole explanation for the familial dental phenotype. A 50-year-old man with DS and oligodontia carried the recurrent pathogenic BBS1 p.Met390Arg allele in the heterozygous state, together with variants of uncertain significance in PTH1R and STAT3. However, none of these variants independently explained his dental phenotype. The remaining variants were primarily relevant to the associated neurological phenotypes or represented secondary findings. This descriptive case series illustrates the clinical and genetic heterogeneity of TA in individuals with NDDs. Although the findings do not establish causal relationships with TA, they highlight the importance of distinguishing the general clinical significance of a variant from its specific relevance to dental development. Replication in larger cohorts and functional validation will be required to clarify the contribution of the identified candidate variants.

Article.Title: Targeting Redox Homeostasis with Arvanil Is Preferentially Cytotoxic to Glioma Stem Cells
Article.Authors: Nakamura K.; Takenouchi S.; Nakagawa-Saito Y.; Ito Y.; Mitobe Y.; Suzuki S.; Togashi K.; Sugai A.; Sonoda Y.; Kitanaka C.; Okada M.
Article.Abstract: Glioma stem cells (GSCs) are cancer stem cells in glioblastoma (GBM) that are resistant to both radiotherapy and chemotherapy and contribute to tumor recurrence. Therefore, the development of GSC-targeted therapies is urgently needed to improve the poor prognosis of GBM patients. Given the growing interest in redox homeostasis, which is closely linked to mitochondrial metabolism supporting the unique properties of GSCs, we focused on capsaicin, a widely used exogenous calcium channel agonist, and its structural analogs as candidate compounds capable of disrupting redox homeostasis in GSCs. Based on a comprehensive evaluation of the effects of the candidate compounds, we found that the capsaicin analog arvanil selectively induced cell death in GSCs with high selectivity over differentiated GSCs at concentrations that were non-toxic to normal cells. Arvanil-induced cell death was associated with a preferential elevation in intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in GSCs over those in differentiated GSCs and was suppressed by a Ca2+ chelator and a mitochondria-targeted antioxidant. These results suggest that arvanil preferentially induced GSC death in association with intracellular Ca2+ dysregulation and mitochondria-related oxidative stress, highlighting potential vulnerabilities in the redox homeostasis of GSCs and supporting further investigations on arvanil as a feasible therapeutic approach for GBM.

Article.Authors: Kumarasinghe H.; Le D.; Kim J.; Kim S.; Kim K.; Perera R.; Kim Y.; Lee M.; Lee D.
Article.Abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is highly aggressive and lacks targeted therapies. This study investigated the anti-cancer mechanisms of sinapaldehyde (SNAH). Cellular responses, including autophagy, mitochondrial function, apoptosis, cell-cycle progression, migration, and colony formation were investigated. In silico studies explored associated regulatory networks and binding targets. Sinapaldehyde (SNAH) treatment was associated with mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by alterations in mitochondrial structural and functional markers, increased reactive oxygen species(ROS) production, and loss of mitochondrial membrane potential. SNAH treatment also altered the expression of PINK1 and Parkin and modulated autophagy-associated markers, including LC3B, p62, LAMP1, Beclin-1, and ATG proteins. SNAH also altered FTH1 and NCOA4 expression, suggesting modulation of ferritinophagy-associated processes, and inhibited migration and colony formation while inducing G2/M cell-cycle arrest. In silico analyses identified potential breast cancer-related molecular targets and signaling pathways associated with SNAH. SNAH induces mitochondrial dysfunction and is associated with alterations in autophagy/mitophagy-associated signaling and activation of apoptosis in MDA-MB-231 TNBC cells. These findings provide insight into the cellular responses to SNAH treatment, while further functional studies are required to establish changes in mitophagic and ferritinophagic flux and the causal relationship between autophagy and apoptosis.

Article.Title: Heparinoid Cream Restores Epidermal Barrier Homeostasis and Attenuates Type 2 Inflammation in MC903-Induced Dermatitis
Article.Authors: Yasuda A.; Saito-Sasaki N.; Hara R.; Sawada Y.
Article.Abstract: Epidermal barrier dysfunction and cutaneous inflammation are closely interconnected in inflammatory skin diseases. However, the molecular effects of heparinoid cream on inflamed skin remain incompletely understood. Eight-week-old female BALB/c mice were treated topically with MC903 for 7 consecutive days, with or without concomitant application of heparinoid cream. Skin barrier function, histological changes, inflammatory markers, and gene expression were evaluated by transepidermal water loss measurements, histology, immunohistochemistry, quantitative PCR, and RNA sequencing. Therapeutic effects were also assessed by applying heparinoid cream after dermatitis had been established. RNA sequencing identified 816 differentially expressed genes following heparinoid cream treatment, including 146 upregulated and 670 downregulated genes. Upregulated genes were enriched in epidermal differentiation- and barrier-related pathways, whereas downregulated genes were enriched in immune and inflammatory pathways. In parallel, expression of multiple epidermal differentiation- and barrier-associated genes, including members of the Lce family, Flg, and Flg2, was restored. Therapeutic application of heparinoid cream after establishment of dermatitis was also associated with improved barrier function, increased Flg expression, reduced Tslp mRNA expression, and decreased epidermal KLK5 and TSLP immunohistochemical staining. Secondary reanalysis of a previously published human keratinocyte RNA-seq dataset revealed changes in selected barrier- and innate immunity-associated genes following MPS treatment under non-inflammatory monolayer culture conditions. These findings demonstrate that heparinoid cream treatment is associated with concurrent improvements in epidermal barrier-related parameters and attenuation of type 2 inflammatory responses in MC903-induced dermatitis. These findings provide molecular insights into the changes associated with topical application of a heparinoid-containing formulation in inflamed skin, although the specific contribution of MPS remains to be established.

Article.Title: Entropy Estimation: From Statistical Physics to Classification
Article.Authors: Vello F.; Fortuna S.; Fogolari F.
Article.Abstract: Driven by the common entropy formalism in statistical physics and information theory, here we show that methods developed for the analysis of molecular configurational ensembles may be successfully used for classification. Entropy is estimated using the k-th nearest neighbor method combined with the Maximum Information Spanning Tree method to account for the mutual information between variables. This formalism is used to classify new samples using their estimated cross-entropy with the training set. The method is tested using the hand-written digits MNIST and the functional genomics CuMiDa datasets. The results obtained on these diverse datasets are comparable to those obtained by machine learning methods, or better when the number of samples is small. The methods described here have the advantage, compared to other classification methods, of directly linking variables and pairs of variables to the assigned class, a valuable feature when aiming at identifying causal relationships between features and classes (e.g., the relationship between genes and diseases).

Article.Title: Temporal Multi-Omics Analysis of Mouse Bone Marrow Responses to Radiation Exposure
Article.Authors: Clifton A.; Jeppesen M.; Shaffiey S.; Chatterjee A.; Liermann-Wooldrik K.; Adebisi O.; Takkar S.; Mutha N.; Oberley-Deegan R.; Guda C.; Pierobon M.; Checco J.; Powers R.
Article.Abstract: Large-scale radiation catastrophes and localized exposure incidents remain major threats to public health. Effective treatment following radiation exposure is challenging because radiation dose, timing, and affected tissues can vary widely between individuals. To better understand the biological response to radiation injury, we employed a multi-omics approach integrating transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics. In this study, mouse bone marrow was analyzed at 1, 6, and 24 h after whole-body irradiation and compared with bone marrow from non-irradiated mice. Multivariate and univariate analyses revealed time-dependent changes across transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiles. We further applied machine learning-based integrative analysis and biomarker discovery approaches to identify key molecular responses associated with radiation exposure. Integrated analysis showed that the acute radiation response in bone marrow included immune-related processes, followed by intermediate metabolic reprogramming, and later disruptions in cell cycle regulation. Biomarker analysis identified several promising candidates, including the transcripts Sapcd2 and Cd28, proteins FRIL1 and CDK1, and the metabolites 3-hydroxyisobutyrate and taurine. Overall, our findings demonstrate that bone marrow from irradiated mice undergoes dynamic and coordinated molecular changes over time. These responses include activation of ferroptosis defense mechanisms, mitotic dysfunction, and pathways associated with programmed cell death.

Article.Title: Aluminum Chloride-Induced Planarian Model with Cognitive Impairments Through Neuronal Damage, Neurotransmitter Imbalance, Apoptosis, and Oxidative Stress
Article.Authors: Wang Q.; Wang S.; Xu Z.; Song L.; Yang K.; Zhang C.; Cheng X.
Article.Abstract: The prevalence of Alzheimer’s disease has significantly increased, which will place a heavy burden on families and society. Cognitive impairment is a typical feature of Alzheimer’s disease. Rodent models play a key role in AD research, but their considerable expense and slow development pose challenges to the pace of therapeutic discovery. Here, we established a new model of cognitive dysfunction in planarians using AlCl3. After exposure to 50 μM AlCl3 for 48 h, the planarians exhibited cognitive dysfunction in the phototaxis test, dual-stimulus decision test and T-maze test. Immunohistochemical and immunofluorescence experiments confirmed that AlCl3 damaged the neural structure of planarians. Moreover, AlCl3 disrupted the balance of neurotransmitters, leading to cell apoptosis and oxidative stress. Finally, we confirmed that donepezil alleviated the cognitive impairment caused by AlCl3. This indicates that the model we established for cognitive dysfunction in planarians was feasible. However, planarians lack the amyloid-β plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles typical of AD. Therefore, the planarian model can be considered a promising complementary platform for high-throughput screening of candidate drugs for cognitive impairment.

Article.Title: The Sedentary–Stress Paradox in Esports: Neuroendocrine, Metabolic, and Endothelial Pathways to Cardiovascular Risk
Article.Authors: Tero-Vescan A.; Ștefănescu R.; Ősz B.; Buț M.; Pușcaș A.; Pastorello Y.; Slevin M.
Article.Abstract: Esports and gaming resemble traditional sports and physical activity because both involve sustained cognitive and emotional stress; however, this stress occurs against a background of prolonged sedentary behavior. This narrative review examines the neuroendocrine, metabolic, and endothelial consequences of this “stress without movement” phenotype and its potential implications for long-term cardiovascular health. Activation of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis and sympathetic nervous system disrupts sleep and circadian rhythms. Continuous neuroendocrine activation may impair muscle–adipose tissue crosstalk and nitric oxide-dependent endothelial function. Although direct longitudinal evidence linking gaming to cardiovascular disease is currently lacking, these convergent mechanisms identify prolonged sedentary gaming as a potential cardiovascular risk amplifier, particularly when combined with occupational sitting, sleep disruption, adiposity, and other cardiometabolic risk factors.

Article.Title: Multi-Omic Analyses Reveal VPS72 Associations with Chromatin Remodeling, Proliferation, and Stress-Response Programs Across Human Cancers
Article.Authors: Solone X.; Reza M.; Renauer P.; Subedi K.; Parajuli N.; Zhou L.; Mi Q.
Article.Abstract: Malignant cells hijack epigenetic processes to sustain proliferation and to tolerate stressors that would otherwise limit cell growth, yet the chromatin remodeling activities that establish and maintain these programs are poorly defined. H2A.Z is a histone variant deposited into nucleosomes by the SRCAP and TIP60 chromatin-remodeling complexes, which share VPS72 as a chaperone subunit. VPS72 is located at 1q21, a region recurrently gained in human cancers, yet its contribution to tumor biology remains largely unexplored. Here, we show that VPS72 copy-number gain occurs in more than one-third of tumors and its expression is enriched beyond that expected from neighboring 1q21 genes and remains elevated over normal tissue in copy-neutral tumors. Across cancer types, higher VPS72 expression was associated with proliferative transcriptional programs, cell-cycle–related chromatin accessibility, and genomic instability. Single-cell analyses localized these associations primarily to malignant cells. Higher VPS72 expression and copy-number gain were associated with shorter overall survival in several solid tumors, although these relationships varied by lineage. VPS72 copy-number gain was also associated with shorter overall survival after adjustment for age and sex. Cancer-cell screens further identified recurrent VPS72 dependency, and VPS72 depletion suppressed proliferative programs while inducing stress, inflammatory, and apoptotic responses that were only partly shared with H2A.Z depletion. Together, these findings identify VPS72 as a recurrently altered component of tumor chromatin regulation associated with proliferative and stress-response states and support further investigation of its therapeutic significance.

Article.Title: USP30 Beyond Mitophagy: A Context-Dependent Deubiquitinase in Cancer Progression
Article.Authors: Liao W.; Xu N.
Article.Abstract: Ubiquitin-specific protease 30 (USP30) is a mitochondrial outer membrane-associated deubiquitinase best known for antagonizing PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)/Parkin-dependent ubiquitination and suppressing mitophagy. This established role has linked USP30 to mitochondrial quality control and neurodegenerative diseases. However, emerging studies in cancer have expanded the biological scope of USP30, revealing functions that cannot be explained by mitophagy regulation alone. USP30 regulates diverse cancer-associated substrates through deubiquitination, thereby affecting protein abundance, subcellular localization, protein interactions, and downstream transcriptional programs. These substrate-dependent effects influence mitochondrial dynamics, lipid synthesis, glucose and amino acid metabolism, redox homeostasis, apoptosis, ferroptosis, epithelial–mesenchymal transition, cancer stemness, T-cell exhaustion, and therapy resistance. Although most studies indicate tumor-promoting roles of USP30 in hepatocellular carcinoma, breast cancer, colorectal cancer, oral squamous cell carcinoma, ovarian cancer, bladder cancer, prostate cancer, and leukemia models, context-dependent tumor-restraining activities have also been reported. In this Review, we examine cancer-associated functions of USP30 that extend beyond its established role in PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy, discuss the spatial and substrate-dependent mechanisms underlying these activities, and highlight opportunities and challenges for therapeutic targeting.

Article.Title: M4-like Macrophages Drive Skeletal Muscle Fibrosis and Suppress Myogenesis via the MMP12/SPP1/NF-κB Axis
Article.Authors: Yao S.; Lu Z.; Zhao G.; Liu Y.; Wu S.; Zhang J.; Dong R.; Hu Y.; Zhang Y.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Acute skeletal muscle repair depends on a finely tuned balance between myogenic regeneration and fibrotic remodeling. Macrophages are essential to this process, and specific subsets have been linked to fibrosis in some organs. The M4-like macrophage, a distinct polarization subset implicated in fibrotic diseases, has not been well characterized in the context of injured muscle, particularly regarding its impact on fibroblast activation and myogenic suppression. The study aims to explore the effects of M4-like macrophages in the repair of muscle injury and possible mechanism. We analyzed a murine single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset from cardiotoxin (CTX)-injured skeletal muscle to identify injury-expanded macrophage subsets and their molecular programs. Immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence staining of muscle sections were used to assess CXCL4 expression and platelet (CD41+) infiltration in injured versus uninjured tissues. CXCL4-induced M4-like macrophages were established as an in vitro model to examine their effects on L929 fibroblasts and C2C12 myoblasts. The MMP12–SPP1 interaction was predicted by AlphaFold3 and validated by co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence colocalization. Loss-of-function and rescue experiments targeting MMP12 and SPP1 were performed to determine their causal roles in fibroblast activation and myogenic suppression. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses were used to define downstream macrophage-intrinsic NF-κB/TNF-α signaling. Finally, AAV-mediated macrophage-targeted SPP1 knockdown and pharmacological NF-κB inhibition were evaluated in the CTX injury model. Using a BALB/c mouse model of cardiotoxin (CTX)-induced acute skeletal muscle injury and a publicly available murine scRNA-seq dataset from CTX-injured skeletal muscle, we observed an injury-induced MMP12/SPP1-positive macrophage subset with an M4-like transcriptional signature. Mechanistically, co-immunoprecipitation assays and immunofluorescence colocalization supported an association between MMP12 and SPP1. MMP12 knockdown attenuated the pro-fibrotic and anti-myogenic effects of M4-like macrophages, whereas recombinant SPP1 largely restored these phenotypes. Furthermore, transcriptomic and biochemical analyses revealed that autocrine SPP1 activated NF-κB signaling in M4-like macrophages, and increased TNF-α secretion. Pharmacological inhibition of NF-κB signaling with QNZ reduced fibroblast activation and restored the expression of myogenic markers. However, QNZ is not TNF-α specific and may affect multiple cell types. In vivo, AAV-mediated macrophage-targeted SPP1 knockdown driven by the F4/80 promoter, as well as QNZ treatment in the CTX-induced muscle injury model, markedly decreased collagen deposition, enhanced myogenic regeneration, and improved functional recovery. These findings identify an MMP12/SPP1/NF-κB signaling pathway in M4-like macrophages, with TNF-α as a potential downstream mediator, that may contribute to an imbalance between regeneration and fibrosis and may represent a therapeutic target for enhancing skeletal muscle repair after acute injury.

Article.Title: R278H Substitution Reduces Mouse Tyrosine Hydroxylase Activity and Increases Susceptibility to Catechol Inhibition
Article.Authors: Alsalloum I.; Terentieva E.; Moskaliuk V.; Antonova S.; Ilchibaeva T.; Kulikov A.
Article.Abstract: Tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) catalyzes the hydroxylation of L-tyrosine to L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA), which is the rate-limiting step in dopamine (DA) synthesis in the brain. Certain mutations in the human TH gene are associated with severe neurological and psychiatric disorders. The c.886C>T mutation in the mouse Th gene, which results in the R278H substitution, decreases TH activity in the mouse midbrain. Here, we compared the molecular characteristics of the wild-type (TH-278R) and mutant (TH-278H) recombinant forms of TH. Both recombinant proteins were expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 cells and purified by immobilized metal affinity chromatography using Ni-NTA agarose resin. TH activity was assayed by HPLC, and the thermal stability of the recombinant proteins was assessed by differential scanning fluorimetry. The R278H substitution markedly decreased Vmax and increased the KM for the cofactor 6,7-dimethyltetrahydropterin (DMPH4), but had no effect on the KM for the substrate L-tyrosine. The substitution did not affect the T50 of thermal inactivation but markedly increased the Tm of thermal unfolding of the TH-278H protein. The substitution decreased the IC50 values for dopamine and 1,2-dihydroxybenzene several-fold, both of which contain a catechol moiety that is also present in L-DOPA. These results indicate that the R278H substitution alters the sensitivity of TH to catechol-containing compounds. Although direct evidence is lacking, endogenous L-DOPA produced during the reaction may interact differently with the catalytic center of the TH-278H mutant than with that of the wild-type TH-278R.

Article.Title: MicroRNAs’ Therapeutic Potential in Multiple Human Diseases
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Cai Z.
Article.Abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a class of short single-stranded non-coding RNAs widely present in multicellular eukaryotes, including animals, plants, and fungi. Typically, approximately 22 nucleotides in length (with some ranging from 22 to 25 nucleotides), miRNAs are predominantly localized to non-coding genomic regions and exhibit high evolutionary conservation. As key post-transcriptional modulators of gene expression, miRNAs are non-protein-coding molecules. They bind complementarily to the 3′UTR of target mRNAs. This interaction triggers mRNA breakdown or inhibits protein translation. In this way, miRNAs regulate nearly 30% of cellular protein expression. MiRNA biogenesis is tightly regulated. Abnormal miRNA expression alters disease-related genes and signaling pathways. It further drives the onset, development, and pathological processes of various human diseases. This review outlines recent progress in research on miRNA functions across multiple illnesses. These illnesses cover neurological, metabolic, tumor, and cardiovascular disorders.

Article.Title: Chronic Intermittent Hypoxia and MASLD in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Critical Appraisal of Mechanistic and Causal Evidence
Article.Authors: Cebuc Simeanu G.; Dragne I.; Mitrea A.; Clenciu D.; Protasiewicz-Timofticiuc D.; Popa A.; Mitroi D.; Pîrvu B.; Efrem I.; Glodeanu A.; Mirea A.; Ștefan A.; Roșu M.; Radu-Gheonea T.; Vladu B.; Efrem A.; Dijmarescu L.; Fortofoiu M.
Article.Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) frequently coexist and share a common cardiometabolic substrate through a shared cardiometabolic substrate. This narrative review critically appraises the epidemiological, experimental, and interventional evidence proposed to link chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) and sleep fragmentation to hepatic steatosis, steatohepatitis, and fibrosis. We summarize the candidate mechanisms, including mitochondrial oxidative stress, hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha signaling, sympathetically driven lipolysis, and Kupffer and stellate cell activation and then examine the limits of the evidence supporting them: hypoxia-induced hypophagia and the scarcity of pair-fed controls in rodent models, species differences in the physiological response to hypoxia, publication bias, common-cause confounding by age and systemic inflammation, and the rarity of progressive liver disease in lean patients with anatomically driven OSA. We further review non-invasive diagnostic tools, polysomnographic hypoxemia indices, transient elastography, METS-IR, FIB-4, and emerging biomarkers, such as omentin-1 and follistatin-like 1, that enable bidirectional screening between sleep and hepatology clinics. Finally, we discuss therapeutic strategies, including continuous positive airway pressure, structured weight loss, and incretin-based pharmacotherapy (GLP-1 and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists), highlighting recent phase 3 evidence for tirzepatide in OSA and semaglutide in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis. Current evidence supports CIH as a context-dependent amplifier of liver injury in patients with pre-existing metabolic dysfunction rather than as an established independent cause of MASH. This interpretation still justifies integrated screening and treatment pathways, while identifying the study designs needed to test causality directly.

Article.Title: Natural History and Therapeutic Response in Ophthalmic Plasminogen Deficiency: Two Cases and Call for Registry-Based Data
Article.Authors: Khan S.; Vogt A.; Khan O.; Tan J.; Nusrat S.
Article.Abstract: Plasminogen deficiency is an ultra-rare disorder of fibrinolysis that most commonly presents as ligneous conjunctivitis. Ophthalmic manifestations often precede systemic diagnosis, making ophthalmologists essential to early detection and management. We report two contrasting cases illustrating the spectrum of disease and therapeutic response. A 65-year-old woman with untreated type 1 plasminogen deficiency developed recurrent ligneous conjunctivitis leading to enucleation and multisystem morbidity, while a 4-year-old girl with autosomal dominant type 1 disease achieved sustained remission following systemic plasminogen replacement therapy (Ryplazim). These cases highlight the evolution of management from supportive care to disease-modifying therapy and the critical importance of early recognition. Long-term outcomes and treatment durability remain poorly defined, underscoring the need for registry-based collaboration to better characterize disease progression, therapeutic response, and quality-of-life impact in plasminogen deficiency.
