Article.Title: Breed-by-Altitude Interaction Reveals Cardiac miRNA–mRNA Regulatory Hubs Associated with Hypoxia Adaptation in Tibetan Pigs
Article.Authors: Li P.; Cheng W.; Shang P.; Tao Z.; Zhang H.; Zhang B.
Article.Abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are important post-transcriptional regulators of cardiac responses to hypoxia, but how breed and altitude interact to shape cardiac miRNA expression remains unclear. We used a 2 × 2 factorial design involving Tibetan and Yorkshire pigs raised at high (3000 m) or low (100 m) altitude. Small RNA sequencing identified 1104 miRNAs, including 370 known and 734 putative novel miRNA candidates. Pairwise comparisons revealed greater breed-related divergence at high altitude and a stronger altitude-associated miRNA response in Tibetan pigs than in Yorkshire pigs. The breed-by-altitude interaction analysis identified 94 breed-by-altitude interaction-responsive miRNAs, including 25 not detected by pairwise comparisons. K-means clustering further identified a Tibetan high-altitude-enriched miRNA module whose predicted targets were associated with hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1), mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR), adrenergic, calcium, and metabolic pathways. Integration with previously published cardiac messenger RNA (mRNA) differential-expression results for high-altitude Tibetan versus Yorkshire pigs, generated from the corresponding biological samples, prioritized 319 anti-correlated miRNA–mRNA pairs involving 19 miRNAs and 224 mRNAs, with ssc-miR-671-5p as the leading network hub. Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), correlation analysis, and miRanda prediction prioritized three candidate regulatory pairs: ssc-miR-671-5p–ATP1B2, novel-miR-212–ADCY6, and ssc-miR-296-3p–PFKM. These findings characterize breed-dependent, altitude-associated cardiac miRNA expression patterns and prioritize candidate miRNA–mRNA relationships for future functional investigation.

Article.Title: Disruption of Placental Immune Privilege by Complications of Pregnancy: Consequences for Maternal and Child Health
Article.Authors: Mixtega-Ruiz W.; Contreras Escamilla M.; Sevilla-Montoya R.; Olmos-Ortiz A.; Zaga-Clavellina V.; Castro-Rodríguez D.
Article.Abstract: Maternal chronic conditions, including obesity, diabetes, hypertensive disorders, and autoimmune diseases, promote a systemic proinflammatory environment characterized by oxidative stress and chronic inflammation. These alterations lead to reduced expressions of human leukocyte antigen-G (HLA-G) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), decreased regulatory T (Treg)cell activity, and increased T helper (Th)1/Th17 responses, disrupting placental immune privilege and resulting in increased production of proinflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress, trophoblastic dysfunction, and placental senescence. This change in immune privilege contributes to fetal growth restriction, preterm birth, congenital anomalies, and long-term cardiometabolic programming in offspring. Understanding the mechanisms underlying placental immune dysregulation may facilitate the development of targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring immune tolerance and reducing inflammatory and hypoxic signaling pathways to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. This review summarizes the current state of the field of placental immunological privilege and how maternal chronic conditions like obesity, diabetes, hypertensive disorders, and autoimmune diseases can disrupt it and its possible consequences on the progeny.

Article.Title: ROCK Inhibition Suppresses Thrombospondin-1 and Rewires DNA Methylation in the Trabecular Meshwork
Article.Authors: Shan S.; Choy K.; Ling C.; Li H.; Lung H.; To C.; Do C.
Article.Abstract: Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) inhibitors reduce cytoskeletal tension in trabecular meshwork (TM) cells, but the mechanisms linking this acute response to sustained extracellular matrix remodelling remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated whether the ROCK inhibitor Y39983 regulates thrombospondin-1 (THBS1) and DNA methylation programs, elements known to modulate extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling, in primary human trabecular meshwork (hTM) cells. Primary hTM cells were treated with Y39983, 5-azacytidine (5-Aza, a DNA methyltransferase inhibitor), or both in combination. Gene expression of THBS1, DNA methyltransferase, ECM, and cytoskeletal molecules was assessed using RT-qPCR. THBS1 promoter methylation was examined through methylation-specific PCR, while genome-wide methylation remodelling was profiled using whole-genome bisulphite sequencing (WGBS) followed by pathway enrichment analysis. 5-Azacytidine abolished Y39983-dependent effects on DNMT1 and DNMT3A and attenuated THBS1 regulation. Methylation-specific PCR suggested altered THBS1 promoter methylation after Y39983 treatment, while whole-genome bisulphite sequencing identified 8845 differentially methylated genes, including 5608 hypomethylated and 3237 hypermethylated genes, enriched in ErbB signalling, focal adhesion, and regulation of the actin cytoskeleton. Independently, Y39983 reduced the basal and stimulus-induced expression of THBS1, as well as ECM- and cytoskeleton-associated genes, including COL4A1, COL6A1, and ACTG1. These findings demonstrate that ROCK inhibition is associated with changes in DNMT-related gene expression and DNA methylation patterns in hTM cells. However, because 5-azacytidine has effects beyond selective DNMT inhibition, further studies using orthogonal approaches are required to establish whether DNA methylation directly mediates transcriptional responses to Y-39983.

Article.Title: Immunomodulatory Effects of MSC-Derived ExtracellularVesicles in Celiac Disease
Article.Authors: Ciccocioppo R.; Mottola I.; Zuliani V.; Adamo A.; Vitale S.; Krampera M.; Camarca A.; Rotondi Aufiero V.; Pisapia L.; Capuano F.; Mazzarella G.; Del Pozzo G.; Gianfrani C.
Article.Abstract: Coeliac disease (CeD) is the most frequent chronic enteropathy, in which intestinal lesions are caused by a dysregulated immune response to gluten proteins. We aimed to investigate whether extracellular vesicles (EVs) from mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) exert immunomodulatory effects in experimental models of CeD and are potentially useful to treat CeD. A population of MSCs was obtained from bone marrow blood of adult healthy donors. EVs were purified by ultracentrifugation of MSC-supernatants and characterized in terms of size, protein content and expression of surface markers. The immunomodulatory effects of MSC-EVs were evaluated in vitro on gliadin-specific T-cell lines by detection of interferon (IFN)-γ production and ex vivo by using duodenal mucosa biopsies by measuring lymphocyte infiltration (CD3 and CD25 positive cells), IFN-γ and interleukin (IL)-10 secretion. EVs obtained from non-celiac adult fibroblasts were used as controls. A significant and dose-dependent reduction of IFN-γ production by T cells in response to gliadin stimulation was observed in the presence of MSC-EVs (p < 0.05), but not with fibroblast-EVs. No modification of the expression of HLA class II molecules and costimulatory CD83 and CD86 markers on B cells upon EV-MSC incubation was found at any tested dose. Moreover, EVs from both MSCs and fibroblasts inhibited the gliadin-induced expansion of CD3+ and CD25+ T cells in organ cultures (p < 0.05), while increasing the IL-10 production (p < 0.05) and reducing IFN-γ (p = n.s) in organ supernatants. MSC- EVs modulated selected components of the immune response to gliadin in experimental models of CeD, including antigen-induced IFN-γ production and cellular responses in intestinal organ cultures. The effects observed in organ cultures were not exclusive to MSC-EVs, as EVs from fibroblast also modulated cellular responses. These findings provide a rationale for further preclinical investigation of EV-mediated immunomodulation in CeD.

Article.Title: An Overview of Seed Germination Mechanisms as a Target for Seed Priming
Article.Authors: Smolikova G.; Demidchik V.; Medvedev S.
Article.Abstract: As a central developmental phenomenon, seed germination is highly vulnerable to abiotic stresses, which strongly influence subsequent plant development and ultimately determine crop establishment and yield. An improved understanding of seed germination mechanisms has enabled the development of diverse crop enhancement strategies. Among these, seed priming has become a key tool in sustainable agriculture, widely used to boost plant stress tolerance and improve overall productivity. Among the various priming techniques, hydropriming involves the controlled hydration of seeds that initiates germinative events, followed by drying to arrest metabolism. The effectiveness of hydropriming depends on the precise modulation of germination to activate stress-related physiological responses. However, limited knowledge of the molecular dynamics underlying seed germination remains the main bottleneck for developing next-generation priming methods. This review comprehensively covers the genetics, epigenetics, and biochemical mechanisms of germination induced by hydropriming of seeds in higher plants.

Article.Title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy in Patients with Cancer: A Review of Clinical Outcomes
Article.Authors: Andronescu A.; Ciumărnean L.; Orășan O.; Cozma A.; Leah N.; Lucaciu R.; Hangan A.; Procopciuc L.
Article.Abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used for the management of obesity and type 2 diabetes, including among patients with cancer. Although previous research has mainly focused on cancer incidence, their associations with clinical outcomes after cancer diagnosis remain less well characterized. Therefore, the present study aimed to evaluate the oncologic and survival outcomes associated with GLP-1 RA use in adults with an established malignancy. We performed a systematic review of comparative studies evaluating GLP-1 RA use in patients with a confirmed cancer diagnosis. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for English-language publications from 1 January 2016 to 8 August 2026. Twenty-six retrospective cohort studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Thirteen studies included selective GLP-1 RAs and tirzepatide within the same exposure group. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Twenty-five studies evaluated overall survival and/or all-cause mortality, while nine assessed cancer recurrence, progression, or related outcomes. Survival and mortality outcomes more often favored the exposed group (especially compared with nonuse) than not, but findings were less consistent in active-comparator analyses. Evidence for recurrence and progression was sparse and heterogeneous, and no clear signal of increased risk was observed. Because all of these were observational studies with substantial differences in populations, comparators, exposure definitions, and duration of follow-up, the survival associations do not imply causality or direct antitumor effects of GLP-1 RAs. Clinically, the preponderance of evidence does not support the use of GLP-1 RAs as cancer-directed therapy, and their use in patients with cancer should be guided by established indications such as obesity and type 2 diabetes. Potential explanations include effects on glycemic and cardiovascular risk factors, treatment selection, residual confounding, or combinations thereof. Prospective studies and randomized controlled trials with cancer-specific outcomes and longer follow-up are needed to further evaluate these associations.

Article.Title: Interaction Analysis of VDR rs7975232 Polymorphism and the Triglyceride-Glucose Index in Relation to Metabolic Outcomes in Older Adults
Article.Authors: Michniewicz S.; Chmielowiec K.; Chmielowiec J.; Czyżniewski B.; Strowski M.; Pruszyńska-Oszmałek E.; Kołodziejski P.; Kowalski M.; Grzywacz A.; Gibas-Dorna M.
Article.Abstract: Ageing is associated with increasing metabolic heterogeneity driven by interactions between adipose tissue dysfunction and altered glucose-lipid metabolism. The vitamin D receptor (VDR) rs7975232 polymorphism has been investigated in relation to metabolic traits; however, its relationship with glucose–lipid metabolic characteristics remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association of the VDR rs7975232 polymorphism with metabolic markers and whether their relationships with the TyG index differ according to genotype in older adults. The study included 95 older adults living in a long-term care facility (mean age 62.71 ± 14.13 years). Anthropometric and fasting biochemical parameters were assessed, and the triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) were calculated. VDR rs7975232 genotyping was performed using real-time PCR. Multivariable linear regression models assessed genotype × TyG interactions after adjustment for age, sex, and waist-to-hip ratio. The rs7975232 genotype was not independently associated with TyG, NEFA, AIP, or other metabolic characteristics. In multivariable models using continuous TyG, genotype × TyG interactions were not statistically significant for NEFA or AIP. A nominal interaction was observed for fasting glucose, whereas no significant interactions were observed for log-transformed fasting insulin or log-transformed HOMA-IR. None of the genotype × TyG interactions remained statistically significant after Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. In the exploratory categorical sensitivity analysis, AA genotype × higher TyG category interactions had nominal p-values < 0.05 for NEFA and AIP. In this exploratory cross-sectional cohort, VDR rs7975232 was not independently associated with the assessed metabolic traits. The primary analyses did not provide robust evidence of genotype-dependent differences in TyG–metabolic associations. Nevertheless, exploratory analysis using categorized TyG suggested potential genotype-dependent differences in associations with NEFA and AIP. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

Article.Title: Progesterone Receptor Expression in Different Regions of Glioblastoma Multiforme and in an In Vitro Model
Article.Authors: Szubert D.; Kojder K.; Jeżewski D.; Tarnowski M.; Tomasiak P.; Piotrowska K.; Kolasa A.; Bosiacki M.; Szućko-Kociuba I.; Kołodziejczak M.; Kapczuk P.
Article.Abstract: The progesterone receptor (PGR) is involved in processes associated with tumor progression, also in glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). GBM is characterized by regional heterogeneity, with distinct tumor areas differing in their cellular profiles and access to nutrients and oxygen. The aim of this study was to assess the effect of the tumor microenvironment on PGR mRNA and protein expression and to characterize PGR expression in different regions of GBM. To this end, GBM tumor tissues were collected from patients, and an in vitro model was established using the U87 cell line to reproduce hypoxic (H) and nutrient-deficient (ND) conditions. PGR mRNA expression was assessed by real-time PCR, while PGR protein expression was analyzed using ELISA, Western blot, confocal microscopy, and immunohistochemistry. The microenvironmental conditions examined, including H and ND, did not affect PGR protein expression in U87 cells, while H conditions significantly increased PGR mRNA expression. Different GBM regions showed variable levels of PGR protein expression, with the highest expression observed at the peritumoral area. No effect of sex on PGR expression was observed in any of the GBM regions analyzed. Overall, the results indicate regional heterogeneity of PGR expression in GBM.

Article.Title: Application of Genotyping-by-Sequencing for Analysis of Breeding Signatures in Russian Spring Barley Collection
Article.Authors: Afonnikova S.; Pronozin A.; Kiseleva A.; Piskarev V.; Kukoeva T.; Sotnik A.; Vasiliev G.; Afonnikov D.; Salina E.
Article.Abstract: The high adaptability of barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) facilitated its cultivation across almost the whole Russian territory and various extreme environments. However, the genetic diversity and population structure of historical Russian barley collections remain poorly characterized at the genomic level. This study provides the first comprehensive genomic description of the barley panel maintained in the GeneAgro seed bank. Using genotyping by sequencing (GBS), we obtained high-quality genotyping data of 158 Russian and 21 foreign accessions. We evaluated genome-wide diversity and population structure, revealing a clear genetic stratification into two-rowed and six-rowed barley. Russian accessions complemented the diversity of the more than 19,000 domesticated barley accessions from the Leibniz Institute of Plant Genetics and Crop Plant Research (IPK), expanding the representation of germplasm developed specifically for Russian environments and economic demands. To identify genomic regions that may have been shaped by breeding, we scanned the native GeneAgro barley accessions for selective footprints. We detected multiple such regions across the genome. Some were shared by two-rowed and six-rowed barley, while others were specific to one row type, which may reflect differences in their breeding histories. These regions contain candidate genes previously associated with spike architecture, plant morphology, flowering time, fertility, grain color, photosynthesis, seed dormancy and resistance to fungal pathogens. These candidates provide hypotheses for future allele-level and phenotypic studies.

Article.Title: In Silico and Experimental Evidence for Theasaponin E2 as a Modulator of the AKT1/GSK-3β Signaling Axis in Osteoclast Differentiation
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Ding Y.; Bao X.; Deepak V.
Article.Abstract: Theasaponin E2 (TE2) is a triterpenoid saponin isolated from Camellia sinensis seeds with reported anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antitumor activities; however, its effects on osteoclasts remain unclear. In this study, TE2 markedly inhibited RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation in RAW264.7 cells without affecting precursor-cell viability. TE2 also significantly reduced the number and viability of mature, differentiated osteoclasts. Mechanistically, TE2 suppressed RANKL-induced phosphorylation of AKT at Ser473 and GSK-3β at Ser9, as determined by ELISA. Molecular docking predicted that TE2 could interact with the interdomain allosteric pocket of AKT1 at the pleckstrin homology–kinase domain interface (PDB ID: 7NH5; docking score, −9.8 kcal/mol) and the ATP-binding pocket of GSK-3β (PDB ID: 5K5N; docking score, −7.7 kcal/mol). The selected docking poses contained multiple hydrogen-bonding interactions with donor–acceptor distances of 2.79–3.19 Å. Collectively, these findings indicate that TE2 suppresses osteoclast differentiation and reduces mature osteoclast viability, potentially through modulation of the AKT/GSK-3β signaling axis. TE2 may therefore represent a promising natural-product candidate for further investigation in conditions characterized by excessive osteoclast-mediated bone resorption.

Article.Title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Network Pharmacology Analyses Reveal Potential Mechanisms of Codonopsis pilosula in Mountain Sickness
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Wu J.; Tan Z.; He W.; Tan W.; Fu M.; Bai B.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Mountain sickness comprises a spectrum of high-altitude disorders associated with hypobaric hypoxia, including acute mountain sickness (AMS) and high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE). Although Codonopsis pilosula has been widely used in traditional medicine for conditions related to hypoxia, its molecular basis in mountain sickness remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, machine-learning-based feature selection, single-cell RNA sequencing, and molecular docking to explore potential molecular associations between Codonopsis pilosula-related candidate targets and mountain sickness. We identified a set of Codonopsis pilosula-associated candidate targets enriched in biological processes related to hypoxia response, oxidative stress, inflammation, and vascular regulation. Integrated transcriptomic analyses across high-altitude exposure, AMS, and HAPE revealed convergent alterations in immune-related and oxygen transport-associated programs. Machine-learning analysis further provided internal computational prioritization of candidate genes associated with high-altitude exposure, with recurrent selection across complementary algorithms within the analyzed paired cohort. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis provided additional cellular context for these candidates, revealing distinct expression patterns across peripheral blood and lung cell populations. Molecular docking further identified potential interactions between selected Codonopsis pilosula compounds and candidate proteins, with MMP9, CA2, and BCL2 showing comparatively favorable predicted interactions. Together, these findings provide an exploratory framework for evaluating potential associations between Codonopsis pilosula-associated candidate targets and transcriptional and cellular responses to high-altitude hypoxia, and identify candidate molecular pathways and targets for further experimental investigation.

Article.Title: Circulating α-Klotho Is Elevated in Breast Cancer and Positively Correlates with IGF-1
Article.Authors: Ben Neriah S.; Abboud M.; Berlin A.; Hemi R.; Aks R.; Shapira S.; Wolf I.; Rubinek T.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most commonly diagnosed cancer among women worldwide. Klotho is an anti-aging protein implicated in tumor suppression; however, the relationship between circulating Klotho levels and BC remains unclear. We measured serum Klotho by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in 372 participants: 166 patients with BC, 24 patients with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), and 182 controls, and examined its relation to clinicopathological characteristics, including estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), HER2 and lymph node status, body mass index (BMI), and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1). Serum Klotho levels were significantly higher in invasive BC and DCIS patients compared with controls (p = 0.003 and p = 0.001, respectively), whereas no significant difference was detected between invasive BC and DCIS. After adjustment for age, Klotho levels remained significantly higher in BC and DCIS patients than in controls. Klotho levels correlated positively with IGF-1 (p = 0.0043), but not with BMI, ER, PR, HER2, or lymph node status. These preliminary findings demonstrate an association between elevated circulating Klotho and BC, as well as a positive relationship between Klotho and IGF-1. Further studies using age-matched cohorts and diagnostic-performance analyses are required to determine whether circulating Klotho has clinical utility as a BC biomarker.

Article.Authors: Castillo-Roque M.; Ramos-Silva J.; Fuentes-Garibay J.; Reyes-Becerril M.; De la Torre-Zavala S.; Hernández-Melgar A.; Figueroa M.; Ramos-Hinojosa E.; Galán-Wong L.; Avilés-Arnaut H.
Article.Abstract: Microalgae are increasingly recognized as valuable sources of natural products with potential applications in cancer prevention and therapy due to their ability to produce structurally diverse bioactive metabolites. In the present study, methanolic extracts from microalgal strains isolated from the oligotrophic desert oasis of the Cuatro Ciénegas Basin (Mexico) were evaluated for their antioxidant activity and in vitro cytotoxic effects against human breast (MCF7), colon (Caco2), prostate (DU145), leukemia (MOLT-4), and ovarian (OVCAR-3) cancer cell lines. The isolates were identified by rbcL gene sequencing and phylogenetic analysis as members of the genera Asterarcys, Chlorella, and Neochloris. Antioxidant properties were evaluated using complementary in vitro assays, whereas cytotoxicity was assessed using the MTT assay and apoptosis-associated cellular responses were investigated by morphological analysis, acridine orange/ethidium bromide staining, and measurement of executioner caspase-3/7 activity. Neochloris sp. PA3 showed the highest total antioxidant capacity and detectable ferrous ion-chelating activity, whereas Chlorella sp. PS exhibited the strongest superoxide radical scavenging activity. Among the evaluated strains, the methanolic extract of Neochloris sp. PA3 exhibited the most favorable overall antiproliferative profile, with IC50 values of 17.1, 19.0, and 19.1 µg/mL against MCF7, Caco2, and DU145 cells, respectively, while displaying markedly lower cytotoxicity toward the non-tumorigenic Vero and Detroit 548 cell lines, indicating differential cytotoxicity between the tested cancer and non-tumorigenic cell models. The extract induced time-dependent reductions in cell viability, morphological and nuclear alterations consistent with apoptotic cell death, and increased executioner caspase-3/7 activity. Collectively, these findings provide preliminary in vitro evidence of differential cytotoxicity and an apoptosis-associated cellular response in Neochloris sp. PA3-treated cancer cells.

Article.Title: Characterization of Kluyveromyces marxianus Extracellular Vesicles as a New Potential Delivery System for Biologically Active Compounds
Article.Authors: Rogalska M.; Kmita K.; Wrońska A.; Gryciuk A.; Sitkiewicz E.; Bakun M.; Świadek M.; Milner-Krawczyk M.; Mierzejewska J.
Article.Abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by probiotic microorganisms may be involved in intercellular communication via transferring their cargo to other cells. Proteomic analysis identified 161 core proteins common to all strains, yielding 33 potential biomarkers lacking significant human homology, which would be useful for tracking yeast EV carriers in subsequent studies. In addition, yeast EVs were found to have a high affinity for human cells, transporting biologically active molecules (doxorubicin) and the Nile Red dye into recipient cells. Altogether, this study provides clear evidence that the EVs of K. marxianus could be considered a drug delivery system.

Article.Title: Evaluation of PSII Thermal Stability in Grapevine Germplasm and Identification of Candidate Genes Based on a Genome-Wide Association Study
Article.Authors: Wu W.; Sun L.; Xu R.; Guo R.; Wang J.; Hu C.; Fan X.
Article.Abstract: Heat stress damages the photosynthetic apparatus of grapevine leaves. It also restricts plant growth and reduces fruit yield and quality. However, natural variation in photosystem II (PSII) thermal stability under heat stress in grapevine and its genetic basis remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluated 404 genetically diverse grapevine accessions. We measured the maximum quantum efficiency of photosystem II (Fv/Fm) after treatment at 47 °C. Phenotypic analysis, cluster analysis and genome-wide association analysis were then used to investigate the genetic basis of PSII thermal stability. The coefficient of variation for Fv/Fm increased from 4.52% at 25 °C to 40.60% at 47 °C. Wild accessions generally retained higher Fv/Fm than interspecific hybrids and Vitis vinifera cultivars. We also identified 21 accessions with relatively high PSII thermal stability. A genome-wide association analysis of 5,074,860 high-quality SNPs detected a suggestive association signal on chromosome 4. The lead SNP was Chr4_1743280_G_A. We integrated gene annotations within the associated interval, putatively functional variants and diplotype–phenotype comparisons. This analysis prioritized seven candidate genes potentially associated with variation in PSII thermal stability. The Hap2/Hap2 diplotype of Vitvi005414 was associated with higher Fv/Fm. However, these associations should be regarded as candidate hypotheses for further validation rather than evidence of causal relationships. These findings provide candidate loci, genes and diplotypes for understanding the genetic basis of PSII thermal stability. They also support the use of germplasm with relatively high PSII thermal stability, validation of candidate variants and future breeding for improved heat resilience.

Article.Title: Proteomic Remodeling in the Female Heart During Spaceflight and Recovery
Article.Authors: Ahmed A.; Figueiredo D.; Woolsey R.; Quilici D.; Puukila S.; Alwood J.; Ronca A.; Christenson L.; Tahimic C.
Article.Abstract: Spaceflight profoundly impacts cardiovascular physiology. To gain insight into the underlying molecular adaptations, we examined the female cardiac proteome during spaceflight and recovery. We hypothesized that spaceflight remodels the cardiac proteome, including mitochondrial bioenergetics and redox homeostasis pathways, during both flight and recovery, altering cardiovascular health risk. Proteomic analysis was performed on hearts from female C57BL/6J mice flown aboard the International Space Station (ISS) for 55 to 60 days as part of the NASA Rodent Research-20 (RR-20) study and a recovery cohort returned to Earth after 42 days, with sampling occurring five days after landing, and corresponding ground controls. Consistent with our hypothesis, spaceflight enriched mitochondrial bioenergetic pathways relative to ground controls, including cellular respiration, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation. These changes occurred alongside the remodeling of antioxidant pathways, suggesting altered redox regulation during flight and increased susceptibility to reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in the heart versus controls. Postflight recovery was characterized by distinct metabolic, redox, and structural remodeling signatures, including pathways associated with sarcomere organization, contractile function, and extracellular matrix regulation. These findings reveal cardiac proteomic remodeling during and after spaceflight and provide molecular insights relevant to cardiovascular risk assessment and countermeasure development for exploration missions.

Article.Title: Acetylcholine and Prolactin, Other Factors in Breast Cancer
Article.Authors: Calaf G.; Andrade-Madrigal C.; Crispin L.; Miranda V.; Aguayo F.
Article.Abstract: Acetylcholine (ACh) and prolactin (PRL) are increasingly recognized as additional factors potentially influencing breast cancer biology. Their effects may depend on tumor-cell context and on the molecular signaling state of individual breast cancer subtypes. This study aimed to evaluate phosphorylation responses to ACh and PRL and examine transcriptomic associations involving related signaling genes. MCF7, T47D, and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines were treated with ACh, PRL, or combined ACh + PRL for 4 h. Significant changes in selected phosphoproteins were summarized for proteins related to AKT–S6 kinase, EGFR–ERK, TP53–Src/PLC-γ1, and STAT3–JUN signaling. Transcriptomic analyses evaluated associations between acetylcholinesterase (ACHE) or prolactin receptor (PRLR) expression and selected signaling-related genes in breast cancer cohorts, including subtype-specific analyses, tumor-versus-normal comparisons, and overall-survival associations. ACh and PRL produced distinct, cell-line-specific phosphorylation patterns. The MCF7 cell line showed increased AKT, p70S6K, and p53 phosphorylation after ACh, whereas combined treatment increased AKT and STAT3 phosphorylation. The T47D cell line showed a mixed response, with combined treatment increasing p70S6K, PLC-γ1, and Src phosphorylation but reducing AKT, ERK1/2, and c-Jun phosphorylation. The MDA-MB-231 cell line showed the broadest response, with combined ACh + PRL increasing AKT, RSK, STAT3, and c-Jun phosphorylation. Transcriptomic analyses identified subtype-dependent associations of ACHE and PRLR with genes encoding AKT, S6 kinase, ERK, Src/PLC-γ1, STAT3, and JUN-related proteins. Several genes also showed differential tumor-versus-normal expression or survival associations. ACh and PRL are associated with context-dependent signaling responses in breast cancer. Experimental phosphoprotein changes and tumor transcriptomic associations converged on related signaling modules but represented different molecular levels and did not establish complete pathway activation or direct causality. These findings support further investigation of ACh–PRL interactions and their potential contribution to breast cancer biology.

Article.Title: Systematic Identification of Candidate Substrates of the UCH Family of Deubiquitinases
Article.Authors: Ramirez J.; Prieto G.; Barrio E.; Atxa-Espiga A.; Presa N.; Arteaga-Cabeza O.; Mayor U.; Osinalde N.
Article.Abstract: Deubiquitinases (DUBs) of the ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase (UCH) family play critical roles in regulating ubiquitin-dependent signaling, yet their substrate specificity and functional organization remain incompletely defined. Here, we systematically characterized the ubiquitination landscape associated with UCH family members (UCHL1, UCHL3, UCHL5, and BAP1) using a quantitative proteomics workflow combining siRNA-mediated DUB silencing, bioUb-based enrichment of ubiquitinated proteins, and label-free mass spectrometry. Proteins exhibiting increased ubiquitination following DUB depletion were identified as candidate substrates. Our analysis revealed that UCH family members regulate largely distinct subsets of ubiquitinated proteins, with limited overlap in their candidate profiles despite sharing conserved catalytic domains. In parallel, site-resolved ubiquitinomics identified 851 ubiquitination sites, including 106 not previously reported, expanding the current landscape of experimentally validated ubiquitin-modified lysines. Functionally, substrate networks link individual UCH enzymes to distinct yet partially overlapping cellular processes, including hypoxia signaling, RNA metabolism, vesicle trafficking, apoptosis, and chromatin regulation. Notably, known substrates such as HIF-1α validated the approach, while recurrent detection of key regulators, including MCL1, pointed to convergence at the level of apoptosis control. Together, these findings provide a resource for exploring the distinct and potentially overlapping roles of UCH deubiquitinases within cellular ubiquitin-regulatory networks.

Article.Title: Cuproptosis in Inflammation-Related Respiratory Diseases
Article.Authors: Fu Q.; Zheng Y.; Zou Y.; Cui X.; Wei R.; Gu Y.; Qin L.; Sun S.
Article.Abstract: Cuproptosis is a newly identified form of regulated cell death. The core molecular events of cuproptosis involve copper homeostasis dysregulation, aggregation of mitochondrial lipoylated proteins, loss of iron–sulfur cluster proteins, and mitochondrial proteotoxic stress. Multiple signaling pathways regulate cuproptosis, such as the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α), and the p53 pathway. Cuproptosis plays an important role in various inflammation-related respiratory diseases, including lung cancer, acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ALI/ARDS), asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and tuberculosis. Cuproptosis inhibits malignant progression and therapeutic resistance in lung cancer, while it aggravates ALI/ARDS. In addition, cuproptosis promotes airway inflammation and remodeling of asthma. However, the role of cuproptosis in COPD and tuberculosis remains unclear. Moreover, the mechanism of cuproptosis affecting inflammation-related respiratory diseases is unclear. Accordingly, cuproptosis may play an important role in various inflammation-related respiratory diseases.

Article.Title: Host Protein-Degrading Cathepsin L-like Proteases of Ostertagia ostertagi
Article.Authors: Karunakaran A.; Aponte Y.; Rajendrakumar A.; Liu Y.; Boschiero C.; Miramontes E.; Beshah E.; Shao J.; Vinyard B.; Liu G.; Zhu X.; Tuo W.
Article.Abstract: Ostertagia ostertagi is the most pathogenic gastrointestinal nematode of cattle and causes major productivity losses. With rising anthelmintic resistance and significant economic impact, alternative control measures, such as vaccination, are urgently needed. This study aimed to generate functionally active recombinant cysteine proteases from O. ostertagi, enzymes involved in nutrient acquisition and immune evasion, to evaluate their potential as vaccine candidates. Two phylogenetically predicted cathepsin B (catB)-like proteases, OoCBP1 and OoCBP2, were cloned into the pcDNA3.1+ vector and expressed in FreeStyle 293-F cells. Purified proteins were assessed using fluorogenic substrates and various host protein substrates, including fibrinogen, albumin, hemoglobin, IgG, mucin, and gelatin, at pH 5.0 and 7.4 with or without a reducing agent. OoCBP1 was detected in the parasite across the life stages, while OoCBP2 was only detectable in adult worms. OoCBP1 partially degraded host proteins at pH 5.0, with reduced activity at pH 7.4, whereas OoCBP2 efficiently degraded all tested proteins at both pH levels except IgG, which was only partially degraded. OoCBP1 showed catB/L activity only at acidic pH, while OoCBP2 was active at both pH conditions. Activities were inhibited by catB, catB/L, or other cysteine protease inhibitors. OoCBP1, but not OoCBP2, required low pH-mediated autoactivation for substrate degradation. OoCBP1 had no effect on coagulation under physiological conditions, while OoCBP2 accelerated clot formation with reduced clot density. With in vitro activation, both proteases delayed coagulation. These findings indicate that OoCBP1 and OoCBP2 may contribute to nutrient acquisition and immune evasion, supporting their potential as targets for vaccines or chemotherapeutics against ostertagiosis.

Article.Title: Development of an Experimental Protocol for Combined Electroporation and Phototherapy Treatment Against Melanoma Cells
Article.Authors: Spugnini E.; Onofrj M.; Assumma C.; Condello M.
Article.Abstract: Melanoma is the most common cutaneous tumor with significant challenges for successful pharmacological treatment. The aim of this study was to determine the optimal treatment conditions using a combined therapy based on electroporation and the photoactivation of acridine orange (AO) with a blue LED lamp, designed by Biopulse srl. The effect of combined therapy was investigated by MTT assay and optical microscopy observations. Drug uptake and apoptosis induction were analyzed by flow cytometry. The best treatment schedule was obtained using electric pulses (sequences of eight biphasic pulses lasting 50 + 50 μs with 300 μs interpulse, at a voltage of 300 V), an AO concentration of 0.01 μg/mL, and LED exposure for 30 s. The combined treatment was more effective against melanoma cells than human dermal fibroblast-adult cells. The results demonstrated that electroporation increased AO accumulation, allowing for reduced drug concentrations and exposure times. This combination induced programmed cell death consistent with apoptotic features in melanoma cells, as shown by cell cycle analysis. These preliminary results demonstrated the efficacy of combination therapy based on electroporation and phototherapy with AO on melanoma cells, and they encourage the possibility of testing efficacy on melanoma models in veterinary oncology.

Article.Authors: Kiseleva A.; Sotnikova E.; Zharikova A.; Kutsenko V.; Imaeva A.; Balanova Y.; Kapustina A.; Vyatkin Y.; Pokrovskaya M.; Ershova A.; Shalnova S.; Meshkov A.; Drapkina O.
Article.Abstract: Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising biomarkers of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-MACE): CVD death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and non-fatal stroke. This nested case–control study included 479 participants: 166 cases with 3P-MACE and 313 controls matched individually for sex, exact baseline age, and region of residence. Median follow-up was 10.4 years [7.0; 11.7]. Total RNA was isolated from EDTA plasma using the miRNeasy Serum/Plasma Advanced Kit. Libraries were prepared with the QIAseq miRNA UDI Library Kit and sequenced on a NextSeq 550 (1 × 75 bp). After adjustment for six and twelve preanalytical and clinical covariates, eleven and five differentially expressed (DE) miRNAs retained significant associations with 3P-MACE or CVD death, respectively. Although these findings support plasma miRNA profiles as potential MACE biomarkers, all DE miRNAs remain exploratory. Further studies in larger independent populations with cross-validation are required before integration with traditional risk markers to predict future MACE.

Article.Title: Divergent RUNX2-Associated Regulation of FAM20A and FAM83H in the Enamel–Eruption Developmental Axis
Article.Authors: Mao S.; Wei S.; Jia H.; Hou Y.; Ruan W.; Dong J.; Xu J.; Duan X.
Article.Abstract: Amelogenesis imperfecta (AI) associated with family with sequence similarity 20 member A (FAM20A) and family with sequence similarity 83 member H (FAM83H) may be accompanied by both enamel defects and tooth-eruption abnormalities; however, the tissue-level and molecular mechanisms underlying the relationship between these phenotypes remain poorly understood. To explore the mechanism, here we studied seven AI individuals from three families by oral and radiographic examination and whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing. Eruption abnormalities in FAM20A- and FAM83H-related AI were analyzed by integrating these seven cases with our previous retrospective datasets and newly reported cases from the literature. FAM20A and FAM83H expression was examined by RNA sequencing of human dental tissues and by immunohistochemistry in human dental follicle tissue and P0/P7 mouse tooth germs. RUNX2 regulation of FAM20A and FAM83H was assessed by CUT&Tag in dental follicle and RUNX2 siRNA knockdown. Genetic analysis identified two distinct heterozygous pathogenic truncating FAM83H variants in six patients from two families and compound heterozygous FAM20A variants in one patient from the third family. Eruption abnormalities were observed in the FAM20A patient and four of the six patients with FAM83H variants. In the combined dataset, eruption abnormalities were documented in 36 of 37 (97.3%) evaluable FAM20A cases and 18 of 58 (31.0%) evaluable FAM83H cases. In human dental follicle tissues surrounding impacted third molars, both proteins localized predominantly to epithelial lining components. In developing mouse tooth germs, both proteins were enriched in odontogenic epithelial/enamel-organ compartments with weaker staining in mesenchymal compartments. Dental-follicle RNA profiling further revealed an epithelial/keratin signature and detectable FAM20A/FAM83H expression. CUT&Tag identified RUNX2 binding at FAM20A but not FAM83H, and RUNX2 knockdown reduced FAM20A expression without a corresponding decrease in FAM83H. We conclude that FAM20A- and FAM83H-associated AI exhibit distinct patterns of eruption abnormalities in addition to enamel defects. Our findings support FAM20A as a candidate RUNX2-regulated target in dental follicle cells, whereas no comparable regulatory relationship was evident for FAM83H under the experimental conditions.

Article.Title: Polyphenols and Flavonoids in microRNA-Regulated Pathways of Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiotoxicity: Mechanistic Evidence, Biomarker Potential and Translational Gaps
Article.Authors: Lampropoulou D.; Kouskouti A.; Gioxari A.; Pliakou E.; Argyri K.; Dedes V.; Panoutsopoulos G.; Gazouli M.
Article.Abstract: Although doxorubicin remains a cornerstone of anticancer therapy, its clinical utility is limited by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity. Current tools for the early detection of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) remain suboptimal, prompting interest in microRNAs (miRNAs) as mechanistic regulators and circulating biomarkers. Natural cardioprotective compounds, particularly polyphenols and flavonoids, have also attracted attention because of their ability to modulate oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, autophagy and regulated cell death. However, the mechanistic and translational strength of this evidence varies considerably. This critical narrative review is based on targeted PubMed literature searches up to 14 August 2026, supplemented by selective reference-list screening of relevant original articles and reviews. The literature search was not intended to be exhaustive, and the studies discussed were selected to illustrate different levels of mechanistic evidence. Studies investigating miRNA-mediated mechanisms in DIC were distinguished from circulating biomarker studies, while phytochemical evidence was classified as direct miRNA-linked, miRNA-associated without causal validation, or pathway-convergent. Among the selected examples, taxifolin provides direct miRNA-linked evidence involving the miR-200a/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, with functional miR-200a inhibition demonstrated in H9c2 cells. Blueberry extract provided miRNA-associated evidence; miR-140-5p expression was assessed together with Sirt2 and Nrf2 expression, but a causal role for miR-140-5p was not functionally validated. For the other selected compounds, the available evidence was predominantly pathway-convergent. Although miRNAs and phytochemicals offer complementary perspectives on DIC mechanisms and cardioprotection, their clinical application remains premature. Future studies require functional miRNA validation, standardized biomarker assessment, pharmacokinetic evaluation and confirmation that cardioprotection does not compromise antitumor efficacy.

Article.Title: Research Progress and Challenges in Targeting GLUT1 in Tumors
Article.Authors: Chen T.; Peng B.; Yuan X.; Liu Y.; Zhang J.; Su Y.; Hu G.; Tao Z.; Long G.
Article.Abstract: The solute carrier family 2 member 1 (SLC2A1), which encodes glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1), has long been recognized as a key driver of aerobic glycolysis in cancer. However, accumulating evidence has substantially expanded this view, revealing that GLUT1 functions not only as a critical mediator of metabolic reprogramming but also as an important regulator linking tumor metabolism to immune evasion. Notably, GLUT1 expression, regulation, and functional dependence are highly context-dependent across tumor types, disease states, and cellular compartments. Recent studies further link GLUT1-dependent glycolytic flux to immune regulation through glucose competition, lactate accumulation, and metabolite-dependent epigenetic programs within the tumor microenvironment. Reflecting this evolving understanding, therapeutic strategies targeting GLUT1 have progressed from simple metabolic inhibition to approaches that exploit tumor-specific metabolic dependencies and extend to regulated cell death, combination therapy, precision delivery, and selective modulation of malignant and non-malignant cellular compartments. These advances support a shift from expression-centered targeting toward strategies guided by functional GLUT1 dependence and cellular context, while recognizing the metabolic and physiological constraints that shape the therapeutic window. In this review, we systematically summarize recent advances in GLUT1 expression heterogeneity, multilayered regulatory networks, metabolic–immune crosstalk, diagnostic and prognostic relevance, and therapeutic targeting, and discuss how these insights may refine biomarker development, patient selection, and the clinical translation of GLUT1-directed precision metabolic therapy.

Article.Title: Lactoferrin and Nanotechnology: New Perspectives and Therapeutic Applications for This Multifunctional Protein
Article.Authors: Superti F.; Mariano A.; Scotto d’Abusco A.
Article.Abstract: Lactoferrin, a multifunctional glycoprotein belonging to the transferrin family, is proving to be an extremely promising drug delivery vehicle, with numerous applications in the field of nanotechnology. This protein is biocompatible and well-tolerated and, regarding cell targeting, it is capable of binding to low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1, a large multifunctional transmembrane receptor that mediates endocytosis, cell signaling, and protein clearance. Interestingly, lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 is overexpressed in various cell types, particularly on tumor cells and blood–brain barrier endothelial cells. The purpose of this review is to summarize the most important beneficial activities demonstrated by lactoferrin nanoparticles obtained through various methods, aiming to identify potential prospects for their future applications in nanomedicine. Due to its remarkable stability and safety, interaction with specific cellular receptors, and ability to cross various key biological barriers in the human body, including the blood–brain barrier, lactoferrin has been successfully used to deliver therapeutic agents directly to their targets. This reduces systemic side effects while improving bioavailability and therapeutic outcomes. The main specific characteristics of lactoferrin nanoparticles include controlled release of the active ingredient at acidic pH, the ability to deliver hydrophobic drugs through various routes, and the greater efficacy and lower toxicity of the encapsulated drug compared to the free drug. This review highlights scientific evidence from in vitro and in vivo studies regarding the benefits of lactoferrin-based nanoformulations to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of molecules and drugs used to treat communicable and noncommunicable diseases. However, given that their practical application has remained rather limited to date, it is anticipated that lactoferrin nanoparticles will increasingly attract the attention of researchers across various fields, such as biology, medicine, and nanotechnology, with the aim of enabling their clinical application.

Article.Title: The Genetic Landscape of Pompe Disease in the Middle East, North Africa, and Turkey (MENAT Region): A Systematic Review of GAA Variants and Genotype–Phenotype Correlation
Article.Authors: Alantry A.; Hamdan S.; Kubbara E.; Rezk M.; Mohamedain A.; Mohamedain E.; Makki Y.; Kamal E.; Hamdan H.
Article.Abstract: Pompe disease is a rare autosomal recessive multisystem disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) gene, resulting in lysosomal glycogen accumulation and a broad clinical spectrum ranging from rapidly fatal infantile-onset disease (IOPD) to slowly progressive late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD). The genetic epidemiology of Pompe disease across the Middle East, North Africa, and Turkey (MENAT) region remains poorly characterized despite high regional rates of consanguinity. We systematically searched PubMed, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and Scopus from inception to July 2026 for studies reporting GAA variants in patients with Pompe disease from MENAT countries, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. We included 24 studies comprising 134 patients with Pompe disease, identifying 61 distinct GAA variants. Twelve variants were unique to the MENAT region. Missense variants were the most common variant type, accounting for 50.8% of all distinct variants, followed by frameshift variants 19.7%. Egypt contributed the largest number of reported patients (24/134, 17.9%) followed by Saudi Arabia, Iran, and Iraq (18/134, 13.4%) for each country. The most prevalent variant across the MENAT region is the leaky intronic splice-site variant c.-32-13T>G, reported in 11.2% of all patients and in cases from Turkey, Algeria, Iran and Egypt. Of the 61 distinct variants, 35 were associated with IOPD and 24 with LOPD, with c.1064T>C (p.Leu355Pro) and c.2104C>T (p.Arg702Cys) reported in association with both phenotypes. This systematic review identified country-specific variants in the MENAT region related to Pompe disease that are distinct from other reported variants worldwide. Further studies with larger sample sizes are needed to comprehend the genotype–phenotype correlation for Pompe disease in the MENAT region.

Article.Title: The Transcription Factor SOX5 as a Potential Marker of Resistance to Chemotherapy in Gastric Cancer Cell Lines
Article.Authors: Reyes-González J.; Valenzuela G.; Musleh M.; Landeros N.; Contreras H.
Article.Abstract: Chemoresistance is one of the major barriers to effective treatment in gastric cancer (GC), contributing to disease progression and poor patient survival. SRY-box transcription factor 5 (SOX5) has been associated with aggressive cancer phenotypes in several malignancies; however, its relationship with chemoresistance in GC has yet to be fully characterized. This study investigated whether SOX5 expression is associated with molecular features linked to aggressive GC phenotypes, including multi-drug resistance proteins, cancer stem cell (CSC) antigens, epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers, and proteins involved in drug efflux and DNA repair. SOX5 expression was evaluated in AGS and MKN-45 GC cell lines using Western blotting, real-time quantitative PCR, and immunofluorescence. Markers associated with EMT (Snail1, ZEB1, and E-cadherin), CSC phenotypes (CD44 and CD133), DNA repair (XRCC1 and ERCC2), and drug efflux (ABCB1) were analyzed. Cellular sensitivity to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and oxaliplatin (Ox) was assessed using an MTT-based viability assay. In addition, publicly available GC datasets were analyzed to evaluate the association between SOX5 expression and overall survival. AGS cells exhibited significantly higher SOX5 expression at both the mRNA and protein levels compared with MKN-45 cells. High SOX5 expression was associated with increased expression of the transcription factors Snail1 and ZEB1, which are associated with EMT, leading to decreased E-cadherin expression. Furthermore, SOX5 expression was associated with increased expression of CD133, the DNA repair genes XRCC1 and ERCC2, and ABCB1 transcripts. Consistent with these molecular findings, AGS cells exhibited greater viability following exposure to 5-FU and Ox, either alone or in combination, suggesting reduced sensitivity to these agents. Furthermore, high SOX5 expression was associated with poorer overall survival across independent GC patient cohorts. Overall, these findings suggest SOX5 as a potential biomarker associated with an aggressive molecular phenotype characterized by EMT activation, enhanced DNA repair capacity, stemness-associated features, and reduced sensitivity to FOLFOX-based chemotherapy. Future mechanistic studies are warranted to establish whether SOX5 directly drives these processes.

Article.Title: Heparan Sulfate, Chondroitin Sulfate, and Keratan Sulfate as Regulators of Tumor Malignancy
Article.Authors: Ohkawa Y.; Taniguchi N.
Article.Abstract: All mammalian cells, which include cancer cells, express sugar chains on their cell surfaces. These sugar chains bind with proteins, lipids, and RNAs. These chains consist of as few as two or three monosaccharides in the shortest chains, and as many as several hundred to a thousand monosaccharides in the longest chains. The chains appear to have a multilayered structure, which makes cells appear to be covered in a coating of sugar. The expression patterns and levels of these sugar chains, also known as the glycocalyx, vary greatly depending on the cell or tissue, and are therefore thought to perform unique localized biological functions. Furthermore, changes in the glycocalyx changes in conjunction with the onset of disease are believed to be closely related to the development of pathological conditions. In this study, we focus on glycosaminoglycans such as heparan sulfate, chondroitin sulfate, and keratan sulfate—relatively long chains of glycans that constitute the glycocalyx—and introduce their biological functions and potential applications in cancer treatment.

Article.Title: Allergenic Responses Elicited by Goat Milk Protein Hydrolysates in Cow Milk-Sensitized Mice
Article.Authors: Zhao W.; Lu S.; Liu Y.; An P.; Cong Y.
Article.Abstract: This study established a BALB/c mouse model of milk allergy to investigate the allergic responses elicited by goat milk protein hydrolysates prepared using three proteases—alkaline protease, bromelain, and trypsin—in sensitized mice. Serum-specific IgG and total IgE levels were measured, and allergic symptom scores and histopathological changes were evaluated. The results showed significant differences in clinical symptom scores among the different treatment groups (p < 0.05), with a significant difference observed between the bromelain hydrolysate group and the GM group (p < 0.05). Serum-specific IgG and total IgE levels were also significantly lower in all three hydrolysate groups than in the whole goat milk protein group (p < 0.05), with the lowest specific IgG level observed in the trypsin hydrolysate group. The bromelain hydrolysate group exhibited the lowest clinical symptom score and serum histamine level. Histopathological analysis further confirmed that, compared with the whole goat milk protein group, the hydrolysate groups exhibited less intestinal mucosal damage and reduced splenic congestion. In summary, this study evaluated the elicitation response to goat milk protein hydrolysates in cow milk protein-sensitized mice. The three hydrolysates elicited weaker allergic responses than total goat milk protein. However, because the hydrolysates were administered only during the challenge phase, their intrinsic sensitizing capacity was not assessed. These findings provide a basis for further investigation into the potential use of hydrolysates in hypoallergenic goat milk-based formula foods, which will require additional studies.

Article.Title: Differential Regulation of Cholesterol-Related Gene Expression by HDAC Inhibition in Neuron-Enriched and Glia-Enriched Rat Primary Cultures
Article.Authors: Samorodova A.; Beletskiy A.; Balaban P.; Borodinova A.
Article.Abstract: Brain cholesterol homeostasis is a highly sophisticated, epigenetically regulated process where neurons and glia play distinct roles in maintaining metabolic balance. Disruption of this tightly regulated system is a hallmark of many neurological disorders, including Alzheimer’s disease. Histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitors were shown to regulate transcription of metabolic genes in the brain. However, their influence on cholesterol-related gene expression in functionally different neural cell populations remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we used a model of rat primary cultures enriched in either neurons or glial cells to compare the culture-specific transcriptional responses induced by the HDAC inhibitor trichostatin A (TSA). Using quantitative PCR, we analyzed the relative mRNA expression of representative genes involved in cholesterol synthesis (Hmgcs1, Mvd, Lss, Dhcr7), transport (Apoe, Apod), uptake (Vldlr, Ldlr), efflux (Abca7, Abcg1), and elimination (Cyp46a1). Our results suggest that HDAC inhibition induces complementary yet distinct and epigenetically tunable transcriptional responses in the neuronal and glial cell cultures maintained under their respective culture-specific conditions. We hypothesize that these transcriptional changes may have functional consequences for cholesterol metabolic pathways, including altered cholesterol accumulation in both cell types and enhanced cholesterol efflux in neurons. However, this requires further experimental validation. Overall, our results provide a framework for understanding how cell-type-specific epigenetic regulation of cholesterol-related genes may shape brain lipid homeostasis. These insights may facilitate the development of cell-targeted epigenetic therapies for neurological disorders associated with metabolic dysfunction.

Article.Title: Cerium Dioxide-Based Scavenging of Environmentally Persistent Free Radicals in Fine Particulate Matter: A Prospective Review
Article.Authors: Liu Q.; Yang Z.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Environmental persistent free radicals (EPFRs) are a class of long-lived, redox-active species that persist on fine particulate matter (PM2.5) surfaces for days to months. Upon inhalation, EPFRs catalyze the generation of hydroxyl radicals through Fenton-like cycling, driving oxidative stress and inflammation at the site of deposition. Current air filtration technology focuses almost exclusively on physical interception of particulate matter, leaving the surface-bound radical activity of captured PM entirely unaddressed. This review advances a testable hypothesis rather than reporting a validated outcome: that cerium dioxide (CeO2)-based materials, whose Ce3+/Ce4+ redox cycling is well-established as a broad-spectrum antioxidant mechanism in biomedical contexts, can be functionally migrated to air filtration to chemically quench EPFRs on captured PM2.5. We first summarize the formation and health impacts of EPFRs, then introduce the mechanistic basis of CeO2 radical scavenging, emphasizing its self-regenerating valence cycling. We then examine the existing but functionally distinct use of CeO2 in air pollution control, including its role as an oxygen storage component in three-way catalysis and as an additive in filter media, and argue that these high-temperature oxidation applications do not constitute a functional precedent for ambient-temperature radical scavenging. The central gap is that no study has systematically tested whether CeO2 can chemically quench EPFRs on PM2.5 surfaces under filtration conditions. We articulate the key experimental questions that must be resolved—direct EPFR quenching versus ROS interception, the effects of humidity, airflow, and contact time, and the long-term fate of CeO2 under realistic filtration conditions—and argue that the demonstrated gaseous ROS scavenging of CeO2 in cigarette smoke, together with its self-recovery capability, provides sufficient mechanistic justification to pursue this direction experimentally.

Article.Title: Linear Combination Properties of Spectral Phasors Allow Thermodynamic Analysis of Reversible Denaturation of Multidomain and Membrane Proteins
Article.Authors: Angelini A.; Malacrida L.; González Flecha F.
Article.Abstract: Denaturation of small globular proteins is often described as a reversible two-state transition between native and denatured conformations. Conversely, multidomain and membrane proteins frequently populate several partially folded intermediate states during denaturation. Traditional thermodynamic analysis of fluorescence intensity often fails to reliably identify these intermediate states. Alternatively, spectral phasors provide an effective model-free way to monitor these complex conformational changes by resolving overlapping fluorescence signals with small differences in the position or shape of the spectra. Nevertheless, converting phasor trajectories into quantitative thermodynamic information remains challenging when quantum yields do not remain constant during a given process, thus limiting their application to protein stability studies. In this work, we introduce a thermodynamic framework for quantifying protein stability from phasor trajectories. We validate this formalism using simulated spectral data generated from two- and three-state transitions, including changes in fluorescence quantum yields, successfully recovering the thermodynamic parameters used to generate the simulations. Additionally, we applied this approach to analyze published data on urea-induced unfolding of E. coli Outer Membrane Protein A. Phasor analysis identified a two-state transition, and the thermodynamic parameters agreed well with those obtained from total fluorescence intensity, supporting the validity of the proposed approach. Finally, applying this framework to the SDS-induced denaturation of Archaeoglobus fulgidus Cu(I)-transport ATPase enabled a complete thermodynamic characterization of the three transitions identified by phasor analysis of intrinsic fluorescence, which could not be resolved using fluorescence intensity alone. This formalism establishes fluorescence spectral phasors as a powerful quantitative approach for protein stability analysis.

Article.Title: Hijacking the Message: Insights from Targeting mRNA Export and Translation in AML.
Article.Authors: Borden K.; Guzman M.
Article.Abstract: Cancer cells hijack RNA metabolism, including splicing, polyadenylation, nuclear export and translation, to change both the amount and the form of the proteins they produce. This creates therapeutic vulnerabilities beyond the mutations and translocations that have guided drug development in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), where outcomes remain poor. Using AML as a paradigm, this review focuses on two nodes of RNA metabolism: the eukaryotic translation initiation factor eIF4E, a cap-chaperone that escorts mRNAs through processing, export and translation, and CRM1/XPO1, the major nuclear exporter of proteins and select RNAs that partners with eIF4E for specific mRNA export activity. We describe the RNA biology dysregulated in patients, the mechanisms of the inhibitors that target these pathways, and their pre-clinical and clinical data across AML and other malignancies. Indeed, early-stage clinical trials in AML and other malignancies show promise, including the use of CRM1/XPO1 inhibitors (selinexor, eltanexor) and eIF4E inhibitors (including ribavirin and tomivosertib). We discuss how selecting patients by eIF4E status, confirming on-target activity, and designing rational combinations could improve next-generation therapies.

Article.Title: Stable Strontium Distribution and Effects on Plants
Article.Authors: Seregin I.; Kozhevnikova A.
Article.Abstract: Strontium (Sr) is a wide-spread alkaline earth metal that is similar to calcium (Ca) in its chemical properties, although it does not play the physiological role inherent to the latter. At low doses, Sr can stimulate plant growth and development. However, at elevated levels in the environment, it has a negative effect on many processes occurring in plant cells, leading to growth inhibition and reduced productivity. The majority of studies have been focused on the effects of radioactive Sr isotopes which produce additional toxic effects due to ionizing radiation, but the effects of stable Sr have not received enough attention. The current scoping review summarizes the data on the uptake mechanisms and transport pathways of stable Sr and examines the characteristic patterns of its distribution in plant tissues and organs. Available data on the effects of stable Sr on enzyme activity, mineral nutrition, photosynthesis, plant growth, and morphogenesis are analyzed. Understanding the transport pathways of Sr, as well as the factors determining its dual effects on plant growth and development, underlies the development of approaches used in biofortification and phytoremediation technologies. The review may be useful for researchers working on plant mineral nutrition, metal stress, and phytoremediation.

Article.Title: Metabolomic Profiling Reveals Heat-Responsive Metabolic Markers in Honey Bee Workers Under Contrasting Diets
Article.Authors: Jang H.; Kim H.; Frunze O.; Kwon H.; Kim B.; Jung J.
Article.Abstract: Acute heat exposure challenges honey bee (Apis mellifera) workers, yet the associated small-molecule response and its relationship to nutritional status remain incompletely resolved. Workers were conditioned for 7 days on bee bread plus sucrose (B+S) or sucrose alone (S), maintained at 37 °C or exposed to 45 °C for 3 h, and thorax–abdomen metabolites were profiled by untargeted Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF/MS). Three independent cages were used per diet × temperature group, with 15 workers per cage pooled to generate one cage-level biological replicate (n = 3 per group). Putative metabolite annotation used accurate-mass (10 ppm) and isotope-pattern matching against METLIN and the Agilent Personal Compound Database and Library (PCDL), followed by manual curation, without tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) o or authentic-standard confirmation. After statistical filtering and biological curation, 149 heat-responsive metabolite annotations were retained under B+S and 123 under S. Targeted re-extraction of proteinogenic amino acids from the same raw files recovered 16 common peaks across all samples. Fifteen increased at 45 °C in both diets, whereas proline decreased; 14 of 16 showed a larger fold change under B+S. Phenylalanine-related metabolism showed the strongest convergence across targeted amino-acid analysis, untargeted phenylpyruvate detection, and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment. Lipid-class responses also differed descriptively between diets, with a bias toward decreased free fatty acyls under B+S and decreased phospholipids under S. These findings define coordinated metabolic markers of acute heat exposure in worker bees and show that, within the targeted amino-acid dataset, response magnitudes were generally larger under B+S while retaining the same overall direction.

Article.Title: PSY Inhibits Colorectal Cancer Growth and Exhibits an In Vitro Synergistic Interaction with 5-Fluorouracil
Article.Authors: Han S.; Kim H.; Choi H.; Oh M.; Lee M.; Lee J.; Ha I.; Ahn K.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: PSY is a three-herb formula comprising Patriniae Radix, Mori Cortex Radicis, and Coix Seed that was previously shown to inhibit STAT3 signaling in colorectal cancer (CRC) cells. Here, we investigated molecular and metabolic responses to PSY, its antitumor activity in an HCT116 xenograft model, and its interactions with chemotherapy in vitro. Representative chemical markers were qualitatively verified by UPLC-ESI-QTOF MS/MS. Exploratory RNA sequencing with two biological replicates per group highlighted stress-associated and metabolic processes for further investigation. PSY increased BiP, phosphorylated eIF2α, ATF4, and CHOP levels, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and mitochondrial membrane depolarization, while reducing the phosphorylation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR- and ERK-associated proteins. PSY increased the p-AMPK/AMPK ratio and decreased the p-ACC/ACC ratio. PSY reduced several lipid-biosynthetic transcripts and decreased the relative abundance of selected fatty acids in xenograft tumors. Oral administration of PSY suppressed HCT116 xenograft growth without significant body-weight loss. Combination-index (CI) analysis indicated CI-defined in vitro synergistic interactions with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) at multiple concentration pairs, with interaction patterns varying across HCT116, HT-29, and SW480 cells. Direct cell counting supported the combination response in HCT116 and SW480 cells. The combination increased apoptosis and reduced STAT3 and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation relative to single treatments. These findings characterize concurrent, partly discordant signaling and metabolic responses to PSY and support further preclinical evaluation of its in vitro interaction with 5-FU.

Article.Title: Potential Roles of Flavonoids from Chrysanthemi Flos and Chrysanthemi Indici Flos in Modulating Bile Acid Metabolism: Mechanistic Insights and Future Perspectives
Article.Authors: Zhao S.; Zeng L.; Tang H.; Cui Y.; Zeng R.; Xie J.
Article.Abstract: Changes in bile acid metabolism are associated with metabolic liver disease, inflammation, and immune dysfunction. Chrysanthemi Flos and Chrysanthemi Indici Flos contain many bioactive flavonoids and have several reported pharmacological effects. However, how their flavonoids regulate bile acid metabolism has not been reviewed in detail. This review summarizes 52 flavonoids identified in Chrysanthemi Flos and Chrysanthemi Indici Flos. We also consider how these pathways may affect inflammation and metabolic disorders. This review relates the reported mechanisms to the traditional use of these medicinal plants for “clearing the liver and promoting bile flow.” It also outlines research needs for assessing natural hepatoprotective and metabolic disease interventions that target bile acid metabolism.

Article.Title: Limited Gut Microbiome Differences Between Relapsing–Remitting and Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: A Shotgun Metagenomic Study
Article.Authors: Vacaras C.; Vacaras V.; Nistor C.; Vesa S.; Jucan C.; Furdui I.; Strilciuc S.; Stefanescu E.; Chira D.; Rafila A.; Muresanu D.
Article.Abstract: The gut microbiome may contribute to multiple sclerosis (MS) pathophysiology, but its relationship with disease phenotype and progression remains unclear. Alpha diversity and overall microbial community composition were similar across groups. SPMS showed greater interindividual microbial community dispersion than RRMS in the full cohort, with a similar direction and magnitude but attenuated statistical significance in the age-overlap sensitivity analysis. Exploratory taxonomic signals were not confirmed by FDR-controlled analyses. No robust phenotype-specific differences in predicted SCFA-related pathways or associations of taxonomic or functional features with disability or circulating biomarkers were identified. Greater microbial community dispersion in SPMS was observed in the full cohort, but this finding was attenuated in the age-overlap sensitivity analysis and should be considered preliminary. Overall, these findings do not support a distinct SPMS-associated gut microbiome signature, although potential phenotype-related differences cannot be excluded.

Article.Abstract: The receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE/AGER) is an important mediator of inflammatory signaling and has been implicated in chronic low-grade inflammation associated with aging. Reduced RAGE expression was confirmed at the mRNA, protein, and cell-surface levels, identifying sh1 and sh2 as lead candidates. An AGER-focused workflow for lentiviral shRNA construct screening and experimental validation was established, providing a reproducible approach for generating stable cell models with reduced AGER/RAGE expression. Further work is required to confirm isoform specificity, assess off-target effects, and define the functional consequences of RAGE suppression.

Article.Title: Exploring Pathophysiological Processes Shared Between Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Osteoarthritis
Article.Authors: Majeed Y.; Schulze-Tanzil G.; Kokozidou M.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and osteoarthritis (OA) are highly prevalent chronic disorders with increasing global burdens that frequently coexist and share common risk factors, including obesity, aging and chronic low-grade inflammation. This narrative review aims to summarize current evidence regarding the epidemiological, clinical and molecular links between T2DM and OA and to highlight potential therapeutic implications. Growing evidence suggests that T2DM contributes to OA development and progression through multiple interconnected mechanisms. These include advanced glycation end-product (AGE) accumulation, oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, extracellular matrix degradation, impaired autophagy, ferroptosis, mesenchymal stem cell dysfunction and microvascular impairment within joint tissues. In addition, shared genetic and molecular pathways, including AGE–RAGE, IL-17, PI3K/Akt/mTOR and LGR6/Wnt/β-catenin/NRF2 signaling, further support a biological connection between the two diseases. Clinically, T2DM is associated with increased OA severity, enhanced pain sensitization, accelerated disease progression and higher rates of joint arthroplasty. Emerging evidence also suggests that antidiabetic agents, particularly metformin and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, may exert disease-modifying effects through anti-inflammatory, metabolic and chondroprotective mechanisms. Overall, T2DM and OA should be regarded as interconnected metabolic-inflammatory disorders. Improved understanding of their shared mechanisms may facilitate earlier intervention, therapeutic repurposing and integrated multidisciplinary management strategies to reduce disease burden and improve patient outcomes.

Article.Title: From Chronic Infection to Microbial Imbalance: Rethinking Chronic Rhinosinusitis
Article.Authors: Łabaz J.; Guth M.; Kaleta J.; Kaczmarek J.; Kinczel M.; Kornak K.; Kaczor M.; Leszczyszyn A.; Dorobisz K.; Pazdro-Zastawny K.
Article.Abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) has traditionally been viewed as a chronic inflammatory disease in which microbial factors are implicated. However, increasing evidence suggests that CRS may be better understood as a disruption of sinonasal microbial homeostasis rather than as a chronic infection caused by a single pathogen. This review summarizes current knowledge on healthy sinonasal microbiome composition and function as well as microbial alterations in CRS. Particular attention is given to dysbiosis involving potentially pathogenic microorganisms, including Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, as well as biofilm formation and its interactions with the epithelial barrier and host immune response. We also discuss host-related, therapeutic, hormonal, and environmental factors that may contribute to microbial imbalance. Current evidence does not clearly establish whether dysbiosis is a cause or consequence of chronic inflammation. Based on the evidence synthesized here, we propose that CRS may be understood as a dynamic, bidirectional interaction between microbial imbalance and chronic inflammation, whereby microbial alterations may contribute to epithelial and immune dysregulation, while changes in the host environment influence the sinonasal ecosystem. By integrating these microbiological and host-related perspectives, this review provides a boarder framework for understanding CRS pathophysiology and guiding future research into individual patterns of sinonasal microbial homeostasis.

As a secondary, hypothesis-generating analysis, we simulated histidine protonation of the Cx43 hemichannel as a simplified model of acidic conditions. Cerebral pH was not measured, and the simulations do not explain the sleep-associated Cx43 increase. Article.Authors: Rocha F.; Figueroa-Emiliani J.; Vargas-Castellanos E.
Article.Abstract: Dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS) of the spermatic cord is an exceptionally rare and aggressive malignancy for which diagnostic and therapeutic guidelines remain limited. We report the case of a 73-year-old man who presented with a rapidly enlarging left inguinal/paratesticular mass. Initial ultrasonography showed a 4.3 × 3.0 × 3.7 cm hypoechoic lesion interpreted as suggestive of leiomyoma. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging subsequently demonstrated a 10 × 5 × 5 cm neoplastic mass arising from the spermatic cord. The patient underwent radical left orchiectomy. Histopathological examination revealed a high-grade spindle-cell neoplasm with marked pleomorphism and up to 30 mitoses per 10 high-power fields. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for p16, MDM2, and CDK4, with a Ki-67 proliferative index of 95%, supporting the diagnosis of high-grade DDLPS. Although surgical margins were negative, the disease progressed rapidly. Nineteen days after surgery, the patient developed bilateral pleural effusion, pleural infiltration, pulmonary metastases, and a probable pathological T11 fracture. Because of extensive metastatic disease and clinical deterioration, systemic antineoplastic therapy was not initiated in this advanced setting. The patient died 27 days after hospitalization due to progressive metastatic disease. This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty, aggressive biological behavior, and need for early multidisciplinary management of spermatic cord DDLPS.
