Article.Title: Gammaherpesvirus infection of myeloid cells reveals divergent outcomes regulated by host and viral factors
Article.Authors: Vragel G.; Noell K.; Tseng A.; Kostelecky R.; Alexander E.; Cohen S.; Galvan C.; Dalwadi M.; Gomez B.; Medina E.; Oldenburg D.; Goodspeed A.; Clambey E.; van Dyk L.
Article.Abstract: The gammaherpesviruses establish a lifelong infection, with the cellular outcome of infection intimately regulated by cell type. Myeloid cells are an early infection target characterized by diverse outcomes. To investigate this, we use murine gammaherpesvirus 68 to demonstrate that macrophages are readily infectable, resulting in three divergent infection outcomes dictated by viral and host factors. Infection in vivo and in a cell culture model results in a high frequency of viable cells characterized by restricted viral transcription and unexpected transcription of the ORF75 locus, with rare cells initiating lytic replication. Restricted infection can be fully converted to productive lytic replication by pre-treatment with the host cytokine interleukin 4 (IL-4). Finally, infection with a high viral dose also results in productive infection, but it triggers increased cell death. These studies demonstrate stepwise regulation of virus infection and identify virus and host factors that dictate divergent outcomes in a single cell type.

Article.Title: Chemical modifications to enhance the stability of DNA nanoparticles for biological applications
Article.Authors: Glumm A.; Mathur D.
Article.Abstract: Synthetic DNA nanoparticles offer unique modularity and chemical versatility to build systems for biomedical applications. Extensive research into DNA nanoparticles has led to superior control over loading therapeutic cargo, adding targeting and imaging moieties, and designing desired geometries. One of the main barriers to translating DNA nanoparticles into clinical therapies, however, is their stability in biological environments. Introduction of DNA nanoparticles in biological environments exposes them to various stressors such as nuclease enzymes, depleted salt conditions, and alterations in oxidizing conditions. It is therefore necessary to develop strategies to protect DNA nanoparticles against such stressors to preserve their structural integrity and function. In this review, we highlight dominant chemical modifications that have been optimized to secure DNA nanoparticles against stressors with a focus on biological applications. We provide comprehensive accounts of notable examples from recent results and discuss aspects of DNA nanoparticle stability that require the community's attention.

Article.Title: Gas gill respiration enhances underwater copulation in a water scorpion
Article.Authors: Hyun H.; Tatarnic N.; Han C.
Article.Abstract: To overcome physiological constraints during submergence, many air-breathing aquatic animals utilize an air store. If this store functions as a gas gill for dissolved oxygen uptake, this will extend underwater copulation when atmospheric oxygen is inaccessible. We tested this hypothesis using water scorpion Nepa hoffmanni (Hemiptera: Nepidae). Our field surveys showed that, although N. hoffmanni typically inhabit shallow water, males cannot access atmospheric oxygen via their respiratory siphon during underwater copulation. Laboratory experiments revealed active oxygen use from the air store beneath the wings during submergence. Furthermore, under higher dissolved oxygen treatments, males copulated longer and more frequently, while mate-guarding behavior remained unaffected. These findings provide the first direct evidence that dissolved oxygen uptake via a gas gill enhances copulation efficiency in air-breathing aquatic insects, highlighting the importance of environmental oxygen availability for aquatic reproductive strategies, especially in the context of ongoing climate-driven changes to freshwater ecosystems.

Article.Title: What modern genomes overlook: Ancient DNA rewrites the phylogeography of European atlantic salmon (Salmo salar)
Article.Authors: García-Souto D.; Mallick S.; Barreiro-Docío E.; Rohland N.; Kearns A.; Saura M.; Garcia de Leaniz C.; Straus L.; González Morales M.; Reich D.; Consuegra S.
Article.Abstract: Conservation plans for declining species often rely on contemporary genetic/genomic data to infer historical population structure and evolutionary history of the species. However, modern samples alone may not accurately reflect historical genetic variation, especially after severe population declines or intensive management, and need reference baseline data prior to anthropogenic impact. We analyzed whole-genome sequences dating to 18,800-16,700 years ago from Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), that experienced major declines over the past century. Comparing Paleolithic and modern genomes, we found that ancient salmon from the Iberian glacial refugium were genetically closer to present-day northern European populations than to modern Iberian salmon, consistent with southward displacement of northern lineages during glacial periods, postglacial decline of Iberian populations, and contemporary human impacts. We identified ancient SNPs linked to reproduction and age at maturation in modern salmon populations, while high ancient mitochondrial effective population size suggests greater prehistoric female lineage diversity. These genetic discontinuities between ancient and modern Iberian salmon, not evident in modern samples alone, highlight the value of ancient genomics in conservation.

Article.Title: Acarbose differentially affects gut microbial metabolism of maltose and sucrose, distinctly modulating host metabolism
Article.Authors: Yoshikawa H.; Lee E.; Hatano R.; Taki Y.; Takaya A.; Eguchi A.; Goto Y.; Miyamoto J.; Kimura I.; Tanaka T.; Miki T.
Article.Abstract: Gut microbiota act as beneficial symbionts of the hosts. Administration of α-glucosidase inhibitors (α-GIs) is considered to promote the microbiota's carbohydrate availability, modulating short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production. However, it remains unclear whether host-microbiota interaction differs depending on α-GI types (e.g., acarbose versus miglitol) and carbohydrate types co-administered. In this study, we demonstrate that acarbose is transported through bacterial outer membrane porins, LamB and ScrY, and inhibits maltose metabolism in Escherichia coli. Furthermore, studies using Klebsiella pneumoniae reveal that acarbose suppresses utilization of maltose, but not that of sucrose. When co-administered with acarbose in mice, sucrose, relative to maltose, enhances SCFA production, suppresses glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) secretion, and protects against high-fat diet-induced obesity, underscoring the importance of sucrose as a microbiota-dependent beneficial factor, but not a culprit in host metabolism. In conclusion, acarbose regulates host metabolic processes partly by modulating gut microbial metabolism in a carbohydrate-type-dependent manner.

Article.Title: Optical pulling force in carbon nanotubes: Manifestation of non-local conductivity
Article.Authors: Berghaus T.; Miloh T.; Slepyan G.
Article.Abstract: We develop a new theory of an optical force exerted on a carbon nanotube (CNT) with a non-local conductivity. To determine the optical force, we employ an integral-equation-based approach in terms of the current density. The analysis is constructed for a finite-length cylindrical CNT by rigorously accounting for edge effects. In addition to numerical solutions of the integral equation, we obtain an approximate analytical expression for the optical force acting on the CNT, which shows good agreement with numerical simulations. We also demonstrate the existence of some frequency ranges in which the optical force becomes negative, corresponding to the optical pulling effect. Such a pulling behavior is shown to originate from the non-locality of the conductivity. This work advances theoretical understanding of optomechanical interactions in low-dimensional conductors and clarifies the role of spatial dispersion in the emergence of optical pulling forces.

Article.Title: No practice and still perfect: Different routes for promoting offline gains in perceptual learning
Article.Authors: Kolken Y.; Roberts M.; Naseri P.; De Martino F.; Censor N.; De Weerd P.
Article.Abstract: Visual perceptual learning is thought to require extensive training, but a few reminder trials can sometimes replace daily practice. In a 5-day texture discrimination learning experiment, we showed that both accounts need amendment. Following an initial training session, we found that further skill acquisition can be accomplished either with repeated daily administration of a few reminder trials or by offline learning without any further training, depending on attentional context and task demands. In dual-task conditions involving the simultaneous discrimination of a peripheral texture target and a central fixation target, reminders were as effective as daily training, whereas no learning occurred without reminders. In contrast, in a single-task condition without a fixation task, learning emerged without reminders or training. Hence, attentional context and task demands may determine the ability of reminders or protracted consolidation to yield offline learning gains that are comparable to those delivered by daily training.

Article.Title: AI-driven environmental performance index using deep autoencoders for monitoring sustainable development goals
Article.Authors: Khan A.; Shuangjie L.; Alomair A.; Almusallam N.; Rehman Z.
Article.Abstract: This study develops an autoencoder-based environmental performance index (AE_EPI) to assess environmental performance across 38 countries in five regions. Using a deep autoencoder, AE_EPI captures complex nonlinear relationships in high-dimensional, multi-region data and is benchmarked against a principal component analysis-based index (PCA_EPI). Linear Regression, Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost, combined with SHAP analysis, are used to identify key environmental drivers. Results show that AE_EPI outperforms PCA_EPI in reconstruction accuracy, stability, and robustness to noise, while RF yields the most consistent predictions. Globally, electricity access and renewable energy are the dominant drivers. Regionally, governance and innovation are most important in East Asia; urbanization in South Asia; renewable energy in Central Asia; digitalization in MENA; and economic capacity, electricity access, and governance in Sub-Saharan Africa. These findings support region-specific, data-driven policies that advance energy transitions, strengthen institutional capacity, and address local environmental priorities for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.

Article.Title: Long COVID is associated with lipoxygenase-catalyzed metabolism of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids
Article.Authors: Moss M.; Pons S.; Tavares L.; Tang Y.; Alter G.; Karlson E.; Baden L.; Walt D.; Levy B.
Article.Abstract: Long COVID (LC) represents a failure of healthy resolution mechanisms for inflammation after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Dietary essential polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and their downstream metabolites can orchestrate inflammation resolution, suggesting these pathways may be altered in LC. In this study, plasma samples from two independent participant cohorts totaling 106 participants (designated by chart review as LC or Recovered) were collected longitudinally in the 12 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection and analyzed by mass spectrometry for targeted PUFA metabolites. In the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection, upregulation of PUFA metabolites downstream of 12-lipoxygenase was associated with later development of LC. In the months following infection, LC participants displayed uncoupling of PUFA-related lipid metabolism and altered lipoxygenase-driven metabolism over time compared to recovered participants. These results provide new mechanistic insights for the development of LC and suggest potential therapeutic strategies for this prevalent and debilitating disorder.

Article.Title: Overexpression of endoplasmic reticulum acetyl-CoA transporter AT-1 alters neuronal metabolism, growth, and synaptic activity
Article.Authors: McGregor E.; McGill C.; Arp N.; Clark J.; Baldwin D.; Cui Y.; Nassar A.; Kuang D.; Fernandez-Fuente G.; Choi Y.; Pearson K.; Nagorski J.; Li L.; Simcox J.; Fan J.; Puglielli L.; Anderson R.
Article.Abstract: Acetyl-CoA is a molecule central to cellular metabolic homeostasis. As part of the secretory pathway, acetyl-CoA is imported into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) by a membrane-bound transporter AT-1 (SLC33A1). AT-1 mutations have been linked to peripheral neuropathy, developmental delay with premature death, and intellectual disability with progeria. Here, we show that AT-1 overexpression impacts diverse phenotypes related to neuronal function and plasticity. Differences in ribosomal, synaptic processing, and metabolic pathways were identified at transcriptomic and proteomic levels. Metabolic adaptations included changes in mitochondrial membrane potential, architecture, and respiration, and tracing experiments revealed changes in the fate of glucose favoring glycogen storage over the pentose phosphate pathway. Altered redox was linked to NAD-dependent proteins SIRT1 and CtBP2. Depletion of lipid stores was associated with greater plasticity in fuel substrate utilization. Metabolic adaptation was coincident with decreased synaptic activity, indicating that neuronal communication is coordinated, in part, through acetyl-CoA metabolism.

Article.Title: Phototrophs trade growth for defense through graded regulatory states under escalating oxidative stress
Article.Authors: Johnson Z.; Sadler N.; Garcia M.; Gilliam A.; Hill E.; Li X.; Trejo J.; Qian W.; Cheung M.; Bohutskyi P.
Article.Abstract: Oxygenic phototrophs face a paradox: the reactions powering growth generate oxidative stress, whose damage or costly defense reduces fitness. In Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942, we profiled steady-state growth, photophysiology, and transcription across a dissolved oxygen gradient (0-374% air saturation). Independent component analysis of these transcriptomes within a 407-sample compendium resolved 78 regulatory modules (iModulons) explaining 72.3% of variance. Growth rate followed a graded, sigmoidal dose-response, which we divide into low, moderate, and severe stress regimes (14% and 47% decline, then arrest). Stress-responsive module activities shifted across these regimes: low stress activated SufR and PerR at minimal growth cost; moderate stress modulated three RpaB states, then ManR, CopR, and Rre1; and severe stress triggered a dual-control checkpoint with a fourth RpaB state linking redox sensing to the stringent response and growth arrest. Protein oxidation, pigments, and energy transfer tracked these transitions, suggesting cells trade growth for defense through discrete regulatory states.

Article.Title: PFOS exposure and periodontitis from adolescent burden to genetic and multiomics evidence
Article.Authors: Wan H.; Wang Z.; Peng H.; Wang X.; Xiong L.; Zou X.
Article.Abstract: Periodontitis can develop early in life and may be influenced by persistent environmental exposures. We integrated Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, Mendelian randomization, transcriptomics, machine learning, immune profiling, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and in vitro validation to investigate links between perfluorooctane sulfonate exposure and periodontitis. Periodontal disease burden remained substantial among individuals aged 5-20 years and varied across sociodemographic strata. Genetically predicted PFOS exposure was associated with increased periodontitis risk by inverse-variance weighted Mendelian randomization. Multi-omics analyses identified 151 shared targets enriched in immune-inflammatory pathways and prioritized a ten-gene signature with strong diagnostic discrimination. Single-cell analysis implicated migration inhibitory factor (MIF)-centered immune communication, whereas molecular modeling supported stable PFOS-STK17B interactions. PFOS exposure in human gingival fibroblasts increased expression of the ten prioritized genes. These findings connect population burden with genetic, molecular, and experimental evidence supporting immune-inflammatory mechanisms linking PFOS exposure to periodontitis.

Article.Title: Stathmin 1 regulates mitophagy and non-proliferative cellular function in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells
Article.Authors: Chiquetto L.; Schuetz M.; Dong Q.; Warmka M.; Valin L.; Jones A.; Hunt P.; Petermeier C.; Wang J.; Roundy N.; Greenberg Z.; Yang W.; Zhang C.; Challen G.; Luke C.; Signer R.; Beatty W.; Sykes S.; Li W.; Kast D.; Schuettpelz L.
Article.Abstract: Stathmin 1 is a cytoplasmic phosphoprotein that regulates microtubule dynamics. Stathmin 1 expression is a feature of proliferating cells, and it is overexpressed in many cancers, including leukemias. In contrast to its roles in proliferating cells, considerably less is known of stathmin 1 in quiescent cells. Importantly, stathmin 1 is highly expressed in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), and herein we found that stathmin 1 loss is associated with altered microtubule architecture and markedly impaired HSPC function. Transcriptomic studies suggested metabolic differences in Stmn1 -/- HSPCs, and further mechanistic studies revealed defective mitochondrial structure and function. Microtubules facilitate autophagosome formation and mitophagy, and indeed we found that this critical mitochondrial quality control process is impaired in Stmn1 -/- HSPCs. Finally, stimulation of autophagy improved Stmn1 -/- HSPC colony-forming ability. Together, these data identify a non-proliferative role for stathmin 1 in the regulation of HSPC mitochondrial quality control and cellular function.

Article.Title: Breast cancer burden risk attribution and productivity loss in Chinese women aged 25 to 49
Article.Authors: Bai Y.; Zhang J.; Tian T.; Wang K.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer among Chinese women aged 25-49 years has substantial clinical and societal consequences. We integrated Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates for 1990-2023 with Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2022, United Nations population projections, International Labour Organization labour-force participation, and World Bank indicators. Incident cases rose from 50,064 to 87,221, while the weighted death rate declined from 9.25 to 4.72 per 100,000. Demographic changes explained 63.0% of additional cases. In exploratory extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) analyses interpreted with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), the fasting-plasma-glucose-related population attributable fraction (PAF) ranked first in several formulations but weakened after removing age and temporal structure; the selected high-body-mass-index (BMI) PAF series was constant at zero and unrankable. Potential mortality-related productivity loss was US$6.161 billion in 2023. Article.Title: The carbon neutrality effect of green fiscal stimulus policy: City-level insights from the decarbonization-greenization nexus
Article.Authors: Cheng S.; Wang K.; Chen X.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Growing evidence from decarbonization practices suggests that carbon neutrality requires policies that curb emissions and strengthen carbon sequestration. However, the nexus of decarbonization policies on carbon reduction and carbon sequestration remains underexplored. Based on China's comprehensive fiscal policy pilot for energy conservation and emissions reduction, this study develops a decarbonization-greenization nexus efficiency indicator to measure the prefecture-level carbon neutrality effect and provides the first assessment of green fiscal stimulus policy (GFSP) from this perspective. The results show that GFSP has a positive carbon neutrality effect. Through annual and final evaluations, the policy generates discontinuous effects. By linking performance evaluation to incentive funding, GFSP enhances government and public green attention, thereby contributing to carbon neutrality. Additionally, the policy produces composite effects with new energy, national forest, and carbon trading pilots, whereas no significant composite effect is observed with the low-carbon pilot. Finally, differentiated optimization strategies are proposed for pilot cities.

Plasmopara viticola, the causal agent of grapevine downy mildew, provides a model to address this question. Using β-tubulin sequences and whole-genome data, we reconstructed its invasion history and adaptation in China. Our analyses support a North American ancestral origin of Chinese P. viticola, while demographic modeling and ABBA-BABA tests indicate historical connections between Chinese and European-related lineages, suggesting a complex invasion history. Article.Title: β motifs and molecular flux promote fibril growth at condensate interfaces
Article.Authors: Biswas S.; Potoyan D.
Article.Abstract: Biomolecular condensates can age into gel-like or solid-like states, and their interfaces can promote amyloid fibril formation. Yet the physical principles selecting distinct interfacial aging pathways remain unclear. Here, we develop flux-driven molecular dynamics (FD-MD), a coarse-grained framework to disentangle the roles of rigid β-prone motifs, hydrophobic sequence patterning and molecular deposition rate. We show that rigid motifs can sustain orientational order that converts interfacial adsorption into directional fibrillar growth, whereas flexible chains form spreading surface aggregates. Furthermore for fixed molecular architecture, changing the rate and manner of molecular delivery redirects assembly between lateral spreading, outward fibrillar growth, and bridging between opposing interfaces. Counterinutively, stronger initial drift toward the interface accelerates surface coverage but slows axial fibril elongation, consistent with competition between interfacial accumulation, orientational ordering and outward growth. Molecular architecture thus provides the capacity for directional assembly, while molecular supply selects it morphological outcome. Our findings provide a minimal physical framework for distinct condensate-aging pathwasy and suggest routes to redirect aging through molecular delivery and tuning of interfacial properties of condensates.

Article.Abstract: Kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC) carries substantial clinical challenges. Article.Title: EGaIn-based thermal management for high heat flux electronics
Article.Authors: Joung J.; Na H.; Yoon S.; Jeong Y.; Lee M.; Majidi C.; Kim H.
Article.Abstract: The increasing power density of modern electronic systems makes efficient thermal management essential for maintaining device performance, reliability, and operational lifetime. Among emerging thermal management materials, eutectic gallium-indium (EGaIn) has attracted attention because it uniquely combines metallic thermal conductivity with room-temperature fluidity, enabling efficient heat transfer and conformal contact with interfaces. In this review, we examine EGaIn as an adaptive thermal management platform and connect its material properties with the thermal functions they enable, their implementation in cooling systems, and the associated engineering challenges. We discuss challenges including oxidation, leakage, corrosion, electrical insulation, and long-term reliability, together with engineering strategies to address them. Finally, we provide perspectives for developing reliable EGaIn-based thermal management technologies for next-generation electronic and energy systems.

Article.Abstract: Neural oscillations support cognition and perception by organizing information across oscillatory cycles. Article.Authors: Lee H.; Frazel P.; Singer-Freeman E.; Cavanagh A.; Shin H.; Rice K.; Selvaraj S.; Alu M.; Kim H.; Loomis C.; Liddelow S.; Baek M.; Dasen J.

Article.Title: Migraine burden inequities and 2050 projections in Africa based on global burden of disease 2023

Article.Title: Bridging soil resistome and clinical inference: A four-tier evidentiary framework

Article.Abstract: Soils support a varied range of microbial communities and are important repositories of antimicrobial resistance genes. Nevertheless, discovery alone does not indicate activity, transferability, exposure, or clinical relevance. This review contends that better clinical inference requires tying presence-based signals to function, mobility, and exposure routes, rather than just increasing survey volume. We offer a four-tiered evidentiary paradigm that distinguishes between detection, functional or expression-based evidence, mobile genetic element context, and exposure-linked evidence in environmental, animal, and human compartments. Article.Title: Antibiotic resistance genes in aquaculture: Molecular detection, environmental dynamics, and biological control strategies
Article.Authors: Loveymi H.; Roomiani L.; Tadayoni M.
Article.Abstract: Antibiotic resistance in aquaculture is a major threat to sustainable fish production and global public health. Article.Title: Senescence and tumor immunology: A multifaceted interplay of influence
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Zhang J.; Wang S.; Rao D.; Zhang J.; Ao Y.
Article.Abstract: Medical advances and global population aging have propelled aging and cancer research into a new period of discovery. Article.Title: A hierarchical framework of representational emergence: From feature binding to supramodal emergence
Article.Authors: Paraskevopoulos E.; Bamidis P.
Article.Abstract: Multisensory integration is traditionally conceptualized as transient, stimulus-driven feature binding. Drawing on recent mammalian evidence for cross-modal associative memory neurons and experience-dependent network reorganization, this framework proposes how local synaptic selection may scale into increasingly autonomous cognitive modules. Article.Abstract: Climate change challenges many species. To persist, species can shift ranges, respond plastically, and adapt, which all require variation. Article.Title: A machine learning classifier reveals hidden rare biallelic heterozygous variants in the coding regions of Meniere disease genome
Article.Authors: Mohseni S.; Khan M.; Cruz-Granados P.; Bagheri-Lotfabad K.; Beheshti A.; Lopez-Escamez J.
Article.Abstract: Meniere disease (MD) is a rare inner ear disorder with a significant genetic contribution. We developed the MD classifier, an ML tool to distinguish familial from sporadic MD cases using rare variants in coding regions. We have generated a disease-specific gene variant score incorporating gene, variant, and disease-specific features. A gradient boosting classifier achieved the highest performance, with a test AUC of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.702-0.948) and an accuracy of 81.5%. Reclassification of sporadic cases into the familial group ranged from 16.6% to 28.3%. The model identified a burden of biallelic heterozygous variants suggesting hidden recessive inheritance that may affect up to 38% of MD patients. Gene-enrichment analysis using major classifier features revealed distinct biological pathways between familial and sporadic MD. This ML-based framework integrates unique genetic features that may improve the diagnostic yield of rare disorders and is universally applicable to conditions with both familial and sporadic phenotypes, enabling the identification of compound heterozygous recessive inheritance.

Article.Title: Cortical substrates of perceptual confusion between pitch and timbre
Article.Authors: Ou Y.; Allen E.; Kay K.; Oxenham A.
Article.Abstract: Pitch and timbre, two fundamental perceptual attributes of sound, are critical for both speech and music. Although governed by different acoustic parameters, pitch, and brightness (one of the primary dimensions of timbre) can be perceptually confused. Here, we identify potential neural substrates of this well-known illusion by independently manipulating pitch and brightness while measuring fMRI responses. First, we show that the preferred pitch of individual voxels within auditory cortex decreases systematically as stimulus brightness increases, and vice versa, consistent with predictions from perceptual confusion. Second, we demonstrate that pitch and brightness share a common tuning gradient across auditory cortex, implying a shared trajectory of cortical activation for changes in each dimension. The pattern of results at both local and global cortical levels are consistent with the principle of efficient coding, with the brain exploiting correlations between pitch and brightness in natural sounds via a shared neural code.

Article.Title: Biomechanics-guided computational design of virtual terrestrial vertebrate morphogenesis
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Feng X.; Xu X.
Article.Abstract: To date, experimental development biology still faces challenges to efficiently model the morphogenesis of cross-species vertebrates, spanning from the embryonic development to postnatal growth. No effective computational methods are yet available to reproduce this complex and long-term process. However, recent advancements in large-scale computation and multi-voxel assembly theory have created unprecedented opportunities for establishing a virtual platform to simulate these morphomechanical processes. In this context, we propose a spatiotemporal topological evolution (STTE) method that can investigate the morphogenesis and postnatal growth of three-dimensional multi-voxel virtual embryoids. In this model, the optimization goal is to achieve extensive motion capabilities for the heads of virtual organisms in the vertical direction, thereby facilitating the formation and maintenance of conserved morphological structures characteristic of vertebrates. This proposed theory can rapidly and massively generate digital vertebrates with diverse adult body shapes, and this virtual morphogenesis pipeline offers novel perspectives and technologies for developmental biology.

Article.Title: Condensin upregulation induces intestinal stem cell senescence, driving cell death and increased intestinal permeability
Article.Authors: Khan A.; Ray G.; Musich R.; Selmi I.; Gjojdeshi A.; Talley M.; Oliver J.; Bashaar A.; Rayan C.; Fulmer C.; Peterson J.; Bai I.; West G.; Johnson E.; McDonald C.; Rieder F.; Longworth M.
Article.Abstract: Intestinal stem cell maintenance ensures the integrity of the continuously renewing intestinal barrier, promotes repair, and prevents immune cell activation in the underlying tissue. Intestinal barrier defects contribute to the development of Crohn's disease (CD), a type of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We show that expression of subunits of the genome-organizing complexes, condensins, is upregulated in intestinal epithelial cells of patients with ileal CD. Using cultured intestinal epithelial cell lines and the in vivo model of Drosophila melanogaster, we show that overexpression of condensin proteins rearranges heterochromatin and induces senescence of intestinal stem cells, which leads to cell death in both stem and non-stem cells. In Drosophila, this increases intestinal permeability. These findings suggest that restriction of condensin expression maintains ileal stem cell homeostasis, providing support for future mechanistic exploration of pathologic roles for condensins and senescent stem cells in CD and other diseases involving intestinal barrier dysfunction.

Article.Title: Distinct neural oscillatory patterns underlying music-evoked emotions: Evidence from MEG and subjective reports
Article.Authors: Espino-Payá A.; Prantner S.; Chalas N.; Wollbrink A.; Gross J.; Pastor M.; Fuentes-Sánchez N.; Junghöfer M.
Article.Abstract: Music has a powerful capacity to evoke emotional responses. This study explored the neural and subjective correlates of pleasant and unpleasant emotions elicited by music. 30 volunteers (15 women) listened to 60 film musical excerpts (30 unpleasant and 30 pleasant) from the Film Music Stimulus Set (FMSS) while their neural activity was recorded using magnetoencephalography (MEG). Participants gave self-reports of hedonic valence, emotional arousal, happiness, fear, and musical preference on nine-point Likert scales. Results showed that pleasant music was evaluated as more pleasant, happier, and preferred compared to unpleasant music, which was rated as more arousing and as evoking higher levels of fear. Neural activity revealed greater source-level oscillatory power for pleasant music in theta and beta frequency bands, with distinct regional patterns in the brain. These findings enhance understanding of music-induced emotions and suggest potential clinical applications for treating mood disorders and emotional dysregulation.

Article.Title: Low-frequency parasitized cells in bone marrow alter myelopoiesis following immunization with the live attenuated Leishmania major Cen−/− vaccine
Article.Authors: Azodi N.; Pacheco-Fernandez T.; Klenow L.; Markle H.; Tirrell N.; Murray A.; Brino M.; Kumar S.; Acharyya N.; Silberstein E.; Satoskar A.; Karaiskos S.; Nakhasi H.; Gannavaram S.
Article.Abstract: Leishmaniasis lacks an effective vaccine. We developed a live-attenuated Leishmania major Centrin-deficient strain (LmCen -/-) that is safe and protective in murine and canine models through IFN-γ-producing effector T cells. Because persistent low-level infection supports durable immunity, we investigated latent parasites and immune remodeling in the bone marrow. Dual single-cell RNA sequencing detected parasitized bone marrow cells 28 days after intradermal inoculation with either virulent LmWT or attenuated LmCen -/-. Flow cytometry showed increased myelopoiesis following LmCen -/- immunization compared with LmWT infection. Cell-cell communication analysis implicated enhanced granulin-Sort3 signaling as a potential driver of this response. Bone marrow monocytes from LmCen -/--immunized mice efficiently cleared virulent LmWT parasites in co-culture, consistent with the induction of trained innate immunity. These findings identify the bone marrow as an active site of anti-Leishmania immune programming and suggest that LmCen -/- vaccination promotes durable protection through coordinated adaptive and innate mechanisms.

Article.Title: Single-cell-resolved dynamic immune remodeling following Omicron infection and recovery in vaccinated individuals
Article.Authors: Khare K.; Kumar S.; Chattopadhyay P.; Halder S.; Bano M.; Gupta A.; Patel A.; Soni J.; Tarai B.; Budhiraja S.; Pandey R.
Article.Abstract: Breakthrough SARS-CoV-2 Omicron infections occur despite vaccination, yet post-infection immune recovery remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic and targeted proteomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy individuals and vaccinated patients during infection, early recovery, and 3-month post-recovery. Omicron infection induced coordinated immune remodeling with contraction of T and B cell compartments; expansion of plasma, regulatory T, and dendritic cells; and suppression of inflammatory and metabolic pathways, including TNFα-NF-κB and mTORC1 signaling. Innate populations rebounded rapidly, whereas adaptive compartments recovered slowly with sustained suppression of IL-2, IL-12, and IL-15 modules. Chemokine surges (CXCL1, CXCL5, and CXCL8) resolved during convalescence, whereas selective cytokines (CCL5 and CCL8) and interleukins (IL-6, IL-18, and IL-24) persisted. Trajectory analysis revealed non-uniform remodeling of T cell states with persistent differentiation signatures across naive, effector, and memory compartments. Overall, vaccination tempered early immune collapse and accelerated innate rebound, highlighting interleukin-linked checkpoints and metabolic regulation underlying post-vaccination immune resilience.

Article.Title: Avoiding spiders: Affective context shapes tactile sensitivity during movement
Article.Authors: Arikan B.; McManus M.; Fiehler K.
Article.Abstract: Tactile sensitivity is typically reduced during voluntary movements, a phenomenon known as tactile suppression. While affective context is known to modulate tactile processing, it remains unclear how it influences tactile suppression. In a virtual reality (VR) environment, we investigated tactile sensitivity during movements to avoid threatening (spider) or approach non-threatening (rabbit) stimulus, involving arm flexion or extension and during the limb at rest (baseline). Tactile sensitivity was measured using brief vibrations delivered through the VR controller. Detection thresholds were higher during movement than at baseline, confirming tactile suppression. Both affective context and movement type modulated suppression: avoiding threatening stimulus and extending the arm, each increased suppression. A control experiment using neutral, geometric objects showed similar tactile sensitivity for arm extension and flexion. These findings demonstrate that affective context shapes tactile suppression during movement.

Article.Title: Deep TMS modulates neurovascular responses and enhances dual-task computation in healthy adults
Article.Authors: Zeng B.; Wang W.; Ding Z.; Wang C.; Li C.; Yuan R.; Zhou B.; Zhu Y.
Article.Abstract: Dual-task performance requires coordination between cognitive control and motor systems. This study examined how deep transcranial magnetic stimulation (DTMS) influences cortical responses and computational performance during dual-task processing. In a randomized crossover study, 19 healthy adults underwent DTMS targeting the bilateral prefrontal cortex and anterior cingulate cortex and sham stimulation in separate sessions, with functional near-infrared spectroscopy and dual-task assessments performed before and after each intervention. Compared with sham stimulation, DTMS increased task-related cortical activation in regions involved in cognitive-motor processing and improved computation number without affecting accuracy. Activation changes involving the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, secondary motor cortex, and language-related regions were associated with dual-task performance. These findings suggest that DTMS may modulate distributed cortical dynamics supporting cognitive-motor coordination and inform its potential application in populations with cognitive-motor impairments.

Article.Title: Epigenetic age acceleration enhances prediction of overall survival in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer
Article.Authors: Gandara I.; Du M.; Li Y.; Su L.; Kothari J.; Lanuti M.; Gainor J.; Christiani D.
Article.Abstract: Epigenetic age, influenced by environmental factors like smoking, predicts mortality in general populations but remains under-explored in early-stage lung cancer. We analyzed blood DNA methylation from 75 Boston Lung Cancer Study participants with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), of whom 63 died during follow-up. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was estimated using Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, and GrimAge2 clocks and assessed using Cox models and random survival forests (RSFs). Across clocks, EAA significantly predicted survival in early-stage NSCLC. GrimAge2 EAA achieved the highest predictive accuracy (C index = 0.73±0.04) and emerged as the dominant predictor of survival among RSF models (variable importance = 5.7%), surpassing smoking and age. GrimAge2 EAA showed a non-linear association with mortality in which current smokers had >10% higher predicted mortality risk than former or never smokers at equivalent EAA, a pattern confirmed in Kaplan-Meier analyses. GrimAge2 EAA is a promising biomarker for personalizing risk stratification alongside traditional clinical factors.

Article.Title: Single-cell dissection of self-derived versus donor-derived T cell exhaustion niches in patients with acute myeloid leukemia
Article.Authors: Yu C.; Chen Y.; Zhang X.; Xu L.; Wang Y.; Chen H.; Chen Y.; Wang F.; Sun Y.; Zhang Y.; Lv M.; Mo X.; Cheng Y.; Liu K.; Zhao X.; Sun X.; Zhao X.; Huang X.; Chang Y.
Article.Abstract: Relapse remains the main cause of death in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and T cell exhaustion is related to relapse in both non-allografting and allografting settings. However, differences in exhausted T cells (Tex) across different disease contexts remain incompletely understood. We performed single-cell RNA and T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing to systematically characterize Tex in AML. Both self-derived Tex in non-transplantation and donor-derived Tex in post-transplant settings express similar surface markers, but NFATC1/NFATC3 with downstream TOX and EOMES are enriched in self-derived Tex, while NFATC2 with downstream NR4A2 predominates in donor-derived Tex. Both self-derived and donor-derived bone marrow environments are enriched with immunosuppressive monocytes, dendritic cells, and regulatory T cells. Cell-cell interaction analysis reveals strong direct and indirect interactions between Tex and AML cells, primarily mediated by galectin-9, MIF, and TGF-β1. These findings highlight differences and commonalities between self-derived and donor-derived Tex and identify potential therapeutic targets for reversing Tex in AML.

Article.Title: GClnc1 as an emerging oncogenic regulator with mechanistic insights and clinical implications in human cancers
Article.Authors: Dong Q.; He Y.; Yu R.; Gong X.; Li J.; Liu F.
Article.Abstract: Gastric cancer-related long non-coding RNA1 (GClnc1) is an emerging oncogenic regulator in multiple malignancies, including gastric, colorectal, ovarian, and bladder cancers, as well as osteosarcoma. It promotes proliferation, inhibits apoptosis, and enhances drug resistance and metastasis. Mechanistically, GClnc1 dysregulates key cancer-related regulators and pathways, such as p53, MYC, NF-κB, and the SIRT3/SOD2 axis. Clinically, GClnc1 shows diagnostic and prognostic potential across cancers, with aberrant expression in tissues and altered circulating levels. Notably, exosomal GClnc1 serves as a circulating biomarker for early gastric cancer detection and predicts response to fluorouracil-based chemotherapy. This review summarizes current evidence on GClnc1's regulatory mechanisms and discusses its translational applications. GClnc1 may serve as a multi-cancer biomarker and a promising therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Enhancing cervical squamous cell carcinoma diagnosis under distribution shift via domain-adaptive representation learning
Article.Authors: Huang Z.; Liu Y.; Jin S.; Wang Y.; Fu M.; Ouyang J.; Yu D.; Zhu T.; Zeng F.; Pan X.; Ye J.; Wang J.; He X.; Cheng X.; Zhao M.; He Y.; Zhang H.; Hu B.
Article.Abstract: Summary: Automated whole-slide image (WSI) analysis for cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) is challenged by limited pathological specificity in general models and poor cross-center generalization. We propose CSCC-PAG (pre-training, adaptation, generalization), a framework integrating domain-specific pre-training with self-supervised domain adaptation. Utilizing 8,041 CSCC WSIs, we applied the self-supervised pre-training for CSCC (SPC) feature extractor, which significantly outperforms pan-cancer baselines in the typing, grading, and segmentation tasks. To address domain shift, we developed representative sample domain adaptation (RSDA), combining masked autoencoders (MAEs) with a k -means buffer strategy for label-free adaptation. The results demonstrate that SPC captures fine-grained CSCC morphology, while RSDA effectively recovers performance degradation across centers without requiring target-domain annotations. This study provides a comprehensive solution for automated CSCC diagnosis, covering the entire pipeline from large-scale pre-training to few-shot generalized deployment, demonstrating its immense potential for real-world clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Microbiome-dependent phytosterol sulfates production and tissue distribution in mice
Article.Authors: Tomita K.; Nakano T.; Morozumi S.; Okahashi N.; Arita M.
Article.Abstract: Microbial biotransformation of dietary lipids, such as cholesterol, influences host homeostasis. Despite extensive studies on animal sterols in host-microbiota interactions, the role of phytosterols in homeostasis remains unclear. In this study, we characterized phytosterol sulfates as microbiota-derived metabolites using untargeted lipidomic data mining. The levels of sitosterol sulfate (SIS), campesterol sulfate, and stigmasterol sulfate, the three major phytosterol sulfates, along with coprostanol sulfate, were reduced in the feces of germ-free mice compared with those of specific pathogen-free mice. We characterized a series of Bacteroidota species and their sterol sulfotransferases that produced phytosterol sulfates more efficiently than mammalian enzymes. Furthermore, SIS significantly accumulated in host tissues in a microbiota- and age-dependent manner, whereas unconjugated phytosterols were mostly undetectable. Our work provides insights into host-microbiome interactions via gut bacterial phytosterol metabolism.

Article.Title: Dual roles of AXIN1 as a β-catenin p-S60-dependent cytokinesis machinery and an ESCRT component
Article.Authors: Lee N.; Lee N.; Kyun M.; Yu J.; Kim S.; Na Y.; Kwon T.; Cho H.; Lim K.; Lee K.
Article.Abstract: AXIN1 functions as a scaffolding protein in several signaling pathways, including TGF-β, SAPK/JNK, and Wnt; however, as there have been no reports on the function of AXIN1 in cytokinesis, we investigated this link to determine if this scaffold coordinates cell division. Here, we demonstrate that AXIN1 is located in the central dark zone of the intercellular bridge, known as the Flemming body, where it forms a midbody ring structure. We also demonstrated that AXIN1 functions in coordination with β-catenin p-S60-dependent cytokinetic machinery during early telophase. Furthermore, AXIN1 regulates the hierarchy of the ESCRT complex by positioning itself between MKLP1 and CEP55 in late telophase cells. Based on our findings, we propose that AXIN1 has dual functions in cytokinesis by facilitating ECT2 recruitment during early telophase and promoting recruitment of abscission components during late telophase, highlighting the transformative role of this signaling scaffold as structural machinery in coordinating cell division.

Article.Title: Integrative genomics and experimental validation identify a mechanosensitive gene signature associated with colorectal cancer liver metastasis
Article.Authors: Yang T.; Yuan Y.; Li X.; Wang J.; Li C.; Xu Z.
Article.Abstract: Summary: The mechanical tumor microenvironment critically influences colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and metastasis, yet the underlying molecular mediators remain poorly defined. By integrating single-cell transcriptomics, bulk RNA-seq, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and 117 machine learning algorithms, we identified a six-gene mechanosensitive signature ( SNX7 , SDC1 , CDCP1 , PTGES , EMP2 , and CALB2 ) associated with CRC liver metastasis. This signature demonstrated superior prognostic performance (mean C-index 0.68) across multiple independent cohorts compared to 74 published CRC signatures. Among these genes, SDC1 was consistently upregulated in CRC cells and tissues, and its expression was further induced by increased matrix stiffness in tunable hydrogel culture systems. These findings support a mechanosensitive gene signature with robust prognostic value and identify SDC1 as a stiffness-responsive candidate regulator, providing insights into the mechanobiological regulation of CRC metastasis.

Article.Title: Linking nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal microbiota to immune responses during influenza-like illness in an aging population
Article.Authors: Kool J.; Konstanti P.; van Dijken H.; Chu M.; Nanlohy N.; Bijvank E.; van Woudenbergh E.; van Beek J.; van Baarle D.; Fuentes S.
Article.Abstract: Older adults are vulnerable to influenza-like illness (ILI). To study how infection shapes the respiratory microbiota, we profiled nasopharyngeal (NP) and oropharyngeal (OP) communities alongside local immune mediators in adults aged 60–88, comparing asymptomatic, ILI, and recovery states. NP communities clustered into three community state types (CSTs): Moraxella -dominated (CST-1), Haemophilus/Streptococcus/Staphylococcus -associated (CST-2), and Corynebacterium/Dolosigranulum -dominated (CST-3). During infection, compositional shifts were restricted to the NP niche, where CST-1 and CST-2 were more frequent. Streptococcus, Haemophilus and Moraxella were positively associated with inflammatory and interferon-related mediators, including IL-6, CXCL9 and CXCL10, while Corynebacterium showed negative associations. Immune activation was strong in the NP but limited in the OP, and stayed above healthy levels at follow-up, suggesting incomplete recovery. NP composition was also associated with symptom burden, viral and bacterial co-detection and smoking status. These site-specific microbiota-immune relationships identify the nasopharynx as the primary site of immune modulation during ILI in older adults.

Article.Title: Wearable-derived sleep and circadian features associated with electronic health record-documented persistent postsurgical pain
Article.Authors: Kim R.; Evanski J.; Smith T.; Forger D.; Kaplan C.; Clauw D.; Whibley D.
Article.Abstract: Summary: A substantial percentage of surgical patients develop persistent postsurgical pain, and sleep disruption is an established, modifiable contributor. We examined temporal dynamics linking sleep and circadian rhythms to persistent postsurgical pain, using longitudinal Fitbit and electronic health record (EHR) data from the NIH All of Us Research Program to track sleep and circadian changes preceding EHR documentation of pain beyond expected surgical recovery. Patients later documented with persistent pain showed systematic shifts in wake timing and in heart rate circadian rhythms (elevated amplitude and mesor), with wake timing decoupled from heart rate circadian timing. These changes were absent in a comparison cohort without persistent pain documentation, indicating specificity to persistent postsurgical pain rather than a postoperative or clinical-encounter effect. Findings align with evidence linking altered sleep to pain outcomes and identify cardiac circadian disruption as a distinct marker, suggesting wearable-derived features could capture physiological changes before documentation and inform intervention.

Article.Title: S-adenosylmethionine ameliorates spermatogenic dysfunction and sperm DNA damage via transsulfuration pathway
Article.Authors: Deng C.; Jin Z.; Wu H.; Fang Z.; Yang Y.; Zhao Q.; Hang J.; Zhang Z.; Jiang H.
Article.Abstract: Summary: Male infertility is a global concern, with high sperm DNA fragmentation linked to oxidative stress. Untargeted metabolomics in 111 men revealed downregulated S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) in patients with high sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI). In vitro experiments demonstrated that SAM supplementation effectively reduced oxidative stress-induced DNA damage of human sperm and restored motility. In vivo , SAM administration in cyclophosphamide-induced oligoasthenozoospermia mice improved testicular structure, sperm quality, and DNA integrity. SAM restored glutathione levels and upregulated the expression of key transsulfuration enzymes, cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) and cystine/glutamate transporter (xCT), thereby enhancing glutathione biosynthesis and mitigating oxidative stress. RNA sequencing and protein analysis further revealed that SAM attenuated the expression of proapoptotic markers caspase-3 and caspase-8 and reduced germ cell apoptosis. These findings suggest that SAM may alleviate spermatogenic dysfunction and DNA damage, an effect that may involve enhancement of the transsulfuration pathway and improved redox homeostasis. This offers mechanistic insights and supports further exploration of its therapeutic potential on male infertility.

Article.Title: Pharmacological AhR activation attenuates airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling in a mixed allergen asthma model
Article.Authors: Reza M.; Balraj P.; Kumar A.; Heyob K.; Walum J.; Britt R.; Sathish V.
Article.Abstract: Summary: Airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling are major features of asthma. We investigated whether pharmacological activation of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) modifies these responses in a mixed allergen (MA) mouse model of asthma. MA exposure increased airway resistance, contractility, inflammation, and remodeling, with elevated AhR expression in whole lung and airway smooth muscle but limited canonical AhR target gene activation. Treatment with the high-affinity AhR agonist 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD) improved lung mechanics, reduced inflammatory cell and cytokine accumulation, attenuated airway remodeling, and decreased airway narrowing in precision-cut lung slices. Bulk lung RNA sequencing further showed suppression of inflammatory, neutrophil-associated, and remodeling pathways following TCDD treatment, together with induction of canonical AhR target genes. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that AhR activation suppresses inflammatory gene networks, limits airway remodeling, and improves airway mechanics in experimental asthma, supporting the therapeutic potential of targeting AhR signaling to mitigate airway dysfunction and structural remodeling.

Article.Authors: Whitman B.; Karimianghadim R.; Auch B.; Liachko I.; Monaghan T.; Pakpour S.; Kao D.
Article.Abstract: Summary: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) effectively prevents recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI). However, the mechanisms underpinning FMT efficacy are incompletely understood. We used proximity-ligation metagenomics, metaproteomics, and metabolomics to profile dynamic changes in rCDI. We analyzed samples collected from the first 7 responders during a clinical trial comparing two donor-based treatments (lyophilized FMT [LFMT] or lyophilized sterile fecal filtrate [LSFF], free of intact microorganisms) to prevent rCDI. LSFF is enriched in Caudoviricetes, lipids, fatty acids, and human and extracellular bacterial proteins compared with LFMT. LFMT recipients had donor microbial engraftment, while LSFF recipients achieved only partial microbial community recovery without donor’s contribution. Our multi-omics analyses identified a functional convergence following both treatments, shifting away from oxidative and antibiotic stress survival pathways toward enhanced carbon-nitrogen utilization pathways, suggesting that FMT mechanisms may involve metabolic reprogramming and host-microbial amino acid co-metabolism. Our findings provide important hypothesis-generating insights that warrant further validation.

Article.Title: Similar degenerative patterns of olfactory receptor genes in the giant panda and marine carnivores
Article.Authors: Kang L.; Chen J.; Hong M.; Wei W.; Xiang Z.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Olfactory receptor (OR) genes constitute the largest mammalian gene family and are critical for olfactory perception and ecological adaptation. OR gene variation is associated with interspecific differences in habitat, diet, and sensory reliance, yet the relative contributions of these ecological factors to OR evolution remain unclear. Here, we systematically analyzed OR repertoires across 25 carnivoran species occupying diverse niches. Marine carnivorans exhibit convergent OR degeneration, with fewer intact genes and ancestral orthologs, higher pseudogene ratios, and relaxed purifying selection compared with terrestrial species. Notably, bamboo-specialized giant pandas display identical degenerative signatures, possessing the smallest intact OR repertoire and most lost ancestral OR groups among terrestrial carnivorans. Our models show habitat primarily shapes intact OR quantity, while dietary specialization governs pseudogenization and selective constraints. These findings reveal convergent OR functional decay under aquatic adaptation and extreme dietary specialization, illustrating complex links between lifestyle and chemosensory genome evolution in mammals.

Article.Title: H3K18 lactylation promotes Treg/Th17 imbalance via PTPRM-STAT3 axis in hepatocellular carcinoma
Article.Authors: Yi J.; Chen Z.; Zhu H.; Liang R.; Guan J.; Qiu Y.; Zhou B.; Wu H.; Yu X.; Zou S.; Wang K.; Hu Z.
Article.Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits elevated lactate levels and Treg/Th17 imbalance, but underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Western blot revealed significantly elevated histone lactylation in HCC PBMCs, with H3K18la showing the most pronounced increase. Genome-wide H3K18la profiling by CUT&Tag identified global epigenetic reprogramming at immune-related loci. Integrating epigenomic and transcriptomic data revealed PTPRM as a key gene with enhanced H3K18la enrichment and elevated expression. H3K18la enrichment at the PTPRM locus was significantly increased in HCC samples compared with controls, whereas treatment with the LDHA inhibitor oxamate markedly reduced this enrichment. PTPRM knockdown decreased Tregs, increased Th17 cells, and promoted STAT3 Y705 phosphorylation in vitro and in a murine HCC model. Article.Authors: Diao J.; Han X.; Du H.; Wu J.; Jia J.; Zhang Z.; Rahman M.; Shu M.
Article.Abstract: Keloids are benign dermal tumors, and keloid fibroblasts (KFs) play a critical role in their formation through hyperproliferation. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis revealed that CD147 played an important regulatory role in controlling the cell cycle of KFs, and centromere protein F (CENPF) expression was substantially downregulated following CD147 inhibition. Furthermore, CENPF knockdown attenuated the proliferation-inducing effects of CD147 in KFs, potentially promoting cell apoptosis via the p53 signaling pathway. Article.Title: A linear calibration method for scattering semiconductors using the Kubelka-Munk function
Article.Authors: Zhao S.; Luo L.; Zhang F.; Jiang B.; Jaroniec M.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Absorption spectroscopy of solids is hindered by strong scattering, which violates assumptions underlying the Beer-Lambert (BL) law. Although calibration approaches have been reported for scattering solids, their mechanistic basis in terms of the absorption and scattering coefficients remains unclear, and their applicability to semiconductors has not been well documented. Here, we measured ultraviolet-visible diffuse reflectance spectra for nine inorganic semiconductors. From reflectance, we calculated pseudo-absorbance and the Kubelka-Munk function (KMF). The results show that absorbance departs from BL linearity but is well described by an expression derived from KMF with mixture additivity of the coefficients. In contrast, KMF increases linearly with mass fraction within a low-loading regime, and the relation persists across distinct morphologies. Compositions of mixtures recovered from KMF agree closely with preparation values. This work underscores a simple, rapid, and non-destructive calibration strategy for scattering semiconductors that uses KMF as a linear axis for composition.

Article.Authors: Yamamoto Y.; Ohno R.; Shoda K.; Suzuki T.; Momoi K.; Fujii S.; Kenmochi Y.; Yoshikawa T.; Shimomura M.; Tsukamoto N.; Ohnuki K.; Tani H.; Soma Y.; Fukuda K.; Nakatsura T.; Tohyama S.

Article.Abstract: A single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) of the alpha5 subunit of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) increases human risk for nicotine dependence, alcohol use disorders (AUDs), and schizophrenia. Article.Title: “Locking” CDK9 inhibition by activating integrator function in HIV transcription
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Zapatero-Belinchón F.; Geleziunas P.; Ott M.
Article.Abstract: The positive transcription elongation factor b (P-TEFb) is a critical host factor for HIV transcription, yet pharmacological inhibition of its CDK9 subunit yields transient suppression with cytotoxicity. The drug combination's HIV-inhibiting effect is somewhat resistant against elevated HIV activity in the presence of cocaine or morphine. Article.Title: Lactate-driven histone lactylation by AARS1 promotes pulmonary arterial hypertension
Article.Authors: Chen Z.; Cai Z.; Lin Y.; Chen A.; Cao R.; Yu L.; Cai K.; Lian G.; Xie L.
Article.Abstract: Glycolytic reprogramming drives lactate accumulation in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). H3K18la was enriched at the Ctnnb1 promoter and correlated with enhanced Ctnnb1 transcription. These findings suggest that lactate may act as an epigenetic signal, linking glycolysis to Ctnnb1 activation through AARS1-associated H3K18la, thereby offering a potential target for PAH treatment.

Article.Title: LPS and quorum sensing protect Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteria from phagocytosis and destruction by Dictyostelium discoideum amoebae
Article.Authors: Ayadi I.; Pain E.; Oddy J.; Lamrabet O.; Vijay H.; Koehler T.; Distler T.; Persat A.; Munoz-Ruiz R.; Cosson P.
Article.Abstract: Free-living amoebae like Dictyostelium discoideum and environmental bacteria like Pseudomonas aeruginosa are engaged in complex predator-prey interactions. Article.Authors: Wang D.; Di X.; Gao F.; Li G.; Lin L.; He S.; Zhang D.; Xu J.; Jin Y.; Liang Y.; Cecchini M.; Lacy J.; Kunstman J.; Kunz P.; Du J.; Liu Y.

Article.Authors: Yang H.; Huang C.; Wang H.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) has a high mortality rate, creating an urgent need to identify novel therapeutic targets. Article.Title: StrokeTime: A comprehensive longitudinal scRNA-seq atlas of the ischemic mouse brain
Article.Authors: Anrather J.; Garcia-Bonilla L.
Article.Abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers profound, dynamic changes in the brain's cellular landscape. To systematically characterize these dynamics, we integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data from 21 mouse stroke studies (103 samples; 414,359 cells) spanning multiple models and post-stroke intervals. The atlas contains 17 major cell classes and 120 fine-grained transcriptional states within myeloid, lymphoid, vascular, epithelial, neuronal, and glial populations. Myeloid cells showed the greatest plasticity, including disease-associated microglia/macrophage programs shared across resident and infiltrating cells, whereas lymphocytes featured activation and regulatory signatures within lineage constraints. Vascular and mural cells shifted from early inflammatory and barrier-disruptive programs to later fibrotic and angiogenic states. Article.Authors: Xu H.; Gu R.; Serville Torvund A.; Grønlien I.; Xomalis A.; Nguyen H.; Yu Z.; Zhao Z.
Article.Abstract: In clinical oncology, label-free identification of colorectal tumor-associated fibroblast (CAF) subtypes is challenging. Similarly, for EIT modes, when light is polarized along the orthogonal polarization, myCAFs result in a frequency red-shift while apCAFs result in blueshift. To validate our results, we conducted flow cytometry and gene expression analyses that confirmed distinct hallmarks of myCAFs and apCAFs, consistent with the resonance frequency shifts observed in THz metasurface measurements. Article.Authors: Lingemann M.; McGee T.; Sidoti Migliore G.; DeLuca J.; Whitehead S.; Bonsignori M.

Finally, DH1017.IgM confirmed inhibition of ADE at sub-neutralizing concentrations in sera of ZIKV-infected individuals. Article.Abstract: Working memory (WM) enables us to maintain and directly manipulate mental representations, yet we know little about the neural implementation of this privileged online format. Article.Authors: Li H.; Zhao L.; Xu S.; Tang S.; Lin J.; Hu Y.; Chen X.; Lu C.; Chen D.
Article.Abstract: Bronchiolitis obliterans (BO) represents a major complication limiting long-term survival after lung transplantation, with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) serving as a core pathogenic mechanism. The TGF-β1 signaling pathway plays a critical role in EMT induction and can activate serum/glucocorticoid-regulated kinase 1 (SGK1) expression. Article.Title: Early-warning signals of critical transitions in global ecoregions
Article.Authors: Hirsch E.; Koren I.
Article.Abstract: Terrestrial ecoregions represent coherent ecological units shaped by shared environmental conditions and biological communities. As ecosystems approach critical transitions, their resilience declines, showing slower recovery from perturbations and increasing temporal autocorrelation. By combining spatial clustering, vegetation trend analysis, and resilience indicators, we identify ecoregions exhibiting both vegetation change and declining resilience. We find that approximately one-quarter of ecoregions, covering over one-third of Earth's land surface, show consistent signals of emerging structural transitions. Many of these occur in regions with low direct human modification, suggesting a strong role for large-scale environmental drivers. The detected patterns reveal increasing internal fragmentation within ecoregions and highlight regions potentially approaching critical transitions. This framework provides a scalable approach for identifying ecosystems at risk and supports targeted monitoring and conservation planning.

Article.Title: Vagal maneuvers and pharmacological cardioversion in stable PSVT: A systematic review with implications for emergency nursing practice
Article.Authors: González-García M.; Carrillo-Franco L.; Morales-Luque C.; Rocha I.; Dawid-Milner M.; López-González M.
Article.Abstract: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT) is a common arrhythmic emergency for which vagal maneuvers offer a non-pharmacological route to cardioversion before drug escalation. This systematic review compared the effectiveness and safety of vagal maneuvers—particularly the standard and modified Valsalva maneuvers—against pharmacological cardioversion in adults with stable PSVT. Following PRISMA 2020 guidance, eleven studies published between 2014 and 2024 were identified across six databases and synthesized narratively owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity. The modified Valsalva maneuver consistently achieved higher cardioversion rates than the standard technique and carotid sinus massage, with a favorable safety profile, while adenosine remained effective but more frequently associated with recurrence and discomfort. Effectiveness varied by age, arrhythmia subtype, and care setting. Collectively, the evidence supports the modified Valsalva maneuver as a safe, low-cost, first-line option before pharmacological escalation, with particular relevance to nurse-led management in emergency and prehospital care.

Article.Title: Greenery or fear: Site use of Himalayan ibex in a predator-dominant landscape
Article.Authors: Ali H.; Sutherland C.; Din J.; Nawaz M.
Article.Abstract: The Himalayan ibex ( Capra sibirica ), a prized trophy and crucial prey species of the snow leopard (Panthera uncia ), has increased in abundance alongside snow leopard populations due to ongoing conservation efforts. However, the behavioral strategies that enable ibex to persist in the predator-rich mountain ecosystems of Pakistan remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we investigated habitat use and co-occurrence patterns of Himalayan ibex and snow leopards by using occupancy modeling. Ibex occupancy was positively associated with rugged terrain and higher elevations and negatively associated with distance from roads. Snow leopards showed a preference for rugged habitats. The co-occurrence of these species was mediated by roads. Ibex avoided snow leopard abundant areas by shifting toward more remote locations to reduce predation risk, whereas snow leopards adaptively track these prey movements. This study suggests that protecting remote, heterogeneous landscapes is essential for sustaining mountain ecosystems and predator-prey dynamics in northern Pakistan.

Article.Title: Periodontitis as a potential contributor to lung cancer: Epidemiological evidence, proposed mechanisms, and clinical implications
Article.Authors: Dong H.; Xin H.
Article.Abstract: Periodontitis has been proposed as a potential contributor to lung cancer (LC), but the epidemiological, mechanistic, and clinical evidence remains heterogeneous. This structured narrative review evaluates the association between periodontitis and LC, the directness of proposed biological mechanisms, and the implications for risk assessment and supportive care. Observational studies generally report positive associations, although effect estimates vary according to periodontal ascertainment, study population, and adjustment for smoking. Clinically assessed periodontitis, self-reported or administrative diagnoses, tooth loss, periodontal-associated microbial markers, and general oral microbiome profiles represent distinct exposure domains and should not be interpreted interchangeably. The absence of a clear association among lifelong never smokers and the lack of supportive Mendelian randomization evidence further limit causal inference. Human studies demonstrate oral-lower airway microbial overlap, while experimental LC models support microbiota-related inflammatory and oncogenic signaling; however, periodontal origin, directional microbial transmission, and a continuous causal pathway from periodontitis to LC have not been established. Clinically, periodontitis should not modify current eligibility for low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening, and oral or respiratory microbiome biomarkers remain investigational. Perioperative oral care has comparatively stronger evidence for reducing postoperative pulmonary infectious complications, but this benefit should not be extrapolated to tumor recurrence or survival. Overall, current evidence supports an observational association and biological plausibility, whereas independent causality and an oncologic benefit of periodontal treatment remain unproven.

Article.Title: Deep protease profiling deconvolutes protease signatures released from activated neutrophils
Article.Authors: Yu E.; Holding M.; Huang R.; Chan A.; Teney C.; Desch K.; Kretz C.
Article.Abstract: Dysregulated protease activity drives the progression of cancer, cardiovascular, and inflammatory diseases. Current substrate-based detection methods lack specificity, breadth, and require prior knowledge of protease content. We have advanced deep protease profiling, through differential enrichment, substrate motif, and deconvolution analyses, to provide comprehensive, unbiased, and scalable characterizations of protease activity. Phage libraries were screened against neutrophil serine proteases or activated neutrophils, and high-throughput sequencing determined cleaved peptides. Cathepsin G, neutrophil elastase, and proteinase 3 (PR3) cleaved 5,985, 5,325, and 1,285 peptides, with substrate recognition motifs that align with natural substrates. Activated neutrophil supernatants cleaved 5,166 peptides, and inhibition of serine proteases caused 95% reduction in signal. Deconvolution algorithms identified protease signatures for elastase, cathepsin G, and PR3 proportional to their levels in neutrophils. This approach enables systematic functional analysis of proteolysis, adaptable across proteases, samples, and scenarios to advance disease understanding, diagnosis, and management.

Article.Title: Regio-specific glycan expression within the mammalian brain and tumors
Article.Authors: Tulin E.; Noel M.; Pepi L.; Florido M.; Muerner L.; Cielen L.; von Gunten S.; Cummings R.
Article.Abstract: The mammalian brain exhibits a complex glycan code that orchestrates neural connectivity, yet the spatial organization of functionally critical modifications of glycoproteins, such as fucosylation and sialylation, remains unclear. Using novel monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) designed for glycan detection, we mapped expression of glycan epitopes with unprecedented sensitivity, revealing non-overlapping expression patterns. Combined with targeted N -/ O -glycan profiling, we found that expression of fucosylated and sialylated glycans occurs in anatomically distinct domains in both murine and human central nervous system (CNS). Key findings include fucosylated O -glycans marking brain endothelial cells, sialylated O-glycans decorating lecticans at the nodes of Ranvier, whereas the accessory olfactory bulb harbors unique fucosylated N -glycans. RNAseq and co-localization studies confirm regio-specific glycosyltransferase activity driving this partitioning. We also found that brain tumors are distinguished by upregulated expression of specific fucosylated/sialylated epitopes compared to normal tissue. The mAb-based approach uncovers regio-specific glycan expression with implications for neurodevelopment and cancer diagnostics.

Article.Authors: Wang A.; Xu X.; Jiang W.; Li B.; Zhu W.; Xiao Q.; Xu L.; Sun J.; Chen K.; Yi Y.; Guo Y.; Qiang X.; He J.; Zhou H.; Lin Y.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: The global antimicrobial-resistance crisis is exacerbated by environmental bacterial reservoirs. This work investigated antibiotic-resistance genes (ARGs) carried by E. coli from 118 surface-water samples across the Taihu Lake watershed. Article.Title: Inhibition of asparagine endopeptidase extends the lifespan and improves health span during aging
Article.Authors: Yang M.; Meng X.; Xie Z.; Wang M.; Qian Z.; Ye K.
Article.Abstract: Asparagine endopeptidase (AEP), also known as legumain, is a lysosomal cysteine protease whose activity increases with age and contributes to age-related tissue dysfunction. We tested whether chronic AEP inhibition could slow aging phenotypes in naturally aged mice. Here, we show that chronic treatment with the AEP inhibitor #11a extended lifespan and improved health span in aged C57BL/6 mice, together with reduced frailty and improved physical and cognitive performance. #11a treatment also attenuated several senescence- and inflammation-associated readouts in multiple organs. Mechanistically, #11a treatment suppressed AEP-dependent cleavage of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), accompanied by an increased NAD + /NADH ratio and higher SIRT1 levels. These findings support further investigation of pharmacological AEP inhibition as a strategy to promote healthy aging.

Article.Title: Chitosan-stabilized electrospun nanofiber dressings with embedded flame-made nanosilver for the treatment of resistant infections
Article.Authors: Ramachandran R.; Geara Semaan J.; Samara M.; Thersleff T.; Fielden M.; Sommar P.; Xu Landén N.; Sotiriou G.
Article.Abstract: Wound healing can be severely compromised by infections, particularly those caused by antibiotic-resistant bacteria such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The 2–10 nm Ag NPs are embedded within ∼200 nm fibers, enabling a high and sustained Ag + ion release with no detectable nanoparticle release, which may help mitigate concerns associated with nanoparticle exposure. Chitosan structurally stabilizes the fibers while modulating swelling and local pH to enhance Ag + diffusion. The dressings achieved >99.9999% bacterial reduction in vitro and up to 99% ex vivo using freshly excised human skin. Crucially, the dressings maintained >90% viability of human keratinocytes and fibroblasts and showed no detectable impairment of short-term wound healing. This study introduces a scalable, safe-by-design nanofiber platform for infection-resistant and healing-compatible wound care and supports its further evaluation in preclinical studies.

Article.Title: A longitudinal study of rotenone-induced Parkinsonism in mice
Article.Authors: Joshi P.; Fan F.; Lou X.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra. Environmental toxins such as rotenone are widely used to model PD pathology and evaluate new drugs in PD; however, the long-term consequences of toxin exposure remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a longitudinal mouse study to examine the onset, progression, and long-term outcomes of rotenone-induced PD-like phenotypes. A 21-day regimen of rotenone (2.5 mg/kg/day, intraperitoneal) produced robust Parkinsonism-like phenotypes by week 4, including impaired locomotion, anxiety-like behaviors, and deficits in motor coordination and learning, accompanied by reduced tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression and loss of TH + neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta. Unexpectedly, these behavioral and neuropathological deficits gradually resolved over time. After 12 months of toxin cessation, rotenone-treated mice exhibited behavioral performance and TH expression levels comparable to untreated controls. These findings reveal a previously underappreciated capacity for adaptive resilience within the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system following toxic injury.

Article.Title: A single arm phase II trial of chidamide plus cisplatin in advanced adenoid cystic carcinoma
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Chen G.; Xue K.; Zhang Q.; Xia Z.; Ji D.; Jin J.; Lv F.; Liu X.; Wang Y.; Hong X.; Cao J.
Article.Abstract: Systemic therapy for recurrent or metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma remains limited, and durable disease control is difficult to achieve. We conducted a prospective, single-arm phase 2 trial of chidamide, a histone deacetylase inhibitor, plus cisplatin in 24 patients with recurrent or metastatic disease. Patients received a short chidamide lead-in followed by combination therapy for up to six cycles. The study did not meet its prespecified objective response target, with a confirmed objective response rate of 13.6% among 22 efficacy-evaluable patients. However, disease control was observed in 86.4% of patients, median progression-free survival was 17.9 months, and median overall survival was 40.3 months. Toxicity was manageable, with no treatment-related deaths. These findings support further evaluation of histone deacetylase inhibitor-platinum strategies as a disease-control approach in this rare cancer, while requiring validation in larger studies.

Article.Title: Wolf-dog hybridization: Population structure confounds genetic assignment and hybrid classification
Article.Authors: Cetkovská E.; Eliášová K.; Šrutová J.; Tkáčová N.; Matějů P.; Jelínková J.; Kutal M.; Vorel A.; Nowak C.; Hulva P.; Černá Bolfíková B.
Article.Abstract: Accurate hybrid detection is increasingly important for conservation, yet genetic assignment can be strongly biased when structured populations are analyzed as if they were homogeneous. Using four years of routine wolf monitoring in Czechia, a Central European contact zone of differentiated lineages, we show that ignoring population structure can inflate admixture and generate false signals of hybridization. Population-specific calibration combined with independent validation resolved ambiguous assignments and provided no evidence for ongoing wolf-dog introgression within the monitored wolf population. Our results demonstrate that population structure must be explicitly considered when interpreting hybridization signals and provide a practical framework for conservation monitoring in other structured wildlife populations.

Article.Authors: Krishnavajhala A.; Gingras M.; Santiago-Rodriguez T.; Chen Y.; Bandaranaike D.; Bhamidipati S.; Qin X.; Kottapalli K.; Momin Z.; Santhanam A.; Walker K.; Wang Q.; Griffin S.; Masternak M.; Ross M.; Muzny D.; Wu J.; Urquieta E.; Gibbs R.; Doddapaneni H.

Article.Authors: Ma J.; Ma T.; Zhang Y.; Wei H.
Article.Abstract: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), a major cause of end-stage renal disease, involves podocyte injury and immune dysregulation. Article.Authors: Hori S.; Hirose Y.; Matsuo-Dapaah J.; Zheng J.; Tsuji T.; Fujita H.; Nanao M.; Tsuji R.
