Article.Authors: Jia H.; Ahmadianfar I.; Karbasi M.; Farooque A.
Article.Abstract: Accurate drought forecasting enables the management and reduction of impacts on water resources and farming systems. Article.Authors: Martorell N.; Medan V.

Although the Tectum is traditionally considered a visual center, its role in integrating auditory and visual danger signals is not fully understood. Notably, the heightened tectal response during multisensory stimulation is strongly correlated with increased activity in hindbrain neurons implicated in escape-like motion events, connecting tectal integration to premotor circuits that drive behavioral output. Article.Title: A randomized crossover study of cardiologist reporting of severe aortic stenosis with/without assistance from artificial intelligence (AI)
Article.Authors: Playford D.; Brescacin D.; Frampton C.; Younis N.; Strange G.
Article.Abstract: Inaccurate echocardiographic diagnosis of severe aortic stenosis (AS) may be improved by AI. A randomised case-control fully-crossed, paired-reader, paired-case (MRMC) study evaluated the performance of AI in assisting cardiologist reporting of severe AS. 200 echos were independently adjudicated by expert cardiologists, 100 with severe AS (cases) and 100 without severe AS (controls). The AI was then applied and correctly classified all (100%) cases of severe AS, and 18 (36%) of moderate AS with signs of cardiac damage. Five independent cardiologists reported all echos according to the MRMC protocol. Without AI, cardiologists frequently misdiagnosed low-gradient severe AS. With AI, AS diagnosis rates were not improved, but AI improved reader concordance, referral for further investigation and reporting time. Cardiologists frequently misdiagnose low gradient severe AS, whereas measurement AI showed excellent accuracy. Lack of improvement in cardiologist accuracy with AI assistance highlights opportunities to improve trust in AI.

Article.Title: Sleep deprivation impairs ventral hippocampus-medial prefrontal connectivity and task learning in rats
Article.Authors: Zheng W.; Geng D.
Article.Abstract: Sleep is essential for memory consolidation, and sleep loss has long been associated with cognitive impairment. However, the circuit-level mechanisms through which sleep deprivation disrupts hippocampal-prefrontal communication during learning remain poorly understood. Here, we combined a T-maze learning task with simultaneous local field potential (LFP) recordings in the ventral hippocampus (vHPC) and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) of rats. Using dynamic causal modeling (DCM), we quantified directional connectivity during task acquisition under normal and sleep-deprived conditions. We found that learning strengthened forward connectivity from vHPC to mPFC while weakening backward connectivity from mPFC to vHPC. Sleep deprivation impaired this forward connectivity, resulting in slower learning and reduced task accuracy. These findings characterize the altered circuit dynamics by which sleep loss disrupts hippocampal-prefrontal circuit dynamics, providing insight into how impaired cross-regional communication may underlie cognitive deficits observed in sleep-related psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders.

Article.Title: NDUFAF2 promotes abdominal aortic aneurysm formation through mitochondrial dysfunction-induced apoptosis
Article.Authors: He H.; Peng J.; Chen H.; Zhang Y.; Zhan S.; Chen L.; Han X.; Yin H.
Article.Abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease closely associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis. Article.Title: Evidence for a sensorimotor prediction in action observation
Article.Authors: Hilt P.; Gueugneau N.; Demougeot L.; Fadiga L.; Pozzo T.; Papaxanthis C.
Article.Abstract: The mirror neuron network is activated during both execution and observation of the same action, enabling visual-to-motor transformation. Two main hypotheses account for this process: the direct matching hypothesis proposes a direct link between visual cues and the observer's motor representations, whereas the predictive hypothesis suggests that motor predictions are generated and compared with visual information. We tested these hypotheses during a locomotion task. Motor prediction was assessed by comparing actual and imagined walking (forward or backward) over a 9 m path. Action observation (AO) was examined through a time-estimation inference task in which participants observed an agent walking 3 m before occlusion and estimated when the agent would reach the end of the 9 m path. We manipulated these tasks by mechanically vibrating the leg muscles, creating sensory illusions. We found that vibration-induced sensory illusions altered motor imagery timing, affecting sensorimotor prediction. Opposite effects on AO and numerical simulations supported the predictive hypothesis.

Article.Authors: Qiu L.; Liu Y.; Qi R.; Zhang Z.; Cheng X.; Li J.; Pan J.; Wu W.; Zhang L.; Lu G.
Article.Abstract: Adaptive survival requires flexibly choosing passive or active defenses as threat intensity varies. Article.Authors: Tanimoto R.; Miyamoto K.; Tamura K.; Kondo S.; Kuroda J.

Article.Title: Beyond predictive accuracy: A case for mechanism-informed, uncertainty-aware machine learning in food microbiology
Article.Authors: Ezzaky Y.; Yap E.; Chen W.
Article.Abstract: Foodborne illness and avoidable food waste both depend on decisions about how microorganisms behave in a food. Machine-learning (ML) models can achieve strong predictive accuracy within a defined data domain, but a held-out test error alone does not establish reliability for food-safety decisions. Conventional predictive-microbiology models are usually empirical rather than fully mechanistic, although their parameters have biological interpretation; ML offers flexible learning of complex, high-dimensional relationships. Mechanism-informed hybrids can incorporate kinetic or physiological constraints within a learning workflow. Such constraints may improve plausibility, data efficiency, and interpretability within a declared applicability domain, but they do not confer universal or unrestricted extrapolation. We outline four hybrid design patterns and propose a food-specific validation framework that includes context-relevant external validation, calibrated predictive uncertainty, and decision-focused evaluation.

Article.Title: Neural subspace reorganization reflects value-based decision-making
Article.Authors: Li H.; Chrysanthidis N.; Brincat S.; Rose J.; Miller E.
Article.Abstract: Value-based decision-making requires maintaining and comparing multiple options to guide behavior. Before the decision, representations were organized by presentation order. These findings suggest that value-based decisions reorganize LPFC population activity to selectively represent the chosen option, enabling efficient downstream readout for action selection.

Article.Abstract: Scaffolds that simultaneously provide bioactivity, osteoinduction, and structural stability are essential yet remain elusive in bone tissue engineering. Article.Abstract: Loess deposits can undergo substantial deformation upon wetting, posing risks to infrastructure in loess-covered regions. Article.Title: Coordinated regulation of the metaboproteome by Hsp90 chaperones controls metabolic plasticity
Article.Authors: Perez R.; Mochi G.; Burkacki J.; Zoccoli-Rodriguez V.; Arcadi L.; Backe S.; Wilmore J.; Woodford M.
Article.Abstract: Heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) chaperones participate in the stabilization and activation of hundreds of proteins, thereby acting as signaling hubs. Proteomic and metabolomic evaluation demonstrated that Hsp90 regulates the mitochondrial metabolic network, including respiration, fatty acid oxidation, and redox homeostasis. Loss of the mitochondrial chaperone tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated protein 1 (TRAP1) induced compensatory binding of Hsp90s to TRAP1-dependent proteins, indicating a mechanism for the role of Hsp90 chaperones in metabolic reprogramming. When considered with previous findings, a temporal pattern of regulation emerges whereby Hsp90s control the transcription, translation, import, and assembly of mitochondrial protein complexes. Our findings expand the scope of Hsp90-regulated processes and potentially inform the effects of isoform-specific Hsp90 inhibitors on metabolic reprogramming in cancer and other diseases.

Article.Title: From pixels to conservation: Deep learning for automated monitoring of rare and endangered wildlife
Article.Authors: Xuan D.; Cai Y.; Xu M.; Long C.; Cai N.
Article.Abstract: Conservation of rare and endangered species requires scalable monitoring solutions to address accelerating biodiversity loss. Deep learning has transformed wildlife monitoring, enabling automated species identification, individual tracking, demographic inference, and behavioral analysis from camera traps, drones, and video surveillance. This review systematically analyzes 159 wildlife monitoring studies (2014-2026) across four technical domains: species recognition, individual re-identification, soft biometrics (age/sex estimation), and behavior/pose analysis. We examine architectural evolution across three architectural paradigms-CNN-based models, Attention & Sequence Architectures, and Foundation Models- documenting performance advances and ecological applications. Key challenges-environmental interference, data scarcity, domain shift, computational constraints-and optimization strategies, including data augmentation, transfer learning, and model compression, are systematically addressed. Case studies demonstrate real-world impact across diverse taxa: giant pandas, Amur tigers, great apes, and marine mammals. We identify critical research gaps and emerging opportunities in foundation model adaptation, multimodal learning, spatiotemporal modeling, and edge deployment. This review bridges computer vision research and conservation practice, providing actionable insights for developing robust, deployable monitoring systems that translate algorithmic advances into conservation impact.

Article.Authors: Zhang M.; Wang Z.; Chen J.; Huang Q.; He Y.; Cao K.; Xu Y.; Guo C.; Guan T.

Intensity-aware weighted loss (IA-Loss) reweights optimization according to local brightness to improve preservation of high-intensity signals under signal-dependent noise. Using Noise2Void (N2V) as the baseline, we developed structure- and intensity-prior-guided Noise2Void (SI-N2V) with a Mamba-UNet backbone for global contextual modeling. Experiments on an in-house pathological dataset and public fluorescence microscopy datasets show that SAPM and IA-Loss independently improve denoising and achieve the largest gains when combined. Article.Title: A synthesis of recorded fine-scale threats to imperiled species in the United States
Article.Authors: Niederman T.; Nunes L.; Dreiss L.; Gainsbury A.
Article.Abstract: Biodiversity in the United States faces mounting anthropogenic pressures, with an increasing number of species at risk of extinction. Species occupying multiple ecosystems tend to see more recorded threats on average, and threat prevalence differs by ecosystem. Article.Title: Retrospective attention reveals a decaying theta rhythm in conscious access to a preceding stimulus
Article.Authors: Yun S.; Kim Y.; Jeong J.; Kim Y.
Article.Abstract: Conscious perception is often presumed to arise immediately upon external stimulation. However, retroperception-conscious access to a stimulus after it has disappeared-challenges this perspective by demonstrating temporally flexible awareness. Here, we tested three competing models for the temporal architecture of retroperception: a monotonic decay, a sustained oscillation, and a damped oscillation. Through spectral analysis and computational modeling, we found that both behavioral accuracy and subjective visibility exhibited theta-band fluctuations, with model comparison modestly favoring a damped oscillatory profile over sustained oscillatory or non-oscillatory alternatives. Furthermore, we found that oscillations in accuracy and visibility were temporally aligned, suggesting temporal coordination between attention and perception during post-stimulus access. These findings suggest that conscious access to recent sensory information may be rhythmically structured and temporally limited, placing computational constraints on models of retroperception.

Article.Authors: Shen J.; Tian S.; Zhang Z.; Li Z.; Lu H.; Wang P.; Sun L.; Wei L.; Xie S.; Zhang Q.
Article.Abstract: Electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking underpins China's low-carbon steel transition, while uneven regional resources and energy conditions greatly constrain its low-carbon development. Together, these domains offer a route to landscapes that sustain both commodity production and biodiversity.

Article.Abstract: The T2T-CHM13v2.0 reference genome added previously uncharacterized genomic sequences and improved the accuracy of repetitive stretches compared to former human genome assemblies. Article.Authors: Dokuzparmak E.; Sezer E.; Ceylan İ.; Çetin N.; Özçelik H.; Akgöl S.

Article.Abstract: Dynamic sensory processing helps animals adjust behaviors in response to changing environments and internal states. Article.Abstract: Lymph node (LN) fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) are key immunomodulators that regulate adaptive immune responses and provide structural support via extracellular matrix (ECM) production. Article.Authors: Feng M.; Qiu Y.; Chen J.; Lou J.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Power outages are increasingly shaped by aging infrastructure, climate stress, and rising electricity demand. Article.Title: Substrate-dependent performance patterns in nanocoatings across interior materials
Article.Authors: Boostani H.; Altan H.
Article.Abstract: Nanostructured coatings are widely used to enhance surface durability while preserving visual appearance, yet it remains unclear whether performance is primarily governed by coating chemistry or by the underlying substrate. Here, we address this question through a structured scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) of 80 eligible empirical studies spanning seven material classes relevant to interior environments. Across 311 standardized observations, we find that substrate class emerged as the strongest observed association with simultaneous functional and optical performance. Non-porous substrates (e.g., glass, glazed ceramics) achieve dual performance targets in 67-82% of cases, compared to only 11-22% for highly porous materials (e.g., wood, textiles), revealing an approximately 4-fold performance gradient. This pattern is consistent with interfacial film formation mechanisms, including capillary depletion, hygroscopic stress, and surface heterogeneity. Exploratory study-level logistic regression (N = 80) supports this trend, with highly porous substrates showing substantially reduced odds of dual-axis success (odds ratio (OR) = 0.24; adjusted confidence interval (CI): 0.11-0.52). Coating chemistry, deposition conditions, and interfacial interactions further influence performance within these substrate-dependent trends: TiO2-based systems enhance antimicrobial efficacy but incur greater optical degradation relative to SiO2-based formulations. These findings support the interpretation of nanocoating performance as strongly influenced by substrate-dependent interfacial phenomena rather than a formulation-driven outcome alone. More broadly, they suggest that thin-film performance in complex environments is constrained by substrate-controlled transport and stress regimes, with implications for material selection and surface engineering beyond coating systems. As a synthesis based on proxy classification, these results are hypothesis-generating and highlight the need for controlled experiments directly testing substrate-controlled thin-film performance.

Article.Authors: Kato M.; He B.

Article.Authors: Chaudhary S.; Wadhwa M.; Sinha A.; Saxena D.

Maternal Complications were using four self-reported pregnancy complication indicators. Heat exposures metrics included mean UTCI and mean of daily maximum UTCI calculated for full gestational period and for trimester-specific windows. Multivariable logistic regression models estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) per 1°C (1 K) increase in UTCI, adjusting for maternal age, parity, household wealth quintile, and place of residence, with state fixed effects. In contrast, the mean of daily maximum UTCI showed an inverse association (full pregnancy aOR 0.993; 95% CI: 0.988-0.998; p = 0.005), which was significant in the first and second trimesters. Higher parity was associated with lower odds of maternal complications, while urban residence showed marginally higher odds. Sustained gestational heat load measured with UTCI was modestly associated with maternal complications in India with a possible mid pregnancy vulnerability. Antenatal services and Heat Action Plans should incorporate heat risk screening, scheduling, cooling, and hydration, and future studies should test non-linear exposure relationships and extreme heat events.

Article.Title: Metabolic reprogramming in diabetic panvascular disease: Molecular mechanism and therapeutic strategies
Article.Authors: Bai Y.; Bai Y.; Liu S.
Article.Abstract: Diabetes mellitus substantially increases the risk of cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, renal, retinal and peripheral vascular complications. These are collectively referred to as diabetic panvascular disease. A traditional approach that treats each complication separately is no longer sufficient. An emerging framework places metabolic reprogramming at its center. This review examines how the diabetic environment, including hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia, rewires core metabolic pathways in vascular cells. Major changes include the diversion of glucose through the polyol, hexosamine and AGE-PKC axes, lipotoxicity resulting from excessive fatty acids, disruption of amino acid networks such as BCAA and one-carbon metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction with increased mtROS production, and epigenetic modifications that drive metabolic memory. These interconnected abnormalities promote oxidative stress and chronic inflammation, which in turn lead to endothelial dysfunction, atherosclerosis, microvascular rarefaction, and end-organ damage in the heart, brain, kidney, retina, and peripheral nerves. We also describe the current therapeutic landscape, ranging from established agents such as metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, RAAS blockers, and anti-VEGF therapies to emerging mechanism-based strategies including aldose reductase inhibitors, glucokinase activators, PKC, RAGE, NOX, and NLRP3 inhibitors, miRNA modulators, and exosome therapy. Finally, we highlight unmet needs and future directions. These may include multi-omics guided precision phenotyping, cross-organ causal inference, single-cell metabolic flux technologies, and adaptive clinical trial designs. By shifting from a glucose-centric to a metabolic reprogramming-centric paradigm, this review aims to provide a roadmap for developing more targeted therapies for diabetic panvascular disease.

Article.Abstract: Secreted factors are essential mediators of cellular communication that are exploited by tumors to control their environment and evade immune attack. Here, we apply a click chemistry-based approach to selectively profile the secretome of patient-derived colorectal cancer (CRC) and healthy colon organoids. We observe cancer cell-intrinsic rewiring of the secretome during malignancy, with clear separation between microsatellite stable (MSS) and instable cancers. Article.Title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction
Article.Authors: Wang B.; Xie X.; Zou H.; Peng S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from multiple pretrained protein language models, aligns graph-based structural features with pretrained semantic embeddings for drugs under subspace constraints, and progressively refines drug-protein interaction representations through cascaded cross-modal signal propagation. Experiments on six benchmark datasets under standard, cold-start, and cross-domain settings demonstrate that SF-DTI achieves competitive performance relative to seven state-of-the-art baselines across evaluation scenarios. These results suggest that SF-DTI is a promising framework for DTI prediction and may support virtual screening, drug repositioning, and drug discovery.

Article.Title: Patent insights on advanced polymer composites for transport systems
Article.Authors: D B.; V B.; S S.; S D.; M V.
Article.Abstract: Polymeric materials have become increasingly important in transportation and aerospace due to their low weight, processability, and ability to provide tailored functional properties. This study examines the patent landscape of polymeric materials used in these sectors through a combined keyword and International Patent Classification (IPC) search strategy. The results show that the United States accounts for the largest share among national patent offices, while the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) represents the major international filing route. The leading IPC categories include B29C, C08L, C08K, C08F, C08J, B32B, C09D, and C08G. Recent patent activity is concentrated on lightweight structures, protective and flame-resistant coatings, thermal management, bio-based resins, fiber-reinforced composites, graphene-based materials, and high-temperature polymers. Article.Authors: Zhang P.; Chen Y.; Shi Y.; Zhao R.; Guo T.; Guo H.; Chen L.; Yu P.

Article.Abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Article.Authors: Henriques H.; Silva M.; Guerreiro R.; Mendonça S.; Durão C.; Rosario Pinto M.; Teixeira J.
Article.Abstract: Sleep quality strongly affects hospitalized patients' recovery, yet pain, anxiety, and environmental factors such as noise and light frequently disrupt it. Article.Abstract: The energy transition and transportation electrification have increased the reliance of lithium ion battery supply chains on critical minerals, including lithium, cobalt, and nickel. Article.Authors: Awotoro E.; Anžel A.; Anyabolu C.; Willrich N.; Hattab G.

Article.Title: Sonocavitation therapy for pancreatic cancer: Research progress, clinical application and future perspectives

Article.Abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PC) remains one of the most lethal malignancies, characterized by a dense desmoplastic stroma, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and poor response to conventional therapies. Proposed mechanisms include sonoporation, cascade cavitation, vascular normalization, and mechano-acoustic remodeling of the stroma. Early clinical studies suggest that USMB-assisted chemotherapy is feasible and may improve disease control, although the evidence remains heterogeneous and is based largely on small, single-center or early-phase studies. Article.Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) mesoporous materials are an emerging class of porous nanostructures that combine mesoporosity with an ultrathin 2D geometry. Article.Title: Metal-organic frameworks for the treatment of endocrine-disrupting chemicals
Article.Authors: Thanh N.; Natarajan A.; Nguyen C.
Article.Abstract: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) are exogenous agents that target hormone biosynthesis, cellular signaling, transport, metabolism, and receptor activity. EDCs are also known to contaminate aquatic and wildlife ecosystems via bioaccumulation, environmental persistence, and disruption of biological processes. To overcome the drawbacks of conventional techniques, researchers developed metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for water remediation. MOFs are superior materials because they have high surface area, tunable pore structure, chemical versatility, and catalytic capabilities through functionalization. MOFs have demonstrated strong potential for the sensitive detection and degradation of diverse endocrine-active pollutants, including bisphenols and related micropollutants. In this review, sources, classifications of EDCs, routes of exposure, molecular mechanisms, health effects, and socioeconomic effects of EDCs were discussed with illustrative figures. Therefore, integrating MOFs with water treatment strategies using advanced materials engineering will efficiently reduce EDC contamination.

Article.Title: Bidirectional photoriboswitch for translational regulation in mammalian cells
Article.Authors: Hu Y.; Li C.; Fu L.; Sun Y.; Zhang M.; Yau T.; Xiong C.; Shi P.; Kuang Y.
Article.Abstract: Photoriboswitches are invaluable tools for synthetic biology because they provide direct, precise, and on-demand control of translation. While most existing photoriboswitches are predominantly one-directional, this study presents a bidirectional photoriboswitch platform capable of mimicking the orthogonal RNA-binding protein-mediated up-/downregulation of multiple mRNAs. Inspired by intein-based split protein reconstitution and light-induced protein dimerization, we first engineered a Light-OFF system that uses photodimerization to block intein reconstitution. We then validated that this Light-OFF system can function orthogonally with a Light-ON system that reconstitutes a different split intein pair under light. Together, a bidirectional photoriboswitch is generated, which senses light to orthogonally reconstitute RNA-binding proteins to tune the translation of their respective target mRNAs. We have demonstrated that the photoriboswitch produces bidirectional translation regulation. Importantly, the functional modules of the photoriboswitch can be easily altered to adapt for different purposes, allowing the bidirectional photoriboswitch to serve as a versatile tool for translation regulation.

Article.Title: Lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio predicts survival in localized osteosarcoma in Vietnamese patients
Article.Authors: Thu Hien T.; Quoc D.; Thanh T.; Thanh Hai T.; Quang Sang N.; Dung T.; Nguyen X.; Vu S.
Article.Abstract: Inflammatory markers such as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), alongside hemoglobin (Hgb) levels, have been proposed as prognostic tools in osteosarcoma, though their reliability remains unclear. We retrospectively evaluated the prognostic significance of these pre-operative markers in a cohort of 100 Vietnamese patients with stage IB-IIB osteosarcoma, specifically focusing on the post-neoadjuvant, pre-operative window, a clinically critical yet underexplored time frame. In the primary dichotomized multivariable analysis, LMR emerged as an independent predictor of poor overall survival, whereas PLR showed only univariable associations, and NLR and Hgb were not statistically significant. While LMR demonstrated robust prognostic value for overall survival, it failed to predict disease progression within 24 months. To address cutpoint bias, sensitivity analyses modeling these markers as continuous variables combined with internal bootstrap validation (1000 resamples) confirmed parameter stability only for LMR, but not PLR and NLR. Reflecting these continuous trends, the final multivariable model achieved an apparent C-index of 0.729, which adjusted to an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.628. External literature-derived median cutoffs did not show significant associations when applied to this post-neoadjuvant cohort, highlighting key population- and timing-specific limitations. Although these peripheral blood markers demonstrate prognostic potential, our findings remain exploratory, and validation in independent multi-center cohorts with longitudinal prospective evaluation is required before their clinical utility can be established.

Article.Authors: Tschan M.; Jetzer T.; Obenloch M.; Blank A.; Yong C.; Nair N.; Cabon L.; D’Arcangelo E.; Lutolf M.
Article.Abstract: T cell bispecifics (TCBs) are potent immunotherapies with proven efficacy in hematological cancers but limited success in solid tumors, where on-target, off-tumor toxicity has restricted their therapeutic index. Using a multi-modal approach combining flow cytometry, cytokine profiling, and multiplexed immunofluorescence, we show that EpCAM and FolR1 TCBs drive robust T cell activation and, critically, quantifiable epithelial cell killing above background levels. Article.Title: An AI-driven framework for property-oriented fuel design toward sustainable engine combustion
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Li A.; Li Y.; Fan Y.; Qi Y.; Zhang C.; Zhu L.; Huang Z.
Article.Abstract: Co-optimizing renewable synthetic fuels and internal combustion engines is critical for decarbonization, with fuel design as a crucial approach. However, the combinatorial explosion of fuel compositions renders composition-driven design infeasible. While artificial intelligence (AI) offers optimization tools, data scarcity hinders its application in engine research. Therefore, we propose an AI-driven fuel design framework using physicochemical properties to bridge fuel composition and engine performance. Treating properties as direct design variables, this framework reduces design dimensionality and enables standardized integration of data from different studies. Based on a literature-mined dataset, we trained a predictive model and applied it in a proof-of-concept demonstration to identify a tailored property combination. Relative to diesel, this combination improved thermal efficiency by 6.62% and reduced NOx and soot emissions by 19.28% and 67.76%, respectively. This framework provides a pathway for AI-driven engine research and facilitates property-oriented design, which could instruct upstream synthesis and help reduce trial-and-error in fuel development.

Article.Authors: Huang X.; Zhang Z.; Zhong Z.; Weng Z.; Xu Y.; Zhong G.; Li W.; Wang Q.; Du B.; Peng M.; Ma C.

Article.Title: Response speed is modulated by respiratory phase
Article.Authors: Yamazaki E.; Paller K.
Article.Abstract: Mere milliseconds can determine whether a sprinter or swimmer wins or places second. Would it help to intentionally control breathing while awaiting the starting signal? Here, we analyzed sustained-attention performance in 35 adults and found that response speed varied with respiratory phase. Article.Authors: Liang X.; Guo Z.; Xiong K.; He Z.; Zhang D.; Kang S.; Chen H.; Du M.; Kui X.; Wen X.; Chen Z.

Article.Authors: Donaka R.; Awad K.; Khrystoforova I.; Hezkial B.; Brotto M.; Karasik D.

Article.Authors: Zhan Y.; He B.; Pu L.; Bi W.; Wei G.; Li G.
Article.Abstract: The independent and combined associations of resting heart rate (RHR) and physical activity (PA) with mortality in diverse chronic kidney disease (CKD) populations remain unclear. Article.Title: Multitasking boosts human muscular endurance task performance due to elevated arousal

Article.Abstract: Multitasking is generally thought to impair performance because of the interference between tasks arising from the limited processing capacity. A similar effect was observed when monetary reward was offered for the cognitive task. These facilitation effects were associated with greater pupil dilation elicited by the cognitive task. Article.Title: Non-volatile memristors as prospective radio frequency switches for 6G communications - A review
Article.Authors: Keat Seow E.; Toh R.; Ang D.
Article.Abstract: As communication technologies continue to improve to the 6G standard, highly performing radio frequency (RF) switches that have short switching times, high energy efficiency, high cutoff frequencies, capabilities of operating beyond 100 GHz while maintaining reasonable RF performance, and high data transmission rates of 100 Gbit s-1 are needed. Existing RF switches based on solid-state and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technologies fall short of meeting these requirements because of their volatility and parasitic inductive effects that lead to undesirably high insertion losses at high frequencies. Non-volatile memristors are emerging as likely candidates to replace traditional switches. They offer numerous benefits, including virtually zero static energy consumption, fast switching speeds, and excellent scalability. This review will provide an overview of the progress and challenges associated with implementing four types of non-volatile memristive technologies as RF switches: Resistive random access memory (ReRAM), conductive bridge random access memory (CBRAM), phase change memory (PCM), and memory based on two-dimensional (2D) materials, specifically molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The performance of these prospective switches is compared against one another and subsequently benchmarked against existing switch technologies. The review will provide an objective critique of the future readiness for 6G for the four main types of memristive switch technologies based on factors such as RF performance, CMOS compatibility, and fabrication maturity. Special attention is paid to 2D material-based memristors involving MoS2 and hBN, which have attracted significant research interest for multiple benefits that are claimed to be distinctive. Finally, it will also propose research directions to further the progress of future memristive RF switches.

Article.Abstract: Energy transition studies often present hundreds of scenarios, yielding large datasets that are challenging to interpret. Here, we show that decision trees, a popular machine learning technique, bridge this disconnect by distilling numerous scenarios into a small set of interpretable storylines centered around policy-relevant levers. We demonstrate this approach across three global and European case studies: First, we translate 1000 integrated assessment model scenarios into three storylines distinguished by their degrees of heating and industry electrification. Second, we show that 2°C warming pathways with continued fossil fuel usage only work under unusually mild climate responses. Third, we use 441 European pathways to show that high bioenergy or electrification are required for cost-effective climate neutrality. Our transferable approach helps decision-makers interpret large scenario sets by revealing how policy-relevant outputs are associated with different transition pathways.

Article.Abstract: Bacterial spores pose a significant challenge to the food industry due to their ability to germinate from dormancy and their extreme resistance. Spores are encased by a multilayered proteinaceous structure termed the spore coat. Previous studies on spore coat assembly have predominantly focused on the interactions among coat proteins, while the involvement of broader protein quality control systems remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that the molecular chaperone DnaK is essential for the proper assembly of the inner spore coat in Bacillus subtilis. Deletion of dnaK leads to mislocalization of key morphogenetic protein SafA, reduced accumulation of full-length SafA, altered transcriptional dynamics of spoIIID and sigK, and ultimately impaired coat integrity and function. Our findings reveal that DnaK facilitates spore coat assembly through both transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms, uncovering a previously unrecognized regulatory layer in spore coat morphogenesis.

Article.Title: Why cost reduction alone cannot deliver bankable carbon dioxide removal
Article.Authors: Smart J.; Mac Dowell N.
Article.Abstract: Carbon dioxide removal (CDR) is indispensable for net-zero, yet CDR projects remain unbankable for institutional lenders. Using a stochastic project-finance model in which financing terms follow from simulated cash flows rather than being assumed, we examine when BECCS and DAC become bankable. Under unhedged conditions bankability is effectively zero, with lender coverage failing across most of the financing space and equity hurdles met in less than 0.1%. Contrary to the emphasis on cost reduction, credit-worthy offtake is the primary determinant. Learning alone lowers the levelized cost of removal by up to 38%, yet leaves projects unbankable, whereas offtake raises BECCS bankability to 43%, or 57% with learning. DAC requires offtake above US$2,500 per tCO2 and remains marginally bankable, reflecting sole dependence on carbon revenues. An electricity-anchored BECCS pathway can reach investment grade without fully contracted carbon revenues. These results show where revenue support must be targeted to mobilize institutional capital.

Optogenetic activation of excitatory cerebellar output in the superior cerebellar peduncle suppressed ultrasonic vocalizations with frequency-dependent potency while inducing distinct motor phenotypes. Deep brain stimulation of the PAG rescued vocal deficits in a model of cerebellar dysfunction without rescuing motor incoordination. Article.Abstract: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is a complex multisystem disorder requiring coordinated multidisciplinary care. This study aimed to develop consensus recommendations for NF1 management in the Asia-Pacific region. A modified Delphi process involving two survey rounds and a virtual meeting was conducted with experts from nine countries. A total of 141 statements were evaluated using a 9-point Likert scale with a 75% consensus threshold. Consensus was achieved across key domains including diagnosis, genetic testing, surveillance, and management. These findings provide regionally relevant guidance to support consistent and practical NF1 management across diverse healthcare systems.

Article.Abstract: Hirschsprung disease (HSCR) is characterized by distal intestinal aganglionosis and persistent dysfunction of the enteric nervous system after surgical treatment. Article.Abstract: Traditional dressings often fail to address the dynamic progression of infected diabetic wounds, which requires early bacterial elimination followed by timely control of oxidative stress and inflammation. Chlorin e6 (Ce6) and celastrol were co-encapsulated in a gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) hydrogel. Article.Abstract: In many Proteobacterial species, transcription and RNA degradation are physically separated through segregation of the main ribonucleolytic machinery-the RNA degradosome-into RNase E-driven membrane-anchored assemblies that form discrete foci. Article.Title: Genomic structural variations distinguishing archaic and modern humans are associated with neurodevelopment

Article.Title: Domain-autonomous MKLP1 modules divergently regulate mitotic fidelity and polyploidy in a holocentric system

Article.Title: Trait anxiety selectively amplifies reward learning under uncertainty, while N3 sleep attenuates it
Article.Authors: Deshmukh R.; Ramakrishnan A.
Article.Abstract: Adaptive learning under uncertainty requires distinguishing random variability (stochasticity) from true environmental change (volatility), yet how trait anxiety and sleep together influence it remains unclear. Hierarchical Bayesian modeling showed that in stable but noisy environments, individuals with higher trait anxiety appeared to treat stochastic fluctuations as indicators of genuine change, resulting in over updating and lower evidence accumulation, while preserving normative trends in volatile environments. In a second experiment combining task performance with overnight sleep electroencephalography, greater N3 sleep was associated with reduced updating and higher evidence accumulation in stable environments among individuals with higher trait anxiety. Article.Title: Bidirectional metabolic-vascular feedback loops in heart failure: From myocardial energetics to multisystem cardiometabolic crosstalk
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Li Y.; Qin C.; Chen X.; Wang K.; Zhang M.; Cheng W.
Article.Abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a multisystem syndrome in which myocardial dysfunction is shaped by metabolic, vascular, and extracardiac abnormalities. Article.Authors: Ding J.; Boonman A.; Eitan O.; Werber Y.; Troupin D.; Sapir N.; Yovel Y.
Article.Abstract: Urbanization reshapes local climates, potentially altering how animals respond to environmental variation. Rural specialists avoided cities and were active within relatively narrow environmental ranges, while generalists occurred in both habitats and used broader activity conditions in cities. Here, we examined cognitive function and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) enkephalin profiles in rats with a history of chronic EtOH exposure. Using a longitudinal operant-based approach, we assessed cognitive flexibility during early abstinence and delay-dependent working memory during protracted abstinence. We then quantified methionine-enkephalin (Met-ENK) and leucine-enkephalin (Leu-ENK) and profiled the proenkephalin-A (PENK)-derived peptide pool in the mPFC. EtOH history did not alter overall trials or errors to criterion during strategy set-shifting or reversal learning. During reversal, however, EtOH rats showed greater perseverative bias, with response adjustments less aligned with recent feedback and more strongly influenced by prior reinforcement. During initial testing at the longest working memory delay, EtOH rats also showed lower accuracy. Performance across these tasks was correlated in EtOH rats, suggesting individual differences in cognitive susceptibility were maintained across abstinence. Targeted analyses showed comparable levels of Met-ENK and Leu-ENK between groups. Although individual PENK-derived sequences did not differ in abundance, compositional analysis showed a greater summed relative contribution of C-terminal fragments in EtOH samples. These findings indicate that EtOH history produces lasting cognitive vulnerabilities that emerge under greater task demands, with some animals remaining more susceptible than others. C-terminal PENK profiling may reveal novel targets associated with enduring mPFC adaptations during abstinence.

Article.Title: SV2A attenuates interictal anxiety in pharmacoresistant epilepsy via the SYT3–GluA2 axis
Article.Authors: Li C.; Pan T.; Ren M.; Wang X.; Shi Y.; Ren S.; Wu G.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: Objective: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) is an established target of antiseizure therapy; however, its role in excitatory synaptic function and downstream postsynaptic machinery remains poorly defined. This study examined whether SV2A limits excitotoxic signaling by recruiting synaptotagmin-3 (SYT3), thereby modulating the α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor subunit GluA2. Methods: A multilevel strategy was used to define the contribution of SV2A to anxiety in a pharmacoresistant epilepsy (PRE) model. The phenobarbital/phenytoin-resistant PRE phenotype was established in rats using the lithium-pilocarpine paradigm. Lentiviral vectors were delivered to the hippocampal CA1 region for bidirectional manipulation of SV2A expression. Protein abundance and molecular interactions were examined using western blotting, immunofluorescence, co-immunoprecipitation, and molecular docking. Synaptic plasticity was assessed using long-term potentiation (LTP) recordings, and anxiety-related behavior was evaluated using the elevated plus maze and open field test. Results: A special interaction between SV2A and SYT3 was confirmed at the protein level. PRE rats exhibited pronounced anxiety-like behavior, increased seizure frequency, reduced SV2A expression, and aberrantly potentiated LTP in the CA1 region. Hippocampal SV2A overexpression reduced SYT3 levels, suppressed GluA2 internalization, and attenuated both exaggerated LTP and anxiety-like behavior. Conversely, SV2A knockdown increased SYT3 expression, promoted GluA2 endocytosis, and further aggravated aberrant LTP and anxiety-like behavior. Conclusion: SV2A plays a pivotal role in interictal anxiety associated with PRE. PRE downregulates SV2A and weakens the SV2A-SYT3 interaction, thereby driving aberrant LTP and the emergence of anxiety-like behavior.

Article.Title: Molecular mechanism of the interaction between kaempferol and human nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
Article.Authors: Yang J.; Moon M.; Yun J.; Yeom H.; Kamau V.; Lee M.; Lee G.; Lee J.
Article.Abstract: Kaempferol has been investigated for its potential neuroprotective properties and its ability to modulate mood-regulating pathways through the regulation of neurotransmitter systems. Evidence suggests that it may inhibit the reuptake of selective neurotransmitters, thereby enhancing their synaptic availability. Here, using two-electrode voltage-clamp recordings in Xenopus oocytes expressing five human nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) subtypes, we found that kaempferol selectively and potently inhibits α3β4 nAChRs, with weaker inhibition of α3β2 receptors and no effect on α7, α4β2, or α4β4 subtypes. This inhibition was reversible, voltage-independent, and non-competitive with acetylcholine, indicating an allosteric mechanism of action rather than direct competition at the orthosteric binding site. To identify the structural basis of this subtype selectivity, molecular docking of kaempferol onto the α3β4 nAChR structure was performed, and candidate binding residues at the α3-β4 interface were prioritized based on binding energy for site-directed mutagenesis. The results showed that the inhibitory effect of kaempferol was abolished in the α3 W55A and β4 R151A double mutant. These findings confirm that kaempferol selectively and effectively inhibits the α3β4 nAChR subtype via an allosteric site formed by residues W55 (α3) and R151 (β4), supporting the hypothesis that it interacts with a specific region of this receptor distinct from the acetylcholine-binding site.

Article.Title: Distinct protein synthesis requirements for coupled excitatory and inhibitory long-term co-plasticity in mouse hippocampus
Article.Authors: Jabłońska J.; Orzoł D.; Ciurko D.; Wiera G.; Mozrzymas J.
Article.Abstract: The functioning of neuronal networks critically depends on the coordinated interaction between excitation and inhibition. The properties of glutamatergic and GABAergic synapses are finely tuned by network activity, and the heterosynaptic nature of inhibitory plasticity further emphasizes their functional coupling. Although the dependence of glutamatergic plasticity on protein synthesis is well established, the role of translation in inhibitory plasticity remains unclear. Herein, we investigated how protein synthesis supports the concurrent plasticity at inhibitory and excitatory inputs onto CA1 pyramidal neurons. To this end, we applied a high-frequency stimulation protocol of CA3-CA1 input combined with prolonged postsynaptic depolarization of principal cells. This induced both glutamatergic long-term potentiation (LTP) and inhibitory LTP (iLTP) at synapses formed by somatostatin-expressing interneurons onto pyramidal neurons. Although LTP was observed in slices from both juvenile (≤45 days) and adult (>45 days) mice, iLTP was only present in the adult group, revealing an unusual developmental profile. Moreover, in adult animals, excitatory LTP was required for the induction of iLTP but did not determine its magnitude. We found that bath application of translation inhibitor cycloheximide (CHX) strongly attenuated LTP and converted co-occurring iLTP into iLTD. However, when CHX was restricted to the recorded postsynaptic neuron, the initial phase of iLTP proceeded normally, but GABAergic currents gradually returned to baseline levels, indicating intact induction but impaired maintenance. In contrast, postsynaptic CHX left excitatory LTP unaffected. Together, these findings identify two distinct translational mechanisms: a postsynaptic one necessary for strengthening inhibition and a non-postsynaptic process required to potentiate excitation.

Article.Title: Route-dependent behavioral, dopaminergic, and transcriptomic adaptations to nicotine aerosol inhalation and systemic injection in male mice
Article.Authors: Ma Y.; Song Z.; Chen Y.; Liu G.; Li X.; Han S.; Fu Y.; Chen H.; Hou H.
Article.Abstract: Nicotine is one of the most widely used psychoactive substances, yet most preclinical studies rely on subcutaneous injection, which does not fully model inhalation-based exposure. How different nicotine delivery paradigms shape neurobehavioral adaptations remains unclear. Here, we compared subcutaneous nicotine injection and nicotine aerosol inhalation in male mice across behavioral, dopaminergic, and transcriptomic domains. Nicotine aerosol inhalation produced concentration-dependent modulation of conditioned place preference, accompanied by rapid nicotine absorption and delayed cotinine accumulation. Fiber photometry recordings in the nucleus accumbens revealed distinct dopamine dynamics during nicotine-associated contextual processing, with nicotine-paired contexts eliciting shorter time-to-peak but reduced amplitude and area under the curve. High-dimensional behavioral tracking under mecamylamine-precipitated withdrawal conditions demonstrated that nicotine exposure conditions reshaped behavioral organization rather than producing generalized hyperlocomotion. Subcutaneous nicotine and aerosol exposure produced partially overlapping but compositionally distinct behavioral profiles influenced by nicotine exposure, delivery paradigm, and aerosol formulation. Transcriptomic analyses further revealed region-specific molecular signatures, including metabolic pathways in the ventral tegmental area and synaptic/neuroimmune-related pathways in the nucleus accumbens after aerosol exposure. Together, these findings demonstrate that nicotine delivery paradigms shape distinct neurobehavioral and molecular responses, emphasizing the importance of inhalation-based models in preclinical nicotine research.

Article.Title: Effects of metabotropic 2/3-glutamate receptor agonism and antagonism on activity-based anorexia model in mice
Article.Authors: Varjelus T.; Oksanen A.; Kaljala L.; Ryazantseva M.; Aitta-aho T.
Article.Abstract: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder disproportionately found in female teens and young adults. It is often resistant to treatment, has a significant chance of relapse and is more lethal than other eating disorders, such as bulimia nervosa or Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID). There is no specific medication for the treatment of anorexia nervosa. Treatment consists of psychosocial means, psychotherapy, psychoeducation, and nutritional counseling. Medication is usually used for treating comorbidities such as anxiety or to decrease obsessive-compulsive tendencies. These medications cannot help the patient regain weight or treat core symptoms. Metabotropic 2/3-glutamate (mGluR2/3) receptor agonist (LY379268) and antagonist (LY341495) are promising pharmacological agents to treat psychiatric disorders. Both have been reported to be anxiolytic, while antagonists have shown antidepressant-like effects in preclinical studies. The activity-based anorexia (ABA) paradigm is used to study mechanisms related to anorexia nervosa. It consists of giving mice access to a running wheel and restricting their feeding time. This causes mice to exercise more than mice without feeding time restriction and to eat less than mice without access to a moving running wheel. In this study, we subcutaneously injected female ABA model mice with a metabotropic 2/3-glutamate receptor agonist (LY379268) and antagonist (LY341495) in two experiments. Both compounds exacerbated weight loss by decreasing food intake as well as increasing physical activity. It can be concluded that the pharmacological manipulation of mGluR2/3 receptors is detrimental for the female ABA model and, therefore, might be potentially harmful for anorexia nervosa as well.

Article.Title: Altered hsa_circ_0005567 expression in schizophrenia: exploratory clinical associations and cellular evidence involving RPL7A
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhong Q.; Long J.; Lu R.; Lv M.; Huang X.; Zhong Z.; Lan W.; Liao F.; Su L.
Article.Abstract: Background: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a chronic mental disorder with unknown etiology and complex pathophysiology. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as important regulators in neuropsychiatric disorders. This study investigated the clinical relevance, functional role, and potential mechanism of hsa_circ_0005567 in SCZ. Methods: hsa_circ_0005567 expression was measured by qRT-PCR in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 160 patients with SCZ and 160 healthy controls. Associations with clinical symptoms and laboratory parameters were explored. Functional studies were conducted in MK-801-treated SH-SY5Y cells after hsa_circ_0005567 knockdown or overexpression. Cell viability, apoptosis, and inflammatory cytokines were assessed. Candidate hsa_circ_0005567-interacting proteins were explored using chromatin isolation by RNA purification (CHIRP), mass spectrometry, RNA immunoprecipitation, and Western blotting. Results: hsa_circ_0005567 expression was significantly increased in PBMCs from patients with SCZ (P < 0.001) and in SH-SY5Y cells following MK-801 treatment (P = 0.026). Higher hsa_circ_0005567 expression remained associated with SCZ status after adjustment for age and sex. Exploratory analyses of PANSS scores and laboratory parameters showed only nominal associations, none of which remained significant after FDR correction. In vitro, hsa_circ_0005567 manipulation affected cell viability, apoptosis, and TNF-α expression in MK-801-treated SH-SY5Y cells. RPL7A was identified as a candidate hsa_circ_0005567-interacting protein, and its protein expression was altered following hsa_circ_0005567 knockdown or overexpression. Conclusions: hsa_circ_0005567 is upregulated in PBMCs from patients with SCZ and is independently associated with SCZ status. Functional experiments suggest that hsa_circ_0005567 may participate in cellular responses under MK-801-induced stress conditions, while RPL7A represents a candidate interacting protein. Further clinical and mechanistic validation is needed.

Article.Title: Suppression of ER stress underlies Montelukast's neuroprotective actions in D-gal/AlCl3-induced Alzheimer's disease in rats
Article.Authors: Mahmoud A.; Ibrahim S.; El-Yamany M.; Gowifel A.; Mohammed R.
Article.Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative ailment characterized by neuronal and cognitive dysfunctions. Notably, cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 1 (CysLT1R) overexpression was detected in various AD models. It was closely associated with other hallmarks of AD, including increased oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, amyloid beta (Aβ) deposition, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. Montelukast (MTK), a CysLT1R antagonist, is an anti-asthmatic drug possessing antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Consequently, this study aimed to mechanistically investigate MTK's neuroprotective potential on D-galactose/Aluminum Chloride (D-gal/AlCl3)-induced AD in rats. This was accomplished by allocating thirty-six adult male Wistar rats into four equal groups as follows: Group I served as the control group, and Group II was orally treated daily with MTK (10 mg/kg) for eight weeks. At the same time, groups III and IV were administered D-gal (65 mg/kg/day, SC) and AlCl3 (200 mg/kg/day, p.o.), starting from week 3 until the end of the experiment, for the remaining six consecutive weeks, to induce AD. Group IV received MTK orally daily for eight weeks. The findings showed that dampening CysLT1R expression by MTK ameliorated D-gal/AlCl3-induced amyloidopathy. MTK rectified the behavioral outcomes, as evidenced by the improved parameters in the novel object recognition, Y-maze, and Morris water maze tests. MTK hampered oxidative stress (MDA and GSH), inflammatory (NF-κB and TNF-α), glial activation (GFAP and Iba1), apoptotic (Caspase-3), ER stress, and Aβ biomarkers. Additionally, MTK, as a CysLT1R antagonist, exerted these favorable actions via adjustment of PERK/IRE1-α/CHOP, NF-κB, mTOR, and apoptotic axes. In conclusion, this study underscored the use of MTK as a promising neuroprotective approach for mitigating AD via modulation of ER stress, neuroinflammatory, and apoptotic trajectories.

Article.Title: Adult-administered chronic nicotine remodels nigral dopaminergic and pedunculopontine cholinergic physiology
Article.Authors: Chen R.; Hosseini H.; Hall S.; Zhang S.; Evans R.
Article.Abstract: Nicotine is linked to neuroprotection and has been proposed as a potential preventative treatment for Parkinson's disease (PD). Because PD is an aging disorder, such a treatment would necessarily be administered to adults. However, previous studies examining the effects of chronic nicotine in neurons vulnerable to PD have primarily been conducted in juvenile animals. Here we administer chronic nicotine to adult mice of both sexes. We examine nicotine-induced functional adaptations in two brain structures vulnerable to PD, the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) and the pedunculopontine nucleus (PPN). Using whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology and two-photon calcium imaging, we observed changes in cellular properties that potentially contribute to reduced risk of PD associated with nicotine exposure. Chronic nicotine decreased pacemaking frequency, burst propensity, and rebound firing in SNc dopaminergic neurons, while decoupling tonic firing rate from dendritic calcium levels. These changes in the SNc occurred without altering L-type channel contributions, dendritic arborization, or excitatory synaptic drive. Although the PPN degenerates in PD and is the primary cholinergic input to the SNc, no previous studies have evaluated the effects of chronic nicotine on this structure. We find that chronic nicotine induced subregion-specific plasticity in the PPN. Rostral PPN neurons showed depolarized membrane potentials, broadened action potentials, and dendritic pruning, whereas caudal PPN neurons showed reduced spike frequency adaptation and accelerated excitatory postsynaptic current kinetics. While these PPN alterations do not have a previously established link with cellular vulnerability, synaptic and physiological changes in this region may have unexpected contributions to PD progression. In addition, these findings reveal novel mechanisms that could underlie nicotine's modulation of brainstem circuitry controlling arousal, sensory gating, and drug dependence.

Article.Authors: Rodríguez-Rangel S.; Coronado O.; Ortega B.; Sun Y.; El-Saadi S.; Brugarolas P.; Sánchez-Rodríguez J.
Article.Abstract: Aminopyridines, including 4-aminopyridine (4AP), 3,4-diaminopyridine, and [18F]3-fluoro-4-aminopyridine, are voltage-gated potassium (KV) channel blockers used clinically to enhance conduction in neurological disorders and to image demyelination by positron emission tomography (PET). Here, we characterized the physicochemical properties (pKa, logD), KV channel-blocking activity, toxicity (LD50), and pharmacokinetics of a novel compound, 4-methyl-3-aminopyridine (4Me3AP). 4Me3AP was less basic and more lipophilic than 4AP and showed greater blocking potency across multiple KV channels expressed in Xenopus oocytes. In mice, 4Me3AP exhibited lower acute toxicity (LD50 = 29.3 mg/kg) than 4AP (LD50 = 12.7 mg/kg) and a longer plasma half-life. These findings indicate that 4Me3AP is a potent KV channel blocker with favorable pharmacological properties, supporting its potential for symptomatic treatment of demyelinating diseases.

Article.Title: Molecular pathways implicated in antidepressant actions exhibits diurnal fluctuations in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus of adult male and female mice
Article.Authors: González-Hernández G.; Rozov S.; Berrocoso E.; Rantamäki T.
Article.Abstract: Epidemiological and experimental studies have demonstrated a bidirectional relationship between mood disorders and the circadian system, with disrupted circadian rhythms contributing to depressive states, and their restoration playing a key role in antidepressants effects. In this context, we sought to examine whether selected molecular pathways implicated in antidepressant responses exhibit diurnal regulatory patterns. Naïve adult male and female C57BL/6 mice were euthanized at 3-h intervals beginning at Zeitgeber Time 0 (ZT0), and hippocampal (HC) and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) tissues were collected for RT-qPCR and Western blot analyses. We observed statistically significant diurnal rhythmicity in all analyzed transcripts (cFos, Arc, Nr4a1, Dusp1, Dusp5, and Dusp6) in both HC and mPFC samples, with peak expression occurring during the dark (active) phase (ZT15-18). Phosphorylation levels of TrkBY816 (tropomyosin-related kinase) and GSK3βS9 (glycogen synthase kinase 3β) also showed patterns suggestive of temporal rhythmicity, peaking during the light (inactive) phase. Levels of p-ERK2T185/Y187 (extracellular-signal regulated kinase) did not display rhythmic fluctuations, but peaked during the light phase in the HC, especially in males. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that antidepressant-related signaling is subject to diurnal regulation, highlighting the importance of integrating circadian biology and time-of-day as relevant variables in the development of translationally relevant antidepressant research.

Article.Title: Structure-activity relationships of BnOCPA derivatives at native pre- and postsynaptic adenosine A1Rs
Article.Authors: la Mache C.; Preti B.; Wani M.; Lochner M.; Frenguelli B.; Wall M.
Article.Abstract: The addition of a benzyloxy group to the adenosine A1R agonist cyclopentyladenosine (CPA) produces a compound (BnOCPA) that selectivity activates A1R signalling via the G protein alpha subunit Gob. In rat hippocampus, BnOCPA inhibits CA3-CA1 synaptic transmission (IC50 65 nM) likely via Gob, with no effect on Goa-mediated postsynaptic membrane electrophysiology at concentrations up to 1 μM. We have investigated how modifications of the benzyloxy group of BnOCPA affects signalling: addition of methoxy group, MBnOCPA, substituting a phenoxy group, PhOCPA; and addition of bromide to the phenoxy group, BPhOCPA. These derivatives, previously shown to be selective A1R agonists, were assessed through inhibition of hippocampal CA3-CA1 synaptic transmission and postsynaptic effects on CA1 pyramidal neurons. All compounds inhibited synaptic transmission and increased paired-pulse facilitation, indicative of presynaptic actions. At a concentration that inhibited synaptic transmission (>75 %), none of the compounds hyperpolarised the resting membrane potential and thus retained the pre-vs postsynaptic selectivity of BnOCPA. Increasing their concentration allowed a measure of the selectivity range. BnOCPA hyperpolarised ∼40 % of neurons at 3 μM (∼50x the IC50 for synaptic inhibition). For PhOCPA and MBnOCPA, hyperpolarisation, occurred for some neurons, at 1 μM. For BPhOCPA, no hyperpolarisation occurred at concentrations up to 10 μM. Pre-application of the derivatives (at 300 nM) reduced adenosine-mediated hyperpolarisation, showing they bind but do not activate postsynaptic A1Rs. This data shows that modifying the structure of BnOCPA changes the discrimination between different native A1Rs, likely based upon selective activation of G-protein coupling.

Article.Title: Global Malat1 deletion in two genetic mouse models reveals sex-dependent effects on select ethanol-related behaviors
Article.Authors: Gil D.; Baratta A.; Ferguson C.; Miskanic M.; Iker A.; Homanics G.; Farris S.
Article.Abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a widespread psychiatric condition, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying its development remain poorly understood. While prior studies have largely focused on protein-coding genes, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) remain underexplored in AUD. Malat1, a highly abundant and evolutionarily conserved lncRNA, is elevated in post-mortem brain tissue of human AUD subjects and rodents chronically exposed to ethanol; however, its causal contribution to AUD-relevant behaviors remains unknown. Using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, we generated two complementary global Malat1 knockout mouse models to assess its role in ethanol intake and related phenotypes. Constitutive knockout selectively attenuated acute functional tolerance rate and every-other-day two-bottle-choice (EOD-2BC) ethanol intake in females. These results were supported by an inducible adult conditional global knockout model, which reduced EOD-2BC ethanol consumption in females without altering taste preference. Together, our findings provide the first causal evidence that Malat1 regulates select ethanol-related behaviors in a sex-specific manner, supporting further investigation into its underlying mechanisms in AUD.

Article.Title: Psychoneuroimmunology of glioblastoma: How emotional states shape tumor biology
Article.Authors: de Melo M.; Bezerra T.; de Souza P.; Sales V.; da Rosa M.
Article.Abstract: Psychological states profoundly influence physiological processes, with growing evidence linking emotional dysregulation to cancer progression. Within the framework of psychoneuroimmunology, recent findings have shown that chronic stress, depression and anxiety disrupt immune surveillance and promote a pro-inflammatory environment that favors tumor growth. Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), the most aggressive brain tumor, appears particularly sensitive to these neuroimmune influences. Some stress mediators and neurotransmitters-such as glucocorticoids and catecholamines- modulate the GBM microenvironment, fostering tumor-supportive pathways and epigenetic changes. This comprehensive review synthesizes evidence connecting emotional disturbances and glioma biology, highlighting shared neuroimmune mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities. We propose that integrating psychosocial and neuropharmacological strategies into GBM care could improve patients outcomes by targeting both tumor biology and emotional well-being.

Article.Title: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone increases dorsal premammillary nucleus neuron activity and darting behavior
Article.Authors: Coletta C.; Laing B.
Article.Abstract: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) is classically recognized for its role in regulating the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis; however, it also functions as a central neuromodulator influencing arousal, locomotion, and autonomic processes. Despite these established roles, the circuit-level mechanisms through which TRH modulates behavior remain poorly defined. The dorsal premammillary nucleus (PMd) is a hypothalamic structure implicated in high-imminence defensive states, yet whether TRH directly engages PMd circuits is unknown. Here, we assessed the role of TRH as a modulator of PMd neuronal activity and behavioral output using in situ hybridization, electrophysiology, calcium imaging, and behavioral assays in male and female mice. TRHR mRNA was co-localized with a subset of PMd CCK-positive neurons. TRH increased firing rate in a subset of PMd neurons in brain slices, revealing functional activation of a subset of the population. This finding was corroborated by calcium imaging that showed increased activity following TRH exposure. In vivo, intrahypothalamic administration of TRH produced darting and behavioral effects. Together, these findings identify a subpopulation of PMd neurons that serve as a functional hypothalamic target of TRH signaling associated with rapid locomotor behavioral output.

Article.Title: Deficiency of synaptotagmin 9 in the hippocampal region induces synaptic damage and cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease mice via BDNF/TrkB signaling
Article.Authors: Xu N.; Du C.; Li Y.; Yang W.; Li W.; Perez R.; Yu S.; Lou H.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive impairment is a prominent non-motor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD) that severely affects patients' quality of life, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the role of hippocampal Synaptotagmin 9 (Syt9) in PD-related cognitive deficits. We found that Syt9 expression was significantly downregulated in the hippocampus of both MPTP-induced subacute PD mice and A53T α-synuclein transgenic mice, concomitant with cognitive impairment and synaptic damage. To determine causality, we performed hippocampal Syt9 knockdown and overexpression using AAV-mediated gene delivery. Syt9 knockdown exacerbated, while Syt9 overexpression alleviated, cognitive deficits and synaptic structural abnormalities in PD mice. Proteomic sequencing and pharmacological manipulations revealed that Syt9 may regulate the BDNF/TrkB signaling pathway at the protein level, likely by influencing BDNF vesicular transport, release, or stability. Intra-hippocampal BDNF supplementation rescued synaptic damage and cognitive impairment, whereas the TrkB antagonist ANA-12 reversed the protective effects of Syt9 overexpression. Collectively, our findings identify the Syt9/BDNF/TrkB axis as a key mechanism in PD-related cognitive impairment and suggest that targeting this pathway may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for PD.

Article.Title: Gallic acid attenuates PTSD-like behavioral and hippocampal neuroplasticity deficits induced by single prolonged stress in male rats
Article.Authors: Meamar M.; Mohamadi Yarijani Z.; Parsaei H.; Vafaei A.; Rashidy-Pour A.; Raise-Abdullahi P.
Article.Abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with persistent cognitive and emotional disturbances linked to hippocampal dysfunction, oxidative stress, and impaired neuroplasticity. Gallic acid, a naturally occurring polyphenol, possesses antioxidant and neuroprotective properties, but its effects in trauma-related disorders remain incompletely understood. Male Wistar rats were subjected to single prolonged stress (SPS) to induce PTSD-like phenotypes and, beginning 24 h after SPS, received gallic acid (10 or 100 mg/kg) or saline for 14 days. Anxiety-like behavior, fear extinction, and spatial learning and memory were assessed using the elevated plus maze, contextual fear conditioning with extinction, and Morris water maze, respectively. Hippocampal oxidative stress markers (MDA, SOD, and TAC), BDNF protein expression, and CA3 dendritic morphology were evaluated. SPS exposure induced anxiety-like behavior, impaired fear extinction, and deficits in spatial learning and memory, accompanied by increased lipid peroxidation, reduced antioxidant capacity, decreased hippocampal BDNF expression, and CA3 dendritic atrophy. Early post-stress gallic acid administration attenuated these behavioral alterations and was accompanied by improvements in hippocampal oxidative status, BDNF expression, and CA3 dendritic morphology, without detectable effects on locomotor activity or relative adrenal gland weight. Collectively, these findings indicate that early post-stress gallic acid administration attenuates SPS-associated behavioral and hippocampal abnormalities and that these effects are associated with antioxidant and neuroplasticity-related changes rather than establishing a causal mechanism. Further studies using delayed treatment paradigms and pathway-specific approaches are needed to determine the efficacy of gallic acid after establishment of the PTSD-like phenotype and to clarify the mechanisms underlying its effects.

Article.Title: N-acetylcysteine decreases toluene conditioned place preference and modulates corticostriatal activity in adolescent rats
Article.Authors: Carampel A.; Asis J.; Munar J.; Gregorio C.; Medina P.; Quirk G.; Cena-Navarro R.
Article.Abstract: Inhalant (toluene) use disorder (IUD) continues to be a public health problem especially among Filipino adolescents. Animal models of IUD have not yet explored neurobiological changes from chronic toluene exposure, or possible treatments for long-lasting toluene-induced deficits. In rats repeatedly exposed to 3000 ppm of toluene vapor over 12 days, we report that daily administration of N-acetylcysteine (NACys; 100 mg/kg i.p. or 0.9 g/l oral), but not melatonin (10 mg/kg i.p.), during 8 days of abstinence reduced toluene conditioned place preference in both male and female adolescent Sprague Dawley rats. Using immunofluorescence, we found that toluene-exposed rats showed decreased c-Fos densities in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), dorsolateral striatum, and ventrolateral orbitofrontal cortex (vlOFC) after 8 days of abstinence. NACys partially rescued c-Fos expression in vlOFC. We found that c-Fos densities in both vlOFC and prelimbic cortex were significantly correlated with CPP values and with c-Fos densities in the DMS across treatment groups, suggesting that a history of toluene exposure may act by reducing cortical modulation of the dorsal striatum to promote long-lasting drug context seeking. Our findings suggest that NACys may be a promising treatment for IUD in adolescent males and females.

Article.Title: Cholinergic-dependent metaplasticity in the amygdala–insula pathway during incubation of cocaine craving
Article.Authors: Salin A.; Lardeux V.; Dugast E.; Balado E.; Thiriet N.; Jaber M.; Solinas M.; Belujon P.
Article.Abstract: The time-dependent increase in drug seeking during abstinence, termed 'incubation of craving' is believed to play a major role in the persistent risks of relapse. This phenomenon is associated with synaptic plasticity changes across brain structures involved in reward processing, executive functions, emotion regulation and inhibitory control. The basolateral amygdala (BLA) and the anterior insular cortex (aIC) are two interconnected structures involved in processing internal and external drug-related cues and are known to play a role in drug craving. However, whether chronic cocaine alters synaptic plasticity within the BLA-aIC circuit and how these changes evolve during abstinence remains unclear. Here, using cocaine self-administration and in vivo electrophysiological recordings in anesthetized male rats, we demonstrate that, while long-term potentiation in the BLA-aIC pathway remains intact, long-term depression is disrupted throughout abstinence in both cocaine- and sucrose-rats, indicating a persistent impairment in synaptic weakening mechanisms. Importantly, a loss of depotentiation was observed after late but not early abstinence, and was specific to cocaine self-administration, identifying it as a hallmark of incubation of craving. Systemic, but not local intra-aIC, blockade of muscarinic receptors with atropine restored depotentiation and reduced cocaine-seeking behavior. Finally, qPCR analysis revealed region-specific transcriptional adaptations, with upregulation of muscarinic, NMDA and AMPA receptor transcripts in the BLA and a selective decrease of Grin2a in the aIC. Together, these findings point to cholinergic regulation of BLA-aIC metaplasticity as a candidate mechanism underlying incubation of cocaine craving.

Article.Title: zDHHC11 is a common palmitoyltransferase regulating microglia-mediated neuroinflammation across neurodegenerative diseases
Article.Authors: Luo H.; Jiang D.; Hao Z.; Bu J.; Wang J.; Xu N.; Nie X.; Zhang Y.; Yin Q.; Zhuang P.
Article.Abstract: Purpose: Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is a shared feature across Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and diabetic cognitive impairment (DCI), but the convergent molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether protein S-palmitoylation serves as a common regulator of microglial neuroinflammation across distinct neurodegenerative diseases etiologies and aimed to identify the key palmitoyltransferase involved. Methods: In vivo ND models (APP/PS1 for AD, MPTP for PD, STZ/high-fat diet for DCI) and in vitro BV2 microglial models stimulated with amyloid-β (Aβ), lipopolysaccharide (LPS), or high glucose (HG) were established. Microglial morphology, inflammatory responses, and the TLR4/MyD88 pathway were assessed by immunofluorescence, RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, and ELISA. Protein palmitoylation levels were evaluated using 2-BP and ABE assays. Palmitoyltransferase expression profiling was performed, and protein-level validation was conducted both in vitro and in vivo. Subsequently, the identified common enzyme, zDHHC11, was knocked down by siRNA to determine its functional role. Results: All three ND models showed robust microglial activation with a pro-inflammatory amoeboid morphology. Aβ, LPS, and HG each upregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines and activated the TLR4/MyD88 pathway in BV2 cells. Palmitoylation inhibition with 2-BP attenuated cytokine production, and all three stimuli increased total protein palmitoylation. Among all palmitoyltransferases screened, zDHHC11 was uniquely and consistently upregulated by all three stimuli. This upregulation was further corroborated at the protein level, with elevated zDHHC11 expression observed both in cultured cells and in brain tissue sections. Knockdown of Zdhhc11 suppressed cytokine expression/secretion and reduced TLR4/MyD88 levels, indicating that zDHHC11 acts upstream of this common pathway. Conclusion: Protein S-palmitoylation mediated by zDHHC11 is a convergent mechanism driving microglial pro-inflammatory activation across distinct ND etiologies. zDHHC11 represents a common regulator of TLR4/MyD88-dependent neuroinflammation and a potential therapeutic target for multiple NDs.

Article.Title: Therapeutic potential and toxicological trade-offs of nanoparticle-enhanced valproic acid in glioblastoma: Behavioral and oxidative insights
Article.Authors: Khodayari N.; Sedghy F.; Ranjbar M.; Pashazadeh Azari P.; Houshmand F.; Shahrokhi Raeini A.; Mahmoodi M.; Bashiri H.; Kheirandish R.
Article.Abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a poor prognosis. In the current research, the therapeutic and behavioral efficacy of valproic acid (VPA) and its nanoparticles (Nano VPA) with or without temozolomide (TMZ) was investigated in the C6 glioblastoma rat model. Methods: We divided eighty-four adult male Wistar rats into seven groups (n = 12/group): sham, tumor, TMZ, VPA, nano VPA, VPA + TMZ, and nano VPA + TMZ. To induce tumors, C6 cells were injected into the brains of the rats. On days 12 to 15, behavioral performance was assessed using the social interaction test, elevated plus maze, open field, rotarod, and passive avoidance. On day 18, tumor size, edema, and histopathology were examined. Oxidative stress parameters in brain tissue and serum were measured by ELISA. Results: VPA and Nano VPA significantly inhibited tumor growth, either alone or with TMZ. All treatments except Nano VPA + TMZ improved survival compared with tumor controls. Treated groups showed enhanced anxiety regulation, sociability, learning, and memory. Motor coordination improved following VPA or Nano VPA therapy. Tumor induction reduced serum SOD, CAT, and TAC levels; treatments raised serum TAC and lowered brain MDA, but further reduced serum SOD. Conclusion: Our results suggest that oxidative stress modulation may contribute to the neurobehavioral and antitumor effects of both VPA and nano-VPA. While nano-VPA showed greater tumor reduction, conventional VPA was more effective in improving survival. Combining VPA with TMZ may enhance outcomes, and support further study of Nano VPA as an adjuvant therapy for GBM.
