Article.Abstract: Watermelon [ Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai] belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family and is widely cultivated for both fruit and seed-purpose. In India, indigenous seed-purpose watermelons, locally known as Mateera, Kalingada, or Karingada are predominantly grown in semi-arid regions such as Rajasthan and Gujarat. Unlike sweet dessert types, seed-purpose watermelons are less sweet but are valued for their edible, oil-rich seeds, culinary uses, medicinal properties, and use as animal feed. The present study was conducted using a randomized complete block design with twelve seed-purpose watermelon genotypes across four locations, namely Sardarkrushinagar (Gujarat), Sihori (Gujarat), Mandor (Rajasthan) and Jobner (Rajasthan), over the kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024, to identify stable and high-yielding seed-purpose watermelon genotypes using GGE biplot and WAASB analyses. Fruit yield and 100-seed weight were selected for stability analysis because they represent overall productivity and seed size, respectively. Combined analysis of variance revealed highly significant ( p < 0.001) effects of genotype, environment, and genotype × environment interaction (GEI) for both traits. In the GGE analysis, the first two principal components explained 78.63% (41.46% and 37.17%) of the G + GE variation for fruit yield and 59.69% (36.51% and 23.18%) for 100-seed weight. GGE biplot analysis integrating mean performance and stability identified SKNK-1704 as the most desirable genotype for fruit yield, followed by RMK-2. For 100-seed weight, SKNK-1407 achieved the best combined rank primarily because of its highest mean performance, despite intermediate stability, whereas GK-2 exhibited the greatest stability. The genotype NBPGRK-1 exhibited near-average performance for fruit yield and 100-seed weight, indicating its potential as a consistent performer across diverse environments. Additionally, genotype SKNK-2007 demonstrated broad adaptability for both fruit yield and 100-seed weight. The WAASB (50:50) index further confirmed SKNK-1704 and NBPGRK-1 as the superior genotypes for fruit yield, while NBPGRK-1, SKNK-1407, SKNK-2007, RMK-4, GK-2, and CAZJK-13-2 for 100-seed weight. Collectively, the integrated GGE biplot and WAASB analyses identified SKNK-1704 as a promising genotype for fruit yield, SKNK-1407 showed the highest combined performance for 100-seed weight, whereas NBPGRK-1 emerged as a promising dual-purpose candidate genotype across environments. These findings provide a basis for prioritizing genotypes for further validation and breeding evaluation in seed-purpose watermelon under hot semi-arid environments.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Genetics and Plant Breeding; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Genetics > Advances in Cucurbitaceae Research; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Agricultural Practices and Plant Genetics

Article.Title: Quantum similarity estimation with hybrid discrete-continuous encoding: algorithm and application to atomtronics precision measurements
Article.Authors: Jana S.; Raghav S.; Mehta V.; Roy U.
Article.Abstract: We introduce a quantum similarity estimation algorithm which employs an entangled discrete-continuous representation and a modified SWAP-test protocol using conditional displacement and controlled-SWAP operations. The corresponding exact form of the similarity metric is analytically derived and its feasible circuit implementation is provided. We apply this result to interferometric images, which are numerically generated from an experimentally viable atomtronics setup. A ring-shaped potential, confining a localized Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), is considered where the BEC manifests fractional revivals during its confined time-evolution. We perform a precise identification of nonlinearity, originated from interatomic interactions, which can be tuned by Feshbach resonance and thus, the presented method paves the possibility for a magnetic field sensor. Moreover, we perform quantum simulation with Shot-noise of the proposed quantum circuit with public benchmark datasets and analyse the resource and computational complexities of the proposed algorithm.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Quantum Computing Algorithms and Architecture; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Quantum Information and Cryptography; Physics and Astronomy > Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics > Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates

Article.Title: Dynamic event-triggered fractional-order super-twisting control for practical fixed-time quadrotor tracking under DoS attacks
Article.Authors: Li W.; Zhang Z.; Wan H.
Article.Abstract: Denial-of-service (DoS) attacks interrupt controller-to-actuator communication in quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), preventing timely control updates and degrading trajectory-tracking accuracy. External disturbances and limited communication bandwidth further complicate precise tracking under such attacks. To address these problems, a dynamic event-triggered fractional-order super-twisting control strategy is proposed to achieve practical fixed-time trajectory tracking under DoS attacks. First, a fractional-order sliding surface with nonsingular dual-power feedback is designed to improve the tracking performance of the position and attitude subsystems. Subsequently, a generalized super-twisting controller is constructed to enhance disturbance rejection and alleviate chattering. Considering the limited communication bandwidth during remote control, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism (ETM) with a strictly positive threshold floor is developed to reduce unnecessary command transmissions. An acknowledgment-based retry strategy is introduced to restore command updates after communication interruptions, while the actuator retains the most recently received command during the outage. Within the prescribed operating domain, Lyapunov analysis establishes practical fixed-time stability under DoS attacks for the closed-loop system on a prescribed compact set of initial conditions. Moreover, a strictly positive lower bound on successive transmission attempts is derived to exclude Zeno behavior. Finally, numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Adaptive Control of Nonlinear Systems; Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Stability and Control of Uncertain Systems; Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Distributed Control Multi-Agent Systems

Article.Title: Ex vivo IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-8 responses 2 years after critical COVID-19 are associated with age and innate immune activation
Article.Authors: Hiti L.; Kandušer M.; Burnik T.; Karas Kuželički N.; Farkaš Lainščak J.; Miholič M.; Pal E.; Lainscak M.; Mlinarič-Raščan I.; Markovič T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A cytokine storm drives critical COVID-19, yet the determinants and long-term consequences of this exaggerated inflammatory response remain unclear. We investigated whether cytokine responsiveness remains altered 2 years after recovery from critical disease. In a cohort of 117 individuals with mild, severe, or critical COVID-19, acute-phase clinical and laboratory parameters were analyzed in moderate–severe and critical cases. Long-term immune function was assessed by ex vivo stimulation of whole blood with PMA/ionomycin, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and phytohemagglutinin (PHA), followed by cytokine quantification and correlation with clinical parameters. A biobank of 76 patient-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCL cells) was established to evaluate the stability of cytokine responses. During acute illness, critically ill patients exhibited marked inflammatory dysregulation, including lymphopenia (72%), neutrophilia (51%), elevated neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios, and increased C-reactive protein (median 91 mg/L) and ferritin (median 1,153 μg/L), consistent with a hyperinflammatory–hypercoagulable phenotype. Two years post-infection, individuals with prior critical disease showed more than threefold higher secretion of IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-8 following PMA/ionomycin (p < 0.0001) and LPS stimulation (p < 0.05) compared with younger mild cases, whereas PHA-induced responses remained comparable. PBMC counts were also higher in the moderate–severe and critical groups 2 years post-infection (p < 0.001), highlighting differences in cellular composition. LCL cells from critically ill donors secreted 79% more IL-8 and TNF-α than those from mild cases (p < 0.05). Collectively, these findings indicate differences in cytokine responsiveness 2 years after COVID-19 which correspond to prior disease severity and are associated particularly with age and innate immune activation.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Infectious Diseases > COVID-19 Clinical Research Studies; Medicine > Neurology > Long-Term Effects of COVID-19; Medicine > Infectious Diseases > SARS-CoV-2 and COVID-19 Research

Article.Title: Dynamic construction behavior recognition through domain-adaptive multimodal evidence fusion
Article.Authors: Liu C.; Zhong C.; Li L.; Lian J.
Article.Abstract: Construction behavior recognition must remain reliable when acquisition conditions or participants differ from the training data. Existing adaptation can admit unsupported target samples, while multimodal fusion can become overconfident when streams are degraded, missing, or temporally misaligned. We propose reliability-coupled domain-adaptive evidence fusion (RDAEF), which derives a shared diagnostic state from signal quality, class-prototype distance, evidential uncertainty, open-set risk and, when multiple streams are available, temporal lag and opinion conflict. The shared state is mapped to a target-admission weight during training and modality-specific evidence discounts during inference. Evaluation uses two complementary configurations: the Construction Meta Action (CMA) benchmark supplies RGB clips for cross-condition adaptation, whereas the Scaffolding Worker IMU Time-series (SWIT) benchmark supplies synchronized pose and inertial sequences for cross-participant adaptation and multimodal fusion. RDAEF achieved target-domain macro-F1 scores of 0.798 on CMA and 0.783 on SWIT, exceeding the strongest unsupervised baselines by 3.4 and 5.9 percentage points, respectively. Removing conflict discounting increased the risk–coverage area (RCA) from 0.118 to 0.198, indicating poorer selective decisions.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Context-Aware Activity Recognition Systems; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Domain Adaptation and Few-Shot Learning; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Human Pose and Action Recognition

Article.Title: Climate change adaptation barriers among beekeepers across agroecological zones in Gedeo, Ethiopia: evidence from problem confrontation index and multinomial regression
Article.Authors: Mengistu E.; Kenea T.; Asfaw N.
Article.Abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens apiculture by reducing floral resources, water availability, and colony productivity. Although beekeepers adopt various adaptation measures, barriers to effective adaptation remain poorly understood across different agro ecological settings. This study examined the determinants and severity of climate change adaptation barriers among beekeepers across three agro ecological zones in Gedeo Zone, southern Ethiopia. A cross-sectional mixed-methods design was employed using data from 398 beekeeper households, complemented by 15 focus group discussions and key informant interviews. The Problem Confrontation Index (PCI) was used to prioritize adaptation barriers, while the Kruskal–Wallis H test assessed differences across agro ecological zones. Multinomial logistic regression identified socioeconomic and institutional determinants of perceived adaptation barriers. The most severe adaptation barriers were lack of improved beekeeping technology (PCI = 1056), lack of credit (PCI = 1047), water scarcity (PCI = 939), lack of training (PCI = 934), and shortage of bee-forage plants (PCI = 921). Significant agro ecological differences were observed for water scarcity ( p = 0.011), pests and diseases ( p = 0.017), and lack of finance ( p = 0.025), whereas most institutional and technological barriers were common across zones. Multinomial logistic regression revealed that age, sex, education, income, climate information, and particularly beekeeping practices significantly influenced the likelihood of experiencing different adaptation barriers ( p < 0.05). Climate change adaptation barriers in apiculture arise from interacting technological, financial, institutional, and environmental constraints. Strengthening access to improved beekeeping technologies, affordable credit, climate information, extension services, and training, while implementing agro ecology-specific interventions, is essential for enhancing the climate resilience and sustainability of beekeeping livelihoods in Ethiopia.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Ecology, Evolution, Behavior and Systematics > Climate change impacts on agriculture; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Insect Science > Insect and Pesticide Research; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Soil Science > Agricultural risk and resilience

Article.Title: Sequence-aware genotyping improves the accuracy of molecular markers associated with cassava mosaic disease resistance loci
Article.Authors: Krinsky K.; Sizani B.; Rey M.
Article.Abstract: Cassava ( Manihot esculenta ) is a critical food crop for sub-Saharan Africa. Cassava mosaic disease (CMD), caused by cassava geminiviruses, can severely reduce crop yield. Historically, CMD-resistance breeding has played a pivotal role in CMD management. Marker-assisted selection (MAS) for three CMD-resistance–associated quantitative-trait-loci (QTLs) (CMD1, 2 and 3) formed the basis for many elite cassava breeding lines currently deployed across Africa. Six molecular markers linked to these loci (SSRY40, SSRY28, NS158, NS169, RME1, and NS198) are still employed in contemporary CMD resistance breeding. False discovery in MAS for CMD resistance is frequently attributed to epistasis and recombination, but the contribution of size homoplasy remains under-researched. Sequencing and mapping of CMD-linked marker loci (MLs) revealed a substantial (10–20%) and significant ( p < 0.05) rate of homoplasy-induced false discovery. Furthermore, mapping revealed CMD-linked MLs in genic regions. Four putative CMD-response genes ( PDCD7 , HMGB1 , PP2A-B’δ and LOC128695772) were identified through transcriptional and ontological analyses of genes containing CMD-linked MLs. Based on a small but phylogenetically diverse collection of cassava germplasm, this study demonstrates the potential of sequence-aware marker genotyping to improve the efficiency of CMD-resistance breeding. Marker non-neutrality was identified as an additional source of error in CMD QTL-mapping and screening.
Article.Topic: Genetic Mapping and Diversity in Plants and Animals
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Genetics > Genetic Mapping and Diversity in Plants and Animals; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Cassava research and cyanide; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Plant Virus Research Studies

Article.Title: Physical exercise and esports performance: an updated systematic review and study-level meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Wu W.; Zhong Z.; Liu R.
Article.Abstract: Physical exercise has been proposed as a means of supporting esports-relevant cognition and gaming performance, but the evidence is heterogeneous and frequently reports multiple correlated outcomes. We updated a systematic review of controlled interventions and reconstructed the meta-analysis with the study as the independent unit. The original searches covered PubMed, Scopus and PsycINFO through May 2026; supplementary searching on 3 August 2026 identified additional controlled evidence, and the database/citation searches were rerun during revision through 4 September 2026, with no further eligible studies identified. Twelve controlled study clusters (660 enrolled or randomized; 608 reported analysed) were included. Nine evaluated exercise-only interventions; five estimable exercise-only studies (184 enrolled; 182 analysed) contributed 18 outcomes to quantitative synthesis after within-study aggregation (assumed between-outcome correlation rho = 0.50), whereas four exercise-only studies were synthesized narratively because compatible sampling variances or effect metrics were unavailable. The primary interpretive focus was placed on outcome domains: cognitive/psychomotor outcomes yielded Hedges' g = 0.465 (95% CI 0.073–0.856; k = 4), whereas gaming-specific outcomes were imprecise (g = 0.574, 95% CI − 0.002 to 1.150; k = 3). An exploratory cross-domain omnibus composite yielded g = 0.512 (95% CI 0.214–0.810; k = 5). Because only five of nine exercise-only studies were statistically convertible, this pooled signal may be affected by availability bias and does not summarize the complete eligible exercise evidence. Four additional exercise trials, two active-virtual-reality trials and one multicomponent trial were synthesized narratively. Evidence certainty was very low. Although I-squared and tau-squared were estimated as zero in the quantitative models, with only k = 3–5 independent studies these heterogeneity statistics have low power and should not be interpreted as evidence that effects are truly homogeneous across esports titles, exercise protocols or outcome constructs. Exercise may benefit selected cognitive or psychomotor outcomes relevant to esports, while evidence for improvement in actual gaming performance remains uncertain; the repeated-exercise subgroup (k = 2) is descriptive only, and no definitive performance prescription or acute-versus-repeated superiority claim is supported.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Physiology > Physical Activity and Health; Psychology > Developmental and Educational Psychology > Sport Psychology and Performance; Medicine > Orthopedics and Sports Medicine > Sports Performance and Training

Article.Title: Variable ontology and target-leakage screening in industrial PLC-SCADA data using name-based and behavioral evidence
Article.Authors: Şahin M.; Talu M.; Kürker F.; Onat C.; Öztürk M.; Dağ A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Contemporary cement plants measure thousands of PLC-SCADA variables, and the semantics of those variables is unclear, since the tags and labels are usually incomplete, inconsistent, and/or deceptive. The problem affects not only control-advisory systems but also data-driven models via inclusion of non-manipulated variables into the decision space or introduction of target-related variables resulting in leakage. In this paper, we propose the two-evidence variable ontology and leakage-auditing approach for industrial PLC-SCADA data. We combine name-based evidence, behavior-based signal evidence, expert validation for exceptional cases, and target-leakage auditing within a unified pre-modelling workflow. Within this workflow, the staircase score is used as a lightweight behavioral descriptor for distinguishing piecewise-constant setpoint-like signals from continuously varying measurements. The proposed approach is applied to the real industrial dataset of a cement clinker production line with 2.46 million samples, 375 variables, and 11 logged operational days. Among the 26 documented control parameters, eight exhibited actively changing setpoint behavior during the analyzed 11-day period, while one additional operational control was confirmed through process-engineering validation. Besides the label anomaly where the continuously changing signal is labeled as the setpoint, three leakage types for the industrial multivariate regression are considered in this paper: definitional/mass balance, component, and computed feature leakage. Removal of leakage drops the performance of the firing-calorie model from R² = 0.9999 to R² = 0.8109. Supplementary analyses showed that the behavioral separation of setpoint-like and continuous signals was unchanged under unsupervised (Otsu) threshold selection, was reproduced in two sub-periods with different logging rates, and required about 21 s for all 375 variables, with runtime scaling linearly with data size. A blinded annotation of all 375 variables by a second, independent process expert agreed with the final ontology for 89.3% of the variables (κ = 0.755) and assigned all nine control variables to CONTROL.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Fault Detection and Control Systems; Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Industrial Automation and Control Systems; Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Advanced Control Systems Optimization

Article.Title: Etiology of otitis media, antimicrobial susceptibility pattern and risk factors among under five children in Jimma, Oromia, Southwest Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Dabsu R.; Beyene G.; Mihret A.; Negash A.; Abebe G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Otitis media (OM) represents a major public health challenge and one of the most frequent causes of pediatric consultations worldwide. Although previous studies have investigated the prevalence of OM and antimicrobial resistance in Ethiopia, most were conducted before the widespread implementation of Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines or included all age groups rather than focusing specifically on under five years children. Continuous surveillance of the bacterial etiology spectrum and evolving patterns of bacterial antibiotic resistance is crucial to inform evidence-based prevention and treatment strategies. Therefore, this study was aimed to determine the etiology of bacterial OM, the distribution of pneumococcal serotypes, and the susceptibility pattern of isolates among under five children in Jimma city, Jimma, Oromia, Southwest Ethiopia. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 237 children suspected of having OM in Jimma City from March 01, 2023 to February 26, 2024. Interviewer based questionnaire was used to collect data. Middle ear discharges were collected, cultured and isolates were identified. Susceptibility tests were done using disk diffusion method. S. pneumoniae isolates from culture were extracted using alkaline lysis DNA extraction method as previously described. Amplification of autolysin ( lytA ) gene of S. pneumoniae was performed using primers lytA-F: 5’ CAACCGTACAGAATGAAGCGG-3’ and lytA-R; 5’TTATTCGT G CAATA CTCGTGCG-3’. Serotyping using oligonucleotide primers used in 41 conventional multiplex PCR assay. Data were summarized and presented in frequency table and while variables significant at p < = 0.25 in bivariate logistic regression were used in multivariable model to identify independent associations. Variables in the multivariable model were considered as significant at P < 0.05. Results were then reported as crude odds ratio (COR) and adjusted odds ratio (AOR) with 95% confidence interval (CI). The prevalence bacterial OM was 65.4% (155/237). Of the total growth, 13.5% (32/237) had polymicrobial growths while 52% (123/237) had monomicrobial growth. Of total the bacterial isolates, 58.7% (111/189) were Gram positive bacteria isolates while Gram negatives bacteria were 41.3% (78/189). Among the total isolates, the most frequently isolated species were S. aureus 54% (102/189), P. mirabilis 8.5% (16/189), and E. coli 5.3% 910/189). Prevalence of multidrug resistant (MDR) bacteria was 47.6% (90/189). Six serotypes/serogroups were identified among the S. pneumoniae isolates, with 66.7% (4/6) of them being non-vaccine serotypes. Rural individuals had a lower risk of OM ( p = 0.018), whereas those having history of allergies had a threefold higher risk of being positive ( p = 0.006). The prevalence of OM was high with alarming MDR isolates. Residence and history of allergies were significant predictors of OM. Periodic surveillance of bacterial OM and drug resistance patterns as well as risk factor reduction is warranted.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Otorhinolaryngology > Ear Surgery and Otitis Media; Medicine > Epidemiology > Pneumonia and Respiratory Infections; Immunology and Microbiology > Microbiology > Bacterial Infections and Vaccines

Article.Title: Psychosocial stress is associated with lipidomic gut microbial and brain connectivity differences relevant to cardiometabolic vulnerability
Article.Authors: Vignolle G.; Dong T.; Wang D.; Hung M.; Vora P.; Querol C.; Hernandez-Kapila A.; Gee G.; Church A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Discrimination-related chronic psychosocial stress is associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk through multisystem dysregulation. Stress-associated differences in gut microbial ecology, lipid metabolism, and intrinsic brain connectivity may contribute to cardiometabolic vulnerability, but integrated multiomic evidence remains limited. We studied 117 premenopausal women recruited from Los Angeles and stratified by Everyday Discrimination Scale (EDS) scores into higher (> 6, n = 64) and lower (≤ 6, n = 53) exposure groups. Participants completed clinical and psychological assessments, fasting blood and stool collection, and neuroimaging via MRI. Microbiome profiling targeted the V4 region of 16S rDNA; lipidomics was performed using LC–MS. Analyses included covariate-adjusted group models, exploratory cross-domain correlations, single-mediator mediation models, and moderation models. Participants with higher EDS scores exhibited higher anxiety, depression, perceived stress, and gastrointestinal-specific anxiety, together with lower mental and physical health scores. Lipidomic profiling identified lower Phosphatidylethanolamine and altered Phosphatidylcholine, fatty acids, Lysophosphatidylcholine, and Plasmenyl‑phosphatidylethanolamine species; total Phosphatidylserine was directionally lower but not significant in the group-level general linear model. Microbiome analyses identified higher Mollicutes RF39 and Ruminococcaceae UCG.009, whereas Prevotella 2 and Candidatus Stoquefichus showed directional but non-significant differences in this subset. Resting-state fMRI identified higher connectivity primarily among parieto-occipital/occipital region of interest (ROI) pairs and one supramarginal-insular connection. Mediation, moderation, and cross-domain correlation analyses yielded hypothesis-generating indirect-effect, interaction, and association signals involving selected microbial, lipidomic, and connectivity features. Because these analyses were exploratory and cross-sectional, they do not establish temporal ordering, biological pathways, or mechanistic mediation. Higher discrimination-related psychosocial stress was associated with psychological symptoms and selected microbial, lipidomic, and resting-state connectivity differences in premenopausal women. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to establish the reproducibility and temporal relationships of these findings.
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Gut microbiota and health; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Metabolomics and Mass Spectrometry Studies; Social Sciences > Health > Health disparities and outcomes

Article.Title: An explainable machine learning and human-computer interaction analytical framework for predicting learning outcomes in public music education in minority regions
Article.Authors: Du H.; Butkaew P.
Article.Abstract: Public music education in minority regions of Southwest China faces constraints related to educational resources and digital infrastructure. Integrating machine learning (ML) with human-computer interaction (HCI) offers a means of analyzing learning behaviors, perceived platform experience, and learning outcomes. This study develops and evaluates a theory-informed, ML-enhanced HCI analytical framework for predicting learning outcomes and identifying interpretable predictive patterns in public music education. The framework is predictive and diagnostic rather than intervention-based. Data were collected from 1,200 non-music-major students across four universities in Southwest China. XGBoost, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and a voting regressor were evaluated for predicting learning outcomes. SHAP was used for model interpretation, while adapted SUS- and NASA-TLX-informed measures assessed perceived HCI experience. Assessment-overlap-controlled modelling, leave-one-university-out validation, and university-level sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate predictive robustness and cross-institutional stability. Additional measurement-model analyses were used to assess the reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity of the adapted HCI measures. In the principal assessment-overlap-controlled analysis, XGBoost achieved R² = 0.736 for the examination-only outcome. For the composite final-score outcome, XGBoost achieved R² = 0.812 after predictors directly overlapping with assignment and participation components were removed. The full-feature models yielded higher performance, with the voting regressor achieving R² = 0.856 (RMSE = 4.18) and XGBoost achieving R² = 0.847; these higher estimates were interpreted cautiously because of predictor–criterion assessment overlap. For the same examination-only outcome and assessment-overlap-controlled predictor set, leave-one-university-out validation yielded a mean R² = 0.713 ± 0.028 across the four institutions. Adding university fixed effects changed test performance only slightly(R² = 0.742 versus 0.736 without university indicators). Video completion, assignment submission, and satisfaction were the leading factors associated with model predictions. Video completion showed an observed nonlinear region between approximately 50% and 70% in the fitted model rather than a validated intervention threshold. Frustration showed a statistically significant but very small association with performance (r = −0.087, p = 0.003) . A Welch heteroscedastic robustness analysis of ethnic-group final scores remained nonsignificant (F _ Welch(14, 156.8) = 1.37, p = 0.176); this finding does not establish ethnic-group equivalence, algorithmic fairness, or educational equity. The framework provides interpretable predictive evidence and generates evidence-informed platform-design hypotheses. Because the study is observational, it does not demonstrate causal effects, improvements in educational efficiency, or the effectiveness of the proposed design strategies. Its principal contribution lies in integrating multi-source predictive learning analytics, cross-institutional validation, and explainable model interpretation in an under-researched public music-education setting, rather than in demonstrating an implemented HCI intervention. Future research should use direct time-on-task measures and multi-region longitudinal or experimental validation.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Science Applications > Online Learning and Analytics; Arts and Humanities > Music > Diverse Music Education Insights; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Educational Technology and Pedagogy

Article.Title: Development and characterization of an Eugenol–Shilajit–Chitosan nano-gel composite with anticancer activity against oral squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Aati S.; Hamd A.; Alshamrani A.; Aljaber M.; Aati H.; Aboseada M.; Raslan M.; Ahmed O.; Hassan H.
Article.Abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) accounts for over 90% of oral malignancies and remains associated with high morbidity, recurrence, and poor long-term survival rates. To address these clinical challenges, the development of multifunctional nanotherapeutic systems capable of improving active stability and localized anticancer activity has become a vital focus in oral oncology and dental nanomedicine. The present study aimed to fabricate, structurally characterize, and biologically evaluate a novel Shilajit/Eugenol/Chitosan (SEC) biohybrid nanocomposite against human OSCC cell lines. The SEC nanocomposite was synthesized via homogenization and amalgamator-assisted mixing. Comprehensive physicochemical characterization (UV–Visible spectroscopy, FTIR, SEM, XRD, and zeta potential analysis) confirmed the successful incorporation and stabilization of shilajit and eugenol within the chitosan polymer matrix through intermolecular hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions. Dynamic light scattering revealed a monodisperse nanoscale distribution with an average particle size of 366.1 nm, accompanied by strong colloidal stability indicated by a highly positive zeta potential of + 47.3 mV. Biological profiling established that the SEC nanocomposite possesses robust radical-scavenging activity (ABTS IC 50 = 34.089 ± 0.93 µg/mL; ORAC = 39.784 ± 1.33 µM TE/L) alongside potent 5-lipoxygenase inhibitory action (IC 50 = 1.12 ± 0.03 µg/mL), confirming its dual antioxidant and anti-inflammatory capacity. MTT cytotoxicity assays demonstrated significant dose-dependent antiproliferative efficacy against human OSCC cell lines, displaying IC 50 values of 7.645 µg/mL (SCC-9), 4.687 µg/mL (SCC-15), and 3.702 µg/mL (SCC-25). Mechanistic flow cytometric analysis confirmed that this anticancer action was driven by marked G0/G1 phase cell cycle arrest and significant induction of apoptotic programmed cell death in SCC-25 cells. While these results provide strong in vitro proof-of-concept, the findings reflect preliminary cell line evaluations and warrant further validation in complex 3D culture platforms and in vivo models. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the developed SEC nanocomposite represents a highly effective, multifunctional nanoplatform with therapeutic potential for oral cancer treatment and localized dental applications.
Article.TopicFields: Pharmacology, Toxicology and Pharmaceutics > Pharmaceutical Science > Advanced Drug Delivery Systems; Materials Science > Biomaterials > Nanocomposite Films for Food Packaging; Materials Science > Biomaterials > Nanoparticle-Based Drug Delivery

Article.Title: Livestock farming dominates nitrogen and phosphorus loads under interannual rainfall variability in the Shaying River Basin
Article.Authors: Peng S.; Fang Y.; Zeng X.; Qin H.; Yan H.
Article.Abstract: Non-point source pollution (NPSP) poses a significant threat to water quality in the Shaying River Basin, yet the impacts of interannual rainfall variability and topographic factors on nutrient load estimations remain poorly understood. This study improved the Export Coefficient Model (ECM) by integrating rainfall and topographic factors to estimate total nitrogen (TN) and total phosphorus (TP) loads in the Henan section of the basin during a normal-flow year (2023, 830 mm) and a pluvial year (2024, 1010 mm). Monte Carlo simulations were employed to quantify the 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and assess uncertainties under varying hydrological conditions. The results showed that the enhanced model effectively captured the spatial heterogeneity of NPSP. During the wet year, the heavily and sub-heavily polluted zones expanded substantially, covering over 57% of the total basin area. Source apportionment revealed a marked structural shift: livestock and poultry breeding has replaced agricultural land use as the dominant contributor to both TN (76%) and TP (87.9%) loads in this basin, driven by China’s fertilizer reduction policies and the intensive livestock farming. Within the livestock sector, cattle farming dominated TN loads, while pig farming dominated TP loads. The 95% CIs for TN and TP were significantly wider in the wet year than in the normal year. This increased uncertainty indicates that NPSP loads are highly sensitive to rainfall anomalies. Our findings underscore the impracticality of fixed annual reduction targets under climate change. We propose a “flexible threshold” management framework, advocating for stricter controls during wet years and relaxed limits during normal years. The quantified CIs provide a robust scientific basis for implementing these climate-adaptive water quality strategies, offering critical insights for targeted NPS pollution mitigation in the face of increasing hydroclimatic extremes.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Environmental Chemistry > Soil and Water Nutrient Dynamics; Environmental Science > Water Science and Technology > Hydrology and Watershed Management Studies; Environmental Science > Water Science and Technology > Water Quality and Pollution Assessment

Article.Title: Evaluation of γδ T cells in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
Article.Authors: Cilek H.; Uysal C.; Aslan K.; Goren D.; Demiray A.; Eken A.; Kocyigit I.
Article.Abstract: We investigated alterations in peripheral adaptive immune cell subsets, particularly γδ T cells, in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). Fifty patients with ADPKD at different chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages and 12 healthy volunteers were enrolled. Peripheral blood T-cell subsets were analyzed by flow cytometry. Conventional CD4+, CD8+, and TCRγδ+ T cells were evaluated for frequency and cytokine production. Mean age of ADPKD patients was 48.3 ± 13.2 years. 31 patients (62%) had rapid disease progression. Total CD3+ T cell proportion did not differ, whereas the proportion of CD3+TCRγδ+ T cells was significantly lower (p = 0.012) in ADPKD patients (6.1% to 12.9% across CKD stages) than in healthy controls (15.1%). The proportion of CD3+TCRγδ+ T cells correlated positively with height-adjusted total kidney volume (p = 0.017) and inversely with eGFR (p = 0.006). Across CKD stages, significant differences were observed in cytokine production by T-cell subsets; including IFNγ, IL17A, TNFα, perforin, granzyme B. In rapid progression group, the proportions of CD8+ T cells (p = 0.025) and TCRγδ+ T cells (p = 0.001) were significantly higher, whereas the proportion of CD4+ T cells (p = 0.016) was significantly lower. Furthermore, among the evaluated T-cell variables, the frequency of CD3+TCRγδ + T cells was independently associated with rapid progression status (OR 1.182; 95% CI, 1.011–1.383; p = 0.036). Patients with ADPKD exhibit altered distribution and functional profiles of peripheral T-cell subsets, particularly reduced proportions of circulating of CD3+TCRγδ+ T cells and changes in cytokine production.
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Genetics > Genetic and Kidney Cyst Diseases; Immunology and Microbiology > Immunology > T-cell and B-cell Immunology; Medicine > Transplantation > Renal Transplantation Outcomes and Treatments

Article.Title: SCLC-SBT: a spectral-bilinear transformer for small cell lung cancer histopathology image classification
Article.Authors: Liang S.; Liang Y.; Zheng Q.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is among the most lethal thoracic malignancies, and timely and accurate histopathological classification is critical for guiding treatment decisions. Existing deep learning approaches face difficulty simultaneously capturing the high-frequency nuclear texture features characteristic of SCLC—such as hyperchromatic salt-and-pepper chromatin and dense nuclear moulding—and the long-range spatial dependencies of tissue organisation, limiting classification reliability. To address these challenges, this study proposes SCLC-SBT, a hierarchical Spectral-Bilinear Transformer for automated SCLC histopathological image classification. The network deploys re-parameterizable Hybrid-Conv Blocks (HCB) with frequency-domain Spectral-Channel Attention (SCA) in the first three stages to extract fine-grained multi-scale local features, and employs a novel Dual-Branch Conv Linear Integration Transformer (DBCLIT) in the deepest stage to jointly model local morphology and long-range dependencies via bilinear selective state space modelling. Evaluated on a 1,974-image binary classification benchmark comprising Normal and SCLC tissue patches, SCLC-SBT achieves 0.9697 accuracy (95% CI 0.9495 to 0.9865), 0.9728 F1-score, and 0.9971 AUC, attaining the best point estimate among eleven compared architectures including DeiT, MLP-Mixer, DaViT, and CAFormer on five of the seven reported metrics. Bootstrap confidence intervals and pairwise McNemar’s tests indicate that this advantage is statistically significant relative to five of the eleven baselines. Relative to the six strongest baselines, DeiT, MLP-Mixer, CAFormer, Swin-T, and the tied PoolFormer and DaViT pair, the difference is not statistically significant at $$\alpha =0.05$$ on the 297-sample test set, so SCLC-SBT is best interpreted as achieving competitive to superior accuracy at a substantially better accuracy-efficiency trade-off while maintaining competitive model efficiency with approximately 17 M parameters and 7.0 G FLOPs. The results demonstrate that integrating spectral-domain channel recalibration with bilinear state space modelling provides an effective inductive bias for SCLC histopathological feature learning.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > AI in cancer detection; Medicine > Radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Imaging > Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Digital Imaging for Blood Diseases

Article.Title: Effect of quarry dust particle sizes on the mechanical and microstructural properties of concrete
Article.Authors: Obianyo I.; Umar A.; Dayyabu A.; Sanusi A.; Agbili M.; Onyelowe K.; Hanande S.; Kamchoom V.
Article.Abstract: Natural river sand is becoming scarce and harmful to the environment due to excessive mining and consumption in the built environment. Quarry dust is obtained from crushing stones and is often treated as waste, but it can be used to replace natural river sand in concrete. The research focuses on examining the effects of quarry dust particle sizes on the microstructural and mechanical properties of concrete. This study examines the effects of different quarry dust particle-size fractions obtained through sieve classification, with sieve sizes of 2.36 mm, 1.18 mm, 600 μm, 300 μm and 150 μm, on the mechanical and microstructural properties of concrete. Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) were used to study the microscopic properties of the specimens. Some preliminary tests were also carried out including extracting different particle sizes and specific gravity. This study also tested the strength of the concrete to see how well it performs at different curing times of 7days, 14days and 28days. The results show that quarry dust with a particle size of 600 μm produced the highest compressive strength and dry density, indicating better particle packing and improved bonding. Microstructural tests also confirmed the presence of hydration-related compounds and more compact internal structure in this sample. This study concludes that quarry dust is a sustainable alternative to natural river sand, and that its particle size significantly influences the strength and internal structure of concrete.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Mechanical Engineering > Materials Engineering and Processing; Engineering > Building and Construction > Recycled Aggregate Concrete Performance; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Concrete and Cement Materials Research

Article.Title: Metabolic syndrome and colorectal cancer share GPAT3 and PLAU as candidate genes: Mendelian randomisation, machine learning, single-cell knockout and docking
Article.Authors: Zhou L.; Hou Y.; Zhang L.; Han C.; Liao M.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) associates with colorectal cancer (CRC), but the direction and linking nodes are unresolved. We integrated bidirectional Mendelian randomisation (MetS as a latent genetic liability), MetS–CRC transcriptomic intersection, machine-learning prioritisation, immune deconvolution, single-cell virtual knockout and docking. MR supported a MetS-to-CRC effect (inverse-variance-weighted OR = 1.231, 95% CI 1.052–1.439, P = 0.0093); the reverse direction was non-significant and, with only seven instruments, inconclusive. The transcriptomes shared 200 co-differentially expressed genes, 36 within a TNF/NF-κB prior set from MSigDB hallmark founder sets. Of seven hubs retained by all three algorithms, GPAT3 and PLAU were significant in both GSE10950 and TCGA/GEPIA2, GPAT3 being directionally concordant between the MetS and CRC contrasts and PLAU concordant only across tumour platforms. GPAT3 virtual knockout perturbed blood-vessel morphogenesis, extracellular-matrix organisation and myeloid activation. PLAU correlated most strongly with tumour neutrophils ( r = 0.376). Docking of three ligands against the PLAU catalytic domain predicted binding for all three, strongest for AGB (N-(1-adamantyl)-N′-(4-guanidinobenzyl)urea) and amiloride. These findings are consistent with a causal MetS-to-CRC direction (robust to MR-PRESSO outlier correction and MR-RAPS, and placed in context by multivariable MR) and nominate GPAT3 and PLAU as candidate nodes for testing.
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Cancer Research > Cancer, Lipids, and Metabolism; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Genetics > Genetic Associations and Epidemiology; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Bioinformatics and Genomic Networks

Article.Title: Experimental investigation on the performance of waste plastic-modified hot mix asphalt in dry and wet processes
Article.Authors: Desta S.; Getahun B.; Asamenew Z.; Gudeta L.
Article.Abstract: Waste plastic materials have become a current environmental issue, while conventional flexible pavement designs need to improve their appreciable pavement performance by incorporating compatible waste Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) plastic materials as a bitumen binder modifier. A study experimentally investigated the performance of waste PET plastic-modified hot-mix asphalt in dry and wet processes. The selected plastic material as a partial replacement of bitumen binder of the hot mix asphalt (HMA) is polyethylene terephthalate (PET). Tests based on international test techniques are addressed for bitumen, aggregates, and PET waste plastic materials processing. Gradation, specific gravity, water absorption, aggregate crushing value, flakiness, and soundness are among the tests for aggregates, while specific gravity, ductility, penetration, and softening point tests were bitumen tests established to meet the specifications set in the standards by ASTM, AASHTO, BS, and ERA (Ethiopian Road Authority). After characterization of the materials, the conventional Marshall Mix design of the hot mix Asphalt was performed to get the optimum plastic content of dry and wet processes plastic-modified hot mix asphalt. Plastic-modified asphalt mixture tests, such as moisture susceptibility, flow, volumetric properties, Marshall Stability, indirect tensile strength, and rutting resistance, were conducted and evaluated with respect to the controlled conventional asphalt mixtures. The plastic modified HMA resulted with amended tensile strength, Marshall Stability, and resistance to moisture compared with the conventional control HMA. Under the experimental conditions investigated, Plastic Modified HMA in the wet Process showed uniform binder modification, but the dry process resulted in better stability. The results indicate modified hot mix asphalt with optimum PET plastic content showed enhanced mechanical properties, which can improve its performance and engineering application of the HMA pavement. Later on, optimization of dry and wet process performances was conducted. The methods to optimize these processes, multi-criteria decision analysis, particularly TOPSIS, are implemented. The closeness coefficients of the dry and wet process are 0.97, and 0.49 respectively. Within the scope of this study, the dry process has greater value hence it is selected for its performance over the wet process. Therefore, PET plastic-modified HMA enhanced the Engineering performance of flexible pavement.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Asphalt Pavement Performance Evaluation; Engineering > Mechanical Engineering > Materials Engineering and Processing; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Geotechnical and construction materials studies

Article.Title: An integrated machine learning framework for accurate, real-time and non-destructive vitamin C quantification from Vis/NIR spectral data
Article.Authors: Pourali S.; Afkari-Sayyah A.; Taghinezhad E.; Motevali A.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a hybrid framework integrating feature selection and regression modeling for the nondestructive prediction of vitamin C, soluble solids content, and firmness in dried kiwifruit. Within this framework, the spectra of 250 dried kiwifruit samples were acquired using visible–near-infrared spectroscopy over the wavelength range of 470–980 nm. Four feature selection methods, including the ant colony optimization algorithm, competitive adaptive reweighted sampling, genetic algorithm, and minimum redundancy–maximum relevance, were employed to identify and compare the most informative wavelengths. Thirty wavelengths selected by each method were subsequently used as input variables for four regression models, namely partial least squares regression, random forest, support vector regression, and extreme gradient boosting. Model performance was evaluated during the validation stage using the coefficient of determination (R 2 ), root mean square error, and residual predictive deviation. The results showed that, for the prediction of vitamin C and soluble solids content, the combination of SVR with ACO achieved the highest validation performance, with RPD values of 5.52 and 5.17, respectively. In contrast, for firmness prediction, the combination of PLSR and CARS exhibited more stable predictive performance, yielding a validation R 2 of 0.91, RMSE of 0.43, and RPD of 3.50. Comparison of the feature selection methods also enabled an assessment of the degree of overlap among the selected wavelengths and their potential roles in predicting different quality attributes of dried kiwifruit. These findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of feature selection depends on both the target quality attribute and the type of regression model, and that integrating appropriate feature selection methods with suitable regression algorithms can improve the nondestructive prediction of quality attributes in dried kiwifruit. Future studies should employ larger and independent datasets and evaluate the proposed framework under real-world and online conditions to further assess its generalizability and practical applicability
Article.TopicFields: Chemistry > Analytical Chemistry > Spectroscopy and Chemometric Analyses; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Smart Agriculture and AI; Medicine > Radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Imaging > Optical Imaging and Spectroscopy Techniques

Article.Title: RSTNet: sandstorm image enhancement using a residual saturation and transmission estimation network
Article.Authors: Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The degradation of sandstorm images is diverse, as it encompasses color casting and dark and dim conditions. In addition, because the structural degradation of sandstorm images involves imbalanced color channels, an image may seem yellowish or reddish. Moreover, when an image is obtained, because the atmosphere contains various hazy particles such as sand, the sand in the image may seem hazy. The existing sandstorm image enhancement methods improve the image’s color components and mitigate the hazy effect. However, an artificial color component may appear when the enhanced color channels are imbalanced. Therefore, in this paper, an effective color balancing method using convolutional neural networks and image saturation is proposed because image saturation is strongly related to color information. Additionally, a color-balanced image may be hazy because of the presence of hazy particles; thus, in this paper, hazy images are enhanced using transmission networks for dehazing. Overall, a sandstorm image enhancement method using a convolutional neural network that estimates residual saturation and a transmission estimation network (RST-Net) is proposed. The enhanced images obtained using the RSTNet appear natural, and the RSTNet is verified to be suitable for enhancing degraded sandstorm images.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Image Enhancement Techniques; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Image Processing Techniques; Engineering > Media Technology > Image Processing Techniques and Applications

Article.Title: Evaluating the impact of renewable resource data imputation on technoeconomic design of coastal multivector nearly zero energy buildings
Article.Authors: Niu J.; Mostafa L.; Hammour R.; Alshammari S.; Shaban M.; Singh N.
Article.Abstract: Gaps in high-resolution solar and wind records are usually filled before a building energy system is sized, yet the effect of the imputation method on the design is rarely tested. Here, eleven statistical, time-series and learning-based imputation techniques were applied to minutely irradiance and wind-speed series for a hydrogen-integrated coastal nearly zero energy building in Dalian, China, under four missingness levels (5–80%) and two gap patterns. A dual validation combined the root mean square error (pointwise accuracy) with the Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic (distributional fidelity), and the reconstructed series were propagated into off-grid and grid-connected capacity optimization. The two metrics ranked the methods differently, and neither predicted design stability alone. At 80% missingness, annualized-cost deviations ranged from −36% to +95% off-grid, with battery oversizing near 400% for smoothing-dominated methods, while four methods stayed within ±5%. Grid connection capped the worst-case cost penalty at 38% but did not reduce typical deviations; instead, it concealed battery undersizing exceeding 20% for eight methods. A repeated-realization benchmark showed that gap placement, not optimizer noise, dominated variability and that cheaper design from low-error reconstructions violated reliability limits on the true weather. Imputation for design-critical studies should be validated jointly by statistical, capacity and reliability criteria.‬‬‬.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Building and Construction > Building Energy and Comfort Optimization; Energy > Energy Engineering and Power Technology > Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Integrated Energy Systems Optimization

Article.Title: Testing psychological hardiness as a mediator between job satisfaction and mental workload among healthcare personnel in obstetrics and gynecology
Article.Authors: Güney M.; Sarıboğa Y.
Article.Abstract: The relationships among job satisfaction, psychological hardiness, and mental workload among healthcare personnel working in gynecology and obstetrics clinics remain insufficiently understood. To examine the proposed mediating role of psychological hardiness in the relationship between job satisfaction and mental workload among the healthcare personnel working in gynecology and obstetrics clinics. This cross-sectional study included 183 healthcare professionals working in gynecology and obstetrics clinics at a training and research hospital in eastern Turkey. Data were collected using a sociodemographic form, the Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire, the Mental Workload Scale, and the Psychological Hardiness Scale. The proposed mediation model was examined using observed-variable path analysis with maximum likelihood estimation and 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Job satisfaction was positively associated with psychological hardiness (β = 0.439, p < 0.001) and negatively associated with mental workload after accounting for psychological hardiness (β = −0.276, p < 0.001). Psychological hardiness was not significantly associated with mental workload after accounting for job satisfaction (β = 0.094, p = 0.240). The indirect effect was not statistically significant (B = 0.025, bias-corrected bootstrap 95% CI: −0.019 to 0.076, p = 0.228). The model explained 19.3% of the variance in psychological hardiness and 6.2% of the variance in mental workload. Higher job satisfaction was associated with lower mental workload and greater psychological hardiness. The findings did not support the proposed mediating role of psychological hardiness. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationships among these variables.
Article.TopicFields: Psychology > Social Psychology > Stress and Burnout Research; Business, Management and Accounting > Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management > Job Satisfaction and Organizational Behavior; Nursing > Leadership and Management > Healthcare Education and Workforce Issues

Article.Title: Comparative assessment of the significance of designed pavement properties for road quality conditions
Article.Authors: Sivilevičius H.; Tamošaitienė J.; Šernas O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pavement is one of the most important elements of road transport infrastructure interacting with travelling vehicles. Its suitability for traffic is defined by required properties of varying significance that remain understudied. Therefore, this study examines three main criteria: pavement resistance, driving conditions and environmental protection (including sustainability). A team of 33 experts assessed the influence of 12 sub-criteria on overall road quality. To ensure an objective solution, the relative weights of these criteria and their sub-criteria were determined using four methods: the Average Rank Transformation into Weight-Linear (ARTIW-L), Average Rank Transformation into Weight-Non-linear (ARTIW-N), Direct Percentage Weight (DPW) and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The study utilised the relative weight averages yielded by these four approaches. The AHP method was used to compare the results of the experts’ calculations. No conflicting AHP matrices were found, as the consistency ratio of each matrix was less than 0.1. Furthermore, the coefficient of concordance of 0.654 indicated the consistency of the expert judgements, exceeding the critical threshold of 0.054 by approximately 12 times. The study results revealed the most, intermediate and least important pavement indicators according to the experts. Based on the Inverse Hierarchy for Assessment of Main Criteria Importance (IHAMCI) method, pavement resistance is the most important factor, accounting for approximately 53% of pavement resistance, whereas driving conditions and environmental protection accounted for 31% and 16%, respectively.
Article.TopicFields: Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Multi-Criteria Decision Making; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Asphalt Pavement Performance Evaluation; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Transportation Systems and Logistics

Article.Title: Maternal supplementation of hydroxy-analogue of selenomethionine strengthens offspring intestinal tight junction by activating Wnt/β-catenin signal and inhibition of apoptosis in intestinal epithelial cells
Article.Authors: Ding D.; Qin B.; Wen W.; Pu J.; Wu Y.; Tian Y.; Mou D.
Article.Abstract: The intestinal barrier is pivotal for systemic homeostasis, with its dysfunction implicated in numerous gastrointestinal pathologies. This study elucidates effects and mechanisms by which maternal hydroxy-analogue of selenomethionine (2-hydroxy-4-methylselenobutanoic acid, HMSeBA) supplementation augments intestinal defense in offspring. Employing complementary in vivo and in vitro approaches, sows received HMSeBA during gestation period, and jejunal tissues from neonatal/weaned offspring were analyzed. In vitro, IPEC-J2 intestinal epithelial cells were treated with HMSeBA to recapitulate maternally transferred effects, followed by H 2 O 2 challenge to induce oxidative stress. Maternal HMSeBA enhanced offspring intestinal barrier integrity, demonstrated by elevated expression of tight junction proteins (occludin, Zo-1), attenuated oxidative damage through enhanced glutathione peroxidase activity in weaned piglets (postnatal day 28) after LPS infection, and suppressed H 2 O 2 -triggered apoptosis in IPEC-J2 cells. Mechanistically, HMSeBA potentiated cellular antioxidant defenses via increase glutathione peroxidase activity, thereby inhibiting excessive apoptosis in intestinal cells, while concurrently facilitating β-catenin nuclear translocation and upregulating Wnt/β-catenin targets (TCF4, LEF1), thereby preserving epithelial barrier integrity. These findings identify HMSeBA as a novel maternal nutritional strategy that coordinates redox homeostasis and proliferative signaling to fortify intestinal resilience, providing a translational framework for preventing early-life enteropathies.
Article.TopicFields: Nursing > Nutrition and Dietetics > Selenium in Biological Systems; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Animal Science and Zoology > Animal Nutrition and Physiology; Nursing > Nutrition and Dietetics > Trace Elements in Health

Article.Title: Non-volatile, compact, and broadband multimode matrix vector multiplication for photonic neuromorphic computing
Article.Authors: Atri A.; Zarifkar A.
Article.Abstract: Matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) is a fundamental operation in artificial neural networks. While conventional electronic implementations of MVMs face bottlenecks in speed and energy efficiency, here, we design an ultra-compact (185 μm × 21 μm) non-volatile photonic MVM engine leveraging mode division multiplexing (MDM) with the fundamental and first-order transverse magnetic modes. The architecture integrates a multimode-interferometer power splitter (0.98 dB insertion loss), a directional-coupler (de)multiplexer (≈ -10 dB crosstalk suppression, 0.87 dB insertion loss), a weighting core comprising four independently programmable weighting paths, each containing five Ge 2 Sb 2 Se 4 Te 1 (GSST) phase-change cells in series, giving twenty cells in total. By electrically programming individual GSST cells between amorphous and crystalline states, the device supports 1296 distinct matrix configurations with an extinction ratio of 11.29 dB and 17.3 dB for TM0 and TM1 modes, respectively. Electro-thermal simulations indicate ultrafast and reversible switching using a 5 V and 33 ns pulse for crystallization, while a 12 V and 5 ns pulse triggers melting and rapid quenching for amorphization. The non-volatile nature of GSST eliminates static power consumption, enabling energy-efficient operation. The complete MVM exhibits a total insertion loss of 2.76 dB and 3.64 dB at 1550 nm for TM0 and TM1 modes, respectively. This device maintains functionality across a 40 nm bandwidth (1540–1580 nm), offering a scalable pathway for energy-efficient, MDM-enabled photonic computing.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Neural Networks and Reservoir Computing; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Photonic and Optical Devices; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Advanced Memory and Neural Computing

Article.Title: Securing intelligent transportation systems in the internet of vehicles through an AI-driven intrusion detection framework
Article.Authors: Alshammari S.; Malekzadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) with modern vehicles has transformed transportation systems into intelligent, interconnected Internet of Vehicles (IoV) networks. However, this integration increases the attack surface, exposing IoV networks to threats that compromise operational reliability and passenger safety. This work introduces a configurable simulation platform for designing and evaluating IoV networks across diverse topologies and network parameters under normal and adversarial conditions. The platform supports multiple Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks across the communication stack, including application-layer Slowloris and HTTP, transport-layer SYN and UDP, and reflection-based DNS and NTP amplification. It incorporates a dataset-generation module that captures IoV behavior under benign and adversarial conditions to support training and evaluation of security models. Using these datasets, an AI-based detection framework is developed using machine learning, deep learning, and transformer models. A multi-layer evaluation combining communication and AI classification metrics demonstrates the platform’s capability to model complex IoV behavior and support security methods. It further measures deployment trade-offs involving inference latency and communication-energy cost, which reflect the practical constraints of resource‑limited devices. Experimental results show that amplification attacks are the most destructive, while cellular topology demonstrates the highest resilience, with 56.5% loss, whereas VANET and Manhattan show 87.5% loss. Under edge constraints, transformer models achieve 92–93% recovery but incur 136–181 ms inference latency, deep learning achieves 89–91% recovery with 17–45 ms latency, and machine learning provides 72–87% recovery with the lowest latency of 12–27 ms, highlighting the trade-off between detection capability and computational overhead.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Network Security and Intrusion Detection; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs); Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Adversarial Robustness in Machine Learning

Article.Title: De novo transcriptomic analysis reveals salicylic acid-induced biosynthesis of vinblastine and vincristine in undifferentiated Catharanthus roseus callus
Article.Authors: Patel A.; Chandra M.; Thakor A.; Patel R.; Patel R.; Tiwari B.; Sharma A.
Article.Abstract: Catharanthus roseus is a pharmaceutically important medicinal herb known for being the sole natural source of the anticancer dimeric alkaloids vinblastine and vincristine, synthesized via the complex monoterpenoid indole alkaloid (MIA) biosynthetic pathway. The in-planta accumulation of these alkaloids is exceedingly low, primarily due to their intrinsic cytotoxicity and the strict spatiotemporal regulation of MIA biosynthesis, which spans at least four distinct cell types (epidermis, internal phloem associated parenchyma, laticifers, and idioblasts) and five intracellular compartments (chloroplast, vacuole, nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytosol). Previous studies demonstrated that only differentiated multiple shoot cultures of C. roseus can biosynthesize vinblastine and vincristine, whereas undifferentiated systems such as cell suspensions, callus, and hairy roots lack the necessary cellular compartmentalization required for dimeric MIA synthesis. However, limited evidence suggests that abiotic elicitors may activate the latent biosynthetic machinery in callus tissues. In the present study Salicylic acid (SA) elicitation significantly enhanced MIA biosynthesis in C. roseus callus cultures. RNA-seq analysis of callus cultures treated with potassium chloride (3 g/l, 5 g/l), Salicylic Acid (5 mM, 15 mM), and succinic acid (5 mM, 15 mM) treatments identified 12,555 DEGs under SA 5 mM, with strongest activation of MIA pathway genes including TDC, SLS, STR, LAMT, G10H, CrHL2, and late-stage vindoline enzymes. qRT-PCR confirmed 3–8-fold induction of key genes mirroring RNA-seq trends. SA treatments uniquely activated PRX1 peroxidase isoforms essential for vindoline-catharanthine coupling to vinblastine/vincristine. These findings demonstrate SA's superior efficacy in enhancing C. roseus MIA biosynthesis compared to salt or metabolic stress, enabling the biosynthesis of vinblastine and vincristine in an undifferentiated system previously thought to lack this capacity. These findings establish a framework for elicitor-based enhancement of anticancer alkaloid production.

Article.Title: An adaptive transformer-based model with entropy-driven knowledge distillation for single-channel EEG REM sleep detection
Article.Authors: Huang J.; Chen S.; Dwiwahyono I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate detection of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep is critical for neurophysiological monitoring and early identification of sleep-related disorders. An entropy-driven adaptive knowledge distillation framework integrated with a lightweight Transformer was developed to support robust REM sleep detection from single-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. By dynamically adjusting temperature scaling and distillation weighting based on teacher–student entropy, the proposed approach explicitly models uncertainty inherent in REM sleep. When evaluated under subject-independent cross-validation on three public datasets (Sleep-EDF, ISRUC-Sleep, and MASS), the proposed model outperformed CNN, LSTM, and standard Transformer baselines, achieving an average accuracy of 93.2% and an F1 score of 92.8%. Moreover, the distilled student model reduced training time and memory usage by approximately 30%, indicating potential suitability for future optimization toward real-time and wearable EEG applications. These results suggest that uncertainty-aware adaptive distillation may support accurate and computationally efficient REM sleep detection from single-channel EEG under subject-independent experimental conditions.
Article.TopicFields: Neuroscience > Cognitive Neuroscience > EEG and Brain-Computer Interfaces; Psychology > Experimental and Cognitive Psychology > Emotion and Mood Recognition; Medicine > Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine > ECG Monitoring and Analysis

Article.Title: FABWF-LGAR: Fully adaptive Bi-modal weighted fusion with lightweight gated attention refinement for efficient camera-LiDAR 2D object detection
Article.Authors: Dodda S.; Arunachalam M.
Article.Abstract: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) engage multi-modal sensor data, including cameras and LiDAR, to recognize their environment accurately. However, fusing various sensor data while maintaining computational efficiency is yet major research. This work introduces Feature-Adaptive Bidirectional Weighted Fusion with Lightweight Gated Attention Refinement (FABWF-LGAR), a lightweight framework created to proceed multimodal sensor fusion for autonomous driving. The proposed work syndicates feature from different sensors with a bidirectional weighted fusion method that differs the contribution from each type of data. A lightweight gated attention enhancement module is fused to focus on suitable spatial and semantic features while reducing noise and redundant information. The proposed method increases the quality of the fused data without raising the computational complexity. The framework directs to enhance perception tasks in ADAS, like object detection and scene recognition, while being suitable for real-time use on resource-limited vehicles. The proposed FABWF-LGAR achieves 55.93% mAP@0.5 on the KITTI validation set, outperforming camera-only and LiDAR-only baselines by 34.5 and 50.7 percentage points, respectively. Experimental results show that this fusion policy specifies stronger and more efficient feature integration compared to traditional methods, highlighting its potential for real-world autonomous driving systems.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Automotive Engineering > Autonomous Vehicle Technology and Safety; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Vision and Imaging

Article.Title: Rolling optimal dispatch method for virtual power plants integrating secondary and tertiary frequency regulation
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Zhu L.; Ren X.; Zhang L.; Zhu Q.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: The demand side of modern power systems contains abundant flexible resources that, when aggregated via virtual power plants (VPPs), can help alleviate the grid’s frequency regulation (FR) burden. In this paper, we propose a rolling optimal dispatch method for VPPs integrating secondary and tertiary frequency regulation. First, the adjustable capacity of various distributed energy resources (DERs) is quantified by accounting for their operational characteristics and the effects of uncertainty. Secondly, the technical characteristics and market mechanisms of secondary and tertiary frequency regulation are analyzed to formulate objective functions for DERs to jointly participate in these services, as well as the response strategy. Finally, based on the proposed strategy and optimization model, a two-stage day-ahead and intra-day rolling optimal dispatch is implemented, and the NSGA-II algorithm is employed to achieve Pareto frontier solutions. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed response strategy and multi-objective optimization model can fully exploit the regulatory potential of DERs, enabling rolling optimal dispatch for FR and dynamic adjustments to strategy parameters.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Smart Grid Energy Management; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Electric Power System Optimization; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Frequency Control in Power Systems

Article.Title: Intelligent prediction of eco-concrete compressive strength based on SHAP-interpretable BO-XGBoost and NSGA-II multi-objective optimization
Article.Authors: Zhao H.; He J.; Ren J.; He J.; Liu Z.; Zhao Y.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction and optimization of eco-concrete compressive strength are important for balancing mechanical performance and material utilization. Based on 400 experimental records, this study developed an interpretable prediction-optimization framework integrating Optuna-TPE-optimized machine-learning models, SHAP, and NSGA-II. Seven mix-design and curing variables were used as inputs, and BO-XGBoost, BO-RF, and BO-SVR were developed for compressive strength prediction. On the independent test set, BO-XGBoost, BO-RF, and BO-SVR achieved R 2 values of 0.958, 0.957, and 0.950, RMSE values of 0.466, 0.475, and 0.509 MPa, and MAE values of 0.376, 0.382, and 0.392 MPa, respectively. BO-XGBoost therefore showed the best overall test-set performance among the three models under the present evaluation procedure. SHAP analysis identified curing age and porosity as the dominant contributors to the model predictions, followed by cement dosage and water-to-binder ratio, and further revealed nonlinear model-attribution patterns across their value ranges. BO-XGBoost was subsequently embedded in NSGA-II to maximize predicted 28-day compressive strength while minimizing cement dosage and water-to-binder ratio. The resulting Pareto front demonstrated clear trade-offs among these objectives. Under the baseline engineering preference, the recommended compromise solution had a water-to-binder ratio of 0.250 and cement dosage of 351.47 kg/m 3 , with a predicted compressive strength of 10.87 MPa. The proposed framework provides an interpretable decision-support approach for eco-concrete mix design.

Article.Title: The effect of a stress coping training on burnout and musculoskeletal discomfort among oncology nurses
Article.Authors: Poursoltani M.; Haghdoost A.; Mohammadian M.; Khanbaba H.
Article.Abstract: Oncology nurses face high rates of psychosocial strain and musculoskeletal disorders that reinforce one another, yet ACT-based interventions targeting this population remain scarce, particularly in Iran. This quasi-experimental before-after study examined the effect of a six-session Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) program on burnout and musculoskeletal discomfort among 40 oncology nurses at a hospital in Kerman, Iran, selected by census sampling. Burnout was measured with the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory and musculoskeletal discomfort with the Localized Postural Discomfort scale before and after the intervention, with data analyzed using paired t-tests and repeated-measures ANCOVA. Following the intervention, overall burnout decreased significantly ( P < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 0.78), driven by reductions in work- and patient-related burnout, while personal burnout remained unchanged. Discomfort in the neck, low back, and shoulders also decreased significantly ( P < 0.05). These findings support ACT-based training as a low-cost, evidence-based strategy for improving oncology nurses' occupational health and patient care quality.

Article.Title: Strategic seasonal nutritional supplementation improves honey quality, colony performance, immune response, and pest resilience in Apis mellifera in Bangladesh
Article.Authors: Sorna A.; Saha R.; Alam M.; Hossain M.; Rahman M.
Article.Abstract: Seasonal nutritional scarcity is a major threat to sustainable apiculture particularly during dearth periods in Bangladesh. This study evaluated whether strategic nutritional supplementation during the dearth period could mitigate the carry-over effects of nutritional deficiency on colony performance, honey quality, pest infestation, and hygienic behavior of Apis mellifera during the subsequent mustard nectar-flow season. Twelve colonies were assigned to four treatments: Sugar syrup as control which is commonly used by beekeepers in Bangladesh, high protein-carbohydrate based formulation with soybean and yeast, balanced nutritional profile with locally available germinated lentil-based formulation, and the richest composite blend. Physicochemical analysis, colony performance metrics, and pest- and disease-associated indicators were assessed, and results showed treatment-dependent improvements with increasing nutritional complexity. The richest composite formulations showed the highest protein content (24.6%), total phenolic content (520 mg Gallic Acid Equivalent (GAE)/kg), and 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical-scavenging activity (68.9% inhibition), together with the highest observed Defensin-1 expression and favorable colony and pest related parameters relative to control. Compared with control, colonies receiving supplemented diets showed higher adult bee population, brood area and lower observed Varroa load. Partial economic analysis showed the highest benefit-cost ratio for high protein and carbohydrate blend (2.87), whereas richest composite blend produced the highest calculated net return (BDT 9,650). These findings indicate that strategic nutritional supplementation during the dearth period was associated with improved colony condition and more favorable health-related indicators during the subsequent nectar-flow period.
