Article.Title: Baseline adipokine profiles have limited predictive value for weight-loss outcomes after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: a prospective longitudinal cohort study
Article.Authors: Dohnal R.; Schovánek J.; Cibičková Ľ.; Popelková K.; Karásek D.; Vaverka P.; Radvanský M.; Kučerová V.
Article.Abstract: Bariatric surgery is the most effective treatment for severe obesity, yet postoperative weight-loss outcomes vary considerably between individuals and reliable preoperative predictors remain lacking. Adipokines regulate energy homeostasis, inflammation, and insulin sensitivity, making them promising candidates for predicting surgical outcomes. Here, we evaluated whether baseline circulating adipokine profiles predict weight-loss magnitude, weight-loss velocity, and weight-loss plateau after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG). We performed a prospective longitudinal study of 83 patients with severe obesity undergoing LSG. Clinical and metabolic parameters together with a panel of eight circulating adipokines were assessed before surgery and during 12 months of follow-up. Associations with postoperative outcomes were evaluated using multivariable regression and survival analyses with false-discovery-rate correction and bootstrap validation. LSG induced substantial improvements in anthropometric and metabolic parameters accompanied by marked remodeling of circulating adipokines. However, baseline adipokines showed limited and inconsistent predictive value for postoperative weight loss. Higher baseline adiponectin was independently associated with lower percentage total weight loss only at 6 months, whereas no adipokine consistently predicted long-term weight loss or weight-loss plateau after correction for multiple testing. In contrast, baseline HDL cholesterol demonstrated a stable inverse association with postoperative weight loss across multiple follow-up time points, outperforming all adipokines as a preoperative predictor. These findings suggest that routine preoperative adipokine profiling has limited clinical utility for predicting weight-loss outcomes after LSG and that conventional metabolic markers may provide greater prognostic value.

Article.Title: Copy number variants (CNVs) interfere with human accelerated regions (HARs) in neurodevelopmental disorders: a large-scale cohort study
Article.Authors: Iuditskaia M.; Semina E.; Pankratova E.; Kurinnaia O.; Guldan E.; Abasov E.; Iourov I.; Chaika Y.
Article.Abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) represent a group of heterogeneous conditions, the etiology of which involves a variety of genetic factors. Human accelerated regions (HARs) are highly conserved genomic elements across mammalian genomes that have accumulated human-specific sequence changes. There is a growing interest in studying HARs in relation to NDDs. These regions are thought to contribute both to the evolution of higher cognitive functions in humans and to an increased susceptibility to NDDs. This is the first study to assess the involvement of HARs affected by copy number variants (CNVs) in NDDs among 821 children. We demonstrate that HARs are susceptible to deletions in contrast to duplications. We identified three recurrent HAR loci that may play a role in neurodevelopmental impairment: HAR_Merge50-02689 (20.58%, EDA ), HAR_Merge50-01379 (13.64%, ERBB4 ) and HAR_Merge50-01486 (8.04%, intergenic region near CYYR1 and ADAMTS1 ). Additionally, HARs affected by CNVs in our cohort are largely located in genomic regions that rarely occur in population databases, show notable frequency deviations compared to other clinical datasets, and are associated with genes carrying pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants (e.g., HARs associated with RBFOX1 , DOC2B , ZMYND11 , AFF2 , OPHN1 ), suggesting the involvement in NDD pathogenesis. Our study sheds light on the possible functional significance of HARs in the evolution and functioning of the human central nervous system, providing new opportunities for understanding their potential contribution to the pathogenesis of NDDs. One may assume future research to highlight the complex regulatory processes within the genome associated with HARs, which might be used for molecular diagnosis and the development of therapeutic interventions.

Article.Title: Fear of falling in parkinson’s disease: a qualitative exploration of patient experiences and coping strategies
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Zheng Z.; Ma Y.; Wu X.; Li J.; Kong X.; Lan M.
Article.Abstract: To explore the psychological experience of fear of falling (FOF) in patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD) and examine their coping behaviors. Sixteen patients with PD, admitted to the Department of Neurology at a tertiary hospital in Hangzhou between July and September 2024, participated in in-depth interviews. The collected data were analyzed, summarized, and refined using a content analysis approach. Two overarching themes with ten subthemes were identified. The first theme, experiences of fear of falling (FOF), revealed profound impacts on daily life, family responsibilities, social activities, and self-esteem, while also highlighting the vicious cycle between recurrent falls and heightened risk perception. The second theme, responses to FOF, encompassed both active coping strategies—such as modifying the home environment, seeking family support, and anticipating professional guidance—and passive avoidance behaviors that further limited independence. Healthcare providers should recognize the psychological burden of fear of falling (FOF) in patients with Parkinson’s disease and consider interventions tailored to their needs. Our findings highlight the importance of addressing FOF in clinical practice and support the development of culturally sensitive, family-centered, and individualized fall-prevention strategies. Future research is needed to evaluate the implementation of these approaches and their potential impact on patients’ quality of life and negative impacts.

Article.Title: Pseudo-label optimization and DIoU-NMS for semi-automatic annotation in scrap steel detection
Article.Authors: Sun S.; Chen J.; Ding Y.; Geng M.; Pan H.; Li H.; Li Z.; Yin W.
Article.Abstract: Industrial scrap steel detection is challenged by dense stacking, fine-grained morphological differences, and severe category imbalance, which make fully manual annotation prohibitively labor-intensive and leave even carefully labeled datasets with missing or imprecise objects. To address this bottleneck, we propose a Semi-Supervised Pseudo-Label YOLO11 detector (SSPL-YOLO11). Built on an offline teacher–student pseudo-labeling framework, SSPL-YOLO11 applies a three-level pseudo-label quality control mechanism—confidence thresholding, DIoU-NMS deduplication, and lightweight manual verification—to recover unlabeled objects at a small manual cost. Controlled experiments quantify the impacts of the confidence threshold, the deduplication strategy, and the pre-trained weight initialization. On the public Scrap Steel Image Dataset (SSID), SSPL-YOLO11 achieves 88.25% $$\text {mAP}_{50}$$ and 65.58% $$\text {mAP}_{50--95}$$ on the independent test set, surpassing the fully supervised YOLO11 baseline by 3.92 and 7.74 percentage points, respectively. The proposed workflow substantially reduces manual annotation cost and provides a practical route toward intelligent scrap steel sorting and recycling.

Article.Title: Rasagiline suppresses glioblastoma cell survival through oxidative stress-mediated modulation of TLR4/NF-Κb signaling and apoptosis
Article.Authors: Akcay G.; Anakok O.; Ozkaraca M.; Yesilyurt F.; Akcay S.; Suicmez M.; Hacimuftuomglu A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults and remains associated with poor prognosis despite multimodal treatment. The identification of clinically approved drugs with novel antitumor activities has emerged as a promising strategy for accelerating therapeutic development. Rasagiline, an irreversible monoamine oxidase-B inhibitor widely used for the treatment of Parkinson’s disease, has demonstrated neuroprotective properties; however, its effects on glioblastoma biology remain largely unknown. The present study investigated the concentration-dependent effects of rasagiline on oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and apoptotic responses in two human glioblastoma cell lines, U87-MG and T98G. Cells were treated with 2.5, 5, 10, 20, and 40 µM rasagiline for 24 h. Cell viability was evaluated using the MTT assay, while membrane integrity was assessed by lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) protein concentration. Oxidative stress biomarkers (superoxide dismutase, reduced glutathione, and malondialdehyde), inflammatory mediators (IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α), TLR4, NF-κB, and caspase-3 levels were determined by ELISA. Immunofluorescence staining was performed to assess TLR4 and NF-κB expression. Rasagiline produced concentration-dependent effects on glioblastoma cell viability and cellular injury, with more pronounced responses observed at intermediate-to-high concentrations. Treatment with rasagiline disrupted intracellular redox homeostasis, as evidenced by increased SOD protein concentration and MDA levels together with depletion of GSH. At intermediate concentrations, particularly around 10 µM, rasagiline produced coordinated alterations in oxidative stress-related and inflammatory parameters, accompanied by modulation of TLR4/NF-κB-related responses. IL-1β and TNF-α levels increased at selected intermediate concentrations, whereas IL-6 levels progressively decreased with increasing rasagiline concentrations. Caspase-3 protein levels increased particularly at higher concentrations, suggesting an association between rasagiline-induced cellular stress and apoptotic signaling. Immunofluorescence findings further supported the concentration-dependent modulation of TLR4 and NF-κB. Although the magnitude of the responses differed between U87-MG and T98G cells, both models demonstrated broadly similar concentration-dependent response patterns, with 10 µM representing a biologically active intermediate concentration for mechanistic interpretation. In conclusion, rasagiline produced concentration-dependent cytotoxic effects in glioblastoma cells, accompanied by alterations in redox homeostasis, inflammatory signaling, and caspase-3-associated apoptotic responses. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of rasagiline as a potential drug-repurposing candidate in glioblastoma, particularly through mechanistic and in vivo studies.

Article.Title: Quantum key distribution over a three-user fiber network with passive optical circulator
Article.Authors: Jeong Y.; Kim S.; Baek I.; Hong C.; Kwon D.; Jang J.; Ji S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We report the implementation of a quantum key distribution (QKD) system over a three-user fiber-optic network in which each user employs an identical bidirectional transceiver, with a single asymmetric interferometer shared between the encoding and decoding paths to reduce duplicated optical resources at the node level. The three users-Alice, Bob, and Charlie-are interconnected through a passive circulator-based hub built from 3-port optical circulators, which enables secure key exchange between any pair of them without active switching or a trusted intermediary. Each user is connected to the central circulator via standard telecom fiber links of 10-15 km, resulting in effective inter-user distances of 20-25 km. We employed the BB84 protocol with a two-decoy-state method (weak and vacuum) for secure key generation. For each user pair, sifted keys of $$10^6$$ bits were processed with a composable security parameter $$\varepsilon \sim 10^{-8}$$ . Secret key lengths were evaluated using three approaches: (1) theoretical estimation based on measured quantum bit error rate (QBER) and gains, assuming an error correction efficiency of 1.16; (2) experimental post-processing using Winnow; and (3) experimental post-processing using Cascade. All links achieved low QBERs and yielded positive secret key lengths. Cascade consistently produced longer final keys due to its higher reconciliation efficiency. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a resource-sharing bidirectional node architecture for secure multi-user quantum communication using passive circulator-based routing.

Article.Title: Integrating causal knowledge with satellite and glider data: a novel framework for marine water quality simulation
Article.Authors: Hashemi M.; Mahjouri N.; Nikoo M.
Article.Abstract: This study presents a causally informed machine-learning framework for jointly estimating coastal marine variables by incorporating prior structural assumptions into model training. The causal-informed neural network (CINN) uses an expert-specified directed acyclic graph (DAG) and model-based feature-perturbation effects as regularization targets; it is designed for prediction and does not identify causal effects from the observational data. The framework combines satellite remote sensing data with high-resolution in-situ glider measurements from the upper 0–2 m to jointly estimate temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, and chlorophyll-a. Under acquisition-date-blocked five-fold cross-validation, in which all observations from the same acquisition date were kept in the same fold, CINN achieved R² values of 0.961, 0.905, 0.898, and 0.725, respectively, and a uniform-average multi-output R² of 0.872. Regularization-weight, matched-input, and output ablations assess predictive sensitivity, while bootstrap intervals and Diebold–Mariano tests quantify uncertainty in the reported observation-level comparisons.

Article.Title: The cervical microbiome in hispanic populations in Texas and Puerto Rico with and without cervical dysplasia
Article.Authors: Walters D.; El Alam M.; Harris T.; Lo D.; Diaz J.; Napravnik T.; Lynn E.; Boatright L.; Figueroa D.; Judge A.; Bhaskar C.; Fontillas A.; Ehsan S.; Wang R.; Jansen Aref S.; Ajami N.; Sastry J.; Sims T.; Romaguera J.; Dorta-Estremera S.; Klopp A.; Godoy-Vitorino F.; Colbert L.
Article.Abstract: Within the United States, Hispanic women, especially those in Puerto Rico, face a high incidence of cervical cancer development. The objective of this cross-sectional study was to explore the cervical microbiota of Hispanic women at high risk of developing HPV-induced cervical dysplasia or with cervical dysplasia treated in Texas and Puerto Rico. Cervical swab samples were collected from 296 participants ( N = 80 Texan Non-Hispanic White, N = 98 Texan Hispanic, and N = 118 Puerto Rican Hispanic) during a gynecological exam. DNA was extracted from the swab samples, and the 16 S rRNA V4 hypervariable region was amplified and sequenced using MiSeq for microbiome profiling. Taxonomic species classification was determined using a custom taxonomic classifier trained on a cervicovaginal-specific database. Alpha and beta diversity were computed using QIIME2 and the microeco R package. Participants’ disease status was classified based on cervical phenotype using cytology or histopathology, where available, within 30 days of sample collection. High-risk normal was defined as all patients who presented to the colposcopy clinic due to a history of abnormal cytology or HPV positivity, but with no current dysplasia. Patients classified as dysplasia had low- or high-grade lesions. HPV types were grouped as HPV 16, other high-risk HPV types, and other using HPV genotyping. Among participants, 71% ( N = 211) were classified as high-risk normal, and 29% ( N = 85) had cervical dysplasia. HPV 16 was detected in 15% ( N = 45), other high-risk HPV types in 33% ( N = 98), while 52% ( N = 152) of patients were classified as “other”. Comparative analysis of microbial community structures across locations revealed distinct compositions, with Texan Hispanic women showing higher alpha diversity for two alpha diversity metrics (Pielou evenness and Shannon Diversity Index). The prevalence of CSTs varied across locations and disease states, with CSTs III and IV-B being among the most common in the study cohorts. Overall, this descriptive study provides a better understanding of the cervical microbiome in Hispanic women across multiple geographic locations, in order to guide future interventions.

Article.Title: Health literacy and medication beliefs in adults with type 2 diabetes enrolled in therapeutic patient education: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Odic P.; Nardi O.; Mutlu G.; Blackwell F.; Gainet A.; Foucault-fruchard L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Therapeutic patient education is a cornerstone of type 2 diabetes management. Medication beliefs, as conceptualized by the Necessity–Concerns Framework, influence how patients perceive and engage with long-term treatment. Health literacy may shape these beliefs, yet its relationship with medication beliefs remains insufficiently explored in adults with type 2 diabetes, particularly in real-world therapeutic patient education settings. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from the DIABREVAL cohort, a structured therapeutic patient education programme conducted in primary care in France. Medication beliefs were assessed using the Beliefs about Medicines Questionnaire-Specific (BMQ-Specific). Health literacy was measured using the Newest Vital Sign (NVS), socioeconomic deprivation using the EPICES score, and educational attainment using three predefined categories. Linear regression models with progressive adjustment for deprivation, age and educational attainment were performed using multiple imputation, with complete-case sensitivity analyses. A total of 494 adults with type 2 diabetes were included (mean age 64.4 ± 10.1 years; 54.0% men). Limited health literacy was common, with 62.8% of participants scoring below 4 on the NVS. Higher health literacy was independently associated with lower medication concerns (β = −0.28, p = 0.047), whereas no independent association was observed with perceived necessity of treatment. Educational attainment and socioeconomic deprivation were not independently associated with medication beliefs, while older age was independently associated with stronger necessity beliefs. These findings suggest that health literacy may be more closely associated with how patients perceive treatment-related risks than with their perceived necessity of treatment. Integrating the assessment of health literacy and medication beliefs into therapeutic education and routine clinical care may help healthcare professionals identify medication-related concerns and support more personalised communication and counselling strategies.

Article.Title: Methodological audit and empirical evaluation of a lightweight whole-volume 3D CNN for preterm brain injury classification
Article.Authors: Yuan B.; Lu J.; Zhang W.; Wu B.; Wang T.; Wang C.; Sun C.; Guo L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study uses methodological auditing to evaluate a proof-of-concept engineering pipeline for classifying radiological severity groups of preterm brain injury (BI) from T2-weighted MRI in the dHCP cohort. Its primary contribution is methodology-driven empirical discovery rather than a new neural-network architecture. GloResNet combines a standard ResNet-10 backbone, MedicalNet initialization, whole-volume array resizing, mixup, and array-axis-0-reversal probability averaging, hereafter referred to as axis-0-reversal averaging; no new CNN block is proposed. The audit identifies concrete mechanisms by which small-cohort imaging results can be overstated, including unit-of-analysis drift, fold-assignment non-traceability, post hoc model-selection bias, and ranking across incompatible evaluation protocols. Building on this framework, we report the first fair, traceable comparison between a de novo trained Vision Transformer (ViT) and a domain-adapted lightweight 3D CNN on a public preterm brain injury dataset. When all sources of bias are controlled, the lightweight CNN achieves comparable or superior performance to ViT, challenging the prevailing assumption that larger, more complex architectures are always preferable in low-data regimes. Applying the audit to the historical evidence also showed that the archived GloResNet mean fold accuracy of $$69.12 \pm 7.42\%$$ was calculated over 180 scan records from 128 subjects, including repeated scans, without retained subject identifiers or out-of-fold predictions. The historical archive is therefore reported separately from the fair, traceable server-side comparison. A separate, auditable subject-level input-representation experiment did not demonstrate superiority of whole-volume input. The resulting minimum reporting standard requires an explicit statistical unit, traceable subject-level folds, retained out-of-fold predictions, prespecified selection rules, and transparent comparator conditions. These internal estimates do not establish clinical screening performance or external generalizability. The source code is available at https://github.com/ICL-SUST/GloResNet-Preterm-Brain

Article.Title: A dual-expert social bot detection model based on R-GCN and LLM fusion reasoning
Article.Authors: Song J.; Gao H.; Xu N.; Guan J.; Shan S.
Article.Abstract: With the rapid development of social media platforms, automated accounts have become an important factor affecting information dissemination, public opinion governance and platform ecology. This paper takes TwiBot-20 as the research object, focusing on the study of social bot detection based on textual semantic information and social topological information. The research objective of this paper is to combine detection performance with readable expert evidence for social bot detection through a data-driven dual-expert model. Firstly, a textual semantic expert based on supervised fine-tuning large language model is constructed. User description, follower count, following count, tweet count, verification status and active years are organized as user profile input, and the textual semantic expert outputs the semantic-side prediction label and evidence summary. Secondly, a topological structure expert based on relational graph convolutional network is built. The construction of this expert includes the construction of user nodes, the construction of Following and Followers relation edges, and the construction of node features by combining account attributes and textual semantic embeddings. Thirdly, a dual-expert fusion reasoning model based on large language model is constructed. The outputs of textual semantic expert and topological structure expert are organized as structured evidence, and user-specific decision weights computed by a model fitted on the development split are used to guide the large language model to generate the final detection result and explanation report. The proposed model achieves 82.76% accuracy and 84.14% bot F1 on TwiBot-20, improving on the stronger single expert by 2.20 and 1.54% points. Its accuracy matches stacking, while the calibrated ensemble achieves a slightly higher bot F1. The model also produces readable reports of expert disagreement and decision cues, illustrated through correct and incorrect arbitration cases.

Article.Title: Construction of a five-gene prognostic model involving T cell exhaustion and metabolic reprogramming for predicting hepatocellular carcinoma risk using LASSO: insights into immune infiltration and drug sensitivity
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Chen Y.; Mao Y.; Chen Z.; Zhang X.; Zhang T.
Article.Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) ranks as one of the most common and deadly malignancies in the world. Its pathogenesis is closely correlated with T cell exhaustion and metabolic reprogramming, these two critical yet underexplored mechanisms can profoundly shape the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and drive disease progression. This study was designed for constructing a prognosis risk model for HCC and elucidating its correlations with immune infiltration and drug sensitivity by integrating these two biological processes. An integrated bioinformatics analysis was performed by using data from two datasets such as Cancer Genome Atlas Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma (TCGA-LIHC) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO, including GSE76427 and GSE10186). Fifty seven overlapping genes associated with both T cell exhaustion and metabolic reprogramming were screened. Thereafter, the protein–protein interaction (PPI) network analyses and Cox regression model analyses were conducted to identify the following five core genes: EZH2, FOXO1, SMARCA2, KPNA2, and SLC2A1. According to the calculated risk scores, HCC patients in the TCGA-LIHC training set were stratified into high- and low-risk groups, which indicated an obvious difference in overall survival (OS) ( P < 0.0001). This model demonstrated good performance in predicting one- and three-year OS, with an area under the curve (AUC) exceeding 0.7, this finding was further confirmed by external validation. Furthermore, the risk scores were correlated with distinct immune cell infiltration patterns and varied sensitivities to anticancer drugs, and the low-risk group exhibited enhanced immune activity and greater drug sensitivity. In summary, this study has constructed a five-gene model that provides computational evidence for prognostic stratification of HCC from the perspective of the intersection between cell exhaustion and metabolic reprogramming. However, its clinical application still requires experimental validation in independent clinical cohorts. These findings offer novel and deeper insights into synergistic effects of metabolic alterations and immune escape on HCC progression.

Article.Title: DAF-EfficientNetV2: distribution-aware feature enhancement for plant leaf disease recognition in complex environments
Article.Authors: Du L.; Ma Y.; Xue R.; Zhao Y.; Xie X.; Yu H.
Article.Abstract: Plant leaf diseases in complex natural growing environments are characterized by significant scale variation and morphological heterogeneity, which pose severe challenges to the feature representation capability and inference efficiency of recognition models. Although existing convolutional neural networks have achieved certain progress in disease recognition tasks, they are still constrained by inherent local inductive bias, resulting in limited capability in modeling long-range dependencies and bridging the semantic gap across hierarchical features. To address these issues, this paper proposes a plant leaf disease recognition model termed DAF-EfficientNetV2 (Distribution-Aware Feature-enhanced EfficientNetV2) based on the EfficientNetV2-S backbone. Under the premise of maintaining parameter efficiency and fast inference of the backbone network, the proposed model introduces an integrated Global–Local Semantic Fusion Module (GMSF). Through a spatially orthogonal global modeling strategy, the module efficiently captures cross-region lesion correlations within a single computational unit, and, together with an adaptive semantic calibration mechanism, effectively alleviates the semantic inconsistency among features from different levels. As a result, the model’s panoramic perception capability for scale distortion and complex lesion morphologies is significantly enhanced. In addition, a Shuffle Attention feature re-calibration mechanism is incorporated, which jointly optimizes channel-wise and spatial responses through a “group–parallel–reassemble” strategy, guiding the model to focus on diagnostically valuable lesion regions while suppressing redundant noise from complex field backgrounds in a computationally efficient manner. Furthermore, a lightweight cross-scale aggregation strategy is adopted to achieve efficient integration and alignment of features at different resolutions. Experimental results on the Plant Pathology 2020-FGVC7 and Plant Pathology 2021-FGVC8 datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves classification accuracies of 95.43 ± 0.51% (best 96.14%) and 88.39%, respectively, outperforming existing mainstream approaches and validating the effectiveness and robustness of DAF-EfficientNetV2 in complex plant disease recognition tasks. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/mayue0606/DAF-EfficientNetV2 .

Article.Title: Factors associated with chronicity in children with immune thrombocytopenia in Inner Mongolia
Article.Authors: Wu Q.; Fang K.; Zhang N.; Zhang C.; Sheng S.; Gu Y.; Wang Y.; Du R.; Ning L.; Chen Q.; Zhang X.; Rong L.; Liu L.; Zhao X.; Zhang X.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the related factors influencing the progression of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) to chronic immune thrombocytopenia (cITP) in children, aiming to evaluate their potential value in early risk stratification and prognosis assessment. Clinical data from pediatric ITP patients at 12 tertiary hospitals in Inner Mongolia, collected between January 2018 and September 2025 were analyzed. Through univariate and binary logistic regression analysis, we identified independent factors influencing the prognosis of children. (1) General information: A total of 549 patients were included, comprising 290 males (52.82%) and 259 females (47.18%), with a male-to-female ratio of 1.12:1. Among them, 146 (26.6%) developed chronic ITP, while 403 (73.4%) were non-chronic. (2) Univariate analysis showed that age, triggering factors (infection and/or vaccination), platelet count (PLT) at initial diagnosis, absolute lymphocyte count (ALC), T lymphocyte count, CD4⁺ T lymphocyte count, natural killer (NK) cell count, bone marrow megakaryocyte (MK) count, antinuclear antibody (ANA), and initial treatment modality were significantly associated with prognosis (P < 0.05). (3) Multivariate logistic regression revealed that age, CD4⁺ T lymphocyte count, and ANA positivity were independent factors for chronicity in pediatric ITP (P < 0.05). Children with ITP who were older at diagnosis and had a positive ANA were more likely to progress to chronic ITP; the higher CD4⁺ T lymphocyte counts may be protective. These factors may assist in early risk stratification and help identify patients requiring closer monitoring, thereby providing a reference for prognosis evaluation. However, their role in guiding individualized treatment strategies requires further validation in prospective studies.

Article.Title: Aerobic exercise induced skeletal muscle MOTS-c secretion: A novel therapy for MASLD via hepatic ACE2 regulation
Article.Authors: Li R.; Li F.; Chen Q.; Gao Y.; Wu Z.; Deng H.; Yuan L.
Article.Abstract: Aerobic exercise is pivotal for managing metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but its mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates the anti-MASLD effects of MOTS-c, a mitochondrial peptide secreted during aerobic exercise, in diabetic MASLD mice and HepG2 cells. Our study found MOTS-c expression in skeletal muscle was reduced in the MASLD mice but restored by aerobic exercise. Both MOTS-c and aerobic exercise significantly improved hepatic steatosis in MASLD mice by suppressing lipid synthesis and inflammation. MOTS-c’s protective effects were diminished in ACE2-knockout mice. The results revealed a synergistic reduction in pAMPK and ACE2 expression in the MASLD mice, partially reversible by MOTS-c intervention. In HepG2 cells, MOTS-c-induced hepatic ACE2 upregulation was counteracted by the AMPK inhibitor Compound C. These findings suggest that aerobic exercise-induced secretion of skeletal muscle MOTS-c ameliorates MASLD via hepatic ACE2 upregulation, providing a novel non-pharmacological target for metabolic liver diseases.

Article.Title: Greater cirrhosis severity is associated with a higher prevalence of echocardiographically defined cirrhotic cardiomyopathy
Article.Authors: Ngo N.; Phan T.; Le K.; Van Vo H.; Nguyen T.; Le M.
Article.Abstract: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM) is a silent but important contributor to adverse outcomes across the liver–heart–kidney axis. We therefore conducted this study to evaluate the association between cirrhosis severity (Child–Pugh and MELD) and echocardiographic cardiac dysfunction defined by the 2019 Cirrhotic Cardiomyopathy Consortium criteria, and to explore candidate Child–Pugh and MELD thresholds associated with CCM as a basis for future validation. We performed a cross-sectional study (September 2023–September 2024) enrolling 77 clinically stable adults with cirrhosis and no prior cardiovascular disease. Clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic data were collected, with emphasis on impaired left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS), diastolic dysfunction, and CCM. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with each outcome, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to explore candidate Child–Pugh and MELD cutoffs for CCM, with optimal values determined by the Youden index. The cohort (mean age 61 ± 10 years; 50.6% male) demonstrated diastolic dysfunction in 49.4%, impaired LVGLS in 28.6%, and CCM in 32.5%. Median Child–Pugh and MELD scores were 6 (IQR 5–8) and 11 (IQR 9–14), with 51.9%, 32.5%, and 15.6% classified as Child–Pugh A, B, and C, respectively. The MELD score emerged as an independent correlate of diastolic dysfunction (aOR = 1.43; 95% CI: 1.15–1.78; p = 0.002), while the Child–Pugh score was independently associated with impaired LVGLS (aOR = 1.30; 95% CI: 1.01–1.68; p = 0.045) and CCM (aOR = 1.33; 95% CI: 1.03–1.72; p = 0.027). ROC analysis identified MELD ≥ 10.5 (AUC 0.708) and Child–Pugh ≥ 8.5 (AUC 0.691) as potential thresholds for identifying patients at higher risk of CCM. Greater cirrhosis severity was associated with a higher likelihood of CCM. The MELD score may be useful for detecting diastolic dysfunction, whereas Child–Pugh score appeared more sensitive in identifying reduced LVGLS and CCM. The cutoffs of MELD ≥ 10.5 and Child–Pugh ≥ 8.5 could serve as preliminary reference points for risk stratification, supporting the consideration of cardiovascular screening in patients with cirrhosis; however, these exploratory thresholds require validation in larger prospective cohorts before clinical application.

Article.Title: Integrated mechanical, durability, and sustainability assessment of low-clinker hybrid-blended HSC under sulfate and elevated temperatures exposure conditions
Article.Authors: Elbauomy A.; Fathy I.; Elgabry A.; Hamdy G.; Sakr M.; Saif M.
Article.Abstract: Hybrid-blended waste powders can produce high-strength concrete (HSC) with enhanced durability and improved environmental sustainability through reduced embodied carbon. In this study, nine blended HSC mixtures incorporating silica fume (SF), dealuminated metakaolin (DK), and limestone powder (LS) in binary, ternary, and quaternary binder systems were produced at a constant water-to-binder ratio of 0.30 and cement replacement levels up to 35%. At ambient conditions, results showed that SF-DK systems exhibited the greatest mechanical properties enhancement, with the 15SF5DK mixture achieving the highest 28-day compressive strength, approximately 39.07% higher than the control mixture, with notable improvements in splitting tensile and flexural strengths. Additionally, scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM–EDX) analyses suggested that this performance was driven by microstructural densification and a reduced Ca/Si ratio of 2.21 within the binding matrix. Transport-related properties were significantly improved in the blended systems, with water absorption and water penetration depth reduced by up to 40.9% and 29%, respectively, indicating a denser microstructure and reduced capillary connectivity. Furthermore, 8 months of exposure to a 10% sodium sulfate solution revealed a transition from an early transport-controlled regime to a later chemistry-governed deterioration phase. While SF-rich and 15SF10LS systems showed superior stability, standalone DK mixtures experienced severe late-stage degradation—with 10DK recording the highest 8-month mass loss of 5.80% and lowest strength retention (56.2%) due to reactive alumina phases. However, the quaternary blends successfully mitigated this chemical instability, restricting 8-month mass loss while preserving high residual strength. Following exposure to 500 °C, SEM–EDX microstructural observations revealed more silica-rich binding phases and lower Ca/Si ratios in the high-performing blended systems, consistent with improved residual compressive strength and reduced microstructural deterioration. From a sustainability perspective, the quaternary blend 15SF10LS10DK achieved the greatest environmental benefit, reducing embodied carbon by approximately 31.4% while maintaining high-strength performance. Collectively, the findings of the current study demonstrate that the strategic incorporation of SF, DK, and LS can effectively enhance the mechanical performance, durability, and environmental impact of low-clinker HSC.

Article.Title: AI-quantum hybrid channel modeling and noise mitigation for 5G/6G wireless networks: the AQCME framework
Article.Authors: Sharma S.; Dewan B.
Article.Abstract: Channel estimation is one of the most fundamental and performance-limiting operations in fifth-generation (5G) and emerging sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks, where ultra-massive MIMO arrays, millimetre-wave and terahertz carrier frequencies, and non-Gaussian hardware-induced noise combine to render classical least-squares and minimum mean squared error estimators inadequate. Deep learning has narrowed the performance gap, yet it offers no information-theoretic guarantee on how close any particular network architecture is to the fundamental noise floor. This paper introduces the AI-Quantum Channel Modeling and Estimation (AQCME) framework, which integrates variational quantum circuits, quantum signal processing, and a quantum eigenspace denoising operator into a unified trainable architecture for simultaneous channel estimation and noise suppression in MIMO-OFDM systems. The defining theoretical result is a quantum Cramer-Rao lower bound on normalised mean squared error, grounded in the quantum Fisher information matrix of the encoded channel state, together with a rigorous proof that the AQCME estimator approaches this bound as training data grows – to the best of our knowledge the first constructive achievability result of its kind in the wireless channel estimation literature. The framework is supported by formal analysis of quantum channel state preparation, quantum kernel universality with an explicit barren-plateau trainability discussion, ergodic spectral efficiency, Nakagami-m outage probability, and convergence of the hybrid quantum-classical gradient descent. Monte Carlo simulations over 50,000 channel realisations, reported with 90 percent confidence intervals throughout, validate every theoretical prediction. Ablation studies across circuit depths and qubit counts, a hardware-noise sweep over gate error rates from 1e-4 to 1e-2, and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis confirm robustness. At 20 dB signal-to-noise ratio, AQCME reduces normalised mean squared error by 4.8 dB over MMSE and by 2.1 dB over the best deep learning baseline; under emulated near-term noisy quantum hardware conditions it still outperforms MMSE by 2.6 dB. All quantum results in this work are obtained by exact classical statevector emulation of the variational circuit; no physical quantum processor was used, and reported hardware-noise behaviour is modelled by a depolarising channel. Spectral efficiency improves by up to 22.4 percent in massive MIMO scenarios, the URLLC outage target of 1e-5 is met at 6.2 dB lower signal-to-noise ratio than with MMSE, and inference complexity scales logarithmically with antenna count rather than quartically as with MMSE matrix inversion.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: noise mitigation; channel modeling; artificial intelligence

Article.Title: Coenzyme Q10 mitigates methotrexate induced salivary gland injury via antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms
Article.Authors: Salem E.; Abdelfatah O.; Elnawawy G.; Alghonemy W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Methotrexate (MTX) is widely used as a chemotherapeutic and immunosuppressive agent; however, its clinical use is often associated with salivary gland (SG) toxicity, primarily mediated by oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), a potent antioxidant, has been proposed as a protective agent against drug-induced tissue injury. This study aimed to evaluate the protective effect of CoQ10 against MTX-induced SG damage through biochemical, histological, and ultrastructural assessments. Forty adult male rats were randomly divided into four groups: control, CoQ10-treated, MTX-treated, and MTX + CoQ10-treated groups. MTX was administered intraperitoneally at 20 mg/kg/week, while CoQ10 was given orally at 100 mg/kg/day for 6 weeks. Oxidative stress markers: Malondialdehyde (MDA) and Nitric oxide (NO), antioxidant parameters: Reduced glutathione (GSH), superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and glutathione peroxidase (GPx), and pro-inflammatory cytokines:tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and interleukin-6 (IL-6), were assessed. Histological examination was performed using H&E and Masson’s trichrome staining, as well as scanning and transmission electron microscopy (SEM and TEM, respectively). MTX administration induced significant oxidative stress, evidenced by increased MDA and NO levels, decreased antioxidant enzyme activities, and elevated TNF-α and IL-6 levels ( p < 0.05). Histological analysis revealed severe acinar degeneration, inflammatory infiltration, and increased collagen deposition. SEM and TEM findings confirmed marked structural and ultrastructural alterations. CoQ10 co-administration significantly ameliorated these changes, restoring antioxidant balance, reducing inflammation, and improving glandular architecture and cellular ultrastructure ( p < 0.05). Coenzyme Q10 exerts a protective effect against MTX -induced SG toxicity through its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. These findingssuggest therapy to mitigate MTX-related oral complications. SG dysfunction is a clinically significant complication associated with MTX therapy, often leading to xerostomia, impaired oral function, and reduced quality of life. The present findings suggest that CoQ10, through its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, may offer a protective strategy against MTX-induced SG damage. The observed preservation of glandular architecture and reduction in oxidative and inflammatory markers highlight the potential of CoQ10 as a supportive adjunct in patients undergoing methotrexate treatment. Incorporating CoQ10 supplementation may help minimize oral complications and improve patient comfort and treatment outcomes. However, further clinical studies are required to validate these findings and to establish optimal dosing regimens and long-term safety in human subjects.

Article.Title: Psychological distress and sleep quality related to cognitive function in older adults with cognitive impairment
Article.Authors: del Mar Carcelén-Fraile M.; Melguizo-Garín A.; Mendoza-Díaz I.; Medina-Ramírez R.; García-Gutiérrez A.; del Carmen Carcelén-Fraile M.; Castellote-Caballero Y.; Aibar-Almazán A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to examine the associations between cognitive function, psychological distress, and sleep quality in older adults with cognitive impairment (CI). A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in 129 older adults with CI. Cognitive functioning was assessed using standardized neuropsychological instrument, including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), together with complementary cognitive tests. Psychological distress was evaluated through anxiety, depression, and perceived stress measures, while sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). The results showed the coexistence of cognitive impairment, moderate levels of psychological distress, and poor sleep quality in the sample. Significant correlations were observed between sleep quality and cognitive functioning, indicating that poorer sleep quality was associated with lower cognitive performance. Psychological distress variables were also significantly related to cognitive functioning and sleep quality. Multiple regression analyses indicated that global cognitive performance was significantly associated with sleep quality, perceived stress, and anxiety levels. These findings highlight the simultaneous association and potential interaction between sleep quality, psychological distress, and cognitive functioning in older adults with cognitive impairment and underscore the importance of considering these factors together when assessing cognitive health in aging populations.

Article.Title: Harmonizing national drug lists: an eight-pattern ATC/DDD analysis
Article.Authors: Rajabi M.; Mahmoudi Meymand M.; Vesali Sharif M.
Article.Abstract: The Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification and Defined Daily Dose (DDD) system of the World Health Organization (WHO) are recognized internationally as the gold standard in research methodology for drug use. Our focus is on drugs with multiple ATC codes and those with discrepancies in Route of Administration (Adm.R) and DDDs. A list of these medications was created to alert drug agencies to the critical need to audit and verify the accuracy of their national list harmonization. We analyzed the latest WHO ATC/DDD dataset, updated in July 2026, which includes 2737 Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API) with assigned DDD. A Python-based data-cleaning and harmonization workflow was developed to address variations in ATC codes, DDDs, and Adm.R. A decision-tree-based screening scheme with eight possible patterns was applied across the five ATC hierarchical levels to classify and harmonize ATC/DDD variants. Among 2737 WHO ATC/DDD records with assigned DDDs, 466 unique molecules met at least one of the eight classification conditions, yielding 913 distinct scenarios. Across the five ATC levels, 107 scenarios changed classification, whereas 806 remained stable. Changes occurred across four condition pairs (1/5, 2/6, 3/7, and 4/8), with the greatest variability observed when both DDD and Adm.R differed. Classification stabilized beyond ATC level 3. The 8-Pattern systematic screening scheme provides a systematic and reproducible approach for identifying multiclassified medicines and harmonizing ATC/DDD data. By preserving differences in ATC codes, DDDs, and Adm.R, it can reduce information loss and classification-related errors, supporting more accurate drug-utilization analyses, facilitating harmonization of National Drug Lists (NDLs), and improving Drug Utilization Research (DUR).

Article.Title: HGCN-GRU: temporal memory learning for hypergraph sequential recommendation
Article.Authors: Saghafi F.; Mirzaei S.
Article.Abstract: Sequential recommendation systems aim to predict users’ future interactions by modeling the temporal evolution of their preferences. Hypergraph-based representations are particularly well suited to this setting because they can capture high-order, non-pairwise dependencies among multiple users and items within a unified relational structure, enabling the modeling of complex collaborative patterns beyond conventional pairwise interactions. Despite this advantage, existing hypergraph-based sequential recommenders often rely on shallow temporal propagation, such as residual gating or single-step hypergraph convolution across adjacent snapshots, which limits their ability to preserve long-range semantic dependencies across distant time periods. Moreover, when trained solely with supervised signals, these models suffer from data sparsity, as the limited interaction density in real-world scenarios provides insufficient supervisory evidence for learning discriminative representations. In this work, we propose HyperGraph Convolutional Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (HGCN-GRU), a sequential recommendation framework that addresses both limitations through two complementary contributions. First, we replace the residual gating mechanism of existing hypergraph-based models with a Gated Recurrent Unit coupled with a temporal attention module. Unlike single-step propagation, the GRU models the sequence of per-period hypergraph embeddings as a temporal process, enabling the accumulation of semantic information across distant time steps, while the attention module adaptively emphasizes the most informative historical periods. Second, we introduce a self-supervised contrastive learning objective that generates auxiliary training signals directly from the hypergraph structure via stochastic hyperedge dropout augmentation. By aligning user representations derived from two independently augmented views, the contrastive module compensates for the scarcity of supervised signals in sparse interaction settings without requiring additional annotations. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets of varying density, namely Amazon Review, MovieLens-1 M, and Yelp, demonstrate that HGCN-GRU consistently outperforms seven competitive baselines across all evaluation metrics. The proposed model consistently outperforms the strongest baseline across datasets with varying interaction densities. The improvements remain substantial across datasets, including the sparsest setting, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework under different levels of interaction sparsity. Ablation studies further confirm that the GRU-based temporal memory and the contrastive objective address complementary weaknesses of existing hypergraph recommendation frameworks.

Article.Title: Unraveling nonlinear ecosystem water use efficiency dynamics and environmental drivers across Iran using remote sensing and XGBoost-SHAP
Article.Authors: Kazemzadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Understanding how ecosystems regulate the trade-off between carbon assimilation and water loss is essential for assessing ecohydrological stability in water-limited regions. This study investigated ecosystem water use efficiency (WUE) dynamics across Iran from 2001 to 2025 using an integrated framework combining multi-source remote sensing datasets, polynomial trend analysis, optimized eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) modeling, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and Morris global sensitivity analysis (Morris GSA). A polynomial regression approach was employed to characterize linear and nonlinear WUE trends across Köppen–Geiger climate zones and land cover types. In addition, XGBoost-SHAP-Morris GSA modeling identified dominant climatic and environmental drivers, characterized their nonlinear effects, and quantified WUE sensitivity. The results indicated that valid WUE estimates covered approximately 44% of Iran’s total area, of which 23.75% experienced significant long-term WUE trends, with increases (20.39%) substantially exceeding decreases (3.36%). Linear trends were the dominant pattern, covering 17.1% of this area (72.2% of all significant trends), while nonlinear trends accounted for 6.6% of this area. The magnitude of significant WUE trends ranged from –0.97 to 0.90 g C m −2 mm −1 decade⁻ 1 , with increasing trends mainly distributed across western, southwestern, and northern coastal Iran, particularly along the Zagros and Alborz mountain ranges, where changes were more associated with changes in GPP than ET. Among land cover types, grasslands (11.9%) and croplands (5.8%) showed the largest proportions of significant WUE trends. The XGBoost–SHAP analysis revealed that NDVI (50.98% relative contribution), LAI (19.81%), and solar radiation (17.44%) were the dominant factors explaining the variability of WUE. The Morris GSA indicated that modeled WUE responses were primarily sensitive to NDVI (24.00% relative sensitivity, μ* = 0.827), followed by air temperature (20.35%, μ* = 0.701) and solar radiation (16.52%, μ* = 0.569), whereas LST, soil moisture, and wind speed exhibited comparatively weaker overall sensitivity. This study characterizes WUE dynamics across Iran and identifies key environmental factors associated with WUE variability, providing insights into ecosystem water-use dynamics in water-limited regions.

Article.Title: Locomotive dysfunction and spinopelvic sagittal alignment in relation to falls and stumbling in community-dwelling adults: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Nakano T.; Wada K.; Kumagai G.; Kaneko S.; Alnouri M.; Murashita K.; Tanaka S.; Ishibashi Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Falls and stumbling are commonly analyzed as a single outcome, although only falls cause injury and the two events may have different correlates. We examined both in 531 adults from the 2021 Iwaki Health Promotion Project who answered separate questions about falls and stumbling and underwent standing full-spine lateral radiography. Logistic regression models included age, sex, skeletal muscle index, sleep medication use, the 25-question Geriatric Locomotive Function Scale (GLFS-25), and one spinopelvic sagittal parameter. Overall, 83 participants (15.6%) reported a fall, 165 (31.1%) stumbling, and 188 (35.4%) either event. GLFS-25 was associated with all outcomes in every age stratum: the adjusted odds ratio per point was 1.095 (95% CI 1.055–1.137) for either event and 1.062 (1.028–1.098) for falls alone. Removing its two anxiety items reduced the area under the curve only from 0.702 to 0.682. Sagittal alignment was significantly associated only with stumbling: a smaller sagittal vertical axis in participants aged < 65 years and a larger T1 pelvic angle in those aged ≥ 65 years. However, multinomial regression did not distinguish its associations with stumbling and falls. Locomotive dysfunction was associated with both events and can be assessed without equipment, whereas the radiographic findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Article.Title: Risk assessment of insulator contamination in thermal power plants by integrating dynamic physical priors and spatiotemporal heterogeneous graphs
Article.Authors: Qi Z.; Hua Z.; Su Z.; Li W.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: To address the problem of predicting insulator fouling risks at thermal power plants resulting from the combined effects of various source-side facilities and meteorological conditions, we propose the Causal-STHGN model. This spatiotemporal heterogeneous graph model integrates dynamic physical priors. This paper first constructs a semantic graph of power plant entities. Source-side facility nodes are mapped to insulator monitoring points as heterogeneous nodes. Then, by integrating spatial geometric relationships, wind field directionality, source-side state characteristics, and moisture condition modulation, the model calculates dynamic physical causal priors and edge-weight priors. Furthermore, it constrains spatial dependency learning through a prior-bias graph attention mechanism. A parallel temporal structure is employed to jointly model short-term disturbances and long-term evolutionary trends. Finally, leakage current is used as a supervised proxy to calibrate the continuous risk representation, thereby evaluating the model’s ability to characterize key processes such as moisture-induced excitation and rain scouring. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method demonstrates strong overall performance across metrics including overall prediction accuracy, risk alerts, and physical consistency, and exhibits risk responses that are more in line with reality within typical event windows.

Article.Title: Contrasting responses to climate change in two Dianthus species of the Irano-Anatolian biodiversity hotspot
Article.Authors: Behroozian M.
Article.Abstract: The Irano-Anatolian biodiversity hotspot harbors exceptional plant richness and endemism but faces severe threats from climate change. I used MaxEnt-based ecological niche models to evaluate the current and future distributions of two closely related species, Dianthus floribundus and Dianthus szowitsianus . Models were projected for mid-century (2041–2070) and late-century (2071–2100) under SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. Temperature-related predictors, particularly annual mean temperature (bio1) and temperature seasonality (bio4), were the dominant drivers, yet the species showed markedly different responses to future climates. D. floribundus , characterized by a narrow thermal niche, is predicted to undergo severe habitat contraction (up to 60%) and pronounced elevational and latitudinal shifts toward northern high-elevation refugia, consistent with the “escalator to extinction” paradigm for cold-adapted mountain taxa. In contrast, D. szowitsianus displayed a broader modeled climatic suitability, maintaining most of its core range while expanding into newly suitable habitats, with projected gains exceeding 50%. These asymmetric outcomes highlight the species-specific nature of climate change impacts even among closely related endemics and forecast a decoupling of historical assemblages, with potential consequences for montane community structure and species interactions. Moreover, the reduction of overlap between the two species and the limited representation of persistent habitats within current protected areas underscore the urgent need for forward-looking conservation strategies. My findings emphasize that conserving montane biodiversity in global hotspots requires species-focused vulnerability assessments, identification of future refugia, and adaptive management frameworks to mitigate differential risks and preserve endemic diversity under climate change.

Article.Title: Prognostic significance and clinicopathologic prediction of tumor deposits in non-metastatic colon mucinous adenocarcinoma
Article.Authors: Qu Y.; Gong J.; Lan W.; Zhang J.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Colon mucinous adenocarcinoma (CMAC) is a prognostically unfavorable subtype in which tumor deposits (TDs) are an under-recognized adverse feature with uncertain prognostic relevance and a risk of under-detection. From the SEER database we assembled 1372 non‑metastatic CMAC patients (7:3 training/internal‑validation split) plus an external cohort of 398 patients from the Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University, using Kaplan–Meier analysis, multivariable Cox regression, and logistic regression to characterize TD prognosis and to develop a model predicting TD presence. TDs were independently associated with poorer cancer-specific survival after adjustment for positive lymph node (PN) burden; no statistically significant TD × PN interaction was detected ( P > 0.05), although the PN = 0 subgroup estimate was imprecise and not statistically significant. A nomogram using six routine clinicopathologic predictors—tumor size, site, grade, invasion depth, PN count, and perineural invasion—predicted TD presence with good discrimination (AUC = 0.820, 0.768, 0.784 for training, internal‑validation, and external cohorts), good calibration (Brier 0.095, 0.098, 0.086), and positive net benefit at 5–25% threshold probabilities. Collectively, TDs provide adverse prognostic information after accounting for nodal burden in CMAC, and the nomogram, externally validated only for TD prediction, estimates the probability of recorded TD positivity and may help identify cases warranting additional pathological attention; the survival findings require further validation in multicenter studies.

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of graph-based metabolic network representations using graph Kernels
Article.Authors: García I.; Palmer-Rodríguez P.; Chouaia B.; Llabrés M.; Simeoni M.
Article.Abstract: Background: Metabolism comprises a series of interconnected chemical reactions, forming a complex network that can be naturally represented as a graph. In this paper, we investigate the expressive power of three graph-based representations of metabolic networks: Abstract Metabolic Networks (AMNs), metabolic Directed Acyclic Graphs (m-DAGs), and Reaction Graphs (RGs). These representations provide a hierarchical view of metabolism, with AMNs being the most abstract, m-DAGs representing an intermediate level of detail, and RGs offering the most fine-grained view. Results: Using a comprehensive set of species from the KEGG database, we construct their metabolic networks with all three representations (i.e., AMN, m-DAG, and RG), resulting in three corresponding datasets. We apply topological analyses to highlight the distinct characteristics of the three datasets and conduct a series of metabolic network comparison tests using five selected graph kernels. The conducted experiments empirically show that, although RGs provide the highest level of detail, their expressiveness is comparable to, and in some cases slightly lower than, that of m-DAGs. AMNs, while less expressive overall, perform comparably to m-DAGs and RGs when comparing organisms from very distant taxonomic groups or those adapted to different environments, suggesting that coarse-grained representations can still capture key metabolic differences under certain conditions. Conclusions: The conducted tests empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of all three representations and the relevance of the chosen kernels for comparing metabolic networks. Additionally, these findings could serve as a useful baseline reference for exploring representation and kernel choices in metagenomic or metatranscriptomic datasets derived, e.g., from environmental samples.

Article.Title: Analytical framework for corona discharge modelling at small distances integrated with established propulsion relationships
Article.Authors: Moshkbar-Bakhshayesh K.
Article.Abstract: Electro-hydrodynamics (EHD) propulsion systems have attracted attention due to its potential for maintenance-free operation, greener energy, quieter, and more efficient technologies. This study aims to develop an analytical framework to investigate corona discharge characteristics in wire-NACA 00xx airfoil electrode configurations, which can serve as a module within a larger modular propulsion system. The analytical method developed in this study follows a step by step aiming for compatibility with experimental results. One of the most critical elements of this approach is creating an accurate approximation for corona discharge, which is rigorously validated against experimental data. The comparison between the proposed analytical results and experimental data shows a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 4.13% for a 20 mm electrode gap, indicating strong predictive accuracy for corona discharge at small distances. The framework integrates established analytical relationships for EHD force, drag force, thrust, power consumption, and effectiveness to provide a complete engineering analysis tool. Various parameters such as effectiveness (i.e., thrust to power), thrust, power consumption, electric potential, and corona discharge are investigated in relation to each other and in relation to the gap between the electrodes, for the given module. While the corona discharge component is experimentally validated, the remaining propulsion quantities are derived from established physical relationships and are intended for preliminary engineering guidance and parametric studies. The summary of the results can be given in two main parts. (1) The ionic wind propulsion is impractical for large aerodynamic systems (e.g., achieving 330 kN thrust of a commercial jet engine would require approximately 500 million modules) and it can be used as independent propulsion for very small systems and as an auxiliary propulsion for small to medium systems. (2) The ionic wind propulsion is a constrained multi-objective optimization problem with the constraints including the main system parameters (e.g., minimum thrust needed, mass, etc.) and the input parameters (e.g., high voltage power supply (HPVS)), and objectives including thrust, effectiveness, etc.

Article.Title: Prioritizing heat stress indices for cognitive performance assessment using a Fuzzy Delphi–FAHP framework
Article.Authors: Mousavi S.; Dehghan H.; Yazdanirad S.
Article.Abstract: Occupational heat exposure induces physiological strain and can impair cognitive performance, exacerbating occupational error and accident risks. Although numerous heat stress indices exist, their theoretical and practical suitability for cognitive-related assessments remains ambiguous. This study established a structured multicriteria decision-making framework integrating the Fuzzy Delphi Method (FDM) and Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) to prioritize candidate heat stress indices for occupational cognitive risk evaluation. Candidate indices and screening criteria identified via literature review and expert consensus ( \(n=25\) ) were evaluated using FDM, followed by FAHP with Chang’s extent analysis to derive criteria weights and overall index priorities. A one-at-a-time \(+10\%\) sensitivity analysis was performed to verify model stability. Following FDM screening, six criteria and seven indices were retained. Predictive capability for cognitive performance (weight: 0.265), physiological relevance (0.229), and reliability/reproducibility (0.177) emerged as the most critical evaluation criteria. Among evaluated indices, the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI, priority: 0.214) ranked highest, followed by Predicted Heat Strain (PHS, 0.201) and Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT, 0.168), whereas traditional empirical indices demonstrated lower suitability. Sensitivity analysis confirmed exceptional rank stability (Spearman’s \(\rho\:=0.964-1.000\) ). Overall, comprehensive, physiologically grounded thermal indices provide superior suitability for cognitive-related heat stress assessment over simple empirical metrics. The proposed framework delivers a transparent, robust decision-support tool for occupational safety and health practitioners.

Article.Title: Development of a nonparametric spatial standardized precipitation–temperature index for regional drought characterization
Article.Authors: Bint E Nasir F.; Khan N.; Ali Z.; Scholz M.
Article.Abstract: Drought is one of the most damaging natural hazards, caused by prolonged shortages of precipitation and changes in temperature that reduce water availability. Reliable assessment of drought conditions across space is essential for sustainable water resource management and effective climate adaptation. However, most existing drought indices are designed for temporal analysis and often rely on probability distribution assumptions that may not adequately capture the spatial variability of drought-related variables. This study proposes a new drought monitoring framework, the Spatial Standardized Precipitation–Temperature Index (SSPTI), for assessing drought conditions across space. The index is based on a precipitation–temperature drought variable and employs a nonparametric standardization procedure applied independently at each time step. To examine the suitability of distribution-based standardization, several probability distributions and three component GMM were evaluated. The results showed considerable variation in distributional behavior over time, indicating that probabilistic framework may not consistently represent the spatial drought variable. The proposed methodology was applied to monthly precipitation and temperature records from 42 spatial locations across Pakistan for the period 1981–2021. Variogram analysis revealed clear seasonal differences in spatial dependence, while geostatistical interpolation techniques were used to generate continuous drought maps. The resulting SSPTI provides a simple, flexible, and distribution-free measure of relative spatial dryness and wetness conditions. By avoiding restrictive distributional assumptions, the proposed framework provides a practical tool for drought monitoring and spatial drought assessment over large geographical regions.

Article.Title: A hybrid artificial intelligence framework for three-dimensional electromagnetic field mapping using airborne measurements in general aviation
Article.Authors: Michałowska J.; Tomiło P.
Article.Abstract: The increasing electrification of aircraft systems and development of autonomous aviation technologies increase the need for accurate characterization of electromagnetic field (EMF) distributions under operational conditions. However, dense three-dimensional EMF measurements in aviation environments are difficult to obtain because airborne observations are typically sparse, irregularly distributed, and collected under varying flight conditions. Here, we present an artificial intelligence-based framework for three-dimensional reconstruction of the electric field component of EMF from real-world airborne measurements in general aviation. The study uses more than 80 h of measurements collected during operational activities involving four aircraft types and a low-cost, high-sensitivity sensing platform recording synchronized electric-field and geospatial data over the 1-8000 MHz frequency range. Geostatistical and machine-learning approaches, including Kriging, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, and Exact Gaussian Processes, were evaluated for three-dimensional field reconstruction. Based on this comparison, we developed a hybrid Deep Gaussian Process Kolmogorov-Arnold Feature Extractor (DGKAN), combining nonlinear feature representation with probabilistic spatial modeling and uncertainty estimation. DGKAN achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 0.0381 and a mean squared error of 0.0071, reducing the mean absolute error by approximately 27.6% relative to the strongest baseline model. These results demonstrate that combining Kolmogorov-Arnold representations with probabilistic Gaussian Process modeling enables accurate reconstruction of three-dimensional electromagnetic field distributions from sparse airborne measurements. The proposed framework provides a data-driven approach for electromagnetic environment assessment in general aviation and establishes a basis for further development of intelligent EMF monitoring and prediction methods under operational flight conditions.

Article.Title: Fossil shark teeth record a microscale pathway for ferromanganese oxide nucleation and Li–Ni enrichment in deep-sea biogenic substrates
Article.Authors: Felipe T.; Ferraz A.; Bernardini S.; Chappaz A.; Becker-Kerber B.; Galante D.; Jovane L.; Ulsen C.; Ardakani O.; Czas J.; Moreno V.; Caradec V.; Millo C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Marine ferromanganese crusts and nodules are major reservoirs of critical metals considered essential for a low-carbon economy, yet the mechanisms governing their initial formation remain poorly documented. Here, we integrate Micro-CT, SEM-EDS, EPMA, LA-ICP-MS, TEM, Raman spectroscopy, and XANES to reconstruct the initial stages of Fe–Mn oxide (FMO) formation in fossil shark teeth from the Rio Grande Rise (southwestern Atlantic Ocean). We document a four-stage FMO mineralization sequence preserved within dentin tubules: (1) bioapatite alteration and organic matter degradation, potentially associated with endolithic bioerosion; (2) precipitation of nanoscale goethite onto dentin tubule walls, associated with phosphate release and pH buffering; (3) Mn oxidation and precipitation of lithiophorite, a layered Mn(III–IV) oxide enriched in Li (~ 650 µg g –1 ) and Ni (~ 37,000 µg g –1 ) overgrowing goethite, with lithiophorite-bearing domains characterized by a high average Mn oxidation state of ~ 3.6; and (4) selective redistribution of REY into altered bioapatite, while Ce remains preferentially associated with FMO, followed by late clay-rich infilling. These results highlight the importance of biogenic substrates and confined dentin microenvironments in early FMO nucleation and phase-specific metal redistribution and retention, providing a microscale model for metal partitioning during the initial stages of deep-sea FMO mineralization.

Article.Title: Fine-scale characterization of dispersed-village landscapes: data challenges and methodological advances for rural landscape mapping and assessment in Pomerania, Poland
Article.Authors: Piniarski W.; Stępniewska M.; Borysiak J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dispersed-village landscapes in Pomerania are shaped by local environmental conditions and long-term farming practices, yet standard spatial datasets generalize many fine-scale landscape elements. In this pilot study, we developed and tested a fine-scale mapping and assessment approach at the 64-ha Knyki-1 reference site using a custom 3-level land-use/land-cover (LULC) scheme, an uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-derived digital surface model (DSM), field mapping, plant-cover inventories, and GIS analysis. We compared custom mapping with CORINE Land Cover (CLC) and the Topographic Objects Database (BDOT10k) using landscape- and class-level metrics. At the Knyki-1 site, standard datasets strongly generalized or omitted small patches, linear elements, woody structures, and structural transition zones that may correspond to ecotonal structures. The custom mapping represented 21 LULC classes and 148 patches, versus 2–6 classes and 6–28 patches in the standard datasets, showing how dataset choice affects landscape representation and structural inference. Field inventories documented ancient-forest indicators, archaeophytes, and protected vascular-plant taxa across multiple landscape components. The resulting fine-scale baseline may support future repeated monitoring and, after multi-site validation, regional landscape assessment, conservation planning, and management. These natural–cultural rural landscapes remain absent from national landscape classifications and are increasingly vulnerable to pressures from the abandonment of traditional agriculture.

Article.Title: The associations between muscle strength and executive function among Chinese adolescents
Article.Authors: Li L.; Zhang M.; Zhang F.; Bi C.; Sun P.
Article.Abstract: Executive function, as a core cognitive function of the brain, holds significant importance for adolescents’ academic performance and future achievements. However, there has been relatively little research on this topic in the past. This study may provide theoretical support for the promotion and intervention of executive function in Chinese adolescents. A stratified cluster random sampling method was employed to conduct a cross-sectional assessment of grip strength, standing long jump, executive function, and related covariates among 10,145 adolescents aged 13–18 years across five distinct regions of China. In the stratified analyses, higher MSI was associated with progressively lower odds of deficits in executive function in mid-to-late adolescence, and the inverse association between MSI and working-memory insufficiency was stronger in girls(OR = 0.802, 95% CI: 0.763–0.843, P = 0.006) than boys(OR = 0.888, 95% CI: 0.792–0.996, P = 0.006). After controlling for relevant covariates, each 1-SD increase in MSI was associated with decreases of 0.254 ms, 41.185 ms and 20.311 ms in the reaction times for inhibition, working memory, and shifting, respectively (all P < 0.01). Muscle strength in Chinese adolescents correlates with working memory and shifting abilities but shows no associationwith inhibition. These findings suggest that muscle strength is associated with specific components of executive function in Chinese adolescents; because the data are cross-sectional, longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine whether promoting muscle strength can enhance executive function.

Article.Title: Discovery of natural flavanones as potential PRMT4 inhibitors with antiproliferative activity against colorectal cancer cells
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Li M.; Liu K.; Liang S.
Article.Abstract: Protein arginine N-methyltransferase 4 (PRMT4) has been a novel target to discover anticancer drugs, and PRMT4 inhibitors offer a promising option for the treatment of colorectal cancer. In this work, a series of natural flavanones were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against PRMT4. Among them, Lespedezaflavanone H was a potent and selective PRMT4 inhibitor with an IC 50 value of 1.73 µM. Lespedezaflavanone H was predicted to form hydrogen bonds with ASN-265 and ARG-267 of PRMT4, as revealed by molecular docking. Chemical descriptors and molecular electrostatic potential analysis of Lespedezaflavanone H were deeply investigated. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that the complex between PRMT4 and Lespedezaflavanone H maintained a stable binding mode. Importantly, Lespedezaflavanone H inhibited the proliferation of colorectal cancer cell lines RKO, SW620, COLO 205, and LS180 with IC 50 values of 3.93, 2.32, 5.68, and 11.26 µM, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report that Lespedezaflavanone H acts as a PRMT4 inhibitor and exhibits antiproliferative activity against colorectal cancer cells.

Article.Title: Robust multi-weather UAV small object detection framework with complex entropy-aware and wavelet convolution
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Li G.; Zhou B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In adverse weather conditions such as fog, haze, rain, and snow, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) small object detection faces decreased accuracy due to reduced image quality and blurred object features, which seriously affects the reliability of low-altitude detection tasks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a robust multi-weather UAV small object detection framework based on unsupervised domain adaptation with a teacher-student self-training paradigm. The proposed framework introduces complex entropy-aware attention and wavelet convolution to enhance target representation under severe weather degradation. Aiming at the domain distribution differences in multi-weather scenarios, the framework alleviates such differences through more robust category-level prototype matching and global statistical characteristic learning based on DATR (domain adaptive detection transformer model). First, to alleviate feature uncertainty introduced by adverse weather noise, we design a complex entropy-aware attention mechanism that estimates channel-wise Shannon entropy and assigns adaptive weights according to feature information concentration. Instead of simply emphasizing uncertain responses, the proposed mechanism suppresses high-entropy ambiguous features while preserving low-entropy discriminative representations that remain more reliable under weather-induced degradation. Next, to solve the limitations of traditional convolution in capturing the global context of small objects and distinguishing objects from noise, we propose to use wavelet convolution to leverage frequency-domain multi-scale decomposition and large receptive fields, strengthening the capture of global context for small objects and improving the distinction between objects and noise through frequency filtering. Finally, to further improve the stability of teacher model evolution under cross-weather domain shifts, we design a grouped EMA (exponential moving average) strategy. Unlike conventional Mean Teacher or BYOL frameworks that employ a globally fixed decay coefficient, the proposed strategy dynamically adjusts grouped parameter updating rates according to feature adaptation requirements, providing a more flexible optimization trajectory for domain adaptation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves UAV small object detection performance under several adverse weather domain-shift scenarios, while showing promising robustness against weather-induced feature degradation.
