Article.Title: Neutral versus Trendelenburg position for ultrasound-guided internal jugular vein catheterization: a randomized, controlled non-inferiority trial
Article.Authors: Bae J.; Yoo J.; Heo J.; Park S.
Article.Abstract: The Trendelenburg position is traditionally regarded as the standard maneuver for enhancing the success of internal jugular vein (IJV) catheterization, but its necessity under real-time ultrasound (US) guidance is unclear. We aimed to determine whether the neutral (supine) position is non-inferior to the Trendelenburg position for catheterization success under real-time US guidance. In this randomized, controlled non-inferiority trial, 216 adults undergoing elective surgery requiring central venous catheterization were randomly assigned to the Trendelenburg (10° tilt) or neutral position. Ultrasound-guided IJV catheterization was performed by experienced anesthesiologists using a short-axis out-of-plane approach. The primary outcome was the first-attempt success rate; secondary outcomes were catheterization time, complication rate, and IJV dimensions. The non-inferiority margin was prespecified at an absolute 5% in the approved study protocol. First-attempt success was 95.33% in the Trendelenburg group and 99.07% in the neutral group. The between-group difference (neutral − Trendelenburg) was + 3.75% (95% CI, − 1.2% to + 9.6%); the lower bound remained above the − 5% non-inferiority margin, confirming non-inferiority ( P = 0.001). Non-inferiority was maintained in the intention-to-treat analysis and in sensitivity analyses using margins of 3% and 7%. Although the Trendelenburg position produced significantly greater IJV vertical length and cross-sectional area, this did not affect clinical success. In elective adult surgical patients under general anesthesia in whom catheterization is performed by experienced operators under real-time US guidance, the neutral position is non-inferior to the Trendelenburg position, and routine use of the Trendelenburg position may not be necessary in this setting.

Article.Title: Pupillary signs are associated with subsequent Hirschsprung disease diagnosis and malignant adrenal neoplasm in congenital central hypoventilation syndrome
Article.Authors: Eleiwa T.; Bayoumy A.; Azhari J.; Abboud I.; Malek D.; Gaier E.; Phillips P.; Elhusseiny A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To evaluate the association between pupillary signs and the risk of late-diagnosed Hirschsprung disease (HD) and Malignant Neoplasm of the Adrenal Gland (MNAG) in pediatric patients with Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome (CCHS), and to systematically review ocular manifestations in CCHS. We performed a retrospective cohort analysis with integrated systematic literature review. A cohort of 680 pediatric CCHS patients (2004–2024) was identified from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Patients with pre-existing HD or MNAG were excluded. CCHS patients with pupillary signs (ICD-10 codes H21.56, H57.0, G90.2) were compared to those without. Primary outcomes were subsequent HD diagnosis or MNAG at 3 and 5 years, assessed using adjusted Hazard Ratios (aHRs). A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of CCHS ocular findings was also performed. Among 680 CCHS patients (mean age 3.4 years), 38 (5.6%) had pupillary abnormalities. The presence of pupillary signs was significantly associated with an increased risk of subsequent HD diagnosis [5-year aHR, 4.93 (95% CI: 2.72–8.84; p < .001)] and MNAG [5-year aHR, 5.72 (95% CI: 2.31–14.33; p < .001)]. The systematic review (8 studies, n = 32 patients) found pupillary signs were present in 100% of tumor-positive patients and co-occurred with HD in 56%. Pupillary signs in pediatric CCHS were significantly associated with increased risk of subsequent HD diagnosis and MNAG. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support the incorporation of structured pupillary assessment into the multidisciplinary evaluation of pediatric CCHS patients, pending prospective validation.

Article.Title: Ontology-guided neuro-symbolic convNeXtV2–swin transformer for explainable cytological classification of papillary thyroid carcinoma
Article.Authors: Ahmed I.; Senan E.; Alyousef A.; Khan M.; Ali E.; Othman E.; Fati S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The cytological assessment of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) relies on microscopic evaluation of cellular and nuclear morphology. Subtle cytomorphological differences, interobserver variability, and specimen heterogeneity can complicate interpretation. This study developed an explainable hybrid ConvNeXtV2–Swin Transformer framework that integrates fine-grained cytological representation with broader spatial-context modeling for PTC classification. ConvNeXtV2 provides fine-grained nuclear and cellular representations, whereas Swin Transformer captures broader contextual relationships across cytological regions. These complementary representations support classification and subsequent pathology-informed interpretation of nuclear, architectural, and stromal evidence. Interpretability combines Biomarker-Guided Attention Modeling, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM)-style quantitative attribution analysis, and ontology-guided post-classification semantic interpretation. On the independent test set, the hybrid framework achieved 96.19% accuracy, 96.16% sensitivity, and 96.16% specificity. Precision was 95.27%, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) reached 0.9702. External testing achieved 91.4% accuracy, 91.0% sensitivity, 92.0% specificity, and 94.0% precision. Quantitative attribution analysis showed greater activation heterogeneity and stronger localized responses in PTC tissue. Non-PTC tissue showed broader and more uniform responses associated with preserved follicular morphology. The neuro-symbolic component subsequently organized compartment-level responses according to predefined thyroid cytopathology relationships. These outputs provide pathology-informed computational interpretation without constituting independent biomarker detection or expert-equivalent pathological reasoning.

Article.Title: Artificial Intelligence, climate policy uncertainty, and renewable energy transition: nonlinear evidence on sustainable energy resilience
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Grace S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The transition toward renewable energy is central to achieving sustainable development and climate mitigation objectives. At the same time, artificial intelligence (AI) and climate governance have emerged as critical forces shaping the pace and resilience of clean energy transformation. Despite growing attention to these factors, limited evidence exists regarding their nonlinear and asymmetric influences on renewable energy performance. This study investigates the asymmetric effects of AI development and climate policy uncertainty (CPU) on renewable energy transition using monthly data spanning 2013 to 2023. Employing a nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag (NARDL) framework, AI and CPU are decomposed into positive and negative partial shocks to capture heterogeneous short-run and long-run responses. The empirical results reveal pronounced asymmetries in the renewable energy transition process. Negative shocks to AI development generate larger and more persistent adverse effects on renewable energy performance than positive AI shocks generate benefits, indicating that disruptions in digital innovation substantially weaken the resilience of sustainable energy systems. Likewise, adverse climate policy uncertainty shocks exert stronger and longer-lasting impacts than favorable policy developments, increasing investment risk, delaying clean energy deployment, and weakening confidence in long-term low-carbon planning. Dynamic multiplier analysis confirms gradual adjustment toward long-run equilibrium, highlighting the presence of transition costs and delayed adaptation mechanisms within renewable energy markets. Furthermore, financial conditions and conventional energy prices significantly influence renewable energy performance through market-based transmission channels. Overall, the findings demonstrate that resilient renewable energy transitions depend on sustained technological innovation, stable climate governance, and supportive financial environments. By uncovering the asymmetric interactions between AI, policy uncertainty, and renewable energy dynamics, this study contributes to the emerging literature on sustainable development and offers policy insights for strengthening energy transition resilience and accelerating progress toward long-term decarbonization goals.

Article.Title: Spatial heterogeneity in PM₂.₅ mitigation from a 25% biomass burning scaling over northern Thailand using WRF-Chem
Article.Authors: Chakhamrun N.; Thepanondh S.; Sooktawee S.; Sirithian D.; Keawboonchu J.; Malakan W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Northern Thailand experiences severe PM₂.₅ pollution during the dry season from biomass burning, yet the response to incremental emission reductions remains poorly quantified. Using WRF-Chem v4.4, we simulated a 25% biomass-burning emission reduction scenario (Red25, i.e., fire emissions scaled to 75% of Base) over northern Thailand during 1–15 February 2020, evaluated against 15 Pollution Control Department (PCD) stations at 07:00 LT within a two-domain nested system (12 km and 4 km; analyzed at 4 km). The Base simulation showed limited quantitative skill (normalized mean bias − 42.9%, station-averaged correlation 0.25) and substantial meteorological biases, including warm (+ 3.58 °C), dry (− 35.23%), and wind-speed (+ 423%) biases, which constrain confidence in the modeled response magnitude. The Red25 scenario revealed pronounced spatial heterogeneity in the modeled, upper-bound decrease: station-level reductions ranged from 92.1% to 95.5% (station-averaged: 25.1 µg m⁻³, 93.8%), largest in high-fire-density provinces and smallest in urban centers. Across the gridded domain, ΔPM₂.₅ ranged from − 0.5 to − 80.6 µg m⁻³ (domain-averaged: −20.5 µg m⁻³, 88.4%). The mitigation signal showed a suggestive, though not statistically significant, association with temperature bias ( r = − 0.40, p = 0.22) and humidity bias ( r = − 0.46, p = 0.15) at 11 co-located stations. This heterogeneity indicates that uniform emission targets would likely yield heterogeneous benefits, and spatially differentiated strategies may be more effective for policy. However, given the model’s limited skill and exploratory design, the simulated reduction magnitude should be interpreted as an upper-bound diagnostic of model sensitivity, not a validated prediction of real-world air-quality improvement.

Article.Title: Antimycobacterial and cytotoxic activities of compounds isolated from Zanthoxylum flavum subsp. pistaciifolium leaves
Article.Authors: González-Fernández R.; García-Díaz J.; Timbilla A.; Kuneš J.; Jenčo J.; Bokhari S.; Heredia-Díaz Y.; Escalona-Arranz J.; Janďourek O.; Konečná K.; Malaník M.; Rojas-Vargas J.; Havelek R.; Cahlíková L.; Chlebek J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Zanthoxylum flavum subsp. pistaciifolium (Griseb). Reynel (Rutaceae) is an endemic Cuban plant traditionally used for respiratory infections. This study evaluates the antimycobacterial and cytotoxic potential of its leaves, leading to the isolation of six known compounds characterized by LC-MS, 1D/2D NMR, and ECD spectra. The crude ethanolic extract ( ZPE ) exhibited moderate activity against M. kansasii (MIC = 31.25 µg/mL), while the hexane-butanone fraction ( A ) was active against M. kansasii and M. tuberculosis H37Ra (MICs of 31.25 and 62.5 µg/mL). From the fraction A , skimmianine ( 1 ), γ -fagarine ( 2 ), ( S )-clausenaside G ( 3 ), ( S )-marmesin ( 4 ) were isolated. Compound 2 was identified as the main bioactive constituent, exhibiting good activity against M. kansasii (MIC = 3.91 µg/mL) and moderate effects against M. tuberculosis H37Ra (MIC = 31.25 µg/mL), M. aurum , and M. avium (MICs = 62.50 µg/mL). In contrast, the fraction ethyl acetate ( B ) and its isolated flavonoid glycosides ( 5 and 6 ) were inactive at the highest concentration tested (MICs ≥ 250 µg/mL). An additive effect was observed when γ -fagarine was combined with rifampicin against M. kansasii using the checkerboard assay, which could be considered as a basis for adjuvant therapy. Molecular docking suggested potential interactions of γ -fagarine with several mycobacterial proteins, particularly DprE1, MmpL3, and DNA gyrase. These computational predictions provide hypotheses for subsequent target-based studies but do not establish direct protein inhibition or a mechanism of antimycobacterial action. Moreover, γ -fagarine exhibited cytotoxicity against the carcinoma cell lines A549, A2780, and MCF‑7 at 10 µM, while no toxicity was observed against MRC-5 (the non-carcinoma cell line of lung fibroblasts). These findings support the traditional medicinal use of this species and highlight its potential as a source of metabolites with dual‑interest scaffolds for antimycobacterial and anticancer drug development.

Article.Title: A framework to determine the optimum number and configuration of wastewater treatment plants
Article.Authors: Mansour D.; Mahdi I.; Ebid A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Clean water is essential for life, ecosystems, and economic development. As water treatment technologies advance and sewage systems grow more complex, wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are essential for protecting public health and water resources. However, constructing these plants—particularly in developing countries—remains economically and technically challenging. This research investigates the optimum number and configuration of wastewater treatment plants (WWTP) for certain zones considering their served area, aspect ratio, and population density. The research methodology is developed to evaluate six different plant configurations, ranging from a single WWTP to four WWTPs. A parametric study is conducted to assess the impact of these three key factors on the total cost of the system, including pipes networks, pump stations, and treatment facilities, and excluding land acquisition and operational costs and considering plant cost model depending on number of buildings. The results clarify that land area is the strongest predictor of total system cost, while population density has a weak effect. The aspect ratio of the service area plays a secondary role, with ratios between 1.0 and 1.5 minimizing costs. Among the six configurations, Alternative 1 (Single WWTP) delivers the lowest total cost when WWTP cost is relatively high compared with network cost. On the opposite side, Alternative 6 (four WWTPs) becomes optimal when WWTP cost is relatively low. These findings provide engineers and urban planners with a practical framework for making early-stage decisions about wastewater infrastructure.

Article.Title: Development of thiazole-based α-amylase inhibitors: synthesis, in vitro evaluation, and computational insights via DFT and molecular docking
Article.Authors: Khan M.; Fayaz A.; Mobin J.; Alam A.; Shah A.; Elhenawy A.; Shah S.; AlAsmari A.; Alasmari F.; Alam A.
Article.Abstract: In this research, a new series of thiazole-based hydrazone derivatives (9–14) was designed, synthesized, and evaluated for α-amylase inhibitory activity as a strategy to manage postprandial hyperglycemia in type 2 diabetes (T2DM). The target compounds were obtained via a two-step procedure: condensation of thiosemicarbazide with substituted aromatic aldehydes to form hydrazones, followed by cyclization with phenacyl bromide. All derivatives exhibited potent inhibition against porcine pancreatic α-amylase, with IC 50 ranging from 1.04 ± 0.08 µM to 4.47 ± 0.08 µM, outperforming the clinical standard acarbose (IC 50 = 4.30 ± 0.04 µM) in most cases. Compound 10 , bearing an ortho -nitro substituent, was the most active (IC 50 = 1.04 µM), while the dimethoxy analogue 14 showed the weakest activity. Structure–activity relationship (SAR) analysis indicated that electron-withdrawing groups (-NO 2 , -Cl) enhance inhibition, whereas electron-donating groups (-OCH 3 ) are detrimental. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the B3PW91/D3/6 31G** level revealed that the high potency of 10 correlates with the highest electrophilicity index (ω = 4.04 eV) and the most negative chemical potential (μ = –3.816 eV). Molecular docking against human pancreatic α-amylase (PDB ID: 3BAJ) demonstrated that compound 10 establishes favorable binding interactions through hydrogen bonds with Asp197 and Tyr62, and electrostatic contacts with Glu233. The combined experimental and computational approach identifies the ortho -nitro-substituted thiazole scaffold as a promising preliminary hit for further development as α-amylase inhibitors.

Article.Title: Biochemical and textural profiling of a novel value-added hilsa (Tenualosa ilisha) mince stock incorporated in rice and pulse dishes (khichuri)

Article.Abstract: This study is the first to report the development and quality assessment of hilsa ( Tenualosa ilisha ) mince stock and of hilsa khichuri , a traditional rice and pulse dish incorporating this stock. The quality of the developed product was comprehensively evaluated through proximate composition, chemical spoilage indicators, and sensory analysis to determine its shelf life and nutritional quality over six months of frozen storage at − 25 °C. Proximate analysis revealed significant differences (p < 0.05) between fresh hilsa and hilsa mince stock. The mince stock showed reduced moisture (48.37 ± 0.42%) and significantly higher levels of protein (24.50 ± 0.07%), lipid (18.00 ± 0.25%), ash (3.00 ± 0.29%), and fiber (5.13 ± 0.27%), compared with fresh hilsa, indicated higher concentrations of these proximate compositions in the mince stock on a wet-weight basis. Chemical (TVB-N, TMA-N, PV, pH, histamine) and microbial (TVC) indices increased progressively and significantly (p < 0.05) throughout storage. Sensory evaluation by trained panelists indicated that both hilsa mince stock and hilsa khichuri remained acceptable up to the six months of storage. Hilsa mince stock resulted in progressive but acceptable deterioration of texture profile parameters (p < 0.05). This pioneering effort in preparing stable hilsa mince stock highlights its potential as a nutrient-rich value-added product from oily fish mince, supporting its commercial viability and contribution to fish-based food innovation.

Article.Authors: Raja P.; Selvan R.; Sarvesh S.; Ramu M.; Petru J.; Thenarasu M.
Article.Abstract: In the quest to improve crash safety in automotive structures, lightweight energy absorbing lattice architectures have gained considerable attention. This study presents a combined numerical and experimental investigation of additively manufactured uniform and functionally graded (FG) lattice structures for automotive crash-box applications. Four lattice topologies Body-Centered Cubic (BCC), Body-Centered Cubic with vertical stiffeners (BCCz), Octet Truss, and Re-entrant Auxetic are evaluated under quasi-static and dynamic loading conditions. The novelty lies in the comparative analysis of multiple lattice topologies and the development of functionally graded Re-entrant auxetic lattices under identical loading conditions. Parametric models with varying unit cell size, strut thickness, and re-entrant angle are developed and analysed using finite element simulations. Among all configurations, the Re-entrant Auxetic lattice shows superior deformation stability and specific energy absorption behaviour. Uniform lattices with different packing factors and FG lattices with layer-wise density variation are further investigated under quasi-static compression and impact loading. The functionally graded re-entrant auxetic lattice exhibited approximately 17.9% higher specific energy absorption (SEA) than the corresponding uniform lattice, indicating improved crashworthiness performance. Finally, the optimized FG lattice is integrated into a crash box, which absorbs more energy (72,343 J vs. 69,654 J) and has a higher specific energy absorption (38.54 vs. 37.39 kJ/kg) than the uniform-lattice crash box, with a smoother force response, although at the cost of a higher peak crushing force and a lower crash force efficiency (0.61 vs. 0.72). These results indicate the potential of FG lattices for lightweight automotive crashworthiness applications.

Article.Title: Robust distributed generation and demand-balanced hierarchical multi-layer control strategy for real-time adaptive power management in interconnected microgrids using RTDS
Article.Authors: Uddin R.; Islam S.; Ahmad S.; Nazmul Huda A.; Ahmed T.; Karimi M.; Mokhlis H.; Mekhilef S.; Amin N.; Alsisi R.
Article.Abstract: Interconnected microgrids (IMGs) improve resilience and renewable utilization, but coordinated inter-MG power exchange, storage-constrained dispatch, and reliable multi-mode operation remain challenging. This paper proposes a new real-time Hierarchical Multi-Layer Control Strategy (HMLCS) integrating primary, secondary, and tertiary control with explicit inter-MG power sharing and constraint-aware battery dispatch. Algebraic active-power balances coordinate grid-connected, interconnected, islanded, and self-healing modes according to generation–load imbalance and neighboring support capability. Battery operation is constrained by a 20–90% state-of-charge (SoC) range, 0.6 C charge/discharge limit, 70% depth-of-discharge constraint, and SoC-dependent derating. Small-signal converter models verify closed-loop stability across the four modes, including platform latency. Implementation uses a Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) with 50 µs network and 2.5 µs converter time steps. Validation covers mode transitions, unbalanced and nonlinear loading, irradiance transients, prolonged islanding, and severe fault-plus-( N − 1) outage conditions. Over the 20 s sequence, PV supplies 72.95% of load energy, with battery storage, diesel generation, and grid support contributing 14.73%, 5.14%, and 7.19%. The maximum frequency excursion is 0.260 Hz, with primary arrest in 0.25 s and full restoration in 1.71 s. Current THD is 1.604% under nominal conditions and 2.492% with 30% nonlinear loading. During 90 min of islanding, 100% of critical-load energy is served with a final SoC of 21.66%. Under the severe-disturbance sequence, self-healing provides 12.4–17.6 kW of inter-MG support without load disconnection and reduces frequency restoration time by 39.0%. Energy not served is zero and the load-energy service ratio reaches 98.37%, confirming the dynamic, power-quality, storage-aware, and resilient real-time performance of the proposed HMLCS.

Article.Title: Residual-triggered active sensitivity estimation for topology-change detection and voltage control with MAPO-SOP
Article.Authors: Zheng Y.; Xu Y.; Yang Y.; Lu Y.; Weng D.; Jiang Y.
Article.Abstract: Distribution-network reconfiguration changes the equivalent feeder impedance seen from a soft open point (SOP), thereby invalidating fixed-parameter analytical voltage-control models. This paper proposes a residual-triggered active sensitivity estimation method for model-assisted power optimization using an SOP (MAPO-SOP). An analytical point of common coupling (PCC) voltage model is first formulated to coordinate active and reactive power under the converter apparent-power constraint. Voltage-prediction residuals exceeding a common threshold of 0.055 kV for 0.10 s are then used to identify potential model mismatch. Once triggered, a safety-oriented feedback controller returns the PCC voltage to a prescribed recovery band, after which a one-sided coordinated perturbation is applied to estimate the updated voltage–power sensitivity. The equivalent feeder parameters are subsequently reconstructed under the assumption that the $$\:X/R$$ ratio remains approximately unchanged. In a two-feeder system operating at 10 kV, the measured sensitivity-feature change indices were 30.05% and 61.08% for the two switching directions, with corresponding parameter errors of 0.20% and 2.51%. Photovoltaic (PV) fluctuations alone did not trigger additional active estimation, whereas the combined PV/topology-change case was correctly identified with a parameter error of 0.44%. The proposed method enables temporary voltage containment and lightweight parameter adaptation without continuous probing or real-time topology communication.

Article.Title: Evaluating the effectiveness of coal bottom ash on the mechanical durability and microstructural characteristics of lightweight cellular concrete
Article.Authors: Al-Sodani K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Coal bottom ash (CBA), a byproduct of coal-based power plants, offers a potential route for reducing the environmental footprint of cement-based materials used to produce lightweight cellular concrete. This study experimentally investigates the influence of CBA as a partial cement replacement on the fresh, mechanical, durability, non-destructive, and microstructural properties of lightweight cellular concrete. For this purpose, six mixtures were developed at a target density of 1600 kg/m 3 . The whole experimental procedure includes a control mix, a mix having 5% silica fume (SF) only (S5CB0) and other mixes containing a constant 5% SF with 0–20% CBA replacement. Compressive strength (CS) and splitting tensile strength tests were performed along with ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV) to assess the destructive and non-destructive properties. Furthermore, water absorption and rapid chloride permeability were measured to assess durability performance. In addition, scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive spectroscopy were evaluated for evaluating microstructural morphology. Based on the results, 10% CBA replacement achieved 8.85% and 10.59% increases in CS over the S5CB0 mix at 28 and 56 days, respectively. The same mix recorded UPV improvements of 11.74% and 8.52%, respectively. Furthermore, the chloride-ion charge passed decreased by 11.55% and 10.87% at 28 and 56 days, respectively, for 10% CBA replacement over the mix having 5% SF only. Microstructural observations and EDS results further supported the formation of a comparatively compact aluminosilicate-rich matrix at moderate CBA content. In addition, the 10% CBA and 5% SF combination reduced embodied CO 2 emissions by almost 8.95% relative to the S5CB0 mix. Overall, under the investigated conditions, 5% SF with 10% CBA combination provided balanced mechanical, durability, microstructural, and environmental performance.

Article.Title: Estimating chronological age from flicker-induced retinal vascular reactivity: a machine learning approach
Article.Authors: Assaf A.; Alsaify B.; AlJarrah O.; Li S.; Schmidt-Trucksaess A.; Kilani A.; Kotliar K.; Lanzl I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study proposes a novel, non-invasive approach to chronological age (CA) estimation by leveraging the Extra Trees Regressor to analyze retinal vessel reactivity to flicker light stimulation as a unique biomarker. By capturing and interpreting the dynamic responses of retinal blood vessels, we aim to develop an accessible and reliable tool for assessing chronological age, contributing to the emerging field of personalized anti-aging medicine through individualized insights into aging. Our method focuses on vascular function analysis using non-invasive dynamic vessel response measurements, offering a unique contribution compared to existing techniques. In this paper, multiple machine learning and deep learning models are employed to conduct experiments that estimate patient age using retinal arterial and venous vessel diameter changes across three flicker cycles. The best-performing model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 9.3, a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 12.4, and a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) value of 17.7%, demonstrating acceptable reliability and accuracy. Additionally, the application of Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) to our time series age estimation model provided valuable insights into the key features influencing predictions. To our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate that retinal vascular reactivity can serve as a functional biomarker for estimating chronological age, providing a foundation for future research on non-invasive markers of aging.

Article.Title: Ultrasonic welding of Cu/Al cables: a study on the finite element model and characteristics of the gaps
Article.Authors: Cheng X.; Liu F.; Pan X.; Yang K.
Article.Abstract: A thermomechanical coupling model for the ultrasonic welding of Cu/Al cables was developed using Abaqus software. The effects of ultrasonic softening and thermal softening on the yield strength of Cu/Al cables are evaluated within the finite element model. By incorporating heat flux equivalent to frictional heat generation and the heat generated by plastic deformation at the weld interface, a highly efficient and accurate thermomechanical coupling model for the ultrasonic welding of Cu/Al cables was established. The accuracy of the model was verified by the temperature measurements and morphological analysis of the welded joints. The simulation results indicate that the stress concentration at the edges of the Al wire, leading to a reduction in the effective load-bearing area, is the primary cause of joint degradation. In addition, the results of the joint gap analysis indicate that the joint quality is optimal when the gap volume is approximately 2.36 mm 3 , with the tensile strength reaching 398.6 N (300 J).

Article.Title: Failure investigation and degradation study of long term hydrothermally stressed PVC reinforced with ZnO nanocomposites for cable insulation applications
Article.Authors: Faiza F.; Butt S.; Khattak A.; Mahmood A.; Khan Y.; AlKhalid K.
Article.Abstract: Water and temperature are critical environmental stresses that significantly affect the performance and longevity of insulation systems, particularly polymeric insulators. These factors lead to the degradation of the physical and chemical properties of polymers, ultimately resulting in failure. To investigate this, ZnO-based PVC nanocomposites (PZ0, PZ2, PZ4, and PZ6) were developed with varying concentrations of ZnO (0, 2, 4, and 6 phr). These nanocomposites were subjected to hydrothermal aging for 5000 h, divided into five cycles of 1000 h each, to assess their structural stability and performance over prolonged exposure to harsh conditions. Characterization of the nanocomposites was performed using techniques such as X-ray diffractometry (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The analyses revealed that the nanocomposites generally outperformed neat PVC in terms of structural integrity and resistance to aging. Notably, PZ2 exhibited the highest contact angle of 78° after the aging period, indicating improved hydrophobicity. Additionally, surface roughness measurements showed that PZ2 had significantly less roughness compared to the other composites, suggesting better durability and performance against environmental stresses. The FTIR analysis highlighted substantial degradation of the polymer structure, with all samples experiencing over 80% chain scission after 5000 h of aging. In particular, PZ4 demonstrated 56% and 86% degradation in specific absorption bands related to -CH2 stretching and C–C bending. Thermal stability was assessed using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), which indicated that hydrothermal aging affected the melting points of the composites. Despite this, effective dispersion of the ZnO nanofiller within the polymer matrix provided enhanced stability, mitigating some adverse effects of aging. The failure analysis showed that PZ0 experienced 77% degradation after the first aging cycle, while PZ4, PZ0, and PZ6 exhibited 55%, 50%, and 66% degradation, respectively, underscoring the critical role of nanocomposite formulation in enhancing performance under environmental stress.

Article.Title: Longitudinal recurrence and change in attention-check responses across five waves of a Japanese web panel
Article.Authors: Hori D.; Koda M.; Fujii K.; Tabuchi T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Attention checks are widely used to screen web-survey responses, but whether panel respondents who fail a check once tend to fail again, pass, or be absent in later waves is unclear. We analyzed five annual waves (2022–2026) of the Japan Society and New Tobacco Internet Survey (JASTIS), which used the same instructed-response item each year (157,000 person-wave observations; 66,384 participants). For each adjacent pair, the next-wave state was pass, fail, or not observed. Annual failure rates ranged from 7.0% to 8.5%. Among those observed in the following wave, adjusted next-wave failure was 24.9% after a failure and 5.6% after a pass; failure tended to recur, although about three-quarters of failers passed when observed again. Adjusted next-wave observation was similar: 66.9% after failure and 67.9% after pass. Across all transitions, unadjusted next-wave failure was 3.5%, 11.9%, and 23.9% for cumulative failure counts of 0, 1, and ≥ 2, respectively. A single failure on the repeated attention check may therefore be better viewed as one point in a respondent’s longitudinal history than as a permanent classification, whereas repeated failures were associated with higher subsequent failure risk. Retaining wave-specific pass/fail/not-observed histories can distinguish recurrent failure from later non-observation.

Article.Title: Electrolyte-pore interface architecture for high performance activated carbon supercapacitors
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Singh P.; Aldosari S.; Punetha V.; Aldbea F.; Tripathi B.; Diantoro M.; Alheety M.; Singh M.
Article.Abstract: Redox-additive electric double-layer supercapacitors (EDLCs) were fabricated using phytagel-derived activated carbon (PhAC) electrodes and a cellulose acetate/EMImTFSI/KI redox biopolymer electrolyte. Activated carbons were synthesized via ZnCl₂-assisted chemical activation with varied precursor-to-activator ratios to tailor pore structure and surface area. The assembled symmetric cells (1 × 1 cm²) were systematically evaluated by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), cyclic voltammetry (CV), and galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD) in a two-electrode configuration, and the impact of redox additive, polymer electrolyte, and pore size of activated carbons is discussed. The incorporation of KI enabled reversible redox reactions at the electrode–electrolyte interface, providing additional pseudocapacitance beyond conventional double-layer charge storage. Among all devices, the PhAC-1–based supercapacitor exhibited the best overall performance due to its balanced micro/mesoporous architecture, delivering a high single-electrode-normalized specific capacitance of ~ 215 F g -1 at a current density of 0.5 A g -1 , together with a device-level energy density of ~ 7.47 Wh kg -1 and an effective power density of ~ 205 W kg -1 . Comparative studies with non-redox cells showed that the redox-additive electrolyte enhanced charge storage, although its effects on series resistance, relaxation dynamics, and effective power density depended on the electrode material and cell configuration. The PhAC-1-based redox supercapacitor exhibited nearly a fourfold enhancement in specific capacitance and energy density compared to its non-redox counterpart, while exhibiting a different effective power-density response due to the redox-mediated discharge behaviour. Cycling tests over 5000 cycles at 0.5 A g⁻¹ revealed an initial capacitance loss of approximately 48% in Cell#2 R (PhAC-based redox cell), followed by comparatively stable cycling with 95–98% Coulombic efficiency. These results demonstrate an effective strategy to improve EDLC energy density using sustainable porous carbons and redox-active polymer electrolytes.

Article.Title: Greater postural sway during mastoid and neck vibration in vestibular migraine
Article.Authors: Cortese E.; Özdemir H.; Upadhyay P.; Valnarov-Boulter I.; Bancroft M.; Koohi N.; Kaski D.
Article.Abstract: Vestibular migraine is a leading cause of episodic vertigo but objective physiological markers and mechanistic understanding remain limited. Postural instability is a recognised feature, possibly linked to abnormal central integration of vestibular, visual, and proprioceptive inputs. This study examined whether targeted vibrational stimulation alters postural control and visuospatial orientation in patients with vestibular migraine. An exploratory cross-sectional study was conducted involving 15 patients with vestibular migraine in the interictal phase, diagnosed according to Bárány Society criteria, and 15 age-matched healthy controls. Participants received vibrational stimulation at the mastoid, upper cervical region, and a deltoid control site. Postural sway was quantified using stabilometric force-platform measures under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Visuospatial orientation was assessed with a rod-tilt paradigm. Baseline postural sway and rod-tilt performance were similar between groups. VM patients exhibited significantly greater displacements of the body’s centre of pressure (CoP) in response to both upper neck and mastoid vibration, compared with healthy subjects (all p < 0.05) and with their own negative-control stimulus (deltoid, all p < 0.001). Deltoid vibration produced no group differences. Rod-tilt performance remained comparable across groups. In this exploratory cross-sectional study, patients with vestibular migraine exhibited increased postural sway during vestibular and cervical proprioceptive perturbations, despite comparable baseline balance and visuospatial orientation. These findings identify differences in postural responses to sensory perturbations in vestibular migraine and warrant further investigation in larger cohort studies.

Article.Title: Divergent socioeconomic gradients of allostatic load and all-cause mortality in the United States and China: evidence from NHANES and CHARLS
Article.Authors: Guo J.; Zhang J.; Zeng J.; Zhang Y.; Chen J.; Ma G.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Socioeconomic disadvantage and unhealthy lifestyles are both associated with greater physiological wear (allostatic load). Whether socioeconomic conditions modify the associations between health-related behaviors and allostatic load is unclear. We analyzed data from 24,187 US adults (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey [NHANES] 2007–2018) and 17,507 Chinese adults (China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study [CHARLS] 2011, extended follow-up to 2020). Socioeconomic disadvantage was quantified using country-specific Social Determinants of Health (SDoH) scores, and cumulative physiological wear was assessed via the Allostatic Load (AL) score. Following an exploratory XGBoost-based ranking of candidate predictors, survey-weighted generalized linear models and restricted cubic splines (RCS) were applied to evaluate socioeconomic effect modification on AL. Finally, survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess subsequent all-cause mortality risks. Clear but opposite socioeconomic gradients in allostatic load were observed: age- and sex-adjusted allostatic load declined with higher SDoH in the US (2.13 to 1.68; P for trend < 0.001) and increased in China (2.91 to 3.46; P for trend < 0.001). SDoH modified the association between systolic blood pressure and allostatic load in both cohorts (q = 0.030 in the US and q < 0.001 in China); the diastolic blood pressure interaction remained significant after FDR correction only in China (q = 0.010). This systolic interaction was attenuated after removing blood pressure components from the allostatic load score (US trend P = 0.006). In China, the association between allostatic load and current smoking was also modified by SDoH (P_interaction = 0.010; q = 0.033). In the US, body-mass index also showed an SDoH interaction that survived FDR correction (q = 0.030). No other factor retained significance in either cohort. In the US, the lowest SDoH stratum had substantially higher all-cause mortality than the highest (HR = 5.55; 95% CI 4.12–7.47), and allostatic load was independently associated with mortality (per 1-SD: HR = 1.37; 1.23–1.54). In China, both allostatic load (per 1-SD: HR = 1.18; 1.11–1.26) and socioeconomic disadvantage (lowest vs. highest SDoH stratum: HR = 1.78; 1.30–2.45) predicted all-cause mortality. The allostatic load–mortality association was consistent in the full sample and after excluding deaths within the first 12 months. Socioeconomic conditions were associated with variations in the associations between health-related behaviors and allostatic load, most consistently for blood pressure in both cohorts and for smoking in China, whereas the shape of the diet quality–allostatic load association did not differ significantly across socioeconomic strata. The divergent physiological patterns indicate that the relationship between social position and physiological dysregulation differs across populations. Strategies to promote equitable healthy aging must address both structural barriers and individual behaviors, though these observational findings warrant confirmation in prospective cohorts.

Article.Title: Health-related quality of life and EQ-5D utility across the MASLD and MASH spectrum - a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Kamalashree G.; Kavya V.; Murugadoss H.; Basheer A.
Article.Abstract: Health utility estimates are required for health technology assessment and economic evaluation in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), yet EuroQol 5-Dimension (EQ-5D) values vary across disease stages, populations, instrument versions, and national value sets. We aimed to characterise this evidence and explore sources of variation. Methods PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 16 February 2026. Adult studies reporting directly measured EQ-5D utility and/or EQ-VAS obtained through EQ-5D administration in MASLD/MASH or compatible historical non-alcoholic fatty liver disease/steatohepatitis (NAFLD/NASH) populations were included. Structured qualitative synthesis was primary. Exploratory REML random-effects meta-analysis, prediction intervals, subgroup and sensitivity analyses, domain-level proportion analysis, meta-regression, and small-study-effect assessment were secondary. Certainty was appraised using a GRADE-informed framework adapted to descriptive utility evidence. Results Fourteen studies contributed EQ-5D utility data for 12,265 participants and six contributed EQ-VAS data for 3,520. The macro-level pooled EQ-5D estimate was 0.836 (95% CI 0.781–0.890; I²=99.6%). Fibrosis severity provided the clearest clinical signal: pooled utility was 0.775 (95% CI 0.732–0.817) for F0–F2 and 0.582 (95% CI 0.367–0.797) for F3–F4. The conventional advanced-minus-early difference was − 0.186 (95% CI − 0.359 to − 0.012), while Hartung-Knapp sensitivity widened the interval to − 0.570 to 0.199. Anxiety/depression (35.5%) and pain/discomfort (32.8%) were most frequently affected. Certainty in pooled magnitudes was very low. Conclusions Health utility in MASLD/MASH is context-dependent rather than universally transferable. Fibrosis stage, EQ-5D version, tariff, and population context should guide utility selection. Locally valued, stage-matched EQ-5D evidence should be prioritised, while the overall pooled estimate is best used as a benchmark or sensitivity input.

Article.Title: Schizophrenia classification from multichannel EEG using EEGNet with SHAP and Grad-CAM
Article.Authors: Pandey M.; Guruviah V.
Article.Abstract: Schizophrenia affects cognition, perception and neural information processing. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive and relatively low-cost way to study these changes. This study evaluates two deep learning models for separating paranoid schizophrenia patients from healthy controls using the public RepOD resting-state EEG dataset, which contains 14 patients and 14 healthy controls recorded from 19 electrodes at 250 Hz. To prevent participant level data leakage, all final testing kept participants separate using Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) and Stratified Group 5-Fold validation. The three-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) used Short-Time Fourier Transform representations (STFT), while EEGNet used the channel-time EEG epochs directly. At the reference settings used for the final controlled analysis, EEGNet gave an accuracy of 0.750, F1-score of 0.767, Cohen’s kappa of 0.497 and AUC of 0.797 under LOSO validation. Under Stratified Group 5-Fold validation, the corresponding values were 0.679, 0.695, 0.357 and 0.757. EEGNet showed stronger performance than the 3D-CNN, particularly under Stratified Group 5-Fold validation, where the 3D-CNN achieved a kappa of 0.011. Participant-based bootstrap confidence intervals quantified the uncertainty associated with the 28-participant cohort. Additional tests of learning rate (LR) and STFT resolution confirmed that the 3D-CNN was sensitive to model settings and fold composition. A separate ICA cleaning test showed that removing likely artifacts did not correct the weak 3D-CNN stratified result, while EEGNet performance improved after cleaning. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) were used to examine which EEG channels and signal regions influenced the model decisions. The XAI results were clearer for EEGNet, while SHAP and Grad-CAM assigned different rankings to individual electrodes. These findings provide a basis for further validation using larger and independent datasets.

Article.Title: RGaKE: randomized and global-aware knowledge graph embedding for link prediction
Article.Authors: Wang Q.; Wang M.; Zhu Q.; Li C.; Shen T.; Chen W.; Yuan H.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, deep neural network-based knowledge graph embedding (KGE) has become prevalent for link prediction. However, existing methods for KGE adopt single embedding arrangements, which limits the fine-grained interaction between entities and relations. Furthermore, these models inadequately incorporate global structural information, and thus lack the ability to capture long-range dependencies of entity-relation embedded elements. To address the above problems, we propose a novel Randomized and Global-aware Knowledge graph Embedding model, named RGaKE, which integrates randomized embedding strategy with global-aware module. Specifically, a randomized perturbation embedding strategy is first proposed to enhance the semantic expression diversity of entity-relation embedding through randomized arrangement. Furthermore, a global awareness module is introduced to strengthen the ability to capture global contextual information through spatial attention and channel recalibration. Finally, the multi-scale feature attention fusion module dynamically aggregates interaction features across different receptive fields and captures complex relational patterns and contextual semantics. The experimental results on four representative knowledge graph benchmark datasets, i.e. FB15K-237, WN18RR, YAGO-10, and KINSHIP demonstrate that the proposed RGaKE exhibits significant advantages in link prediction task and superior generalization ability.

Article.Title: Evaluation of airborne PFAS concentrations in PFAS-using industrial facilities
Article.Authors: Lee M.; Ham S.; Yoon C.
Article.Abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used in various industrial applications; however, information on airborne PFAS exposure in different manufacturing environments remains limited. This study investigated and compared airborne PFAS concentrations and particle characteristics in two PFAS-using industrial settings: a fire extinguisher manufacturing facility and a frying pan coating factory. Area and personal air sampling were conducted, along with real-time particle number concentration monitoring and electron microscopy analysis. Airborne PFAS concentrations ranged from 138.0 to 2041.0 ng/m 3 in the fire extinguisher manufacturing facility and from 226.3 to 410.8 ng/m 3 in the frying pan coating facility, suggesting a potential contribution from the mechanical handling of PFAS-containing materials. In contrast, the frying pan coating factory exhibited PFAS emission characteristics associated with coating application and thermal processes. Across both facilities, short- and medium-chain perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids and fluorotelomer sulfonates were dominant, while perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) was consistently detected (15.5–19.4 ng/m 3 ), despite ongoing global phase-out efforts. Fluorotelomer sulfonates reached concentrations up to 747.4 ng/m 3 , and emerging PFAS such as HFPO-DA (29.2–109.4 ng/m 3 ) and 9/11Cl-PF3OUdS were identified, indicating continued industrial use of both legacy and replacement PFAS. Real-time monitoring revealed progressive increases in indoor particle number concentrations during work activities, with nanoparticles accounting for 82.0–85.3% of total particle numbers in process areas. Electron microscopy confirmed widespread dispersion of nano-sized particles across both facilities. These findings demonstrate that airborne PFAS exposure occurs via distinct process-specific mechanisms in different manufacturing industries and highlight the need for tailored control strategies to mitigate occupational inhalation risks.

Article.Title: Modulating biochemical and phytochemical profiles in Lallemantia royleana callus culture via graphitic carbon nitride nano-elicitation
Article.Authors: Golkar P.; Heydari F.; Bazarganipour M.; Peralta-Videa J.
Article.Abstract: Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ) nanoparticles, as emerging nanomaterials, have attracted increasing attention due to their potential to modulate phytochemical traits in plants as elicitor. In the present study, the impact of synthesized graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ) nanoparticles (50, 150, and 300 mg/L) was evaluated on various morpho-biochemical characteristics in callus culture of Lallemantia royleana Benth. The successful synthesis of g-C 3 N 4 NPs was confirmed through XRD, FT-IR, SEM, and DLS techniques. This novel elicitor increased H 2 O 2 , malondialdehyde, and antioxidant activity in a non-dose-dependent manner. Compared with the control, at 150 mg/L, there was a significant increase in total phenolic content (TPC) (1.47- fold), phenylalanine ammonia-lyase (PAL) activity (2.07-fold), ascorbate peroxidase (APX) (2.03-fold), and total saponin (1.84-fold). There was no difference in total flavonoids content at 150 mg/L (78.10 mg QE/g DW) and 300 mg/L (68.71 mg QE/g DW).The highest accumulation of mucilage (24.83 g/g DW%) was observed at 300 mg/L. This study demonstrates the use of g-C₃N₄ NPs to boost phytochemicals, especially saponins and mucilage, through callus culture in L. royleana . This research also helps address the knowledge gap regarding novel elicitors for the in vitro production of important phytochemical compounds in medicinal plants.

Article.Title: High-accuracy and high-resolution rainfall measurement using an improved dual tipping-bucket rain gauge
Article.Authors: Norouzi R.; Barati R.; Zangooei M.
Article.Abstract: Tipping-bucket rain gauges (TBRs) are widely used for precipitation monitoring due to their low cost, simplicity, and low energy requirements. Despite their widespread use, conventional TBRs often underestimate rainfall, especially under high-intensity conditions, limiting measurement accuracy and resolution. Most existing solutions rely on algorithmic calibration while assuming a fixed mechanical structure. This study introduces a novel structural approach to enhance TBR performance. The proposed design doubles the maximum measurable rainfall intensity from 10 mm/min to 20 mm/min and improves temporal resolution from 0.1 mm to 0.05 mm per minute, without compromising accuracy. The design also provides flexibility to prioritize either higher resolution or higher intensity measurement according to application needs. A prototype implementing the improved double tipping-bucket configuration was fabricated and tested at the Regional Water Company of Khorasan Razavi, Iran. Results demonstrate a high correlation with standard non-recording rain gauges, confirming the reliability of the proposed methods. The stepwise approach further reduces variations in water inflow to the buckets, enhancing accuracy under rapidly changing rainfall conditions. The proposed methods offer a robust and high-precision solution for rainfall monitoring, suitable for hydrological modeling, flood forecasting, and climate research.

Article.Title: Exploration potential of middle jurassic shale gas in the Yabulai Basin, Northwest China
Article.Authors: Lin Y.; Liu H.; Zheng R.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Jurassic continental shale strata are widely distributed across several small- to medium-sized sedimentary basins in northwest China. Currently, shale gas exploration and development in China are primarily concentrated in large basins, while long-term exploration and evaluation of small- and medium-sized basins with unique geological characteristics remain insufficient. Focusing on the J 2 x and J 2 q shales of the Middle Jurassic in the Yabulai Basin in northwestern China, this study examines their gas generation potential, gas genesis, reservoir properties, and gas content, ultimately identifying favorable areas for shale gas exploration. The findings indicate that the J 2 x and J 2 q shales have high organic matter abundance, favorable organic types, and moderate maturity, thereby possessing significant potential for gas generation. The adsorbed gas from these shales is classified as low-maturity gas of organic origin. Both the J 2 x and J 2 q shales exhibit significant potential for hydraulic fracturing. Their pores structures are primarily composed of mesopores and macropores, with comparable permeability and gas adsorption capacities. Under in-situ temperature and pressure conditions, the total gas content of the J 2 x shale ranges from 1.52 to 3.43 m 3 /t, while that of the J 2 q shale ranges from 1.84 to 2.60 m 3 /t. Vertically, the shale gas exploration potential of the J 2 x formation is generally higher than that of the J 2 q formation. Horizontally, the exploration potential is highest in the western and eastern regions and lower in the central region. These results provide a geological reference for shale gas exploration and development in other similar small- to medium-sized basins, both domestically and internationally.

Article.Title: Durability and impact resilience of OPS coir fibre reinforced concrete with experimental insights and machine learning predictions
Article.Authors: Ja’e I.; Muda Z.; Alengaram U.; Hee-Min T.; Bafeto M.; Abu Osman N.; Ramesh S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The impact and crack resilience are critical parameters for assessing concrete under dynamic loading, while durability governs its long-term resistance to deterioration from weather and chemical attack. Oil Palm Shell (OPS) is a promising sustainable lightweight aggregate with the potential for enhanced impact and durability performance. This study investigates the durability, impact and crack resilience of OPS concrete reinforced with coir fibre, focusing on fibre length and slab boundary conditions. Durability was further assessed under varying curing ages and conditions. Experimental testing utilised 300 mm square slabs of 30 mm thickness subjected to low-velocity impact loading, complemented by machine learning (ML) predictions using SVM and ANN. The ML models predicted responses at crack initiation, with optimal responses identified through a graphical optimisation technique. Findings demonstrated notable improvements in impact and crack resilience, proportional to fibre length and support configurations. Peak performance of up to 135 Joules and 631 N/mm 2 was achieved with 50 mm coir fibre under four support configurations, with fibre effects most pronounced in simply supported slabs. The ML models effectively predicted the impact and crack responses, with the ANN achieving the highest predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.76), followed by SVM-Linear. The durability assessment revealed up to 97% reduction in permeability in water-cured specimens, attributed to pore sealing and potential blocking due to the continued hydration process. Overall, the OPS–coir fibre reinforced concrete exhibited enhanced impact resilience and durability, suitable for application in sustainable construction where durability and impact resistance are of primary importance.

Article.Title: Cue-dependent fear learning drives nucleus accumbens spine plasticity
Article.Authors: Ratna D.; Gray C.; Lee E.; Kiaris C.; Hamilton M.; Francis T.
Article.Abstract: Nucleus accumbens (NAc) dopamine 2 receptor-expressing medium spiny neurons (D2-MSNs) are involved in stress and aversive fear learning and stress responses, where repeated exposure to aversive stimuli and stress increases excitatory spine density. Whether this plasticity reflects cue-specific aversive fear learning or a cue-independent response remains unknown. Using Pavlovian fear conditioning, we dissociated associative plasticity from that induced by foot shock exposure in the NAc. Acute fear conditioning produced distinct physiological outcomes between aversive stimuli in the presence or absence of a cue. Conditioning for 7 days consolidated cue learning and increased excitatory transmission frequency via an increase in the total spine density. However, repeated exposure to foot shock did not lead to this synaptic remodeling. Our results suggest that morphological changes supporting synaptic plasticity in NAc D2-MSNs are due to cue-dependent aversive fear learning, but not foot shock stress alone. We propose that NAc D2-MSNs encode fear learning and responses to threat cues, which may heighten stress responsivity.

Article.Title: Calcium silicate mitigates PEG-6000-induced osmotic stress in in vitro–grown Aechmea blanchetiana (Bromeliaceae) through anatomical, physiological, and biochemical adjustments
Article.Authors: Cipriano R.; Costa D.; Martins J.; Miranda J.; Mendes M.; das Neves L.; Cuzzuol G.; Falqueto A.; Gontijo A.
Article.Abstract: Aechmea blanchetiana is a bromeliad endemic to the Atlantic Forest, occurring predominantly in Restinga ecosystems characterized by sandy soils and fluctuations in water availability. This study evaluated the anatomical, physiological, photochemical, biochemical, and morphological responses of in vitro-grown A. blanchetiana previously cultured with calcium silicate (CaSiO₃) and subsequently exposed to polyethylene glycol (PEG)-6000-induced osmotic stress. Shoots were cultured for 60 days in MS medium without or with 14 µM CaSiO₃ and then transferred to stationary liquid MS medium containing PEG-6000 to impose osmotic potentials of 0, − 4, or − 6 MPa for 30 days. Osmotic stress reduced relative water content (RWC), altered leaf and root anatomy, and impaired photosynthetic performance, particularly at − 6 MPa. CaSiO₃ increased RWC under − 6 MPa and promoted anatomical and photochemical adjustments under − 4 MPa. At − 4 MPa, CaSiO₃ increased chlorophyll a , carotenoid, and total chlorophyll contents and improved photosynthetic performance, increasing PI (Total) while reducing ABS/RC and DI 0 /RC by 36.3% and 51.5%, respectively. CaSiO₃ also increased starch accumulation and reduced sucrose content under osmotic stress. Overall, the effects of CaSiO₃ depended on stress intensity, with the most pronounced beneficial responses occurring at − 4 MPa. Under − 6 MPa, CaSiO₃ improved water retention but did not prevent the decline in photosynthetic performance. Thus, CaSiO₃ contributed to the mitigation of moderate PEG-induced osmotic stress but showed limited protective effects under severe stress in A. blanchetiana .

Article.Title: Adjunctive pirenoxine is associated with transient tear biomarker changes without sustained ocular surface benefit after refractive surgery: a randomized clinical trial
Article.Authors: Upaphong P.; Apaijai N.; Tananuvat N.; Chaidaroon W.; Chattipakorn N.; Chattipakorn S.
Article.Abstract: Adjunctive pirenoxine (PRX) was evaluated for its effects on ocular surface outcomes and tear inflammatory biomarkers after refractive surgery. In this randomized contralateral-eye trial of bilateral photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) or laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK), one eye received PRX plus standard care and the fellow eye received standard care alone. PRX was administered four times daily from 2 weeks preoperatively to 6 months postoperatively. The primary outcome was the Schirmer test. The secondary outcomes included tear evaporation, corneal staining, conjunctival redness, corneal densitometry, and tear biomarkers, assessed up to 6 months. Ninety-two eyes (PRK, n = 48; LASIK, n = 44) were analyzed. The results showed that PRX did not produce sustained improvements in clinical outcomes. In PRK, PRX had no effect on tear biomarkers. In LASIK, Schirmer values improved at 1 month but did not persist. PRX was associated with transient reductions in inflammatory cytokines, including MCP-1 at 1 day, 1 week, and 1 month (effect ratios 0.56–0.62) and IL-8 at 1 week (0.41 [0.18–0.92]), along with increased NGF at 1 month (2.12 [1.19–3.78]). Overall, adjunctive PRX did not provide sustained benefit in the primary clinical outcome but was associated with transient changes in inflammatory tear biomarkers, primarily after LASIK, suggesting potential biological activity. However, short-term inflammatory modulation in selected contexts warrants further investigation. No treatment-related adverse events were observed.

Article.Title: Prolonged length of hospital stay and associated factors among hospitalized stroke patients in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Mamo B.; Tefera D.; Beyene E.; Tesema B.; Getnet K.; Gebre F.; Geram F.; Fasil N.
Article.Abstract: Stroke is a major cause of long-term physical disabilities, negatively impacting an individual’s quality of life. Prolonged length of stay following a stroke inflates health care costs, increases the risk for hospital-acquired complications, in- hospital death and has been associated with unfavorable outcomes. Addressing the factors that determine hospital stay improves the overall treatment outcome, minimizes health costs, increases bed turnover, and improves patient satisfaction. The main objective of this study is to assess the magnitude of prolonged length of hospital stay and associated factors among hospitalized stroke patients. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on stroke patients at Yekatit12 Hospital. The data were collected from medical charts of stroke patients. Descriptive statistics were used to describe the study variables and bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to assess the factor association with prolonged length of hospital stays. A p-value < 0.05 was set for statistical significance. A total of 521 patients were included in this study. Half of the participants, 261 (50%), were male. The median length of hospital stays of the participants was 7 days, with IQR of 6 days. About, 29.4% (95% CI:25.1–33.4) of participants had prolonged length of hospital stays. Those aged between 45-65years, (AOR: 0.47 95%CI: 0.25,0.86),Age 66 and above (AOR:0.39 95% CI:0.22, 0.70) were associated with prolonged length of hospital stays compared with age below 45 years. Participant with Stroke-associated pneumonia had a two-fold higher probability of prolonged length of hospital stay (AOR = 1.82;1.15–2.87) compared with those without Pneumonia during the hospital stays. The study found that stroke patient with urinary tract infection were two times more likely to experience prolonged length of hospital stay compared to those had no urinary tract infection during the hospital stays. In addition, stroke patient who had electrolyte abnormality, compared to those had no electrolyte abnormality in the hospital was two times (AOR: 2.31; 95% CI: 1.46, 3.65) more likely to experience prolonged length of hospital stays. Nearly one-third of the stroke patients had prolonged length of hospital stays. Younger age of the patient, stroke-associated pneumonia, urinary tract infection and electrolyte abnormalities were associated with prolonged length of hospital stays.

Article.Title: Revealing gut microbiome signatures in inflammatory bowel disease
Article.Authors: Chulenbayeva L.; Guevara F.; Nurgaziyev M.; Muhanbetzhanov N.; Jarmukhanov Z.; Kozhakhmetov S.; Zhetkenev S.; Tanabayeva A.; Kaibullayeva J.; Agzamova Z.; Kongyrbayeva N.; Vinogradova E.; Shoaie S.; Kushugulova A.
Article.Abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), is a chronic gastrointestinal disorder characterized by immune dysregulation and microbial imbalance. This study presents a gut microbiome analysis of Kazakhstani IBD patients, comparing stool microbiota from 132 IBD patients and their 132 non-IBD relatives using 16S rRNA sequencing. The results revealed a significant reduction in microbial diversity and distinct dysbiosis patterns in UC and CD. UC was associated with an overrepresentation of pathogenic genera (e.g., Streptococcus, Haemophilus ), while CD exhibited increased abundance of metabolically adaptive taxa (e.g., Olsenella, Flavonifractor ). Functional profiling revealed an increase in predicted pathways related to oxidative stress response and antibiotic biosynthesis, together with a reduction in steroid biosynthesis and bacterial motility pathways in UC. Random forest models using microbial and functional features achieved good classification performance (AUC = 0.83 and AUC = 0.75, respectively), identifying candidate diagnostic biomarkers. Correlation analyses linked microbial shifts with systemic inflammation (CRP, ESR), disease duration, and depressive symptoms, suggesting possible involvement of the gut–immune–brain axis. These findings underscore the microbiome’s diagnostic and therapeutic potential in IBD and highlight the need for personalized, microbiota-directed strategies tailored to regional microbial profiles.

Article.Title: Factors associated with postoperative ileus after surgery for epithelial ovarian cancer: a retrospective case-control study
Article.Authors: Fang F.; Wang X.; Lin Y.; Ni K.; Shen Y.
Article.Abstract: Cytoreductive surgery is the main treatment for ovarian cancer (OC), aiming to remove as much tumor as possible. However, being a complex surgery, it increases the risk of complications. Postoperative ileus (POI) is a severe complication after abdominal and pelvic surgery and disturbs the recovery after surgery. This study aims to investigate the incidence and factors associated with POI in epithelial OC patients following gynecologic surgeries. In this retrospective case-control study, a total of 4017 patients who underwent surgery for epithelial OC between January 2018 and May 2025 at two tertiary hospitals were identified. Among them, 68 patients developed POI. These cases were matched by hospital site and calendar year of surgery at a 4:1 ratio with 272 non-POI controls. The epithelial OC patients in the POI group had longer total hospitalization days than those in the non-POI group. Preoperative anemia was associated with higher odds of POI. Higher surgical complexity unexpectedly correlated with lower POI odds, but this exploratory finding requires prospective validation and should not be interpreted as causal. In exploratory subgroup analyses, intestinal resection was associated with POI in the laparoscopic subgroup, while postoperative intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (IV-PCA) showed an association with lower POI odds in the laparotomy subgroup. These findings identify several exploratory perioperative associations with POI that warrant validation in larger prospective cohorts.

Article.Title: Exploring the relationship between cancer type and non-cancer pain management (ARISE-1 study)
Article.Authors: Donati C.; Galietta E.; Cellini F.; Di Rito A.; Portaluri M.; De Tommaso C.; Santacaterina A.; Tamburella C.; Mammini F.; Di Franco R.; Parisi S.; Cossa S.; Bianculli A.; Ziccarelli P.; Ziccarelli L.; Genovesi D.; Caravatta L.; Deodato F.; Macchia G.; Fiorica F.; Napoli G.; Cammelli S.; Cavallini L.; Buwenge M.; Rossi R.
Article.Abstract: This investigation sought to elucidate the suboptimal management of non-cancer-related pain in oncology patients, with a focus on those receiving radiotherapy. The study aimed to identify factors that could predict the effectiveness of pain management in this demographic. A detailed examination of a subset of participants from the ARISE study was undertaken, targeting those reporting non-malignant pain. A standardized pain taxonomy was applied to classify each patient’s pain as tumor-related, treatment-related, non-cancer, or mixed pain. The non-cancer pain was definited as pain etiologically unrelated to cancer or its treatments, with an independent underlying cause. We collected comprehensive demographic and clinical data, alongside pain intensity ratings. The pain management index (PMI) was utilized to evaluate the adequacy of pain management. Advanced computational analyses, including least absolute shrinkage and selection operator algorithm and the classification and regression tree analysis, were employed to establish a predictive model for pain management outcomes. The cohort included 446 individuals reporting non-cancer pain. According to the pain management index, 73.1% of patients were classified as receiving inadequate pain management. Breast cancer : 83.8% of breast cancer patients experienced suboptimal pain management. Geographically, northern Italy had a lower incidence of inadequate pain management (67.7%) compared to southern and central regions (86.6%). Age differences in breast cancer : among patients from southern and central regions, younger partecipants (< 50 years) reported a higher prevalence of poorly managed pain (92.9%) compared to older patients (85.4%). Non-breast cancer types : Overall : 63.6% of patients with non-breast cancers experienced inadequate pain management. Gastrointestinal cancer : Patients reported better pain management outcomes (PMI < 0: 62.5%) relative to other non-breast cancer diagnoses (PMI < 0: 66.5%). Head and neck tumors : These patients had a more favorable pain management outcome (PMI < 0: 59.6%) compared to others with non-breast and non-gastrointestinal cancers (PMI < 0: 68.5%). In this cohort, inadequate management of non-cancer pain was common, with notable variations across tumour types, age groups and geographical areas. Tumour type emerged as a predictive factor associated with inadequate pain management within our model, suggesting that differences across cancer types may influence how non-neoplastic pain is assessed and treated in oncology settings. However, this association should be interpreted with caution. Further studies using rigorous pain taxonomies and validated measures of analgesic adequacy are needed to clarify whether these patterns reflect tumour-related characteristics, misclassification of treatment-related pain, or variations in clinical practice. A deeper understanding of these factors may support the development of more tailored and effective approaches to pain management in oncological care.

Article.Title: Clinical utility of procalcitonin testing in critically Ill COVID-19 patients: a two-center retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Shawaqfeh M.; Alshehri A.; Aljuhani O.; Alshaya A.; Alharbi A.; Nasser S.; Alzahrani M.; Alqahtani R.; Almarhabi H.; Alshahrani W.; Albahlal H.; Alomran A.; Alamri K.; Alsharif R.; Aljahdali S.; Al Turki L.; Alyami W.; Ghamdi G.; Albekery M.; Alghareeb M.; Alghareeb R.; Alluwaym Z.; Al Sulaiman K.
Article.Abstract: Procalcitonin (PCT) is particularly sensitive to bacterial infections due to its response to specific bacterial cytokines. Even though viruses generally do not induce these cytokines, PCT levels are frequently ordered for viral infections in practice. However, among patients with COVID-19, it remains unclear whether baseline PCT measurements or change in PCT levels overtime are strongly associated with bacterial co-infection and clinical outcomes. Therefore, this study evaluated the association between baseline and dynamic procalcitonin (PCT) levels and microbiological and clinical outcomes in critically ill patients with COVID-19. A two-center retrospective cohort study included adult critically ill patients with COVID-19 who were hospitalized in intensive care units (ICUs) between March 2020 and December 2021. Eligible patients were divided into two sub-cohorts: those with PCT values < 0.25 ng/mL and those with values ≥ 0.25 ng/mL. The primary outcome was the rate of positive bacterial and fungal cultures within five days. Propensity score (PS) matching with a 1:1 ratio was used. Regression analyses were performed as appropriate. PCT monitoring was performed as part of routine clinical care rather than under a standardized prospective protocol, and dynamic PCT analyses were therefore based on clinically obtained follow-up values within the predefined window. A total of 553 patients were included. After PS matching, 184 patients were included in each group. Patients who had a baseline PCT ≥ 0.25 had higher odds for the positivity of bacterial and fungal cultures; however, this was not statistically significant (OR 1.36 (CI 0.75, 2.45); p-value = 0.29 and OR 2.07 (CI 0.60, 7.11); p-value = 0.24, respectively). In the subgroup analysis based on the change in PCT from baseline, 30-day mortality was significantly higher in the PCT increase group in both the crude and regression analyses (40.4% vs. 25%; p-value = 0.02 and OR 2.07 (CI 1.08, 3.92); p-value = 0.02, respectively). Our findings show that dynamic increases in procalcitonin correlate with higher mortality rates and poorer outcomes, while baseline PCT did not show a statistically significant association with early microbiological outcomes, limiting its utility as a stand-alone marker of bacterial or fungal co-infection. These findings support a cautious interpretation of PCT in critically ill COVID-19 patients, with greater emphasis placed on its dynamic trends rather than baseline values alone.

Article.Title: Integrated intelligent smoke management system: integrating electrostatic precipitation with PID-controlled air recirculation for charcoal-grill restaurant kitchens
Article.Authors: Chumkhuntod S.; Intarapadung A.; Kandananond K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Charcoal-grill restaurants can contribute to localized air pollution through emissions of particulate matter, including PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀, particularly in small kitchens with limited ventilation. This study developed and experimentally evaluated an intelligent smoke management system integrating a dual-stage electrostatic precipitator (ESP), PID-controlled multi-pass air recirculation, and a compact smoke-capture hood for small charcoal-grill restaurants. The prototype was tested in an enclosed kitchen with a volume of 25 m 3 under Single-pass and Recirculation operating modes at airflow velocities of 2 and 3 m/s using six paired experimental runs (n = 6). System performance was evaluated based on PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀ removal efficiency, particulate removal rate, Equivalent Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADRₑq), and electrical energy consumption. The results showed that the Recirculation mode at an airflow velocity of 3 m/s achieved the highest particulate-removal efficiencies, reaching 95.15% for PM₂.₅ and 95.50% for PM₁₀. These values were significantly higher than those obtained under the corresponding Single-pass condition (p < 0.001). Under this operating condition, the measured average system-level electrical power was 68.2 W, corresponding to an energy consumption of 11.4 Wh per 10-min experimental cycle. The equivalent Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADRₑq), estimated from the experimentally derived airflow and measured particulate-removal efficiency, was approximately 813.1 m 3 /h for PM₂.₅ and 816.1 m 3 /h for PM₁₀. These findings demonstrate that integrating a dual-stage ESP with PID-controlled multi-pass air recirculation improved particulate-removal performance under the specific experimental conditions investigated. However, because the system was evaluated at a single test site using six matched experimental runs, further validation across different kitchen environments and cooking loads, together with direct ozone and VOC measurements and long-term operational assessment, is required before broader commercial applicability can be established.

Article.Title: A tight inducible model for oncogene function and drug testing
Article.Authors: Hamdorf M.; Wallner L.; Sternberg S.; Kristiansen G.; Tischler V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Precise control of oncogene expression is crucial for advancing tumor biology research and therapeutic testing. To address the limitations of current systems, we developed a novel, tightly regulated, genome-integrable inducible expression platform based on an optimized cumate gene-switch system. By engineering a KRAB-fused, NLS-enhanced CymR repressor (CSwitch-Silencer), a CpG-free hybrid promoter, and a PiggyBac-based integration strategy, insulated by matrix attachment regions, we achieved robust, reversible, and dose-dependent transgene expression with basal activity below detection. With the receptor tyrosine kinase cMET as a model, we generated CRISPR–Cas9-derived cMET -deficient A549 cells and established inducible lines expressing wild-type and clinically relevant variants, including exon 14 skipping and H1094Y. The system enabled precise tuning of expression levels and faithful recapitulation of downstream signaling and phenotypic responses. Pharmacological profiling revealed variant-specific sensitivities to clinically relevant MET inhibitors, with the H1094Y mutation exhibiting increased sensitivity to the type II inhibitor cabozantinib, while exon 14 skipping conferred reduced sensitivity. These effects were consistent across biochemical and functional assays, including receptor activation and cell migration. Collectively, this platform provides a versatile and scalable approach for modeling oncogene function and drug response in a controlled genetic context. Its tight regulation, modular design, and stable genomic integration make it broadly applicable for functional characterization of cancer-associated variants and for preclinical evaluation of targeted therapies.
