Article.Title: Mechanical characterisation of Dendrocalamus asper bamboo and examination of idealised bamboo glulam joints in sustainable materials
Article.Authors: Aduldejcharas R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, mechanical tests are performed on three-year-old Dendrocalamus asper , while the research focuses on conducting an exploratory finite-element study of five idealized bamboo-glulam joints. Compression samples (n = 15) were examined using an adjusted protocol referenced to withdrawn ISO 22157–1:2004; the archived H/D ≈ 2 geometry, deliberate node inclusion, and missing moisture/density records are not equivalent to ISO 22157:2019. Meanwhile, ASTM D3039-type tabbed dog-bone coupons (n = 5) were employed to measure longitudinal tension for practical gripping. However, that composite-material method does not equal the bamboo-specific ISO process. The findings highlighted mean nominal compression and tension strengths of 56.99 and 77.88 MPa, respectively, while the bottom-node group exhibited the highest descriptive compression mean (66.54 MPa). Nonetheless, these findings and not characteristic design values and are not condition-specific. The FE models employ literature-based orthotropy, homogeneous node-free materials, bonded contacts and assumed friction without matched glulam/joint examinations. Meanwhile, model-specific global mesh-sensitivity reruns resulted in adjacent mesh differences of less than 5% in maximum total deformation and equivalent stress at the finest refinement step. Nonetheless, local interface stresses and failure modes have not yet been validated. Thus, numerical contours identify probable hotspots and priorities for future validation.

Article.Title: RiceExtent v1.0: a global rice-specific land cover product from multi-source data integration
Article.Authors: Patel A.; Bawa A.; Park S.; Chawanda C.; Jun S.; Choi S.; Himanshu S.; Srinivasan R.; Jeong J.
Article.Abstract: Accurate land cover information is fundamental for monitoring land-use dynamics, supporting sustainable agriculture, and informing environmental and climate-related decision-making; however, detailed and globally consistent crop-specific datasets, particularly for rice, remain limited. The study presents RiceExtent v1.0, a harmonized global rice-specific land cover dataset athigh (10 m) and moderate (250 m) resolution, developed by integrating verified local, national, and regional rice maps with ESA WorldCover v200 using a hierarchical multi-criteria dataset ranking and spatial merging approach that prioritizes source accuracy and spatial detail. Using an extent-based merging strategy that aggregates multi-source rice data, RiceExtent derives a maximum observed rice cultivation extent rather than annual mean estimates, thereby capturing double and triple cropping patterns, fragmented smallholder fields, and inter-annual variability often underrepresented in other products. The final product was evaluated using area-based statistical comparison metrics against Spatial Production Allocation Model (SPAM), RiceAtlas, and GloRice, along with USDA rice production statistics. Validation using independent ground-truth samples was performed using True Positive Rate (TPR). The developed dataset captures an estimated global rice area of ~ 1.67 million km² and shows broad agreement with official statistics and improving representation in Southeast Asia, South Asia, Africa and the Americas. RiceExtent v1.0, provided through an open repository ( https://dataverse.tdl.org/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18738/T8/JYAEHV ) with accompanying Python script, offers a robust resource for agricultural monitoring, crop and hydrological modeling, and climate impact assessments, while enabling collaborative refinement of global rice mapping.

Article.Title: Prediction of intraoperative energy consumption during thulium fiber laser lithotripsy using stone volume and density
Article.Authors: Selmi V.; Afghan M.; Taspinar M.; Sari S.; Caniklioglu M.; Isikay L.
Article.Abstract: Urinary stone disease is a global health concern where surgical planning often relies on surgeon experience. This study aims to quantify the relationship between stone characteristics and total Thulium Fiber Laser (TFL) energy consumption and to derive a predictive energy coefficient to optimize operative efficiency. This prospective, observational clinical trial included 61 patients undergoing ureterorenoscopy or retrograde intrarenal surgery between June 2025 and January 2026. Preoperative stone volume (V) and density (Hounsfield Units, HU) were measured using non-contrast CT. Intraoperative parameters, including total energy (Joules) and ablation time, were recorded. A Specific Energy Coefficient (Jx10 3 /mm 3 xHU) was calculated, and a multiple linear regression model validated via bootstrapping (1000 resamples) was developed to predict energy requirements. The median stone volume was 417.50 mm 3 , and the mean density was 944.21 HU. The median total energy used was 22,079 J. The median Specific Energy Coefficient, scaled for practical clinical utility, was 48.13 Jx10 3 /mm 3 xHU. A very strong positive correlation was found between stone volume and total energy (rho = 0.961, p < 0.001). The regression model (E = -1190.917 + 39.694 x V + 0.666 x D) demonstrated excellent predictive power (Adjusted R 2 = 0.934). Bootstrapping validation confirmed the stability of the predictors, identifying stone volume as the primary independent driver. Thulium Fiber Laser lithotripsy demonstrates promising preliminary predictability driven primarily by preoperative stone volume. The developed model serves as a preliminary framework for forecasting energy requirements using CT parameters; however, multi-center studies with larger independent validation cohorts are strictly required before widespread clinical application.

Article.Title: Matrilineal social rank is associated with patterns of attention to social scenes in male infant rhesus macaques
Article.Authors: Ford A.; Pilgeram N.; Wang A.; Alvarado M.; Jonesteller T.; Wesson J.; Bailey K.; Ginsberg S.; Karur P.; Sanchez M.; Bachevalier J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Visual attention to others in our immediate environments serves as an adaptive mechanism for early learning across primate species. This study leverages longitudinal eye-tracking data from male infant rhesus macaques collected at up to 14 timepoints from birth to six months to chart visual attention patterns to social videos of unknown conspecifics or mother-infant dyads in a group setting. The distribution of oculomotor movements that index the extent of infant attention to the video stimuli – fixations, saccades, and inattention, i.e., data lost to offscreen looks or movement – stayed constant during this developmental period. Attention to different body areas – mouth, head and body - showed subtle and progressive changes from birth to six months, except for attention to the eyes of conspecifics, which showed two distinct periods of significant increase. The matrilineal social rank of the infant was also investigated as a social factor related to patterns of attention. Rank was significantly associated with the percent of time infants spent making saccades, such that low-ranking infants spent more viewing time making saccades than their high-ranking peers. This association was established by five weeks of age. Collectively, these results provide insight into processes of social attention related to social status in rhesus macaques during infancy.

There are 29 main drying parameters, and by adding the second-order interaction, the parameters increased to 435 parameters to capture interaction effects. For non-linear and high-dimensional data, traditional models cannot handle the problem. Then, we applied the Elman Neural Network (ENN) based on the Whale Optimization Algorithm, support vector regression, ENN, and partial least squares regression methods to develop the predictive models. From the results, the hybrid WOA-ENN model is better, with the root mean square error of prediction of 0.0710, a correlation coefficient of 0.9974, and the relative percent deviation of 3.1165.

The distinct differences in the probability of choosing and spending on public and private transportation indicate groups targeted for possible change in transportation choice. Low-income households and recipients of public assistance as well as those working in agriculture will benefit from guidance and assistance in choosing less-polluting transportation. Article.Authors: Lin T.; Lian Q.; Zhong B.; Lin C.
Article.Abstract: Monascin (MS) and ankaflavin (AK) are bioactive yellow pigments produced by Monascus species, known for their health benefits and safety profile compared to monacolin K. This study developed an integrated strategy combining Response Surface Methodology (RSM) for submerged fermentation optimization and a downstream purification process to maximize MS and AK production by Monascus purpureus TST. Although the results of this study demonstrate that RSM did not successfully predict the optimal production conditions, the RSM optimization revealed significant interactions between sucrose, ammonium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate heptahydrate. Verification experiments confirmed that the optimal culture conditions for M. purpureus TST were 200 g/L sucrose, 17.5 g/L (NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 , and 0.1 g/L MgSO 4 · 7H 2 O. Under these conditions, MS and AK yields reached 2987 ± 530 mg/L and 1678 ± 259 mg/L, representing 5.98-fold and 3.72-fold increases, respectively, while restricting CT production to 0.96 mg/L. Furthermore, a streamlined purification protocol involving an aminophilic reaction for orange pigment removal, followed by n -hexane extraction and column chromatography, was established. This method achieved purification factors of 7564 and 10,679 for MS and AK, respectively, with high purity (> 90%, determined by an HPLC calibration curve on a weight basis). These findings represent highly competitive MS and AK productivities in Monascus submerged fermentation using non-genetic engineering approaches. providing a potential basis for industrial-scale production. Although this study explored the optimization of MS and AK production through Monascus submerged fermentation, many critical influencing factors are difficult to adequately investigate in shake-flask cultures. Building upon the findings of this study, future research should employ bioreactors for more in-depth investigations into fermentation production.

Article.Authors: Kim A.; Goh M.; Song B.; Sinn D.; Gwak G.; Paik Y.; Choi M.; Lee J.; Kang W.
Article.Abstract: The influence of antibiotic (ATB) exposure on the therapeutic efficacy of immunotherapy remains unclear for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC). This study aims to investigate the impact of early and late ATB exposure during atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (atezo/bev) therapy on progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) in uHCC patients. In this retrospective cohort study, patients with uHCC receiving atezo/bev as first-line therapy between August 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed. We used propensity score (PS) matching at a 1:2 ratio for covariates. A total of 177 uHCC patients were analyzed. Early ATB exposure was associated with significantly shorter PFS (2.3 vs. 6.3 months, Log rank p = 0.025; HR 1.92, p = 0.025) and OS (5.8 vs. 16.9 months, Log rank p = 0.0016; HR 2.30, p = 0.019). Similar results were observed in PS-matched analyses of PFS and OS. Late ATB exposure, in comparison to no ATB exposure, showed comparable PFS (6.1 vs. 6.5 months, Log rank p = 0.60; HR 0.74, p = 0.39) and OS (8.2 vs. 16.9 months, Log rank p = 0.31; HR 1.06, p = 0.89). In addition, late ATB exposure was associated with longer PFS and OS compared to early ATB exposure. Article.Title: Territorial African wood-doves respond differently to intruders with higher and lower frequency of songs
Article.Authors: Osiejuk T.; Niśkiewicz M.; Szymański P.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to examine the potential influence of long-distance acoustic signal frequency produced by the blue-headed wood-doves, Turtur brehmeri , on responses to a simulated territorial intrusion by a stranger male. The blue-spotted wood-dove is an African equatorial forest inhabitant that defends long-term, stable territories and exhibits different responses to known neighbours and unknown strangers. Males repeat their single song with a highly repetitive structure, including frequency parameters. Although the limited sample size reduced our power to detect subtle associations, our results do not provide evidence for a within-species relationship between body size and song frequency. Song frequency may nevertheless influence territorial interactions through mechanisms other than signalling body size. Hypothesizing that these doves tune their response to unknown rivals based on the perception of their song frequency, we predicted that males differentiate the strength of their response to intruders characterised by relatively low or high song frequency and should respond stronger or more cautious to songs of intruder which are lower than their own song frequency, in comparison to the songs which have higher frequency. A total of 25 males were tested twice, in random order, with either a low- or a high-frequency song of the unknown intruder. Birds differed significantly in their responses and avoided approaching the playback in the low-frequency treatment, which we interpreted as more cautious response, as staying at a greater distance from the speaker decreases the chance of a physical fight. We also observed a single male attempting to lower the frequency of his song in response to low-frequency playback, which, however, resulted in distortion of the phrase structure. The findings of this study enhance our understanding of how birds, especially doves, perceive differences in song frequency. They clearly indicate that birds take this characteristic into account even when it is not strongly linked to simple body features associated with size. Repeatability of song structure and rare attempts to change the frequency suggest that the change in frequency is constrained by a production mechanism or by vocal-tract characteristics.

Article.Title: Treatment depth effects on settlement and deformation compatibility of dynamic compaction replacement foundations in coastal soft soil

Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate treatment-depth effects on settlement and deformation compatibility in coastal soft soil, a two-dimensional axisymmetric finite-element model was developed for the Huanhu Road section in Dongfang City. The dynamic compaction replacement region was represented as an equivalent linear-elastic improved zone within a total-stress framework, while two prescribed groundwater-depth cases were used only as auxiliary sensitivity checks of the adopted density-based representation. As treatment depth increased from 3.0 to 6.0 m, settlement in the treated area changed only slightly, whereas settlement in the adjacent untreated area increased from 0.252 to 0.350 m. Consequently, differential settlement increased from 0.052 to 0.132 m and the differential settlement ratio from 20.8 to 37.8%. Stress- and strain-response analyses indicate that this trend is associated with vertical stress redistribution and an increasing mismatch in compressive deformation between the treated and untreated areas. The 3.5–4.0 m cases showed a relatively balanced response between settlement control and deformation compatibility within the investigated range. Article.Title: Association between urine calcium creatinine ratio and arterial stiffness among Chinese adults undergoing health screening with normal renal function
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Ouyang W.; Wu H.; Zhao Z.; Yang P.; Qin Y.; Deng J.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Arterial stiffness is a significant precursor of cardiovascular diseases (CVD), influenced by calcium metabolic homeostasis. This study included 21,834 subjects from annual health check-ups (2017–2020) and a prospective cohort of 3219 subjects followed from 2020 to 2024 at the Third Xiangya Hospital in Hunan, China. Arterial stiffness was assessed by brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) and classified as normal-to-mild (baPWV ≤ 1700 cm/s) or moderate-to-severe arterial stiffness (moderate-to-severe AS). Logistic regression models were used for cross-sectional analysis, and Cox proportional hazards models were used for the cohort analysis. In the cross-sectional study, a significant nonlinear association was observed between UCa/Cr and moderate-to-severe AS ( P overall < 0.001, P nonlinearity = 0.010). Compared with the lowest UCa/Cr group (< 0.049), the highest group (≥ 0.109) had a 36% higher odds of moderate‑to‑severe AS (aOR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.11, 1.65). In the cohort study, over 7144 person-years of follow-up, 145 individuals developed moderate-to-severe AS. A significant overall association was observed between UCa/Cr and the risk of moderate-to-severe AS ( P overall = 0.014). Compared with the lowest UCa/Cr group (< 0.049), the highest group (≥ 0.109) had more than a two-fold higher risk of incident moderate‑to‑severe AS (aHR = 2.12, 95% CI: 1.18, 3.82). Further adjustment for continuous SBP and DBP attenuated both associations, which were no longer statistically significant. In the primary analyses, UCa/Cr was associated with both prevalent and incident moderate-to-severe AS, with the association most evident at higher UCa/Cr levels, but the findings were sensitive to adjustment for SBP.

Article.Title: Prognostic value of RDW-to-platelet ratio for short- and long-term mortality after cardiac surgery: dual-center MIMIC-IV and external validation

Fully adjusted hazard ratios for T3 were 2.168 (95% CI 1.300–3.614) for 28-day mortality and 1.575 (95% CI 1.111–2.233) for 365-day mortality. RCS revealed a nonlinear U-shaped relationship (P for nonlinear < 0.001 and = 0.001, respectively). Subgroup effects were more pronounced in females, hypertensive patients, and those without diabetes, heart failure, or COPD (P for interaction < 0.05). These findings were validated in the external cohort, which showed similar effect magnitudes and nonlinear patterns (P for nonlinear = 0.001 for 28-day; = 0.003 for 365-day mortality). Kaplan–Meier analysis confirmed significant mortality differences across RPR tertiles in both cohorts. RPR is independently and nonlinearly associated with increased short- and long-term mortality after cardiac surgery, suggesting its utility in perioperative risk stratification.

Article.Authors: Oimpitiwong P.; Hombut P.; Lekvijittada J.; Choontanom R.
Article.Abstract: Telemedicine may support longitudinal management of dry eye disease (DED) through remote communication and symptom monitoring. DEQS also decreased, with a median paired reduction of 8.54 points (IQR, 1.67–15.94; BCa bootstrap 95% CI, 4.58–10.83; Wilcoxon signed-rank p < 0.001). In exploratory multivariable analysis, baseline behavioral factors were not independently associated with OSDI change, whereas higher baseline OSDI was associated with greater subsequent reduction. Ninety participants (93.8%) would use telemedicine again, and 91 (94.8%) reported overall satisfaction. Messaging-based follow-up was highly acceptable, and patient-reported outcomes improved during follow-up; however, these improvements cannot be attributed specifically to telemedicine because usual ophthalmic care continued and no concurrent control group was included.

Article.Title: Statistical mechanics of restroom choice
Article.Authors: Franckart A.; Luyckx A.; Araújo N.; Delens M.; Opsomer E.; Vandewalle N.
Article.Abstract: Human behavior is influenced not only by social interactions but also by the way people interact with their environment. Understanding these different interactions in constrained environments is a central question in behavioral science, but it remains challenging due to the difficulties of data collection. We focus on restrooms with a given number of sites, such as urinals or toilets, as a minimal setting for investigating human behavior. We introduce a web-based platform that enables the collection of large-scale data on sequential occupancy choices in controlled restroom layouts. We analyze transition probabilities between configurations using a statistical physics framework inspired by the Ising model, from which we infer effective interpersonal interactions and site-dependent biases. We further develop a kinetic model describing individual arrivals and departures, which allows us to predict site usage as a function of the utilization factor. Finally, we demonstrate that the model generalizes across restroom of different sizes, enabling prediction of usage and dynamics from limited data. Beyond this specific system, our results demonstrate how simple local rules can generate predictable collective behavior in constrained environments, with implications for a broad class of public spaces such as waiting room or public transportation.

Article.Title: Quality of life and associated factors in patients three months after spinal tumor surgery
Article.Authors: Laska E.
Article.Abstract: Spinal tumors constitute a heterogeneous group of neoplasms that may lead to neurological deficits, pain, and functional impairment. Beyond tumor biology and oncological treatment, patients’ quality of life (QoL) is shaped by psychosocial adaptation, yet early postoperative data are limited. This study evaluated QoL, functional independence, illness acceptance, and perceived social support three months after spinal tumor surgery to characterize early recovery needs. Sixty-seven patients were evaluated using four standardized instruments: the World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF (WHOQOL-BREF), Zimet’s Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS), the Lawton Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale (I-ADL), and the Acceptance of Illness Scale (AIS). Statistical analysis included Spearman’s rank correlation, the Mann–Whitney U test, the Kruskal–Wallis test, and exploratory multiple linear regression. QoL differed significantly across disease stages, with the highest scores in stage I and progressive declines in later stages. Perceived social support also varied by disease stage, with the lowest values observed in stage IV. AIS correlated positively with all QoL domains (ρ = 0.42–0.69), while I-ADL correlated with the psychological, social, and environmental domains (ρ = 0.31–0.51). Disease stage correlated negatively with QoL across domains (ρ = −0.54 to − 0.89). Exploratory regression showed that AIS and MSPSS were independently associated with several QoL domains, while I-ADL was independently associated only with the psychological domain. These findings indicate that three months after spinal tumor surgery, QoL is associated with disease stage, illness acceptance, functional independence, and perceived social support, supporting psychosocial and functional screening in early postoperative rehabilitation.

Article.Title: Biochar and PGPR co-application mitigates salinity stress in Malabar spinach (Basella alba L.) by modulating growth, stress markers, and antioxidant defense
Article.Authors: Altihani F.; Elbagory M.; EL-Khateeb N.; El-Nahrawy S.; Mohamed I.; El-Sharkawy M.; Arya A.; Kumar P.; Širić I.
Article.Abstract: Soil salinity is a major problem for agricultural productivity, adversely affecting plant growth, physiology, and biochemical performance. Malabar spinach ( Basella alba L. ), an important leafy vegetable with high nutritional value, is sensitive to salinity stress, leading to reduced yield and market quality. Developing sustainable strategies to mitigate these effects is essential for its cultivation in marginal soils. This study aimed to evaluate the individual and combined application of biochar and plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) in alleviating salt stress in B. alba . Proline accumulation increased as part of the osmotic adjustment response typical under salt stress. For example, 150 mM NaCl reduced plant height by approximately 36% and chlorophyll content by 30% compared with the control. The combined biochar + PGPR treatment improved plant height by 54% and chlorophyll levels by 39% relative to the salted control, while also lowering Na⁺ accumulation by 41%. Both amendments individually improved growth, RWC, K⁺/Na⁺ balance, and antioxidant enzyme activity under salinity, while the combined biochar + PGPR treatment produced the strongest recovery, showing the greatest improvements in pigment stability, ionic balance, and oxidative stress reduction. This work provides one of the first detailed evaluations of biochar–PGPR co-application in B. alba , demonstrating a practical biological strategy for improving crop tolerance in salt-affected systems.

The relative duct-parenchymal ratio at 5 years was greater in the TG group (P = 0.044). Function-preserving gastrectomy based on the sentinel node concept was associated with better pancreatic volume preservation than TG. This difference reflects the combined effects of the extent of gastric resection and lymphadenectomy and requires prospective confirmation.

Article.Authors: Coşkun Y.; Özyılmaz L.; Aydın M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Simulation-based controller comparisons can report a single winner even when score differences are too small to justify a unique engineering preference. Under the common uncertainty score, PID had the lowest controller robustness index in every band, but the four leading indices remained within 3.87%. In the pooled ± 15% domain, all ten paired comparisons were detectable after Holm correction, yet 69.40% of 2,000 scenario blocks lacked a unique practical preference. PID retained rank one in 99.95% of paired-bootstrap replicates but only 63.16% and 43.06% under two weight-variation analyses. Post-review sensitivity analyses showed that the principal practical-separation conclusion was robust to the tested CRI coefficient, realization-specific median normalization, and heavier-tail dependence models, while command delay altered separation among near-tied controllers. These findings are specific to the fixed controller portfolio, score definition, RIP model, and simulated uncertainty domain.

Article.Authors: Yang L.; Tan X.; Wang N.; Jin Y.; Li G.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to examine the association between early warm and safe memories and healthy eating among college students, and to delineate the statistical mediating pathways involving anxiety and subjective well-being. Bivariate correlation analyses revealed that early warm and safe memories were negatively associated with anxiety ( r = -0.331) but positively associated with subjective well-being ( r = 0.366) and healthy eating ( r = 0.237). Anxiety was negatively associated with both subjective well-being ( r = -0.378) and healthy eating ( r = -0.206), whereas subjective well-being was positively associated with healthy eating ( r = 0.185). After adjustment for sex, age, parental educational attainment, grade level, and only-child status, the full model—incorporating early warm and safe memories, anxiety, subjective well-being, and the covariates—accounted for 8.6% of the variance in healthy eating. The unstandardized total indirect effect was estimated at 0.026, corresponding to 29.55% of the total effect. Decomposition of this effect yielded an unstandardized indirect effect of 0.015 through anxiety alone (17.05%; 95% CI [0.010, 0.021]), 0.008 through subjective well-being alone (9.09%; 95% CI [0.004, 0.012]), and 0.003 through the complete serial pathway from early warm and safe memories via anxiety and subjective well-being to healthy eating (3.41%; 95% CI [0.001, 0.004]). Overall, early warm and safe memories displayed the relatively strongest standardized direct association with healthy eating. Among the three indirect pathways, the pathway mediated solely by anxiety made the largest contribution, whereas the complete serial pathway contributed only marginally. Article.Title: Count-based popularity control under-corrects semantic-popularity exposure in text-aware recommender systems
Article.Authors: Esmeli R.; Abdullahi H.
Article.Abstract: Popularity bias in recommender systems is commonly measured from an item’s own interaction count, leaving the popularity structure encoded by semantically related items largely unaccounted for. Across five Amazon Reviews 2023 categories, direct semantic control reduced SPE more than matched count-based control at every positive penalty strength, and this ordering remained consistent with independent LightGCN and SASRec recommenders in all 10 dataset-backbone combinations under a baseline-relative 5% NDCG floor. At matched achieved NDCG, semantic control also produced lower mean SPE at every non-baseline utility target, while neighbourhood ablations showed that random-neighbour, category-mean and count-based signals were substantially weaker than semantic-neighbour signals. Across the five dataset-level units, the slope-based count-to-semantic transfer closely tracked the pre-intervention correlation between count popularity and semantic popularity (Pearson \(r=0.873\) ; mean absolute deviation \(=0.029\) ), supporting \(T\approx r\) as a descriptive first-order approximation rather than an exact law. These findings show that interaction-count popularity and semantic popularity represent distinct exposure dimensions in text-aware recommender systems, and suggest that semantic neighbourhood structure should be audited alongside conventional popularity measures when designing popularity-control mechanisms.

Article.Title: Multi-angle validation of the iFalcon V700 rebound tonometer against implantable pressure sensor in ex-vivo rabbit eyes
Article.Authors: Cui X.; Liu Y.; Yang L.; Chen Q.; Fu J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rabbits are widely employed as ophthalmic models due to their favorable corneal geometry and biomechanical properties; however, intraocular pressure (IOP) measurements in both clinical and experimental settings are frequently performed under non-ideal body positions that may introduce off-axis spatial orientations relative to gravity. Despite this reality, no rebound tonometer has been validated for multi-angle use in rabbit eyes, leaving the impact of spatial inclination and gravitational deviation on measurement accuracy unknown. To validate the performance of the iFalcon V700 rebound tonometer across a 0–90° spatial inclination range (while maintaining strict perpendicularity between the probe and cornea) using an implanted pressure sensor as the gold standard. Experimental laboratory investigation. Four ex-vivo rabbit eyes. A motorized mechanical assembly facilitated multi-angle positioning of the eyes at seven distinct angles from 0° to 90° using 15° increments. An adjustable lead screw was used to gradually increase pressure to generate a physiologically relevant IOP range (8–50 mmHg). Simultaneous measurements were acquired using the iFalcon V700 tonometer (in rabbit-specific mode) and the implanted sensor, with precise synchronization ensured by a host computer program. Data distribution, linear regression, and Bland-Altman analyses were performed. IOP measurement agreement, correlation, and range-dependent biases between the rebound tonometer and the implanted sensor across various angles. Violin plot distributions of the iFalcon V700 closely mirrored the implanted sensor across all angles, with absolute median differences (|Δ Median|) remaining clinically negligible (range: 0.34–1.35 mmHg) and no significant measurement differences detected ( P = 0.398–0.973). Regression analysis revealed a strong positive correlation (R² = 0.962–0.989). However, range-dependent biases were present; a negative intercept suggested underestimation at lower IOP, whereas a slope > 1 (range: 1.00–1.11) indicated systematic overestimation at higher pressures. Bland-Altman analysis corroborated this slight overestimation bias, demonstrating mean differences ranging from 0.05 mmHg (at 0°) to 1.12 mmHg (at 90°), with 95% limits of agreement tightly confined, reaching a maximum width of -4.46 to 5.89 mmHg at 45°. Validated against an implantable pressure sensor, the iFalcon V700 rebound tonometer demonstrated high agreement across the 8–50 mmHg range and maintained robust mechanical and algorithmic stability throughout 0–90° multi-angle measurements under controlled ex vivo conditions. Despite range-dependent overestimation at higher pressures, this study, heavily constrained by its small sample size ( n = 4 eyes), must be interpreted strictly as a preliminary pilot study and an engineering proof-of-concept for multi-angle tonometry. Therefore, adequately powered, large-scale validation in living animals and clinical populations is definitively required before any translational claims regarding dynamic positional monitoring can be established.

Article.Title: Concurrency aware artificial intelligence for real-time intrusion detection in software-defined networks
Article.Authors: Kanimozhi R.; Padmavathi V.; Latha M.
Article.Abstract: Contemporary software systems are now being used in environments that are highly concurrent, data-intensive, and latency-sensitive. Software-Defined Networks (SDNs) applications like real-time intrusion detection need fast pattern recognition in large amounts of data streams through time. Although deep learning models have impressive detection capabilities, failure to perform well in real-world deployments is usually limited by poor concurrency management, inflexible scheduling, centralized learning pipelines, and fault tolerance. In this study, the authors suggest a concurrency-aware artificial intelligence (CA-AI) framework that directly incorporates actor-based concurrency control, workflow-based load-aware scheduling, deep long short-term memory (LSTM)-based temporal learning, agent-based parallel feature extraction, and feedback loops based on monitoring. The framework is evaluated for SDN-oriented intrusion detection workloads, where concurrency management is implemented at the system architecture level through actor-based execution, workflow scheduling, and asynchronous inference and tested on real network traffic data samples (NSL-KDD, CIC-IDS2017, and UNSW-NB15). Experimental results demonstrate that concurrency-aware system design leads to a significant improvement in the detection accuracy achieving up to 98.9% detection accuracy across multiple benchmark datasets, including NSL-KDD, CIC-IDS2017, and UNSW-NB15, throughput improved by 2.1 × compared with the centralized IDS baseline, while throughput increased by approximately 1.19 × when concurrency increased from 10,000 to 100,000 flows within the proposed CA-AI framework, average latency was reduced by approximately 57.5% compared with the centralized IDS baseline (146 ms to 62 ms), while maintaining high reliability under concurrent workloads. The proposed framework establishes concurrency as a fundamental architectural principle for scalable AI-driven pattern recognition systems.

Article.Authors: Kamei A.; Nishio Y.; Muramatsu Y.; Tsukada K.; Oka Y.; Tsujikawa K.; Morinaga H.; Kurahashi H.; Muramatsu H.; Takeichi T.; Nakazawa Y.; Okumura A.; Takahashi Y.; Saitoh S.; Ogi T.

Here, we describe two siblings with typical SLS features (developmental delay, hypotonia, and ichthyosis) together with laryngeal cartilage calcification and recurrent airway obstruction, a previously unreported manifestation. Exome sequencing identified compound heterozygous ALDH3A2 variants: a canonical splice-site variant and a synonymous variant of uncertain DNA-level pathogenicity. Iso-Seq quantified three aberrant isoforms with distinct fates: the exon 5–skipped transcript was a primary target of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD); the exon 2–skipped transcript carried a premature termination codon but escaped NMD; and the in-frame exon 4–5–skipped transcript escaped NMD and was the only aberrant isoform predicted to yield a translated in-frame protein, despite an internal 109-amino-acid deletion spanning both NAD-binding and catalytic domains. Structural modeling predicted reduced stability and enzymatic function, and ALDH3A2 protein was virtually undetectable in patient cells, supporting pathogenicity. Long-read transcript analysis thus quantitatively prioritizes the dominant protein-producing isoform for functional interrogation, and expands the clinical spectrum of SLS to include laryngeal cartilage calcification.

Article.Title: Variable diameter configurations influence propane air deflagration and pressure rise in industrial pressurized pipelines
Article.Authors: Zhou N.; Zhou G.; Rao R.; Li X.; Chen B.; Huang W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Variable-diameter sections are widely used in industrial gas transmission, exhaust, and collection pipelines; however, their effects on deflagration-induced pressure loading remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a validated large eddy simulation (LES) scheme integrated with a premixed turbulent combustion model was adopted to investigate the effects of different variable-diameter configurations on propane-air deflagration and transient pressure loading. Four typical configurations were investigated, including contraction-then-expansion, expansion-then-contraction, continuous expansion, and continuous contraction, and their influences on flame propagation dynamics, transient pressure-rise characteristics, and turbulent flow-field evolution were comprehensively examined. The results demonstrate that pipeline geometric parameters dominantly control deflagration hazard evolution via jet flow generation, shear layer intensification, flow recirculation, and vortex-flame interaction. In contraction-then-expansion pressurized pipelines, the contraction segment markedly exacerbates early-phase deflagration. Across the LML and LSL contraction-expansion configurations, the peak flame velocity increases from 44.03 to 112.56 m/s, while the contraction-stage peak pressure-rise rate increases from 10.37 to 61.37 MPa/s. The highest overall pressure-rise rate, 67.48 MPa/s, occurs in the MSL configuration, where the downstream expansion receives the high-momentum flow generated by the upstream contraction. In expansion-then-contraction pressurized pipelines, the expansion segment enhances initial flame fluctuation, whereas the downstream contraction restrains late-phase flame propagation and pressure accumulation. Among the continuous configurations, continuous expansion generates persistent vortical disturbances and induces the most severe overall deflagration hazard, whereas continuous contraction sustains persistent flow confinement and reduces the peak pressure-rise rate to 6.89 MPa/s. These results reveal that expansion-dominated configurations can significantly elevate transient explosion-induced pressure loads, whereas contraction-dominated configurations exhibit superior performance in attenuating pressure-rise intensity. This study offers key engineering guidance for configuration optimization and hazard risk control of industrial pressurized pipelines in explosion-prone process facilities.

Article.Title: JARID2 promotes prostate cancer progression associated with TET3-mediated activation of the FAK/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Liu Y.; Li Y.; Xu L.; Ning J.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: JARID2, a regulatory Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) component, has diverse roles in cancer development, yet its function in prostate cancer (PCa) remains unclear. We analyzed JARID2 expression using TCGA-PRAD data and clinical samples. Functional assays, including CCK-8, wound healing, and Transwell assays, were conducted to assess the influence of JARID2 overexpression or knockdown in PCa cell lines. The JARID2-TET3 interaction was validated by co-immunoprecipitation, and rescue experiments were performed to evaluate TET3’s functional role. Pathway enrichment was analyzed by GSEA and KEGG while assessing in vivo tumor growth employing a xenograft model. JARID2 exhibited a significant overexpression in PCa tissues and cell lines, and was related to advanced N stage and escalated Gleason scores. Functionally, JARID2 enhanced cell proliferation and invasion in vitro, while its knockdown impeded tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, JARID2 interacted with and upregulated TET3, which activated FAK/PI3K/AKT signaling. TET3 knockdown attenuated the oncogenic effects of JARID2 overexpression, whereas TET3 overexpression restored the phenotypes induced by JARID2 silencing. Our findings identify JARID2 as a novel oncogenic factor in PCa that drives tumor progression associated with TET3-dependent FAK/PI3K/AKT signaling activation, highlighting a new epigenetic regulatory axis with potential diagnostic and therapeutic implications.

Article.Title: Cross-sectional associations with symptomatic gallstones among women in Chile
Article.Authors: Daniels M.; Jebai R.; Argirion I.; Pfeiffer R.; Cortés S.; Van De Wyngard V.; Curry M.; Mardones N.; Hildesheim A.; Cook P.; Araya J.; Ferreccio C.; Koshiol J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gallstones (GS) affect 10–20% of adults around the world with a prevalence of around 40% in Chile. Most individuals with GS are asymptomatic, which may reflect underlying differences in disease severity and associated health risks. Few studies have comprehensively assessed factors associated with GS symptomatology. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from the Chile Biliary Longitudinal Study (Chile BiLS), a prospective cohort of middle-aged Chilean women with ultrasound-diagnosed GS. Symptomatic GS (sGS) was defined as self-report of ever having biliary colic or acute cholecystitis. Associations between sGS and personal and clinical characteristics, socioeconomic status, ultrasound characteristics, medication use, occupational pesticide exposure, and key lifestyle factors were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Compared to women with asymptomatic gallstones (aGS), those with sGS were younger, had lower educational attainment, reported more frequent and intense nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms, and had a higher prevalence of several gallbladder ultrasound abnormalities ( P < 0.05). Current occupational pesticide exposure was positively associated with sGS (aOR: 2.26; 95% CI 1.26, 4.06). In this cross-sectional study of women with ultrasound-confirmed gallstones in the Araucanía region of Chile, sGS were associated with younger age, lower educational attainment, greater gastrointestinal symptom burden, several gallbladder ultrasound abnormalities, and current occupational pesticide exposure. These findings characterize differences between symptomatic and asymptomatic gallstone disease in this population and warrant confirmation in longitudinal studies, particularly for occupational pesticide exposure.

Article.Title: Environmental distribution of African swine fever virus DNA in pig farm wastewater and Amblyomma javanense ticks in Vietnam
Article.Authors: Mai T.; Duong D.; Dong V.; Tran T.; Cao T.; Huynh T.; Bui T.; Dao V.; Nguyen T.; Hoang T.; Bui T.; Nguyen T.; Yamazaki Y.; Yamazaki W.
Article.Abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) is a major threat to pig production, yet its environmental distribution in Southeast Asian farming systems poorly understood. We investigated ASFV DNA in pig farm wastewater and Amblyomma javanense ticks collected from rescued Sunda pangolins in Vietnam. In field samples, ASFV DNA was detected more frequently after PEG concentration, and additional detections were supported by an independent p54 -targeting rPCR. Infectious virus was not recovered from rPCR-positive wastewater. ASFV DNA was also detected in a small proportion of the examined ticks, with independent-target testing providing additional molecular support in available material. These findings broaden information on the environmental distribution of ASFV DNA and support further evaluation of wastewater and wildlife-associated ticks as complementary molecular surveillance matrices, without demonstrating environmental transmission or tick vector competence.

Article.Title: Effects of podcast supported multicomponent education on treatment adherence and self care management in patients with hypertension
Article.Authors: Bahçecioğlu Turan G.; Alanoğlu M.
Article.Abstract: Podcast-supported education may provide flexible and repeated access to health information; however, evidence regarding its use in hypertension remains limited. This study aimed to determine the effect of a podcast-supported multicomponent educational intervention on treatment adherence and self-care management in patients with hypertension. This study employed a randomized controlled experimental design. The study included patients with hypertension attending the internal medicine outpatient clinic of a university hospital in eastern Türkiye. Participants were randomly assigned to the intervention ( n = 47) or control ( n = 47) group. The intervention group received eight podcast episodes over four weeks, with two episodes delivered per week. Participants were asked to listen to each episode at least once during its initial delivery, once again during the second month, and once during the third month. Repeated engagement was supported through scheduled reminders and monitored using participant-coded Google Forms and available Spotify analytics. The control group received conventional face-to-face education and a printed booklet covering the same core educational content. Treatment adherence and self-care management were assessed at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months. Significant time × group interactions were observed for treatment adherence, F(1.74, 160.30) = 10.108, p < .001, ηp² = 0.099, and self-care management, F(1.70, 156.01) = 40.870, p < .001, ηp² = 0.308. At 1 month, treatment adherence scores were lower in the intervention group than in the control group (10.32 ± 5.18 vs. 15.98 ± 7.79, p < .001), while self-care management scores were higher (129.74 ± 12.15 vs. 113.15 ± 21.80, p < .001). At 3 months, treatment adherence scores remained lower in the intervention group (8.83 ± 5.00 vs. 17.89 ± 7.51, p < .001), whereas self-care management scores remained higher (132.23 ± 11.29 vs. 97.94 ± 14.94, p < .001). The improvements observed at 1 month were maintained at 3 months. The podcast-supported multicomponent educational intervention was associated with greater improvements in treatment adherence and self-care management than conventional education among patients with hypertension. Because podcast delivery was combined with repeated access, reminders, engagement monitoring, and technical support, the findings reflect the overall intervention package rather than the independent effect of the podcast component.

Article.Title: Automated grain-size characterization of GTAW Ti-6Al-4 V weldments using OpenCV and comparison with ASTM-based intercept methods
Article.Authors: Gudisi M.; Talari M.; Gopal A.; Nagallapati V.
Article.Abstract: Quantitative measurement of grain size in the fusion zone (FZ) of Ti-6Al-4 V GTAW weldments is difficult because the large, uneven grain morphologies can introduce operator bias in conventional metallography. Four GTAW conditions were considered: conventional DC, pulsed DC, ultrasonic vibration-assisted (UAV) DC, and UAV pulsed DC. The workflow comprises grayscale conversion, filtering, boundary detection, segmentation, morphological operations, grain identification and spatial calibration at approximately 3.03 μm/pixel for the FZ micrographs. Relative to the planimetric, linear-intercept and three-circle methods, the OpenCV mean biases were − 20.18, -65.13, and − 128.12 μm, with mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 6.47%, 17.04%, and 29.60%, respectively. Although the OpenCV approach enables consistent grain-size determination, it should not be regarded as an exact replacement for ASTM E112 analysis.

Article.Title: Experimental enhancement of a double-slope solar still using external reflectors and nano-coated absorber plates for solar desalination
Article.Authors: Agegnehu B.; Sinte Y.; Ali H.; Kebede M.
Article.Abstract: Freshwater scarcity, particularly in arid and off-grid regions, demands efficient and low-cost desalination technologies. While solar stills offer a sustainable solution, their low productivity remains a key limitation. Studies on the combined effect of external reflectors and nanoparticle-coated absorber plates in double-slope solar stills are scarce, and no such investigation has been conducted under the climatic conditions of Gondar, Ethiopia. Experiments were conducted in December 2023 and May 2024 at water depths of 2 cm, 2.5 cm, and 3 cm to optimize performance. A water depth of 2 cm consistently produced the highest distillate output across all configurations. The CuO-coated absorber plate with reflectors achieved the maximum productivity of 4.95 L day −1 (3.30 L m −2 day −1 ) with a thermal efficiency of 38.38%, substantially exceeding the typical efficiency range for conventional double-slope stills (25–34%). Reflectors alone increased productivity by 130.7% (1.37 to 3.16 L day −1 ), while the combined use of reflectors and CuO coating improved productivity by 261.3% (1.37 to 4.95 L day −1 ) and thermal efficiency by 27.10% points. The CuO coating outperformed Al 2 O 3 by 6.7% after normalization for irradiance variations. Theoretical predictions agreed closely with experimental results for the CuO configuration (difference < 0.5 L day −1 ), though the model over-predicted the black-paint case by 49%, highlighting the importance of accurate absorptance inputs. The proposed system offers a passive, low-cost solution for decentralized water production in off-grid communities, with demonstrated potential for significant productivity enhancement. Water quality testing is recommended to confirm compliance with drinking water standards in future studies.

Volatile profile of virus-injected pupae differed from controls. The ultimate consequence of such differences might lead to virus specific hygienic responses.

Peripheral and hepatic venous sampling showed strong concordance, supporting peripheral blood as a practical sampling alternative. These findings support an exploratory, research-stage tumor–immune balance framework for risk stratification after radioembolization and provide a rationale for validation of CTC/lymphocyte-based biomarkers in contemporary HCC cohorts.

Article.Authors: Zhao Q.; Zhi D.; Wu Y.

Experiments on HRSC2016, NWPU VHR-10, and DOTA-v1.5 datasets show that the proposed method outperforms the baseline RT-DETR by 9.0% in precision, 16.5% in recall, 19.0% in mAP@50, and 14.1% in mAP@50:95. A two-endmember mixing model constrains the product of the stored fraction ( f ) and the mean age of stored carbon ( \({{\bar{\uptau }}}\) ) to ≈ 1.3–1.7 year, and for \({{\bar{\uptau }}} \) = 2–3 year, f = 0.5–0.7 (0.70 ± 0.27 for an exponential-age pool). The leaf Δ 14 C zero-crossing in 2024 lagged the atmospheric crossing by 2.2 ± 0.3 year, and the offset re-opened to + 11‰ in 2024 as the Suess-effect decline steepened. Article.Authors: Suliman L.; Zhong Z.; Liu X.; Zhou X.
Article.Abstract: Tunnel excavation through fill slopes under extreme rainfall involves complex hydro-mechanical interactions among excavation-induced stress redistribution, rainfall infiltration, slope deformation, and adjacent infrastructure. This study investigates the response and stability of a tunnel–fill slope system using integrated physical model testing and numerical simulation. The physical experiments examined rainfall infiltration, ground settlement, stress redistribution, and pore-water-pressure evolution during excavation. The validation test simulated an upper-range heavy-rainfall event of 200 mm/day for 12 h at prototype scale, corresponding to approximately 16.67 mm/day applied for 1 h in the 1:120-scale model. Agreement between the experimental and numerical results confirmed the model’s ability to reproduce the principal hydraulic and deformation responses. Two parametric investigations were subsequently conducted. The first evaluated the effects of adjacent buildings and foundation systems under rainfall and dry conditions, focusing on building settlement and slope-supporting pile displacement. The second assessed riprap, geocell reinforcement, and vegetation under rainfall without building loads by examining slope deformation and pore-water-pressure development. The results demonstrate that rainfall intensifies hydro-mechanical responses and structural deformation, while the effectiveness of protection measures varies according to their hydraulic and mechanical functions. These findings support the selection of suitable foundation systems and slope-protection strategies in complex urban fill-slope environments.

Article.Abstract: In biological sciences, biofluids often display complex behavior due to the presence of nanoscale particles such as cells, molecules, and microorganisms. The Casson-Maxwell-Oldroyd-B nanofluid model is instrumental in analyzing the physical and thermal characteristics of such fluids in biological processes, including microbial movement and blood flow. This study explores the combined effects of entropy generation and microbial motion in the electrically conductive flow of a Casson-Maxwell-Oldroyd-B nanofluid over an inclined cylindrical surface embedded in a porous medium. Important physical phenomena such as activation energy, chemical reactions, variable thermal conductivity, electric forces, and viscous dissipation are incorporated into the model. The problem is formulated as a system of nonlinear partial differential equations with appropriate boundary conditions, which are then transformed into a dimensionless form using suitable scaling techniques. The dimensionless equations are solved numerically using an efficient RKF45 computational method. The effects of key physical parameters are analyzed and illustrated through graphical and tabular results. The final outcomes of this study provide valuable insights for the development of biomedical devices, including drug delivery systems, artificial blood flow models and may more.

Article.Title: Prevalence and associated factors of multiple unhealthy lifestyle behaviors among older adults in Iran: insights from the STEPS 2021 survey
Article.Authors: Mossavarali S.; Azizpour Y.; Azadnajafabad S.; Ebrahimpur M.; Sharifi F.; Mirzad M.; Akbarpour S.; Payab M.; Rezaei N.
Article.Abstract: Unhealthy lifestyle behaviors (ULBs) are major contributors to non-communicable diseases, yet nationally representative evidence among Iranian older adults remains limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence, clustering, and determinants of ULBs in this population. This cross-sectional secondary analysis included 5,650 participants aged ≥ 60 years from Iran’s 2021 STEPS survey. Among 5,960 participants who met the age criterion, 310 were excluded due to missing data on lifestyle or other key variables. This study assessed five ULBs: inadequate fruit/vegetable intake (< 5 mean servings/day), insufficient physical activity (< 150 min/week moderate-to-vigorous activity), current smoking (any use in the past year), current alcohol consumption (any use in the past year), and abnormal BMI (underweight < 18.5 or overweight/obese ≥ 25 kg/m²). The number of ULBs was summed and categorized as 0–1, 2, 3, or ≥ 4. Weighted prevalence estimates were calculated, and sex-stratified multinomial logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with the number of ULBs. Overall, 98.8% of participants had at least one ULB, and 53.4% had ≥ 3. The most prevalent behaviors were inadequate fruit and vegetable intake (87.3%), insufficient physical activity (77.6%), and abnormal BMI (69.3%). The prevalence of multiple ULBs was higher among individuals with hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases. Among females, age ≥ 80 years and a middle wealth index were associated with higher relative risk ratios (RRR) for having both 2 and 3 ULBs versus 0–1 ULBs, while a history of hypertension was associated with a higher relative risk ratio for having 3 ULBs versus 0–1 ULBs. Among males, a history of hypertension was associated with higher RRRs for having both 2 and 3 ULBs versus 0–1 ULBs. Age 70–79 years was associated with lower RRRs for having 3 and ≥ 4 ULBs, while age ≥ 80 years was associated with a lower RRR for having ≥ 4 ULBs. Higher wealth was generally associated with lower RRRs, particularly for ≥ 4 ULBs. ULBs are highly prevalent and frequently co-occur among Iranian older adults, with distinct sex-specific patterns. Integrated, multi-behavioral interventions leveraging existing primary healthcare systems are needed to promote healthy aging.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based ensemble model for the risk stratification of myocardial injury in physical examination data
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Wang Q.; Lu S.; Gu J.; Zhou S.; Li P.; Jin Z.; Zhao T.; Tian F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inflammatory diseases such as myocarditis, which can be caused by a variety of factors, severely impact cardiac function and may lead to heart failure and death. Myocardial injury is widely recognized as an early and common pathological manifestation in the progression of myocarditis. With the widespread adoption of health check-ups, physical examination data has become a valuable resource for the early detection of diseases. This study aims to develop a machine learning-based model for assessing the risk of myocardial injury using routine physical examination data. Participants recruited in 2024 and 2025 were used for model development and temporal validation, respectively. Variable and sample selection were performed based on missing values, followed by multiple imputation via chained equations. A hill climbing algorithm was utilized to optimize model selection and parameter tuning, resulting in the integration of five ML models: Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Classification and Regression Trees (CART) Classifier, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM) Classifier. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC, calibration plot and Brier score. Feature importance was assessed using the SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) method. Performance evaluation results demonstrated that the ensemble model showed modest but statistically supported improvement over all individual classifiers in risk prediction of myocardial injury, as verified by paired DeLong test for AUC and McNemar’s test for classification discordance. The ensemble model achieved 81.8% AUC (0.2-2.0 increase), 89.7% accuracy (0.2%-2.7% improvement), 70.1% recall (2.9%-15.2% increase), and 75.8% F1-score (1.7%-8.2% higher) on the test set, while it retained stable performance on the temporal validation cohort with an AUC of 0.812 (95% CI: 0.768–0.856) and accuracy of 88.8% (95% CI: 0.847–0.929). Ablation experiments confirmed that each base classifier contributed predictive gain to the integrated framework, and our hill climbing-based weight adjustment strategy yielded highest overall performance compared with fixed equal-weight fusion. The ensemble model proposed in this study provides support for the risk stratification of biochemical myocardial injury. High-risk individuals identified by this model allows targeted further myocarditis-related examinations, facilitating early screening and timely early intervention. The final prediction model was implemented into a web application to enhance its practicality in clinical settings.

Article.Title: Improving prenatal thalassemia carrier detection with a combined MCV and MCH strategy: a 24-year retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Chen H.; Lin S.; Li C.; Ko T.; Yang Q.; Tai Y.
Article.Abstract: Carrier screening for thalassemia conventionally uses a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) cutoff ≤ 80 fL. However, silent carriers harboring mild mutations often present with borderline indices, which, if missed, may result in offspring with hemoglobin H disease or other significant hemoglobinopathies. Thus, we aimed to evaluate whether alternative hematological cutoffs could reduce this detection gap. Of 15,212 prenatal samples collected in Taiwan between 2000 and 2024, this retrospective cohort study analyzed 9,949 genetically confirmed thalassemia carriers (α-thalassemia, n = 7,473; β-thalassemia, n = 2,476) and 3,025 genotype-negative individuals, who served as the noncarrier reference group. The sensitivity and specificity of the conventional MCV threshold and alternative strategies incorporating higher MCV cutoffs and mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) ≤ 27 pg were calculated and compared, stratified by sex. -- SEA deletion (78.71% of α-thalassemia carriers) and IVS-II-654 mutation (34.65% of β-thalassemia carriers) were the predominant genotypes. Under the conventional MCV threshold, approximately 5.3% of carriers were missed, including 6.3% and 2.3% of α- and β-thalassemia carriers, respectively. Among the predefined candidate thresholds evaluated, the MCV ≤ 82 fL or MCH ≤ 27 pg criterion achieved sensitivity exceeding 99% in both sexes in this cohort and reduced the missed-carrier rate to < 1%, with lower specificity and more false-positive classifications. Because the preferred MCV threshold was selected after examination of the observed candidate performance, these findings are exploratory, apply to initial screening rather than diagnosis, and require prospective validation in an unselected prenatal population.

Article.Title: A supportive intervention on infertile couples for continuing infertility treatments: a randomized trial
Article.Authors: Ghorbani M.; Keramat A.; Yunesian M.; Salehin S.; Talebi S.; Hoseini F.
Article.Abstract: Infertility affects 10-15% of couples globally, with high treatment dropout rates (22-72%) due to psychological, financial, and cultural barriers. Despite evidence supporting psychosocial interventions, few address post-failure continuation in resource-limited settings like Iran, where stigma and costs disproportionately impact adherence. The aim of this RCT was to evaluate a tailored intervention for improving treatment continuation intention, reducing infertility-related stress, and enhancing mental health among Iranian couples with prior treatment discontinuation. Parallel-group RCT (CONSORT-compliant) with block randomization (1:1 allocation, block size = 4) was done on 130 women (18–42 years) who discontinued IVF/ICSI/FET after at least one unsuccessful infertility treatment in Jahad Daneshgahi Infertility Center, Qom, Iran (June–December 2021). Primary outcome was treatment continuation intention (assessed by researcher-made questionnaire based on the Transtheoretical Model). Secondary outcomes included infertility stress (assessed by Newton’s Fertility Problem Inventory (FPI)), mental health (assessed by General Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28)), and communication skills (assessed by Queendom Communication Skills Test (CSTR)). The Intervention included four weekly online sessions (psychoeducation, CBT techniques, and communication skills) plus six asynchronous modules. Controls received an assessment-only control condition. Study questionnaires were completed by participants at baseline (pre-intervention) and two weeks’ post-intervention. The intervention group showed 11.5-fold higher odds of treatment continuation (aOR = 11.49, 95% CI: 2.24–58.77, p = 0.003), with 84.2%of initially reluctant participants opting to continue vs. 28.0% in controls ( p < 0.001). There were no significant improvements in infertility stress or mental health and communication skills. While the intervention significantly improved continuation intentions, its limited psychological impact suggests that infertility-related stress in this population of treatment-discontinued couples may be more closely related to decisional conflict and motivational barriers to re-engaging with treatment than to clinical psychiatric symptoms. Cultural stigma and economic burdens emerged as critical, under-addressed dropout drivers. Brief, low-cost psychoeducation can enhance treatment adherence in high-stigma settings, but integrated financial support and culturally adapted mental health care are needed for holistic impact. Trial registration: The study is registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials with the IRCT20210516051315N1 (30/05/2021).

Article.Title: Integrating dft-based spectroscopic analysis, molecular docking, admet prediction, and natural biosorbent adsorption studies of flupyradifurone
Article.Authors: Türköz Altuğ D.
Article.Abstract: Using Density Functional Theory calculations, the molecular structure, molecular electrostatic potential surface analysis, boundary molecular orbital analysis, chemical reactivity, nonlinear optical properties, UV-Vis analysis, FTIR and Raman spectra of flupyradifurone were comprehensively investigated. The experimentally obtained UV-Vis, FTIR, and Raman spectra were compared with theoretical results. The interaction mechanisms of flupyradifurone with human DNA and p53 protein were theoretically investigated. Risk predictions regarding human health were also made using ADMET calculations. Adsorption experiments were conducted using natural materials such as walnut, peanut, and cherry seed shells to minimize the potential environmental impacts of flupyradifurone. Changes in FTIR and Raman spectra were observed in the ranges of 3000–2800 cm⁻¹ and 1600–1400 cm⁻¹ in untreated and flupyradifurone-treated insecticide-containing samples. The SEM images showed that flupyradifurone accumulated around the pore regions of the treated samples. According to the EDS results, N, F, and Cl atoms were identified as weight percentages after the treatment with flupyradifurone. In the adsorption spectra, the vibrational bands of these elements were most clearly observed around 1600 cm⁻¹. Molecular docking studies indicated that flupyradifurone can interact with human DNA and p53 protein. ADMET predictions gave probabilities of 0.77 for drug-induced liver injury and 0.24 for carcinogenicity, and the docking runs gave best binding affinities of -5.6 kcal mol⁻¹ for DNA and − 6.8 kcal mol⁻¹ for p53. FTIR, Raman, SEM, and EDS findings showed that walnut, peanut, and cherry seed shells could adsorb flupyradifurone.

Article.Title: Assessment of the technical, economic, and carbon reduction potential of recycled concrete aggregate for sustainable roads in Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Alharbi F.; Almoshaogeh M.; Jamal A.; Alhuthayl J.; Almijmaj M.; Shafiquzzaman M.
Article.Abstract: Construction and demolition (C&D) waste has been creating significant environmental and economic challenges associated with landfill disposal and depletion of natural resources. In Saudi Arabia, the growing volume of C&D waste highlights the need for sustainable recycling strategies that support the objectives of Vision 2030 and circular economy principles. This study evaluated the feasibility of utilizing recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) as a substitute for natural aggregate in both hot-mix asphalt (HMA) and base layer applications for road construction. RCA was obtained from a landfill in Buraidah, Saudi Arabia, processed, and evaluated through aggregate suitability tests, Marshall mix design, Proctor compaction, and California Bearing Ratio (CBR) testing. Economic performance was assessed using construction and life-cycle cost calculations, while construction-stage CO₂ emissions were estimated using a scenario-based carbon-screening approach. A multi-criteria ranking framework integrating engineering, economic, and carbon-performance indicators was also applied to compare RCA alternatives. The RCA satisfied the specified aggregate requirements, although its water absorption (7.83%) and abrasion loss (40.55%) were higher than those of the natural aggregate. In HMA mixtures, RCA contents up to 20% showed comparatively favorable volumetric and mechanical performance within the tested binder range, whereas mixtures containing 30–50% RCA exhibited elevated air voids and reduced VFA, indicating the need for further binder optimization. For base layers, increasing RCA content reduced maximum dry density from 2.29 to 1.73 g/cm³ and increased CBR from 96.8% for the control to 172.5% at 100% RCA, while swell decreased from 0.45 to 0.004%. Economic analysis indicated net savings of 2.35–9.73% for HMA mixtures, with the highest savings at 10% RCA, while base-layer costs decreased by up to 25.1% at 100% RCA. The estimated construction-stage CO₂ reduction increased from 4.67% to 23.37% for HMA and from 23.07 to 79.02% for base layers with increasing RCA content. Under the adopted equal-weight multi-criteria framework, 10% RCA provided the most favorable HMA option considering technical feasibility and overall performance, whereas 100% RCA ranked highest for the base layer. Overall, the findings indicate that RCA has substantial potential for sustainable pavement construction in Saudi Arabia, particularly in base-layer applications, while higher RCA contents in HMA require further optimization and durability validation.

Article.Title: Pro-vaccination communication requires tailoring: Evidence from an experimental and longitudinal comparison of communication strategies on vaccination-related cognition and intentions
Article.Authors: Damnjanović K.; Ilić S.; Kušić M.; Mišić K.; Ninković M.; Paunovic D.; B. Petrović M.
Article.Abstract: Effective vaccination communication requires evidence-based strategies, yet direct comparisons are scarce. In a longitudinal experiment (N = 901, four time points), participants were exposed to six pro-vaccination communicative texts, all centered on the concept of herd immunity to maintain consistency in information content while varying the communication style — nudge, boost, psychological inoculation (PI), patient-concerns-centred communication (PCCC), dismissive informational load (DIL), and neutral informational load (NIL) — compared against a control. We assessed the immediate and sustained, i.e., after a period of 7 and 14 days, impact on vaccination intention (personal and proxy), information-seeking habits, and vaccine-related biased reasoning. No single communication strategy was universally superior; effectiveness depended on the decision context and pre-existing attitudes. PCCC most effectively increased immediate personal vaccination intention. Pre-existing attitudes and beliefs were strong moderators of the effect (e.g., PI and NIL were more effective for individuals reporting higher levels of vaccine conspiracy beliefs when making proxy decisions). Critically, our findings reveal what these brief interventions can and cannot achieve: while initial gains in intention from PCCC remained stable, the impact on information-seeking habits was modest, and these brief-exposure interventions were insufficient to alter ingrained cognitive processes, such as vaccine-related biased reasoning. While brief communication can shift immediate intentions, changing how people think requires more sustained efforts. We argue that communication must be tailored to the audience and decision type, emphasizing the importance of considering patient concerns and suggesting abandoning the DIL approach given its tone and ineffectiveness.

Article.Title: Vision impairment, depressive symptoms, and risk of incident coronary events: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Ling J.; Sun G.; Yu F.; Zhu J.
Article.Abstract: Vision impairment (VI) is a common yet underrecognized age-related condition, but its association with coronary heart disease (CHD) risk remains unclear. Using data from 6,906 adults aged ≥ 50 years in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (2004–2023), we examined the associations of baseline self-reported vision status and vision transitions between Waves 2 and 3 with incident CHD and explored whether depressive symptoms statistically accounted for part of these associations. During a median follow-up of 12 years, 502 incident CHD cases were identified. Participants with baseline VI had a 40% higher risk of CHD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.40; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.08–1.80), and those whose vision deteriorated had a 55% higher subsequent risk (HR 1.55; 95% CI 1.12–2.15). Each one-point higher mean vision score was linked to a 21% lower CHD risk (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.69–0.90). Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that depressive symptoms statistically accounted for a modest proportion of the baseline VI–CHD association. Poorer self-reported vision and deterioration were associated with a higher subsequent risk of CHD. Depressive symptoms statistically accounted for a modest proportion of the baseline association, suggesting that perceived visual decline may mark broader cardiovascular vulnerability in later life.

Article.Title: Relationship between autistic traits, emotional symptoms and adverse life events in Chinese adolescents: mediating effects of resilience
Article.Authors: Zeng L.; Liu Y.; Wang H.; Cao Q.; Ji Z.; Gong X.; Su X.; Zhao L.; Yin T.; Liu Q.; Sun B.; Han G.; Liu Y.; Jin Y.; Tang X.; Li X.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: Few studies have explored links between autistic traits and multifaceted adverse outcomes with culturally specific mediators. This study aimed to examine associations of autistic traits with emotional symptoms and adverse life events, and analyze the mediating effect of resilience in Chinese adolescents. A total of 5666 Chinese adolescents were enrolled to assess autistic traits using the Autism Spectrum Screening Questionnaire, emotional symptoms using the Child Depression Inventory and the Screen for Child Anxiety Related Emotional Disorders, adverse life events using the Adolescent Self-Rating Life Events Checklist, and resilience using the Resilience Scale for Chinese Adolescent. Spearman correlations and multiple linear regression analyses were conducted to examine the associations between autistic traits and both two types of outcomes. The Bootstrap percentile confidence interval method was adopted to analyze the mediating effect of resilience. Autistic traits were correlated with emotional symptoms and adverse life events, among which the social interaction showed the strongest correlations. Relationship pressure and being punished were the adverse life events with the largest effect sizes. Resilience significantly mediated the associations of autistic traits with both emotional symptoms and adverse life events. Specifically, individual power exerted a stronger effect on the link with emotional symptoms, whereas supportive power had a stronger effect on the link with adverse life events. The association between autistic traits and mental health among Chinese adolescents is multidimensional. Culturally distinctive resilience with dual layers should be incorporated into targeted intervention design.

Article.Title: High-speed FPGA implementation of the CORDIC algorithm using carry lookahead adders
Article.Authors: Kanadal K.; Pradhan A.; S A.; Roy C.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents an efficient hardware architecture for sine and cosine generation using the CORDIC (Coordinate Rotation Digital Computer) algorithm. The design employs a pipelined scale-free CORDIC datapath integrated with a carry look-ahead adder (CLA) to reduce critical path delay and improve computational speed compared to conventional ripple-carry adder (RCA) implementations. To achieve an optimal balance between performance and hardware cost, hybrid CLA–RCA configurations are introduced, where CLAs are selectively used in timing-critical stages while RCAs are retained in non-critical paths. Furthermore, mutually exclusive micro-rotation techniques are utilized to reduce the number of iterations and eliminate the need for scale-factor compensation, thereby enhancing efficiency. The proposed architecture is implemented and synthesized on both FPGA and ASIC platforms to validate its performance and portability. FPGA implementation on Xilinx Artix-7 confirms accurate sine and cosine outputs with low power consumption of 0.175W, while a standard-cell ASIC realization on the open SkyWater 130 nm (Sky130) PDK using the Yosys–OpenROAD flow further demonstrates a core area of \(0.88 \textrm{mm}^{2}\) , an achievable clock frequency of \(32 \textrm{MHz}\) , and a total power of \(10.2 \textrm{mW}\) , confirming successful timing closure with zero violations across all sign-off corners.

Article.Title: Performance evaluation of recycled cement-stabilized gravel strengthened with multi-source solid-waste-based composite slurry and its mixtures
Article.Authors: Jia S.; Ding J.; Gao H.; Wen P.; Wang C.
Article.Abstract: To improve the mechanical performance of cold-recycled cement-stabilized gravel and address practical problems including poor mechanical properties and high dispersion of recycled cement-stabilized gravel (RCSG), a strengthening method for RCSG coated with multi-source solid-waste-based composite slurry was proposed. A multi-source solid waste-based composite slurry containing slag powder, steel slag powder and carbide slag was developed. The recommended paste-to-aggregate mass ratio and slurry concentration for RCSG strengthening were determined. The mixing proportion of slurry raw materials together with the strengthening procedure for RCSG were recommended. The effects of strengthening procedure and RCSG replacement content on the performance of cold-recycled cement-stabilized gravel mixtures were evaluated. The results show that the recommended mass ratio of ground granulated blast-furnace slag, steel slag powder, carbide slag, and sodium silicate was 60:40:4:1. A slurry concentration of 50%, a paste-to-aggregate mass ratio of 1:8, and mechanical mixing for 5 min were recommended as the strengthening parameters based on the experimental results. After treatment with this procedure, the 7 d and 28 d interfacial bonding strengths of fine RCSG reached 0.71 and 0.96 MPa, respectively, with the 7 d interfacial bonding strength increased by 77.5% compared with the untreated group. The crushing and abrasion values of coarse RCSG decreased to 19.09% and 8.98%. At a 30% replacement rate, the 7 d and 28 d unconfined compressive strengths of the strengthened cold-recycled cement-stabilized gravel mixtures increased by 104.4% and 103.8%, respectively. The proposed multi-source solid-waste-based composite slurry effectively improved the mechanical performance of RCSG and cold-recycled cement-stabilized gravel mixtures. This study provides experimental support for the strengthening and reuse of RCSG in pavement base applications.
