Article.Title: A flow simulation method based on digital rock analysis in multi-layer heterogeneous reservoir
Article.Authors: Wang C.; Wang Y.; He H.; Han D.; Hu R.
Article.Abstract: Conventional multi-tube parallel-flooding experiments and single-/double-layer pore network models are insufficient to characterize interlayer interference and microscopic residual oil distribution in thin interbedded heterogeneous reservoirs. This study constructs a triple permeability combined pore network framework from micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) digital rocks. Three digital rock models for high, medium and low permeability fluvial sandstone rhythmic layers are obtained via micro CT scanning and Otsu threshold segmentation, each satisfying Representative Elementary Volume (REV) criteria at 1.2 mm × 0.8 mm × 0.8 mm. Vertically connected three layer digital rock assemblies are built for invasion percolation based quasi steady state two phase imbibition drainage simulation. With a permeability ratio of ~ 3 across layers, permeability is jointly controlled by pore throat size and coordination number, leading to non monotonic variation between mean pore radius and bulk permeability. Reduced permeability narrows the oil water co flow interval; intensified capillary trapping in fine throats dominates this effect, and weakened pore connectivity plays a secondary role. Imbibition exhibits staged flow behaviors: water first occupies large conduits in medium/high permeability layers at low water saturation, and later invades fine pores in low permeability layers, generating layered feature relative permeability curves. Preferential flow occurs in medium and high permeability zones, while irreducible water and residual oil mainly reside in low permeability strata. Under the given permeability contrast, it preliminarily reveals the pore scale control trends of permeability gradients on capillary characteristics and relative permeability evolution. It can provide a microscale simulation reference for waterflooding development of thin interbedded heterogeneous reservoirs. Note that this simulation adopts idealized pore network simplifications under one fixed permeability contrast and mixed wet condition.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving factors of green transformation in resource-based cities of Western China
Article.Authors: Teng Z.; Zhang H.; Cao X.
Article.Abstract: Western China’s resource-based cities (WRBCs) have characteristics of “resource dependence” and “development lag,” and all resource-based cities will face difficulty accomplishing green transformation (GT). This paper uses 39 samples of WRBCs from 2003 to 2021, identifying the sources of differentiation in GT in WRBCs through the Dagum Gini coefficient, Kernel density function, and spatial Durbin model. Furthermore, we analyze the driving factors and effects of GT. The results show that the overall GT of WRBCs assumes a fluctuating upward tendency. Interregional disparities are the primary source of differentiation in the GT of WRBCs, and absolute differences within the region are generally narrowing. The digital economy (DIG), agglomeration of productive service industries (SEV), urban industrial innovation (UINV), infrastructure level (IL), and GDP can promote GT. DIG and IL produce positive spillover effects promoting the adjacent region’s GT; however, economically developed regions, the siphoning effect occurs, which is adverse to the GT of the adjacent region. The results are still valid after a series of robustness tests. GT has a positive spatial spillover effect, with an effective spillover boundary of 400 km and a peak of 300 km. This study can support the quantitative for promoting GT and balancing regional inequality in resource-based cities.

Article.Title: Innovative magnetic anastomosis enables immediate liver transplantation without cold preservation
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Liu P.; Yu J.; Lu Q.; Qian Y.; Xiang J.; Shi A.; Wei S.; Lv Y.; Yang L.
Article.Abstract: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) traditionally relies on static cold preservation, which may contribute to ischemia–reperfusion injury associated with abrupt temperature transitions. This study investigated the feasibility of immediate liver transplantation without cold storage using rapid magnetic anastomosis. Eighty-eight adult male Sprague–Dawley rats were randomly divided into two groups: Cold Storage Transplantation Group (CSTG) and Immediate Transplantation Group (ITG). Partial liver transplantation was performed using magnetic anastomosis, with the ITG group undergoing direct transplantation without cold preservation. Thermal imaging, histological analysis, oxidative stress markers, cellular proliferation, apoptosis, liver function, and inflammatory responses were evaluated at 1 and 5-days post-transplantation. The ITG demonstrated several key advantages: more stable temperature profiles during transplantation, significantly reduced oxidative stress during the ex vivo phase, enhanced hepatocyte proliferation and decreased cellular apoptosis ( P < 0.05 at day 5). Liver function markers showed improved recovery in the ITG, with significantly lower alanine aminotransferase (ALT) on day 5 ( P < 0.05 at day 5). The 14-day survival rates were comparable between groups (80% ITG vs. 70% CSTG, P = 0.629). Immediate liver transplantation using magnetic anastomosis appears feasible and may offer potential biological benefits, providing a novel approach that avoids conventional cold storage and warrants further investigation as a strategy for limiting preservation-related ischemic stress. This method demonstrated promising outcomes in terms of graft temperature stability, cellular proliferation, and reduced apoptosis, together with a lower serum ALT level on day 5. However, the delayed elevation of IL-1β and IL-6 and the incompletely defined mechanisms warrant further investigation. Further research in large animal models is warranted to validate these findings and evaluate the safety and translational potential of this approach.

Article.Title: Multi-scenario probabilistic hazard assessment of flash flood disasters in Chengkou County based on a multi-state system model
Article.Authors: Xiaosong L.; Congxuan Z.; Meili W.; Yin P.; Xin X.
Article.Abstract: Flash flood disasters pose a serious threat to lives, property, and regional sustainable development in mountainous areas. Existing hazard assessment methods often rely on static indicator systems, which suffer from excessive subjectivity in weight assignment and difficulties in integrating dynamic triggering factors effectively. To address these limitations, this study introduces multi-state system theory and, using Chengkou County in Chongqing as a case study, constructs a multi-scenario probabilistic hazard assessment model that couples a disaster-forming environment subsystem (static background) with a rainfall-triggering subsystem (dynamic driver). The disaster-forming environment subsystem is characterized by a parallel structure to represent baseline susceptibility, while the triggering subsystem uses a series structure to simulate the activating effect of rainfall. Based on GIS and multi-source data, each system component is classified into four states—from Level I (high hazard) to Level IV (very low hazard)—and a multi-state system probability model is applied to quantitatively analyze the hazard levels of 25 townships under different rainfall scenarios. Results show that, without rainfall triggers, the disaster-forming environment in all townships remains at Level IV (very low hazard), indicating low baseline susceptibility. However, heavy rainfall significantly alters the spatial pattern of hazard. During the extreme rainfall event on May 28, 2023 (precipitation ≥ 180 mm), 18 townships were classified as high-hazard, and their spatial distribution showed strong consistency with recorded local disaster data. Because both the rainfall inputs and disaster records are derived exclusively from local sources within Chengkou County, this evaluation should be regarded as an internal/local consistency check rather than independent external validation; cross-regional transferability remains unproven. In contrast, lower-intensity rainfall events resulted in a marked reduction in hazard magnitude. By adopting a multi-state system model, this study reduces subjective weight assignment and quantifies flash flood hazard probabilistically across multiple rainfall scenarios, offering a new probabilistic paradigm for county-scale hazard assessment in mountainous regions. The model’s outputs represent relative hazard probabilities rather than deterministic flood predictions, and its thresholds require site-specific recalibration when applied to other regions.

Article.Title: Head-to-head comparison of [18F]FAPI and [18F]FDG PET/CT in the clinical value of hepatocellular carcinoma
Article.Authors: Zhang R.; Li L.; Liu W.; Ge X.; Chen M.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the clinical utility of fluorine-18-labeled fibroblast activation protein (FAP) inhibitor ([ 18 F]FAPI) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) relative to [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose ([ 18 F]FDG) PET/CT for tumor detection and staging in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. A cohort of 38 individuals (median age, 61 years; interquartile range, 56–68 years), all with pathologically confirmed primary or recurrent HCC, were enrolled. All participants underwent both [ 18 F]FDG and [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT. Maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), tumor-to-background ratio (TBR), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), FAP expression tumor volume (FTV), total lesion glycolysis (TLG), total lesion FAP expression (TLF), and clinical staging were compared. Each patient had at least one intrahepatic lesion confirmed by surgical resection or percutaneous biopsy. Histopathologic confirmation was available for 46/66 intrahepatic lesions, 3/56 lymph-node (LN) metastases, and 4/33 distant metastases; the remaining lesions were adjudicated using a composite reference standard based on multimodal imaging follow-up and treatment response. Additionally, correlations between PET imaging findings and serum biomarkers, comprising alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist II (PIVKA-II), were analyzed. The cohort included 32 primary and 6 recurrent HCC cases. [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher lesion detection rates than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT for primary intrahepatic lesions (96.7% vs. 60.0%; p < 0.001), LN metastases (94.6% vs. 80.4%; p = 0.021), and distant metastases (78.8% vs. 48.5%; p = 0.002). For primary intrahepatic lesions, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher SUVmax (7.90 vs. 4.80, p < 0.001) and TBR (5.45 vs. 2.60, p < 0.001) than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT. In the patient-level volumetric analysis of the 32 initial-staging patients, FTV was 21.04 vs. MTV 13.75 ( p < 0.001), and TLF was 135.36 vs. TLG 51.44 ( p < 0.001). For LN metastases, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher SUVmax (7.98 vs. 6.63, p = 0.048) and TBR (7.85 vs. 4.95, p < 0.001), as well as higher FTV than MTV (6.55 vs. 4.55, p < 0.001) and TLF than TLG (67.65 vs. 52.75, p < 0.001). Positive correlations were observed between [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT tumor uptake parameters and AFP and PIVKA-II levels (nominal p < 0.05). Relative to [ 18 F]FDG, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT produced staging changes in 19/32 patients undergoing initial staging, including 6 true upstagings, and identified 3 additional local recurrences; a FAPI-informed management change was implemented in 57.9% (22/38) of patients. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.947, 0.921, 0.895, and 0.864 for SUVmax, TBR, FTV, and TLF, respectively. [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher lesion detection in selected HCC settings than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT for primary intrahepatic, lymph-node, and distant metastatic lesions and may provide complementary information for staging and treatment planning in this preliminary single-center cohort. Article.Title: Every drop counts: optimizing water use efficiency for sustainable tomato production
Article.Authors: Villa e Vila V.; Bedum G.; Gelain M.; da Mata Melo Junior A.; Gomes T.; da Silva R.; Marques P.
Article.Abstract: Ensuring food production in the face of increasing water scarcity is one of the main challenges for sustainable agriculture worldwide. As climate change intensifies and water availability becomes increasingly limited, the adoption of strategies that enhance water use efficiency in agriculture is imperative. The objective of this study was to evaluate whether the combination of deficit irrigation and biostimulant application can maintain tomato yield while improving water and energy use efficiency, thereby contributing to more sustainable horticultural production systems. The study evaluated five irrigation replacement levels, 40, 60, 80, 100, and 120% of crop evapotranspiration (ETc) with or without the application of a biostimulant derived from Ascophyllum nodosum extract (ANE), under protected cultivation over two production cycles. As tomato plants were subjected to increasing levels of water deficit, the negative impacts on crop performance became more pronounced. However, when comparing the same irrigation replacement levels, the ANE applications proved beneficial by mitigating the water stress effects on the crop. The study demonstrated that moderate deficit irrigation (80% ETc) combined with ANE promoted stability across both production cycles, sustaining yields comparable to full irrigation (100% ETc without ANE) while reducing water use by 20%. Plants under 80% + ANE enhanced photosynthetic rates by up to 5.7–7.8% and kept leaf relative water content and temperature close to unstressed plants. This strategy also achieved favorable energy productivity, ranging from 0.70 to 0.72 kg MJ − 1 . Conversely, overirrigation (120% ETc) added an unnecessary energy cost of 0.6 MJ plant − 1 and decreased water use efficiency by up to 15.7–16.9%, triggering a diminishing returns effect. The integrated management strategy of applying 80% ETc + ANE proved to be an environmentally responsible solution for water saving in horticulture, contributing to more resource-efficient food systems through improved water management in tomato production.

Article.Title: IGFBP5 knockdown is associated with improved early neurovascular regeneration after sciatic nerve injury
Article.Authors: Ock J.; Kim W.; Huang Y.; Fridayana F.; Lee S.; Yin G.; Ryu J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Peripheral nerve injury (PNI) disrupts neurovascular integrity and leads to persistent sensory and motor dysfunction. Insulin-like growth factor binding protein 5 (IGFBP5) regulates insulin-like growth factor bioavailability and has also been implicated in apoptosis, fibrosis, and extracellular matrix remodeling; however, its role in peripheral nerve regeneration remains unclear. This study investigated the temporal expression pattern of IGFBP5 following sciatic nerve injury (SNI) and examined whether its suppression is associated with early neurovascular regenerative responses. A murine SNI model was established, and IGFBP5 was silenced using perineural delivery of lentiviral short hairpin RNA. Neurovascular remodeling, cellular responses, and stress-related changes were evaluated at 5 days post-injury, and functional recovery was assessed longitudinally up to 12 weeks. We observed that IGFBP5 expression was markedly increased in both proximal and distal nerve segments after injury. IGFBP5 knockdown was associated with increased endothelial and axonal marker signals, accompanied by enhanced Schwann cell– and macrophage-associated responses and reduced myelin-associated signals. In parallel, reduced oxidative and nitrosative stress and decreased apoptotic markers were detected, together with increased proliferative activity during the early phase of regeneration. In addition, IGFBP5 suppression was associated with increased phosphorylation of PI3K–AKT and ERK signaling pathways. Functional assessments indicated improved motor recovery and higher sciatic functional index scores compared with controls. Together, these findings suggest that IGFBP5 knockdown is associated with a more favorable early neurovascular microenvironment following peripheral nerve injury. Targeting IGFBP5 may represent a potential strategy to modulate early regenerative processes, although further studies are required to define its mechanistic role and long-term effects.

Article.Title: Citizenship reduces welfare chauvinism - evidence across unemployment benefits, social assistance, and sanctions
Article.Authors: Brinkmann M.; Hamdorf S.; Naumann E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We examine whether welfarechauvinistic attitudes, the preference for restricting immigrants’ access to welfare benefits, differ by benefit type and whether citizenship attenuates migrant penalties in welfare deservingness. Using a between-subjects multifactorial survey experiment embedded in a probability-based online panel (March 2019; N = 4,890), we asked respondents to evaluate an unemployed benefit claimant on three outcomes: support for earnings-related unemployment benefits, needs-based social assistance, and benefit sanctions. Across outcomes, migrant profiles are judged less deserving than otherwise identical ethnic German profiles. Penalties are of similar magnitude for unemployment insurance and social assistance while sanction differentials are smaller and limited to some, more culturally distant groups. Citizenship, as an institutional signal of integration, attenuates penalties within shared ethnic origin but does not fully close the gap to ethnic Germans, even under favorable deservingness cues.

Article.Title: Genome-wide characterization of endogenous retroviral envelope genes across primate lineages reveals evolutionary diversity and recombination
Article.Authors: Chabukswar S.; Grandi N.; Soddu E.; Lin L.; Tramontano E.
Article.Abstract: Endogenous Retroviruses (ERVs) are remnants of ancient germline infections by now extinct exogenous retroviruses and constitute a substantial fraction of vertebrate genomes, serving as “fossil” records for the ancestral retroviral diversity and evolution. Among ERV genes, the characterization of env gene is particularly informative to understand ERVs’ evolutionary trajectory and infer their potential physiological/pathological role. However, detailed characterization has been performed for few domesticated env genes, while a comprehensive survey of their abundance and diversity among primates’ genomes is still lacking. Here, we reconstructed 32 representative Env consensus sequences from Class I, II, and III human ERVs and used them to screen 55 primate species across the Catarrhini and Platyrrhini parvorders. Similarity-based search, phylogenetic analysis, and recombination events detection revealed ERV diversification and broad distribution. Notably, we identified and extensively characterized in detail the presence of the HERV-K supergroup in the Platyrrhini parvorder, indicating initiation of its spread > 40 million years ago. Furthermore, we confirmed inter- and intra-class env recombination events, frequently involving LTR insertions within env coding regions, confirming the phenomenon of “ env snatching” among primates’ ERVs and domain disruption. Overall, our findings highlight the value of Env reconstruction for investigating ERV evolution and expands our current understanding of retroviral diversification, recombination dynamics, and primate genome evolution.

Article.Title: Echocardiographic findings in children with malaria: a systematic review and narrative synthesis
Article.Authors: Chinawa J.; Okafor H.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular involvement has been described in children with severe malaria, but reported echocardiographic findings are heterogeneous. Some studies demonstrate transient haemodynamic abnormalities or pulmonary pressure elevation, whereas others report preserved ventricular function. We therefore updated and reframed the evidence base to describe the spectrum of echocardiographic findings rather than assume that cardiac dysfunction is universal. To synthesize and critically describe the echocardiographic findings reported in children with malaria, characterize the spectrum of cardiac structural, functional and haemodynamic abnormalities, explore factors that may explain differences between studies, and identify important methodological gaps in the existing evidence. This systematic review was structured according to PRISMA 2020. Eight predefined eligibility criteria required studies to include children/adolescents aged ≤ 18 years with laboratory-confirmed malaria; evaluate cardiac function using transthoracic echocardiography; report at least one echocardiographic structural or functional measure; use an eligible observational or interventional design; be a full-text peer-reviewed article; be published in English; provide separately extractable paediatric data where adults were also enrolled; and satisfy the prespecified publication/design exclusions. The original search covered the six prespecified databases from inception to 30 April 2025; the archived export preserved yields for five databases, while the historical AJOL yield was not preserved. A new post-search evidence update was undertaken through systematic screening of the supplied 174-reference bibliography, backward and forward citation checking, and current bibliographic surveillance through 10 September 2026. Seven eligible observational studies involving 550 children with malaria were included. Studies were conducted in Kenya, Mali, Mozambique, Uganda, Ghana and Nigeria. Findings were heterogeneous. Yacoub et al. reported mild admission abnormalities that improved during follow-up. Janka et al. reported increased pulmonary arterial pressures and myocardial wall stress. Mocumbi et al. and Murphy et al. reported largely preserved ventricular function. Nguah et al. and Kotlyar et al. demonstrated high-output physiology associated with anaemia rather than generalized systolic failure. The 2026 Nigerian study reported higher tricuspid regurgitant velocity, lower mean LVEF and higher frequencies of abnormal TAPSE, MRV and MAPSE compared with controls. No quantitative pooling was performed because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Echocardiographic abnormalities can occur during paediatric malaria, but the available evidence does not support a single universal phenotype of cardiac dysfunction. Findings range from preserved ventricular function to transient haemodynamic disturbance, pulmonary pressure elevation and selected right- or left-sided functional abnormalities. Severe anaemia and acute haemodynamic state appear important modifiers.

Article.Title: Evaluation of the relationship between insomnia and inflammatory markers in geriatric individuals: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Beler M.; Özdeş A.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association between insomnia severity and systemic inflammatory indices, specifically neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), in geriatric individuals aged 80 years and older, a subgroup for whom evidence on this relationship remains scarce. This cross-sectional study included 384 patients aged ≥ 80 years attending a geriatric outpatient clinic. Insomnia severity was assessed using the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). Inflammatory markers, namely the NLR, PLR, and SII were derived from routine hematological parameters and analyzed via correlation analyses and multivariable linear regression. Insomnia was identified in 38.5% of participants. ISI scores showed significant positive correlations with NLR, PLR, SII, chronic disease burden, and medication count (all p < 0.001). Inflammatory marker levels were significantly elevated in those with insomnia ( p < 0.001). After full covariate adjustment, SII (β = 0.07, p < 0.001) and NLR (β = 0.666, p = 0.004) remained independent predictors of insomnia severity, whereas PLR lost significance. Insomnia is highly prevalent in the oldest-old and independently associated with systemic inflammatory burden. SII and NLR, as accessible and non-invasive parameters, may serve as pragmatic biomarkers for stratifying insomnia severity in geriatric practice. Longitudinal studies are warranted to establish causality and evaluate anti-inflammatory interventions.

Article.Title: Rockburst risk assessment based on multi-parameter critical indicators: CW-TOPSIS approach
Article.Authors: Wu Z.; Tang Z.; Huang A.; Wang A.; Zuo W.
Article.Abstract: Rockburst occurrence is governed by multiple interacting factors. To improve rockburst risk assessment in coal mines, five key parameters—critical softening radius, critical load, critical convergence displacement, critical energy, and critical mining depth—were selected as critical indicators, and a CW-TOPSIS-based method for rockburst risk assessment using multi-parameter critical indicators was proposed. A three-tier evaluation framework comprising the target, primary-indicator, and secondary-indicator layers was established through theoretical analysis. The analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and entropy weight method (EWM) were used to determine the subjective and objective weights of the indicators, respectively. These weights were integrated using a Euclidean distance optimization method to obtain the combined weights, which were subsequently used to construct a weighted decision matrix. The combined-weight Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (CW-TOPSIS) model was then employed to calculate the relative closeness coefficients and construct a rockburst risk assessment space for risk-level classification. The proposed method was applied to the 4207 working face of a coal mine. The results classified the working face as having a low rockburst risk, consistent with the result obtained using the comprehensive index method. Compared with the comprehensive index method, the proposed method provides a more quantitative representation of rockburst risk in terms of both numerical evaluation and risk-level classification. This study provides a quantitative approach for rockburst risk assessment in coal mines.

Article.Title: Sex differences dominate urinary extracellular DNA concentrations and variability in humans and rodents
Article.Authors: Potočárová A.; Janovičová Ľ.; Feješ A.; Šebeková K.; Celec P.; Tóthová Ľ.; Tamášová B.
Article.Abstract: Urinary extracellular DNA has emerged as a promising non-invasive biomarker for kidney and urinary tract diseases. However, its physiological concentration, variability, and potential sex-dependent differences in healthy individuals are poorly defined. This lack of baseline knowledge limits the clinical and translational use of urinary extracellular DNA. Morning urine samples were collected from 66 healthy adults (33 women and 33 men), as well as from female and male mice and rats. Extracellular DNA was isolated from urine supernatant and quantified fluorometrically. Nuclear and mitochondrial DNA were measured using quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Urinary creatinine, osmolality, and deoxyribonuclease activity were assessed to evaluate potential confounding factors. Fragment size distribution was analysed using capillary electrophoresis. Sex differences were analysed using unpaired statistical tests, variability was assessed by comparing variances and coefficients of variation, and correlations were evaluated using Pearson analysis. Women exhibited approximately 5-fold higher concentrations of urinary extracellular DNA than men and showed markedly greater inter-individual variability. These differences persisted after normalization to creatinine and osmolality and were significant for nuclear DNA but not mitochondrial DNA. Female mice and rats also demonstrated higher extracellular DNA concentrations than males, with approximately 2-fold higher levels in mice and 11-fold higher levels in rats. No association was found between extracellular DNA concentration and urine concentration parameters, menstrual cycle phase, or urinary deoxyribonuclease activity. Most urinary extracellular DNA consisted of nucleosome-sized fragments. Biological sex is a major determinant of urinary extracellular DNA concentration and variability in humans and rodents. The high physiological variability, particularly in females, limits the use of absolute urinary extracellular DNA levels as a standalone biomarker. These findings underscore the necessity of incorporating sex-specific considerations into the design, analysis, and interpretation of urinary extracellular DNA studies.

Article.Title: QCSA: LLM-driven progressive quadruple construction and prompt-augmented learning for robust citation sentiment analysis
Article.Authors: You X.; Zhang Q.; Lu L.; Zhang K.
Article.Abstract: Citation sentiment analysis (CSA) faces several challenges, including implicit sentiment expression, class imbalance, and the unstable availability of fine-grained structured evidence. Existing methods use structured quadruples to make evaluative information in citation contexts more explicit. However, LLM-generated outputs may still suffer from invalid structures, limited textual alignment, and varying semantic quality, especially for neutral citations with weak evaluative signals. To address these issues, we propose QCSA, an LLM-driven framework for progressive quadruple construction and prompt-augmented learning. For neutral citations with weak structured evidence, QCSA adopts a conditional three-stage construction strategy. It prioritizes valid semantic evidence while improving the completeness of structured prompt inputs. For classification, QCSA uses a shared semantic anchor-guided gated residual fusion mechanism to jointly model the original citation context and quadruple prompts. A weighted multi-backbone ensemble is further used as an optional enhancement to explore complementary information across pretrained language models. Experimental results show that QCSA achieves a Macro-F1 of 87.81% on the Athar dataset, while QCSA-Single (RoBERTa) reaches 96.49% on CSCE. These results indicate competitive performance on both benchmark datasets. Ablation and multi-seed experiments further show that the progressive quadruple construction provides a relatively stable contribution, while gated residual fusion offers a limited supplementary gain.

Article.Title: Ultrasound-assisted deep eutectic solvent extraction of total flavonoids from Houttuynia cordata Thunb. and their in vitro activity
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Liu M.; Meng L.
Article.Abstract: This study optimized ultrasound-assisted deep eutectic solvent (DES) extraction of total flavonoids from Houttuynia cordata Thunb. and evaluated their in vitro antioxidant and antibacterial activities. Among eight screened DESs, choline chloride–lactic acid (1:1, 30% water) was selected as the optimal solvent. Using single-factor experiments and Box–Behnken response surface methodology (R 2 = 0.9942), the optimal extraction conditions were determined as a solid–liquid ratio of 1:30 g/mL, ultrasonic power of 360 W, temperature of 40 °C, and time of 50 min, yielding a maximum extraction yield of 4.67%. The extract exhibited concentration-dependent scavenging activity against DPPH, hydroxyl, ABTS⁺, superoxide anion, and nitrite radicals. Furthermore, it demonstrated potent antibacterial effects against Staphylococcus aureus subsp. aureus (MIC = 0.0187 g/mL, inhibition zone = 21.76 mm) and Escherichia coli (MIC = 0.0375 g/mL, inhibition zone = 18.03 mm). These findings confirm that the optimized DES-based extraction process is efficient and that the H. cordata flavonoid extract possesses significant antioxidant and antibacterial potential.

Article.Title: A semi-empirical correlation for critical wind velocity in inclined mine roadways
Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Song A.; Ge J.; Wang W.; Liu Y.; Yang D.
Article.Abstract: In inclined roadways, the longitudinal wind speed required to suppress smoke back-layering varies with inclination. This study examines that variation using FDS critical-velocity results at 0°, 3°, 6° and 9°, together with reduced-scale experiments at 11 angles. The FDS threshold increased from 0.69 m/s at 0° to 1.83 m/s at 6°, then decreased to 0.81 m/s at 9°. Experimental airflow settings were placed around Froude-scaled numerical targets to obtain approximate brackets for smoke suppression, indicating a peak near 4°–6°. The enhancement–attenuation correlation gave an in-sample R 2 of 0.987 for the four FDS values, although its predictions exceeded the experimental brackets at several angles. In 4000 refits using independent uniform draws from the brackets at the ten angles within 0°–9°, the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the fitted peak angle were 4.9° and 5.2°. In the configuration studied, critical velocity first increased and then decreased with inclination, with higher required wind speeds near 4°–6°.

Article.Title: P2226 alleviates respiratory inflammation and depression related behaviors with modulation of cytokines and gut microbiota in mice
Article.Authors: Park H.; Jang H.; Ma X.; Kim D.
Article.Abstract: Many patients with allergic rhinitis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) suffer from depression. Gut dysbiosis has been implicated in respiratory inflammation through the gut–lung axis. Based on these findings, we investigated whether P2226, a mixture of Lactococcus lactis P22 and Bifidobacterium longum P26, could alleviate ovalbumin-induced allergic rhinitis, pancreatic elastase-induced COPD-related symptoms, and combined ovalbumin/pancreatic elastase-induced respiratory inflammation, together with associated depressive-related behavioral changes in mice. Oral administration of P2226 significantly improved allergic rhinitis- and COPD-related symptoms and depressive-related behavioral changes, reduced TNF-α, IL-4, IL-17, and total IgE levels, restored IL-10 and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression, suppressed NF-κB-positive cell populations, and increased BDNF-positive neurons. P2226 also partially attenuated gut dysbiosis by decreasing the relative abundance of Rikenellaceae and Odoribacteraceae. Furthermore, fecal microbiota transplantation from combined ovalbumin/pancreatic elastase-exposed mice induced respiratory inflammatory symptoms, which were alleviated by P2226. In vitro, P2226 suppressed TNF-α expression in macrophages and the differentiation of splenic T cells into Th1, Th2, and Th17 cells while promoting IL-10 expression and Treg cell differentiation. Collectively, these findings suggest that P2226 alleviates allergic rhinitis-like inflammation, COPD-like lung injury, and their associated depression-like behaviors, accompanied by modulation of cytokines and gut microbiota.

Article.Title: Resolved-sideband micromotion sensing in trapped $$^{171}$$Yb$$^+$$ ions using Lindblad/Rate equation
Article.Authors: Salami N.; Aslaninejad M.; Solaymani S.; Sabbaghzadeh J.
Article.Abstract: We have investigated excess micromotion for a Yb \(^+\) ion in a Paul trap. In the presence of light modulated by excess micromotion, we calculate the cooling florescence spectrum of the 369.53 nm transition by finding the steady periodic state solution of the Lindblad master equation including the time-dependent Hamiltonian. We have shown that applying a 369.53 nm laser for specific RF parameters does not resolve efficiently micromotion sidebands. To sense well-resolved sidebands micromotion, we solve the Lindblad equation for the four-level optical transitions of the cooling cycle by incorporating the introduced time-dependent Hamiltonian and the branching ratio for spontaneous decay rates at the low intensity limit. However, in the weak-driving regime the rate equation under adiabatic approximation is implemented to detect the excess micromotion effects on the cooling florescence as a function of the repump detuning. This steady state florescence rate of P-state based on the rate equation approach leads to results in agreement with the Lindblad master equation, but with much less computational effort and no numerical issues. We show that by scanning the detuning of the repump laser, the cooling spectrum could be applied as an efficient micromotion sensor at \(\Omega _\mathrm{{c/r}}=0.1 \Gamma _\mathrm{{P/B}}\) . Our comprehensive discussion provides a theoretical and practical framework to predict the accurate experimental observations of sideband micromtion sensing in the trapped Yb \(^+\) ion which can be used and also extended.

Article.Title: lncRNA SNHG29-RPS-CYLD axis is mitochondrially localized and mediates apoptosis in rituximab-resistant DLBCL
Article.Authors: Xu X.; Wang X.; He H.; Zhong Q.; Zheng X.; Rong C.; Yang L.; Ding W.; Tang Z.; Lei Y.
Article.Abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), and some cases are resistant to first-line rituximab (RTX) treatment, leading to poor prognosis. Our previous research found that phosphorylated cylindromatosis (CYLD) is a target regulating apoptosis in RTX-resistant DLBCL. Given the emerging role of lncRNA in apoptosis regulation, and the fact that CYLD-related lncRNA reversing drug resistance in various solid malignancies, this study aims to explore whether lncRNA can regulate phosphorylated CYLD to promote apoptosis in RTX-resistant DLBCL and the molecular mechanisms. RTX-resistant DLBCL models were generated via dose escalation. Mitochondrial dysfunction was assessed by ROS flux. Integrated multi-omics analyses combining RNA sequencing (Ribonucleic acid sequencing, STAR v2.7.10a, https://www.encodeproject.org/data-standards/rna-seq/long-rnas/ ) with computational and biochemical approaches identified CYLD as an apoptotic hub and SNHG29 as a resistance mediator. Mechanistic studies employed mitochondrial subfractionation, Co-IP, and lentiviral perturbation. Preclinical validation used xenograft mice models and clinical specimens, supported by assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with high throughput ATAC-Seq (Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin using Sequencing, Bowtie2 v2.2.9, https://www.encodeproject.org/experiments/ENCSR637XSC/ ), ChIP-qPCR, and Bayesian network modeling. Through this research, we identified that high expression of phosphorylated CYLD is involved in the tumorigenesis and progression of DLBCL and serves as the core regulatory mechanism for DLBCL resistance to RTX. SNHG29 is an lncRNA associated with DLBCL resistance to RTX treatment. SNHG29 collaborates with CYLD through ribosomal proteins (RPS), and down-regulation of SNHG29 can down-regulate phosphorylated CYLD on the mitochondria, promoting apoptosis in RTX-resistant DLBCL. Nuclear transcription factor κB (NF-κB) is involved in this SNHG29 -RPS-CYLD axis regulation mechanism. This study reveals the molecular mechanism by which the SNHG29 -RPS-CYLD axis regulates apoptosis in rituximab-resistant (RTX-resistant) DLBCL at the mitochondria, thereby providing a novel target for drug development.

Article.Title: Pragmatic intention detection in Amharic using transformer-based model
Article.Authors: Asmare L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding what a speaker intends to communicate is an important challenge in natural language processing, particularly when the intended meaning goes beyond the literal words of an utterance. Despite recent progress in multilingual language technologies, Amharic remains relatively underrepresented in research on pragmatic intention detection. This study investigates pragmatic intention detection in Amharic by developing a balanced, nine-class dataset and evaluating several machine learning and neural language models. The dataset contains 11,475 Amharic sentences covering Assertion, Complaint, Phatic, Promise, Refusal, Request, Sarcasm/Irony, Suggestion, and Warning, with 7,955 sentences used for training, 1,857 for validation, and 1,663 for testing. Three independent annotators labeled the dataset, achieving 99.90% agreement and a Fleiss' kappa of 0.9993, indicating very high annotation reliability. We compare TF-IDF with Support Vector Machine, BiLSTM, mBERT, XLM-R, and AfroXLM-R. Among these models, AfroXLM-R achieved the strongest performance on the held-out test set, with 79.98% accuracy and a macro-F1 score of 76.93%. Its performance was also significantly better than that of XLM-R according to McNemar’s exact test ( p < 0.001). These findings demonstrate the potential of multilingual transformer models for identifying pragmatic intentions in Amharic and provide a reproducible benchmark for further research. The study contributes an annotated resource and empirical baseline for advancing Amharic pragmatic natural language processing and developing more inclusive language technologies.

Article.Title: Magnetite-based SPME-SQT-FAAS for trace chromium determination in rice
Article.Authors: Uzan S.; Aydin F.; Aslan M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rice, an essential carbohydrate and nutrient source grown in aquatic environments, is a staple food globally. Due to the high toxicity of chromium (Cr), monitoring its trace levels in agricultural products is critical for human health. In this study, Total Cr concentrations were determined in two distinct rice varieties: Karacadağ rice (Turkey) and Baldo rice (Italy). A novel Magnetic Solid-Phase Extraction (MSPE) protocol using oleic acid-coated magnetic nanoparticles (OAMNPs) was developed and coupled with slotted quartz tube flame atomic absorption spectrometry (SQT-FAAS) for trace chromium quantification. Following systematic optimization of key operational parameters such as sample pH, eluent and buffer volumes, and magnetic nanoparticle (MNP) dosage, the method yielded a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.30 µg/L, a limit of quantification (LOQ) of 4.33 µg/L, and a linear range of 5–100 µg/L (R 2 = 0.9989), delivering a remarkable enhancement factor of 104.78. High precision was confirmed with a relative standard deviation (RSD) of 5.78%. The method demonstrated excellent accuracy and robustness, supported by recovery values ranging between 93 and 105% in the presence of common interfering ions. These quantitative outcomes underscore that the developed analytical platform is highly sensitive, precise, and efficient for monitoring trace chromium in complex food matrices. Methodological accuracy and robustness were successfully validated through recovery assays. These outcomes underscore that the proposed OAMNP- MSPE-SQT-FAAS framework represents a highly sensitive, precise, and efficient analytical platform for detecting trace chromium within complex matrices.

Article.Title: An explainable hybrid CNN-transformer framework for multi-representation leukaemia classification
Article.Authors: Nikhare Y.; Badhiye S.
Article.Abstract: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia (ALL) is a severe form of hematologic cancer that requires precise and prompt diagnosis for improved survival rates of patients. The conventional technique of examining microscopic images of peripheral blood smears is quite subjective, laborious, and heavily reliant on expert opinion. However, recent developments in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), specifically deep learning, have made automated detection of leukaemia possible; but the available techniques are biased due to training datasets, lack generalizability and are poorly interpretable. This paper presents a novel Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Multi-Class Classification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia using EfficientNet and ViT Models. The framework uses convolutional networks for feature extraction, transformer networks for global representation learning, and handcrafted features. We evaluate the method on two clinical datasets: ALL-IDB2 and the ALL Image Dataset from Kaggle, both of which include benign and malignant types (Benign, Early, Pre, Pro). The comparison with benchmark methods shows that the proposed approach outperforms others. To improve model interpretability, we used Grad-CAM visualisations and Vision Transformer attention maps to examine image regions associated with the model’s predictions, complemented by quantitative faithfulness analysis. The proposed model achieves strong accuracy, F1-scores, specificity, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). Although the framework demonstrated strong performance on both datasets, patient-wise separation could not be independently verified because reliable patient identifiers were not consistently available; therefore, further patient-wise and multi-centre external validation is required. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed explainable hybrid framework for accurate and interpretable leukaemia classification.

Article.Title: Simulation-based active cell balancing of a four-cell lithium-ion pack using a Cuk converter and fuzzy-PID current control
Article.Authors: Lammecha T.; Huluka A.; Nallamothu R.
Article.Abstract: Cell-to-cell inconsistency limits the usable capacity and service life of series-connected lithium-ion battery packs. This simulation study evaluates active balancing of a four-cell pack in which a shared Cuk converter, connected through a dual-layer donor/receiver switch matrix, is driven by a cascaded controller. A Mamdani fuzzy inference system converts the average pack state of charge (SOC) and the SOC spread into an equalization-current reference (0–5 A), and a continuous-time PID block, tuned to integral-only action, tracks this reference through 10 kHz PWM with the duty ratio limited to 0.75. Each cell is a second-order RC model with SOC-dependent parameters adopted from a published identification study; all cells share these parameters, and imbalance is imposed through initial SOC values of 55%, 50%, 45% and 47%. With fuzzy-PID control the cells converged in about 415 s at rest, 390 s during discharge and 350 s during charge, compared with 575, 800 and 700 s for conventional fuzzy control (27.8–51.3% shorter). The model-level donor-to-receiver energy-transfer index was 87.52%. Because the cells are identical, SOC feedback is ideal and no hardware was tested, the results are a simulation proof of concept; sensitivity bounds and the validation required before EV use are reported.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning reveals a compact, low-dimensional geometric basis underlying sheet and skeletal TPMS architected materials
Article.Authors: Mermigkis G.; Liakopoulos C.; Rodopoulos D.; Hadjidoukas P.; Karathanasopoulos N.
Article.Abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) architectures constitute one of the largest and most diverse families of architected materials, yet the geometric principles governing their mechanical and thermal behavior remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate fourteen TPMS topologies spanning both sheet- and skeletal-based realizations and characterize their geometry through a set of sixteen physically interpretable descriptors. Combining finite element simulations with explainable machine learning, we establish descriptor hierarchies for the effective mechanical and thermal properties across the TPMS design space. Surface area and compactness emerge as universal descriptors shared by both architecture classes, while descriptors of diminishing importance differ between sheet and skeletal networks, reflecting distinct manifestations of geometric heterogeneity. Despite these differences, a unified four-descriptor representation is identified that accurately predicts Young’s and shear moduli, thermal conductivity, as well as uniaxial and shear yield limits across all topologies for both network classes with coefficients of determination exceeding \(R^2=0.93\) . Interestingly, both principal component analysis (PCA) and the nonlinear Levina-Bickel intrinsic dimension estimator reveal that the geometric descriptor space and the associated performance space collapse onto a compact, nearly two-dimensional manifold, indicating that the apparent complexity of TPMS architectures arises from a remarkably low-dimensional organization. These findings provide a unified framework, applicable across sheet- and skeletal-based network classes, for interpretable modeling and materials informatics of TPMS architected materials, and establish a compact basis for future inverse-design methodologies.

Article.Title: Anti-HER2 immunotoxin scFv-PE35KDEL internalizes via receptor-mediated endocytosis and induces apoptosis in ovarian cancer cells
Article.Authors: Saeidi M.; Gheisari Z.; Shafiee F.; Chou C.; Akbari V.
Article.Abstract: Ovarian cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, highlighting the need for more effective targeted therapies. Immunotoxins have emerged as promising therapeutic agents for recurrent and metastatic ovarian cancer. In this study, we evaluated the binding, cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, and pro-apoptotic activity of an anti-HER2 immunotoxin, anti-HER2-scFv-PE35KDEL, composed of an anti-HER2 single-chain variable fragment (scFv) derived from pertuzumab fused to a modified 35-kDa fragment of Pseudomonas exotoxin A containing a KDEL sequence. The binding activity and cellular uptake of anti-HER2-scFv-PE35KDEL were evaluated in two ovarian cancer cell lines, SK-OV-3 and OVCAR-3, using flow cytometry, fluorometric analysis, and fluorescence microscopy. Cytotoxicity was assessed using MTT assay, while apoptosis induction was analyzed by Annexin V/PI staining and Western blot analysis of apoptosis-related proteins. The immunotoxin demonstrated significantly greater binding and cellular uptake in HER2-overexpressing SK-OV-3 cells compared with HER2-low OVCAR-3 cells, suggesting receptor-mediated internalization. Chlorpromazine treatment reduced cellular uptake, indicating the possible involvement of clathrin-mediated endocytosis. MTT analysis revealed concentration-dependent cytotoxicity against SK-OV-3 cells with an IC50 value of 10.90 nM, whereas OVCAR-3 cells exhibited substantially lower sensitivity with an IC50 value of 76.79 nM. Furthermore, treatment with anti-HER2-scFv-PE35KDEL induced apoptosis in SK-OV-3 cells in a concentration-dependent manner and increased the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio. These findings suggest that anti-HER2-scFv-PE35KDEL may exert preferential cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic effects against HER2-overexpressing ovarian cancer cells and support further preclinical investigation of this immunotoxin as a potential targeted therapeutic agent.

Article.Title: Integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and transcriptome analysis to explore uric acid–related biomarkers and regulatory mechanisms in preeclampsia
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Hou L.; Xie C.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a pregnancy-specific syndrome that occurs after 20 weeks of gestation. Abnormal uric acid metabolism may play a pivotal role in the onset and progression of PE. This research aimed to extensively analyze and pinpoint biomarkers related to uric acid in PE and elucidate their potential molecular mechanisms. Data related to PE and uric acid were obtained from the public databases. Biomarkers were selected and validated through differential expression analysis, machine learning algorithms, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and expression level validation. Moreover, a nomogram was applied to construct a uric acid-related predictive model for PE. Enrichment analysis, immune infiltration analysis, molecular regulatory network, drug prediction, and molecular docking were performed to further verify the regulatory roles of biomarkers. Furthermore, the expression patterns of biomarkers in core cells were investigated using dataset GSE173193. Finally, validation of biomarkers expression was performed by western- blotting and qRT-PCR. Overall, four biomarkers (ENG, JAK1, LEP, and SLC6A8) were identified as significantly associated with uric acid in PE. A predictive nomogram based on these biomarkers showed promising apparent diagnostic performance in the GSE35574 cohort. The biomarkers were significantly enriched in the “housekeeping genes”, “mitochondria”, and “signaling by Robo receptors”. Notably, JAK1 was positively correlated with gamma delta T cells, while SLC6A8 was negatively correlated with gamma delta T cells. Subsequently, 348 microRNAs (miRNAs) (like hsa-miR-4486) and 25 transcription factors (TFs) (like CTCF, TBP, and MAFK) were associated with the biomarkers. Molecular docking predicted favorable interactions for the reported biomarker-compound pairs. Moreover, ENG, JAK1, and SLC6A8 exhibited relatively high expression in extravillous trophoblasts (EVT). Finally, the results of qRT-PCR and Western blot showed that the mRNA and protein expressions of ENG, SLC6A8, and LEP in placental tissues from the PE group were higher than those in the control group, while the mRNA and protein expressions of JAK1 were lower in the placental tissues of the PE group compared to the control group, which is consistent with the expression patterns observed in the RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets. Four uric acid-related biomarkers (ENG, JAK1, LEP, and SLC6A8) were identified in PE, providing preliminary molecular clues and a theoretical reference for further mechanistic exploration and the screening of potential therapeutic targets of PE.

Article.Title: The photosynthetic efficiency and heavy metals levels in Silybum marianum L. treated with azoxystrobin
Article.Authors: Adamczyk-Szabela D.; Krakowiak D.; Wolf W.
Article.Abstract: Silybum marianum L. (milk thistle) is valued worldwide for its medicinal properties. Currently, there is growing interest in the organic cultivation of this herb under controlled conditions. Unfortunately, its plantations are often exposed to fungal diseases, which pose a significant threat. The aim of the present study was to determine the effect of the fungicide azoxystrobin on photosynthesis and the uptake of manganese, copper, cadmium, lead, iron, and zinc by milk thistle. Moreover, using the Folin-Ciocalteu method, we determined changes in the level of phenolic compounds, which may reflect the potential response of plants to stressors. The concentrations of metals either in soil or plant samples were determined using ICP-OES technique. In general, azoxystrobin stimulated photosynthesis as indicated by the increase of gas exchange parameters which returned to initial values after 42 days of cultivation. Notable, the decrease of chlorophyl index was observed 28 days after the fungicide application. Nevertheless, the total phenolic content in milk thistle was gradually increasing over the time of cultivation. The highest influence of azoxystrobin was observed for lead and zinc which uptake by roots was significantly reduced after the fungicide application.

Article.Title: Documented preoperative statin exposure and short-term mortality after aortic valve replacement: a multicohort observational study
Article.Authors: Kang M.; Sohn S.; Choi J.; Hwang H.; Kim K.; Kang Y.
Article.Abstract: Whether documented preoperative statin exposure is associated with short-term mortality after aortic valve replacement (AVR) is uncertain. This retrospective multicohort study included 5,291 AVR records from SNUH, MIMIC-IV, and eICU. The primary analysis compared no documented versus any documented statin exposure for recorded 30-day mortality in SNUH and MIMIC-IV using overlap weighting and fixed-effect pooling. Exposure-window, recorded 365-day, IPTW, and SNUH available-follow-up analyses were sensitivity analyses; eICU and agent-specific analyses were exploratory. Overlap-weighted 30-day risks with versus without documented exposure were 1.29% versus 2.55% in SNUH and 1.18% versus 2.36% in MIMIC-IV; the pooled HR was 2.01 (95% CI, 0.98 to 4.11; P = 0.056). A 1-day MIMIC-IV window reclassified seven records and, pooled with the SNUH 24-h definition, yielded an HR of 2.29 (95% CI, 1.14 to 4.61; P = 0.020) at 30 days; the recorded 365-day HR was 1.76 (95% CI, 1.00 to 3.09; P = 0.050). Thirty-day IPTW estimates and the SNUH available-follow-up estimate were significant but remained sensitivity analyses. Absence of documented exposure showed consistently higher adjusted mortality estimates, but the primary analysis was inconclusive. Residual confounding, exposure misclassification, and incomplete death ascertainment limit causal interpretation.

Article.Title: Psychological distress is associated with early ultrasound-detected median nerve changes in asymptomatic young adults
Article.Authors: Marini A.; Iliou K.; Stergiou A.; Kitsouli N.; Chatzoglou T.; Kitsoulis P.; Varvarousis D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is a common compressive neuropathy, caused by entrapment of the median nerve within the carpal tunnel. CTS has a vast range of symptoms, resulting in sensory and motor dysfunction of the hand. Whether psychosocial factors are associated with CTS remains obscure. The present study examined the relationship between median nerve ultrasonographic cross-sectional area (CSA) and stress and depression among asymptomatic young individuals. The study involved 169 healthy Greek medical students (67 men and 102 women). Age, gender, dominant hand, medical history, daily hours of computer use, and family background were recorded. Two validated psychiatric questionnaires estimating stress and anxiety were self-completed. Median nerve status was examined using ultrasonography. A CSA of < 10 mm² was considered normal and > 12 mm² pathological. Data were analyzed using Pearson linear correlation and t-test. Mean CSA of the median nerve was 0.082 cm (SD = 0.018). Total daily time of computer use was positively correlated with CSA ( p = 0.012). Mean Zung Scale Score for depression was 38.89 (± 8.76), while STAI-Y1 and STAI-Y2 for anxiety estimation were 37.28 (± 9.78) and 41.14 (± 11.21) respectively. CSA of the median nerve was positively associated with ZUNG ( p = 0.001), STAI-Y1 ( p < 0.001) and STAI-Y2 ( p < 0.001) scores. The daily hours of computer use, depression and anxiety are positively associated with median nerve CSA among healthy young adults. The correlation between anxiety, depression and CSA highlights the need for both biomechanical and psychiatric interventions in asymptomatic subjects with psychological distress.

Article.Title: Traits associated with novel foraging success in urban mesopredators
Article.Authors: Stanton L.; Caspi T.; Estien C.; Huber G.; Schell C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urbanization is transforming ecosystems worldwide, creating novel environmental conditions that wildlife must adjust to. Because urban species differ markedly in ecological strategies, functional traits, and societal perceptions, they experience divergent pressures that shape their responses to the challenges associated with city living. A comparative framework can therefore reveal how both individual and species-level differences influence behaviors such as risk-taking and problem solving, even among related taxa in the same habitat. Here, we challenged free-ranging mesopredators with a novel foraging task and predicted a gradient of species-specific behavioral responses, hypothesizing that boldness, exploration, and effort would influence problem-solving success within and across species. We collected data from 110 locations across the East Bay of California for five mesopredator species: raccoons, opossums, striped skunks, coyotes, and domestic cats. Individuals from all species solved the task multiple times, but raccoons and coyotes emerged as the most successful despite divergent approaches. Across species, effort was the strongest predictor of success, whereas within species, exploratory individuals were most likely to solve. In contrast, boldness did not predict success. These results illustrate how trait differences within and among a taxonomic guild shape behavioral responses to novel challenges, offering insights on the strategies that facilitate urban persistence.

Article.Title: Automated optimization of solar energetic particle acceleration and transport parameters against five-spacecraft observations of the 9 October 2021 event
Article.Authors: Ishikawa H.; Fujita N.; Kato Y.; Kurihara M.; Minoshima T.; Shiota D.; Iwai K.; Pinto M.; Gomes A.; Murakami G.; Kusano K.; Mitsuda C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Solar energetic particle (SEP) events threaten space infrastructure, yet physics-based prediction models depend on numerous poorly constrained free parameters. We introduce the Fujitsu Solar Energetic particle Intelligent Tuning and Evaluation Network (SEITEN), which couples the MHD model of CME propagation to , a diffusive shock acceleration and focused transport model, through the shock conditions supplies, and automatically optimizes the free parameters of the particle model against the SEP event of 9 October 2021. The mean free path and the injection efficiency vary independently along each magnetic field line and heliolongitudinal bin, giving a 19-dimensional problem solved by quasi-Monte Carlo sampling followed by a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator. The optimized model reproduces proton flux profiles at five spacecraft with a mean absolute error of $$\approx 0.45$$ in log10 flux, and the inferred mean free paths show a clear east–west structure; these are effective parameters conditional on the assumed transport geometry. Six independent runs show that whether mean free paths or injection efficiencies dominate depends on the MHD shock strength, and that injection efficiencies differ by orders of magnitude between MHD configurations despite nearly identical fit quality. Joint MHD–SEP parameter estimation is therefore a necessary next step toward generalized, operational SEP forecasting.

Article.Title: Modeling of peak shear strength of rock joints based on a three-dimensional roughness index
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Man C.; Qi J.; Gao W.; Zheng J.; Chen Y.; Li X.; Ban L.
Article.Abstract: Rock joints are widely present in engineering rock masses, and their peak shear strength directly governs the stability of jointed rock masses. To investigate the influence mechanism of joint surface morphology on the peak shear strength, this study fabricated 35 sets of joint specimens with five distinct morphological types using a combination of three-dimensional laser scanning and CNC engraving technologies. Based on the scanning results, an improved 3D apparent dip angle distribution function was proposed, which more accurately captures the spatial distribution characteristics of joint surface morphology. By integrating this function, a new 3D roughness index was developed. This index exhibits a clear linear relationship with the sampling interval and decreases as the interval increases. Subsequently, a series of constant-normal-load direct shear tests on rock joints was conducted. Test results revealed a strong linear correlation between this roughness index and the initial (zero-normal-stress) peak dilation angle. Moreover, the degradation trend of the peak dilation angle with increasing normal stress can be effectively described by an exponential function. On this basis, a peak dilation angle degradation model was defined, which enables accurate prediction of peak dilation angles under varying normal stress conditions. By incorporating this model into the Mohr-Coulomb criterion, a peak shear strength model was established. Comparative analysis with existing models, including validation against published data on granite joints, demonstrates that the proposed model offers the highest prediction accuracy ( R 2 = 0.978; mean relative error = 4.25%), making it suitable for reliably estimating the peak shear strength of rock joints.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: peak shear strength; rock joints; Mohr-Coulomb criterion; joint surface morphology; joint roughness; normal stress dependence; direct shear test

Article.Title: Privacy-preserving collaborative transfer learning with generative adversarial networks (CTL-GAN) for classification of dry eye disease
Article.Authors: Kim B.; Won Y.; Kim H.; Cha J.; Lim D.; Jeon J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated whether a collaborative transfer learning generative adversarial network (CTL-GAN) can generate synthetic fluorescein corneal images and enhance multiclass dry eye disease (DED) grading across institutions. We retrospectively included 1,600 fluorescein-stained anterior segment images from patients with DED at Samsung Medical Center (SMC) and 260 images from the public Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU) dataset, graded on the Oxford scale. A StyleGAN3 generator trained on SMC data produced synthetic images. Pretrained generator weights were transferred to a simulated site represented by the SYSU dataset and fine-tuned on local images, without exchanging raw images. DenseNet classifiers trained with GAN-based augmentation were compared with a benchmark model trained on real images only. GAN-based augmentation improved validation accuracy on SMC data from 64.2% to 75.5%, and transferring pretrained weights increased SYSU validation accuracy from 41.4% to 66.3%. Peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR 13.95 ± 1.54 dB), structural similarity index (SSIM 0.428 ± 0.111), and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS 0.510 ± 0.047) showed low similarity to real images. In a blinded 10-item multiple-choice realism survey, 37 ophthalmologists answered correctly in 28.4% of cases, against a 20% chance level. CTL-GAN indicates that image synthesis from shared generator weights can improve external DED grading without exchanging patient images.

Article.Title: Enhanced surface hydrophobicity in the combined treatment of chaplins and rodlins from Streptomyces griseus
Article.Authors: Shamsol Anuar N.; Suhaimi N.; Suzuki K.; Sunagawa N.; Ohnishi Y.; Tezuka T.; Hara H.
Article.Abstract: Many microorganisms depend on their hydrophobic hyphal surfaces to grow into the air and disperse their spores. In Streptomyces species, this property is conferred by chaplin and rodlin proteins. In the present study, we examined the potential of chaplins and rodlins from Streptomyces griseus IFO 13350, focusing on their contributions to surface hydrophobicity. In vitro assays with recombinant chaplins (ChpC and ChpH) and rodlins (RdlA and RdlB) demonstrated that ChpH alone increased the hydrophobicity of glass slides. The combination of ChpH with RdlA/RdlB enhanced water repellency, yielding a contact angle of 66.7 ± 2.6°, which was significantly greater than that of either ChpH or RdlA/RdlB alone. The long chaplin, ChpC, did not show such an enhancement with RdlA/RdlB. Gene disruption experiments supported the assumption that short chaplin ChpH plays a dominant role in generating hydrophobic surfaces and acts cooperatively with RdlA and/or RdlB to produce strongly water-repellent surfaces. We showed that hydrophobicity can be maintained even in the absence of rodlet structures, highlighting the flexibility of the chaplin–rodlin system. Based on these findings, we propose a hypothetical model in which rodlins act as molecular scaffolds that align short-chaplin fibrils into ordered rodlet arrays, thereby amplifying surface hydrophobicity. This study also suggests that chaplins in combination with rodlins have potential as effective additives for surface hydrophobicity.

Article.Title: Performance evaluation of Spar equipped with solitary and double heave plate for use in east coast of India
Article.Authors: Sudhakar S.; Lavanya V.; Ramshankar P.; Devi T.; Sunagar P.; Dharek M.
Article.Abstract: Numerical techniques which are effective and affordable can be used to model and solve complex situations in ocean engineering problems. Either the time domain or the frequency domain can be used to solve the fluid structure interaction problems involving regular and random waves. The ANSYS AQWA program which is built on three-dimensional panel method which falls under the category of Boundary Element Method is designed to analyze the interaction between surface waves and offshore structures using diffraction radiation phenomenon. Heave plates have been extensively employed on Spar as dampening mechanisms to minimize its motion responses. These plates are effective in offering viscous damping and considerable added mass in heave mode. This hybrid approach began with 1:100 scale free-decay tests of the Spar, run both bare-hulled and with a damping plate fitted, to capture its physical heave behaviour. The resulting hydrodynamic response of the Spar carrying twin heave plates was then simulated under regular and irregular sea states in ANSYS AQWA, a potential-flow-based solver. Because AQWA cannot capture viscous effects on its own, the gap between the total damping measured experimentally and the radiation damping predicted numerically was treated as non-linear viscous damping and fed back into the model as an external user-defined input. The role of relative spacing on Spar’s motion response was assessed and subsequently presented in the analysis. The simulated results revealed that the Spar featuring a pair of heave plates with a relative spacing ranging from 30 to 40% greater than that of Spar integrated with a solitary heave plate possessing a diameter ratio of 1.3 was highly effective in reducing responses under both regular and random wave conditions. The adoption of motion-reduction technologies in these platforms facilitates the development of clean energy solutions, thereby contributing to the achievement of United Nations Sustainable Development Goals on affordable and clean energy.

Article.Title: A robust deep learning framework for smart grid stability classification using statistical validation
Article.Authors: Kalyankumar K.; Saraswathi P.; Vanitha C.; Robin L.; Zewdu M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The classification of smart-grid stability is difficulty due to nonlinear interactions among the participant reaction-time, elasticity of power consumption and electricity-price. This paper proposed a comparative deep-learning model of classifying stable and unstable operating conditions based on 10,000 observations of simulated four-node electrical-grid stability dataset. To avoid deterministic redundancy and target leakage, we omitted p1 and the continuous stability variable stab, making 11 input predictors. They were data-quality assessment, training, standardization, stratified data partitioning and five-fold cross-validation. Four traditional machine-learning models (Logistic Regression, RBF-SVM, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting) and five deep-learning models (DNN, AutoEncoder-DNN, 1D-CNN, CNN1D-LSTM and FT-Transformer) were tested using a similar conditions. The DNN achieved the best overall test performance, with an accuracy of 97.10%, precision of 97.28%, recall of 98.20%, F1-score of 97.74%, ROC-AUC of 0.9963 and PR-AUC of 0.9980. AutoEncoder-DNN and RBF-SVM had the accuracy of 96.90% and 96.05, respectively. Precise paired McNemar tests with Holm correction indicated that the DNN performed better in comparison to the other tested networks with the exception of the AutoEncoder-DNN where the difference was not statistically relevant. The analysis of SHAP and feature-group ablation showed that the most impactful predictor groups were reaction times and price-elasticity coefficients of participants. The DNN achieved 95.60% accuracy with standardized Gaussian noise with a value of 0.10, but dropped to 90.90% in the case of 10% of measurements random and median-imputed. These results indicate that the DNN is effective on the studied simulated benchmark. However, it needs to be validated with actual PMU or SCADA measurements and larger and more heterogeneous grid topologies prior to operational implementation.

Article.Title: Mitochondrial diversity and demographic history of Arctica islandica (Bivalvia: Venerida) in the German waters of the Baltic Sea
Article.Authors: Schulz L.; Kniesz K.; Stuckas H.; Wolf F.; Zettler M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The semi-enclosed Baltic Sea is a comparatively young brackish ecosystem characterised by strong environmental gradients that can shape genetic diversity and demographic history in marine species. The amphi-Atlantic bivalve Arctica islandica (Linnaeus 1767) inhabits the southwestern Baltic Sea, where populations experience environmental conditions distinct from fully marine habitats. We analysed mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I ( COI ) and cytochrome b ( CytB ) sequences to assess mitochondrial diversity and infer historical demographic patterns of A. islandica in the German waters of the Baltic Sea. Mitochondrial diversity was high, with haplotype diversity of 0.82–0.84 and nucleotide diversity of 0.69–0.74%. Widespread haplotype sharing and no evidence of regional structuring were observed. Most genetic variation occurred within rather than among regions (F ST = − 0.025, p = 0.99). Demographic analyses supported a history of population expansion, while comparison with previously published CytB haplotypes showed that specimens from the German waters of the Baltic Sea predominantly shared common haplotypes with samples from multiple regions across the species’ distribution. Overall, the mitochondrial data indicate that A. islandica populations in the German waters of the Baltic Sea retain substantial shared mitochondrial diversity despite inhabiting environmentally distinct brackish habitats. These patterns are consistent with relatively recent colonisation or expansion within the Baltic Sea and a shared demographic history and provide a baseline for future genome-wide studies of population connectivity and adaptive variation.

Article.Title: Design and development of a full-scale oxygenator model for future biohybrid lung application
Article.Authors: Singh A.; Janning K.; Simbolon D.; Mouzakis F.; Kashefi A.; Mottaghy K.; Neidlin M.; Olmer R.; Jockenhoevel S.; Cornelissen C.; Thiebes A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Use of conventional oxygenators is typically limited to 10–14 days due to poor hemocompatibility. Endothelialization of gas exchange membranes can create a natural non-thrombogenic surface and has proven effective in small laboratory models, but this approach requires a specific oxygenator design that can support both effective gas exchange and future membrane endothelialization. Thus, we developed a modular spiral-coil oxygenator using a fabrication approach that enables the production of a large membrane surface area with integrated blood channels. We designed and fabricated multiple oxygenator prototypes using a rolled flat-sheet PDMS/spacer/PDMS membrane structure and evaluated their gas exchange and fluid flow. Prototypes were tested for gas exchange performance following ISO 7199:2016 standards. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed to assess flow distribution and wall shear stress (WSS). Among the tested prototypes, two designs provided the most promising results. They achieved surface areas of 0.20 m² and 0.34 m² with priming volumes of 348 mL and 312 mL, respectively. Both models showed quantifiable gas exchange supporting the feasibility of the proposed concept. CFD simulations revealed no stagnant areas and low WSS. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a modular spiral-coil oxygenator with a large-area flat-sheet membrane and millimeter-scale blood channels. While gas transfer requires improvement before clinical applicability for extracorporeal CO 2 removal, the fabrication approach provides a foundation for future endothelialization and development of long-term biohybrid lung support devices.

Article.Title: Synergistic integration of graphene-CNT-doped stearic acid PCM and graphene–metal oxide hybrid nanofluids for enhanced photovoltaic thermal–electrical performance
Article.Authors: Kumar N.; Barik D.; Tudu K.; Ranjan A.; Resmi S.; Ashok N.; Shanmugapriya D.; Gnanasekaran L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To enhance the durability of the solar PV systems, it is necessary to use novel materials and methods for cooling and disposal of unwanted heat. In this perspective, phase change materials (PCMs) with hybrid nanofluids are one of the best choices for efficient thermal management. This experiment proposes a novel PV cooling system that uses graphene and CNT nanoparticles (1:1) and (6 w/w%) added stearic acid as a PCM with hybrid nanofluids to maximize heat dissipation and system overall efficiency. The novelty lies in the synergistic combination of graphene-CNT-doped PCM (melting point 59 °C) with graphene-metal oxide hybrid nanofluids. Three hybrid nanofluids were prepared: G-TiO₂, G-Al₂O₃, and G-SiO₂, at a volume concentration of 0.5%, and different flow rates of 2, 4, 6, and 8 LPM were tested. The results proved that the 6 LPM flow rate, with the G-Al₂O₃ nanofluid, gave the best thermal and electrical results. In that, the enhanced absolute electrical efficiency was 4.5%, thermal efficiency by 8.3%, and the Nusselt number was 295 in comparison with the base fluid (DI water). Although the pressure drop and friction factor increased by 0.3 N/m² and 0.08, respectively, with G-SiO₂, it is still controllable with normal pumping. The proposed solar PV cooling system is highly applicable in building-integrated systems, hot climates, and hybrid renewable micro-grid systems.

Article.Title: Efficient removal of fusidic acid from aqueous solution using synthesized zinc magnesium aluminum layered double hydroxide adsorbent
Article.Authors: Asmel N.; Alwared A.; Sulaiman F.; Mohammed N.; Kalla R.; Knani S.; Ansari A.; Lakkaboyana S.
Article.Abstract: Pharmaceutical residues in the water have become a growing environmental concern because of their potential ecological and human health effects and their persistence. The Zn-Mg-Al layered double hydroxides (LDH) were prepared by the co-precipitation method, and their efficiency was tested as an adsorbent for the elimination of fusidic acid (FA) from aqueous solution. Characterization of the synthesized material was done by FTIR, SEM, XRD, EDS, BET, and TGA. The parameters affecting adsorption performance, such as pH, dosage of the adsorbent, contact time, initial concentration of FA and temperature, were investigated by batch adsorption experiments. The most efficient removal was obtained in 210 min at the optimum conditions of FA adsorbent dosage (1.25 g/L), agitation speed (250 rpm), concentration (20 mg/L), pH 5, and temperature (20 ± 1 °C), and showed the best agreement with the PSO model. Kinetic analysis suggested the PSO model best fitted the experimental data, while isotherm studies showed good agreement with the Freundlich model, indicating a heterogeneous adsorption behavior. Thermodynamic analysis shows that adsorption process was thermodynamically favorable. Besides, the reusability and structural stability of the adsorbent improved after calcination treatment, whereas the adsorption rate was slightly decreased. The results indicated that the Zn-Mg-Al LDH is a promising and economical adsorbent for the removal of pharmaceutical contaminants from aqueous stream.
