Article.Title: Structure-guided design and dynamic evaluation of VP4-targeting siRNAs against rotavirus A
Article.Authors: Ahmed A.; Satu K.; Rahman A.; Hasan S.; Sakib M.; Hossan M.; Bhattacharjee A.; Chowdhury Z.; Joy Z.; Islam M.; Hossain M.
Article.Abstract: Rotavirus is a major cause of severe diarrheal disease in children under the age of five, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, with no currently available antiviral therapeutics and treatment being largely supportive. In this study, we developed an integrative in silico approach to design and evaluate siRNAs targeting conserved mRNA transcript of the VP4 gene of Rotavirus A across six geographically diverse countries. Candidate siRNAs were screened using established design rules, target accessibility assessment, regression-based scoring with off-target filtering and thermodynamics analysis. The predicted interactions showed conserved binding within TRBP and AGO2 domains, corroborating efficient RISC compatibility. Molecular dynamics simulations (100 ns) showed stable conformational behavior of AGO2–siRNA–mRNA complexes, with low RMSD values (~ 0.2–0.5 nm) and limited residue fluctuations (< 0.2 nm). MM/PBSA analysis showed that siRNA02 exhibited the most favorable AGO2 binding free energy (-453.62 kJ/mol), suggesting enhanced RISC stabilization, whereas siRNA01 demonstrated the strongest target mRNA interaction (-60.63 kJ/mol), indicating superior target recognition. Comparative dynamic analyses identified two siRNAs as the most balanced candidate for AGO2 mediated VP4 silencing based on structural compatibility, reduced conformational fluctuations, and stable interactions. These findings provide a rational computational basis for VP4-targeted siRNA development, facilitating experimental validation.

Article.Title: Sustainable meso-conical cup fabrication using recycled e-waste-derived copper: a hybrid RSM–Spherical Fuzzy AHP–fuzzy GRA optimization approach
Article.Authors: Sivam S.; Lazar P.; Kesavan S.; Santhosh A.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates meso-conical cup fabrication using as-received copper (AR) and a recycled copper-based composite feedstock (EW) containing 30 wt.% recovered e-waste-derived copper and 70 wt.% as-received copper. To achieve this, we developed a hybrid Response Surface Methodology (RSM)–Spherical Fuzzy AHP–Fuzzy Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) framework in which feed rate, depth, step size, and material type were treated as control factors. At the same time, surface roughness, dimensional accuracy, production cost and energy consumption were selected as response variables. The findings revealed a pronounced quality–cost–energy trade-off. The A14 condition (AR, 20 mm/min feed, 0.15 mm depth, and 0.10 mm step size) delivered the best quality performance, achieving 1.0 µm surface roughness and 97.0% dimensional accuracy. In contrast, the A10 condition (EW, 30 mm/min feed, 0.15 mm depth, and 0.10 mm step size) had lower production cost (₹6.383/part) and energy consumption (2.289 Wh/part) than A14 (₹9.291/part and 3.294 Wh/part). Relative to A10, A14 improved surface roughness by 28.57% and dimensional accuracy by 1.57%, but increased cost by 45.56% and energy use by 43.91%. The results show that partially incorporating recovered e-waste-derived copper is technically feasible and can reduce production cost and operational energy demand under selected conditions. However, the AR condition remains preferable when surface finishes and dimensional accuracy are the primary requirements.

Article.Title: Early and reliable short-video news verification through event-aware shot modeling and cross-modal evidence fusion
Article.Authors: Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Short-video news combines titles, images, speech, and captions, allowing misleading narratives to emerge from individually authentic components. Whole-video aggregation and undifferentiated fusion can obscure when discrepancies arise and whether their sources are reliable. We present EASE-Fact, a framework for content-based news screening that models ordered visual units under an explicit observation boundary. A causal event-evolution transformer captures title-conditioned transitions, while a reliability-aware router models typed cross-modal relations and distinguishes inconsistent evidence from absent or unreliable sources. The Core model supports complete-video classification and a separately trained streaming configuration with prefix-local preprocessing and committed transcripts. The Full model adds temporally admissible historical debunking records and preserves the Core prediction when usable evidence is unavailable. Chronological and event-disjoint evaluations, matched comparisons, online first-crossing alerts, component ablations, and manual localization assess the framework’s performance and practical boundaries. The findings support temporal structure and source-quality modelling, while statistical uncertainty and event-exclusion analyses qualify comparative and retrieval gains. EASE-Fact provides inspectable diagnostics for news communication and editorial prioritization; benchmark predictions and internal conflicts remain distinct from independent determinations of factual truth.

Article.Title: A post-marketing assessment of critical quality and short-term stability attributes of heat-stable carbetocin injection products marketed in India
Article.Authors: Lambert P.; Parsons M.; Rudd D.
Article.Abstract: Intramuscular carbetocin injection has comparable efficacy to the first-line therapy, oxytocin injection, when used for prevention of postpartum haemorrhage, the leading cause of global maternal mortality. A novel heat-stable injectable formulation of carbetocin, first marketed in 2020, overcomes the requirement for refrigerated storage and aims to increase access to quality-assured uterotonic products in resource-limited settings where cold chain infrastructure is lacking or unreliable. Generic heat-stable carbetocin products have now emerged in India. In the context of widespread evidence that generic oxytocin injection products claiming stability outside of the cold chain do not meet stability requirements for non-refrigerated storage in hot and humid climates, this study is the first to assess the quality and stability of these carbetocin products. Two heat-stable generic carbetocin products were assessed in comparison to the innovator product for key quality attributes (assay, impurities and pH) and stability during a six-month program at temperatures ranging from 2 to 8 °C to 60 °C. All heat-stable products assessed met recognised quality standards for drug content (108.93% − 109.90%) and total impurities (0.57% − 0.85%). The generic products showed robust stability in terms of drug content, with no significant differences in degradation rates to the innovator product at all temperatures over the period tested. However, the rate of total impurity formation was higher than the innovator product at temperatures exceeding 30 °C, largely driven by hydrolytic degradation (e.g. total impurities after six months storage at 40 °C – generic 3.4–3.6%, innovator 1.8%). Impurity formation may be associated with the lower pH of these formulations (generic pH 4.7 vs. innovator pH 5.5) catalysing this degradation process. While long-term testing of multiple batches would be required for definitive conclusions, this study provides no indications of quality issues associated with the generic heat-stable carbetocin products based on the attributes tested. Furthermore, these products demonstrate similar stability to the innovator during short-term stability testing at their registered storage conditions (i.e. up to 30 °C).

Article.Title: OSW-1 impairs autophagic flux via AMPK/mTORC1/TFEB-dependent TFEB activation and STX17 downregulation, leading to necroptosis in colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Zhao D.; Xu Z.; Ma J.; Yao T.; Li C.; Guo H.; Song W.; Wang N.
Article.Abstract: OSW-1, a natural compound with potent anticancer activity, has shown significant therapeutic potential in colorectal cancer (CRC). Although previous studies have implicated necroptosis, the upstream regulatory mechanisms linking autophagy to necroptosis remain incompletely defined. In this study, we systematically investigated the anticancer mechanisms of OSW-1 in CRC cells, with a particular focus on its ability to induce necroptosis via modulation of autophagic flux. The results demonstrate that OSW-1 activates AMPK (AMP-activated protein kinase) and inhibits mTORC1 (mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1), thereby promoting the nuclear translocation of TFEB (transcription factor EB) and initiating autophagy as well as lysosome biogenesis. However, OSW-1 downregulates STX17 (syntaxin 17) via an AMPK-independent mechanism, thereby disrupting autophagosome-lysosome fusion, blocking autophagic flux and causing the accumulation of SQSTM1/p62, which in turn promotes RIPK1 (receptor-interacting protein kinase 1) and RIPK3-mediated necrosome assembly, ultimately leading to necroptosis. The AMPK inhibitor compound C (CC) partially restores autophagic flux and reduces necroptosis, confirming the pivotal role of the AMPK/mTORC1/TFEB pathway in mediating OSW-1’s effects. In vivo experiments further demonstrate that OSW-1 significantly inhibits the growth of CRC xenograft tumors. Following OSW-1 treatment, AMPK is activated, and SQSTM1/p62 accumulation induces necroptosis. This study is the first to comprehensively elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which OSW-1 exerts its anticancer effects through the “autophagic flux blockade-necroptosis” pathway, providing an important theoretical basis for its potential clinical application.

Article.Title: A novel cloud-enabled enterprise information systems framework for accelerating digital transformation strategies
Article.Authors: Xu W.
Article.Abstract: The co-evolution of micro-frontend UIs and backend microservices in cloud-native environments is complicated by UI–API semantic drift, dynamic workloads, and safe-deployment constraints. A tripartite agentic AI framework is introduced that combines reinforcement-learning (RL) agents for adaptive runtime control, large-language-model (LLM) synthesizers for automated artifact generation, and policy-as-code governors for security and compliance enforcement. The co-evolution process is formulated as a drift-aware Markov decision process, while Kubernetes-native traffic shifting supports progressive rollout and rollback. KubeSim was used for offline policy training; the reported performance results were obtained from live AWS EKS, Google GKE, and Azure AKS clusters. Across five benchmarks, the framework achieved a mean resolution success rate of 91.4%, compared with 62.0% for rule-based control, 71.1% for a controlled zero-shot LLM baseline, and 79.0% for partial RL. The framework also reduced normalized mean time to recovery by 80%, normalized change failure rate by 75%, and CPU utilization by 30 percentage points, while attaining a 98% audit pass rate. Component-removal and counterfactual-return analyses indicate complementary contributions from adaptive control, artifact synthesis, and policy enforcement. These results support the effectiveness, scalability, and governability of the framework for cloud-native enterprise digital transformation.

Article.Title: A unified deep learning framework for multi-lesion detection in diabetic retinopathy using fundus images
Article.Authors: Ramesh R.; Lavanya R.; Sikha O.
Article.Abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR), an ocular disease caused by diabetes, is a significant cause of vision impairment. Early and accurate detection of different types of retinal lesions, including Microaneurysms, Haemorrhages, Soft Exudates and Hard Exudates, is essential for DR diagnosis and prevention of associated vision loss. Conventional manual analysis of retinal fundus images is subjective and time-consuming, requiring specialized clinical expertise. Automated diagnostic systems can alleviate these issues and assist clinicians with objective analysis and improved outcomes. This work focuses on simultaneous detection of different lesion types in DR, through a unified framework. In particular, the U-Net architecture is employed for multi-lesion segmentation due to its ability to preserve fine structural details using its encoder-decoder design. Additionally, an Adaptive Batch Scaling (ABS) strategy is employed, wherein the batch size is dynamically adjusted across training epochs, based on the validation Dice score, to optimize pixel-level segmentation accuracy. The performance of U-Net is compared with other DL-based segmentation models such as Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network, YOLOv8, and Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network architectures, in terms of its ability to accurately segment and identify diverse DR lesions in retinal fundus images. Validation is performed on two different publicly available DR datasets, i.e., Indian Diabetic Retinopathy Image Dataset (IDRiD) and Diabetic Retinopathy Detection Dataset (DDR). Specifically, DDR dataset is used for training the model, which is tested separately on each of the two datasets – DDR and IDRiD, to assess intra-dataset and cross-dataset generalization. Performance metrics including accuracy, Dice score, Intersection over Union (IoU) and mean average precision (mAP), are used to evaluate the performance of the models. The findings reveal that the U-Net architecture demonstrates superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 0.925, Dice score of 0.771, IoU of 0.748 and mAP of 0.647. The results demonstrate the potential of semantic segmentation models, particularly U-Net, in automated DR screening. The proposed unified multi-lesion detection system enables simultaneous detection of multiple DR lesions in a single-pass reducing computational overhead, while maintaining reasonable detection performance. The system is envisaged to serve as a reliable tool in DR screening workflow, facilitating early diagnosis and timely intervention, thereby reducing the burden of DR-related vision worldwide.

Article.Title: Combustion assisted sol-gel synthesis of larnite using different fuels for tissue engineering applications
Article.Authors: Mary M.; Vijayakumar N.; Venkatraman S.; Chatterjee A.; Abraham J.; Mohammadi H.; Ebadi M.; Swamiappan S.
Article.Abstract: Larnite (Ca₂SiO₄) has attracted considerable attention for bone tissue engineering because of its favorable bioactivity, controlled ionic dissolution, and ability to support apatite formation. In this study, phase-pure nanocrystalline larnite was synthesized through sol-gel combustion route using tartaric acid and L-alanine as fuels to investigate the influence of fuel chemistry on its physicochemical and biological properties. ICP-OES analysis revealed an initial release of Ca²⁺ and Si⁴⁺ ions into the surrounding medium, followed by a gradual decline in Ca and P ion concentrations due to apatite nucleation and growth, confirming the controlled dissolution behavior of larnite. Antibacterial evaluation showed effective growth inhibition against nine clinically relevant bacterial pathogens at a concentration of 2 mg/mL, while MG63 cell viability assays demonstrated high cytocompatibility, with approximately 97.3% cell viability at 6.25 µg mL⁻¹ for both compositions. Among the investigated fuels, tartaric acid-derived larnite exhibited comparatively improved apatite formation and cytocompatibility. Overall, the findings suggest that combustion-derived larnite possesses favorable bioactivity, controlled ionic dissolution, antibacterial activity, and cytocompatibility, highlighting its potential for bone tissue engineering applications.

Article.Title: Retrospective analysis of LAG3, TIGIT, TIM3 and VISTA immune checkpoints expression in hip and knee periprosthetic joint infection
Article.Authors: Henriksen N.; Bue M.; Ravn C.; Kromann S.; Hansen A.; Ringgaard L.; Pankratova S.; Hansen K.; Odgaard A.; Jensen L.
Article.Abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) poses a major clinical challenge, yet underlying mechanisms relating to the local host immune response remain poorly understood and unexplored. To substantiate the clinical data, immune checkpoint gene expression was measured locally in a porcine model of implant-associated osteomyelitis at 5–19 days post-infection. The mean percentage of immune checkpoint-positive cells was significantly higher in PJI compared to aseptic failures for LAG3 (2.8% vs. 0.7%), TIGIT (8.1% vs. 5.1%) and VISTA (63% vs. 31%), but not for TIM3. VISTA expression was moderately correlated with a history of PJI and joint type. In pigs, LAG3 and TIGIT transcripts increased progressively at 10–19 days post-infection (4.6-9.9-fold compared to saline-inoculated controls). These findings provide a rationale for exploring immune checkpoints as potential biomarkers and non-antimicrobial based future therapeutic targets in PJI.

Article.Title: Correction: Behavioral responses of migratory caribou to semi-permeable roads in Arctic Alaska
Article.Authors: Fullman T.; Joly K.; Gustine D.; Cameron M.
Article.Abstract: After publication, the Authors identified two errors in the data for encounter durations and seasons. In the Article, the Barrier Behavior Analysis classification analyzes movement steps, not location points, to yield information about heading and tortuosity. Because of this the analysis adds a location onto either end of a given burst to ensure a complete step. This results in the starting step for an encounter being the step that takes the animal from outside of a barrier buffer into the buffer, and the last step being that which takes the animal out of the buffer. This also means that for multi-burst encounters a single step signifies the end of one burst and the start of the next, such that the start time of a step is used for the start of burst 2 and the end time of the step is used for the end of burst 1. Additionally, the duration of an encounter and the sum of the durations of each burst within the encounter are not the same for multi-burst encounters. In the original version of the Article encounter duration statistics was reported based on summed burst durations, rather than accounting for overlap. This only affects encounters with multiple bursts. The encounter-scale duration measures and summary statistics are now corrected. As a result, statistics reported in the Results, Table 2, and Supplementary Information 2 have changed as follows.

Article.Title: Application of scanning river surface flow field monitoring system in monitoring complex flow regimes of waterways
Article.Authors: Zhou W.; Yin G.; Feng G.; Gu D.
Article.Abstract: Real-time and accurate monitoring of the surface velocity of rivers is crucial for hydrological research, water resource management, and the safety assurance of waterways. The traditional contact flow measurement method has limitations such as installation difficulties, high maintenance costs, and difficulty in real-time monitoring under complex hydrological conditions. Therefore, this study developed and deployed a non-contact scanning river flow field monitoring system. This system is based on the pulse Doppler system, combined with slot antennas and scanning turntables to achieve wide-angle detection. It integrates intelligent algorithms such as pulse coding matching, distance Doppler processing, WSO optimization clustering, and extreme learning networks to stably invert surface flow velocity and profile flow velocity from complex echoes. Compared with traditional current-measuring radars, the newly developed system has a larger speed measurement range, higher resolution and azimuth resolution. It can achieve coverage of a 120° viewing angle range and has strong anti-interference and fully automatic operation capabilities. In the field application at a hydrological station on the Yangtze River waterway, the system effectively overcame installation deviations and environmental interference, achieving synchronous monitoring of high-resolution surface flow fields and cross-sectional profile flow velocities. The results show that the system provides an efficient, reliable technical solution with broad application prospects for flow pattern monitoring in complex waterway environments.

Article.Title: PLA nanocomposites reinforced with green synthesized AgNPs: its physico-mechanical investigation
Article.Authors: Peidaei Mahmodabad F.; Ahari H.; Moslemi M.; Anvar A.
Article.Abstract: Nanoparticles improve protective characteristics of biodegradable packaging. The aim of this study was to investigate physicomechanical characteristics of polylactic acid film containing 1, 2 and 3% silver nanoparticles synthesized using photo-assisted and ultrasound-assisted methods and aqueous extract of nettle ( Urtica dioica ). Formation of silver nanoparticles was verified using UV-vis spectroscopy. Photochemical and sonochemical synthesized silver nanoparticles were monodisperse with particle sizes of 91.28 and 68.06 nm and polydispersity indices of 0.382 and 0.371, respectively. Solubility and water absorption decreased with silver nanoparticles, especially ultrasound-assisted synthesized ones, into polylactic acid films ( p < 0.05). Nanocomposites containing 2 and 3% of ultrasound-assisted synthesized silver nanoparticles showed the highest tensile strength and elongation at break. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy verified the role of nettle extract as a decreasing, stabilizing and capping agent of silver nanoparticles. In fingerprint region of the spectra, presence of Ag-O bonding and synthesis of silver nanoparticles were verified. Silver nanoparticles improved the thermal stability of polylactic acid nanocomposite films. Therefore, use of silver nanoparticles is recommended to improve physicomechanical and thermal characteristics of polylactic acid films.

Article.Title: How natural dynamic pH conditions could affect compounds mediating marine diatom-bacteria interactions: a chemical theoretical perspective
Article.Authors: Roggatz C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Life in marine diatom-bacteria communities is coordinated through a multitude of chemically-mediated interactions in a highly dynamic environment. Respiration and photosynthesis create steep gradients and large fluctuations in abiotic conditions on diel timescales. But how sensitive biomolecules involved in microbial interactions are to such dynamic microscale environmental impacts has not been assessed so far. Here, I present a predictive chemical-theoretical framework to scope the scale of impact of pH on interactive compounds for representative planktonic and benthic microscale conditions. Focussed on a dataset of 131 compounds from diatom and bacteria interactions, theoretical analyses revealed a high degree of pH-sensitivity, potential links between sensitivity and specific functional chemical groups, differences for source and target organisms and in sensitivity between compounds performing different interactive roles. The predicted effects for some key metabolites matched diel dynamics reported in existing literature for mesocosm and field studies. pH could therefore be hypothesised as a significant factor in mediating chemical exchange and interactions in phototrophic-heterotrophic communities by directly altering diatom and bacteria signals and metabolites. This perspective highlights how microscale pH conditions could play an influential role and provides a framework to derive focussed, testable hypotheses to assess chemical impacts on marine microbial interactions in future experiments.

Article.Title: Determinants of adherence to preoperative oral carbohydrates and short-term outcomes in pediatric congenital pulmonary airway malformation
Article.Authors: Hou S.; Liu J.; An T.; Feng L.; Yuan M.; Gong Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to assess adherence to preoperative oral carbohydrate (CHO) supplementation among pediatric patients undergoing thoracoscopic resection for congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM), and to explore potential influencing factors as well as statistical correlations between supplementation adherence and short-term postoperative outcomes. This observational study consecutively enrolled 110 pediatric patients diagnosed with CPAM who received a standardized preoperative oral carbohydrate protocol. Adherence rate was calculated using the formula: (actual consumed volume/prescribed volume) × 100%. Multivariable linear regression models were applied to screen independent predictors of supplementation adherence. Spearman’s rank correlation and multiple linear regression analyses were further performed to test statistical correlations between adherence and short-term postoperative outcomes. Preoperative CHO supplementation demonstrated good tolerance overall, with CHO-associated adverse events documented in 3.6% (4/110) of enrolled patients. The median adherence rate reached 80%, reflecting that most pediatric patients consumed most of the prescribed CHO solution. Nevertheless, merely nearly half of the participants attained the predefined exploratory cutoff value of adherence ≥ 80%. Independent positive predictors of adherence were identified as later surgical sequence, low nutritional risk screening score, and active parental care. Higher adherence levels presented a positive linear correlation with elevated caregiver satisfaction scores and fewer episodes of postoperative hunger-induced crying. Preoperative oral carbohydrate supplementation may optimize the perioperative experience for pediatric patients with CPAM and showed acceptable feasibility within this study cohort. Adjusting surgical schedules to arrange operations at later time points, implementing targeted interventions for patients at elevated nutritional risk, and strengthening parent-guided care strategies may help elevate treatment adherence. Elevated adherence was statistically associated with fewer postoperative hunger-induced crying episodes and higher caregiver satisfaction scores.

Article.Title: Cluster-aware deep learning framework for bus arrival time prediction in Indian cities
Article.Authors: Singh R.; Garg M.; Kumar B.
Article.Abstract: In transit service operations, accurate and reliable prediction of bus arrival times is essential. The accuracy of travel time prediction depends on both the quality of input data and the prediction algorithm employed. However, most reported studies have selected model inputs either arbitrarily or based on their availability rather than their suitability. In addition, most studies have evaluated prediction methods under a specific traffic and operational environment, limiting the generalizability of their findings. This study addresses these limitations by evaluating three prediction models using data from three Indian cities: Delhi, Mysore, and Surat. In Delhi and Mysore, buses operate under mixed traffic conditions, with Delhi experiencing high travel time variability and Mysore relatively low variability. In contrast, Surat operates a bus rapid transit system with dedicated bus lanes, representing a distinct operational environment. To identify significant input features, temporal analysis was used to determine the temporal features, while the deep embedded clustering algorithm was employed to exploit the spatial variations in travel times by grouping road segments with similar spatio-temporal characteristics. Separate prediction models were then developed for each cluster using long short-term memory (LSTM), convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM), and ConvLSTM with an attention mechanism. Their performance was assessed and compared to determine their suitability for cities with varying operational characteristics. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves prediction accuracy by reducing route heterogeneity and effectively capturing localized spatio-temporal patterns. The findings reveal that the proposed approach not only enhances model accuracy but also offers practical guidance on selecting appropriate prediction models based on city-specific traffic variability, contributing towards more scalable and reliable bus transit operations.

Article.Title: Evaluation of spatiotemporal patterns and uncertainty of multi-source remote sensing GPP products in the Southwest karst region of China
Article.Authors: Dong H.; Wu L.; Li X.; Zhang Y.; Luo A.; Tian F.
Article.Abstract: Accurate estimation of gross primary productivity (GPP) in the karst regions of southwestern China is important for understanding regional carbon-cycle dynamics. We evaluated five GPP products (BESS, GOSIF, GLASS, MOD17, and VPM) during 2001–2018 by comparing site-scale performance, spatial patterns, temporal variations, and relative uncertainties in karst and non-karst regions. GOSIF generally showed the strongest correlations with flux-tower-derived GPP, whereas VPM exhibited relatively low estimation errors at several sites. All products estimated lower annual mean GPP in karst regions than in non-karst regions. Monthly mean GPP was generally highest in summer and lowest in winter, with smaller karst–non-karst differences in summer. BESS, GOSIF, MOD17, and VPM showed significant increasing trends in annual mean GPP, whereas GLASS showed only a weak and non-significant increase. MOD17 had the lowest TCH-derived mean relative uncertainty, followed by VPM. Overall, product performance varied across the evaluation criteria, indicating that product selection should depend on the specific application and evaluation objective rather than on a single overall ranking. These findings provide useful support for carbon-cycle assessment and ecosystem monitoring in karst regions.

Article.Title: Alkaloids from Erythrina crista-galli flowers and their inhibitory activities against acetylcholinesterase: in vitro and in silico studies
Article.Authors: Herlina T.; Akili A.; Hardianto A.; Fajriah S.; Handayani S.; Mayanti T.; Julaeha E.; Latip J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) is a hydrolytic enzyme that breaks down acetylcholine into choline and acetate. In patients with Alzheimer’s disease, the increased AChE activity may contribute to early degeneration of cholinergic neurons in the basal forebrain, resulting in impaired cholinergic signalling. This study aims to evaluate the anticholinesterase activity of alkaloids isolated from Erythrina crista-galli flowers through an integrated approach combining in vitro and in silico studies. Four alkaloids, namely cristamidine (1), erythrinine (2), erythraline (3), and 8-oxoerythrinine (4), were isolated and their structures were confirmed through high-resolution mass spectrometry (HR-MS) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). In vitro assay conducted at a concentration of 50 µg/mL showed that cristamidine has the highest inhibition effect, followed by 8-oxoerythrinine, erythrinine, and erythraline. In silico studies comprising molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations showed that both cristamidine and 8-oxoerythrinine formed stable interactions with the active pocket of AChE. This study highlights the potential of E. crista-galli as a natural source of AChE Inhibitors.

Article.Title: Ultrasound-guided superior costotransverse ligament block versus thoracic paravertebral block for postoperative analgesia after laparoscopic nephrectomy
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Yang P.; Luo C.; Zhong Y.; Zhang X.; Liu Q.; Lan Z.; Qiu Y.
Article.Abstract: Thoracic paravertebral block (TPVB) has been investigated for analgesia after laparoscopic nephrectomy but carries a risk of pleural injury. This prospective randomized non-inferiority trial compared ultrasound-guided superior costotransverse ligament (SCTL) block with TPVB. Patients were randomized 1:1 to SCTL block or TPVB at T10, using 0.4 mL/kg of 0.5% ropivacaine, alongside standardized general anesthesia and morphine-based patient-controlled intravenous analgesia. The primary endpoint was peak cough-evoked numerical rating scale (NRS) pain two hours after skin closure. Of 78 patients screened, 76 were randomized and 72 completed per-protocol analysis (36 per group). One pneumothorax occurred in the TPVB group; none in the SCTL group. The between‑group difference (SCTL group minus TPVB group) was 0.056 (95% CI − 0.341 to 0.452) in the per‑protocol population. In the intention-to-treat analysis ( n = 76), the between‑group difference was 0.12 (95% CI − 0.27 to 0.51). Notably, both CI upper bounds fell below the predefined 1.0 non-inferiority margin, confirming the non-inferiority of the SCTL block. The small sample and low adverse-event count preclude conclusions about comparative safety. A possible reduction in pleural injury with the superficial SCTL injection target remains unproven. (ChiCTR2300075992).

Article.Title: Mine ecological assessment and prediction based on RSEI and a multi-neural-network framework
Article.Authors: Li P.; Wang B.; Guo Y.; Liang Y.; Yan J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) maps ecological quality by integrating greenness, wetness, dryness, and heat. However, because it is calculated from observations acquired at the target date, the RSEI is retrospective: it identifies ecological change after it occurs but does not itself forecast the next period. Moreover, the linear construction of RSEI through principal component analysis does not explicitly capture nonlinear temporal interactions between ecological indicators and external environmental drivers. To address these limitations, this study develops a staged convolutional neural network–long short-term memory–backpropagation neural network (CLB) framework for ecological assessment and one-step-ahead prediction in the Wangpo Mine Field, Shanxi Province, China. The framework assigns the three networks complementary roles: CNN extracts features from multivariable time series, LSTM models temporal dependence and predicts the target-period variables, and BP fuses the predicted remote-sensing indicators with climatic, topographic, and spatial variables to estimate the target-period RSEI one step ahead. Landsat-8 imagery from 2015 to 2020 was used to quantify ecological change; data from 2015 to 2019 were used for model development, and 2020 was reserved for testing. The mean RSEI increased by 12.1%, from 0.6136 to 0.6879, accompanied by an expansion of excellent-quality areas and a contraction of poor-quality areas. For the held-out 2020 data, the predicted RSEI grades were consistent with those calculated from Landsat-8 imagery, with grade-specific accuracies of 87.3–94.1%. By coupling feature extraction, temporal forecasting, and nonlinear multivariable fusion, the CLB framework may provide a methodological reference for one-step-ahead ecological-quality prediction in mining areas.

Article.Title: Corneal biometry changes with 0.01% atropine for myopia control: a randomised controlled trial and case of incidental keratoconus
Article.Authors: Soh A.; Lingham G.; Chan E.; Clark A.; Mackey D.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Changes in corneal curvature have been reported with low-concentration atropine eyedrops for myopia treatment and have been suggested to play a role in the refractive changes observed during atropine therapy. A case of keratoconus was identified from the Western Australia atropine for the treatment of myopia (WA-ATOM) cohort. We tested the null hypothesis that 0.01% atropine eyedrops produce no change in corneal parameters or ectasia risk compared to placebo. Children with progressive myopia (6–16 years; n = 153) were randomly assigned to receive 0.01% atropine eyedrops or a placebo (2:1 ratio) for 2 years, followed by a 1-year washout. Scheimpflug imaging was performed at baseline, 24-months, and 36-months. Changes in corneal parameters were compared between the treatment and placebo groups using linear mixed models. One child allocated to the treatment group developed keratoconus during the treatment phase. At 24 and 36 months, the atropine group had significantly lower BAD-D values compared to placebo, with reductions of − 0.075 (95% CI − 0.126 to − 0.023, p = 0.027) and − 0.115 (95% CI − 0.168 to − 0.063, p = 0.005) from baseline, respectively ( p = 0.029 and 0.005). At 36 months, a significant steepening of K max of + 0.301D (95% CI 0.214 to 0.389, p = 0.039) was observed in the atropine group. All other corneal parameters and cylindrical power remained similar between the groups. The case of incidental keratoconus in the treatment group (1 out of 153 children) is compatible with population prevalence rates. No signal suggesting a treatment-related increase in corneal ectatic changes was identified within the limitations of this cohort, and these findings provide reassurance from a safety perspective, but clinicians should be aware of the rare possibility of keratoconus and refer patients with suspicious corneal findings.

Article.Title: Conformal uncertainty aware prototype discovery for auditing deep chest radiograph clustering
Article.Authors: Jahanian M.; Karimi A.; Eraghi N.; Zarafshan F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep clustering can support exploratory organization of large chest-radiograph repositories, but deterministic assignments can conceal model ambiguity and apparently coherent clusters may reflect acquisition or optimization effects rather than clinically validated phenotypes. We present CUPID-Med, an uncertainty-aware prototype clustering framework combining distributional latent learning, learnable prototypes, anti-collapse regularization, and patient-disjoint split-conformal cluster sets. The evaluated implementation operates on frozen 1,024-dimensional ImageNet-pretrained DenseNet121 embeddings and uses a leakage-controlled 60/10/15/15 Train/Validation/Calibration/Test protocol on 10,000 CheXpert radiographs from 10,000 distinct patients. Model selection is restricted to Validation, and the frozen benchmark evaluates ten matched seeds in a common train-only PCA-64 geometry. On Test, CUPID-Med achieved shared-space Silhouette $$0.0403\pm 0.0041$$ , compared with 0.0440 for Spectral-kNN and 0.0429 for k -means, while yielding higher mean Silhouette than the evaluated deep representation-learning baselines. None of the 63 CUPID-Med-versus-baseline matched-seed comparisons remained significant after Holm correction, so performance differences are interpreted descriptively. At nominal 90% confidence, the primary stochastic APS procedure achieved $$0.9753\pm 0.0070$$ empirical coverage with mean set size 5.61; assignment entropy aligned with cross-seed instability ( $$\rho =0.618$$ , bootstrap 95% CI 0.581–0.652), and frozen weak-view perturbations changed hard assignments in 3.36% of Test cases on average. External evaluation on 112,120 NIH ChestXray14 images retained conservative model-relative coverage under measurable distribution shift. Across ten seeds, the metadata audit identified substantial association between cluster membership and the recorded acquisition-projection field (Cramér’s $$V=0.614\pm 0.039$$ , range 0.515–0.641). The uniformly small internal Silhouette values indicate weak absolute separation for all evaluated methods. CUPID-Med should therefore be interpreted as an exploratory framework for auditing cluster structure and assignment ambiguity, not as a diagnostic or clinically validated phenotype-discovery system.

Article.Title: Data-driven insights into stainless steel pitting corrosion through large-scale literature mining and database construction
Article.Authors: Huang Z.; Duan J.; Liu Y.; Wang C.
Article.Abstract: Pitting corrosion is one of the most prevalent and detrimental forms of localized corrosion in stainless steels exposed to chloride-containing environments. Its initiation and propagation are governed by the combined effects of alloy composition, environmental conditions, and experimental parameters. Although a substantial body of experimental data has been accumulated through decades of research, these data remain largely dispersed across the scientific literature, limiting their accessibility for large-scale statistical analyses and data-driven investigations. To address this challenge, this study proposes a large language model (LLM)-based framework for structured data extraction and database construction from scientific literature. By decomposing the complex information extraction process into multiple subtasks, including experimental condition extraction, pitting potential extraction, and data alignment, the framework enables the automated acquisition and integration of experimental data from unstructured scientific documents. Using the proposed framework, 12,792 candidate publications retrieved using a broad stainless-steel pitting corrosion search strategy were processed, resulting in a structured extraction output containing 36,095 experimental records. The database encompasses key information, including alloy compositions, environmental parameters, and pitting potentials. Stainless-steel-specific descriptive and statistical analyses were subsequently conducted using material-screened subsets of the extracted records. Data quality evaluation demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves strong aggregate performance in structured information extraction from complex scientific texts, while stage-specific validation indicates that pitting-potential extraction and normalization remain more challenging than the overall field-level extraction task. Statistical analysis of the resulting database reveals that existing studies are predominantly focused on room-temperature, neutral chloride environments, as well as austenitic and duplex stainless steel systems. Furthermore, partial correlation analysis revealed conditional associations between the investigated variables and pitting potential. Among these variables, molybdenum exhibited the strongest positive conditional association, whereas temperature showed a negative conditional association. Chloride ion concentration showed only a weak negative association. These trends were generally consistent with established corrosion knowledge and therefore provided a scientific plausibility check for the statistical patterns observed in the constructed database. This work highlights the potential of large language models for knowledge extraction and automated database construction from corrosion-related scientific literature. The proposed framework provides a reusable data resource and technical pathway for corrosion informatics research, while establishing a foundation for future data-driven studies on corrosion mechanism discovery, performance prediction, and materials design.

Article.Title: Exercise self-efficacy plays a mediating role between social support and physical function among patients transferred from the intensive care unit
Article.Authors: Yin M.; Li G.; Wang Y.; Li Z.; Yang Q.; Zhang G.; Ji R.
Article.Abstract: Physical impairment is common after critical illness and may hinder recovery and quality of life. Social support has been associated with physical function among intensive care unit (ICU) survivors, but the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. Exercise self-efficacy may help explain this relationship. This study examined the association between social support and physical function among patients transferred from the ICU and investigated the potential mediating role of exercise self-efficacy. This cross-sectional study included 300 patients transferred from the ICU between July 2025 and March 2026. Social support, exercise self-efficacy, and physical function were assessed using the Social Support Rating Scale, Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale, and Short Physical Performance Battery, respectively. Spearman’s rank correlation, multiple linear regression, and mediation analyses using PROCESS Model 4 were performed. Indirect effects were estimated using 5,000 bootstrap samples with 95% confidence intervals. The median SPPB score was 2 (2, 4). Correlation analysis showed that physical function was positively correlated with exercise self-efficacy ( r = 0.319, P < 0.001) and social support ( r = 0.183, P = 0.005). Regression analysis identified exercise self-efficacy as a factor significantly associated with better physical function. Mediation analysis showed that the total effect of social support on physical function was 0.190 (95% CI: 0.078–0.302). The indirect effect of exercise self-efficacy was 0.051 (95% CI: 0.020–0.092). Social support was positively associated with physical function among patients transferred from the ICU, with exercise self-efficacy accounting for part of this association. Interventions targeting social support and exercise self-efficacy may be worth exploring as potential strategies to support physical recovery after critical illness.

Article.Title: Latent profiles of health science communication competency and associated factors among geriatric nurses in Beijing: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Wang Y.; Zhang Q.; Wang S.; Piao Y.
Article.Abstract: Geriatric nurses are well positioned to translate clinical knowledge into usable health information for older adults; however, evidence on their health science communication competency and its heterogeneity remains limited. This study examined competency levels, latent profiles, and associated factors among geriatric nurses in Beijing. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in Beijing, China, from November to December 2025. In total, 537 valid questionnaires were analyzed. Health science communication competency, general self-efficacy, and perceived organizational support were assessed using validated instruments. Latent profile analysis (LPA) identified competency profiles, and three-step (R3STEP) multinomial logistic regression examined factors associated with profile membership. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in Beijing, China, from November to December 2025. In total, 537 valid questionnaires were analyzed. Health science communication competency, general self-efficacy, and perceived organizational support were assessed using validated instruments. Latent profile analysis (LPA) identified competency profiles, and three-step (R3STEP) multinomial logistic regression examined factors associated with profile membership. The mean overall competency score was 180.11 ± 29.19, and content creation showed the lowest mean item score (4.19 ± 0.80). LPA supported a three-profile solution: low ( n = 59, 11.0%), middle ( n = 238, 44.3%), and high ( n = 240, 44.7%). Higher self-efficacy and greater instrumental organizational support were associated with lower odds of belonging to the low- and middle-competency profiles relative to the high-competency profile. Compared with willingness to participate, unwillingness and neutral willingness were associated with higher odds of belonging to the low-competency profile, while neutral willingness was also associated with higher odds of belonging to the middle-competency profile. In this Beijing sample of geriatric nurses, health science communication competency was moderate to high, and the three profiles primarily reflected overall competency levels. Content creation was relatively lowest, although differences across domains were modest. These findings may inform level-informed capacity-building strategies.

Article.Title: Mechanical load modulates premovement cortical activity during voluntary upper limb movement
Article.Authors: Bhagat V.; Yadav R.; Ghosh S.; Muthukrishnan S.; Roy S.; Dobbins C.; Bo A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Examining how scalp electroencephalography (EEG) activity changes under increasing motor demands may provide insights into how the brain prepares for movement. In this exploratory study, premovement EEG activity was examined in ten healthy male participants (n = 10) performing a unilateral bicep curl task. Cue-locked EEG signals preceding kinematically defined movement onset were analyzed using complementary event-related potential analysis (ERP), time–frequency analysis (TF), and cross-frequency coupling analyses to examine load-dependent EEG responses. As mechanical load increased, premovement EEG activity exhibited temporal, frequency-specific, and spatially distributed changes. Mixed-effects analyses indicated that the relationship between graded mechanical load and premovement EEG activity was better described by a non-linear than a linear model. These differences were pronounced at higher load levels and exhibited non-linear and frequency-specific patterns across the frontal, central, and contralateral sensorimotor scalp regions. These findings provide preliminary insights into how increasing mechanical demand is associated with frequency-specific, spatially distributed, and non-linear changes in premovement EEG activity before movement onset.

Article.Title: Cost-aware evaluation of time-series foundation models for urban air-quality and temperature forecasting
Article.Authors: Fahim M.; Karim M.
Article.Abstract: Cities with the greatest need for hyper-local air-quality and weather forecasts often have the shortest data records and the tightest compute budgets. The usual responses, searching for a tiny architecture or transferring from data-rich cities, assume foundation models are too heavy, an assumption more often adopted than tested. Across 29 cities and two domains (hourly PM2.5 and 2 m temperature), under pre-specified protocols with measured energy and a cost-adjusted decision rule, we compare all three. On PM2.5 three zero-shot foundation models spanning two families and a 4.3-fold size range are statistically indistinguishable from the tuned specialist in mean absolute scaled error (MASE 0.659-0.662 vs. 0.692 under deployable causal covariates) and formally equivalent to one another. The specialist’s apparent temperature edge (0.533 vs. 0.792) depends heavily on covariate timing: 0.638 with covariates carrying measured 24-h forecast error, 0.745 with only values knowable at the forecast origin. Perfect foresight therefore distorts the cross-domain comparison, as it can in any benchmark using future covariates. Transfer learning never significantly beats zero-shot at any budget. Under frequent retraining the untrained model uses roughly ten times less measured energy, though a once-trained specialist eventually amortizes. Where models are refreshed often, downloading one now matches training one.

Article.Title: Concurrent use of NaHCO3 and NH4Cl for synthesis of ZnO–Al2O3 nanocomposite and investigation of its adsorption property
Article.Authors: Shiasi M.; Saffar A.; Ahangar H.
Article.Abstract: The utilization of the adsorption capability of semiconducting materials plays a pivotal role in the treatment of industrial effluents. In the present study, ZnO–Al 2 O 3 binary nanocomposites with varying weight ratios were synthesized via the co-precipitation method. The synthesized nanocomposites were characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), simultaneous thermal analysis (STA), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) to elucidate their functional groups, crystal structure, and morphological features. The experimental results demonstrated that the concurrent use of bicarbonate and ammonium significantly influenced the morphology of the nanocomposites and, consequently, their adsorption performance. Furthermore, with increasing ZnO content, the morphology of the nanocomposites evolved from platelet-like to aggregated structures. Under the optimized conditions of pH = 5, initial dye concentration of 10 mg L −1 , and a nanocomposite dosage of 0.02 g (40 wt% Al 2 O 3 –60 wt% ZnO), a maximum methyl orange removal efficiency of 98% was achieved.

Article.Title: Monolithically integrated photonic beamforming for a phased array receiver antenna
Article.Authors: Rama L.; Rodrigues C.; Santos J.; Vaz D.; Rodrigues F.; Teixeira A.; Varum T.; Nogueira R.; Drummond M.
Article.Abstract: We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first monolithically integrated RF-in/IF-out photonic beamformer for a phased-array receiver antenna, fabricated on an \(8\times 4~\text {mm}^2\) Indium Phosphide die. The beamformer is designed to receive four input RF signals and one RF local oscillator, convert them to the optical domain, apply complex weighting, and down-convert the added signals to a beamformed IF output. The presented photonic beamformer is enabled by a novel laser generation stage requiring no isolation, injection locking, or optical filtering. A conversion loss of 79 dB was measured, primarily dominated by lossy passive devices. Despite the significant conversion loss, beamforming was demonstrated for three beam orientations, \(0^\circ\) and \(\pm 30^\circ\) , for \(f_{\text {RF}}=10\) GHz, \(f_{\text {LO}}=14\) GHz and \(f_{\text {IF}}=4\) GHz, using three out of four designed channels, and considering a virtual linear phased array antenna receiver.

Article.Title: The impact of a synchronized multimodal AI interface configuration on consumer experience journey and satisfaction
Article.Authors: Pan Z.
Article.Abstract: With the rapid integration of multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) into digital interfaces, understanding how combined visual, auditory, and textual cues influence consumers' experience journeys and satisfaction has become critically important for both scholars and practitioners. While prior research has examined individual modalities in isolation, the comparative effects of a specific rich multimodal interface configuration versus a minimal-modality baseline across different stages of the consumer journey remain underexplored. This study draws on cue utilization theory, presence theory, and the customer journey framework to investigate how exposure to a synchronized multimodal AI interface (text + voice + animated avatar) versus a text-only interface affects consumer satisfaction through three experimentally induced journey stages: search, evaluation, and post-purchase. A between-subjects online experiment (N = 320 recruited; 312 retained after screening) was conducted using a simulated e-commerce platform where participants interacted with an AI shopping assistant featuring either text-only or synchronized text-voice-avatar cues. Results from SEM indicate that the synchronized multimodal interface was associated with higher perceived diagnosticity and immersion, which in turn were related to higher satisfaction across all three stages. The configuration–satisfaction contrast was largest for evaluation satisfaction (Cohen’s d = 1.58, 95% CI [1.33, 1.83]); the indirect-effect patterns via perceived diagnosticity and immersion were statistically consistent with, but not demonstrative of, the proposed pathways. We emphasize that the two conditions differ not only in synchronization but also in modality count, anthropomorphic cues, and social presence; accordingly, all findings are interpreted as pertaining to the interface configuration as a whole, not to integration quality as an isolated construct. Theoretical contributions include extending cue utilization theory in the form of a speculative conjecture and identifying stage-specific patterns. Managerial implications suggest that e-commerce platforms should consider synchronized multimodal cue design, particularly during product comparison phases in simulated and early deployment contexts, and should be regarded as preliminary pending field validation.

Article.Title: Meteorological forecasting of respiratory diseases incidence with geospatial and machine learning methods
Article.Authors: Arroquia-Cuadros B.; Marqués-Mateu Á.; Fdez-Arroyabe P.; Sebastia L.
Article.Abstract: Weather conditions play a significant role in shaping human health, particularly in the incidence of respiratory diseases. This study proposes a workflow to predict hospital admissions related to respiratory conditions by integrating heterogeneous environmental and health data sources. A 15-year time series of meteorological data was combined with geographic and demographic information to derive biometeorological indices associated with hypoxia and hyperoxia. To account for spatial variability, three clustering techniques—k-means, Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), and Spatial ’K’luster Analysis by Tree Edge Removal (SKATER)—were applied to define intra-provincial regions for targeted data extraction from raster models. These approaches were compared with conventional aggregation at the provincial level. Interpretable machine learning models, specifically tree-based algorithms, were used to evaluate predictive performance. The proposed spatial clustering strategies achieved comparable or improved performance relative to the baseline approach. Experiments conducted in three Spanish provinces (Cantabria, Madrid, and Valencia) yielded mean absolute errors ranging from approximately 5.4 to 8.2 cases per million inhabitants, depending on the province. Results highlight the relevance of spatially refined environmental data in improving predictive accuracy. The integration of geospatial data, meteorological models, and machine learning provides an effective framework for forecasting respiratory disease incidence. This approach supports the development of early warning systems and risk management strategies based on environmental monitoring. In this article we present how to gather, transform and model datasets from several data sources to predict hospital admissions of respiratory diseases. We also draw the importance of geographical distribution of population in order to determine the appropriate method to extract meteorological data.

Article.Title: CDA-YOLO: an improved YOLOv11 model for PCB defect detection
Article.Authors: Yuan A.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Printed circuit boards (PCBs) are fundamental to modern electronic systems, and their manufacturing quality directly determines the performance and reliability of the final product. However, existing YOLO‑based defect detection models still face critical challenges, including high miss rates for tiny defects and frequent false positives caused by complex background textures. To address these issues, we propose CDA‑YOLO, an enhanced YOLOv11 framework incorporating three key innovations. First, a Cross-level Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (CBiFPN) is designed, which effectively alleviates the loss of fine-grained details of small targets as features propagate through deep layers. Second, a lightweight Dual-Scale Convolution module (DualScaleConv) is proposed, which employs a parallel branch structure to simultaneously capture local details and global contextual information. Finally, a parameter-free average attention mechanism (PfAAM) is integrated into the C3k2 module to enhance the feature response in defect-related regions and suppresses background noise. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves competitive performance on the PCB defect dataset, with mAP@0.5 reaching 96.1% and mAP@0.5:0.95 reaching 56.0%, corresponding to improvements of 2.8% and 3.4% over the baseline YOLOv11, respectively. These results validate that CDA-YOLO offers an efficient and robust solution for industrial-grade PCB defect detection.

Article.Title: Advancing automatic classification of single fine particles via multimodal deep learning framework
Article.Authors: Khadgi J.; Lee H.; Park K.; Choi S.; Kim Y.; Shin H.; Park K.
Article.Abstract: The accurate identification and classification of single fine particles are essential for understanding emission sources, atmospheric processes, and their subsequent impacts on climate and health. However, this task remains challenging due to the highly diverse and overlapping physicochemical characteristics of various particle types. Conventional single particle analysis relies heavily on manual interpretation, which is inherently slow, subjective, and limited in scalability. To overcome these limitations, this study implemented a multimodal deep learning fusion framework that classifies fine particles into seven distinct types: dust (206), fly ash (64), metals (164), organic-rich (551), sea spray (91), soot (299), and sulfur-rich (247), by simultaneously fusing three modalities (morphology, size, and elemental composition). A comprehensive dataset of 1,622 single particles, collected from diverse emission sources and ambient environments, was utilized for model development and evaluation. Three multimodal fusion strategies were systematically evaluated: early fusion (concatenating all modalities at an early stage), traditional joint fusion (integrating independently extracted features), and attention-based fusion (dynamically focusing on the most informative features within and across modalities). The attention-based fusion architecture achieved the highest predictive performance, yielding an overall accuracy of 89.6%, a sensitivity of 0.90, and a specificity of 0.98. Furthermore, an interpretability analysis revealed that the model’s classification decisions were predominantly governed by distinctive elemental composition and morphological patterns. By rapidly classifying thousands of individual particles within minutes, this automated, high-throughput framework provides a highly scalable solution for single-particle analysis, thereby facilitating a more profound understanding of atmospheric aerosol sources, transformation mechanisms, and their broader climate and health impacts.

Article.Title: A calibrated-domain DEM–machine learning assessment of asphalt concrete stiffness and micromechanical response
Article.Authors: Imoh U.; Movahedi Rad M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Asphalt concrete is a heterogeneous composite whose stiffness and damage response depend on aggregate contacts, binder-mediated bonding, air voids, force chain evolution, and progressive bond failure. This study presents a calibrated-domain assessment of an AC-16C mixture using three two-dimensional Discrete Element Method contact/bond formulations: the linear parallel bond, soft-bond, and contact-bond models, together with a machine-learning stiffness surrogate. The 160 records constitute a hybrid laboratory–DEM/parametric dataset within a single AC-16C domain, rather than 160 physically distinct mixtures. The DEM outputs were used to interpret the contact forces, particle displacement, bond breakage, coordination number, energy dissipation, and fracture localization. The Linear Parallel Bond Model produced the stiffest response because it transferred both force and moment; the Soft-Bond Model represented gradual softening and energy dissipation and the Contact-Bond Model exhibited earlier localized bond failure. The machine learning models used uniaxial compressive strength, indirect tensile strength, dynamic modulus, and Poisson’s ratio to predict the experimental elastic modulus; DEM-derived descriptors were not included as predictors. Using a 112/24/24 training, validation, and holdout partition, Random Forest and XGBoost achieved holdout R 2 values of 0.940 and 0.928, respectively, whereas the ANN/MLP was less stable, with an R 2 of 0.847. Because the dynamic modulus dominated the feature importance, the high predictive accuracy primarily reflected the stiffness-variable collinearity within the calibrated domain. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as internal calibrated-domain interpolation rather than external validation or evidence of a general microstructure–property relationship. Broader application requires physically independent mixtures, complete DEM reproducibility information, three-dimensional verification, raw data disclosure, and measured runtime comparisons.

Article.Title: In situ evaluation of 3D polymeric microstructures integrated into a microfluidic channel
Article.Authors: Rekštytė Paipulienė S.; Paipulas D.; Mizeikis V.
Article.Abstract: We investigate the applicability of photoluminescence (PL) mapping technique for in situ evaluation of the polymeric microstructures fabricated by direct laser writing in pre-polymers (DLW-PP), both in open and closed (fully three-dimensional) microfluidic channels, where conventional characterization is often challenging. The technique utilizes quenching of photo-initiator emission in polymerized regions, enabling visualization of fabricated features prior to development. PL mapping enables accurate three-dimensional localization before sample development and can be repeatedly applied during fabrication without damaging the structures. The detected PL signal consistently exhibits a footprint smaller than the final developed structure. These results extend the applicability of PL mapping to fused silica microfluidic platforms and demonstrate its potential as a practical in situ tool for monitoring, alignment, and quality assessment of DLW-PP-fabricated microstructures.

Article.Title: Sensor-fused EKF-based navigation and kinematic modelling of a remotely controlled mobility vehicle in GPS denied agricultural environments
Article.Authors: Patle R.; Sahni R.; Ravuri S.; Harshavardhan K.; Saroj S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate row-following is essential for precision agricultural operations such as fertilizer application, inter-row cultivation, and site-specific crop management. However, reliable navigation in agricultural fields remains challenging under GPS-denied conditions caused by dense crop canopy, uneven terrain, and environmental disturbances. This study presents the development and validation of a low-cost sensor-fusion navigation framework for a remotely controlled agricultural mobility vehicle operating in GPS-denied environments. The system integrates wheel encoders and an inertial measurement unit within an extended kalman filter (EKF) for vehicle-state estimation, while ultrasonic sensing is used independently for obstacle detection and occupancy-grid mapping. A differential-drive kinematic model was employed for vehicle motion estimation, while Dijkstra-based path planning and closed-loop trajectory tracking enabled navigation during straight-row traversal and headland turning. Simulation studies in Gazebo and SolidWorks validated the kinematic behaviour and navigation performance before field implementation. Field experiments demonstrated that odometry-only navigation resulted in lateral-deviation RMSE values greater than 0.40 m, whereas the EKF-based framework achieved lateral-deviation RMSE values of 0.031 m for straight-row trials and 0.034 m for headland U-turn trials relative to an independent taut-line reference under the tested GPS-denied maize-field conditions. These results demonstrate consistent row-following and navigation performance under the tested field conditions.

Article.Title: Making informal religious representations visible in Japanese YouTube comments on Apple’s Crush advertisement
Article.Authors: Tsunematsu A.; Komiya A.; Takano R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While formal religious representations have long been a central focus in psychology and cognitive science, informal religious representations remain understudied because their religious dimension is often embedded in everyday practices, values, and norms. This study examines how such representations may become visible in language on social media, focusing on Japan. We analyzed over 7,000 Japanese- and English-language YouTube comments on news coverage of Apple’s 2024 “Crush!” advertisement, which was criticized in Japan as conflicting with beliefs and values concerning respect for objects. Using a combination of dictionary-based and topic modeling approaches, we examined how emotion- and religion-related language appeared across linguistic contexts. The results showed that, in Japanese-language comments, terms related to respect for objects (e.g., mottainai ) appeared in topics linked to both religion-related and negative emotional language. A comparable pattern was not observed in the English-language corpus, although emotional expressions were prominent in these comments. Together, these findings suggest that informal religious representations can surface in everyday digital discourse through expressions concerning respect for objects that, in some contexts, carry religious resonance.

Article.Title: Prevalence of 406 rare diseases by ethnicity and recorded COVID-19 infection rates among 62.5 million people in England
Article.Authors: Gu Q.; Hasheminasab S.; Pineda-Moncusí M.; Chilala C.; Thygesen J.; Wu H.; Khalid S.; N/A N/A.; Coombe A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rare diseases (RD) are individually uncommon but collectively affect millions of people. Yet national estimates of their prevalence, especially across ethnic groups, are limited, and how the COVID-19 pandemic affected people with RD across ethnic groups is unknown. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of 406 RD by ethnicity, and to describe recorded COVID-19 infection across these RD and ethnic groups, in England. We conducted a cross-sectional study within the National Health Service (NHS) England Secure Data Environment, accessed via the British Heart Foundation (BHF) Data Science Centre’s CVD-COVID-UK/COVID-IMPACT Consortium, linking primary care, hospital, and mortality records for individuals alive on 31 July 2023. We calculated age- and sex-standardised prevalence for 406 RD, and recorded COVID-19 infection rates for the overall group, for each RD, and across the six-group Office for National Statistics (ONS) and 19-group NHS ethnicity classifications. Of 62.5 million people, 1.05 million (1.7%) had at least one of the 406 RD. Recorded COVID-19 infection was higher in the RD group than in the non-RD population (32.8% vs. 29.0%). Within the RD group, infection rates varied by ethnicity (e.g. 27.7% in the Pakistani and 23.8% in the Black African groups, versus 33.7% in the White British group) and by specific RD (24.6–41.2% among the 25 most common). Age- and sex-standardised prevalence also varied widely across ethnic groups, with substantial heterogeneity emerging only when broad categories were disaggregated into the more granular NHS classifications (for example, markedly elevated discoid lupus erythematosus prevalence in Black Caribbean but not Black African individuals, obscured within the aggregate “Black” category). This national, ethnicity-resolved map shows that rare-disease prevalence varies substantially across ethnic groups, with differences largely hidden within broad categories, and that recorded COVID-19 infection among people with RD varied across ethnic groups, with the highest rates observed in the ONS White and NHS White British groups. These findings provide a baseline to support earlier, fairer diagnosis and more targeted care.

Article.Title: Integrating bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify mitochondrial quality control-related key genes in rheumatoid arthritis
Article.Authors: Xiao Y.; zhang J.; Su J.; Wu J.
Article.Abstract: Mitochondrial quality control (MQC) dysfunction contributes to rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but MQC-related genes in RA remain incompletely characterized. We integrated two bulk blood transcriptomic datasets and one peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset (248 RA and 88 control bulk samples; 11,719 cells from 3 RA and 3 healthy donors). Weighted gene co-expression network and differential expression analyses, combined with three machine-learning algorithms, identified candidate genes. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, regulatory network, single-cell, cell–cell communication, pseudotime, metabolic, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) analyses were performed. Nine MQC-related candidate genes were identified; CDC42 and RBBP7 emerged as key genes, with CDC42 upregulated and RBBP7 downregulated in RA. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) linked CDC42 to JAK–STAT signaling, while translation initiation showed opposite enrichment patterns. After multiple-testing correction, 15 immune-cell subsets differed between RA and controls; monocytes positively correlated with CDC42 and negatively with RBBP7. Single-cell analysis showed relatively high RBBP7 expression in B cells, motivating exploratory analyses of B-cell trajectories, metabolism, and predicted CCL5–CCR1 communication with monocytes. RT-qPCR confirmed the mRNA expression patterns. These findings identify CDC42 and RBBP7 as MQC-related key genes associated with distinct immune and metabolic features in blood-derived samples from patients with RA.

Article.Title: Adaptive entropy-guided access point selection for robust multi-floor Wi-Fi fingerprinting
Article.Authors: Bahy El-Din A.; Nafea H.; Samra A.; Abozied M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wi-Fi fingerprinting is widely used for indoor localization. Although a large number of observable access points (APs) can provide richer spatial information, retaining all APs introduces significant computational overhead, increased scanning latency, and reduced generalization under heterogeneity across floors, devices, and contexts. This paper presents an entropy-guided dimensionality reduction framework that selects the most informative APs while preserving localization accuracy. First, each AP is ranked using Shannon entropy computed from its empirical RSSI distribution. The approach is evaluated on the multi-floor JUIndoorLoc dataset (172 AP features, three floors, four devices, and multiple contextual conditions) using a Random Forest classifier with stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and robustness is further assessed under additive RSSI noise and random AP dropouts. Across floors, the proposed adaptive entropy selection achieves substantial dimensionality reduction with negligible accuracy loss: it selects 17 APs on F3 ( $$\approx $$ 90.11% reduction) with only $$-0.41\%$$ accuracy change, 8 APs on F4 ( $$\approx $$ 95.34% reduction) with $$-0.51\%$$ change, and 26 APs on F5 ( $$\approx $$ 84.88% reduction) with $$-0.42\%$$ accuracy loss compared to the baseline configuration using all APs. Robustness experiments show that entropy-based selection can improve resilience under measurement noise on certain floors (e.g., on F5, at $$\sigma $$ =1–3 dB the selected subset achieves 0.8472/0.7748/0.7070 versus 0.7674/0.7084/0.6659 for using all APs), while also revealing floor-dependent trade-offs where extremely compact subsets may become more noise-sensitive under strong perturbations. Overall, the proposed adaptive entropy framework provides a lightweight, floor-aware AP selection mechanism that reduces inference cost and scanning burden while maintaining competitive accuracy and improving robustness in realistic degradation scenarios. The generalizability of these findings to more complex and dynamic real-world environments warrants further investigation.

Article.Title: Comparative performance analysis of adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system, fuzzy logic, and neural network-based maximum power point tracking controllers for permanent magnet synchronous generator-based variable-speed wind energy conversion systems
Article.Authors: Hadush G.; Gebremariam S.; Meresa S.; Alemu B.
Article.Abstract: In this study, the performance of MPPT based Fuzzy Logic Controllers (FLC), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) for a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based variable speed wind energy conversion system (WECS) is evaluated. Controllers are designed in MATLAB/Simulink and subjected to stepwise and time-varying wind speed settings to determine mechanical power extraction, boosted peak voltage, transient response, voltage regulation and steady-state stability. The stepwise wind speed is changed from 5 to 12 m/s and then to 9 and 10 m/s to assess the controller performance under dynamic operating conditions. The results show that all three intelligent controllers are able to successfully track the maximum power operating point, extracting 16.8 kW under the examined conditions, and get a maximum power coefficient of \(C_p=0.48\) . But large differences are observed in their electrical and dynamic responses. ANFIS achieves the best overall performance with maximum boosted voltage of 600 V and steady state DC-link voltage of 480 V with minimum oscillation. It also has the best damping properties, fastest transient response and least settling time compared with FLC and ANN. FLC provides intermediate dynamic performance with less computing complexity. ANN has relatively strong transient oscillations and longest settling response. The results demonstrate that ANFIS offers better dynamic stability and voltage regulation while all three controllers deliver similar maximum power extraction. Thus, ANFIS is proposed as a promising intelligent MPPT technique to enhance the performance and reliability of PMSG based variable-speed WECS under fast varying wind conditions.
