Article.Title: An interpretable model for efficient and robust runoff forecasting via causal-linear attention and adaptive KAN decoding
Article.Authors: Tian W.; Cheng L.; Wang W.
Article.Abstract: Accurate runoff prediction is essential for water resources management, flood control, and disaster mitigation. However, existing deep learning models often face challenges in efficiently modeling long sequences, representing nonlinear runoff responses, and providing interpretable predictions. To address these issues, this study proposes LiTKAN, a hybrid runoff forecasting model integrating Temporal Causal Encoding (TCE), Global Linear Attention (GLA), and a KAN-based Nonlinear Decoder (KND). The proposed model combines temporal information representation, efficient long-range dependency modeling, and adaptive nonlinear mapping. Specifically, TCE incorporates temporal structural information into runoff sequences; GLA reduces the computational complexity of attention-based dependency modeling from O(N²) to O(N), enabling efficient long-sequence feature extraction; and KND employs learnable B-spline basis functions to characterize nonlinear runoff responses and provide data-driven interpretability. To evaluate LiTKAN under different forecasting configurations, this study conducted experiments across dual temporal scales and four representative basins with different hydrological characteristics, including multi-source meteorological-driven forecasting and univariate runoff forecasting scenarios. Results show that LiTKAN achieved competitive prediction performance under the evaluated conditions, with NSE values ranging from 0.878 to 0.994 across the four basins. The model also demonstrated improved representation of extreme runoff variations compared with baseline models. In terms of computational efficiency, the linear attention mechanism reduced runtime and GPU memory consumption compared with the standard Transformer while maintaining high prediction accuracy. Ablation experiments and interpretability analyses revealed that different model components contribute differently under different forecasting scenarios, and the nonlinear response patterns extracted by KND were generally consistent with known hydrological characteristics. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of integrating efficient sequence modeling, nonlinear representation, and data-driven interpretability for multi-timescale runoff forecasting.

Article.Title: Appropriate load assortment in multiple receiver WPT system driven at receiver’s critical limit
Article.Authors: Mohanty P.; Biswal S.; Kar D.; Bhuyan S.
Article.Abstract: Magnetic coupling based Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technology is appealing currently due to its potential in delivering power concurrently to multiple receivers. But in the multiple-receiver WPT system, the power level at the individual load decreases by increasing number of receiver loads. Thus, there is a critical limit to the number of receivers which supposed to be driven with predetermined amount of power for specific input power level. The current research is intended to exploit further the optimal load value under the given critical limit for similar load situation in multiple receiver WPT system. To corroborate the concept, the equivalent circuit model analysis of a series-series (SS) compensated n-receivers WPT system has been presented. The analysis reveals the essential parameters such as delivered load power to individual receiver and overall power transfer efficiency of the multiple receiver WPT system under similar load situation. It is well noticed from the results that there exists a unique combination between the numbers of receiver loads and the load value which needs to be maintained for enrichment of the system efficiency. Any deviation from this optimal load value corresponding to load’s critical limit results deterioration in the efficiency of the system. The inferences supported by both theoretical simulation and experimental tests are crucial in the development of a multi-receiver WPT system.

Article.Title: Architecture diverse TabNet ensemble for crop type classification using harmonized multisource soil data
Article.Authors: Buriboev A.; Abror A.; Narzullo M.; Fayzullo N.; Yusuf Y.; Buriboyev S.; Bazarbaev M.; Abduvaytov A.; Achilov G.; Kuvandikov J.; Indiaminov R.; Jeon H.; Lee C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate analysis of heterogeneous soil records can support data-driven agricultural planning, but integrating datasets from different laboratories and public repositories introduces challenges related to inconsistent units, source-dependent distributions, missing values, duplicate observations, and potential information leakage. This study proposes ADWTabNet, an architecture-diverse TabNet ensemble for multiclass crop-type classification using harmonized multi-source soil data. The integrated dataset contained 18,237 observations representing seven crop classes and a broad set of chemical, physical, microbiological, and categorical soil properties. The proposed framework combines unit standardization, duplicate control, source-distribution harmonization, separate categorical and numerical imputation, tree-structured Parzen estimator-based hyperparameter optimization, structurally diverse TabNet models, probability-level ensemble fusion, calibration assessment, and attention-based interpretation. Under the evaluated stratified holdout protocol, XGBoost achieved a test accuracy of 0.8724 and a macro F1-score of 0.8670. Baseline TabNet improved these values to 0.8863 and 0.8822, respectively, while the TPE-optimized TabNet reached an accuracy of 0.8951 and reduced log loss from 0.3325 to 0.2566. The proposed ADWTabNet ensemble obtained the best reported performance, with a test accuracy of 0.9053, macro F1-score of 0.9025, weighted F1-score of 0.9050, macro ROC–AUC of 0.9930, and normalized multiclass Brier score of 0.0193. Repeated-run evaluation confirmed a stable advantage over the optimized individual TabNet, whereas the difference between validation-weighted and equal architecture-diverse averaging was not statistically significant. Aggregated TabNet attention ranked humus, phosphorus, electrical conductivity, nitrogen, and pH among the leading predictors, and this ranking was independently supported by permutation-importance analysis. These findings demonstrate improved crop-type classification within the evaluated integrated multi-source dataset. However, external validation using previously unseen laboratories and geographic regions is required before broader transferability can be established.

Article.Title: Investigation of the dosimetric characteristics of real-time silicone/Bi2O3 nanocomposites for the diagnostic level X-rays
Article.Authors: Keyvani F.; Gholamzadeh L.; Malekie S.; Kashian S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents the development of high-sensitivity real-time X-ray dosimeters based on room-temperature-vulcanized (RTV-2) silicone nanocomposites incorporating 0–60 wt% Bi 2 O 3 nanoparticles, fabricated via solution casting. Structural and morphological characterization using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) with elemental mapping, and elemental analysis confirmed the uniform dispersion of monoclinic Bi 2 O 3 nanorods within the amorphous RTV-2 matrix. Complementary Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) validated the chemical integrity, thermal stability, and mechanical robustness of the resulting nanocomposites. Dosimetric performance was investigated under diagnostic-range X-ray exposure using a COMET MXR 320/26 source (dose rates: 2.8–12 mGy/min). The I-V characteristics at 4.8 mGy/min exhibited a highly linear response over ± 400 V. At 400 V, the photocurrent increased from ~ 0.56 nA (pure RTV-2) to ~ 1.66 nA (60 wt% Bi 2 O 3 ), corresponding to a ~ 3-fold enhancement in photocurrent. The devices demonstrated good short-term repeatability (standard deviation of 2.3% over ten consecutive measurements) and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of up to ~ 1900 at 400 V. Compared with reported values for commercial MOSFET dosimeters (~ 0.1–1 nA/mGy) and previously reported Bi 2 O 3 -polymer systems, the developed nanocomposites exhibit a higher competitive normalized sensitivity (~ 0.35 nA/(mGy/min), or 878 nC·mGy⁻ 1 ·cm⁻ 3 on a volumetric basis), demonstrating their suitability as lead-free alternatives for low-dose, real-time diagnostic X-ray dosimetry; further evaluation of long-term stability and mechanical durability is needed to establish clinical applicability.

Article.Title: Inhibitory characteristics of a surfactant-enhanced sodium salt inhibitor for coal spontaneous combustion
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Chuai Y.; Li J.; Huo J.
Article.Abstract: Sodium-salt-based physical inhibitors reduce coal–oxygen interactions through moisture absorption and retention in the prevention of coal spontaneous combustion, but their wetting and spreading performance on coal surfaces can be further improved. To enhance the overall inhibition performance of sodium-salt-based inhibitors, the anionic surfactant sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) was introduced to modify the sodium chloride (NaCl) inhibition system, and the optimal composite inhibitor formulation was selected through experimental characterization and comprehensive evaluation using the entropy weight method. The results showed that SDS further enhanced the moisture-regulation capacity of the NaCl system. The coal sample treated with 20% NaCl + 0.15% SDS exhibited an average water absorption of 15.45 g and an average mass loss of 4.76 g during the moisture desorption stage, representing a 99% increase and a 59% decrease, respectively, compared with the sample treated with 20% NaCl alone. Meanwhile, oxygen consumption and CO generation were effectively reduced and suppressed, respectively. Contact-angle and FTIR results showed that SDS improved coal–liquid interfacial wettability, while different inhibitor treatments altered the relative functional-group composition and chemical environment of coal. SDS promoted the wetting, spreading, and effective contact of the NaCl solution on coal surfaces, while the hygroscopic and hydration effects of NaCl enhanced moisture retention, thereby weakening coal–oxygen interactions and retarding low-temperature oxidation. Comprehensive evaluation using the entropy weight method identified 20% NaCl + 0.15% SDS as the optimal formulation. These results provide a reference for formulation optimization and parameter design of surfactant-enhanced sodium-salt inhibitors.

Article.Title: miR-770 as a potential regulator of DNA methylation-related gene expression in glioblastoma: from in silico prediction to functional validation
Article.Authors: Rahemi M.; Mosleh I.; Oraee-Yazdani S.; Nazparvar B.; Mehrabadi M.; Kouhkan F.; Kehtari M.
Article.Abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) remains one of the most aggressive and treatment-resistant brain tumors, in part due to its molecular heterogeneity and dysregulated epigenetic landscape. In this study, the potential tumor-suppressive role of miR-770 and its association with aberrant DNA methylation in GBM was investigated. Using bulk RNA sequencing data from The Cancer Genome Atlas and The Genotype-Tissue Expression, we performed differential expression analysis and introduced a set of genes as methylation-related differentially expressed genes (methylation-DEGs); these are genes involved in DNA methylation and differentially expressed in GBM. Subsequently, employing weighted gene co-expression network analysis, miR-770 was identified as a key microRNA in DNA methylation in GBM progression. Expression analysis confirmed the downregulation of miR-770 in GBM tissues and its co-expression with methylation-related genes, including DNMT1 , UHRF1 , PCNA , and HDAC1 . Functional assays in the U251 glioma cell line revealed that miR-770 overexpression led to reduced cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while promoting apoptosis. Notably, the co-expression of miR-770 with methylation-related genes was also validated in U251 cells. Taken together, our findings suggest that miR-770 represent a regulator of DNA methylation-related gene expression networks in GBM.

Article.Title: Hybrid dual attentional-based pyramidal deep learning model for liver tumor detection
Article.Authors: Patil B.; Veerashetty S.
Article.Abstract: Liver tumors are life-threatening diseases that occur due to the rapid growth of liver cells and even result in a chronic condition. Nevertheless, conventional liver tumor detection struggled with the limitations of poor robustness, difficulties in identifying the complex boundaries, and inconsistent segmentation. Hence, the research introduced a hybrid dual attention-based pyramidal deep convolutional network and deep belief network (HDPCBN) for accurate liver tumor detection. Significantly, the HDPCBN approach deployed a pyramidal architecture to learn deep hierarchical features and intricate patterns of the tumor effectively. Moreover, the integration of the dual attention technique gathers the long-range relationships of both spatial and channel dimensions for accurate liver tumor detection. In addition, the HDPCBN model learns the local patterns and edges from the images, thereby leading to precise tumor detection. The Hybrid deep flow features (HDF2) extraction gathers the discriminative and textural features of the tumor, which significantly reduces the training complexity and leads to accurate tumor detection. Experimental results indicate that the HDPCBN framework obtains exceptional performance, reporting the specificity of 93.77%, accuracy of 96.52%, sensitivity of 97.89%, balanced accuracy of 95.83%, and Macro F1-score of 96.67%, while outperforming the other state-of-the-art methods.

Article.Title: Comparative phytochemical, antibacterial, in-silico molecular docking and ADMET analysis of Cinnamomum camphora and Cinnamomum tamala ethanolic leaf extracts against Aeromonas salmonicida
Article.Authors: Sanwal N.; Kumar A.; Kumar R.; Rawat S.; Upadhyay P.
Article.Abstract: The rapid growth of aquaculture has led to the prevalence of infectious diseases and antibiotic resistance. Therefore, new sustainable strategies are required to prevent this situation from growing. The present study evaluated the effect of ethanolic leaf extracts of Cinnamomum tamala (CTE) and Cinnamomum camphora (CCE) against Aeromonas salmonicida . Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) revealed the presence of total 43 and 56 compounds in CTE and CCE. Both extracts exhibited concentration dependent inhibition from 5 to 25 mg mL -1 . CCE showed inhibition zone of 15.33 ± 0.33 mm diameter and relative inhibition of 36.21 ± 0.50% at 25 mg mL -1 . Furthermore, MBC/MIC ratio of 4 suggested the bactericidal property of both the extracts. Correlation analysis revealed positive associations between antibacterial activity and several compounds, including camphor, vitamin E, eugenol and sesamin. Molecular docking predicted potential interactions of selected phytochemicals with FabI and MurA, structurally characterized Escherichia coli proteins as representative targets for A. salmonicida . Among the evaluated compounds, β-sitosterol exhibited the most favourable predicted interaction with MurA (docking score: -9.7). ADMET analysis provided preliminary in silico predictions and major phytochemicals complied with Lipinski’s rule of five (bioavailability score: 0.55), while molecular dynamics simulations (100 ns) suggested the relative stability of the predicted MurA–β-sitosterol complex under simulated conditions. MM-PBSA and MM-GBSA analyses estimated total binding free energies of -33.40 and − 25.99 kcal mol -1 , respectively These results provide preliminary computational insights and further biochemical, toxicological and in vivo studies are required to validate the efficacy, safety and practical applicability of these extracts under aquaculture conditions.

Article.Title: Computed tomography-based measurements of fat quality are associated with the prognostic nutritional index in gastric cancer patients
Article.Authors: Nishiguchi R.; Asaka S.; Sagawa M.; Usui T.; Yokomizo H.; Machida H.; Kariyasu T.; Hirose Y.; Fukui R.; Furuichi Y.; Shiozawa S.; Dannenberg A.
Article.Abstract: Malnutrition is common among gastric cancer (GC) patients and is associated with poor prognosis. Computed tomography (CT) measurements of the amount of visceral fat (VF) provide insights into nutrition status but the importance of fat density is unknown. The main objective of this prospective study was to examine the association between fat density and a nutrition-related index. The Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI), which combines serum albumin and total lymphocyte count, was employed. Fat attenuation by 70-keV virtual monochromatic imaging (VMI), fat density by dual-energy CT (DECT), and bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) were used to assess the body composition of 54 GC patients. VMI- and DECT-based measurements of fat attenuation and density were negatively correlated. Regardless of sex, the PNI correlated with both VMI and DECT measurements of fat attenuation and density. Serum albumin levels also correlated with both fat attenuation and density. Because serum albumin levels regulate leakage of intravascular fluid into tissues, BIA was used to determine the extracellular water (ECW)/total body water (TBW) ratio. Importantly, the ECW/TBW ratio correlated with PNI, serum albumin, fat attenuation and fat density. Collectively, these findings indicate that PNI and serum albumin levels are associated with extracellular fluid balance and fat imaging characteristics.

Article.Title: Rapid post-earthquake evacuation time prediction in urban bridge networks using a machine-learning-based surrogate model
Article.Authors: Kim M.; Lee H.; Song J.; Yoon S.
Article.Abstract: As the frequency and intensity of earthquakes continue to increase, accurately assessing post-earthquake evacuation performance in urban transportation systems has become a critical challenge. Seismic damage to bridges, which serve as critical links within road networks, can significantly degrade overall network functionality and severely impede vehicular evacuation processes. However, conventional traffic simulation-based approaches require substantial computational resources and time, limiting their applicability for large-scale scenario exploration and real-time decision-making. To address these limitations, this study proposes a machine-learning-based surrogate modeling framework to efficiently predict post-earthquake evacuation performance. The Evacuation Time Estimate (ETE) is adopted as a quantitative indicator of network performance. A large-scale dataset is generated through simulation-based traffic analyses conducted on the real-world road network of Pohang, South Korea, which includes 48 bridges. Bridge damage scenarios are systematically defined based on variations in epicentral locations within road-traffic-dense areas of Pohang City and earthquake magnitudes. In total, 100,000 simulation samples are constructed to train and validate the surrogate model. The trained model is then applied to predict ETE for various earthquake scenarios, achieving a substantial reduction in computational time compared to conventional simulations while maintaining high predictive accuracy. Furthermore, numerical analysis results indicate that evacuation time variability increases with earthquake magnitude, particularly when epicenters are located closer to the road network. These findings demonstrate that the proposed surrogate model effectively captures seismic impacts on transportation systems and provides a practical and efficient tool for rapid post-earthquake evacuation assessment and informed decision-making.

Article.Title: Age modifies the association between body composition and S1P levels in the study of health in pomerania
Article.Authors: Bibi S.; Naeem M.; Bahls M.; Groß S.; Dörr M.; Friedrich N.; Nauck M.; Lieb W.; Schwedhelm E.; Oetjen E.; Rauch B.; Gräler M.; Wielpütz M.; Völzke H.; Markus M.; Ittermann T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate whether age modifies the associations between body composition markers and sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) levels in the Study of Health in Pomerania (SHIP) cohort. Among 4,080 participants (2,275 women, 51.4%), we examined age-specific associations of anthropometric (BMI, waist circumference, waist-to-height ratio) and MRI-derived (visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue, liver fat) body-composition markers with S1P. Sex-stratified linear regression models, including interaction terms with age, were used. Overall, no significant body composition–S1P associations were found without accounting for age interactions. However, age significantly modified these associations: all body composition markers were positively associated with S1P at younger ages (20–30 years), weakened, became non-significant around midlife (35–50 years), and reversed in older adults (≥ 55 years). For example, at younger ages, BMI was positively associated with S1P—men: β = 0.029 (95% CI: 0.008 to 0.050); women: β = 0.025 (95% CI: 0.008 to 0.042), but negatively associated at older ages—men: β = −0.037 (95% CI: −0.056 to − 0.018); women: β = −0.022 (95% CI: −0.037 to − 0.006). Similar age-dependent patterns were observed for others markers. Our findings highlight that age substantially modifies the associations between body composition markers and S1P, underlining the importance of considering age in understanding metabolic risk.

Article.Abstract: Echiochilon pauciflorum (Boraginaceae) is an underexplored coastal medicinal plant. We combined GC–MS profiling, multitarget docking, ADMET prediction and cytotoxicity testing to prioritize its constituents. These compounds, together with those attributed to the species in the BIMP database (185 ligands in total), were docked against estrogen receptor α, progesterone receptor, EGFR, ALK and PARP1, and scores were ranked within each target. Four ligands, sitogluside, β-sitosterol and two spiro-bisnaphthalenes, ranked within the top 10% at two or more targets. In MTT assays (24 h), both extracts were weakly cytotoxic to A549 lung cancer cells (IC₅₀ > 1000 and 699 µg/mL), whereas HEK293 cells were more sensitive (IC₅₀ 48.1 and 36.4 µg/mL); the crude extracts were therefore not cancer-selective. The study provides a tentative chemical profile of E. pauciflorum and prioritized scaffolds for isolation and target-based testing.

Article.Title: F2D-RetinaNet: a feature-to-decision dual-path network with fractional operators for retinal disease detection and grading
Article.Authors: Delu M.; Harjule P.; Kumar R.; Gajjar K.; Nkomozepi P.
Article.Abstract: Visible pathological abnormalities and vascular integrity help diagnose retinal diseases. This paper introduces a unified feature-to-decision framework that first extracts vasculature and enhances lesions. First, this study proposes the fractional anisotropic diffusion–based hybrid enhancement (FADHE) method that selectively amplifies lesion contrast and vessel visibility in the green channel using long-memory fractional diffusion dynamics. Second, this study introduces a fractional Hessian-based attention U-Net (FHAU-Net), a multi-scale vessel segmentation model that leverages fractional Hessian responses across eight fractional orders and attention-guided skip connections to capture fine vessel structures. Finally, this work designs a dual-branch disease grading model, F2D-RetinaNet, which jointly processes the enhanced image and vessel map to learn lesion-related and vascular feature representations for the recognition and grading of retinal diseases. The FHAU-Net model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.8987, a sensitivity of 0.9084, an accuracy of 0.9804, and a specificity of 0.9876 across the unified test set, which contains variations in resolution, acquisition site, camera type, and imaging conditions. The F2D-RetinaNet is evaluated for Diabetic retinopathy (DR) detection, DR grading, and multiclass retinal disease classification tasks. Extensive testing and comparisons to the baseline procedures support the reliability of the proposed methodology on the datasets evaluated here.

Article.Title: A quantitative geophysical–geotechnical framework for slope stability analysis using electrical resistivity tomography
Article.Authors: Widodo N/A.; Panjaya H.; Prassetyo S.; Simangunsong G.; Wattimena R.; Widayat A.; Fatkhan N/A.; Nur T.; Fonna S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Slope instability constitutes a major constraint on infrastructure development in geologically complex and rapidly urbanizing regions such as West Java, Indonesia. Reliable slope stability analysis requires spatial characterization of subsurface mechanical parameters, including cohesion, internal friction angle, and bulk density. Conventional geotechnical investigations provide accurate point-scale data but are often constrained by high cost, limited spatial coverage, and logistical challenges. This study presents an integrated geoelectrical–geotechnical framework enabling the quantitative use of electrical resistivity for slope stability assessment. The investigation was conducted in the Padalarang District, West Bandung Regency, an area dominated by volcanic lithologies. Electrical Resistivity Tomography and Vertical Electrical Sounding were integrated with borehole logs, Standard Penetration Test data, and laboratory measurements to derive empirical correlations between resistivity and key geotechnical parameters. The results indicate a very strong correlation between electrical resistivity (ρ) and cohesion (R 2 = 0.8270), a strong correlation with bulk density (ρᵦ) (R 2 = 0.6860), and a weak correlation with internal friction angle (R 2 = 0.1780). The resistivity-derived parameters were incorporated into limit-equilibrium slope stability analysis under the specified groundwater condition. The representative resistivity-derived parameter model produced a Factor of Safety (FoS) of 2.60, while the final spatially integrated slope model yielded a minimum FoS of 1.23. These results demonstrate that electrical resistivity can provide spatially continuous, site-specific geotechnical information for preliminary slope stability assessment when calibrated and constrained by borehole and laboratory data.

Article.Title: Adaptive storage optimization for deep learning workloads in converged HPC-cloud environments: a reinforcement learning approach
Article.Authors: Baghdasaryan H.; Astsatryan H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Storage systems remain a significant bottleneck in large-scale deep learning training. Most evaluation studies rely on synthetic benchmarks that do not capture the I/O heterogeneity present in real training pipelines. Automated configuration methods often treat parameter selection as stateless, overlooking the temporal structure of recurring training phases. These challenges are addressed using a converged HPC-cloud platform that integrates Lustre with S3-compatible object storage. Three workloads with distinct I/O characteristics were evaluated: ResNet-50 on ImageNet-1K, 3D U-Net on the Medical Segmentation Decathlon, and Whisper Large on LibriSpeech. Time-to-convergence was used as the primary metric. We introduced a deep reinforcement learning framework that combines Proximal Policy Optimization and Soft Actor-Critic with a Transformer-based state encoder to predict workload phase transitions rather than merely respond to them. The learned policies reduced checkpoint write latency by up to 74.6% and improved GPU utilization across all three workloads. The approach generalizes across heterogeneous I/O profiles without per-workload reconfiguration. The results indicate that temporally aware storage control can improve the efficiency of distributed training pipelines in heterogeneous HPC-cloud environments.

Article.Title: Food insecurity and its associated factors among lactating mothers in Ankesha Guagusa Woreda, Northwest Ethiopia: a community-based cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Wondale M.; Tiruneh B.; Mekonen H.; Aniley Z.; Negesse A.
Article.Abstract: Food insecurity is defined as the limited or uncertain availability of nutritious, adequate, and safe food, as well as a constrained potential to obtain suitable foods in socially acceptable manners. Food insecurity leads to both macro/micronutrient deficiency, making lactating women more vulnerable to inadequate human milk production and malnutrition during their optimal lactation period. However, data on the prevalence and associated factors that contribute to food insecurity are sparse within this specific population, where food insecurity might also be worsened in relatively highland areas. Thus, this study aimed to assess the prevalence of food insecurity and its associated factors among lactating mothers in Ankesha Guagusa Woreda, Awi Zone, Northwest Ethiopia. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted from July 1 to August 30, 2025, in Ankesha Guagusa Woreda. The data were collected by a pretested structured questionnaire. The single-population proportion formula was used to estimate sample size. The final sample size was 464. To assess the food insecurity status of mothers, an eight-item Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES) was considered. Data were cleaned, coded and entered into EpiData version 4.6 and then exported to SPSS Version 25 for analysis. Both bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify associated factors of food insecurity. The prevalence of food insecurity among lactating mothers was 70.9%. Mothers residing in rural areas (AOR = 1.97; 95% CI 1.2, 3.2), mothers experiencing an illness (AOR = 1.72; 95% CI 1.11, 2.68) and mothers who did not consume Vitamin A-rich vegetables, roots, or tubers (AOR = 1.99; 95% CI 1.06, 3.73) had higher odds of food insecurity. Conversely, meal frequency (> 3 meals) (AOR = 0.34, 95% CI 0.14, 0.76) and consuming milk and milk products (AOR = 0.5, 95% CI 0.3, 0.9) were inversely associated with food insecurity. The prevalence of food insecurity among lactating mothers was high in the study area. Therefore, to optimize food security, resources must prioritize remote rural kebeles during lean cycles while health extension workers screen for maternal illnesses during postnatal visits. Additionally, establishing community-based dairy cooperatives and supporting Vitamin A-rich home gardens will directly enhance nutrition and lower food access barriers for vulnerable, lactating households.

Article.Title: Antimicrobial resistance profiles and antibiotic resistance gene detection in environmental isolates from urban streams in Ilorin, Nigeria: a One Health cross-sectional assessment
Article.Authors: Kolawole O.; Jimoh A.; Olayemi D.; Jimoh A.; Okunola A.; Aderibigbe J.; Oluwasegun F.; Olagunju A.; Oluwapelumi B.; Saliu F.; Abdullateef O.; Ahuoiza D.; Onifade A.; Olanrewaju F.; Aboyeji A.; Oloruntoba F.
Article.Abstract: Urban streams in sub-Saharan Africa receive continuous inputs of untreated wastewater and solid waste, potentially promoting accumulation of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) and resistance genes (ARGs). Data linking community sanitation to environmental antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in West African cities remain sparse. We assessed physicochemical quality, bacteriological contamination, antibiotic susceptibility, ARG prevalence, and sanitation practices across six urban streams in Ilorin, Nigeria. Three weeks of sampling yielded 247 isolates tested against six antibiotics; 98 multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative isolates were PCR-screened for five ARGs; seven isolates were 16S rRNA-sequenced; 180 households were surveyed to compute a Composite Sanitation Score (CSS) per catchment. All streams deviated from WHO/NSDWQ reference values. Ampicillin resistance was 64–89% per site; MDR prevalence was 43–68%. bla TEM was most prevalent (58–82%), followed by tet A (46–74%) and int I1 (39–61%). CSS correlated strongly negatively with all five AMR indicators (ρ = − 1.00; exact permutation p = 0.003; Bonferroni α = 0.01). With only six catchments, these are exploratory ecological associations, not causal evidence. Sanitation quality is associated with environmental AMR burden in Ilorin streams, supporting WASH investment within One Health AMR strategies, subject to confirmation in larger multi-site studies.

Article.Title: Exports of technologically related environmental goods are associated with higher environmental performance in OECD countries
Article.Authors: Toktaş Y.; Temiz D.; Şeker H.; Altıner A.
Article.Abstract: In this study, the impact of trade in technologically related environmental goods on environmental quality in OECD countries is examined for the period 2000–2023 using the MMQR method. To further address potential reverse causality concerns, the empirical analysis is complemented by the Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel Granger causality test. The study highlights how trade in these goods promotes the diffusion of environmentally friendly technologies, thereby supporting sustainable energy transitions and improvements in environmental performance. Empirical findings show that exports of technologically related environmental goods have a positive and significant impact across all quantiles, indicating that exports contribute consistently to technology diffusion. In contrast, the effect of imports becomes significant only in countries with relatively high environmental performance levels. The Dumitrescu–Hurlin test results further indicate a unidirectional predictive relationship running from both exports and imports of technologically related environmental goods to environmental performance, while no statistically significant feedback from environmental performance to trade variables is detected. The results further reveal that economic growth initially harms environmental quality, but as development progresses, its effect turns positive, confirming the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. Renewable energy consumption provides limited short-term support for environmental performance, whereas urbanization generally exerts positive effects. Overall, the findings suggest that sustainable development policies should be tailored to country-specific structural characteristics. To maximize the benefits of trade in technologically related environmental goods, it is recommended that countries prioritize tax incentives encouraging the export of environmentally friendly products and invest in infrastructure that facilitates the effective domestic use of imported environmental technologies.

Article.Title: Effect of recycled agricultural and industrial by-products on mechanical and durability properties of ultra high-performance fiber reinforced concrete
Article.Authors: Reda N.; Elmaaty M.; Elsayed M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The use of recycled agricultural and industrial by-products as partial cement replacements may reduce cement consumption and associated environmental impacts. This study investigates the effects of replacing cement with rice husk ash (RHA), fly ash (FA), glass powder (GP), and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) at 10% and 20% replacement levels on the fresh and hardened properties of ultra-high-performance fiber-reinforced concrete (UHPFRC). Performance depended on both material type and replacement level. GGBFS20% achieved the highest 28-day compressive strength of 149.1 MPa, an increase of 8.5% compared with the control. It also achieved the highest splitting tensile strength of 10.9 MPa, representing an 18.5% increase, and the highest flexural strength of 29.4 MPa, corresponding to a 19.0% increase. RHA10% increased the 28-day compressive, splitting tensile and flexural strengths by 3.1%, 12.0%, and 11.7%, respectively. FA generally reduced mechanical strength, particularly at 20% replacement, whereas GP reduced compressive, splitting tensile and flexural strengths. FA20% exhibited the highest workability. GGBFS reduced water absorption by approximately 20% and 30% at 10% and 20% replacement, respectively, while RHA20% exhibited the highest water absorption. Overall, RHA10% and GGBFS showed favorable performance for selected properties.

Article.Title: Biopsy-free score for screening myelodysplastic syndrome and related diseases in cytopenic patients
Article.Authors: Sutthinont S.; Kobbuaklee S.; Rattanathammethee T.; Chuncharunee S.; Jiamjarasrangsi W.; Rojnuckarin P.; Polprasert C.
Article.Abstract: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) often present with cytopenia, requiring bone marrow exams for diagnosis, which can be subjective and challenging. This study aimed to develop a non-invasive tool integrating clinical, laboratory, and genetic data to estimate MDS probability in Asian patients with unexplained cytopenia. Data were collected from three University hospitals in Thailand (2018–2023). Participants were adults with unexplained cytopenia. Next Generation Sequencing targeted a 40-gene myeloid panel. The predictive model was validated using bootstrapping. The study enrolled 285 participants, including 210 diagnosed with MDS (MDS: 144, MDS/MPN: 32, AML-MR: 34) and 75 non-MDS controls. The MDS group exhibited more severe anemia (Hb 8.7 vs. 10.2 g/dL; p < 0.001) and lower neutrophil count (1.8 vs. 1.9 × 109/L; p = 0.02) compared to non-MDS. Higher red cell distribution width (RDW ≥ 15%) and ≥ 2 mutations were more common in MDS (75% vs. 44% and 46% vs. 2.7%; p < 0.001). The most common gene mutations were TET2 (20.0%) , SRSF2 (16.7%) , ASXL1 (15.2%) , RUNX1 (11.9%) , and DNMT3A (10.5%) . A univariate analysis showed that Hb < 10 g/dL, ANC<1 × 109/L, platelet<100 × 109/L, RDW ≥ 15%, ≥ 2 mutations, one of six gene mutations ( TET2 , ASXL1 , SRSF2 , RUNX1 , TP53 , SF3B1 ), high-risk mutations ( NRAS , NPM1 , IDH2 , SETBP1 , CEBPA , JAK2 , IDH1 , FLT3 , KRAS ), and other risk mutations ( BCOR , U2AF1 , STAG2 , ZRSR2 , PTPN11 ) were significant predictors. The model containing 13 factors demonstrated an ROC curve area of 0.86. At a probability score of ≥ 45%, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and positive likelihood ratio (LR+) for MDS were 90.5%, 42.7%, 81.5%, and 1.6, respectively. A web-based calculator is available at ( https://tsh.or.th/mds/calculator/ ). A biopsy-free score integrating complete blood counts and gene mutations may help predict the probability of MDS and related diseases in patients with cytopenia. At a predicted probability of ≥ 45%, the score may help prioritize patients for further diagnostic evaluation, including bone marrow examination.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of Risser sign and Kreitner–Kellinghaus modified system for age estimation using iliac crest ossification in Egyptians
Article.Authors: Haiba M.; Eshiba S.; Nagah M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Establishing whether an individual has reached the 18-year legal majority threshold is a central medicolegal task in Egyptian forensic practice. Iliac crest apophyseal ossification is a potentially valuable skeletal marker for this purpose during late adolescence, yet no population-specific normative data exist for Egyptians. This study retrospectively evaluated digital pelvic radiographs of 288 Egyptians (127 males, 161 females; aged 10–30 years) using three concurrent staging systems: Risser-US, Risser-Fr, and the Kreitner–Kellinghaus modified system (KK–MS). Age increased consistently with advancing stage in all systems. No statistically significant sex differences in ossification timing, although statistical power to detect such differences was limited at several mid-stages by small sex-specific subsamples. Complete apophyseal fusion was first observed at 15.5 years in males and 15.1 years in females under Risser-US, and at 15.8 years in males and 15.9 years in females under both Risser-Fr and KK–MS. ROC curve analysis for the 18-year threshold revealed that Risser-Fr (AUC = 0.953; specificity 95.7%) and KK–MS (AUC = 0.956; specificity 95.2%) achieved excellent discriminatory performance, whereas the Risser-US system (AUC = 0.806; specificity 61.2%) performed substantially worse due to its early complete-fusion age. These findings suggest that iliac crest apophyseal ossification may be a useful late‑maturing indicator for forensic age diagnostics in Egyptians and support the consideration of Risser-Fr and KK–MS staging as adjunctive tools in forensic age estimation protocols when pelvic radiographs are available. However, because complete apophyseal fusion under Risser-Fr and KK–MS was first observed as early as 15.8–15.9 years, attainment of these terminal stages cannot by itself exclude minority. Therefore, it should be regarded as raising the probability of adulthood rather than establishing it.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic profiling of tropomyosin isoforms in bladder cancer: multi-platform sequencing and experimental validation
Article.Authors: Humayun-Zakaria N.; Yu M.; Goel A.; Gordon N.; Savill S.; Mason A.; Zeegers M.; Cheng K.; James N.; Ward D.; Bryan R.; Arnold R.
Article.Abstract: mRNA isoform level-based biomarkers are understudied but might complement DNA based approaches. The expression of tropomyosin isoforms differs between normal and cancer cells. Tropomyosin (TPM) isoforms generated by alternative splicing may contribute to Bladder Cancer (BC) biology, but their diagnostic potential has not been defined. We analysed RNAseq data from six independent BC datasets to predict TPM isoform expression. Predictions were validated through targeted long-read sequencing and isoform-specific quantitative PCR (qPCR) in archived tumour tissues (n = 90) and BC cell lines (n = 5). Urine samples from patients with BC (n = 12) and non-cancer controls (n = 16) were assessed for diagnostic performance. The expression ratios of 2 pairs of isoforms Tpm1.7/Tpm1.4 and Tpm4.2/Tpm4.1 were 2.4- and 1.4- fold higher in BC compared with non-BC tissues (p-value = 0.0003, 0.0005, respectively). In urine specimens, the ratio of Tpm4.2/Tpm4.1 was 2.66 times higher in cancer vs controls (p = 0.0031) and achieved 92% sensitivity and 69% specificity for BC detection. TPM isoform switching events are associated with bladder carcinogenesis. Assessment of TPM isoform expression by a non-invasive urine-based qPCR assay shows promise for BC detection and may complement existing diagnostic strategies.

Article.Title: Characterizing the mechanisms that determine the strength of the subjectively perceived discomfort during transcranial magnetic stimulation
Article.Authors: Drakaki M.; Madsen K.; Christiansen L.; Mastropasqua A.; Voso D.; Siebner H.; Thielscher A.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to assess how facial muscle twitches, acoustic noise, and sensory nerve fiber co-stimulation contribute to the subjective discomfort caused by prefrontal transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). Twenty participants underwent two days of testing. Questionnaires were used to characterize the location and magnitude of TMS-induced pain, as well as perceived acoustic noise level. Electromyography (EMG) was used to assess facial muscle activations. On day one, participants received TMS bursts, applying stimulation parameters that are used in approved TMS protocols for treating major depressive disorder (MDD) and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). During the second experimental day, single TMS pulses were used to additionally obtain EMG peak activations at maximal stimulation intensity and input-output curves of facial muscles. Participants localized discomfort predominantly below the coil, with left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex stimulation causing more discomfort than medial prefrontal cortex stimulation. The strength of facial muscle activation did not significantly correlate with subjective discomfort, while perceived acoustic noise levels did. Reducing acoustic noise and optimizing pulse shape to minimize peripheral co-stimulation of sensory fibers might alleviate subjective discomfort. However, optimizing field distribution to minimize facial muscle co-activation appears less pertinent. Our results can help to reduce discomfort in future TMS applications.

Article.Title: Prevalence, types, and clinical distribution of patient-related violence toward dental students: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Döken T.; Sönmez S.; Karataş E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate overall exposure to patient-related violence, its types, and its clinical distribution among dental students during clinical training. A total of 129 dental students actively involved in patient care were included. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing overall exposure to patient-related violence and specific verbal, physical, and threat-related behaviors, along with associated factors such as gender and clinical specialty. Overall, 76.0% of participants reported having experienced patient-related violence during their clinical training. Verbal violence was the most common type (51.2%), whereas physical violence was rare (0.8%). Female students reported significantly higher exposure to violence compared to male students (85.6% vs. 53.8%, p < 0.001). Patient-related violence was reported across different clinical specialties, with endodontics being the most frequently reported specialty. Violence most frequently occurred during treatment procedures. A substantial proportion of students reported perceived patient bias, and the most commonly suggested preventive strategies included strengthening legal regulations, improving patient education, and enhancing security measures. These findings indicate that patient-related violence is frequently reported during dental clinical training, with differences observed across participant and clinical characteristics. Addressing this issue requires a multifaceted approach, including improvements in communication training, institutional policies, and protective measures to enhance student safety.

Article.Title: A two-stage optimization method for wide-range single-electron quantum magnetic sensing
Article.Authors: Guo S.; Liu J.; Le T.; Dai H.
Article.Abstract: Quantum magnetic sensing is a new paradigm for detecting ultra-weak magnetic fields. Its protocol design concerns the devise of optimal sensing parameters to estimate the underlying signals of interest (SoI). Existing studies mainly rely on adaptive algorithms based on black-box AI models or formula-driven principled searches. However, when the SoI spans a wide range and the quantum sensor has physical constraints, these methods may fail to converge efficiently or optimally, causing prolonged interrogation times and reduced accuracy. This work presents a new protocol using a two-stage optimization method, consisting of a Bayesian neural network to first narrow the SoI range and a federated reinforcement learning agent to subsequently calibrate the SoI. The protocol is developed and evaluated in the challenging context of an NV-center spin system with single-shot readout and limited sensing time; and yet it achieves significant improvements in both accuracy and resource efficiency compared to the state-of-the-art.

Article.Title: Cement-free composite brick from waste foundry sand and mixed post-consumer thermoplastic waste for sustainable construction
Article.Authors: Pandey P.; Raju M.
Article.Abstract: The emergence of environmentally conscious construction practices aligned with circular economy principles has become increasingly important due to the accelerating depletion of natural resources. Therefore, this study aims to develop a value-added pathway for the reutilisation of waste plastic and foundry sand to create a cement-free perforated composite brick using waste foundry sand (WFS) and mixed post-consumer thermoplastic waste (PTW). The PTW comprised polyethylene terephthalate (PET), high-density polyethylene (HDPE), low-density polyethylene (LDPE), polypropylene (PP), and multilayer plastic (MLP). The WFS, with a fineness modulus of 2.13, was combined with PTW at a 50:50 mass ratio and processed through melt mixing and compression moulding. Ten composite-brick specimens were fabricated and evaluated for their physical and mechanical properties. The developed perforated composite bricks exhibited a water absorption of 1.11% and a mean compressive strength of 5.32 N/mm². Microstructural observations revealed the mechanical encapsulation of WFS particles within a continuous polymer matrix, while the dense packing of the silica-rich WFS contributed to the compact composite structure. This compact structure reduced interconnected voids, resulting in low water absorption. Overall, the developed PTW–WFS composite brick demonstrated good compressive strength and low water absorption, indicating its technical feasibility and potential as a sustainable, environmentally friendly, cement-free alternative for low-load construction applications.

Article.Title: An enhanced TOGI-based control framework for seamless bidirectional energy management in grid-connected solar PV–EV charging systems
Article.Authors: Malle L.; Udumula R.; Nizami T.
Article.Abstract: The less cost of photovoltaic (PV) modules and the rapid growth of electric vehicles (EV) has accelerated the adoption of solar-powered charging systems. Despite this progress, the use of bidirectional power flow in PV–EV integrated charging infrastructure has received comparatively less attention. An enhanced third order generalized integrator (ETOGI) is utilized to control bidirectional voltage source converter (VSC). A comparison is made between the Selective Harmonic Elimination Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) and Phase Disposition Pulse Width Modulation methods to find the performance of the system based on total converter losses and harmonics. The suggested model is implemented and analysed in Simulink environment and further tested through real-time implementation by a real-time OPAL-RT test platform. Its performance is evaluated by static and dynamic operating conditions during charging and discharging. The results demonstrate effective power management, improved grid power quality through lower current harmonic distortion. These outcomes indicate that the proposed configuration is a reliable and efficient solution for grid-connected solar PV-based EV charging applications.

Article.Title: Single‑cell and bulk RNA sequencing identifies T cell marker genes to predict the prognosis of ovarian cancer
Article.Authors: Sun H.; Huo X.; Li S.; Guo L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background: Ovarian cancer, with high mortality and often late diagnosis, shows high recurrence despite treatment. The variable effectiveness of immunotherapy highlights the urgent need for personalized, advanced therapeutic strategies. Methods: To investigate T-cell marker genes, single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data were sourced from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Additionally, bulk RNA-sequencing data along with clinical information from ovarian cancer patients were retrieved from the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database to establish a prognostic signature. This study involved survival analysis to evaluate associations between different risk groups, and explored cellular communication and relevant pathway analyses, including metabolic pathways. Results: We identified 41 genes showing varied expression between two T-cell subclusters, marking subcluster 0 with CCL5 and GZMA, and attributing the rest to subcluster 1. These markers delineate four prognostic groups within the TCGA OV dataset, with T-cluster 2 exhibiting the poorest survival, in contrast to T-cluster 3, which shows the best. Analysis suggests subcluster 1 T-cells might be dysfunctional, potentially exacerbating ovarian cancer progression. We also developed a T-cell scoring model using eight significant genes, showing improved survival in the low-score group. Moreover, cellular and metabolic pathway analyses underscored the importance of CCL, IL2 and MGMT pathways in these subclusters. Conclusions: The study identifies CCL-5 as a biomarker for T-cell subtypes in ovarian cancer using scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data. A T-cell scoring model based on eight genes predicts survival and progression rates, independent of clinical features. This model could be a prognostic indicator and CCL-5 a potential immunotherapy target in ovarian cancer.

Article.Title: Performance-based evaluation of hyperbolic and parabolic vertical curves for highway geometric design
Article.Authors: Shahvarani M.; Kordani A.; Shirini B.; Moradi F.
Article.Abstract: Vertical curves play a fundamental role in highway geometric design by influencing vehicle dynamics, ride comfort, and safety. Although parabolic curves are widely adopted in current practice, alternative curve formulations may exhibit different dynamic-performance characteristics. To the authors’ knowledge, limited research has examined the vehicle-dynamics implications of hyperbolic vertical curves using multi-body simulation under standard highway-design constraints. Therefore, this study compares the dynamic performance of hyperbolic and parabolic vertical curves using a CarSim-based vehicle model. The analysis covered crest and sag curves designed according to stopping sight distance (SSD) and passing sight distance (PSD) criteria under identical geometric boundary conditions. Vehicle responses were evaluated using four indicators: maximum vertical acceleration, dynamic wheel load, pitch angle, and suspension deflection. The results revealed substantial differences between the two curve formulations. Vertical acceleration was the most sensitive indicator, with hyperbolic curves producing peak responses of up to 0.590 m/s², compared with approximately 0.030 m/s² for the corresponding parabolic curves. Conversely, under sag-curve conditions, hyperbolic curves reduced peak wheel loads by approximately 20–30% and suspension deflections by approximately 15–20% relative to the parabolic alternative. Pitch-angle responses showed only negligible differences between the two formulations. The findings demonstrate a clear performance trade-off between the investigated curve geometries. While the parabolic profile consistently produced lower vertical acceleration, the hyperbolic profile reduced peak wheel load and suspension deflection under the investigated sag-curve conditions. These benefits were accompanied by substantially increased vertical acceleration. The proposed framework provides a performance-based approach for evaluating alternative vertical-curve formulations and supports the integration of vehicle-dynamics considerations into future highway geometric-design studies.

Article.Title: XCAT-UIR: explainable cross-attention guided ConvNeXt-transformer framework for underwater image restoration systems
Article.Authors: Veeramakali T.; Sayeed M.; Yogarayan S.
Article.Abstract: Underwater images play a significant role in ocean exploration, but they frequently suffer from major loss of image quality due to light absorption and scattering in underwater conditions. However, underwater image restoration remains a challenging issue because of various distortions. The primary cause of information degradation includes wavelength-dependent color attenuation, light scattering effects, and blurring of objects. Currently, deep learning methods are widely utilized for image enhancement, leveraging the concept that hidden features can be learned to improve the image quality. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning methods limits the understanding of how the model produces its restoration outputs. This study presents an Explainable Cross-Attention Guided ConvNeXt-Transformer for Underwater Image Restoration (XCAT-UIR) model. The major objective of the proposed XCAT-UIR approach is to increase the visibility, correct color distortions, preserve fine details, and improve the overall quality of degraded underwater images. The proposed approach initially performs preprocessing to improve image quality for further analysis. Subsequently, ConvNeXt and Swin Transformer techniques are employed to extract local texture and global contextual information from the preprocessed images to enhance the feature understanding. The integration of convolution-based and transformer-based feature extraction networks improves the representation capability of the restoration model. Besides, the Cross-Attention Fusion model is used to integrate local features from ConvNeXt and global features from Swin Transformer to generate discriminative fused feature representations. Furthermore, Residual Reconstruction Blocks reconstruct the enhanced underwater image from the fused features while preserving important details and reducing information loss. Lastly, Grad-CAM and cross-attention maps are used to enhance visual evidence for restoration-relevant areas and local-global feature interactions. To ensure the improved performance of the proposed model, a widespread experimental analysis is performed using a benchmark dataset. An extensive comparison study emphasized that the proposed model has gained significant performance over recent methods in terms of different measures, indicating its superiority in underwater image restoration.

Article.Title: A phase 2 trial evaluating polysomnography outcomes and safety of lemborexant in Korean adults with insomnia disorder
Article.Authors: Cho Y.; Yoon I.; Pyo Y.; Takase T.; Kubota N.; Moline M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lemborexant (LEM), a dual-orexin-receptor-antagonist, was evaluated in this study of Korean participants with insomnia disorder. Study E2006-J082-204 (Study 204), a 1-month, multicenter, double-blind, placebo (PBO)-controlled, parallel-group study, evaluated LEM 5 mg (LEM5) or LEM 10 mg (LEM10) in participants aged 19–80 years with insomnia disorder (sleep efficiency [SE] ≤ 85%; latency to persistent sleep [LPS] ≥ 30 min). Korean participants were randomized (2:2:1) to LEM5, LEM10, or PBO, respectively, and received study drug immediately before bedtime for 30 days. Polysomnograms were conducted during an ~ 14-day single-blind PBO run-in (baseline) and after 1 month (Day 30). Changes from baseline in LPS (min; log-transformed; primary endpoint [LEM5 only]; secondary endpoint [LEM10 only]), SE (%; secondary endpoint), wake after sleep onset (WASO; min; exploratory endpoint), and total sleep time (TST; min; exploratory endpoint) were evaluated. Safety data were collected. The full analysis set comprised 64 participants (PBO, n = 13; LEM5, n = 25; LEM10, n = 26). At Day 30, decreases (improvements) from baseline in LPS and WASO were larger with LEM versus PBO. Increases from baseline in SE and TST were larger with LEM versus PBO. LEM was well tolerated. These findings support the clinical applicability of LEM as a therapeutic option for insomnia management in South Korea. Article.Title: Explainable machine learning for identifying nonlinear associations between street vitality and the built environment in a Historic District
Article.Authors: Xi X.; Qian Y.; Ao G.; Zhang H.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Historic districts exhibit fine-grained spatial variation, while street vitality may relate nonlinearly to the built environment. Using 213 micro-sampling points in the Lihuangpi Road Historic District, Wuhan, this study integrates heritage location, functional facilities, transport accessibility, street networks, frontage characteristics, and streetscape visual features. OLS, GAM, and XGBoost were compared, while SHAP, LOWESS, and spatial validation were used to assess nonlinear associations, model interpretation, and reliability. Under nested random validation, XGBoost achieved R² values of 0.474, 0.490, and 0.460 for overall, weekday, and weekend vitality, respectively, outperforming GAM and OLS. However, spatial GroupKFold reduced these values to 0.012, 0.084, and 0.052, with further deterioration as training–test separation increased. In the original ten-predictor models, Distance Heritage Core ranked first (29.7%–30.0%); after adding X and Y coordinates and distance to the study-area boundary, its importance decreased to 10.6%–11.3% and its rank fell to third or fourth, indicating that part of its apparent contribution reflected general spatial position. The results show that explainable machine learning can reveal nonlinear within-area associations, but random-validation performance should not be interpreted as spatial transferability. The framework supports micro-scale diagnosis and cautious, heritage-compatible renewal in historic districts.

Article.Title: Directional magnetic field detection with zero-bias surface acoustic wave sensors
Article.Authors: Nowak M.; Weisheit F.; Spetzler E.; Meyer-Strenzke J.; Lofink F.; McCord J.; Quandt E.; Meyners D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Surface acoustic wave magnetic field sensors are promising candidates in detecting low-amplitude magnetic fields over a broad frequency range. For sensor arrays and portable systems, operating without an external magnetic bias field is essential for reducing system complexity and power consumption. One approach to achieve an internal magnetic bias is to intentionally tilt the magnetic anisotropy of the sensing layer relative to the acoustic wave propagation direction. In this work, we present two types of internally biased surface acoustic wave magnetic field sensors based on exchange-biased multilayer structures. These consist of two multilayer stacks of Ta | (Fe 90 Co 10 ) 78 Si 12 B 10 | Ni 81 Fe 19 | Mn 80 Ir 20 | Ta layers that enable a stable magnetic configuration with low magnetic noise in a nearly single magnetic domain state. The best fabricated sensor reaches a detection limit of 69 pT/Hz 1/2 at 10 Hz and 22 pT/Hz 1/2 at 100 Hz, which is to our knowledge the lowest detection limit reported for SAW magnetic field sensors operated without an external bias field. The sensors exhibit a sinusoidal directional response fitting to an analytical magnetic model that includes magnetic energy contributions from magnetostatic interactions and unidirectional anisotropy.

Article.Authors: Maqsood A.; Mirza H.; Muskan A.; Akram A.; Rashid J.; Alharthi R.; Sarwar N.
Article.Abstract: The most significant problem facing software security firms in the current cybersecurity system is the fact that new strains of malware keep on appearing. The achievement of successful detection of malicious software based on both static and dynamic data remains unmet despite the further realization of different approaches to deep learning and machine learning. Defects in encryption, packaging, and distribution, the discrepancies between the distribution of malware samples in families, make this issue even worse. To do actual malware research that utilizes deep learning methods, you will require data scientists of appropriate competence, large amounts of computer power (particularly GPUs) and time. In order to overcome such issues, this approach involves a hybrid approach to feature extraction that integrates wavelet and other statistical features based on benchmarked malware image sets. A classification model based on gradient-boosting can be used reliably to classify different types of malwares. Further, this paper examined the capability of the machine learning system to Classify in-distribution test samples well. This method is properly tested on the two benchmarked datasets MelVis and MALIMG to ensure its effectiveness. By joining these two sets of data it is possible to test the suggested technique using varied array of samples. The proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques with an incredible accuracy rate of 100% using MALIMG and 98.10 and 98.40% using combined datasets. Its value extends far beyond cybersecurity in such spheres as sustaining IoT ecosystems to assist in improving networked devices and systems.

Article.Title: Identification of a natural product inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro through integrated virtual screening, DFT, and molecular dynamics simulations
Article.Authors: Paudel D.; Shrestha P.; Lamichhane S.; Tripathi G.; Khanal S.; Koirala R.; Aryal P.; Adhikari N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The emergence of vaccine-resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants demands the development of novel antivirals targeting conserved viral proteins, like the main protease (M pro ). For expediting drug discovery, CADD approach of integrating different computational tools have been employed in drug candidate identification. Based on computational analysis, our study aimed to identify potential M pro inhibitors from natural product databases by combining virtual screening, DFT calculations and MD simulations. From 224,205 molecules from ZINC15 natural product database, N-[[(2R,3S,4R,5S)-5-(2-anilino-2-oxoethyl)-3,4-dihydroxyoxolan-2-yl]methyl]-4-methoxybenzamide (Lig14) was a prospective candidate against SARS-CoV-2 M pro . It exhibited binding energy of − 8.2 kcal/mol (Paxlovid with − 7.6 kcal/mol). It showed dipole moment of 12.70 D, HOMO/LUMO energy gap of 123.00 kJ/mol. MD simulations revealed a consistent contact area interference of ~ 360 Å 2 . The binding free energy (MM-GBSA) of − 31.82 ± 6.64 kcal/mol suggested in proper binding. Moreover, MD analysis also exhibited strong sub-diffusive motion (α = 0.49) with 35.2 Å confinement within the M pro active site, demonstrating sustained binding interactions characteristic of competitive inhibitors. The alchemical free energy perturbation calculation gave solvation free energy (ΔG solv ) in water (− 41.22 to − 40.70 kJ/mol) across four methods indicating solubility. The C145Y and π-sulfur bonding with C145 in G143S, G143D, G143N and E166K could disrupt catalytic dyad formation with H41, potentially compromising enzymatic function. Through an integrated computational approach, we identified Lig14 as a promising lead compound for the inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 M pro . While these in silico methods are highly credible for initial screening, their inherent limitations warrant subsequent experimental investigation to validate these findings.

Article.Title: Coupled analytical and finite element investigation of dynamic and cyclic response in cracked functionally graded beams
Article.Authors: Anusha N.; Pachaiappan S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Offshore and marine structures increasingly utilise Functionally Graded Materials (FGMs) because of their superior stiffness and enhanced resistance to damage under combined vibration and cyclic loading induced by waves, wind and operational conditions. This study presents a combined analytical and finite element investigation into the dynamic behaviour of a cracked FGM cantilever beam compared with eight conventional offshore structural steels. A fracture-mechanics-based analytical model, incorporating crack-induced flexibility and stiffness degradation under cyclic loading within a continuum damage mechanics framework, was developed to predict the beam’s natural frequencies and validated against finite element results, with deviations below 2%. The postulated cracks were represented by predefined notches to simulate pre-existing structural damage or defects, with crack depth ratios of a/h = 0.233, 0.333, 0.4, & 0.5 introduced at different locations along the beam length. A nonlinear finite element model developed in ABAQUS was subsequently used to evaluate stress evolution, strain accumulation, and hysteretic force-displacement response under displacement-controlled cyclic loading. As the crack depth ratio increased, both the natural frequency and stiffness decreased, whereas stress concentration, strain accumulation, and hysteresis loop width increased, indicating greater energy dissipation and progressive stiffness degradation. Compared with conventional offshore steels, the FGM beam consistently exhibited higher natural frequencies, lower displacement amplitudes, and stable cyclic behaviour without significant strength degradation. The proposed analytical-numerical framework was further validated against published experimental results, confirming its reliability for assessing the coupled vibration and cyclic behaviour of cracked FGM beams for offshore structural applications.

Article.Title: Hydrogeochemical characteristics, controlling processes, and irrigation suitability assessment of groundwater in the Sanjiang Plain, China
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Liu X.; Xu P.; Guo X.; Hu H.; Su Y.; Wang L.; Wang W.; Xu D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Groundwater is vital for global irrigation water supply, and its quality directly affects sustainable agricultural development. However, studies on irrigation water quality and its dominant controlling factors in semi-humid regions remain limited. Therefore, taking the Sanjiang Plain as a case, hydrochemical analysis, irrigation water quality assessment, and multivariate statistical methods were employed to systematically reveal the hydrogeochemical characteristics, irrigation suitability, and their dominant controlling mechanisms. The results indicate that the main hydrochemical type of groundwater is HCO 3 -Ca, and most ions exhibit moderate to significant spatial variability. Its hydrochemical composition is mainly controlled by rock weathering, dominated by the dissolution of carbonate minerals, silicate minerals, and evaporite rocks, with significant cation exchange and limited contribution from gypsum dissolution. The groundwater in the study area is generally suitable for agricultural irrigation. However, EC, Na%, RSC, and MH values are relatively high in the Jiansanjiang area in the northeast, while the EC and RSC values are high in the southeast, which poses a potential risk of soil salinization. This spatial variation is mainly controlled by natural geological conditions. Carbonate mineral weathering controls the spatial distribution of MH and RSC. The dissolution of halite and silicate minerals affects variations in SAR and Na% and indirectly influences MH by inhibiting cation exchange processes. RSC shows relatively low correlations with various hydrochemical parameters, indicating that its spatial distribution is regulated by multiple coupled factors. These findings can provide a scientific basis for the rational utilization of groundwater resources, irrigation management, and salinity hazard prevention and control in similar regions.

Article.Title: Simulation of compressible flow and convergence enhancement in finned porous medium PCM systems considering non-linear material properties
Article.Authors: Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fin enhanced melting of phase change materials (PCMs) is widely used to mitigate the inherently low thermal conductivity of PCMs in thermal energy storage systems. In this study, lauric acid is selected as the PCM, and numerical models are developed for four configurations: unfinned, single-fin, triple-fin, and triple-fin structures with porous media. The governing equations are derived based on the compressible Navier Stokes equations framework, incorporating nonlinear, temperature-dependent variations in dynamic viscosity, thermal conductivity, and density throughout the melting process. To improve physical fidelity, solid and liquid transition zones and buoyancy driven volume force terms are incorporated. A thermos melting based correction is applied to adjust the specific heat capacity and Prandtl number, while empirical relations are introduced to improve numerical convergence and stability. Numerical simulations are conducted at inclination angles of 0°, 45°, and 90°, and the predicted liquid phase distributions and temperature fields are validated against available experimental data. The results indicate that the modified formulation substantially enhances convergence under strong nonlinear and multiphysics coupling conditions, with improvements of up to 71.9% and an average gain of 65.3% in porous media configurations. The root mean square error for temperature was merely 0.96 K, while the relative error for melting time stood at just 4.4%. The proposed methodology provides a more accurate and stable framework for simulating fin enhanced PCM melting under compressible conditions, offering useful insights for heat transfer analysis in viscous compressible fluids.

Article.Title: Carbon accounting method for industrial sectors at prefectural level: the case of Shanxi Province
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Huang G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurately quantifying carbon dioxide (CO₂) generation from industrial sectors at the prefectural level is both critically important and highly amenable to methodological improvement. This study develops a systematic, machine learning–enhanced framework for precise sectoral CO₂ generation estimation and robust imputation of missing data. Utilizing this framework, an extensive carbon accounting analysis is performed for Shanxi Province, a major energy production hub in China, encompassing 30 industrial sectors across its 11 prefectural regions during the years 2007 to 2022. Furthermore, the resulting dataset is used to characterize the spatial distribution and sectoral heterogeneity of industrial CO₂ generation. This study advances the existing literature along four dimensions: (i) it achieves carbon accounting at a significantly finer spatial and sectoral resolution; (ii) it introduces a more sophisticated, algorithm-driven accounting framework grounded in state-of-the-art machine learning techniques; (iii) it incorporates a broader spectrum of energy types and explicitly accounts for sector-specific variations in carbon emission factors across energy sources; and (iv) it implements a rigorous reclassification of industrial sectors alongside nuanced, deflation-adjusted treatments of monetary indicators to ensure temporal consistency and comparability of industrial carbon dioxide generation estimates over time.

Article.Title: Effectiveness of local infiltration analgesia and femoral nerve block in primary total knee arthroplasty: A prospective, participant and outcome-assessor-blinded randomized trial
Article.Authors: Kocon M.; Fleming M.; Grzelecki D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Postoperative pain following total knee arthroplasty (TKA) can delay mobilization and increase the need for opioids. Local infiltration analgesia (LIA) and femoral nerve block (FNB) are widely used methods in postoperative multimodal analgesia, but the added value of combining these techniques remains uncertain. In this prospective, participant- and outcome-assessor-blinded randomized trial (ISRCTN11696218), 125 patients undergoing primary TKA for idiopathic osteoarthritis (Kellgren–Lawrence grades II–III) were randomized into five groups: (1) Control (no additional intervention), (2) Placebo (periarticular infiltration with 100 mL saline), (3) LIA (periarticular infiltration with ropivacaine 300 mg + epinephrine 1 mg + piroxicam 20 mg diluted with saline to a total volume of 100 mL), (4) FNB (ultrasound-guided, bupivacaine 25–50 mg + epinephrine 25–50 mcg, dosed according to the attending anesthesiologist’s preference, + 100 mL saline infiltration), and (5) LIA + FNB. Outcomes were assessed preoperatively and on postoperative days (POD) 1–5. Primary outcomes included mean opioid consumption converted to morphine milligram equivalents (MME). Secondary outcomes included pain intensity measured by a visual analog scale (VAS), and passive knee range of motion (ROM). Statistically, to exclude the influence of confounding factors in the form of contralateral knee surgery, a longitudinal linear mixed-effects model was constructed. A total of 125 patients were randomized and analyzed. Baseline demographics were comparable across groups. On POD 1, the LIA + FNB group had lower mean opioid requirements (93.7 mg MME) compared to the Placebo group (138.6 mg MME; mean difference − 44.9 mg MME), the isolated FNB group ( 123.7 mg MME; mean difference − 30.0 mg MME), and the isolated LIA group (116.8 mg MME; mean difference − 23.2 mg MME, $$\:\text{p}=0.027$$ ), but there was no difference compared to the Control group (107.4 mg MME) Opioid use dropped sharply after POD 1 and remained relatively low across all groups from POD 2 to POD 5, with minor fluctuations. Early postoperative pain scores remained moderately high (mean VAS 5.5–6.9) on POD 1 across all interventions. The LIA+FNB group demonstrated an early ROM advantage on POD 1 (mean 66.7°); however, from POD 3 onward, LIA alone provided comparable mobility benefits (POD 5 mean 97.6°). Combining LIA and FNB provides a modest, time-limited reduction in early opioid consumption on POD 1 compared to a placebo infiltration or isolated FNB but lacks overall superiority over a standard control or LIA administered alone. LIA utilized as an independent strategy optimizes mobility recovery without the added interventions of peripheral blocks. The addition of FNB to LIA does not substantially alter the overall recovery trajectory.
