Article.Title: Effectiveness of male partner treatment in reducing recurrence of bacterial vaginosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Metz J.; Farr A.; Kiss H.; Witt A.; Heinzl F.; Mendling W.; Mitchell C.; Foessleitner P.
Article.Abstract: Bacterial vaginosis frequently recurs after standard antimicrobial therapy, and reinfection from untreated male partners may contribute to recurrence. We systematically reviewed studies comparing male partner treatment with placebo or no partner treatment in heterosexual couples. Of the 11 included studies, six randomised controlled trials contributed to the meta-analysis. At 4–5 weeks, all evaluable trials assessed oral-only male partner treatment, which was not associated with a significant reduction in recurrence (pooled OR 0.90, 95% CI 0.57–1.40; P = 0.63). Because trials evaluating oral-only and combined oral-topical regimens at 12–16 weeks were clinically and pharmacologically distinct, these were analysed separately: oral-only male partner treatment showed no significant benefit (pooled OR 1.17, 95% CI 0.78–1.77), whereas the single trial evaluating a combined regimen reported a significant reduction in recurrence (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.15–0.62). Five additional studies were synthesised narratively, with qualitative findings suggesting good partner acceptability. These findings do not support routine oral-only male partner treatment. However, emerging evidence indicates that combined oral and topical treatment, targeting both urethral and penile-skin reservoirs, may substantially reduce recurrence. This distinction is biologically plausible, acceptable to couples, and clinically relevant, particularly as several guideline bodies have recently endorsed combined-regimen partner therapy. Future recommendations should differentiate regimen type, recurrence risk, and implementation feasibility rather than applying male partner treatment as a single intervention. Trial registration: PROSPERO number CRD420251111546.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: bacterial vaginosis; recurrence
Article.TopicFields: Immunology and Microbiology > Microbiology > Reproductive tract infections research; Medicine > Epidemiology > Urinary Tract Infections Management; Medicine > Psychiatry and Mental health > Sexual function and dysfunction studies

Article.Title: Aerodynamic stability enhancement and nonlinear flutter control in piezoelectric integrated bolted multi-plate assemblies under dynamic flow conditions
Article.Authors: Safarpour M.; Foong L.; Yaylacı M.; Bayram M.
Article.Abstract: The current research work focuses on studying the aerodynamic stability and active nonlinear flutter control of a bolted joint multi-panel assembly (BJMP). This structure type, due to its nonlinear aeroelastic properties combined with joint friction and the dynamics of flow, represents a great difficulty for the safety of such a structure. In order to suppress the flutter phenomenon, piezoelectric sensors and actuators are attached to this structure and are shunted with a negative-capacitance piezoelectric shunt damping circuit (NC-PSDC). The complete theory of the BJMP system is formulated, where the contribution of elastic and motional energies of each rim part is included in order to find energy functionals for a hybrid multi-panel assembly using Hamilton’s variational principle. The final eigenvalue problem gives complex eigenvalues; the emergence of flutter is marked by any pair of eigenvalues having positive real parts, thus giving the critical flutter aerodynamic pressure (CFAP) and non-dimensional CFAP (NCFAP). In cases where the critical flutter regime has been exceeded, the non-linear phenomenon is accounted for through a time-stepping approach that involves the combination of Newton’s iteration technique and the Newmark integration technique. The study shows that the NC-PSDC improves aerodynamic stability through a combined mechanism: the shunt modifies the effective electromechanical stiffness of the coupled panel–circuit system, while the resistive branch of the circuit dissipates vibrational energy. The net effect is a substantial reduction of nonlinear flutter oscillations, provided the negative-capacitance ratio is selected below its optimal limit.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: aerodynamic stability; piezoelectric control; nonlinear flutter; aeroelasticity; piezoelectric actuators
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Aerospace Engineering > Aeroelasticity and Vibration Control; Engineering > Computational Mechanics > Fluid Dynamics and Vibration Analysis; Engineering > Aerospace Engineering > Plasma and Flow Control in Aerodynamics

Article.Title: Integrating hippopotamus optimization algorithm into machine learning frameworks for predicting suspended sediment concentrations
Article.Authors: Nasrabadi M.; Mehri Y.; Sabbar A.; Nahvinia M.; Omid M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The vertical distribution of sediment concentration is a fundamental component of sediment transport hydraulics, directly impacting the estimation of sediment loads in riverine and channel systems. Therefore, accurate characterization of this distribution remains a critical challenge in hydraulic engineering. To address this, advanced intelligent modeling techniques offer a robust pathway for reliable prediction. This study evaluates the performance of six distinct modeling approaches—ORELM, ORELM-HOA, GPR, GPR-HOA, GMDH-ANFIS, and GMDH-ANFIS-HOA—to predict the relative sediment concentration distribution (C/C a ​). Results indicated that the integration of meta-heuristic optimization significantly enhances the predictive precision of the GMDH-ANFIS, ORELM, and GPR frameworks. Comparative analysis reveals that the GMDH-ANFIS-HOA model achieved the highest predictive accuracy, yielding an RMSE of 0.0434 and R 2 of 0.9747 during the training phase, and an RMSE of 0.0424 and R 2 of 0.9727 during the testing phase. The GPR-HOA model followed as the second-best performer. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis identified the relative depth (y/D) as the most dominant factor influencing model accuracy. These findings demonstrate that the optimized GMDH-ANFIS-HOA model provides a reliable and efficient computational tool for engineers and hydrologists, facilitating improved design and management of irrigation canals, river engineering projects, and sediment-related environmental assessments.

Article.Title: Development of a human respiratory tract effector cell-mediated antiviral assay using blood and airway immune cells from individuals previously hospitalised with COVID-19
Article.Authors: Tomasicchio M.; Semple L.; Londt R.; Esmail A.; Lucas L.; Oelofse S.; Pooran A.; Jaumdally S.; Moore P.; Dheda K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Serum antibody–based neutralisation assays correlate with protective immunity to SARS-CoV-2, but cell-mediated in vitro cytotoxicity assays are lacking. Data on virus-specific respiratory tract immune responses in humans remain limited. Fifteen healthy participants who had previously been hospitalised with severe COVID-19 pneumonia were recruited. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), and nasal lavage (NL) cells were phenotyped by flow cytometry. Cells were stimulated with SARS-CoV-2 S1 receptor-binding domain and nucleocapsid antigens using 15-mer peptide pools or recombinant proteins. Compartment-specific effector cell-mediated cytotoxicity of SARS-CoV-2 Delta pseudovirus by antigen-stimulated effector cells was assessed using a luciferase assay. Cytokine expression was measured by Luminex. Distinct immune profiles were observed across compartments. Macrophages and dendritic cells predominated in BAL, B cells in NL, and T cells and natural killer cells in PBMCs. BAL cells expressed significantly higher IL-1β, while PBMCs showed higher TNF-α, IL-2 and IL-6 expression. Responses did not differ between peptide and protein antigens. Antigen-stimulated PBMC, BAL, and NL cells demonstrated significantly greater pseudovirus cytotoxicity than unstimulated controls ( p < 0.05). This proof-of-concept study establishes a functional human T-cell–mediated SARS-CoV-2 cytotoxic assay in blood and alveolar compartments, providing a platform to study antiviral mucosal immunity relevant to future pandemics.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: peripheral blood mononuclear cells; COVID-19 pandemic; bronchoalveolar lavage; SARS-CoV-2; nasal irrigation; mucosal immunity; nucleocapsid antigen; cell-mediated cytotoxicity; cytokine expression

Article.Title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding Helicobacter pylori resistance among physicians: a multicenter cross-sectional study in Shanxi, China
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Fan B.; Wu T.; Duan Y.; Mi H.; Miao Z.; Yuan L.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to explore physicians’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) resistance to treatment in Shanxi Province, Central China. A multicenter, cross-sectional study was conducted from August to October 2024, enrolling physicians involved in the management of gastrointestinal disorders. A structured questionnaire was developed to collect demographic data and evaluate KAP scores. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to examine the relationships among KAP dimensions. A total of 518 questionnaires were analyzed, with 70.3% of participants being female. The mean knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were 37.67 ± 7.57 (range: 10–50), 28.78 ± 3.41 (range: 7–35), and 27.98 ± 4.26 (range: 7–35), respectively. Knowledge scores (OR = 1.081, 95%CI: 1.048–1.115), attitude scores (OR = 1.079, 95%CI: 1.012–1.149), and department affiliation (internal medicine, pediatrics, or spleen and stomach) (OR = 3.718, 95%CI: 2.132–6.484) were independently associated with the practice. The SEM revealed that knowledge direct positive associations with attitudes (β = 0.336, P < 0.001) and practice (β = 0.396, P < 0.001), and attitudes directly associations with practice (β = 0.301, P < 0.001). Knowledge also showed a significant indirect association with practice through attitudes (β = 0.101, P < 0.001). In conclusion, physicians involved in the management of gastrointestinal disorders in Shanxi, predominantly gastroenterologists and physicians from tertiary hospitals, demonstrate suboptimal knowledge, generally positive attitudes, and suboptimal practices concerning H. pylori antibiotic resistance. These findings highlight the need for targeted educational interventions, particularly among non-gastroenterology physicians and those working outside tertiary centers.

Article.Title: Systemic lupus erythematosus is associated with age-related macular degeneration risk in a nationwide Korean cohort
Article.Authors: Min H.; Lee B.; Kim H.; Kim L.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Using nationwide Korean claims data, we examined whether systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is associated with age-related macular degeneration (AMD), whether associations differ for dry versus neovascular AMD, and whether risk varies by treatment-defined SLE severity. This retrospective cohort study used National Health Insurance Service data (indexed 2011–2020). Incident SLE was defined by ICD-10 M32.x plus rare-disease registration (V136), and individuals with AMD within 12 months before or after index date were excluded. AMD subtypes were classified using Korean diagnosis and copayment codes. We included 9,496 SLE patients and 28,488 matched controls. Over 63,696 person-years, 313 AMD events occurred in SLE. SLE showed higher incidence of any AMD (49.1 vs. 26.7 per 10,000 person-years; IRR 1.84, 95% CI 1.60–2.12), dry AMD (IRR 1.65, 95% CI 1.41–1.93), and neovascular AMD (IRR 3.17, 95% CI 2.26–4.46). In hydroxychloroquine duration-stratified Cox models, neovascular AMD HRs were 2.71 (< 5 years) and 4.00 (≥ 5 years) versus controls. Severe SLE was not associated with higher AMD hazards after adjustment. SLE was associated with higher AMD incidence, particularly neovascular AMD.

Article.Title: Chronic exposure to Salton Sea aerosols elicits pulmonary inflammation and shifts in murine lung and fecal microbiome diversity
Article.Authors: Topacio T.; Maltz M.; Lo D.; Zaza M.; Porter W.; Freund L.; Lyew A.; Cocker D.; Biddle T.; Yisrael-Gayle K.; del Castillo D.; Dingilian H.; Drover R.; Botthoff J.; Aronson E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lung disease is rampant around the Salton Sea, California’s largest inland lake and a major source of airborne particulates. To examine root causes of pulmonary disease, we investigated the exposure impacts of spatiotemporal variation in aerosols collected near the Salton Sea on lung and fecal microbiomes. We collected dust during the summer and fall at three different sites around the Salton Sea from 2020 to 2022. Dust was filtered to remove microbial cells and aerosolized for 7-day chronic murine exposures within controlled environmental chambers, after which mouse lung and fecal samples were used for 16 S rRNA V3-V4 amplicon sequencing. We verified that chronic exposure to aerosols elicits neutrophilic pulmonary inflammation, particularly in mice exposed to collections from the Wister site near the Salton Sea. We found that spatiotemporal variation drove variation in lung microbiome composition in mice exposed to aerosols from 2022. The lung microbiomes of Salton Sea aerosol-exposed mice were found to increase in alpha-diversity and richness, while simultaneously decreasing in evenness. In contrast, the fecal microbiomes of aerosol-exposed mice decreased in diversity and richness. Our findings suggest that chronic exposure to aerosols from Wister, a site immediately Southeast of the Salton Sea, triggers a systemic stress response in mice characterized by high pulmonary neutrophil recruitment, increased lung microbiome diversity, and decreased fecal microbiome diversity. Back trajectory analyses for aerosol surface type frequencies revealed higher contributions from the Salton Sea in 2020 and 2022 collections from Wister. These findings suggest that chronic exposure to Salton Sea aerosols have impacts on host pulmonary and systemic health, as emphasized by significant but opposing effects on lung and fecal microbiome diversity. Furthermore, these findings demonstrate the variable capacity of environmental aerosol exposure to elicit health consequences relative to seasonal weather events.

Article.Title: Evaluating the efficacy of DEET-based topical repellent products against biting midges using a modified arm-in-cage method
Article.Authors: Fagbohun I.; Baxter L.; Logan J.; Dewhirst S.
Article.Abstract: Biting midges ( Culicoides spp.) are vectors of filarial parasites and arboviruses like Oropouche virus, as well as major nuisance biters to humans and animals. Personal protection, including the use of topical repellent, is essential to preventing infective bites. However, no standardised methods exist for testing the efficacy of topical repellent products for humans against biting midges. We have developed, validated, and conducted a modified arm-in-cage (AIC) test with human participants to evaluate the complete protection time of seven insect topical repellent products containing 9.5%, 20%, and 50% DEET at the recommended product application rates. Landing rates, equivalent to those typically observed in the field, were successfully achieved on the untreated forearm, validating the AIC assay before assessing protection on the treated forearms. The 9.5% DEET product demonstrated a complete protection time (CPT) of 07:02 h. Among the 20% DEET formulations, the roll-on recorded the highest CPT of 09:32 h, whereas the 50% DEET roll-on recorded the highest CPT of 10:36 h overall. In conclusion, this modified AIC test method simulates field testing, whilst providing a safe approach for the efficacy evaluation of topical repellents for human use against biting midges. The CPT values obtained for the tested products demonstrate their efficacy in protecting humans against midge bites.

Article.Title: Analytical study on titan yellow sensing using a poly (phenylalanine)-modified carbon nanotube electrochemical sensor
Article.Authors: Moulya K.; Manjunatha J.; Aldossari S.; Deraman M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In the current work, a poly (phenylalanine) modified carbon composite paste electrode (PPCNTPE) allowed for the simple electrochemical measurement of Titan yellow (TY) utilizing differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) and cyclic voltammetry (CV). PPCNTPE was synthesized using electro polymerization method and analysed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The electrochemical results revealed that PPCNTPE increased the rate of TY oxidation by increasing the peak current and decreasing the peak potential as compared to the bare carbon nanotube paste electrode (BCNTPE), making the oxidation process thermodynamically more favourable. The modified sensor had a good sensitivity for simultaneous detection of TY, Carmoisine (CM), and methyl orange (MO). In a linear working range of 20–400 µM, a good detection limit of 0.1034 µM was obtained for TY. The built sensor was successfully used for real sample analysis, with outstanding recovery performance.

Article.Title: Adaptive federated ensemble learning with hyperparameter optimization for distributed healthcare IoT
Article.Authors: Almjally A.; Khan M.; Menshawi A.; Alsubait T.; Ziar R.
Article.Abstract: The rapid evolution of IoT-enabled healthcare systems has resulted in large-scale distributed data generation across various institutions. While federated learning enables collaborative model training without centralized data, it degrades non-identical data distributions and statistical imbalance across clients. Moreover, the convergence instability and hyperparameter sensitivity remain critical challenges in heterogeneous healthcare environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Stability-Aware Secure Federated Ensemble Framework integrated with LampyraCetacea Optimization (ASEFE-LCO). The platform integrates FedAvg and FedProx algorithms with an adaptive multi-model ensemble mechanism to ensure convergence stability under non-IID conditions. To enhance predictive robustness, LampyraCetacea Optimization is employed for dynamic hyperparameter adaptation in non-convex environments. To offer formal privacy tamper-proof protection, an integrated blockchain layer is applied to ensure decentralized auditability. The proposed architecture offers an end-to-end intelligent platform that combines optimization stability, security assurance, scalability, and distributed knowledge integration. As a core tenet of the proposed model, the experimental evaluation of the IoT healthcare security benchmark dataset achieves 99.94% accuracy, indicating a robust, secure, and clinically interpretable solution for an intelligent healthcare system.

Article.Title: Physics-informed neural operators for rapid electric field prediction in transcranial magnetic stimulation of healthy and tumor subjects
Article.Authors: Moser P.; Greifeneder F.; Freinberger D.; Reishofer G.; Ritter P.; Frank L.; Thumfart S.; Freigang S.; Mahdy Ali K.
Article.Abstract: Accurate and rapid prediction of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)-induced electric fields is essential for personalized clinical applications, from individualized therapy in major depressive disorder to presurgical functional mapping in neuro-oncology. Yet conventional finite element methods are often too computationally expensive for interactive use. Existing deep learning surrogate models partly address this limitation but are largely constrained to fixed voxel-grid representations that cannot naturally accommodate the irregular geometry of subject-specific head meshes. We present the first physics-informed neural operator (PINO) for subject-specific prediction of vector TMS electric fields, built on a mesh-native dual-encoder architecture that jointly encodes head anatomy and coil configuration. By incorporating a curl-based regularization term aligned with the curl-free nature of the TMS secondary field, the PINO model promotes physical consistency as a soft regularizer alongside data-driven supervision. Trained on 75 subjects from the IXI dataset, the framework was evaluated across four independent held-out test datasets, including healthy subjects from two additional MRI cohorts and, for the first time in learning-based TMS electric-field prediction, tumor patients. The resolution-agnostic formulation generalizes across subjects, coil types, and spatial resolutions without retraining, predicting vector electric fields on approximately 300,000 gray matter volume nodes in under 100 ms on a consumer-grade GPU. Across all test datasets within the focality-50% region, the PINO model achieved median center-of-gravity errors of 0.39–0.43 mm, RMSE of 0.12–0.16 V/m, and mean angular deviations of 6.7°–7.3°, with performance within or below the error ranges reported by recent deep-learning approaches. At the selected 5% physics-loss weighting, curl loss decreased by 9.1% relative to the data-only model, while RMSE and MAD increased by only 1.6% and 1.3%, respectively. These results suggest that physics-informed neural operators provide a scalable technical foundation for rapid gray-matter electric-field approximation, supporting future studies on real-time electric-field-guided TMS workflows

Article.Title: A hybrid reinforcement learning and Harris Hawks Optimization framework for multi-objective resource management in IIoT
Article.Authors: Dara S.; Elloumi M.; Allam M.; Annepu V.; Banka V.; Touti E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is revolutionizing industrial processes by interconnecting sensors, machines, and computing resources to enable intelligent automation, real-time monitoring, and predictive maintenance. Despite its potential, efficient allocation and management of resources in IIoT networks remain a significant challenge due to the dynamic, heterogeneous, and large-scale nature of industrial environments. Traditional static or heuristic resource allocation methods often fail to satisfy conflicting objectives such as minimizing latency, maximizing throughput, ensuring energy efficiency, and maintaining system reliability. To address these challenges, this paper presents the design and development of an AI-based multi-objective resource management system for IIoT systems. The system integrates reinforcement learning (RL) for adaptive, real-time decision-making with Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) for multi-objective optimization, balancing competing performance metrics across sensing, communication, computing, and control layers. The RL agent predicts system states and dynamically adjusts resource allocation, while HHO fine-tunes the solutions to achieve optimal performance under multiple constraints. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed system outperforms conventional static and heuristic approaches, achieving higher efficiency, faster adaptability, and improved scalability. By intelligently managing resources and optimizing system behavior, this system enhances overall operational reliability and Quality-of-Service in IIoT networks. The results indicate that combining AI-driven decision-making with advanced nature-inspired optimization provides a robust and efficient solution for next-generation industrial applications, paving the way for more intelligent, resilient, and resource-efficient IIoT systems.

Article.Title: Early childhood teachers’ practices and perspectives on the integration of smart devices in children’s learning environments
Article.Authors: Al-Barakat A.; AlAli R.; Alotaibi S.; Aboras A.; Abdullatif A.; Zaher A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Digital technology is increasingly used in early childhood education to support children’s engagement, interaction, and learning. However, limited research has examined how teachers interpret and integrate smart devices into classroom practice, particularly in underrepresented contexts such as Saudi Arabia. This study explores early childhood teachers’ perceptions and practices regarding the integration of smart devices in children’s learning. A qualitative research design was employed with 63 early childhood teachers in Al-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia. Data were collected through classroom observations and semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed four interconnected domains of practice concerning teachers’ integration of smart devices in early childhood settings: children’s digital self-regulation, guidance for technology use, digital collaboration and social interaction, and digital creativity and innovation. The findings suggest that smart-device integration is shaped by teachers’ intentional decisions, pedagogical guidance, and attention to children’s learning needs. The study contributes context-sensitive evidence to the literature on digital technology in early childhood education by providing an empirically grounded account of interconnected pedagogical practices within the Saudi Arabian context. It also highlights the role of teachers in creating meaningful digital learning experiences in which smart devices complement, rather than replace, meaningful interaction and other age-appropriate learning opportunities.

Article.Title: Geochemical inheritance from bedrock insoluble residues controls mineral nutrients enrichment and depletion in karst soils
Article.Authors: Ma Q.; Long J.; Zhao M.; Liu X.; Feng Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the geochemical mechanisms governing mineral nutrients (MNs) enrichment and depletion in stable, non-degraded summit/platform karst soils of Southwest China, to provide a theoretical basis for rocky desertification management, specifically addressing why specific trace elements accumulate despite the inherent nutrient deficiency of carbonate rocks. Using a stepwise tracing approach combined with dynamic bedrock leaching experiments on 20 profiles from these settings in Southwest China, we quantified the migration and transformation of major elements (Ca, Mg, K, Na, Fe, P) and trace elements (Ni, Cu, Mo) from parent material to evolved soil. Results indicate that, relative to background values, the studied karst soils exhibit depletion of Ca, Na, and P alongside enrichment of Fe, Ni, Cu, and Mo. We propose a “Stepwise Inheritance Model” wherein soil MNs are primarily inherited from the bottom soil (T 1 ), effectively retaining the geochemical signature of bedrock insoluble residues (Yt). Notably, while Cu and Mo are strongly influenced by Yt composition through single-source inheritance, Ni exhibits a likely dual-source mechanism governed by both residue inheritance and carbonate fraction leaching. These findings suggest that soil nutrient potential is geochemically inherited from the “pre-weathering history” of Yt in these settings. This implies that ecological restoration strategies in similar karst rocky desertification settings should integrate bedrock geochemical evaluation rather than relying solely on physical soil thickness metrics. These conclusions should not be extrapolated to other karst landforms without further validation.

Article.Title: Botune: an AI-supported scaffolding system for children’s drawing-based narrative expression in nature learning
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Chen Y.; Ji S.; Hu Y.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: Nature exploration fosters children’s cognitive development and environmental awareness; however, kindergarten curricula are often constrained by limited resources and repetitive interaction, leaving children’s observations only weakly integrated into structured understanding and expression. We present Botune, an AI-supported creative-expression tool for kindergarten planting activities that integrates plant observation, drawing, spoken narration, and animation-based sharing. We conducted an exploratory, fixed-order within-participant study in kindergarten planting classes with 27 children and three educators; 24 complete cases were analysed after excluding data from three children who did not complete the drawing task. The traditional activity preceded the Botune-supported activity by seven days. The proportion of activity time spent observing and teacher-rated involvement scores during sharing were higher in the later session. The later narrations contained significantly more actions and character interactions; character counts were descriptively higher but did not remain statistically significant after Holm correction, and state- or emotion-related expressions did not differ significantly. These semantic counts index narrative elaboration rather than overall narrative quality or general narrative ability. These differences cannot be attributed to Botune alone. Scientific knowledge and conceptual understanding were not directly assessed by these measures. The study offers exploratory observations and design considerations for AI-supported narrative expression in kindergarten nature learning.

Article.Title: CFD-DEM modeling and experimental validation of fluidized bed drying using Reaction Engineering Approach
Article.Authors: Nguyen V.; Tran T.; Le K.
Article.Abstract: Fluidized bed drying is an effective technique for drying particulate materials and is widely applied in post-harvest processing of agricultural products as well as in industrial applications. This study develops a numerical drying model based on a coupled Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and Discrete Element Method (DEM) approach to describe heat and mass transfer processes in a gas-solid system. Moisture evaporation is modeled using the Reaction Engineering Approach (REA). The model is presented in detail and evaluated through rigorous comparison of simulation results with experimental data for \(\gamma\) -alumina particles reported in the literature. Rather than relying on simplified continuum approximations, this framework achieves direct particle-scale resolution for a fully resolved system comprising thousands of individual particles. The results demonstrate that the predicted drying rate curves are in good agreement with the experimental data. Additionally, the temperature and humidity fields of the gas phase are analyzed to examine the underlying heat and mass transfer mechanisms in the fluidized bed. The quality of the dried product is systematically evaluated through the spatial moisture distribution of the particles. Furthermore, a polydisperse (multi-size) particle system model is established to investigate the inter-particle distributions of physical parameters in a heterogeneous system. The results indicate that this particle-scale model offers strong potential for application in the optimization, design, and process control of industrial fluidized bed drying.

Article.Title: Delivery of transgenes into Gαo-rich subcortical structures of the mouse brain with potential applications for GNAO1 encephalopathy
Article.Authors: Vassilieva S.; Lunev E.; Tsitrina A.; Yousef A.; Tvorogova A.; Polikarpova A.; Savchenko I.; Dzhenkova M.; Shmidt A.; Galkin I.; Loginov V.; Dokuchaeva A.; Karan A.; Reshetov D.; Egorova T.; Bardina M.
Article.Abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors are widely used for transgene delivery into the mouse brain in preclinical studies, yet AAV methodology requires customization for each neurological disease. In this study, we aimed to identify the optimal approach for AAV-mediated transduction of brain regions with high expression of GNAO1 , which encodes the signaling protein Gαo. Mutations in GNAO1 cause the neurodevelopmental disorder GNAO1 encephalopathy. Using whole-brain confocal imaging, we identified the highest density of Gαo-positive neuronal somata in the striatum, thalamus, cerebellar Purkinje cell layer, and pyramidal layer of the hippocampal CA2 field in the adult mouse brain. We compared intracerebroventricular and intravenous administration of neurotropic AAVs expressing fluorescent reporters in wild-type mice. Intracerebroventricular injection into neonatal mice resulted in poor penetration into deep Gαo-rich brain regions. In contrast, retro-orbital administration of AAV9 in adult mice led to uniform vector distribution across Gαo-positive cortical and subcortical regions. For the AAV9 variant Y446F/Y731F, we demonstrated transgene delivery into neurons of dopaminergic and GABAergic pathways involved in Gαo signaling, with low tropism to GFAP-positive cells. Finally, we used AAV9-Y446F/Y731F to deliver a dual-function vector designed to silence endogenous Gnao1 and express a replacement GNAO1 transgene. Although in vitro testing was successful and brain delivery met expectations, transgene expression remained low, indicating the need for expression cassette improvement. Together, our findings define an effective AAV strategy for targeting Gαo-rich regions of the mouse brain and support development of gene therapy for GNAO1 encephalopathy.

Article.Title: Association of cumulative TCBI exposure with incident stroke in cardiovascular kidney metabolic syndrome stages 0 to 3
Article.Authors: Zhong L.; Chen Q.; Yang W.; Lin H.; Zhu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Stroke continues to impose a substantial global health burden, particularly among individuals with cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) syndrome. Single measurements may not fully reflect metabolic exposure over time. This investigation assessed the associations of cumulative TCBI exposure and two-time-point TCBI patterns with incident stroke among individuals with CKM stages 0–3. This study sought to evaluate how cumulative and temporal changes in the TCBI relate to stroke occurrence across CKM stages by analyzing 4475 CHARLS participants aged 45 years or older, assessing TCBI at two occasions, categorizing longitudinal pattern via K-means clustering, and employing multivariable logistic regression combined with restricted cubic spline modeling. Higher cumulative TCBI (CumTCBI) and membership in the high-level two-time-point pattern group were associated with greater odds of incident stroke. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-unit increase in CumTCBI was associated with 12% higher odds (OR = 1.12, 95% CI 1.07–1.17). The corresponding OR for the high-level versus low-level pattern group was 1.66 (95% CI 1.32–2.08). The association was nonlinear, with an exploratory change point near 27.83, and remained directionally consistent in sensitivity analyses. Higher CumTCBI and high-level two-time-point TCBI patterns were associated with incident stroke among middle-aged and older adults classified as CKM stages 0–3. These findings represent epidemiological associations and do not establish the clinical utility of TCBI for individual risk stratification.

Article.Title: Human myometrial cell fate under chronic oxidative stress for leiomyomagenesis
Article.Authors: Wei J.; Schipma M.; Feng Y.; Qiang W.; Gius D.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Uterine Leiomyoma are the most common benign tumors in women of reproductive age. Studies show that both leiomyoma and surrounding myometrium exist in a state of high oxidative stress, characterized by reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and impaired antioxidant defenses including defects of manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD). Oxidative stress has been proposed as a driver of leiomyoma initiation by promoting oxidative DNA damage leading to mutations in MED12 and leiomyoma growth. We hypothesize that chronic oxidative stress in human myometrial cells induces cellular remodeling and genomic alterations that promote adaptation and contribute to early events in leiomyoma development. To test this hypothesis, we generated stable human myometrial cell lines (Myo-hTERT) of wild type, MnSOD 68K and mutant MnSOD 68Q that impairs MnSOD antioxidant activity thereby imposing sustained oxidative stress. Experiments were performed both in vitro using three-dimensional spheroid cultures and in vivo using xenograft models in immunocompromised mice, with some studies extending up to 10 months to model chronic oxidative stress. Cells were exposed to the oxidative inducer paraquat (PQ) and analyzed using cellular and molecular approaches including spatial transcriptomics and MED12 mutational analysis. Cells expressing MnSOD 68Q exhibited increased intracellular ROS and oxidative DNA damage, as indicated by accumulation of 8-hydroxy-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG). Transcriptomic analysis revealed activation of pathways associated with oxidative stress responses including collagen/extracellular matrix, cellular senescence and IGF/AKT signaling. Xenografts of primary myometrial cells subjected to prolonged oxidative stress demonstrated similar molecular responses and showed an increased frequency of MED12 mutations. These changes were accompanied by modest increases in cell proliferation with minimal induction of cell death. Together, these findings provide mechanistic evidence that sustained oxidative stress can drive molecular and genomic changes in myometrial cells and support a causal role for chronic redox imbalance in the initiation of uterine leiomyomas.

Article.Title: Mixture analysis of urinary parabens and their associations with reproductive hormones in iranian women
Article.Authors: Khazaei S.; Chavoshani A.; Chavoshani M.; Hashemi M.; Moradgholi M.
Article.Abstract: While parabens are widely used, concerns exist regarding their potential to impair reproductive health through endocrine disruption. However, evidence on impacts of paraben mixtures remains insufficient, particularly regarding hormonal regulation in women. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 84 women of reproductive age (18–45 years) at Imam Reza Hospital, Kermanshah. Urinary concentrations of methylparaben (MePB), ethylparaben (EtPB), propylparaben (PrPB), and butylparaben (BuPB) were quantified via GC-MS and adjusted for specific gravity, while serum levels of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), and prolactin were measured using ELISA. We employed multivariable linear regression and exploratory relative-weight analysis to evaluate mixture-based associations, supplemented by non-carcinogenic risk assessment. MePB was most abundant, whereas BuPB accounted for 65.1% of cumulative estrogenic activity (EEQ). Mixture models revealed significant associations exclusively with LH ( n = 35), with PrPB (45%, p = 0.021) and EtPB (24%, p = 0.032) showing positive contributions, and BuPB (23%, p = 0.033) and MePB (8%, p = 0.037) showing inverse contributions; no significant associations were observed for FSH or prolactin. Although hazard quotients remained below 1 (95th percentile HI = 0.0998) and Monte Carlo simulations confirmed negligible non-carcinogenic risk, paraben mixtures may be related to hormonal levels. These findings highlight the subtle endocrine-disrupting potential of parabens at these levels.

Article.Title: Long-term spatiotemporal dynamics, hotspot persistence, and extreme AOD days over Bursa, Türkiye
Article.Authors: Caliskan B.
Article.Abstract: Satellite-based aerosol optical depth (AOD) enables long-term monitoring of atmospheric aerosol loading in regions with sparse ground-based observation networks. In this study, the spatial and temporal variability of 550 nm AOD over Bursa during 2003–2025 was investigated using Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Multi-Angle Implementation of Atmospheric Correction (MAIAC) MCD19A2 Collection 6.1 data at 1 km spatial resolution. Annual and seasonal composites were used to evaluate long-term trends, seasonality, the persistence of high-AOD areas, and extreme aerosol days. The common analysis domain covered 83.20% of the provincial area. The area-weighted annual AOD series showed a small negative trend in the full-period analysis (Theil-Sen slope = -0.510 × 10 − 3 AOD year − 1 ; p = 0.035). The negative slope direction remained consistent across the regional trend sensitivity analyses, whereas statistical significance at p < 0.05 was not retained under several annual-coverage and leave-one-year-out scenarios. After correction for multiple testing, 1,550 pixels exhibited significant trends, of which 1,539 showed decreases. AOD was highest in summer and lowest in winter, while none of the seasonal trends was significant. Persistent high-AOD areas were concentrated along the northern plain and urban corridor, with 102 pixels remaining in the annual upper-decile class throughout all 23 years. No robust trend was detected in the frequency of extreme AOD days. Overall, the different dimensions of the aerosol record did not evolve in parallel: mean AOD showed a modest negative long-term tendency, the spatial structure of recurrent high-AOD areas remained persistent, and extreme-day frequency showed no detectable trend.

Article.Title: Untargeted metabolomics in microbiome-immune crosstalk in cancer: challenges and recommendations for functional interpretation
Article.Authors: Mimpen I.; Toner-Bartelds C.; Parra-Martinez M.; Ricco B.; Catsman J.; Stigter E.; van Faassen M.; Björk J.; Burgering B.; Dijkstra K.; Voest E.
Article.Abstract: The gut microbiome plays a pivotal role in modulating responses to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) through its influence on host immunity. While several studies have identified individual bacterial species associated with ICB efficacy, findings remain inconsistent, and the underlying mechanisms are poorly defined. As microbial metabolic capacity is better conserved across individuals than taxonomic composition and is associated with ICB response, there is growing interest in investigating the role of gut-derived metabolites in response to ICB. Untargeted metabolomics provides an opportunity to study this in an unbiased manner but poses important technical and interpretive challenges. Using untargeted fecal metabolomics from patients with mismatch repair-deficiency/microsatellite instable-high (MMR-d/MSI-H) metastatic cancers receiving ICB, we examine challenges in metabolite annotation and identification, defining reliable response associations, and validating their potential immunomodulatory effects. Based on these data, we outline key lessons and recommendations that may inform future studies linking metabolomic profiling to microbiome-immune dynamics.

Article.Title: Glomalin-related soil protein and aggregate stability across a century-scale quercus liaotungensis restoration chronosequence on the loess plateau
Article.Authors: Sun L.; Liu F.; Liu Q.; Kang L.; Bao L.; Yu W.; Li Q.; Wang G.; Zhang K.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Vegetation restoration can affect soil aggregate stability and organic carbon sequestration, but the role of glomalin-related soil protein (GRSP) within different aggregate fractions remains unclear, especially across century-scale restoration chronosequences. This study used a space-for-time chronosequence of Quercus liaotungensis forests (30, 60, 90, and 120 years) and abandoned farmland as the control (CK) on the Loess Plateau. Soil samples were collected at 0–20, 20–40, 40–60, and 60–80 cm depths. Wet sieving separated macroaggregates (> 250 μm), microaggregates (53–250 μm), and silt-clay particles (< 53 μm). Total GRSP (T-GRSP), easily extractable GRSP (EE-GRSP), and soil organic carbon (SOC) were measured in each fraction. Macroaggregate content and mean weight diameter (MWD) were generally higher in restored stands than in CK, with depth-specific peaks at intermediate restoration ages. SOC increased in all aggregate fractions after restoration relative to CK, especially in macroaggregates at 0–20 cm, and generally decreased with soil depth. T-GRSP generally accumulated with restoration age, whereas EE-GRSP showed a more pronounced peak at 60–90 years, particularly in macroaggregates. The EE-GRSP/T-GRSP ratio varied among fractions and depths and was highest at intermediate restoration stages. MWD was positively correlated with macroaggregate SOC at 0–20 cm and with macroaggregate EE-GRSP/T-GRSP at some deeper depths, but correlations were weak and based on a limited number of restoration-age groups. These results indicate that GRSP pools, especially in macroaggregates, are associated with aggregate stability during forest restoration, although causal relationships cannot be established from this observational chronosequence. The findings provide observational evidence for understanding soil structural recovery in semi-arid restored ecosystems, but broader extrapolation requires further validation across regions and soil types.

Article.Title: Bayesian optimization-driven machine learning for compressive strength prediction of hybrid fiber-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete
Article.Authors: Li C.; Dong R.; Tariq J.; Rushema E.; Hussain M.; Akbar M.; Pinto M.
Article.Abstract: The use of recycled coarse aggregate (RCA) in concrete provides a sustainable approach to reducing construction and demolition waste, but predicting its compressive strength (CS) is challenging due to complex interactions among binder composition, supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs), fibers, and mix proportions. This study develops and compares seven Bayesian optimization (BO) based machine learning (ML) models to predict the CS of hybrid fiber-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete (HFRRAC). A dataset of 281 experimental samples with 14 input variables, including OPC, FA, GGBS, water content, aggregate proportions, and fiber characteristics, was used for model training and evaluation. Performance was assessed using R 2 , RMSE, MAE, and MAPE. The results show that ensemble and boosting methods outperform the conventional approaches evaluated in this study. On the held-out testing subset, the best-performing BO-GP-GBQR model achieved a training R 2 of 0.9959 and a testing R 2 of 0.9348, with a testing RMSE of 3.5675 MPa, MAE of 2.4883 MPa, and MAPE of 8.03%. SHAP analysis identified water content, OPC, and GGBS as the most influential parameters. The proposed framework enables accurate and interpretable prediction of 28-day CS and can support preliminary mixture screening for HFRRAC containing recycled coarse aggregate and hybrid fibers.

Article.Authors: Ushida H.; Kominami T.; Goto K.; Ota J.; Sajiki A.; Inooka T.; Murakami Y.; Wada Y.; Murakami A.; Sonoda K.; Nishiguchi K.
Article.Abstract: This retrospective observational study characterized the clinical features and visual function of early- and later-onset retinitis pigmentosa (RP) caused by biallelic variants in the RPE65 gene ( RPE65 -RP). Nine genetically confirmed patients (seven unrelated individuals and one pair of siblings) from four Japanese institutions were included. Clinical data, including best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), fundus and autofluorescence imaging, optical coherence tomography, Goldmann perimetry, and electroretinogram, were reviewed. Most patients developed symptoms in early childhood (2–7 years), while one showed adult-onset disease. No patients showed nystagmus, and five had BCVA of 20/40 or better at some point by either history or measurement. However, seven patients eventually experienced BCVA of 20/250 or worse in at least one eye. Two patients with compound heterozygous variants, i.e., c.1543C > T (p.Arg515Trp) and c.683A > C (p.Gln228Pro), retained good vision and wider residual ellipsoid zone and visual field. All patients showed retinal degeneration consistent with RP and non-detectable electroretinogram responses. RPE65 -RP resulted in severe visual handicap by early adulthood in many cases. These findings present phenotypic features and variability in RPE65 -RP.

Article.Title: Short-term choroidal thickness modulation with SAT-001 digital software intervention in pediatric myopia: a randomized pilot study
Article.Authors: Han S.; Hahm J.; Bae M.; Lee Y.; Rhiu S.
Article.Abstract: Myopia progression in children is associated with excessive axial elongation, leading to structural changes in the eye, including choroidal thinning. This two-center, randomized, open-label, parallel-group, exploratory study aimed to investigate the effects of SAT-001, a software-based digital therapeutic device, and its modified version (mSAT-001) on choroidal thickness (ChT) in pediatric myopia. A total of 20 myopic children (9.00 ± 2.20 years) were divided into two groups. Group 1 ( N = 10) used SAT-001, requiring 30 min of device application (structured eye-movements and rest modules), while Group 2 ( N = 10) used mSAT-001, requiring 15 min of device application (structured eye-movements only). ChT was measured at the subfoveal and four additional anatomical locations (two nasal, two temporal points from the fovea) in the right eye at baseline, immediately before, and after device application. Both groups showed ChT increases after device application, but Bonferroni-adjusted within-group significance observed only in Group 1. Between-group differences were significant subfoveally and nasally, with subfoveal significance retained in sensitivity analyses (adjusted P < 0.05). These findings suggest that SAT-001 may acutely modulate ChT in children with myopia and support the potential utility of ChT as an exploratory physiological biomarker for evaluating short-term responses to digital therapeutic interventions.

Article.Title: Globally guided multi-agent reinforcement learning with decoupled critics for cooperative UAV path planning
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Liu Q.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cooperative path planning for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) requires the simultaneous achievement of target navigation, collision avoidance, and formation coordination in complex obstacle environments. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning methods often suffer from sparse rewards, local deadlocks, and conflicts between formation maintenance and obstacle avoidance, which can destabilize policy learning. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Globally Guided Decoupled-Critic Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic algorithm (GDC-MASAC). RRT $$^*$$ -based global guidance provides reference waypoints for the leader UAV, reducing inefficient exploration and local deadlocks. Three decoupled Critic branches separately evaluate target navigation, formation maintenance, and safety objectives, while an environment-aware formation reward adjustment relaxes formation tracking near obstacles according to the distance to obstacle boundaries. Experiments under different obstacle densities and swarm sizes show that GDC-MASAC improves mission completion, collision avoidance, and formation coordination. In a scenario with 12 obstacles and 3 UAVs, GDC-MASAC achieves a mission success rate of 86%, whereas the baseline methods achieve success rates below 50%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of GDC-MASAC for cooperative multi-UAV path planning in cluttered environments.

Article.Title: Combining ability and gene action studies for different horticultural traits in pink brinjal (Solanum melongena L.)
Article.Authors: Sharma S.; Bhushan A.; Kumar S.; Kumar B.; Sharma M.; Vaid A.; Chopra S.; Kumar V.; Mehta A.
Article.Abstract: Pink brinjal ( Solanum melongena L.) is a highly preferred and extensively cultivated vegetable crop in Jammu and Kashmir, yet its genetic improvement has been constrained by the limited availability of high-yielding cultivars and the paucity of genetic information for parental selection. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of combining ability and gene action in elite pink brinjal germplasm, generating a strategic framework for hybrid breeding in the specialized market segment. An 8 × 8 half-diallel mating design involving eight elite pink brinjal parental lines produced 28 cross combinations, which along with their parents, were evaluated for twenty horticultural traits in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with three replications. Combining ability was estimated using Griffing’s Method II, Model I. Significant mean squares due to GCA and SCA revealed the simultaneous contribution of additive and non-additive genetic components in trait inheritance. Among the parental lines, Ganderbal Local Selection (P 3 ) and SJPB-22-12 (P 6 ) were identified as good general combiners for the majority of the yield-contributing traits, while Long Kashmiri × Kashmiri Long (P 4 × P 5 ) and SJPB-22-12 × Pink Long (P 6 × P 8 ) exhibited higher per se performance and significant positive SCA effectsfor yield related traits. In contrast, SJPB-22-08 × Pink Long (P 7 × P 8 ) exhibited good specific combining ability effects for quality traits. Beyond identifying promising parental lines and cross combinations, this study establishes a valuable genetic resource for the rational exploitation of heterosis and provides valuable evidence-based breeding strategies for developing high-yielding, good quality pink brinjal hybrids adapted to regional production systems.

Article.Title: Dual-band single negative metamaterial-based MIMO antenna with enhanced performance
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Kumar S.; Pathi S.; Shukla M.; Vimal V.; Kumar G.; Srivastava K.; Soliman N.
Article.Abstract: This work presents a single-layer metasurface characterization and analysis for converting a linearly polarised narrowband antenna to a wideband circularly polarised antenna and its multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) implementation. The single-layer metasurface is supported by grounded dielectric substrate, which is considered wave-guided metamaterial to retrieve the effective refractive index along the propagation direction. The proposed metasurface shows dual-band single negative (SNG) properties, with the first band (3 to 5.9 GHz) having negative permittivity and the second band (5.9 to 9 GHz) having negative permeability, which increases the effective propagation constant and thus allows antenna miniaturisation. The metasurface-integrated MIMO antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth of 3.11 GHz (4.3–7.41 GHz), an axial ratio bandwidth of 1.6 GHz (4.7–6.3 GHz), and the antenna gain ranges from 4.8 to 7.8 dB across the impedance bandwidth.

Article.Title: Nonlinear dynamic analysis of a variable angle tow composite diving board
Article.Authors: Heidarpour B.; Rahi A.
Article.Abstract: This paper investigates the nonlinear dynamic response and energy transfer mechanisms of a Variable Angle Tow (VAT) composite springboard featuring an intermediate unilateral support. While conventional straight-fiber composites are limited by their constant stiffness profiles, VAT composites enable spatial stiffness tailoring to optimize kinematic performance. A fully coupled nonlinear mathematical model is developed utilizing the Timoshenko beam theory and von Kármán geometric nonlinearities to account for large deformations. The governing equations are derived via Hamilton’s principle, discretized using the Galerkin method, and integrated numerically with a penalty approach modeling the unilateral contact. A comparative dynamic analysis between a tailored VAT (45 ∘ -90 ∘ ) and a straight-fiber composite springboard demonstrates that the VAT configuration significantly reduces the fundamental natural frequency while amplifying the maximum tip vertical velocity by over 145% (reaching 2.7 m/s). The results reveal that the variable fiber orientation induces a strong bend-twist coupling ( \(\:{D}_{16}\) ), triggering pronounced torsional oscillations and activating dominant geometric nonlinearities, which are evidenced by asymmetric phase portraits and higher-order harmonics in the frequency spectrum. Furthermore, energy analysis confirms that the VAT springboard possesses a vastly superior mechanical energy capacity, storing approximately 380 J of strain energy and releasing over 300 J of kinetic energy, compared to just 125 J and 50 J in the straight-fiber counterpart. These findings indicate that VAT composites provide substantial dynamic tailorability, alongside enhanced mechanical energy storage and energy return capacity for high-performance diving structures.

Article.Title: Iron oxide nanoparticle-mediated elicitation enhances secondary metabolite production, antioxidant activity, and gene expression in Melia azedarach L
Article.Authors: Rabbani V.; Garoosi G.; Haddad R.; Farjaminezhad R.; Japelaghi R.
Article.Abstract: Melia azedarach L. is an important medicinal plant with various biological activities, such as antidiabetic, antibacterial, antifungal, analgesic, and anticancer. The effect of iron oxide nanoparticles on the contents of azadirachtin, lupeol, stigmasterol, mevalonic acid, and squalene metabolites, expression of genes involved in their synthesis pathway, and the activity of some antioxidants in M. azedarach cell suspension culture has not been extensively studied. The impact of iron oxide nanoparticles at different concentrations (0, 20, 40, and 60 mg/L) and sampling times (3, 6, and 9 days) on cell suspension growth, production, and accumulation of the metabolites, expression of MOF1 and SQS1 genes, and antioxidant enzyme activity was investigated. Also, response surface methodology was used to optimize the applied treatment to achieve maximum accumulation of the secondary metabolites. The results of the RSM showed that the optimal conditions for achieving maximum accumulation of azidarichtin and squalene were a concentration of 20 mg/L of iron oxide nanoparticles on days 8.1 and 5.6 of sampling, respectively, and for lupeol, the optimal conditions were 39.2 mg/L of iron oxide nanoparticles and a sampling time of 4.5 days. The results showed that the highest expression levels of Mof1 and SQS1 genes, with an increase of 30.83 and 10.25-fold compared to the control, were observed under the treatment where squalene accumulation reached its highest level. In addition, the highest proline content, total flavonoid content, and phenol content were found for the 60 mg/L iron oxide nanoparticles and 6 days of sampling, 20 mg/L iron oxide nanoparticles and 9 days of sampling, and 40 mg/L iron oxide nanoparticles and 3 days of sampling, respectively. The catalase and superoxide dismutase enzymes showed the maximum activity in the 20 mg/L iron oxide nanoparticle and 6 days of sampling. The results suggest that optimized iron oxide nanoparticle treatments are associated with enhanced growth, metabolite accumulation, antioxidant activity, and expression of selected biosynthetic genes.

Article.Title: Particle swarm optimization-based type-2 fuzzy modeling for ECG signal prediction
Article.Authors: Pashikanti R.; Rathod V.; Raut A.; Dhotre V.; Tikore S.; Paithankar V.; Admasu D.
Article.Abstract: A hybrid prediction framework based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Inference System (IT2FIS) is proposed in this paper. The major contribution is a systematic methodology for calculating the ideal parameter vector to tune the membership functions of a type-2 fuzzy controller. In contrast to type-1 fuzzy controllers, the interval type-2 formulation provides better robustness in uncertain operating conditions by explicitly modelling uncertainty through a Footprint of Uncertainty (FOU) bounded by upper and lower membership functions. Four performance indices mean square error (MSE), root mean square error (RMSE), error mean, and error standard deviation were used to assess the suggested IT2FIS-PSO framework on typical ECG arrhythmia signal data. The baseline IT2FIS produced an RMSE of 0.1198. This improved to 0.0429, a reduction of almost 75.98%, after PSO-based optimization of both membership function bounds. Experimental data show that the proposed optimization technique significantly improves ECG prediction accuracy relative to the unoptimized baseline, and simulation results confirm that PSO consistently finds the optimal parameters for a type-2 fuzzy controller.

Article.Title: Multistep synthesis of novel indole–benzimidazole hydrazone hybrids as xanthine oxidase inhibitors: In-Vitro evaluation, molecular docking, MD simulations and DFT studies
Article.Authors: Ammara N/A.; Latif A.; Ali M.; Khushal A.; Khan S.; Mammadova K.; Duran S.; Halim S.; Abdellattif M.; Khan A.; Al-Harrasi A.
Article.Abstract: This work reports the synthesis of a focused library of indole-benzimidazole hydrazone hybrids ( 17 - 35 ) via a multistep procedure involving thiolation, hydrazination, and Schiff base condensation. The final structures were confirmed using 1 H-NMR, 13 C-NMR, and FT-IR spectroscopy by observing diagnostic NH, azomethine, and carbonyl peaks consistent with the proposed frameworks. All of the synthesized compounds were evaluated for in vitro xanthine oxidase (XO) inhibition, where only eight compounds possessed significant activity (IC₅₀ = 26.8–91.5 µM). Amongst the active molecules, compound 18 emerged as the most potent inhibitor (IC₅₀ ≈ 26–27 µM), followed by 20 , 17 , and 33 , with several analogues outperforming allopurinol (IC₅₀ = 78.5 ± 1.34 µM), indicating promising lead potential. The structure-activity (SAR) analysis highlights that small, single electron-donating substituents at ortho/meta positions increased XO potency, whereas multiple, bulky, or strongly electron-withdrawing groups created steric clashes, hence reduced activity. Conceptual DFT results supported the biological trends, showing lower HOMO-LUMO gaps (3.75–4.37 eV) and reduced hardness relative to allopurinol, consistent with higher electronic softness and improved target interaction in active compounds. Molecular docking was performed against bovine XO (PDB: 3NRZ), which displayed strong binding of the active compounds ( 18 , 20 , 17 , and 33 ) via cooperative H-bonding (Ser876), π–π stacking with phenylalanine residues, and π-cation/π-sulfur interactions (Lys771, Met770), rationalizing their inhibitory mechanisms. Furthermore, MD simulations were applied to compound 18 , allopurinol as a standard, and APO, and the results reveal that after ligand binding, the protein was stabilized. The ligand-binding complex of compound 18 was found to be more stable than the allopurinol complex. The binding energy was calculated by MMPBSA; compound 18 has -28.839 ± 4.59 kcal/mol, and the allopurinol complex has -7.746 ± 2.53 kcal/mol. This interactive experimental-computational work identifies the indole-benzimidazole hydrazone scaffold, specifically compound 18 , as a viable platform for producing next-generation XO inhibitors for the management of hyperuricemia and gout.

Article.Title: Externally validated machine learning models for prediction of treatment selection and clinical outcomes in posterior communicating artery aneurysms
Article.Authors: Sanker V.; Register E.; Eberle A.; Javed S.; Paul B.; Chang C.; Jensen K.; Kasem R.; Almosawi M.; Scherschinski L.; Catapano J.; Benet A.; Rahmani R.; Lawton M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Posterior communicating artery (PCOM) aneurysms account for approximately 25% of intracranial aneurysms and present clinical challenges regarding optimal treatment selection. This study developed and validated machine learning models to predict treatment modality, complications, and functional outcomes in PCOM aneurysm management using a comprehensive institutional database of 75 patients treated between 2002 and 2023. Five machine learning algorithms—Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and XGBoost—were systematically compared across 7 outcome variables: treatment type (open vs. endovascular), specific open surgical treatment, specific endovascular treatment, intraoperative rupture, complications, angiographic obliteration, and discharge modified Rankin Scale score. Models were developed using preoperative patient-specific (age, sex, family history) and aneurysm-specific (size, presentation, morphology, location) parameters, with rigorous preprocessing that included class-balancing strategies, feature engineering, and regularization to minimize overfitting. Cross-validation performance demonstrated high accuracy for treatment prediction (78.7% Random Forest), complications (94.7% Random Forest; however, sensitivity of 0% indicates that this accuracy should not be interpreted as clinically useful event detection), intraoperative rupture (92.0% Random Forest), and angiographic obliteration (87.3% Random Forest). External validation on an independent cohort from the University of Louisville (n=20–28; n=20 most complete cases for the primary external cohort, with up to n=28 for selected endpoints with available labels) revealed variable generalizability: treatment prediction maintained 78.1% accuracy, and complication prediction showed reduced external performance (70.3%), highlighting institution-specific factors. Comprehensive sensitivity analyses demonstrated that class balancing significantly improved minority class recall (0.0% → 52.2%–86.3%) for rare outcomes. Feature importance analyses identified age, aneurysm size, admission modified Rankin Scale score, and Hunt-Hess grade as the most influential predictors across multiple outcomes. This study represents the first externally validated, multioutcome machine learning framework for PCOM aneurysm management, providing quantitative risk estimates and evidence-based decision support for treatment selection and outcome prediction.

Article.Title: Multi-level malware subfamily attribution from RGB executable images using attention-augmented deep learning
Article.Authors: Saxena M.; Das T.
Article.Abstract: Malware analysis in modern cybersecurity increasingly requires decisions at multiple levels of granularity, including maliciousness detection, malware family identification, and fine-grained subfamily attribution. While image-based malware classification has demonstrated promising performance for binary detection and family-level recognition, the application of RGB executable image representations to hierarchical malware subfamily attribution remains largely unexplored. This study presents a unified hierarchical deep learning framework for malware classification using RGB representations of Windows Portable Executable (PE) files, enabling simultaneous malware detection, family classification, and 33-subfamily attribution within a multi-output architecture. Four attention-augmented transfer learning models ResNet50V2-CBAM, DenseNet169-CBAM, Xception-NonLocal, and VGG19-Triplet Attention were evaluated under identical datasets, taxonomy, preprocessing, and training conditions to ensure fair comparison. Experimental results achieved 99% binary classification accuracy, 96–97% family-level accuracy, and 91–95% subfamily-level accuracy, with macro F1-scores up to 0.89 for fine-grained attribution. A comprehensive experimental evaluation using per-class precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion-matrix analysis showed closely comparable performance among the three strongest attention-based models, with the fully fine-tuned VGG19 variant trailing on the most difficult variants. A protocol-matched comparison with our previously published grayscale framework further showed that RGB executable images provide competitive hierarchical performance while enabling direct compatibility with modern three-channel transfer learning architectures. This study represents one of the first systematic evaluations of RGB executable image representations for hierarchical malware subfamily attribution across a 33-subfamily taxonomy. The proposed framework provides an effective and computationally efficient approach for fine-grained malware attribution, supporting practical applications in digital forensics, cyber threat intelligence, and security operation centers.

Article.Title: Agreement between initial in-person and follow-up telemedicine assessment in patients presenting with first-time headache
Article.Authors: Sarıdaş F.; Oguz-Akarsu E.; Mercan Kara M.; Ur Özçelik E.; Köse N.; Cerrahoğlu Şirin T.; Huseynli Z.; Kocasoy Orhan E.; Gökçay F.; Öztürk V.; Karlı H.
Article.Abstract: Remote healthcare services have markedly increased in recent years. Telemedicine is increasingly considered a practical alternative to in-person evaluations of chronic neurological disorders, including primary headache syndromes. However, prospective data examining its reliability during first-time consultation are limited. This study assessed the consistency between initial in-person examination and subsequent telemedicine follow-up in patients presenting with headache for the first time, and compared costs, time burden, loss of work capacity, and patient and physician satisfaction. Sixty patients (49 women and 11 men) aged 20–40 years who presented with headaches for the first time to six specialized headache clinics were enrolled in this study. Each patient underwent an initial in-person examination, followed by a video-based telemedicine consultation at the same center 45 days later. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, and diagnoses were recorded during interviews. Patients completed cost and burden assessment questionnaires, and both groups completed satisfaction questionnaires. Analyses examined the concordance between the two examination methods and factors influencing them. Headache history showed excellent agreement between in-person and telemedicine assessments (ICC = 0.928, 95% CI 0.882–0.956), while headache frequency and duration demonstrated moderate agreement. Localization and lateralization were consistent in more than 80% of cases, headache intensity in 77.8%, and overall diagnostic concordance reached 95%, with the highest agreement observed for migraine with and without aura. In-person outpatient examinations resulted in a mean time loss of 208.05 ± 119.78 min, whereas telemedicine reduced work-capacity time loss by 87.4%. Patient satisfaction with telemedicine was high (86.2% very satisfied), and physicians rated the overall telemedicine consultation favorably (69% excellent). Patients also expressed greater willingness than physicians to use telemedicine for future follow-up visits (60% vs. 39.7%). Telemedicine shows high consistency with in-person assessments, particularly for migraine patients, and has reduced time, cost, and work loss. These findings support telemedicine as a reliable follow-up approach after an initial face-to-face assessment, particularly for patients with primary headache disorders requiring limited physical examination.

Article.Title: Pain self-efficacy mediates the relationship between illness perceptions and health-related quality of life in women with endometriosis
Article.Authors: Motakef H.; Bani Hani S.; Basyouni N.; Alshahithy Y.; Abu Aqoulah E.; Salem Alshammari L.; Mazied Alshammari S.; Kamel Mosbah Mahmoud S.; Galal Abd Elrazik Siam B.; Aljabbab L.; Ali Marzouk S.
Article.Abstract: Endometriosis is a major health problem affecting about 190 million reproductive-aged women. There is no definite cure for endometriosis; however, there are many medical and surgical options for relieving the severity of the disease and improving the quality of life for these women. This study aims to examine the relationship between illness perception and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among women who have been diagnosed with endometriosis, as well as examining the role of pain self-efficacy as a mediator between these two variables. A cross-sectional design was employed with 300 participants. Data were collected using a structured, self-administered questionnaire that included sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, the Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire, the Pain Self-Efficacy Questionnaire, and the Health-Related Quality of Life: Endometriosis Health Profile-30 (EHP-30). Data were analyzed using. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27 and SmartPLS 4.0. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapping (5000 resamples) was also conducted to test both direct and mediating effects. Statistical significance was set at p < .05. The mean age of participants was 30.0 ± 5.5 years. The majority were predominantly married and attained a bachelor’s education, with a marked symptom burden. Two-thirds of participants were overweight and obese. It was found that 28.7% had Stage III endometriosis, and over 80% reported moderate-to-severe pelvic pain. Both Illness perceptions and pain self-efficacy were at moderate levels, while HRQoL impairment was substantial, especially in pain and emotional domains as well. More negative illness perceptions were significantly associated with worse HRQoL (r = 0.458, p < .001) and lower pain self-efficacy (r = − 0.474, p < .001), whereas higher pain self-efficacy was associated with better HRQoL (r = − 0.542, p < .001). In regression analysis, illness perceptions and pain self-efficacy together explained 34.6% of the variance in HRQoL, with pain self-efficacy demonstrating the stronger independent association. This study demonstrated that illness perceptions and pain self-efficacy are related factors that influence HRQoL in endometriosis patients. Negative illness perceptions were found to be associated with HRQoL, and increased levels of pain self-efficacy were found to be related to HRQoL. Pain self-efficacy also partially mediated the relationship between illness perceptions and HRQoL.

Article.Title: Improved Swin Transformer-based fine-grained human motion understanding approach driven by simulation-based augmentation for intangible cultural heritage in sports
Article.Authors: Yang X.; Huang X.; Yu L.; Dai B.
Article.Abstract: Fine-grained human motion understanding for Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) in sports faces challenges such as high similarity in posture between motion categories and significant differences in temporal rhythms within categories. Existing spatiotemporal motion models suffer from insufficient feature discrimination under small sample conditions and severe degradation in generalization ability when migrating from the simulation domain to the real domain. This paper proposes an improved Swin Transformer-based fine-grained human motion understanding method driven by simulation-based data augmentation for ICH. The method reconstructs the 3D skeleton of ICH motions using the Unity3D simulation engine combined with the OptiTrack motion capture system, and generates multimodal simulation samples by applying random perturbations to lighting, viewpoint, and body shape parameters. Addressing the limitation of the original Swin Transformer window self-attention mechanism lacking inter-frame temporal awareness, a Temporal Difference Attention (TDA) module is embedded after each Stage attention layer. This module explicitly models the rhythmic motion changes of ICH motions through the differential response of feature maps from adjacent frames. A cross-domain alignment loss, \(\:{\text{L}}_{\text{MMD}}\) , based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), is introduced at the top of the feature pyramid to force the convergence of high-level semantic feature distributions between the simulation and real domains, enabling cross-domain transferability of spatiotemporal representations. The overall framework is jointly trained end-to-end to complete closed-loop modeling from simulation generation to real-world action classification and stage localization. Experiments are conducted on the public datasets NTU RGB + D 120 (hereinafter referred to as “NTU”) and Kinetics-400 for system validation. The accuracy rates for fine-grained human action recognition reach 88.6% and 79.3%, respectively. The mean average precision (mAP) in cross-domain scenarios reaches 81.2%; the MMD distance converges to 0.038; the temporal intersection over union (tIoU) for action stage localization reaches 0.76. Further generalization analysis is conducted on the SICHA-Derived sports ICH action test dataset (covering 8 categories of traditional actions such as Tai Chi and martial arts routines, totaling 1,240 annotated videos) derived from NTU. The proposed method achieves a Top-1 accuracy of 82.4%, a 10.6% point improvement over the strongest baseline, validating the framework’s practicality in the sports ICH scenario. Notably, under extreme small-sample conditions with only a single real sample per class, the framework achieves 71.6% accuracy, substantially exceeding both the simulation-only variant at 52.4% and real-data-only fine-tuning at 18.3%, demonstrating the practical value of the simulation-based augmentation and cross-domain alignment mechanisms for real-world sports ICH scenarios where annotations are inherently scarce.

Article.Title: A reliability-oriented multimodal ensemble framework for fake news detection in armed conflict crisis situations
Article.Authors: Muhammad F.; Al-Ahmadi S.; Saeed F.; Hussain N.
Article.Abstract: Social media platforms where people can post fake news threaten public trust, social stability, and the informed nature of people’s choices because of the rapid growth of fake news. Multimedia content is widely accessible today and has added to the complication of misinformation through the use of multimedia (including images, audio, video) in combination with textual information, which often contain emotional language to create narratives that deceive consumers of information. There has been much research over the last few years that has explored ways to detect fake news on multiple platforms, and while this research has resulted in the development of many multimodal fake news detection systems, the majority of these current methods rely on single-classifier architectures and fairly simple fusion strategies that do not provide much in terms of robustness, generalization, or reliability in terms of detection under noisy and ambiguous conditions. To address these limitations, this study presents a novel multimodal fake news detection framework that incorporates both textual and visual representation learning based on transformer models, affective feature modeling, and a stacked ensemble decision-fusion approach. The textual representation learning module in the proposed framework makes use of the XLM-R model, whereas the visual representation learning module uses the ViT-B/16 model. Finally, the affective modeling module utilizes pretrained sentiment and emotion models for capturing and distinguishing the affective signals. The predictions made by the multimodal representations are combined through the meta-classifier to generate the final classification result. In this regard, the proposed architecture enables robust cross-modal reasoning and probabilistic calibration. In what follows, we discuss the empirical results of extensive experiments conducted using four large-scale benchmark datasets (Fakeddit, Ukraine-GitHub, Weibo, and MediaEval), which show that the proposed multimodal detection architecture always outperforms the state-of-the-art multimodal detection approaches proposed recently. The proposed framework performs competitively on four benchmark datasets and achieves the accuracy of 94.66%, 98.23%, 98.12%, and 97.98% on Fakeddit, Ukraine-GitHub, Weibo, and MediaEval, respectively. Evaluations and ablation studies confirm the efficacy of the proposed multimodal ensemble approach under the given experimental settings.
