Article.Title: COOLANT++: concept-bank alignment and confidence-gated reasoning for multimodal fake news detection
Article.Authors: She T.; Ab Hamid S.; Hanif H.
Article.Abstract: Multimodal fake-news detection is complicated by noisy, loosely related, or deliberately mismatched image–text pairs. Existing systems often perform instance-level alignment and evidence aggregation as separate operations, so an alignment score need not directly influence the final modality weights. We present COOLANT++, a framework that represents visual and textual embeddings as distributions over a shared bank of learned prototypes and uses their agreement as an input to a confidence-gated reasoning unit. The model jointly optimizes classification, cross-modal distribution consistency, prototype reconstruction, and gate regularization. On the Twitter and Weibo benchmarks, the submitted experiments report accuracies of 0.900 and 0.923, respectively, with lower performance when either concept alignment or gated reasoning is removed. These results support the proposed coupling on the two evaluated benchmarks; they do not establish that the learned prototypes are human-interpretable concepts or that the model generalizes to unseen events or platforms.

Article.Title: Model-based identification of medication-associated fall-risk signals using EMG time-series analysis: an exploratory mechanistic approach in polypharmacy
Article.Authors: Jung W.; Shin M.; Jeon J.; Lee S.; Moon Y.; Chae J.; Yun H.
Article.Abstract: Falls are the leading cause of functional decline in older adults. Existing fall-risk assessments often overlook the contribution of medications, and emerging sensor-based methods predict who is likely to fall but rarely explain why. We present a model-based approach for identifying medication-related fall-risk signals using high-frequency time-series electromyography (EMG). Fifteen young and 15 older adults performed perturbation-based balance tasks, and nonlinear mixed-effects modelling with bootstrap-assisted covariate selection linked the EMG responses of seven lower-limb and trunk muscles to common medication classes. The simulation-derived co-contraction index (CCI) served as the outcome, compared against a benchmark derived from Falk et al. Through stepwise covariate modelling followed by bootstrap-based confirmation, two drug classes were retained as robust covariates: anticoagulants, associated with a higher co-contraction index, and statins, associated with a lower co-contraction index. In model-based simulations, anticoagulant exposure corresponded to significantly elevated odds of exceeding the CCI benchmark, whereas statins did not increase the simulated odds despite their consistent covariate signal. This exploratory, signal-generating framework foregrounds the identification of medication-associated neuromuscular changes from EMG and may provide a mechanistic context that complements conventional epidemiology. A companion web application illustrates this approach as a supplementary tool to support medication reviews during fall-risk evaluations.

Article.Title: Spatial correlation characteristics and dynamic evolutionary research of logistics resilience associated with new quality productivity: the case of six provinces in Central China
Article.Authors: Liang Y.; Fang Y.; Yuan Z.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of new quality productive forces, this study investigates the developmental trajectory of logistics resilience across the six provinces of central China. Drawing on the dual perspectives of regional economic resilience and evolutionary resilience, an evaluation indicator system is constructed comprising five dimensions: resistance, adaptation, recovery, adjustment, and new types of productive forces, utilizing data from 2010 to 2022. The entropy weight method is employed to measure logistics resilience levels, while a modified gravity model and social network analysis are used to decode the topological structure of the spatial association network. Furthermore, a Markov chain model is applied to analyze its dynamic evolution patterns. The results indicate that: (1) Under the new quality productive forces perspective, logistics resilience in the six provinces has grown steadily, with the mean value increasing from 0.10420 in 2010 to 0.38964 in 2022, representing an average annual growth rate of 11.66%. Notably, the new quality productive forces diension carries a weight of 0.4995, identifying it as the core driver of resilience enhancement. (2) Social network analysis reveals an overall network density of 0.267, which is at a moderate level with significant room for optimization. The network structure exhibits marked non-equilibrium, with Anhui, Henan, and Hunan provinces serving as the core nodes. (3) Dynamic evolution analysis shows that logistics resilience is characterized by significant path dependence, with the probability of maintaining the same state exceeding 60%, while the likelihood of “leapfrog” transitions remains low. Future efforts should focus on leveraging the spillover effects of new quality productive forces and strengthening regional spatial synergy to enhance the dynamic adaptability of the logistics resilience system in central China.

Article.Title: Socioeconomic inequality in teenage pregnancy among adolescent girls in Ethiopia: evidence from the 2019 Mini EDHS
Article.Authors: Shewarega E.; Assres M.; Ashenafi E.; Alem M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Teenage pregnancy remains a major public health and development challenge in Ethiopia and disproportionately affects adolescents from socioeconomically disadvantaged households. Adolescence is a period marked by increased vulnerability to adverse sexual and reproductive health outcomes, including teenage pregnancy. In Ethiopia, there is limited evidence on socioeconomic inequality in teenage pregnancy and the factors contributing to this disparity. Therefore, this study assessed socioeconomic inequality in teenage pregnancy and quantified the contribution of explanatory factors among adolescent girls aged 15–19 years in Ethiopia. Data for this study were extracted from the nationally representative 2019 Ethiopian Mini Demographic and Health Survey. A total of 2,100 adolescent girls aged 15–19 years were included in the analysis. Survey weights were applied in the estimation to account for the unequal probability of selection and produce nationally representative estimates. The Erreygers normalized concentration index and its concentration curve were applied to assess socioeconomic-inequalities in teenage pregnancy. Decomposition analysis was conducted to identify factors contributing to socioeconomic related inequality. The weighted Erreygers normalized concentration index for teenage pregnancy was − 0.091 [95% CI: − 0.150%, − 0.032%] with Standard error = 0.0303 (P value < 0.01), indicating that teenage pregnancy was disproportionately concentrated among adolescents from poorer households. The decomposition analysis revealed that marital status (24.17%), wealth index (17.96%), and educational status (11.12%) were major positive contributors, while media exposure contributed − 13.56% in the opposite direction to the observed pro-poor socioeconomic inequality in teenage pregnancy. This study revealed a statistically significant pro-poor socioeconomic inequality in teenage pregnancy in Ethiopia. Marital status, wealth index, and educational attainment were the major contributors to the observed socioeconomic inequality in teenage pregnancy. Since marital status was the largest contributor to inequality, strengthening interventions to prevent child marriage and enforce the legal minimum age of marriage is essential. Given the substantial contribution of educational attainment, priority should be given to policies that improve school retention and completion among adolescent girls. Furthermore, because wealth-related disadvantage was an important factors to inequality, efforts to expand access to adolescent-friendly sexual and reproductive health services and social protection programs for economically disadvantaged households should be strengthened.

Article.Title: Glaucoma practice patterns in Australia and New Zealand: a binational survey of ophthalmologists
Article.Authors: Kha R.; Brooks A.; Allbon D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We surveyed contemporary glaucoma practice patterns among consultant ophthalmologists in Australia and New Zealand. An anonymous 21-question online questionnaire was distributed at the 2024 Australian and New Zealand Glaucoma Society conference and through the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Ophthalmologists electronic newsletter. Among 135 respondents, 57% self-identified as glaucoma subspecialists. All respondents used visual field perimetry to assess progression and 98% used optical coherence tomography. Prostaglandin analogues were the most common first-line treatment for progressive primary open-angle glaucoma (59%), followed by selective laser trabeculoplasty (39%). Glaucoma subspecialists favoured SLT as first-line therapy. Among 116 respondents who performed minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS), 43% reported routinely combining MIGS with cataract surgery for primary open-angle glaucoma. Among 97 respondents who performed incisional glaucoma surgery, trabeculectomy was the preferred first-line procedure (63%) and glaucoma drainage devices the most common second-line procedure (52%). Compared with surveys conducted two decades earlier, respondents reported greater use of optical coherence tomography, selective laser trabeculoplasty and MIGS. While there is substantial agreement in many aspects of glaucoma management, certain areas exhibit variability. These insights may assist ophthalmologists in benchmarking their practices and inform strategies to enhance glaucoma care.

Article.Title: Contract bound verifiable credentials for replay resistant container image provenance in Kubernetes
Article.Authors: Wijesundara W.; Lee J.; Jeong Y.; Obi T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Container image distribution in cloud-native supply chains is exposed to replay attacks, in which an attacker reuses a valid signature or credential in a context for which it was never issued. This paper presents a contract-bound decentralized identity framework for container image authentication in Kubernetes. Each image is described by a Verifiable Credential that carries two anchors inside the signed payload: the manifest digest of the image and a contract-binding context, defined as the pair consisting of a chain identifier and a smart-contract address that together name the trust domain of the verifier. A validating admission webhook admits an image only when the digest matches, the context declared by the credential equals the context configured for the cluster, the issuer signature verifies against a decentralized identifier document bound to an on-chain record, and the credential is recorded and not revoked on chain. A prototype built on Arbitrum Sepolia, IPFS, and a Kubernetes admission webhook rejected forged, replayed, and revoked credentials in every controlled trial. Mean admission latency was 0.91 s on the cached path and 1.78 s on the fresh path, and revocation reached verifiers within 1.9 s at the 95th percentile when driven by contract events. These guarantees are conditional rather than absolute. They hold while the issuer keys, the deployed contract, and the verifier configuration remain uncompromised, and the design fails closed, so an outage of the blockchain endpoint or of content retrieval denies admission instead of weakening verification. Within those limits, contract-bound credentials give Kubernetes a portable and revocable provenance layer that needs neither a central certificate authority nor registry-specific policy.

Article.Title: Effects of rumen-protected valine supplementation on velvet antler growth, faecal microbiota, serum metabolites, and velvet antler gene expression in sika deer
Article.Authors: Duan X.; Li Y.; Liu H.; Chen S.; Sang J.; Li S.; Zhu Y.; Ma C.; Zhang Y.; Deng R.; Nan W.; Li Z.; Si H.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated the effects of rumen-protected valine supplementation on velvet antler growth and examined the associated changes in faecal fermentation, serum metabolism, and antler gene expression in sika deer. Twenty-one 2-year-old male sika deer were randomly assigned to control (Con), low-valine (LVal; 1 g/d), and high-valine (HVal; 3 g/d) groups. Rumen-protected valine supplementation increased antler weight and average daily antler weight gain ( P < 0.05), with the strongest response in LVal. LVal also increased faecal total volatile fatty acids, propionate, and serum glucose, and altered the faecal bacterial community structure, including increased abundance of Clostridium sensu stricto 1 and Turicibacter . Targeted serum metabolomics identified valine-responsive metabolites related to energy and nucleotide metabolism, including myo-inositol, xylulose-5-phosphate, creatinine, xanthosine, and N-acetylneuraminic acid. Transcriptome analysis showed that the cartilage (CA) layer exhibited the strongest transcriptional response, with differentially expressed genes enriched in nucleotide sugar biosynthesis, insulin and AMPK signalling, and extracellular matrix organisation. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified a CA-layer gene module associated with velvet antler weight and several serum metabolites, while correlation analysis revealed positive pairwise associations among N-acetylneuraminic acid, CDH17 expression, and velvet antler weight. These findings indicate that rumen-protected valine supplementation promoted velvet antler growth and was accompanied by coordinated changes in faecal fermentation, serum metabolism, and CA-layer gene expression.

Article.Title: Long-term associations between land-surface indicators and dust-storm occurrence along the margins of the Taklimakan Desert
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Huo W.; Maihamuti M.; Yang F.; Zhou C.; Yang X.; Mamtimin A.
Article.Abstract: Land-surface change and atmospheric variability jointly shape dust activity in arid regions. We examined land-cover transitions, station dust-storm records, a Sentinel-1 backscatter index, meteorological variables from the fifth-generation European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts reanalysis (ERA5) and dust diagnostics from the Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2) along the margins of the Taklimakan Desert. Within the mapped domain, grassland increased from 9.45% in 1990 to 10.59% in 2023, while barren land decreased from 86.45% to 82.30%. Annual dust-storm-day trends were negative at 21 of 30 stations over available 1990–2024 records, and Sentinel-1 index trends were positive at 22 stations during 2015–2024. Mixed-effects path analysis of 3,804 station-month observations showed that the Sentinel-1 index was negatively associated with modelled dust emission (standardized coefficient = − 0.191; 95% confidence interval: −0.289 to − 0.043). The normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and friction velocity had the highest training-set feature importance in the random forest analysis.

Article.Title: CTAB-functionalized clinoptilolite alginate microbeads for enhanced Congo Red adsorption: performance, kinetics and equilibrium analysis
Article.Authors: Sharoni A.; Nasir N.; Azmi A.; Jaya M.; Ahmad M.; Sani Y.; AlKhabbas M.; Idris I.
Article.Abstract: Congo Red (CR) is an anionic dye that persists in industrial effluents due to its stability against biodegradation, water solubility, and resistance to the conditions found in industrial wastewater. Natural clinoptilolite is a low-cost adsorbent for water treatment. However, its negatively charged surface limits its ability to remove anionic dyes effectively. In this study, clinoptilolite microbeads functionalized with cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) were developed using a calcium-crosslinked alginate matrix to enhance Congo Red (CR) adsorption. The functionalization and characterization of the microbeads were performed using Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) as well as scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). Batch adsorption experiments were performed to evaluate the effects of the initial dye concentration, microbeads dosage, and the contact time on Congo Red removal. Under the investigated batch conditions, the CTAB-functionalized microbeads achieved a maximum experimental adsorption capacity of 51.69 mg g⁻ 1 and a Congo Red removal efficiency of 76.93% using 0.075 g adsorbent after 15 h. Adsorption kinetics were best described by the pseudo-second-order model, while equilibrium data showed better agreement with the Langmuir isotherm models, indicating enhanced adsorption affinity following CTAB modification. In addition to enhanced performance, the microbeads configuration offers practical benefits over powder including less material loss during the recovery process and easier to handle in the wastewater treatment process. In summary, microbeads CTAB-functionalized clinoptilolite are a promising adsorbent for laboratory-scale Congo Red removal.

Article.Title: Reperfusion duration distinctively alters apoptosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and autophagy markers during early reperfusion in isolated rat hearts
Article.Authors: Villarín-Ayala V.; Dávila-Matos J.; García-Báez J.; Jang S.; Capella-Muñíz J.; Torres-Ramos C.; Javadov S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reperfusion injury is a paradoxical phenomenon involving mitochondrial dysfunction and cell death that reduces cardiac performance once blood flow is restored after myocardial infarction (MI). While several cell death mechanisms have been implicated, their specific contributions at different stages of reperfusion in the ex vivo ischemia–reperfusion (IRI) model remain unclear. This study assessed apoptosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis, autophagy, and pyroptosis at multiple reperfusion time points in rat hearts. Isolated hearts from adult male Sprague Dawley rats were perfused via the Langendorff retrograde method using Krebs–Henseleit solution, subjected to 30 min of equilibration, 25 min of global ischemia, and then 5, 30, or 60 min of reperfusion. Cardiac functional parameters were measured during perfusion, and mitochondria were isolated and analyzed for respiration, Ca 2+ -induced swelling, and ROS production. Cell death pathway markers were quantified via SDS-PAGE and western blotting. Cardiac physiological parameters, measured by LVDP and RPP, decreased significantly during reperfusion compared to pre-ischemic values. Mitochondrial State 3 oxygen consumption declined significantly by 38.7% as reperfusion progressed, while ROS production and Ca 2+ -induced swelling significantly increased 2.30- and 2.44-fold, respectively. Apoptosis showed a time-dependent 1.35-fold increase, as evidenced by Caspase-3 cleavage. Glutathione peroxidase 4, an endogenous ferroptosis inhibitor, decreased significantly by 43% during early reperfusion. Autophagy markers p62 and LC3B showed significant time-dependent increases of 2.08- and 1.37-fold, respectively. Necroptosis and pyroptosis markers showed no significant change during 60 min of reperfusion. Our results show an association between cardiac dysfunction and mitochondrial alterations, as well as differential activation of RCD markers during the early reperfusion phase. This suggests that specific mechanisms may predominate over others at different stages of reperfusion, indicating a time-sensitive interaction between these pathways that could influence future therapeutic strategies for MI patients.

Article.Title: Noise-robust bearing fault diagnosis via heterogeneous time-frequency multimodal fusion
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Wu G.; Wang Y.; Peng X.
Article.Abstract: Rolling bearing failures remain the predominant cause of unexpected breakdowns in industrial rotating machinery. Current deep learning–based diagnostic approaches exhibit limited robustness to noise, especially under complex operational conditions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Heterogeneous Time-frequency Multi-Scale Attention Network (HTMSA-Net) for rolling bearing fault diagnosis that jointly leverages complementary vibration and acoustic signals. The network adopts a dual-branch architecture, with each branch built upon a ConvNeXt V2-Atto backbone, to independently extract modality-specific features from heterogeneous time-frequency representations. Specifically, continuous wavelet transform scalograms are used for vibration signals and Mel-spectrograms for acoustic signals. An Attention-based Residual Fusion (ARF) module is proposed to address the feature imbalance between branches, which employs a Multi-Scale Channel Attention mechanism to adaptively reweight modality-specific features before concatenation. The model is initialized with ImageNet-pretrained weights and trained end-to-end. Experiments on the Ottawa UORED-VAFCLS and KAIST datasets demonstrate that HTMSA-Net achieves high diagnostic accuracy under clean conditions and maintains favorable robustness under additive white Gaussian noise ranging from 6 dB to − 6 dB, consistently outperforming mainstream architectures. Ablation studies further reveal that the heterogeneous time-frequency representations and the ARF fusion module both contribute substantially to the diagnostic performance, and the adaptive ARF fusion consistently outperforms static fusion strategies.

Article.Title: Effects of core training on physical fitness in trained adolescent athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Zhang F.; Ji C.; Wang H.; Li C.; Yeremenko O.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Core training is widely used to support youth athletic development, yet its effects in trained adolescent athletes remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether core-focused interventions improve physical fitness in athletes aged 10–19 years classified as McKay Tier 2 or above. PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Scopus were searched for controlled trials, including randomized and non-randomized designs. Random-effects models were used to pool standardized mean differences with Hedges’ g. Thirty-one studies involving 818 athletes were included. Compared with control conditions, core training was associated with significant improvements in countermovement jump, standing long jump, ≥ 20-m sprint, change of direction, dynamic balance, static balance, core stability, dynamic core endurance, and isometric core endurance. The evidence for ≤ 10-m sprint performance was inconclusive. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low. Overall, benefits appeared more consistent for balance and core-related outcomes than for jumping, sprinting, and change-of-direction performance. These findings suggest that core-focused exercises may serve as a supplementary component of regular training, particularly for improving postural control, core stability, and core endurance, while indicating that transfer to jumping, sprinting, and change-of-direction performance may be more limited. Article.Title: Comparative in vitro wound-healing activity of individual and blended black seed, coconut, sesame, and olive oil nanoemulsions
Article.Authors: Helmy N.; Hashim A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate and correlate the in vitro wound-healing efficacy of black seed (BS), coconut (COCO), sesame (SMS), and olive (OVO) oils and their corresponding nanoemulsions using a normal human skin fibroblast (NHSF) cell line. Cytocompatibility was assessed through 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assays and acridine orange staining, confirming the non-toxic nature of all tested oils at the applied concentrations. Wound-healing activity was evaluated using a scratch assay. Native oils exhibited moderate wound closure rates of 32.5% and 35.1% for COCO + BS, respectively. In contrast, oil nanoemulsions demonstrated significantly enhanced wound-healing efficacy, achieving closure rates of 48.3%, 51.3% (SMS), 47.8% (COCO), and 27.0% (BS), compared to the untreated control (38.3%). Notably, the combined OVO + SMS formulation achieved a wound closure rate of 40.6%, which improved to 65.3% upon nanoemulsification. Meanwhile, nanoemulsions of the COCO + BS oil mixture resulted in a wound closure rate of 34.7%. Generally, the results indicate that nanoemulsification markedly enhances the wound-healing potential of natural oils, particularly olive and sesame oils. The observed effects are likely attributable to improved bioavailability and antioxidant activity, highlighting COCO and OVO oil-based nanoemulsions as promising natural candidates for wound-healing and regenerative applications.

Article.Title: Metabolic risk factors and leptin DNA methylation dynamics in a sample of Egyptian women with obesity
Article.Authors: Hassan N.; El-Masry S.; Kamal A.; Mosaad R.; Kobesiy M.; Mehanna N.; Kishta M.; Ismail A.; Badie M.; Alian K.; Afify M.; Aboud H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Metabolic health is negatively affected by obesity, causing a cluster of conditions known as metabolic syndrome that increase the risk for cardiovascular disease and type 2diabetes. Scientific research suggests that actions and expression of the Leptin hormone are strongly influenced by epigenetic changes such as methylation of promoter sites, which is linked to metabolic disorders occurring in obesity. The current study aimed to evaluate metabolic risk factors and its association with DNA methylation at the promoter region of the Leptin gene in a sample of Egyptian women with obesity pre and post dietary intervention. This longitudinal intervention study included 58 obese females aged 25–60 years. Participants were prescribed a 3-month weight loss program. Baseline and endpoint anthropometric parameters were measured and blood samples for metabolic assessment were drawn. The methylation of Leptin gene promoters was investigated using PCR as well as measured Leptin levels before and after the intervention program. The sample was classified into two groups: 35 metabolically healthy women with obesity (MHO) and 23 metabolically unhealthy women with obesity (MUO), based on the presence of three or more of the Metabolic Syndrome criteria. Pre-intervention: higher Leptin methylation was generally associated with better metabolic profiles in the MHO group. While post-intervention, the correlation patterns suggest different epigenetic responses between the two groups, with the MHO group maintaining protective associations, and the MUO group showing correlations indicating improved metabolic dysfunction. Current data suggest that Leptin gene methylation patterns serve as biomarkers for metabolic health status and therapeutic targets for intervention response in individuals with obesity.

Article.Title: Novel K-neighbors and gradient boosting based transfer features for optimizing network attack detection
Article.Authors: Raza A.; Hassan M.; Malik A.; Hussain I.; Montero E.; Alvarado E.; Ashraf I.
Article.Abstract: Network attacks represent unauthorized activities on digital networks that aim to disrupt, damage, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems. These attacks range from denial-of-service (DoS) disruptions to sophisticated intrusion attempts, posing significant threats to the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of information resources. The repercussions of network attacks are extensive, leading to substantial financial losses, compromise of sensitive data, erosion of user trust, and potential damage to an organization’s reputation. This research aims to recognize network attacks using advanced machine learning approaches and transfer feature engineering. We utilized the benchmark CICDDOS2019 database for experiments. We balanced the preprocessed dataset during the initial analysis using the synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE). We introduced an innovative transfer feature generation method that generates salient class probabilistic fused features using the K nearest neighbors classifier (KNC) and gradient boosting classifier (GBC). The proposed KNGB (KNC-GBC) model extracts transfer features, which are subsequently fed into machine learning models to identify network attacks. The experimental results indicate that, using KNGB features, the random forest model attained a high accuracy of 98% for network attack recognition. We also validated the applied machine learning model’s performance results using k-fold cross-validations and improved performance using hyperparameter tuning. Furthermore, we determined the computational complexity of the methods used and conducted a statistical t-test analysis to validate the significance of the results. This research aims to provide a robust, machine learning-based framework that can adapt to the dynamic nature of cyber threats, ensuring the integrity and security of information networks.

Article.Title: AFAP1-AS1/miR-195-5p is associated with malignant phenotypes and glycolysis-related metabolic changes in hepatocellular carcinoma
Article.Authors: Gu P.; Ren W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The long noncoding RNA AFAP1-AS1 is aberrantly expressed in multiple solid tumors, but its functional role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains incompletely characterized. In this study, analysis of the TCGA-LIHC cohort and eight paired HCC and matched adjacent non-tumor tissues showed that AFAP1-AS1 was upregulated in HCC and associated with poorer overall survival in the TCGA cohort. Knockdown of AFAP1-AS1 inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HCC cells. Bioinformatic prediction, expression analysis, and dual-luciferase reporter assays supported a possible regulatory relationship between AFAP1-AS1 and miR-195-5p at the predicted binding site. Inhibition of miR-195-5p increased FOXK1 expression, consistent with the effectiveness of miR-195-5p inhibition, and enhanced HCC cell migration and invasion. It also increased glucose consumption and lactate production, indicating glycolysis-related metabolic changes. Exploratory RNA-seq analysis after miR-195-5p inhibition, integrated with FOXK1 target genes and a glycolysis-related gene set, identified four candidate genes. However, these candidates and the role of FOXK1 in mediating the observed phenotypes were not functionally validated. Rescue experiments showed that miR-195-5p inhibition partially reversed the suppressive effects of AFAP1-AS1 knockdown on HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. In addition, inhibition of miR-195-5p promoted tumor growth in a HCC xenograft model. Overall, these findings suggest a possible association of AFAP1-AS1 and miR-195-5p with malignant phenotypes and glycolysis-related metabolic changes in HCC.

Article.Title: Applying the theory of planned behavior to explain aggressive behavior among Iranian adolescent girls: a structural equation modeling analysis
Article.Authors: Roustaei N.; Mohammadi G.; Behzadi M.; Bideshki M.; Motlagh S.
Article.Abstract: Aggressive behavior during adolescence is a major public health concern because of its adverse effects on mental health, academic achievement, and social functioning. The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) provides a well-established framework for understanding the cognitive and social determinants of behavior. This study examined the applicability of the TPB in explaining aggressive behavior among Iranian adolescent girls using a full structural equation modeling (SEM) approach. This cross-sectional study included 1059 adolescent girls aged 11–15 years attending public middle schools in Noorabad, southern Iran. Participants completed the Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire and a TPB-based questionnaire assessing attitude, subjective norm, perceived behavioral control, and behavioral intention to avoid engaging in aggressive behavior. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was first performed to evaluate the measurement model, followed by SEM to examine the hypothesized structural associations among the TPB constructs and aggressive behavior. Construct reliability and convergent validity of the measurement model were evaluated using composite reliability (CR) and average variance extracted (AVE), and indirect associations were estimated using bootstrap resampling (5000 samples). Participants reported moderate levels of aggressive behavior and behavioral intention to avoid aggressive behavior. The measurement and structural models showed mixed but generally reasonable evidence of model fit, with the final structural model showing χ 2 /df = 2.85, CFI = 0.897, TLI = 0.892, IFI = 0.897, and RMSEA = 0.042. Attitude showed the strongest positive association with behavioral intention to avoid aggressive behavior (β = 0.60, p < 0.001), whereas perceived behavioral control demonstrated the strongest total association with aggressive behavior (β = -0.57, p < 0.001). Behavioral intention to avoid aggressive behavior was significantly associated with lower aggressive behavior (β = −0.34, p < 0.001), whereas subjective norm was not significantly associated with behavioral intention ( p = 0.177). The TPB constructs explained 74.9% of the variance in behavioral intention and 55.8% of the variance in aggressive behavior. The findings support the applicability of the TPB for examining aggressive behavior among Iranian adolescent girls. Perceived behavioral control showed the strongest association with aggressive behavior, whereas attitude demonstrated the strongest association with behavioral intention to refrain from aggressive behavior. Although subjective norms were significantly associated with behavioral intention at the bivariate level, their unique association was not statistically significant after accounting for attitude and perceived behavioral control. This finding should not be interpreted as evidence that social influence is unimportant, but rather as indicating limited unique variance explained by subjective norms within the full TPB model. The observed associations may provide hypotheses for future research examining whether school-based approaches targeting self-regulation, emotion regulation, and attitudes toward refraining from aggression are effective in reducing subsequent aggressive behavior. Given the cross-sectional design, these associations should not be interpreted as causal relationships.

Article.Title: Ultrasound reference value of frontal-occipital horn ratio for neonates born at 25–41 gestational weeks
Article.Authors: Mayier A.; Liu Y.; Liu D.; Guo L.; Yan J.; Yan L.; Peng Y.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to establish a reference range for frontal-occipital horn ratio (FOHR) in neonates and identify factors associated with FOHR variation. This prospective research enrolled neurologically normal neonates born at or admitted to two Chinese Grade 3A Hospitals between July 2022 and November 2023. Spearman's rank correlation and median regression with bootstrap standard errors were utilized to assess factors associated with FOHR. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) were calculated to evaluate the measurement reliability of FOHR. A total of 1,579 neurologically normal neonates were included. The FOHR showed no significant association with any of the variables examined in the adjusted median regression analysis. Its central 90% reference interval (P5–P95) ranged from 0.37 to 0.46, and the potential surgical threshold is 0.55, requiring clinical validation. The intra- and inter-rater ICCs indicated moderate-to-good reliability for FOHR measurement. We present the reference value of FOHR for neonates and compare its upper limits across all available studies. The FOHR showed no significant association with any of the factors examined in the study, and its measurement reliability is clinically acceptable.

Article.Title: Perioperative molecular effects of faricimab versus aflibercept in proliferative diabetic retinopathy: a randomized comparative study
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Zhang L.; Kong X.; Cao D.; Zhuang X.; Huang H.; Hu X.; Cao Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To compare perioperative molecular responses and safety of preoperative faricimab versus aflibercept in proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) undergoing pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), and to determine whether dual Ang-2/VEGF-A inhibition induces distinct intraocular molecular remodeling. This prospective, randomized comparative study included forty treatment-naïve PDR patients undergoing PPV and 10 age- and sex-matched cataract controls. Aqueous humor samples were collected from PDR and age- and sex-matched individuals with uncomplicated cataract. For cross-sectional analysis, untreated or baseline pre-injection PDR samples were compared with cataract control samples. Paired pre- and post-treatment aqueous humor samples were obtained from PDR patients scheduled for PPV following intravitreal anti-VEGF treatment, including a faricimab group and an aflibercept group. Post-treatment samples were collected at the start of PPV, 7 days after preoperative intravitreal injection. Thirty-two predefined proteins were quantified using parallel reaction monitoring (PRM)-based targeted proteomics, and four metabolites were measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Differentially expressed proteins and metabolites were identified using thresholds of |log2 FC| > 0.3 and P < 0.05. Ocular and systemic adverse events were systematically monitored and recorded. Results No serious ocular or systemic adverse events were observed in either treatment group, and the safety profile of faricimab was comparable to that of aflibercept (P > 0.05). In the faricimab group, pro-fibrotic proteins including IGF-1, CCN2 (also known as CTGF), CCL2, FGF2, and GFAP were significantly downregulated after treatment, whereas the inflammatory factor ICAM-1 and the anti-fibrotic protein GALNS were significantly upregulated. Compared with the aflibercept group, the faricimab group showed significantly higher levels of ICAM-1, GFAP, and GALNS, alongside significantly lower NOS2 levels. Among the four metabolites analyzed, 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HPA) was significantly elevated in PDR eyes compared with controls and further increased following faricimab treatment, whereas lactate, an anaerobic glycolysis marker, increased after aflibercept treatment. Principal component analysis (PCA) revealed partial overlap between the two anti-VEGF treatment groups and clear separation from cataract controls. Preoperative intravitreal faricimab administered 7 days before PPV suggests a favorable safety profile in PDR patients. Faricimab significantly suppresses several pro-fibrotic factors in aqueous humor, suggesting a potential benefit in reducing postoperative fibrovascular proliferation. GALNS, ICAM-1, and NOS2 may serve as candidate biomarkers for distinguishing the biological effects of faricimab and aflibercept. The potential role of 3-HPA requires validation in larger cohorts. Clinical trial registration The study protocol adhered to the tenets of the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the Institutional Review Boards of Foshan Second People’s Hospital (Approval No. (2024)-0052). Written informed consent was obtained from all participants prior to enrollment. The study was prospectively registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on April 9th, 2025 (ChiCTR2500100448; PID262770).

Article.Title: Valorization of banana and bamboo leaf ash for sustainable binders with strength, microstructure
Article.Authors: Murali G.; Mason M.; Raju P.; Wong L.; Kurpińska M.; Abdelgader H.; Ramkumar V.; Avudaiappan S.
Article.Abstract: The cement sector is a major emitter of CO 2 , highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives to ordinary Portland cement. At the same time, agricultural residues such as banana biomass and bamboo leaves are largely underutilised, creating environmental burdens. While supplementary cementitious materials (SCM) support low-carbon construction, conventional sources are declining, and agro-waste binders remain poorly understood, particularly in terms of pozzolanic activity, calcination requirements, and cementitious performance. This study addresses these gaps by valorizing calcined banana and bamboo leaf ashes as eco-friendly SCMs, advancing circular resource utilisation and sustainable binder development. Ordinary Portland cement was partially substituted with banana leaf ash (BALA) and bamboo leaf ash (BLA) at replacement levels of 5, 10, 15, and 20%. The resulting mortar mixtures were systematically evaluated for their mechanical performance and microstructural characteristics. The results reveal that 5% BLA achieved the highest compressive strength (63.33 MPa at 14 days and 79.35 MPa at 28 days), whereas higher BLA and all BALA replacement levels reduced strength, with 20% BALA exhibiting the lowest values (45.40 and 61.17 MPa), confirming 5% BLA as the optimum sustainable cement replacement level. This indicating 5% BLA as the optimum replacement level under the present experimental conditions when compressive strength and microstructural densification considered together. However, 15% BLA minimized water absorption, indicating a trade-off between mechanical strength and resistance to water ingress. Microstructural analysis confirmed the higher pozzolanic reactivity of BLA through greater portlandite consumption, enhanced secondary C-S-H formation, and improved thermal stability, while BALA showed slower and weaker reactions. Excessive replacement (≥ 20%) resulted in clinker dilution, increased carbonation, and reduced matrix compactness, highlighting the need for controlled ash dosage.

Article.Title: Interaction between mast cell and eosinophil activation in renal anemia among hemodialysis patients
Article.Authors: Emre T.; Ozer Sensoy N.; Koca N.
Article.Abstract: The bone marrow immune microenvironment plays a poorly understood role in renal anemia. This study aimed to investigate the independent and combined effects of mast cell activation (basal serum tryptase) and eosinophil activation (eosinophil cationic protein, ECP) on erythropoiesis in hemodialysis patients. In this cross-sectional study, 99 maintenance hemodialysis patients were stratified into four distinct phenotypes based on standard cut-off for basal tryptase and ECP: Dual Negative, Isolated Tryptase, Isolated ECP, and Dual Positive. We analyzed clinical characteristics, hematological parameters including red cell distribution width (RDW-SD), and total IgE levels to control for atopic status. Hemoglobin levels varied significantly across the phenotypes ( p = 0.004). The Isolated Tryptase group exhibited the lowest median hemoglobin [9.10 (8.75–10.20) g/dL] and the highest RDW-SD (54.00 fL), suggesting ineffective erythropoiesis. Conversely, patients in the Dual Positive group had significantly higher hemoglobin levels [10.90 (9.80–11.83) g/dL; p = 0.018 vs. Isolated Tryptase]. In multivariable linear regression, ECP showed the strongest positive association with hemoglobin, although the relationship did not reach conventional statistical significance ( p = 0.058), independent of systemic inflammation (CRP), iron status, and total IgE. Furthermore, the positive correlation between ECP and hemoglobin remained significant in the non-atopic subgroup (IgE < 100 IU/mL; rho = 0.314, p = 0.014), confirming that this relationship is not driven by allergy. ECP shows the strongest association with higher hemoglobin levels among the biomarkers tested in hemodialysis patients, an association that persists after adjustment for serum iron and is unrelated to atopic status. Conversely, isolated tryptase elevation is associated with lower hemoglobin and greater erythropoietic stress. These findings suggest that eosinophil–mast cell interactions may represent a previously underrecognized immunological pathway involved in renal anemia.

Article.Title: From embryo flushing to in vitro production: global trends in livestock reproductive biotechnology
Article.Authors: Mata F.
Article.Abstract: Livestock embryo biotechnology is undergoing a transition from conventional in vivo-derived (IVD) embryo production to laboratory-based in vitro embryo production. This study analysed global trends in embryo production/collection and embryo transfer in domestic farm animals using International Embryo Technology Society data for 2017–2024. Embryo activity was classified by year, region, species, activity and technology, and the proportional contribution of in vitro-produced (IVP) embryos was quantified using an IVP adoption index. Temporal trends, chi-square tests, regional and species comparisons, association analyses and exploratory cluster analysis were used to describe adoption patterns. Global embryo production/collection increased from 1,532,240 embryos in 2017 to 2,468,600 in 2024, while embryo transfers increased from 1,193,424 to 1,795,956. This growth was driven mainly by IVP, whose adoption index increased from 64.9% to 84.8% for production/collection and from 62.9% to 80.4% for transfers. The IVD/IVP distribution changed significantly between 2017 and 2024. Cattle dominated global embryo activity and showed the strongest IVP adoption, whereas sheep, goats and horses displayed lower or more heterogeneous patterns. Regionally, North America and South America showed high embryo volumes and high IVP adoption, while Europe retained a larger IVD contribution. These findings indicate that IVP has become the main driver of recent growth in livestock embryo biotechnology, although adoption remains species- and region-dependent.

Article.Title: Carbon potential solution using bidirectional power and rank-adaptive pseudoinverse for transmission-distribution-microgrid systems
Article.Authors: Gui Q.; Hu X.; Zhang E.; Wang J.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Nodal carbon potential quantifies the carbon emissions embodied in each unit of electricity at a bus. It links active-power flow, branch carbon flow, and load-side carbon responsibility. In a coordinated transmission-distribution-microgrid system, bidirectional power exchange causes the carbon intensity at the point of common coupling (PCC) to vary with operating conditions. Reverse flows and near-zero active-power-flow branches alter the effective carbon-flow paths and may render the nodal-carbon-potential equations ill-conditioned or rank deficient. This paper combines a state-dependent PCC boundary, effective propagation topology, and rank-based solution for coordinated transmission–distribution–microgrid systems. Time-series power-flow results are first used to identify the PCC exchange state and update the carbon intensity of a dynamic boundary virtual source. Branch directions are then corrected according to actual active-power flows, and near-zero-flow branches are removed to construct a directed effective carbon-flow topology. Finally, singular-value decomposition diagnoses equation degeneration and determines the effective rank, after a rank-adaptive Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse gives the nodal-carbon-potential solution. The proposed method updates the PCC carbon potential with the power-exchange state and the carbon-flow paths with actual branch flows. It also maintains numerical stability at degenerate operating points.

Article.Title: Green electropolishing of pure titanium using a choline chloride–lactic acid deep eutectic solvent
Article.Authors: Karim W.; Ahmed H.; Kayani K.; Mohammad S.
Article.Abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as environmentally benign alternatives to conventional acid-based electrolytes for metal surface finishing. In this study, we first employed a choline chloride–lactic acid (ChCl, 1:2 molar ratio) deep eutectic solvent as a green electrolyte for electropolishing bulk metallic titanium. An electrochemical study was performed using current–voltage (I–V) and current–time (I–t) measurements to identify the optimum polishing conditions. A stable limiting-current plateau was observed, indicating a mass-transfer-controlled electropolishing regime established by the formation of a viscous interfacial layer. Under an electrochemical potential of 7.0 V for 15 min at 25 °C, a bright, mirror-like titanium surface was obtained. We characterized surface morphology using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM). SEM images revealed the effective removal of machining marks, scratches, and surface irregularities. At the same time, AFM analysis showed a significant reduction in average surface roughness from 727.6 ± 2.4 nm to 190.4 ± 2.1 nm, representing a 73.8% decrease . The results show that the 1 ChCl: 2 Lac deep eutectic solvent is an effective, simple, and environmentally friendly electrolyte for titanium electropolishing, offering a sustainable alternative to conventional acid-based polishing systems and a considerable voltage for advanced surface-finishing applications.

Article.Title: Compact wideband X-band MIMO antenna with enhanced isolation using neutralization line and modified ground structure
Article.Authors: Arajula S.; Kumar J.
Article.Abstract: A compact two-port MIMO antenna is proposed for X-band wireless and radar applications where limited installation space is a key constraint. The antenna is fabricated on a low-cost FR-4 substrate and occupies only \(16 \times 18 \times 0.8~\textrm{mm}^3\) . By optimizing the radiator geometry together with the partial ground plane, an impedance bandwidth of 8–12.5 GHz is obtained. Mutual coupling between the two radiating elements is reduced by integrating a neutralization line with rectangular slots in the ground plane. The neutralization line introduces a controlled coupling path between the elements, while the ground slots alter the surface-current distribution and contribute to isolation enhancement. The antenna provides more than 20 dB isolation over most of the operating band and maintains stable radiation characteristics, with simulated radiation efficiency exceeding 92% over the favorable portion of the band. The MIMO characteristics are further evaluated using ECC, diversity gain, MEG, and TARC, with an ECC below 0.001 and diversity gain close to 10 dB. A fabricated prototype is characterized experimentally, and the measured S-parameters and radiation characteristics exhibit reasonable concordance with the simulated outcomes. The obtained results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed compact configuration for X-band MIMO applications.

Article.Title: A physical activity and sitting time balance index and psychological distress in adolescents: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Luo Y.; Xu S.; Song X.
Article.Abstract: This study introduces a Physical Activity and Sitting Time Balance Index (PASTBI) to address the interplay between physical activity (PA) and sitting time, and to examine its prospective association with psychological distress in adolescents across weight statuses. This prospective cohort study used data from 8753 adolescents in the UK Millennium Cohort Study. PASTBI was calculated as objectively accelerometer-measured moderate-to-vigorous PA (min/day) divided by self-reported sitting time (h/day), both measured at age 14. Psychological distress was assessed at age 17 with the Kessler K6 scale. Linear regression models adjusted for sociodemographics, baseline depressive symptoms, diet quality, and obesity status. Among normal-weight adolescents, PASTBI showed a linear inverse association with distress (β=−0.014, p = 0.030). Among adolescents with overweight/obesity, no linear association was found ( p = 0.996); however, exploratory quadratic models suggested a possible non-linear pattern (quadratic β=− 0.0013, p = 0.003). This pattern was attenuated after Winsorization and should be interpreted cautiously; the estimated turning point should be regarded as exploratory rather than as a validated behavioral threshold. Decomposition analyses showed that active sitting (e.g., homework) was more strongly associated with distress than passive sitting (e.g., TV) (β = 0.465 vs. β = 0.042). The utility of PASTBI in characterizing prospective associations with psychological distress may differ by weight status. Among adolescents with overweight/obesity, exploratory analyses suggested a possible non-linear association, although this pattern was sensitive to Winsorization. Active sitting showed a stronger positive association with psychological distress than passive sitting. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant future trials to test whether altering the PA-to-sitting balance or introducing movement breaks influences adolescent mental health.

Article.Title: Bayesian, network, and cross-validated modeling of suicidal ideation in people with suicide attempt histories
Article.Authors: Soleimanian M.; Sayemiri Z.; Kikhavani S.
Article.Abstract: Suicidal ideation in people with suicide attempt histories may reflect dispositional, contextual, and interpersonal factors. We examined associations among Dark Triad traits, life-event stress, perceived social support, and suicidal ideation in 235 adults with suicide attempt histories recruited from several hospitals and clinics in Iran (53.6% women, 46.4% men; mean age = 33.97 years, SD = 7.90). Participants completed validated self-report measures, and data were analyzed using Bayesian path models, regularized partial-correlation networks, and repeated nested cross-validated elastic-net regression. Across analyses, greater life-event stress was associated with lower perceived social support, and lower perceived support was associated with greater suicidal ideation. Narcissism showed the clearest positive association with suicidal ideation among the Dark Triad traits. The network placed perceived social support at a central position in the multivariable system, and cross-validation indicated that models including perceived social support performed better than models without it. These cross-sectional findings identify perceived social support and narcissism as consistent correlates of suicidal ideation but do not establish temporal or causal relations.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based thorium normalization in airborne gamma-ray spectrometry for enhanced critical mineral exploration
Article.Authors: Derkacz Weihermann J.; Li Y.; Zhang M.
Article.Abstract: Airborne gamma-ray spectrometry (AGRS), also known as radiometric surveying, is one of the most cost-effective large-scale methods for geological mapping, critical mineral exploration, and radiometric anomaly detection through the measurement of potassium (K), uranium (eU), and thorium (eTh) in rocks and weathered materials. However, the identification of radioelement anomalies is often affected by factors such as soil moisture variability, precipitation, and radiation attenuation. While primary single channel maps (K, eU, and eTh) reflect bedrock composition, secondary maps derived through mathematical operations among channels can highlight geochemical processes and modify radiometric contrast. Thorium is an important radioactive element in AGRS due to its relative geochemical stability and its relevance to critical mineral and nuclear energy-related systems and has therefore been widely used to normalize potassium and uranium variations. This study proposes a target-informed, machine-learning-based methodology for normalizing thorium concentrations using a Random Forest regression model to derive a model-estimated thorium reference response. The resulting reference response is then used to calculate relative normalized deviations and enhance thorium radiometric contrast in airborne gamma-ray spectrometry data. In this study, thorium is treated as a relatively stable reference component, and thorium-derived feature transformations, including squared thorium values and radiometric ratios (eTh 2 /eU and eTh/(eU + eTh)), are deliberately combined as part of a target-informed nonlinear normalization procedure. The squared thorium term emphasizes elevated thorium responses, whereas the ratio-based variables represent complementary relationships between thorium and uranium. The model was trained and evaluated using high-resolution AGRS data, and the resulting normalized products were analyzed in a Geographic Information System (GIS) to assess their geological relevance. The resulting model-estimated thorium reference surface response was used to derive normalized thorium values, modifying the spatial contrast of the original eTh response and highlighting spatially coherent thorium variations. Results indicate that the proposed feature transformations provide complementary radiometric information that may support geological interpretation and the identification of areas potentially associated with thorium enrichment and REE-bearing materials, demonstrating the potential of machine learning as an exploratory tool for radiometric data analysis and geological exploration.

Article.Title: Perceptually indistinguishable retinal OCT synthesis and objective computational framework for detection of synthetic images
Article.Authors: Bollepalli S.; Ande S.; Bhaviripudi J.; Gunnam N.; Doshi U.; Hasan N.; Sadeghi E.; Sahoo N.; Sahel J.; Chhablani J.; Vupparaboina K.
Article.Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly deployed in medical imaging to mitigate data scarcity, enable scalable model development, and simulate disease progression; however, as synthetic data approaches photorealism, it introduces a critical vulnerability: the inability to reliably distinguish synthetic from authentic clinical data. In imaging-centric health systems, undetected synthetic data may erode dataset integrity, obscure provenance, propagate bias, and compromise reproducibility and regulatory auditability. Despite these risks, rigorous evaluation of synthetic image detectability remains limited. To this end, we synthesize high-resolution (512 × 512) retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) B-scans using four representative generative architectures, a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN), a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM), R3GAN, and a Latent Diffusion model (LDM) trained on 88,500 images from the AIREADI dataset and systematically evaluate their perceptual realism and structural fidelity. In particular, perceptual indistinguishability is assessed through two blinded human reader studies involving four retinal specialists, comprising a naïve and post-familiarization evaluation for WGAN-generated images and an independent evaluation of DDPM-generated images. In parallel, we introduce an objective computational framework predicated on gradient-derived (Sobel) representations, with downstream dimensionality reduction via principal component analysis (PCA) and support vector machine based (SVM) classifier, to probe latent structural divergences within feature space. Across both reader studies, retinal specialists demonstrated limited ability to distinguish synthetic from real OCT images. Classification accuracy remained near chance both before (59.5%) and after familiarization (56.5%) for WGAN-generated images, while DDPM-generated images yielded a similar near-chance accuracy (50.3%), indicating that perceptual indistinguishability was observed for both adversarial and diffusion-based image synthesis. In contrast, the proposed objective computational method achieved 99.93%, 99.63%, 99.91%, and 99.83% classification accuracy for WGAN, DDPM, R3GAN, and LDM-generated images, respectively on independent test datasets, demonstrating near-perfect discrimination between real and synthetic images. These findings delineate a fundamental disjunction between human perceptual judgment and computational detectability of synthetic medical images. Although generative models yield clinically plausible OCT scans, they encode latent structural signatures that remain imperceptible to expert readers yet are robustly recoverable with objective computational analysis.

Article.Title: Subdivision-based collocation methods for time fractional convection diffusion reaction equation with environmental and biomedical applications
Article.Authors: Bibi S.; Ejaz S.
Article.Abstract: Time-fractional convection diffusion reaction (TFCDR) equations are useful mathematical models to describe transport processes with memory and anomalous diffusion. Many scientific and engineering problems lead to such models, such as contaminant migration in groundwater, dispersion of atmospheric pollutants, delivery of drugs to patients, transport of biological tissue, reaction of chemicals in a heterogeneous medium. In this paper, a subdivision-based collocation method is constructed and used to numerically solve TFCDR equations. The fractional time derivative is taken in the Caputo sense, which gives the possibility to include meaningful initial conditions. The spatial domain is subdivided into uniform segments and approximated using subdivision basis functions. A fully discrete numerical formulation is developed and the stability and convergence of that formulation is thoroughly investigated. The results show that for various values of the fractional order, convection coefficient, diffusion parameter and reaction rate, the proposed subdivision based collocation result is stable and accurate, and the solution obtained by the proposed approach is accurate and stable with low computational cost. The comparisons with exact solutions and existing numerical techniques confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.

Article.Title: Metaheuristic optimized and explainable machine learning for predicting the compressive strength of lightweight foamed concrete
Article.Authors: Elsheikh A.; Qureshi M.; Inam I.; Ahmed H.; Ajwad A.; Aljarah A.; Ragab A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lightweight foamed concrete (LFC) can provide reduced structural dead load and enhanced thermal performance, however the compressive strength of LFC is determined by the complex nonlinear interactions between the mixture constituents, density and testing age, which makes the prediction and proportioning of the product difficult. This study addresses this challenge through leakage-resistant machine learning combined with metaheuristic optimization and explainable artificial intelligence. A literature-derived database of 993 observations was divided by mix-design group into 795 development records representing 276 groups and 198 unseen-test records representing 69 independent groups, with no overlap. Random forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) models, together with their Leopard Seal Optimizer (LSO), Harris Hawks Optimizer (HHO), and Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA) optimized variants, were assessed using 10-fold grouped cross-validation and a completely held-out test set. SHAP and PDP-ICE analyses were subsequently applied to the best-generalizing model. LSO-XGB achieved the strongest grouped out-of-fold performance ((R 2 = 0.888); RMSE = 3.93 MPa), whereas HHO-XGB performed best on unseen data ((R 2 = 0.875); RMSE = 4.10 MPa), reducing the baseline-XGB RMSE by 4.1%. HHO-XGB also produced a median absolute error of 0.82 MPa, with 95.96% and 97.47% of predictions within 5 and 10 MPa, respectively. Binder was the dominant predictor, contributing 45.4% of the global SHAP importance, followed by measured density at 16.9%. The proposed framework within the represented data domain can support preliminary LFC mixture screening and guide locally validated, multi-objective experimental designs balancing strength, density, cost, and environmental impact.

Article.Title: Development and psychometric evaluation of the halal food and nutrition literacy scale (HFNLS) in Turkish adults
Article.Authors: Şahin Bayram S.; Karademir E.; Büyükdere Y.; Arı Gedik B.; Ersoy Yalçın S.
Article.Abstract: Religious beliefs, particularly Islamic halal principles, influence food preferences and consumer behavior. This study highlights the global significance of halal certification and the halal industry. Furthermore, it aimed to clarify the definitions of halal food and nutrition literacy-terms that are not well-defined in the current literature, and to develop the Halal Food and Nutrition Literacy Scale (HFNLS) to assess this concept among Muslim adults. This methodological study was conducted in three stages: (1) literature review and item pool generation, (2) expert evaluation and optimization of items, and (3) psycometric evaluation. Data were collected through a web-based, interviewer-administered method. The study sample size consisted of 552 adults aged 20 years or older. An exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted in 285 participants, and a confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was performed using data from an independent sample of 267 Muslim adults. EFA yielded a 28-item scale with three dimensions that together explained 52.764% of the total variance. As a result of CFA, the fit indices showed an acceptable and near-good fit of the data to the hypothesized model (χ 2 /df = 2.657, p < 0.001, root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) = 0.053, standardized root mean residual (SRMR) = 0.047, goodness-of-fit index (GFI) = 0.913, comparative fit index (CFI) = 0.927, incremental fit index (IFI) = 0.925, Tucker Lewis index (TLI) = 0.906, and normed fit index (NFI) = 0.880). The Cronbach’s alpha (α) coefficient was 0.917 for the total scale, indicating excellent internal consistency. The Cronbach’s α coefficients for each dimension exceeded 0.80. The developed HFNLS demonstrated satisfactory construct validity and high internal consistency as a multidimensional instrument for assessing halal food and nutrition literacy among Muslim adults. The three-factor structure identified by EFA was supported by CFA, indicating that functional, interactive, and critical literacy represent related but distinct dimensions of the construct. These findings support the use of the HFNLS in research and practice; however, further validation in culturally, geographically, and religiously diverse Muslim populations is warranted.

Article.Title: Spatial heterogeneity and driving mechanisms of tourism resources vary across county types in Central China
Article.Authors: Jun L.
Article.Abstract: This paper selects Xinxian County (mountainous revolutionary heritage area), Linzhou City (mountainous complex landscape), and Huaxian County (plain-linear heritage) in Henan Province as representative cases exhibiting pronounced geomorphic and cultural contrasts. The study systematically applies four spatial analytical methods: the Voronoi polygon coefficient of variation, kernel density estimation, standard deviation ellipse, and the Geodetector model. Through this integrated methodological framework, the study reveals the distinct spatial differentiation patterns of tourism resources across the three counties and uncovers their underlying, context-specific driving mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that: (1) While tourism resources in all three counties are spatially concentrated, their configurations diverge markedly: Xinxian County manifests a balanced “multi-core network” structure; Linzhou City is characterized by a terrain-constrained “mountain strip” pattern; and Huaxian County follows a “canal-radiation” corridor structure shaped by historical waterway infrastructure. (2) The dominant spatial drivers differ, representing distinct evolutionary pathways: Xinxian’s development is strongly associated with capital and transportation support; the distribution pattern of Linzhou is closely related to its rugged terrain and ecology; and Huaxian’s distribution is highly correlated with historical heritage inertia coupled with high-density population adherence. (3) Factor interactions exhibit significant synergistic enhancement. By introducing a multidimensional analytical framework comprising a “foundational natural basis,” a “socioeconomic supporting guarantee,” and an “animating socio-cultural core,” this study offers a contribution to the literature beyond single-factor determinism. It suggests that county-level tourism spatial configurations are the outcome of non-linear spatial coupling among geographic constraints, economic investments, and historical legacies. The findings provide empirically grounded, place-sensitive insights that may inform spatial governance to support the differentiated, high-quality development of county-level human-environmental systems.

Article.Title: Self-assembling peptide hydrogel SPG-178 effectively prevents postoperative pancreatic fistula compared with polyglycolic acid mesh with fibrin glue in rats
Article.Authors: Kado T.; Tomimaru Y.; Akita H.; Uesugi K.; Tahara K.; Ueda H.; Sakano Y.; Gotoh K.; Mukai Y.; Sasaki K.; Hasegawa S.; Yamada D.; Noda T.; Takahashi H.; Kobayashi S.; Doki Y.; Eguchi H.
Article.Abstract: Postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) is a common and potentially life-threatening complication after pancreatectomy. Although various methods have attempted to prevent POPF, none have proven to be fully effective. This study used a rat model to compare the efficacy of a self-assembling peptide hydrogel, SPG-178, in preventing POPF with that of polyglycolic acid mesh combined with fibrin glue (PGA + FG). A rat model of POPF was created by pancreatic transection. The rats were randomly assigned to groups in which the pancreatic stump was untreated (control) or treated with SPG-178 or PGA + FG. The groups were compared based on ascitic amylase levels, macroscopic findings at relaparotomy (saponification and adhesion), and histological examination of the resected specimens. Three days after transection, the mean (± standard deviation) ascitic amylase level was significantly lower in the SPG-178 group (109 ± 58 IU/L) than in the control (283 ± 126 IU/L) and PGA + FG (219 ± 128 IU/L) groups ( p < 0.0001). On relaparotomy, saponification around the pancreatic stump and intra-abdominal adhesions were markedly reduced in the SPG-178 group compared with the other groups. Histological analysis also found milder edema, necrosis, hemorrhage, and inflammatory cell infiltration in the SPG-178 group than in the PGA + FG group. SPG-178 demonstrated favorable sealing performance compared with PGA + FG in this rat model. These findings support further preclinical and clinical evaluation of SPG-178 as a novel sealant for preventing postoperative pancreatic fistula.

Article.Title: Enhanced UV-assisted quartz wafer bonding: unveiling the critical role of humidity gradient in surface hydroxylation and interfacial strength
Article.Authors: Wan Y.; Zhan C.; Peng K.; Zhou L.; Wu F.
Article.Abstract: Relative humidity (RH) is a critical but frequently overlooked variable that significantly impacts the reliability of ultraviolet (UV)-activated quartz-crystal wafer bonding. This study examined how relative humidity during UV activation influences hydroxyl- and water-related surface chemistry and measured interfacial strength. Exposing quartz-crystal wafers to combined 185/254 nm UV irradiation under controlled relative humidity (15–90%) revealed a non-monotonic humidity dependence of hydroxyl- and water-related spectroscopic responses, with the largest response at 45% RH. The mean measured tensile strength increased from 2.64 MPa at 15% RH to a maximum of 9.88 MPa at 45% RH. It then decreased with further increasing humidity, reaching 2.01 MPa at 90% RH. This decline is consistent with excess adsorbed water hindering intimate interfacial contact and subsequent silanol condensation. Cross-sectional TEM and EDS compared local interfaces formed at 30%, 45%, 60% and 75% RH, revealing differences in interfacial contrast and Si/O signal profiles. These findings identify a practical humidity-control window for improving the reproducibility and strength of atmospheric-pressure UV-assisted quartz-crystal wafer bonding, supporting its development for wafer-level packaging of quartz crystal resonators.

Article.Title: Interactive effects of moisture level, lactic acid bacteria, and ensiling duration on fermentation and microbial communities in barnyard millet silage
Article.Authors: Jeong S.; Soundharrajan I.; Han O.; Jung J.; Choi K.
Article.Abstract: The present study evaluated the effects of lactic acid bacteria (LAB), moisture content, and ensiling duration on nutrient composition, fermentation quality, and microbial dynamics in barnyard millet (BM) silage. BM forage was ensiled under different moisture conditions using single inoculants ( Lactiplantibacillus plantarum -TC, Lactobacillus brevis 5 M, and Lactobacillus buchneri 6 M) or combined LAB inoculants for 10, 20, and 30 days. LAB inoculation improved fermentation quality by increasing lactic acid and acetic acid production, lowering pH, and inhibiting butyric acid production. Crude protein content remained stable, whereas reductions in neutral detergent fibre (ADF) and acid detergent fibre (NDF) varied with inoculant treatments. Microbial community analysis showed that L. plantarum became the dominant bacterial species, while mixed inoculants promoted greater LAB diversity. Yeast communities were influenced by inoculum, moisture level, and ensiling duration, with Issatchenkia orientalis and Ustilago davisii predominating under different treatments. Fungal communities showed distinct temporal and treatment-dependent patterns, with Ustilago spp. and Mucor circinelloides as major taxa. Correlation analysis revealed positive associations between L. plantarum and lactic acid production, while L. buchneri was associated with acetic acid accumulation. Overall, LAB inoculation was associated with improvements in fermentation quality, microbial stability, and nutrient preservation. However, the inoculants showed significant effects under low-moisture conditions throughout the ensiling period.

Article.Title: Adaptive deanonymization of blockchain transactions leveraging integrative neural architectures in decentralized networks
Article.Authors: Saxena R.; Chaurasia B.; Awasthi A.; Upadhyay L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The pseudonymous nature of decentralized networks like Bitcoin presents tremendous obstacles for regulatory compliance, forensic auditing, and cybercrime investigation. Traditional heuristics and single-modality machine learning (ML) frameworks provide partial transparency but usually suffer from the modality isolation problem, which fails to consider spatial graph structure, temporal transaction velocity, and local metadata patterns simultaneously. To break these limitations, in this paper, we propose an adaptive behavioral deanonymization method for blockchain transactions at the entity level based on an integrative neural architecture (CNN → LSTM → GNN) that dynamically focuses on spatial, temporal, and structural signals based on the behavior of the entity. The integrative neural uses a Disjoint Set Union (DSU) algorithm to combine temporary address artifacts into 140,235 resolved actor clusters, lowering ledger noise by 67.2%. The proposed architecture uses 1D-Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for extracting local structural fingerprints, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for capturing temporal sequence velocity, and Graph Neural Networks (GNN) over a dynamic k-Nearest Neighbor (k-NN) adjacency matrix for aggregating neighborhood context. The architecture uses cost-sensitive learning (weighted cross-entropy) to tackle the significant class imbalance (1:500) to maintain analytical authenticity and forensics standards without synthetic distortion. The proposed architecture is assessed on a sample of a dataset of 427,625 transactions, achieving an overall classification accuracy of approximately 97%, which is better than the baseline models, and generating a transparent, explainable audit trail using SHAP and LIME feature attribution.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: cost-sensitive learning; pseudonymity; Bitcoin; class imbalance; SHAP feature attribution

Article.Title: BioInteract combines residue-level cross-attention with protein-language and physicochemical priors for interpretable drug–target interaction prediction
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Zhang Q.; Liu X.; Wang Z.; Cheng J.; Huang Z.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of drug–target interactions (DTIs) can support the prioritisation of candidate pairs, yet published models are usually compared through numbers quoted across papers whose protocols differ, and their attribution outputs are rarely accompanied by an explicit statement of where the model may be trusted. We present BioInteract, a DTI framework combining a chemistry-aware molecular graph encoder, an ESM-2/physicochemical protein residue encoder with a configured domain-label channel, and bidirectional cross-attention, and we evaluate it inside a matched-protocol benchmark on the Davis kinase inhibitor dataset in which every model is trained with one shared partition, seed, optimiser, schedule and threshold rule. The comparison is a three-model ladder that changes one component at a time, so that adding the frozen ESM-2 representation and then replacing concatenation with cross-attention can be read separately. Both steps help, but by protocol-dependent amounts: the protein language model adds 0.120 and 0.063 AUPRC under the random and Target-ID-held-out protocols, whereas cross-attention adds 0.067 and 0.201 AUPRC under the same two protocols. A breadth check across two further architecture families places these differences in context: on the random split the five architectures tested fall within a narrow band, so the controlled Target-ID-held-out ladder carries the informative contrast. We audit chemical and sequence similarity across all partitions, evaluate exact-sequence-grouped cold-start protocols, and report leakage-aware diagnostic controls. On a strict exact-entity-novel BindingDB cohort, whose construction is documented as a complete row-level filtering waterfall for both the curated-articles snapshot and the full BindingDB release, the frozen Davis checkpoint achieved an AUROC of 0.560 and an AUPRC of 0.340; an applicability-domain analysis attributes this limited transfer principally to ligand and target novelty relative to Davis. The attribution analyses generate hypotheses about model-relevant atoms and residues, but, in line with evidence from models trained with explicit non-covalent interaction supervision, unsupervised attention is not treated here as a recovered interaction mechanism. BioInteract therefore contributes an audited, reproducible and domain-of-applicability-aware DTI reference rather than a new architectural principle.
