Article.Title: Green-synthesized Plectranthus amboinicus derived Z-scheme rGO-based CeO2/g-C3N4 nanocomposite for visible-light-driven dye degradation, antimicrobial activity and ecological safety
Article.Authors: George S.; Sellappa K.
Article.Abstract: Synthetic dyes such as methylene blue (MB) are persistent and not effectively removed by conventional adsorption or biological treatment processes, motivating the development of advanced oxidation technologies. Herein, an rGO/CeO 2 /g-C 3 N 4 ternary heterostructure was synthesized via an eco-friendly route, in which Plectranthus amboinicus leaf extract was used to reduce graphene oxide prior to the incorporating CeO 2 and g-C 3 N 4 . Structural, morphological, and optical characterization confirmed successful formation of the ternary heterostructure, with UV-Vis DRS analysis specifically revealing an optical band gap of 2.50 eV. Process optimization using response surface methodology with central composite design (RSM-CCD) yielded a maximum experimental degradation efficiency of 98.6% within 60 min. Scavenger experiments identified photogenerated holes as the principal oxidizing species, with a secondary contribution from superoxide radicals and only minor involvement of hydroxyl radicals. PL and EIS results, together with XPS and band-position analysis, support the proposed rGO-assisted direct Z-scheme charge-transfer pathway, which facilitates charge separation while retaining strong redox potentials. GC-MS profiling detected partially oxidized aromatic intermediates consistent with stepwise degrdation rather than complete mineralization. The catalyst showed a gradual decrease in activity over five consecutive reuse cycles and concentration-dependent antibacterial activity but no antifungal effect, and reduced MB-associated phytotoxicity from a highly to a moderately phytotoxic range, indicating substantial but incomplete detoxification. These findings demonstrate the potential of the green ternary photocatalyst for visible-light-driven dye wastewater treatment.

Article.Title: Strength-permeability-disintegration evolution and microstructural coupling mechanisms of oil-contaminated silty sand at natural moisture content
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Zheng W.; Liu J.; Du J.; Ai X.; Li G.; Cao J.
Article.Abstract: Petroleum contamination can alter particle contacts and fluid distribution, thereby affecting the engineering behaviour of soil. This study investigates oil-contaminated silty sand under natural moisture conditions using unconfined compression, static-water disintegration, falling-head permeability, SEM–EDS, NMR, image analysis, and apparent water-droplet contact-angle tests. The UCS decreased continuously from 31.95 kPa at 0% oil content to 12.63 kPa at 12%, representing a 60.5% reduction. In contrast, resistance to static-water disintegration increased with oil content: the uncontaminated specimen disintegrated within approximately 50 s, whereas the 8% and 12% specimens remained largely intact after 24 h. Hydraulic conductivity and time to first water discharge showed non-monotonic responses, reaching measured maxima of 13.52 × 10 − 3 cm/s and 120 s, respectively, near 5% oil content. This response is regarded as an empirical turning feature under the present test conditions rather than a universal threshold. The microscopic results suggest changes in local particle-surface appearance, fluid-relaxation behaviour, visible interparticle spaces, and composite-surface wetting response. Overall, oil contamination weakened compressive resistance while delaying static-water disintegration, and the hydraulic response resulted from the combined effects of initial water entry, fluid distribution, local flow-path changes, and possible preferential flow.

Article.Title: Bikinin induces genotype- and time-dependent changes in barley growth, leaf architecture, and phytohormone profiles
Article.Authors: Groszyk J.; Waligórski P.; Oklestkova J.; Przyborowski M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Brassinosteroids are major regulators of plant growth, architecture, and stress responses, but the consequences of perturbing BR signaling may depend strongly on genotype and developmental stage. We investigated the effects of bikinin, an inhibitor of plant Glycogen Synthase Kinase 3-like kinases, on early development of two barley ( Hordeum vulgare L.) cultivars, Golden Promise (GP) and Haruna Nijo (HN). Bikinin induced pronounced genotype-, organ-, and time-dependent responses. In GP, shoot elongation increased from day 6 onward, whereas HN showed an earlier stimulation followed by attenuation of the response. Root biomass increased transiently in both genotypes but declined at later stages in HN. Bikinin strongly increased first- and second-leaf LJI and differentially affected the lengths of successive leaf blades and sheaths. These morphological responses were accompanied by transient increases in abscisic acid, dynamic changes in jasmonic acid, an overall decrease in indole-3-acetic acid, and changes in selected cytokinin forms, including trans-zeatin, cis-zeatin riboside, and isopentenyladenine. No consistent bikinin-induced changes in HvGSK2.1 or HvBZR1 transcript abundance were detected. Endogenous BR profiles showed descriptive genotype- and time-dependent variation but were not subjected to inferential testing. Overall, inhibition of GSK3-like kinases altered barley growth and hormone profiles without uniformly promoting biomass accumulation. The contrasting temporal responses of GP and HN demonstrate that genetic background and developmental stage are critical determinants of bikinin responsiveness.

Article.Authors: Ela A.; Islam M.; Kabir S.; Akter M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ipomoea aquatica possesses high flavonoid and polyphenol content, with pharmacological applications as a liver tonic for digestive disorders, diabetes, and inflammation. Additionally, this study was supported by GC–MS phytochemical profiling, in silico docking, ADMET, toxicity prediction, and molecular flexibility simulation. Stability of the ligand-receptor complex conformations for all four hits was supported by CABS-flex simulation, confirming the predicted binding modes. The results support the further mechanistic and pharmacological exploration of I. aquatica as a potential hepatoprotective natural product candidate.

Article.Title: ECLIPSE v2.0: a reproducible scaffold for severe confirmatory testing through preregistration, single-shot validation, and static-analysis screening
Article.Authors: Sjöberg Tala C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The replication crisis has exposed systematic methodological weaknesses across the empirical sciences, yet existing infrastructure offers little technical enforcement and few reproducible tools for assessing rigor. Three instruments are introduced, each an operational tool rather than a definitive measure: the Eclipse Integrity Score, a heuristic operationalization of protocol-level integrity across five dimensions; the Standardized Test-set Discrepancy Score, a descriptive signal flagging holdout results unusually good relative to cross-validation folds, screened against empirically derived cutoffs rather than nominal significance levels; and an Automated Code Auditor screening scripts for protocol violations. Controlled construct checks demonstrate component non-redundancy and ranking stability under the synthetic generator and weighting schemes used, but not external validity. No retrospective corpus can validly compute the score alongside replication outcomes, so we pre-specify a prospective test of incremental validity over binary preregistration and cite evidence that broad methodological-quality indicators track external-validation performance in clinical prediction models, which is indirectly relevant rather than a validation of those dimensions. ECLIPSE is offered as a scaffold, not a guarantee of compliance.

Article.Title: Interactive team cognition during Apollo 11’s first crewed lunar landing under life-or-death conditions
Article.Authors: Eldadi O.; Pincu I.; Cooke N.; Weigelt M.; Tenenbaum G.; Loeb A.
Article.Abstract: How do expert teams manage uncertainty and emotion when lives depend on coordinated performance? We present the first dual-channel analysis of team cognition in action: how a crew distributes information, coordination and affect between its private (crew-to-crew) and public (crew-to-ground) channels across a complete spaceflight mission. All 13,114 Apollo 11 statements (161,954 words) were coded with a validated six-category taxonomy and an emotional valence scheme. The crew expressed uncertainty at more than double the rate privately (21.11%) compared with the public channel (10.28%), while negative affect was four times more prevalent in private communication (2.82% versus 0.71%). This pattern persisted during the life-threatening descent and landing sequence. The private channel supported iterative uncertainty processing, with an uncertainty statement followed by further uncertainty in 18.78% of cases privately against 8.46% publicly, while the public channel exhibited a tight information–confirmation protocol. An expert team can thus actively partition cognitive and affective processing even under genuine life-or-death conditions, with implications for communication architecture, training and crew autonomy in future deep-space missions.

Article.Title: Convergence bounds for fixed, adaptive, and stochastic gradient methods under Polyak–Łojasiewicz geometry
Article.Authors: Farhang Y.; Öztel B.; Yıldırım S.; Viga Ş.; Cifci M.; Yıldırım F.
Article.Abstract: The Polyak–Łojasiewicz (PL) inequality offers a useful way to study gradient-based optimization beyond the setting of strong convexity, while still allowing linear convergence under suitable smoothness conditions. This study develops a unified descent-based analysis for fixed-step gradient descent, safeguarded objective-gap step rules, Armijo backtracking, and mini-batch stochastic gradient descent. For the deterministic methods, the analysis provides explicit contraction bounds that show how convergence depends on smoothness, gradient domination, and step-selection parameters. In the stochastic setting, conditional unbiasedness together with a bounded conditional variance leads to a finite-time expectation bound and an upper estimate for the asymptotic residual neighborhood. The analysis is further extended to generalized gradient inequalities. Smooth explicit gradient descent yields linear or polynomial convergence depending on the exponent, whereas superlinear behavior for exponents below one half is established separately for an implicit decrease sequence. This distinction avoids transferring continuous-time behavior directly to explicit discrete gradient iterations. For continuously differentiable squared-error models, uniform spectral bounds on the Jacobian Gram matrix are used to derive regional gradient domination relative to the zero-loss target. A complementary path-length argument gives a sufficient condition for trajectory containment and establishes convergence to zero loss under the stated regional assumptions. Numerical illustrations based on quadratic objectives, power functions, implicit recurrences, stochastic models, and a constant-kernel least-squares example are used to examine the theoretical bounds, accepted Armijo steps, backtracking costs, convergence regimes, and stochastic uncertainty.

Article.Title: Fluorescence detection of hypochlorous acid via an ATP-controlled DNA nanodevice
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Zhou X.; He H.; Ma C.; Yuan D.
Article.Abstract: Hypochlorous acid (HClO) is a vital constituent of the reactive oxygen species (ROS) family, predominantly generated during the myeloperoxidase-catalyzed reaction in macrophages and neutrophils. Clinically, HClO is considered a potential biomarker, with abnormal levels closely associated with the onset and progression of numerous diseases, such as atherosclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis. Therefore, a highly sensitive and specific HClO detection method is desired for its quantitative monitoring. Herein, a fluorescence detection method (ATP-controlled DNA nanodevice) is proposed for HClO detection. In this method, HClO can significantly enhance the system’s fluorescence signal by separating the FAM fluorophore from the Dabcyl quencher. The constructed device demonstrated a detection range of 0.01-1 µM with a limit of detection (LOD) of 8.774 nM under optimal conditions. Moreover, the proposed method successfully quantified HClO in practical samples, such as tap water. The presented experimental data confirm the promising efficacy of this method in relevant fields.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: hypochlorous acid detection; DNA nanotechnology; fluorescence sensing
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Advanced biosensing and bioanalysis techniques; Engineering > Biomedical Engineering > Biosensors and Analytical Detection; Chemistry > Spectroscopy > Molecular Sensors and Ion Detection

Article.Title: Metabolic and musculoskeletal implications of a ketogenic diet using animal and coconut saturated fat in rats
Article.Authors: Rodríguez S.; de Araújo I.; Carvalho A.; Neto M.; Dick-de-Paula I.; Jordão Junior A.; Shimano A.; Ramalho L.; Gouveia C.; A. de Paula F.
Article.Abstract: The ketogenic diet (KD) and coconut oil have been associated with weight loss benefits, but their effects on bone health remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a KD containing virgin coconut oil (VCO) on bone metabolism. Eight-week-old Wistar Hannover rats ( n = 8 per group) were assigned to four groups for 8 weeks: soy control (SC) with standard AIN-93 M diet, coconut control (CC) with VCO replacing soybean oil, KD with 81% animal fat, and KD-VCO with 40.5% animal fat + 40.5% VCO. Body composition was measured via dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, while bone parameters were assessed using microcomputed tomography (µCT) and biomechanical testing. KD (40.86 ± 1.06%) and KD-VCO (39 ± 1.06%) groups showed higher fat mass percentages only in comparison to SC (31.66 ± 1.06%); p < 0.05. Lean mass was lower in KD (191 ± 4.64 g) than in SC (245 ± 4.64 g), and lean mass percentage was reduced in both KD (57.75 ± 2.08%) and KD-VCO (59.37 ± 2.08%) compared to SC (66.75 ± 2.08%); p < 0.05. µCT revealed cortical microstructure deterioration in both KD groups. Biomechanical testing showed decreased bone strength in KD groups: SC= (68.23 ± 2.06 N), KD (51.54 ± 2.20 N), and KD-VCO (59.26 ± 2.20 N); p < 0.05. In conclusion, the inclusion of coconut oil in a KD did not prevent the adverse effects on body composition and bone strength.

Article.Title: Dissociative electron attachment dynamics in pulsed Cl2 plasma process: characteristic pulse-OFF time on chamber diameter
Article.Authors: Ono S.; Jhan C.; Saha A.; Shiratani M.; Samukawa S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pulsed-plasmas are widely used in semiconductor dry etching because of lower plasma-induced damage compared with continuous-wave (CW) operation. Notably, in electronegative gases such as Cl, significant amounts of negative ions form in the afterglow, producing an ion-ion plasma that enables the transport of low energy ions to the surface and thereby reducing defects of etch patterns. This work studies the impact of the chamber size on plasma loss characteristics and the resulting timescale for ion-ion plasma formation using time-resolved Langmuir probe measurements applied to plasma systems with two different diameters. Relative to the large diameter chamber, the small diameter chamber exhibited more than twice the radial electron diffusion loss and ion loss to the wall during the discharge. In the pulse-OFF phase, the plasma diffusion rates were ∼1.4 × 10 4 s − 1 and ∼2.9 × 10 3 s − 1 , demonstrating that chamber geometry strongly governs diffusion-driven losses and transient plasma behavior during upscaling. GaN etching revealed a chamber-size-dependent optimal OFF time: the etch rate peaked at 1.8 nm/min at 200 μs using the large diameter and 5.5 nm/min at 100 μs using the small diameter. These results provide practical guidance for pulse-OFF time optimization and establish a foundation for large diameter pulsed-plasma modeling toward mass manufacturing.

Article.Title: The KLF4–SLC25A4 mitochondrial axis regulates ferroptotic vulnerability and sunitinib sensitivity in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Tian S.; Chen H.; Zhao W.; Shen D.; Wang C.; Zhao X.; Liu H.; Ma X.; Zhang X.; Mai H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sunitinib resistance remains a major therapeutic challenge in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). Through integrated transcriptomic profiling and mitochondrial gene screening, we identified SLC25A4 as a ferroptosis-associated tumor suppressor. SLC25A4 expression was significantly downregulated in ccRCC tissues and correlated with poor prognosis, advanced stage, and increased invasiveness. Functional assays revealed that SLC25A4 inhibits tumor proliferation and invasion by promoting ferroptosis, elevating reactive oxygen species (ROS), impairing mitochondrial membrane potential, and suppressing antioxidant defense. Mechanistically, we identified KLF4 as an upstream transcription factor of SLC25A4, regulating its expression in a promoter motif-dependent manner. KLF4 expression was reduced in tumors and positively correlated with SLC25A4 levels and patient survival. KLF4 overexpression reactivated SLC25A4 transcription, restored ferroptotic signaling, and inhibited tumor growth. Importantly, the KLF4–SLC25A4 axis sensitized ccRCC cells to sunitinib in vitro and in vivo. Knockdown of either KLF4 or SLC25A4 conferred drug resistance, whereas KLF4 re-expression re-sensitized resistant cells by enhancing oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. Clinical tissue analysis confirmed reduced SLC25A4 expression in sunitinib-resistant tumors. Together, our findings uncover a previously unrecognized KLF4–SLC25A4 regulatory axis that contributes to ferroptosis and therapeutic response, offering a potential strategy to improve sunitinib sensitivity in ccRCC.

Article.Title: Controlled release of gentamicin from chitosan/TiO2 /berberis aristata bionanocomposite films: from traditional to advanced dressing
Article.Authors: Zainab N/A.; Rehman W.; Shah A.; Bibi S.; Abid O.; Farghaly T.; Rasheed L.; Alzahrani A.; Khan N.
Article.Abstract: Embedding antibacterial and antifungal additives into wound dressing materials is currently an innovative approach. Berberis Aristata (BA) is a potent plant that has been used for wound healing since ancient times. Transitioning from traditional to advanced setup, wound dressing/films based on chitosan (Cs), titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ), and BA were developed. Solution casting-based techniques were employed for the preparation of films. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and X-ray diffraction (XRD), Scanning electron microscopic (SEM) were done for structural and morphological analysis of films. FTIR and XRD confirmed the structural modifications of Cs. Swelling behavior, hydrolytic and oxidative stability, antibacterial and antioxidant activity of Cs/TiO 2 /BA were also evaluated. In vitro Gentamycin (drug) loading and release behavior of films were checked. Cs/TiO 2 /BA (2%) film not only showed excellent drug loading efficiency (72.5%) but exhibited excellent antimicrobial activity (35 mm), oxidative and hydrolytic stability (27 days). The phytochemical analysis confirmed the presence of alkaloids and phenols in BA, which may be the reason for its good antioxidant and antibacterial response. These investigations showed that the Cs/TiO 2 /BA system could be a viable option for applications in wound dressings that require sustained drug loading and release efficiency.

Article.Title: A low-cost environmental monitoring framework for climate-sensitive disease surveillance in the Peruvian Amazon
Article.Authors: Fernandez-Camacho B.; Ascencio E.; Barja A.; Revilla L.; Villa D.; Brou P.; Ferreyra-Chombo Y.; Bartolini-Arana L.; Lowe R.; Carrasco-Escobar G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Malaria, dengue and leptospirosis are endemic in the Peruvian Amazon, where routine surveillance operates without village-scale environmental observation. We report the yield of that monitoring framework, the completeness of its meteorological record, and its cost, operated at village scale alongside notifiable disease surveillance. Across ten villages along the Iquitos–Nauta Highway, we operated drones, automatic weather stations, low-cost particulate monitors and acoustic recorders, inspected terrain and geolocated cases. Co-creation with the regional health directorate and villages governed deployment and data handling. Streams were harmonized into a spatial database at daily to annual resolution. Nine quarterly campaigns between March 2023 and March 2026 covered 14 flight areas, 14 km 2 per round, and produced 756 orthomosaics from 1.16 million images. Sensors returned 678,564 meteorological and 2,778,363 air-quality records and 4349.75 h of audio. Completely missing outdoor-temperature weeks ranged from 5.1 to 61.4% across sites. Of 10,883 notified individuals, 1489 (13.7%) were georeferenced, with coverage of 8.3% in 2010–2015 and 31.1% in 2021–2025. Capital outlay was about USD 22,050, each campaign about USD 3660. The harmonized series is intended to inform vector control and case detection for local health authorities and stakeholders.

Article.Title: Influence of injection solvent and serial dilution on matrix effect in GC–MS/MS multiresidue pesticide analysis: a factorial study across seven herbal matrices
Article.Authors: Enia M.; Mahmoud H.; Nagy H.; Hasanen J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Matrix effects (MEs) remain a major challenge in gas chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (GC–MS/MS) analysis of pesticide residues, often leading to inaccurate quantification and reduced method robustness. In this study, the impact of injection solvent composition and dilution on ME was systematically evaluated for 219 pesticide residues across seven complex herbal matrices (dry mint, chamomile, green coffee, fennel, hibiscus, lemongrass, and thyme) using a factorial design approach. Two injection solvents, ethyl acetate (EA) and hexane–acetone (9:1, v/v; HA), were compared in terms of their ability to minimize signal suppression and enhancement effects. Results revealed that solvent polarity plays a critical role in determining the extent and direction of ME. When EA was used, 60% of the pesticides fell outside the negligible ME range (80–120%), showing a strong enhancement effect (53%). In contrast, HA substantially reduced ME, with only 30% of pesticides affected. Across individual matrices, dilution had variable effects: in most cases (e.g., chamomile, dry mint, fennel), dilution decreased suppression but intensified enhancement, while in pigment-rich matrices such as hibiscus and thyme, suppression became dominant. This study provides practical insights into optimizing injection solvent selection and dilution strategies to control matrix effects in GC–MS/MS analysis. The findings highlight hexane–acetone as a more reliable injection solvent for multi-residue pesticide analysis in complex herbal matrices and underscore the necessity of matrix-specific optimization to ensure accurate and reproducible results. These outcomes contribute to improving analytical method performance and reliability in food safety and regulatory monitoring.

Article.Title: Prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea risk in stroke patients and its association with stroke severity and recurrence in Pakistan: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Noor S.; Naeem S.; Samuel S.; Arif S.; Xia H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is highly prevalent among stroke patients and may adversely affect stroke outcomes. However, data from South Asian populations, particularly Pakistan, remain scarce. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of OSA risk in stroke patients from the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad and to evaluate its association with stroke severity and recurrence. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 306 stroke patients recruited from hospitals, rehabilitation centres, and stroke units between June and September 2024. OSA risk was assessed using the STOP-BANG questionnaire, and stroke severity was evaluated with the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS). Associations between OSA risk categories and stroke severity and recurrence were analysed using chi-square tests. Of the 306 participants (54.9% male, 95% CI 49.3–60.5; the majority were aged 46–60 years), 41.8% (95% CI 36.3–47.4) were classified as high risk, 35.0% (95% CI 29.6–40.3) as intermediate risk, and 23.2% (95% CI 18.5–27.9) as low risk for OSA. Ischemic stroke was the most common subtype (71.2%, 95% CI 66.1–76.3). Stroke recurrence was reported in 48.0% of participants (95% CI 42.4–53.6). Higher OSA risk was significantly associated with greater stroke severity (χ² = 53.444, p < 0.001; OR for moderate-to-severe stroke, high- versus low-risk, 11.87, 95% CI 5.41–26.05) and increased stroke recurrence (χ² = 36.893, p < 0.001; OR for high- versus low-risk, 6.80, 95% CI 3.49–13.24). A high proportion of stroke patients in Pakistan screened at intermediate-to-high risk for OSA using STOP-BANG, and OSA risk category was significantly associated with both stroke severity and recurrence. These findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating; prospective studies with objective OSA testing and multivariable adjustment for shared risk factors are needed before OSA screening can be recommended as a modifiable target in routine post-stroke care.

Article.Title: Complex topologies in phase separated droplets predicted from universal phase diagram
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Karpen G.; Safran S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Phase separation of two phase separating solutes in a common solvent can result in mesoscale (micron-sized) droplets with complex topologies of the domains of each solute within each droplet. Such topologies have been observed in vitro in systems of chromatin oligomers, biomolecular condensates, and polymeric mixtures. In these systems, the solutes phase separate from the solvent into droplets; within each droplet, further phase separation can occur between the two solutes. In some systems, the extent of demixing can be modulated by an additional molecular component. The minimal free energy topologies are predicted as universal functions of the interfacial tension ratios and fractions of each solute within a droplet. We compare the theoretically predicted droplet topologies with those reported in several experimental systems and discuss how the predicted topologies vary with the tensions. Experimental aspects that may depend on the kinetics or molecular weight variations in the system are also discussed.

Article.Title: Combined effects of video self-modeling and preferred music on motor skill acquisition and psychological engagement in adolescent shot-put learning
Article.Authors: Boujabli M.; Jebabli N.; Elkholi S.; Souaifi M.; Chtourou H.; Dhahbi W.
Article.Abstract: This exploratory cluster-randomized pilot study investigated the individual and combined effects of Video Self-Modeling (VSM) and preferred music during warm-up on physical, technical, and psychological performance following a nine-week shot-put learning program in secondary school students. Eighty students, nested within four intact classes, were allocated to four conditions at the class level (one class per condition): neutral self-talk with no music (control), VSM only, preferred music only (PM), and combined VSM plus preferred music (CVSMPM). Shot-put distance, technical execution, rating of perceived exertion, feeling scale, and situational motivation (SIMS) were assessed. Physical performance improved significantly in all groups. Because randomization occurred at the class level with a single class per condition, intervention and class-level effects cannot be statistically separated; results are reported as descriptive contrasts. Descriptive contrast analysis showed medium-to-large effect-size differences favoring the combined intervention over control on physical and technical performance at formative (0.79 < d < 1.50) and summative assessments (0.62 < d < 1.32). Feeling-scale scores increased with large-to-very-large effects in CVSMPM and PM (1.34 < d < 2.02), and situational motivation improved with medium-to-large effects in CVSMPM (0.87 < d < 1.69) and PM (0.79 < d < 1.21). CVSMPM showed the most consistent pattern of medium-to-large effect-size differences in motor skill acquisition, technical proficiency, and psychological engagement relative to the other conditions. Given the cluster design and exploratory analyses, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and hypothesis-generating.

Article.Title: Exploring the Antibacterial Potential of Nepeta crispa Essential Oil Against Agro-Food Bacteria
Article.Authors: Koushki M.; Hajian-Maleki H.; Barazandeh F.; Shams-Bakhsh M.
Article.Abstract: Herbal essential oils are considered suitable candidates for controlling plant diseases due to their safety for humans and the environment, as well as their economic benefits. This study investigates the antibacterial activity of the essential oil of a native plant of Iran, Nepeta crispa Willd. After extraction of the essential oil by hydrodistillation, the antibacterial effect was examined using the disk diffusion method on solid media and MIC and MBC determination by microdilution in liquid media against harmful Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria. The essential oil of N. crispa exhibited strong inhibitory activity in both solid and liquid media against various bacteria, including plant and foodborne pathogens. The highest inhibitory effect on solid media was observed against Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans and Rathayibacter sp., while the weakest antibacterial activity was observed on E. coli and Mycetocola sp. In liquid media, the lowest MIC and MBC values (indicating highest sensitivity) were recorded for Clavibacter tessellarius and Curtobacterium flaccumfaciens , whereas Salmonella typhi showed the greatest resistance. Overall, this essential oil exhibited significant antibacterial activity, particularly against Gram-positive plant bacteria. A total of 94 compounds were identified in the oil, with Eucalyptol (10.93%), Nepetalactone (9.58%), and p-menth-1-en-8-ol (8.4%) being the dominant components. These findings demonstrate the broad antibacterial potential of N. crispa for the first time. Based on the achieved results, the essential oil of N. crispa could be used as a natural antibacterial agent against different bacteria, which would provide opportunities for further applications in the food and agricultural sector.

Article.Title: Automated detection of focal cortical dysplasia in epilepsy using machine learning on structural MRI
Article.Authors: KhoshAkhlagh H.; Rahimi F.; Khodadadegan M.; Solhirad M.; Zare-Sadeghi A.; Rezaeyan A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) represents a structural brain anomaly of developmental origin that significantly contributes to epilepsy. This proof-of-concept study evaluates the feasibility of machine learning (ML) algorithms to distinguish patients with FCD type II-associated epilepsy from healthy controls (HCs) using high-resolution structural MRI. Structural MRI data from a publicly available dataset comprising 167 subjects (both FCD-associated epilepsy patients and HCs) were analyzed. Neuroanatomical features were extracted with FreeSurfer software. Preprocessing steps included dataset reconstruction, feature scaling, dimensionality reduction, and encoding of demographic variables. Multiple supervised ML models—including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Gradient Boosting, and Random Forest—were trained and evaluated using nested cross-validation with 10 outer folds and 5 inner folds. Among the evaluated classifiers, Random Forest achieved the highest AUC (0.791). This model demonstrated balanced classification ability, as reflected by its ROC and Precision-Recall curves. While promising, these results reflect the model’s performance on the current dataset and require further validation. This study demonstrates the preliminary potential of ML techniques to distinguish FCD-associated epilepsy from HCs using structural MRI, providing supportive information for clinical review. However, further studies with larger, independent clinical cohorts are necessary to validate these results before considering any clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Experimental study of the effects of DCA airfoil geometric parameters on the aerodynamic performance at low reynolds numbers flows
Article.Authors: Rahimi H.; Kazemi M.; Boroomand M.
Article.Abstract: This study experimentally investigates the aerodynamic performance of Double Circular Arc (DCA) airfoils at low Reynolds, focusing on the effects of camber angle, relative thickness, and leading/trailing edge radii. Seven configurations were tested in a low-speed wind tunnel under various Reynolds numbers and angles of attack. Lift and drag coefficients were measured, complemented by pressure coefficient distributions and frequency-domain analysis of surface pressure fluctuations using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). Results show that increasing camber angle enhances lift and delays stall, although drag increases at higher angles of attack. Distribution of pressure coefficient (C p ) indicate stronger suction peaks for larger camber, while FFT analysis reveals a dominant frequency between 58–64 Hz, with maximum amplitude for the highest camber case. Peak amplitude also rises with angle of attack, suggesting intensified unsteady flow. Thinner airfoils generate higher lift at low angles, whereas thicker sections improve stall characteristics and boundary layer stability. C p results for thicker profiles show reduced suction, consistent with lower FFT peak amplitudes. Variations in leading and trailing edge radii have minor aerodynamic effects, though sharper edges promote more abrupt stall and slightly higher fluctuation amplitudes. The dominant frequency, significantly below the estimated 100 Hz vortex shedding frequency, suggests coupled aerodynamic mechanisms rather than initial vortex shedding. Although DCA airfoils are traditionally known for their use in transonic flow applications, the findings presented here highlight their promising potential for broader use particularly in the development of wind turbine technology and low speed air vehicles.

Article.Title: Mifepristone modulates response to CDK4/6 inhibition in progesterone receptor isoform A-high breast cancer models
Article.Authors: Pataccini G.; Elia A.; Ambrosio L.; Saldain L.; Rojas P.; Vanzulli S.; Villar K.; Burruchaga J.; Torres F.; Martínez-Vázquez P.; Sartorius C.; Lamb C.; Fabris V.; Novaro V.; Abba M.; Giulianelli S.; Lanari C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract CDK4/6 inhibitors have significantly improved outcomes in estrogen receptor–positive breast cancer. Mifepristone, a progesterone receptor (PR) antagonist, is under investigation in tumors with high levels of PR isoform A (PRA). Here, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of combining mifepristone with CDK4/6 inhibitors. Mifepristone enhanced CDK4/6 inhibitor efficacy in PRA-expressing T47D and T47D-YA cells, whereas it increased proliferation in PR isoform B-overexpressing T47D-YB cells; however, palbociclib retained antiproliferative activity. The combination reduced proliferation through RB dephosphorylation and E2F1 downregulation. ChIP–qPCR and transient transfection assays suggested a direct effect of mifepristone on E2F1 transcription. Ex vivo treatment of breast cancer tissue slices from two of three tumors with high PRA levels showed optimal inhibition with the combination, while complete inhibition was observed with all treatments in the third tumor. Consistent effects were obtained in T47D xenografts in vivo. In murine PR+ mammary carcinomas, sensitivity to palbociclib was independent of responsiveness to mifepristone. Palbociclib sensitivity correlated with elevated CDKN2C expression, whereas resistance was associated with increased NOTCH1 expression. Importantly, pharmacologic Notch inhibition restored palbociclib sensitivity in resistant cells. These findings suggest that mifepristone may potentiate CDK4/6 inhibition in PRA-high breast cancers and identify the Notch pathway as a mediator of intrinsic palbociclib resistance.

Article.Title: From forest to farmland: seasonal habitat suitability and risk areas of human–elephant conflict in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) of Thailand
Article.Authors: Narkyai P.; Chaiyarat R.; Kachenchart B.
Article.Abstract: The Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) is currently undergoing drastic economic income development and some of the most rapid landuse changes in Thailand. This area is also amongst the highest for human–elephant conflict (HEC) especially around the Eastern Forest Complex (EFCOM). Studies regarding ecological risks to the wild Asian elephant ( Elephas maximus ) and the population’s impact on human well-being in the area are limited. Our goal is thus to assess habitat suitability by identifying seasonal HEC risk areas across three buffer zones (0–1, > 1–3, and > 3–5 km). Our objectives include identifying environmental factors, predicting habitat suitability and mapping risk areas, and applying these findings to inform land-use planning. This study utilized 400 questionnaires to identified locations and then incorporated these into the species distribution models of HEC in three stratified areas near the EFCOM boundary. Spatial distribution predictions and HEC risk maps were created using elephant encounters, land-use/land-cover (LULC) information, topographic, and bioclimatic factors alongside Binary Logistic Regression (BLR) and Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt). BLR was specifically employed to estimate the statistical significance and probability of environmental factors influencing the occurrence of HEC. Our results showed that types of forest areas and the prevalence of para rubber plantations were found to be key factors associated with elephant habitats across seasons; revealing a pseudo-habitat – or type of agricultural area, particularly in plantations, which is increasingly used by elephants due to the degradation and fragmentation of natural habitats. In our study it was most commonly found along forest edges, where it facilitates further incursions into farmland. Climatic controls were strongly seasonal, with dry season suitability aligned with cooler conditions (bio11) and limited precipitation (bio17). Whereas wet season suitability peaked under moderate temperatures (bio8) and precipitation variability (bio15). Water bodies further attracted elephants toward agricultural areas. In the wet season, distances of 0–1 and > 1–3 km from the EFCOM boundary were determined to be ‘very high risk’ areas. Chanthaburi had the highest risk of the included provinces, followed by Chachoengsao, Rayong and Sa Kaeo. Crop foraging was also dynamic. Banana and coconut plantations were at risk year round. Rice and southern langsat were risky in the wet season, with the risk then shifting to nearby longan and corn fields. Model performance was moderate for BLR ( AUC = 0.75–0.76) and high for MaxEnt ( AUC = 0.93–0.94). In conclusion, these findings underscore the need for LULC planning around the EFCOM, as well as increased community development toward higher-value crops and non-farm products to reduce HEC, enhance human well-being, conserve wild Asian elephants, and strengthen long-term socio-ecological resilience.

Article.Title: A miniaturized drop-based three-electrode system for sensitive electrochemical determination of azathioprine using pencil graphite
Article.Authors: Rasi Mahmoudi A.; Abbasi Mahmoudabad M.; Asadpour-Zeynali K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract An inexpensive three-electrode system, called a polishable triple graphite electrode, was designed and fabricated using pencil graphite for electrochemical measurement of electroactive compounds. During the manufacturing process, two pencil graphite leads as working and auxiliary electrodes and a silver wire as a pseudo-reference electrode were connected to a special connector and embedded in a Teflon tube. Then, epoxy resin was used to fill the empty spaces between the electrodes. To evaluate the electrode’s performance, the cyclic voltammetry technique was first used in hexacyanoferrate (III)/(II) solution in the presence of KCl supporting electrolyte. Then, the fabricated electrode was used for quantitative analysis of azathioprine in tablet samples using the differential pulse voltammetry technique. Additionally, parameters affecting the analytical performance of the electrode for measuring azathioprine, such as buffer type and pH were optimized. Under the optimized conditions, a linear response was obtained for azathioprine in the concentration range of 5.2-147.2 µM, with a 4.6 µM limit of detection. This three-electrode system offers several advantages, including the capability to measure analytes by dropping the sample solution on the electrode surface, low construction cost due to the use of pencil lead instead of more expensive materials, reduced chemical consumption, and ease of use compared to conventional three-electrode systems. The miniature design of this system facilitates the analysis of small volume samples (in the range of several microliters), which is highly advantageous for the examination of rare or costly biological analytes.

Article.Title: A novel eye-tracking oculomotor score correlates with excessive daytime sleepiness and motor progression in Parkinson’s disease
Article.Authors: Pessoa R.; Bernardi M.; Sanches W.; Schramm M.; Yamaguto G.; Targa A.; Rodrigues L.; de Azevedo E.; Alberti E.; Mendes C.; Lima M.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) progression involves complex interactions between motor and non-motor systems. Oculomotor (OCM) deficits are a known feature, but current eye-tracking metrics are often fragmented. Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) is a prevalent non-motor symptom, yet its relationship with OCM function remains unexplored. Therefore, this study developed a novel global OCM score as a potential sensitive correlate of PD severity and to investigate its association with EDS. In this cross-sectional study, the OCM score integrated saccadic and gaze stability metrics. Participants - PD patients ( n = 44, Hoehn & Yahr stages 1–3) and age-matched controls ( n = 21) - underwent assessment with the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and motor scales during ON-medication states. Strong interocular consistency was found, but PD patients showed significantly lower OCM scores versus controls. Scores showed severity-dependent deterioration: 92% of controls maintained scores ≥ 50, versus only 26% of PD patients, while 40% of PD patients scored < 50. A strong negative correlation existed with H&Y-M stage ( r =-0.66; P < 0.0001). Paradoxically, a positive significant correlation ( r = 0.28; P = 0.02) was found between OCM scores and ESS in PD (higher scores with greater sleepiness), a relationship absent in controls. The OCM score shows promise as a potential indicator of motor impairment and warrants further investigation in longitudinal studies. Its association with EDS suggests a complex interaction between sleep-wake and OCM systems, potentially mediated by sleep deprivation-induced dopaminergic dysfunction. This score holds promise for objective monitoring, patient stratification, and elucidating motor/non-motor interplay in PD.

Article.Title: Physics informed distributionally robust learning for urban distribution network resilience under extreme events
Article.Authors: Bai F.; Yang D.; Wang J.; Li J.; Lei Y.
Article.Abstract: Extreme events expose urban distribution networks to correlated branch outages, uncertain hazard evolution, and rapidly changing operating conditions. Static indices and repeated Monte Carlo studies remain useful, but they either compress recovery behavior into a fixed score or impose substantial computational cost when many hazard realizations must be screened. This study develops a physics-informed, distributionally robust graph-learning framework for estimating node- and system-level resilience from scenario-dependent topology, measured post-event operating states, and hazard information. The contribution lies in the joint implementation of masked graph propagation, auxiliary electrical-state reconstruction, Wasserstein-robust training, and a common recovery-prioritization interface; none of these ingredients is claimed as new in isolation.The network encoder uses branch-availability masks and physical edge attributes to update graph messages. An auxiliary decoder reconstructs voltage, active and reactive injection, and branch-flow quantities, allowing AC-balance, voltage, and thermal residuals to regularize the latent representation. These penalties promote physical consistency but do not constitute hard feasibility guarantees. Distributional uncertainty is represented by a Wasserstein ball over normalized continuous operating and hazard features, while discrete topology masks remain fixed during each inner maximization. The learned resilience score is supervised by a transparent trajectory-based target constructed from restored service, unmet demand, time to 50% recovery, and voltage-violation exposure. The principal quantitative evaluation uses 20,000 operating states generated from 500 hazard scenarios on a modified IEEE 123-bus feeder. Across five random seeds, the full model attains an MAE of \(0.031\pm 0.002\) , an RMSE of \(0.042\pm 0.003\) , and an \(R^2\) of \(0.935\pm 0.008\) . Removing Wasserstein training increases RMSE to \(0.058\pm 0.004\) , while removing the operator block increases it to \(0.052\pm 0.004\) . When every assessment method is coupled to the same restoration simulator, the proposed ranking signal is associated with \(25.1\%\pm 1.5\%\) load shedding at hazard intensity \(\xi =0.8\) and a \(2.48\pm 0.16\) h time to 50% restoration. These recovery quantities measure the effect of assessment-informed prioritization under fixed restoration assumptions; the learning model does not directly issue switching, dispatch, or repair actions.

Article.Title: Vision-spectroscopy cooperative sensing and cold atmospheric plasma inactivation for early warning and management of agricultural product diseases
Article.Authors: Sun B.; Zhang W.; Hu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pathogen-induced disease causes heavy post-harvest losses and threatens food safety, yet routine inspection rarely identifies an infection before it becomes visible. This study evaluates multimodal sensing, threshold-based early warning and plasma-based decontamination for post-harvest disease management in strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa cv. ‘Hongyan’). A dual-branch network, pairing a ResNet-34 visual encoder with a one-dimensional convolutional spectral encoder through bidirectional cross-modal attention, fuses RGB imagery with near-infrared hyperspectral reflectance. Across five severity grades the fused model reached 93.5 ± 0.7% accuracy over fifteen cross-validation runs and 94.2% on a fruit-level held-out test set of 260 samples (95% CI 91.4 to 97.1), with a weighted F1 score of 0.938 and a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.927. Its 2.7-point margin over an unweighted late-fusion baseline did not reach significance after correction for eleven held-out comparisons (continuity-corrected McNemar $$\:{\chi\:}^{2}$$ = 4.00, Holm-adjusted $$\:p$$ = 0.140). Alarms preceded the expert-confirmed transition to a visible lesion by 52.0 ± 9.6 h in the 80-fruit monitoring cohort. Cold atmospheric plasma parameters were screened systematically: 1.5 W/cm 2 in Ar/O 2 for 180 s delivered more than a 3.5-log reduction for Botrytis cinerea , Colletotrichum gloeosporioides and Aspergillus niger ; the measured quality attributes did not differ significantly from untreated controls under the tested conditions. Leakage assays and a sigmoidal dose-response model support membrane damage associated with oxidative stress. The proposed progression from membrane peroxidation through enzyme disruption to DNA damage remains a mechanistic hypothesis. Sensing and treatment were evaluated separately; the present evidence is limited to one commodity, laboratory conditions and no integrated pilot-scale trial.

Article.Title: Quantum eddy current wall thickness tomography using nitrogen-vacancy vector magnetometry for onshore crude oil pipeline integrity assessment
Article.Authors: Fu K.; Li R.; Chen P.; Liu X.; Zuo L.
Article.Abstract: As core infrastructure for global energy distribution, onshore long-distance crude oil pipelines face multiple challenges, including wax deposition, structural stress concentration, and H 2 S release. Traditional non-destructive testing (NDT) techniques, such as eddy current testing and magnetic flux leakage (MFL), suffer from limitations including low spatial resolution, limited penetration depth, and directional blind spots, making high-resolution and omnidirectional defect identification difficult. Diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers have shown strong potential for high-precision vector magnetic sensing. However, their application in pipeline inspection remains limited by insufficient environmental adaptability, the lack of quantitative wall-thickness inversion models, and difficulties in large-scale sensor array integration. To address these issues, this study develops a hybrid framework combining NV vector magnetometry with quantum eddy-current tomography. Directional dependence is substantially reduced through a three-phase orthogonal excitation field, as verified by controlled comparisons with single-phase and dual-phase excitation, while deterministically laser-written NV centers integrated with metal lenses enable sensor array implementation. A machine-learning-assisted tomographic reconstruction algorithm is further proposed to convert discrete magnetic measurements into continuous wall-thickness images. The results show a detection accuracy of 61.0% for a controlled 1 μm nominal wall-thickness perturbation and a coherence time of 70.5 μs under 25 nT noise. In the matched field evaluation, the proposed system achieved an overall detection rate of 93.5%, compared with 65.6% for MFL under the tested conditions, while ultrasonic calibration indicated close agreement between reconstructed and reference thicknesses. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the feasibility of NV-based quantitative pipeline inspection under the evaluated conditions.

Article.Title: Efficacy and safety of three esketamine-based sedation regimens for adults undergoing flexible fibreoptic bronchoscopy: a randomized clinical trial
Article.Authors: Zhong Y.; Wu X.; Peng P.; Xu Y.; Liu T.; Wang X.; Xie C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Esketamine exerts favorable sedative and analgesic effects and represents a promising alternative to opioids. However, the comparative efficacy of esketamine combined with various sedatives remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of propofol, remimazolam or dexmedetomidine respectively combined with esketamine for flexible fibreoptic bronchoscopy (FFB) in adult patients. A total of 130 patients scheduled for flexible fibreoptic bronchoscopy were randomly allocated into three groups: propofol-esketamine group (PE group), remimazolam-esketamine group (RE group), and dexmedetomidine-esketamine group (DE group). All patients received standardized nasopharyngeal airway placement. Manual ventilation was provided when necessary during flexible fibreoptic bronchoscopy. The primary outcome was the incidence of hypoxaemia (defined as SpO₂ < 90% for a duration of > 10 s). Secondary outcomes included hemodynamic changes, cough scores, recovery time, rescue propofol bolus dose and frequency, rescue propofol administration, incidence of intraoperative and postoperative adverse events, satisfaction scores of bronchoscopists and patients, and patients’ willingness to undergo repeat bronchoscopy. Overall, 128 patients were included in the final analysis, 43, 42 and 43 in the PE, RE and DE groups, respectively. The incidences of hypoxaemia in the PE, RE, and DE groups were 34.88%, 26.19%, and 6.98%, respectively ( P = 0.007), with the DE group being significantly lower than the PE group ( P < 0.05). Binary logistic regression confirmed DE as an independent protective factor for hypoxaemia after adjusting for rescue propofol use (adjusted OR = 0.082, 95%CI: 0.018–0.365, P = 0.001). The DE group showed smaller heart rate fluctuations than the PE group at T2 and T3, and than the RE group at T3 ( P < 0.05). The SpO₂ in the DE group was higher than in the PE group at T4 ( P < 0.05). The recovery time in the PE group was shorter than in the RE group ( P < 0.05). For adverse events, the incidence of tachycardia in the PE group was higher than in the DE group (60.47% vs. 32.56%, P < 0.05), and the incidence of injection pain in the PE group was higher than in the RE and DE groups (32.56% vs. 4.76% vs. 0%, P < 0.05). This trial compared three opioid-free intravenous sedation regimens for short-duration flexible fibreoptic bronchoscopy. Dexmedetomidine combined with esketamine reduced the incidence of hypoxaemia and exhibited smaller heart rate fluctuations during the procedure compared with the propofol–esketamine regimen. The incidence of hypoxaemia and other adverse events associated with remimazolam combined with esketamine was between the other two regimens, but the recovery time was relatively prolonged. Trial registration ChiCTR2500102944. This study was registered before enrollment (May 22, 2025). Available at: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=255510 .

Article.Title: Designing dynamic pricing for bike-sharing systems via differentiable agent-based simulation
Article.Authors: Mitomi T.; Makinoshima F.; Makihara F.; Segawa E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bike-sharing systems are emerging in various cities as new eco-friendly transportation systems. In these systems, spatiotemporally varying user trip demand leads to imbalances in inventory at bicycle stations, resulting in additional relocation costs. Therefore, user trip demand must be managed through optimal dynamic pricing for these systems. However, optimal pricing design is challenging because these systems involve users with diverse backgrounds and probabilistic choices. To address this problem, we develop a differentiable agent-based simulation to rapidly design dynamic pricing in bike-sharing systems. We first validate our approach through experiments involving 25 bicycle stations and five time slots, yielding 100 parameters. In this small-scale synthetic scenario, our approach achieves a 73–78% reduction in loss and more than a 100-fold reduction in the number of simulation runs required for convergence compared to differential evolution and finite-difference-based gradient descent. We further validate our approach on a synthetic scenario involving 289 bicycle stations, resulting in 1,156 parameters. While we do not compare against conventional methods due to computational limitations, we observe that the number of simulation runs required by our approach does not increase with the number of optimized parameters. To illustrate the applicability of our method to real-world trip demand, we conduct simulation experiments using NYC Citi Bike data, where user behavior is specified heuristically. The results show that, in simulation, the estimated dynamic pricing can induce balanced inventories without any manual relocation. Additionally, we observe that the cost of discounts required to induce inventory balance can be reduced by choosing appropriate initial pricing parameters, even though this cost is not included in the optimization objective.

Article.Title: Dual-health protocol modelling of Li-ion battery degradation for UAVs with capacity–resistance coupled metrics in aviation duty cycles
Article.Authors: Robin L.; Remmi S.; Mariprasath T.; Zewdu M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Batteries must be able to hold enough usable energy, and have enough power to operate, for high power UAVs and electric VTOLs. But state-of-health based on capacity can deem resistance degraded batteries in good condition for use when there is significant voltage sag risk. This work proposes a dual-health protocol-aware model using both the reference-discharge capacity retention and resistance-derived power retention to assess and schedule the battery degradation. Chronological time, current, cumulative discharge capacity and pulse-resistance measurements were used to reconstruct cycling and reference-performance data for 22 Sony–Murata VTC6 cells based on different aviation duty protocols. The analysis resulted in 439 valid capacity checkpoints, 388 impedance checkpoints and 415 paired health states. A generalized estimating-equation model was used to quantify the nonlinear cycling and protocol effects and to account for the repeated within-cell observations. The leakage-safe leave-one-cell-out validation was used to assess a random-forest predictor. Although there was a strong association between the two degradation measures (Spearman coefficient of 0.882), capacity loss was strongly correlated with resistance growth. The trajectory of the capacity-health was down 2.468% points per 100 mission-equivalent cycles and was highly curved. At the last checkpoint observed, 20 out of 21 cells were resistance-limited for power retention and 1 cell was capacity-limited. The median dual-health scores at 500 cycles varied between 73.52% for extended cruise operation to 90.05% for lower voltage charging. The cell-wise validation showed a mean absolute error of 0.800% point, a root-mean-square error of 1.101% point and coefficient of determination of 0.975. The dual-health metric has the benefit of avoiding over-stating the operational fitness and capacity of a UAV, while providing a conservative state metric for battery eligibility screening, swapping, and risk-aware UAV mission allocation.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: lithium-ion battery degradation; battery replacement; power retention; capacity retention

Article.Title: AI-ready design of realistic 2D materials and interfaces with Mat3ra-2D
Article.Authors: Biryukov V.; Choudhary K.; Bazhirov T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models in materials science are predominantly trained on ideal bulk crystals, limiting their transferability to real-world applications where surfaces, interfaces, and defects dominate. We present Mat3ra-2D, an open-source framework for the rapid design of realistic two-dimensional materials and related structures, including slabs and heterogeneous interfaces, with support for disorder and defect-driven complexity. The approach combines: (1) well-defined standards for storing and exchanging materials data with a modular implementation of core concepts and (2) transformation workflows expressed as configuration-builder pipelines that preserve provenance and metadata. We implement typical structure generation tasks, such as constructing orientation-specific slabs or strain-matching interfaces, in reusable Jupyter notebooks that serve as both interactive documentation and templates for reproducible runs. To lower the barrier to adoption, we design the examples to run in any web browser and demonstrate how to incorporate these developments into a web application. Mat3ra-2D enables systematic creation and organization of realistic 2D- and interface-aware datasets for AI/ML-ready applications.

Article.Title: Observation of long-lived nitrogen afterglow following low-pressure theta-pinch discharges
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Lan T.; Zhang H.; Bai Z.; Mao Z.; Wang K.; Bo W.; Li Y.; Wu J.
Article.Abstract: A pulsed theta-pinch discharge was generated in low-pressure nitrogen and nitrogen–oxygen mixtures. Here, we report multisecond postdischarge emission at a total pressure of 1.44 Pa and a discharge voltage of 11 kV. In pure \(\hbox {N}_{2}\) , the yellow–green afterglow persisted for approximately 18 s and decreased monotonically without measurable chromatic variation. Time-resolved spectroscopy showed that the visible emission was dominated by the \(\hbox {N}_{2}\) first positive system, \(B^{3}\Pi _g\rightarrow A^{3}\Sigma _u^+\) , with \(v'=12\) and \(v'=11\) exhibiting the largest relative upper-state vibrational populations, supporting its identification as a Lewis–Rayleigh-type afterglow. Additional O I emission and NO \(\gamma \) system bands were observed in the nitrogen–oxygen mixture. The slow characteristic decay time decreased from 5.86 s in pure nitrogen to 3.04 s in the mixture containing 79% \(\hbox {N}_{2}\) and 21% \(\hbox {O}_{2}\) , demonstrating oxygen-induced acceleration of the decay under low-pressure conditions. In contrast, a kinetic estimate gives a nitrogen-atom lifetime of only approximately 2.1 ms in atmospheric air, showing that the low-pressure result cannot be directly extrapolated to atmospheric conditions. Selected spectral features partially overlap with those reported for the 2012 Qinghai Plateau ball-lightning event, but this non-unique similarity does not establish a common mechanism. The results provide laboratory constraints for a testable working hypothesis involving nitrogen recombination in a transient oxygen-depleted and/or reduced-density region.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: nitrogen afterglow; low-pressure discharge; afterglow plasma

Article.Title: Digital twin-driven surrogate optimization for maximum power point tracking of photovoltaic systems under partial shading conditions
Article.Authors: Gohila R.; Veena P.
Article.Abstract: Photovoltaic systems under partial shading develop multimodal power-voltage characteristics that render conventional gradient-based MPPT algorithms ineffective. Bio-inspired metaheuristic approaches overcome local-maxima entrapment but introduce a structural scan-phase energy loss: each search iteration physically evaluates a candidate duty cycle on the PV hardware, dissipating real energy at every shading event. This paper presents the Digital Twin-Driven Surrogate-Optimized MPPT (DTSO-MPPT) model, which substantially reduces hardware scan losses by decoupling the global search from the physical PV system and limiting hardware interaction to VTC-based verification. The proposed four layer architecture has a physics calibrated Digital Twin with Recursive Least Squares, a surrogate PV surface builder to evaluate the calibrated model, an Orangutan Optimization algorithm to search the surrogate for the global optimum and finally a validation and transfer controller to verify the accuracy conditions. The proposed model was implemented and numerically evaluated in MATLAB R2024b/Simulink 24.1 under five partial-shading conditions. The simulation results exhibit the proposed model tracking efficiency as 99.1%, GMPP convergence in 0.14s, steady-state power oscillation averaging approximately 0.53 W and remaining within 0.42–0.58 W across the five evaluated cases. The scan-loss reduction energy efficiency metric of 99.4% obtained by the proposed quantifies the reduction in scan-loss, which represents the principal advantage over conventional hardware-coupled MPPT methods.

Article.Title: Integration of natural deep eutectic solvent in a bulk liquid membrane system for tetracycline removal from wastewater
Article.Authors: Abed K.; Wasmi B.; Kurji B.; Abd Rahman S.; Hayyan A.; Basirun W.; Saleh J.; Sen Gupta B.; Salleh M.; Alanazi Y.
Article.Abstract: The presence of tetracycline (TC) in aquatic environments poses significant ecological and public health risks, requiring the development of effective and sustainable methods for its removal. This research details the selective extraction and removal of TC from wastewater using natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES) with a bulk liquid membrane (BLM). NADES was synthesized through mixing thymol (THY), a hydrogen-bond donor, and oleic acid (OA), a hydrogen-bond acceptor, and was further utilized as a green carrier in the BLM system. Extraction parameters, i.e., extraction time, NADES concentration, and mixing speed, were optimized via response surface methodology in order to maximize TC extraction and stripping efficiencies. The conductor-like screening model for real solvents (COSMO-RS) was also utilized for the verification of TC removal, as well as for characterizing the molecular interactions. Under the optimized conditions, the integrated NADES-BLM system attained notable TC extraction and stripping efficiencies of 79.4% and 78.5%, respectively. Moreover, the extraction efficiency was confirmed using COSMO-RS molecular interactions, which was investigated through sigma profile and a sigma potential between the TC molecules and the system phases. This research implies a novel green approach via utilizing NADES as a carrier in the BLM extraction system.

Article.Title: An enhanced LSTM architecture for financial fraud detection with temporal attention, intermediary memory, and camouflage detection
Article.Authors: Khosravi S.; Joloudari J.; Saadatfar H.; Yaraghi S.; Zavvar M.; Zadeh S.
Article.Abstract: Financial fraud detection remains a critical challenge due to the dynamic, imbalanced, and often camouflaged nature of fraudulent transactions. Traditional recurrent models, such as LSTM and GRU, capture sequential dependencies but fail to prioritize temporally relevant events or model complex inter-transaction relationships. More advanced variants, such as Time-LSTM and Phased-LSTM, address irregular temporal patterns but lack mechanisms to detect collusive or camouflaged behaviors. In this paper, we propose a novel enhanced LSTM architecture that integrates four key components: a Temporal Attention Gate to dynamically emphasize recent and contextually significant transactions, an Intermediary Memory Gate to capture cross-transaction dependencies, a Camouflage Detection Gate to identify similarity-based collusion patterns, and Conv1D layers for efficient local feature extraction. The proposed model is evaluated on two real-world fraud detection datasets (Credit Card Transactions and IEEE-CIS) under multiple class imbalance scenarios (5:1, 15:1, 27.3:1, 100:1, and 164.6:1). Experimental results demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms LSTM, GRU, Time-LSTM, and Phased-LSTM across all metrics (Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and AUC). Notably, the proposed method exhibits superior robustness, with only 7.6% points average degradation from mild to severe imbalance on the IEEE-CIS dataset, compared to 12.8% points for the baselines. The performance gap widens as the imbalance increases, achieving up to 32.8% relative improvement in AUC over the best baseline on the Credit Card dataset (at 100:1 and 164.6:1 ratios) and 19.1% on the IEEE-CIS dataset (at 27.3:1 ratio). These findings confirm that the proposed architecture effectively addresses temporal prioritization, relational modeling, and camouflage detection, making it highly suitable for real-world fraud detection in highly imbalanced financial environments.

Article.Title: Epidemiology and clinical outcomes of filler-related complications among transgender women in Mexico
Article.Authors: Marañón-Solorio K.; Vélez-Pintado M.; Martínez-Frías A.; Román-Mar E.; Fong-Ponce M.; Staeps-Gordoa M.; Lastra-Torres J.; Vancini-Nieto E.; Zghaib-Rivero M.; Viveros-Wacher P.; López-Iñiguez A.; Ponce-de-León A.; González-Lara F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Filler-related complications (FRC) arise from the injection of high-density substances used to modify the body in order to harmonize gender identity and/or gender expression and represent an emerging public health problem. Among transgender women, limited access to gender-affirming healthcare, together with other psychosocial, structural, and social factors, may contribute to the use of body modification practices intended to harmonize gender identity and gender expression, including the use of injectable materials. We conducted a retrospective analytical study among transgender women with a history of filler injections receiving care at three public referral centers in Mexico City between September 2024 and July 2025. Participants were identified through review of available clinical records and transgender care registries. Transgender identity was determined based on self-identified gender documented in the clinical record and confirmed through clinical chart review. Demographic, clinical, and social variables were collected to characterize FRC and associated factors. FRC were defined as documented inflammatory, infectious, migratory, or mixed manifestations temporally associated with prior filler exposure and attributed by the treating clinical team to filler injections. A total of 222 transgender women were included, with a median age of 45 years (IQR 38–52). Overall, 99 participants (44.5%) were classified as having FRC, most commonly inflammatory or mixed presentations. Materials referred to as “biopolymers” were the most frequently reported injected substances, followed by injectable oils, and among participants with available information, 93% of injections were performed by non-medical personnel. The time between filler injection and symptom onset exceeded 5 years in 54% of participants with FRC. More than one-third of affected participants required hospitalization attributable to FRC. Nearly half of transgender women with prior filler injections experienced complications, underscoring the substantial morbidity associated with filler injections performed outside supervised medical care. These findings highlight the multifactorial structural and social context surrounding non-medically supervised filler use, including barriers to gender-affirming healthcare, and the need for multidisciplinary care pathways for FRC. Because this retrospective study was conducted at referral centers, severe complications may be overrepresented.

Article.Title: Ultrasonographic evaluation of the association between gonial appositional bone changes and masseter muscle thickness and elasticity in bruxism
Article.Authors: Ünal Erzurumlu Z.; Şahiner S.; Torul D.
Article.Abstract: Increased muscle activity in bruxism has been reported to be associated with appositional bone changes in the gonial region, referred to as bone peaks (BPs). The aim of this study was to evaluate the relationship between the presence of BPs and masseter muscle thickness and strain ratio. Individuals with bruxism were included in this study. The presence of BPs in the right and left gonial regions was assessed on panoramic radiographs. In all participants, masseter muscle thickness and strain ratio were measured at rest and during contraction using ultrasonography and strain elastography, respectively. Factors associated with BP presence were evaluated using generalized estimating equation (GEE) logistic regression. The mean age of the 117 included individuals was 24.64 ± 6.95 years. BPs were detected bilaterally in 41.9% of cases, only on the right side in 9.4%, and only on the left side in 6.8%. A statistically significant association was found between BP presence on the right and left sides( p < 0.001). Age (OR = 1.14, 95% CI: 1.04–1.25; p = 0.008), male gender (OR = 4.05, 95% CI: 1.57–10.44; p = 0.004), and greater masseter muscle thickness during contraction (OR = 1.31, 95% CI: 1.04–1.65; p = 0.021) were significantly associated with BP presence. Within the limitations of this study, BP formation showed a predominantly bilateral pattern, and BP presence was associated with age, male gender, and greater masseter muscle thickness during contraction among individuals with bruxism.

Article.Title: Factors influencing the intention to use smart wristbands among patients with COPD: an extended UTAUT model
Article.Authors: Ye J.; Chen J.; Yao M.; Jing G.; Li W.; Su Y.; Pei H.; Xu J.; Chi C.
Article.Abstract: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) imposes a substantial global health burden. Despite the considerable potential of wearable devices for early detection and disease management, suboptimal engagement limits their clinical utility. This study aims to identify factors associated with the intention to use smart wristbands among patients with COPD. The study extends the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) by incorporating health risk perception and interface presentation. A sequential mixed-methods design was employed, commencing with semi-structured interviews ( n = 28), followed by a questionnaire survey ( n = 233). Structural equation modeling was used to validate the measurement model and examine the hypothesized relationships. All six constructs demonstrated statistically significant positive associations with intention to use ( P < 0.05). Health risk perception (β = 0.272, P < 0.001) and social influence (β = 0.271, P < 0.001) were the primary correlates of intention to use. This study extends UTAUT by identifying factors correlated with COPD patients’ intention to use smart wristbands. The findings offer practical insights for user-oriented device design and intervention strategies, thereby supporting the promotion of digital health monitoring among COPD patients.

Article.Title: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells as a novel source for mitochondrial transplantation therapy in peripheral nerve injury repair
Article.Authors: Gao H.; Wang Z.; Cui Y.; Cheng H.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Peripheral nerve injury remains a significant clinical challenge, with energy metabolism disorders severely hampering complete nerve regeneration. While mitochondrial transplantation has emerged as a promising therapeutic approach to restore cellular bioenergetics and promote neural repair, current mitochondrial sources from mesenchymal stem cells or skeletal muscles require invasive harvesting procedures. This study investigated peripheral blood mononuclear cells as a novel, minimally invasive source for therapeutic mitochondria in peripheral nerve regeneration. Functional mitochondria were isolated from both rat and human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and adipose-derived stem cells using standardized protocols. Mitochondrial structure and function were evaluated through transmission electron microscopy, proteomic analysis, and ATP production assays. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed in both a rat sciatic nerve crush injury model and a 10-mm segmental sciatic nerve defect model bridged with an acellular nerve allograft (ANA). Functional recovery was evaluated by histological, electrophysiological, muscular, and gait analyses. In vitro studies further examined mitochondrial internalization and bioenergetic effects in neuronal cells, while transcriptomic analysis of dorsal root ganglion neurons were performed to explore potential mechanisms underlying mitochondrial-enhanced axonal growth. Successfully isolated peripheral blood mononuclear cell-derived mitochondria demonstrated intact ultrastructure and shared similar protein profiles with adipose-derived stem cell mitochondria, particularly in oxidative phosphorylation pathways. In the sciatic nerve crush model, sub-epineural injection of peripheral blood mononuclear cell-derived mitochondria significantly improved functional recovery at 21 days post-injury, with enhanced axonal regeneration and reduced muscle atrophy comparable to adipose-derived stem cell mitochondria. In the 10-mm nerve defect model, PBMC-derived mitochondria loaded into ANAs improved CMAP recovery, axonal regeneration, Schwann cell-associated nerve reconstruction, target muscle preservation, and gait function at 12 weeks postoperatively. Human-derived mitochondria did not produce an evident systemic inflammatory response or major-organ injury under the conditions examined. In vitro studies showed effective mitochondrial internalization within 3 h, significantly enhancing cellular respiratory capacity. Mitochondrial transplantation promoted axon growth in dorsal root ganglia neurons, with transcriptomic analysis implicating axon-guidance-related pathways. PBMCs represent a readily accessible and minimally invasive source of mitochondria for transplantation therapy. PBMC-derived mitochondria achieved regenerative efficacy comparable to conventional ADSC-derived mitochondria in both crush and segmental nerve defect models, while avoiding the need for additional tissue harvesting and prolonged cell expansion. These findings support the further development of autologous PBMC-derived mitochondrial transplantation as a potential strategy for peripheral nerve repair.

Article.Title: Latent profiles of ambivalence over emotional expression and associations with social support among Chinese patients with cervical cancer
Article.Authors: Peng M.; Yuan Z.; Lu Y.; Wang C.; Li X.; Chen X.; Lu S.; Ye M.
Article.Abstract: Ambivalence over emotional expression (AEE) remains insufficiently characterized among patients with cervical cancer. This study examined AEE profiles, their correlates, concurrent psychological distress, and associations with social support. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 318 Chinese patients with cervical cancer recruited between March and May 2026. Participants completed the Ambivalence Over Emotional Expressiveness Questionnaire (AEQ), 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales, and Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS). Analyses included latent profile analysis, multinomial logistic regression, Bayesian comparisons, and adjusted restricted cubic spline regression. Three profiles were retained: low conflict–low emotional confusion ( n = 84, 26.4%), high conflict–high expressive contradiction ( n = 130, 40.9%), and moderate conflict–low negative inhibition ( n = 104, 32.7%). Depression, anxiety, and stress differed across profiles (all P < .001), with the highest medians in the high-conflict profile. Harmonious family relationships were associated with lower odds of high- versus low-conflict membership (adjusted OR = 0.043, 95% CI 0.019–0.097). Bayesian comparisons supported differences in SSRS scores across all profile pairs (BF₁₀ = 88.06–1.05 × 10¹⁵). Higher total AEQ scores were associated with lower SSRS scores across the observed range, with a somewhat steeper fitted decline in the mid-range and no discrete cutoff suggested by the curve. These findings support considering emotional-expression conflict alongside psychological distress, social support, and family relationships during individualized oncology nursing assessment.
