Article.Title: A simplified mechanics-based model for unified ductility estimation of RC beams under static and dynamic loading
Article.Authors: Amran M.; Hason M.; Abdulhameed A.; Hanoon A.; Alqurashi A.; Abdulhameed H.; Al-Shami Q.
Article.Abstract: One of the most important performance parameters that control the ability of reinforced concrete (RC) members to support inelastic deformation and energy dissipation without catastrophic failure, especially under extreme loading circumstances, is ductility. The accurate prediction of the ductility of curvature is crucial for reliable structural design and seismic performance assessment. However, the majority of current analytical models have been designed for quasi-static loading and are usually employed separately for static and dynamic loading. This separation does not consider the strain-rate sensitivity of concrete and reinforcing steel which results in conservative predictions of concrete ductility, and in a limited applicability to structures exposed to dynamic actions like earthquakes, impact or blast loads. Thus, a unified mechanics-based model is proposed in this study to predict the yielding curvature ductility and ultimate curvature ductility of RC beams under static and dynamic loadings. The proposed formulation combines depth of the concrete compression block, curvature relationships, reinforcement characteristics, and the effect of strain rate in one analytical formulation that is consistent with the provisions of ACI 318 − 19. Dynamic increase factors (DIFs) have been introduced to account for the rate-dependent response of concrete and reinforcing steel, allowing for simultaneous consideration of curvature ductility, moment capacity and failure response as a function of loading rate. The predictive performance of the model was evaluated using statistical analysis and comparing the model. The results indicate good correlation with an R 2 of 0.992 and a CoV of 18.1% between the predicted and observed ductility responses. Based on the results of parametric analysis, it is observed that the most significant factors affecting the curvature ductility are the concrete compressive strength (26.18%), reinforcement area, section geometry and ratio of transverse reinforcement, with the steel yield strength and strain-rate effects having moderate influence. The proposed unified framework provides a reliable tool for ductility assessment of RC beams under combined loading regimes and supports more consistent performance-based design of concrete structures exposed to dynamic actions. The findings contribute to improving structural safety assessment and may assist in refining design recommendations for RC members in seismically demanding environments.

Article.Title: Energy management optimization algorithm for data center microgrids based on solid-state transformers
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Luo W.; Yang X.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: The proliferation of hyperscale data centers, together with tightening carbon-neutrality targets, exposes the limits of the line-frequency transformer (LFT) that still dominates data-center power distribution and motivates a fresh look at the conversion and dispatch layer. This paper develops an energy management framework for a data-center microgrid whose grid interface is a three-stage solid-state transformer (SST), so that renewable, storage, and IT loads sit on independently regulated AC and DC ports rather than behind a passive iron core. A multi-objective mixed-integer nonlinear program (MOMINLP) is formulated to jointly minimise operating cost, carbon emission, a composite power-quality index, and average PUE, subject to bus power balance, SST port transfer, battery SOC, ramp, and demand-response constraints. Uncertainty in PV, wind, and IT workload is condensed through Latin hypercube sampling with Kantorovich-based scenario reduction, and tail risk is capped by a CVaR constraint at the 95% confidence level. Dispatch is decomposed across day-ahead, intra-day, and real-time MPC layers, and the nonconvex problem is solved by an improved whale optimization algorithm (IWOA) that combines Tent chaotic initialization, an adaptive convergence coefficient, differential-evolution mutation, and Lagrangian relaxation of the diesel and battery integer commitments. On a 10 MW-class pilot the proposed scheme raises renewable accommodation by 17.2% points, cuts annual operating cost by 11.7%, reduces $$\:{CO}_{2}$$ emissions by 12.9%, and lowers average PUE from 1.52 to 1.40 relative to a line-frequency-transformer baseline, while keeping bus voltage deviation below 1.7% on the DC bus and 2.4% on the AC bus. Against PSO, GA, standard WOA, and NSGA-II, IWOA halves the iterations needed to reach 1% of the final fitness (78 versus 134–187), tightens the relative gap to the best-known solution to 0.62% (versus 2.4–5.1%), and drops the coefficient of variation to 0.018 (versus 0.061–0.094), showing that the observed gains come from the coupling of hardware-aware modelling and algorithmic tailoring rather than from either alone.

Article.Title: Thymopoiesis-regulating genetic variant rs2204985 affects outcome of liver but not kidney transplantation
Article.Authors: Semenova M.; Tammi S.; Nihtilä J.; Nieuwenhuis L.; Aleksandrova R.; Liukkonen V.; Markkinen S.; Nordin A.; Lempinen M.; Helanterä I.; Ritari J.; Festen E.; de Meijer V.; Åberg F.; Hyvärinen K.; Partanen J.
Article.Abstract: The genetic variant rs2204985 at the T‑cell antigen receptor locus has been associated with regulation of thymopoiesis and outcome in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. We investigated the association of this variant with outcomes of liver and kidney transplantation. We assessed the association of rs2204985 with post-transplantation outcomes in two Finnish cohorts comprising 666 liver and 1,025 kidney transplantations using adjusted logistic regression and Cox models. Findings from the Finnish liver transplant cohort were validated in an independent Dutch replication cohort of 618 liver transplantations. In the Finnish liver transplant cohort, the donor rs2204985*GG genotype was associated with lower overall survival (multivariable Cox regression, hazard ratio = 1.54, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.02–2.34, p = 0.041). In the Dutch cohort, the donor GG genotype increased the risk of graft loss (OR = 1.47, 95% CI = 0.99–2.21, p = 0.059) but not mortality (OR = 1.00, 95% CI = 0.66–1.51, p = 0.981). In the meta-analysis of the Finnish and Dutch liver transplant cohorts the donor rs2204985*GG genotype was associated with graft loss (OR = 1.42, 95% CI = 1.06–1.90, p = 0.019). These results indicate that the genetic variant rs2204985*GG regulating thymopoiesis may affect liver transplantation outcome. Although our study provides no mechanistic clues to the association, the findings emphasize the immunological role of the liver.

Article.Title: Seismic resilience of high-rise buildings: optimizing active tuned mass dampers with advanced control strategies considering soil-structure interaction
Article.Authors: Mousaviyan Safakhaneh M.; Fahimi Farzam M.; Ahmadi H.; Farnam A.
Article.Abstract: This paper investigates the seismic control of a 40-story high-rise building equipped with a Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) and an Active Tuned Mass Damper (ATMD) while considering Soil–Structure Interaction (SSI) effects. The structure is evaluated under four foundation conditions, including fixed-base, soft-soil, medium-soil, and dense-soil cases. A Genetic Algorithm (GA) is used to optimize the design parameters of the TMD and ATMD systems, including the mass ratio, frequency ratio, damping ratio, and, for the ATMD, the control gain of the New Algorithm (NA). The NA strategy is implemented as a displacement-based active control law that generates a counteracting control force through the ATMD system. Time-history analyses are performed under selected earthquake records to compare the uncontrolled, passive TMD-controlled, and active ATMD-controlled responses. The results show that the NA-based active control system considerably improves seismic performance. For the structure on soft soil, the ATMD reduces the average displacement and acceleration responses by 46.4% and 36.7%, respectively. For the structure on dense soil, the corresponding reductions are 42.0% and 13.6%, respectively, compared with the uncontrolled case. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the proposed GA-assisted NA-based ATMD framework in improving the dynamic response of the studied high-rise structure under the considered seismic and soil conditions.

Article.Title: Course-embedded AI-augmented teaching is associated with engagement and performance in software education
Article.Authors: Gai Z.; Wang J.; Wu J.
Article.Abstract: AI-augmented teaching may reduce feedback delays in software courses, but semester-long classroom evidence remains limited. This course-level quasi-experimental study evaluated a course-embedded AI-augmented teaching (AIT) model in an undergraduate Python course. Two intact classes participated: 60 students in the AIT class used a large language model teaching assistant restricted to course-specific materials and instructional rules for question answering, code diagnosis, personalized recommendations, and teacher monitoring, whereas 60 students in the conventional-instruction class received the same course instruction without access to the AIT platform. Student-level analyses, interpreted cautiously because of the class-level design, showed higher posttest, programming assignment and final composite scores in the AIT class after baseline adjustment. Learning engagement also showed clearer gains, especially overall and behavioral engagement. AI usage intensity was moderately associated with engagement but weakly associated with academic performance. Mediation analysis provided clearer evidence for an indirect engagement pathway for project practice performance than for final composite performance. Open-ended feedback indicated that students valued immediate feedback and debugging support but remained concerned about accuracy, dependency and ethical boundaries.

Article.Title: Clinical and placental correlates of high- versus low-grade Villitis of unknown etiology: a retrospective study from Kuwait, 2014–2024
Article.Authors: Al-waheeb S.
Article.Abstract: Villitis of unknown etiology (VUE) is a chronic inflammatory placental lesion associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, particularly in severe disease. Previous studies have mainly compared VUE-positive with VUE-negative placentas or examined selected outcomes; direct evidence on whether routine maternal, obstetric, fetal, and placental features distinguish high-grade from low-grade VUE remains limited. This retrospective case-only comparative study included all 128 placentas with a histologically confirmed diagnosis of VUE identified at a single institution (Maternity Hospital, Ministry of Health, State of Kuwait) between 2014 and 2024, comprising 64 high-grade and 64 low-grade cases. Maternal demographic and obstetric characteristics, pregnancy outcomes, and concurrent placental lesions were extracted from clinical and pathology records. Because no VUE-negative comparison group was included, the analyses evaluated correlates of VUE grade and could not identify risk factors for the occurrence of VUE. Group comparisons used Welch t tests, chi-square tests, or Fisher exact tests as appropriate. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for high-grade VUE with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). No statistically significant associations were identified in the present dataset. Mean maternal age was 30.61 years in the high-grade group and 29.69 years in the low-grade group (mean difference 0.92 years, 95% CI − 0.96 to 2.80; p = 0.334). Parity category ( p = 0.952) and gravidity category ( p = 0.817) were not associated with grade. In the adjusted model, none of the prespecified predictors was independently associated with high-grade VUE. Estimates included maternal age (adjusted OR 1.03 per year, 95% CI 0.95–1.10), parity (adjusted OR 1.05 per birth, 95% CI 0.83–1.33), any pregnancy complication (adjusted OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.51–2.46), and any additional placental pathology (adjusted OR 1.72, 95% CI 0.72–4.13). In this selected case-only cohort of placentas with VUE, the measured maternal, fetal, obstetric, and concurrent placental characteristics did not clearly distinguish high-grade from low-grade disease. The study addresses variation in grade among VUE-positive placentas and does not identify risk factors for developing VUE. The adjusted model had modest discrimination (c-statistic = 0.60), and limited precision, sparse subgroups, possible misclassification, and multiple testing constrain interpretation. The null findings do not establish equivalence or biological independence, and clinically relevant associations may have been missed.

Article.Title: Bioaccessibility, anti-Helicobacter pylori activity and immunomodulatory effects of Hypogymnia physodes (L.) Nyl. extract: in vitro assessment of potential food-related applications
Article.Authors: Dresler S.; Baczewska I.; Sawa-Wejksza K.; Korona-Głowniak I.; Suśniak K.; Sęczyk Ł.; Szwajgier D.; Gustaw K.; Borowski G.; Kukula-Koch W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lichens are a promising but insufficiently explored source of bioactive secondary metabolites. This study aimed to characterize Hypogymnia physodes (L.) Nyl. extract and evaluate, under in vitro conditions, its anti- Helicobacter pylori and urease-inhibitory activity, immunomodulatory effects, gastrointestinal bioaccessibility, food-matrix interactions, and effects on selected lactic-acid bacteria. The extract was dominated by physodic acid (32%), physodalic acid (23%), 3-hydroxyphysodic acid (17%), and atranorin (11%). It inhibited tested H. pylori strains, including isolates with different antibiotic-resistance phenotypes, with MIC values of 31.25–125 mg/L, and inhibited urease with an IC₅₀ of 14.45 mg/L. In LPS-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophages, the extract reduced NO and ROS levels, COX-2 protein levels, and phagocytosis, while cell viability remained largely unaffected up to 75 µg/mL. Simulated gastrointestinal digestion showed limited, metabolite-dependent soluble bioaccessibility; food matrices, particularly protein-rich ones, markedly affected metabolite recovery. Relative protein digestibility decreased by up to 25%, whereas starch digestibility was unaffected. The digested extract did not inhibit the nine tested lactic-acid bacterial strains. Overall, these in vitro findings support further investigation, but toxicological, microbiome, mechanistic, and in vivo studies are required before functional-food applications can be established.

Article.Title: Attention-based and contrastive deep learning models for real-time anomaly detection in Edge-IIoT networks
Article.Authors: Alzighaibi A.; Marks A.; Almudaifer A.; Balaha H.; Halima N.; Elhosseini M.
Article.Abstract: The rapid expansion of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems has increased the cyber-attack surface of critical infrastructure, requiring intrusion detection systems (IDS) that are accurate, robust, and efficient under resource-constrained edge environments. Traditional approaches suffer from limited generalization, poor handling of class imbalance, and lack of statistical reliability and interpretability. This paper proposes a modular deep learning framework integrating TabTransformer, Variational Autoencoder, and contrastive learning, combined through multi-trial training (N = 10), statistical aggregation, and F1-weighted ensemble fusion. Experiments on the Edge-IIoTset dataset ( $$\approx $$ 1.9M samples, 15 classes) achieve 97.60% accuracy and 83.42% F1-score, with multi-trial aggregation reducing the uncertainty associated with single-run reporting. From a computational perspective, training is performed using large-batch optimization (batch size = 16,384) with early stopping (patience = 50), while inference requires a single forward pass per model followed by constant-time fusion. The framework operates on compact tabular inputs ( $$\approx $$ 96 features), resulting in a lightweight memory footprint (on the order of a few megabytes per model) and enabling efficient deployment. The inference pipeline processes batches in a few milliseconds on GPU-class hardware, ensuring real-time responsiveness for high-throughput IIoT traffic streams while maintaining low computational overhead and energy demand. Ablation analysis shows that removing ensemble fusion reduces F1-score by approximately 1%:2%, while eliminating multi-trial aggregation significantly increases variance, highlighting the importance of statistical robustness. Furthermore, SHAP-based explainable AI (XAI) provides insight into feature-level contributions, enhancing transparency and supporting human-in-the-loop security operations. Overall, the proposed framework achieves a balanced trade-off between predictive performance and computational efficiency, delivering a reproducible, interpretable, and deployment-oriented IDS solution for real-time IIoT environments. Practical deployment considerations, including model export to ONNX format and quantization for edge hardware, are outlined as immediate next steps.

Article.Title: Ecosystem health and its constraint transitions in Plateau cities: insights from Lhasa, China
Article.Authors: Gong X.; Nie X.; Pan X.; Zhang Z.; Yang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High-altitude urban ecosystems are exposed to pronounced ecological vulnerability and increasing human pressures. Existing assessments have primarily characterized overall health status and its spatiotemporal variation, whereas temporal changes in the configuration of underlying constraints have received less attention. As the capital of the Xizang Autonomous Region of China, Lhasa’s unique geographic and climatic setting on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau poses distinctive challenges for ecosystem health assessment. This study examined ecosystem health constraint transitions in Lhasa from 2011 to 2020 using a plateau-adapted “Pressure-State-Response” (PSR) indicator system, obstacle degree analysis, and grey relational analysis. The ecosystem health index fluctuated but exhibited an overall upward trend. Municipal solid waste collection volume (SV) ranked first in obstacle degree in most years, with a mean obstacle contribution of 29.41%, identifying it as a recurrent core constraint within the response subsystem. Energy conservation and environmental protection expenditure intensity (EPI), evapotranspiration (ET), drainage pipeline density (DP), and barren land area (BA) constituted secondary constraints whose relative contributions changed over time. SV had the highest grey relational grade with the ecosystem health index (0.7918), indicating the closest temporal correspondence among indicators. Alternative weights, aggregation methods, and classification thresholds confirmed the robustness of the temporal pattern. By revealing constraint transition patterns in high-altitude urban ecosystem health, this study provides a methodological reference for diagnosing changing constraints and prioritizing management in data-limited plateau cities.

Article.Title: Associations Among family environment, self-identity, cognitive emotion regulation strategy use, and physical activity in adolescents: A multi-theory integration perspective
Article.Authors: Ying J.; Feng L.; Feng L.; Qiu W.; Liu C.; Yang X.; Xiao H.; Luo L.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, insufficient physical activity among adolescents has emerged as a significant threat to their physical and mental health. Physical activity is known to be associated with a variety of individual and environmental factors. This study aimed to examine the association between family environment and adolescent physical activity, as well as the sequential mediating effects of self-identity and cognitive emotion regulation strategy use in this relationship. A cross-sectional study design was employed, involving 620 adolescents aged 12–16 years from three secondary schools in the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. Data were collected using paper-based questionnaires, including the Brief Family Environment Scale, the International Physical Activity Questionnaire–Short Form, the Self-Identity Scale, and the Cognitive Emotion Regulation Questionnaire. After excluding invalid responses, 589 valid questionnaires were retained, yielding an effective response rate of 95.0%. Statistical analyses, including normality tests, descriptive statistics, correlation analyses, regression analyses, and mediation analyses, were conducted using SPSS 29.0 and the PROCESS macro (Version 4.2). Significant correlations were observed among family environment, physical activity, self-identity, and cognitive emotion regulation strategy use. Self-identity and cognitive emotion regulation strategy use demonstrated a significant sequential indirect association between family environment and physical activity. The direct association between family environment and physical activity accounted for 63.37% of the total association, while the sequential indirect pathway—family environment → self-identity → cognitive emotion regulation strategy use → physical activity—accounted for 2.91% of the total association. Family environment is significantly associated with adolescent physical activity, and this association is partially mediated sequentially through self-identity and cognitive emotion regulation strategy use. These findings provide novel empirical evidence for understanding the relationship between family environment and adolescent physical activity, and offer valuable insights for future research in this area.

Article.Title: Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins depict a new predictive risk model for ovarian cancer prognosis and immunotherapy
Article.Authors: Hu D.; Ren S.; Zhang Y.; Li X.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins (hnRNPs) are a family of RNA-binding proteins that are highly involved in nucleic-acid metabolism. The pathological effect of a series of hnRNPs family members on ovarian cancer is far from fully elucidated. This study acquired the RNA-seq data of ovarian cancer and imformation about hnRNP from TCGA database and a published study, respectively. The expression, mutation and copy number variation (CNV) of 22 hnRNP genes were analyzed. The hnRNP score, cell cycle and ferroptosis scores of ovarian cancer samples were calculated by ssGSEA. The intersection of hnRNP score related genes with cell cycle related genes or with ferroptosis related genes was taken to construct prognostic risk system by univariate Cox analysis, the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)-regression analysis and multivariate Cox regression analysis, to predict the prognosis and response to immunotherapy. A prognostic risk system based on nine hnRNP score-related genes was created, which independently predicted the prognosis of ovarian cancer cases and has been validated and stable in different ovarian cancer cohorts. The expression of the prognostic signature genes in ovarian cancer tissues was verified by immunohistochemistry, and the correlation between their individual expression and the prognosis of ovarian cancer was investigated. To provide functional and mechanistic support beyond bulk transcriptomics, we integrated an independent high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) single-cell atlas (GSE154600; 50,086 cells) and found that signature genes such as JCHAIN, S1PR4 and HAMP were expressed in a cell-type-restricted manner. In silico knockout predicted that JCHAIN, HAMP and S1PR4 knockdown perturbs plasma-cell humoral, macrophage antigen-presentation and NK/T-cell programs, respectively, and that HNRNPM loss is linked to extracellular-matrix remodeling. DepMap CRISPR dependency data further indicated that ovarian cancer cell lines depend on HNRNPM (median Chronos score -0.906) and RBM17 (-1.157). Promoter-methylation and m6A analyses suggested an epigenetic layer in the regulation of signature genes. Prognostic risk system was related to tumor immunomodulatory pathway and the activity level of some immune cells in tumor microenvironment (TME), and the expression of immune molecules, and immune score, stromal score. And it has potential ability to predict the response of cases to immunotherapy. We systematically demonstrated the expression of hnRNP gene family in different types of cancer, as well as the genetic variation in ovarian cancer and its potential impact on cancer development. We have created a risk system that effectively and steadily quantifies the prognosis of individual ovarian cancer cases and predicts the response to immunotherapy, which provides insight into hnRNP as a possible indicator to guide clinical decision-making.

Article.Title: Combined apparent diffusion coefficient histogram and MRI-based fractal analysis for predicting lymph node metastasis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Liao X.; Ou J.; Liu X.; Liao W.; Li J.; Zhou H.; Zhang X.; Chen T.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the feasibility of whole-tumor apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) histogram analysis based on paired b-value ADC maps combined with fractal and morphological parameters of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) for predicting lymph node metastasis (LNM), 117 prospective ESCC patients from two centers were assigned to the training ( n = 63), internal ( n = 27) and external validation ( n = 27) cohorts. They underwent preoperative T 1 WI and T 2 WI, contrast-enhanced T 1 WI (T 1 CE), and DWI with five b-value combinations including 0 and 800 s/mm 2 . Whole-tumor ADC histogram features from DWI, fractal parameters at all sequences, and gross tumor volume (GTV) at T 1 CE were extracted. In the training cohort, five paired b-value based ADC histogram models, one fractal-dimension (FD) model, and one combined model were developed. In the three cohorts, models’ performance was assessed using area under the ROC curve (AUC), calibration curves, and Brier scores. Our combined model, incorporating the 25th percentile of ADC 0−800 with FD and natural-log-transformed GTV, yielded the highest AUCs (0.846–0.931 across the three cohorts). Calibration analysis showed reasonable overall agreement but slight deviations at higher predicted probabilities, and the combined model yielded Brier scores of 0.093 to 0.176 across cohorts. In conclusion, our combined model may provide a promising noninvasive approach for predicting LNM.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a competing-risk nomogram for predicting cancer-specific mortality in prostate cancer: a SEER population-based study
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Cui F.; Jin W.; Chen S.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Prostate cancer prognosis is complicated by substantial competing risks of non-cancer death, particularly in older patients. Existing SEER-based nomograms for high-risk prostate cancer predominantly use standard Cox regression, which does not directly estimate the absolute probability of cancer-specific mortality (CSM) when non-cancer deaths are common. We therefore developed and validated a competing-risk nomogram based on the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model, and explored N stage interactions and conditional survival in a large, population-based cohort. Patients with high-risk or locally advanced prostate cancer (operationalized from EAU criteria) were identified from the SEER database (2010–2021). The derivation cohort (2010–2015, n = 137,073) was split into training (70%) and internal validation (30%) subsets; the 2018–2021 cohort (n = 105,391) served as an independent temporal validation set. Diagnoses from 2016 to 2017 were excluded a priori to create a temporal gap between the derivation and validation eras. A Fine-Gray competing-risk model was fitted and visualized as a nomogram. Model performance was evaluated using time-dependent AUC, calibration (plots and IPCW-based calibration intercept/slope with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals), IPCW prediction error, and decision curve analysis (DCA) with comparison against re-estimated versions of D’Amico risk stratification, TNM staging, and the Song 2020 nomogram. N stage interactions and conditional survival were explored as secondary analyses. A total of 242,464 patients were included. Competing events accounted for 72.9% of all-cause mortality, so absolute-risk estimates in this population depend critically on explicit handling of competing mortality. The Fine-Gray nomogram incorporated eight variables: age, race, marital status, T stage, N stage, Gleason score, PSA, and treatment. The time-dependent AUC was 0.745 (3-year) and 0.758 (5-year) in training, 0.766 and 0.775 in internal validation, and 0.630 and 0.648 in temporal validation; discrimination was nearly identical to a cause-specific Cox model with the same variables. In the temporal validation cohort, the IPCW calibration slope was 0.74 (95% CI 0.70–0.80) and the 5-year IPCW Brier prediction error was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039–0.042). On DCA, the nomogram’s net benefit was comparable with the best reference model in derivation cohorts and highest in the temporal validation cohort across clinically relevant thresholds (approximately 5–30%). The global N stage interaction test was not significant (P = 0.512); individual interaction tests were exploratory (no individual test reached nominal significance; the corrected T stage x N test yielded chi-square = 1.86, df = 3, P = 0.601), and stratified analyses suggested a less steep Gleason score-CSM association in N1 than in N0 patients (Gleason 5 + 5: HR 3.33 vs. 1.94), a hypothesis-generating finding. In this large, population-based study, a competing-risk nomogram provided directly interpretable absolute-risk estimates of CSM; calibration was strongest in the derivation and internal validation cohorts and moderately attenuated in the temporal validation cohort. Its net benefit was comparable with or higher than three reference models, most clearly in temporal validation. Because treatment was included as treatment received, treatment associations are non-causal and the tool must not be used to compare treatments. The exploratory stratified analyses support further study of N stage-informed prognostication but do not establish effect modification. An interactive online tool is available at https://prostate-cancer.shinyapps.io/high-risk_CSS/.

Article.Title: Performance and eco-efficiency of high-strength concrete incorporating a screened quaternary low-carbon binder
Article.Authors: Shetty P.; Rao A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the development and performance of high-strength concrete designed for an M65 target grade incorporating an optimized quaternary low-carbon binder system comprising Ordinary Portland Cement (50%), Class F fly ash (20%), ground granulated blast furnace slag (15–25%), and calcined seashell powder (5–15%). Binder proportions were systematically investigated using an S/N-ratio-based comparative screening approach to rank the predefined mixtures based on compressive strength. A comprehensive experimental evaluation was conducted to assess mechanical properties, durability characteristics, and eco-efficiency. Results indicate that the incorporation of industrial and aqua-industrial waste materials significantly reduces carbon footprint and embodied energy compared to conventional OPC-based concrete, while demonstrating continued strength development at later ages and enhancing long-term durability. The developed quaternary binder system demonstrates strong potential as a sustainable and practically viable solution for high-performance concrete, promoting effective waste valorisation and contributing to the objectives of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 9, 12, and 13).

Article.Title: A hybrid predictive and uncertainty-aware framework for renewable hydrogen system efficiency assessment and sustainable energy planning
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Tellapati A.; Alkhrissat T.; Spoorthi B.; Johar M.; Choudhury S.; Radhika S.; Kaur G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Renewable hydrogen is emerging as a critical element in the transition toward low-carbon and sustainable energy systems; however, accurately evaluating system efficiency remains challenging due to complex, nonlinear interactions among technical and environmental factors. This study proposes a hybrid predictive and uncertainty-aware framework for assessing renewable hydrogen system efficiency and supporting sustainable energy planning. The framework integrates Elastic Net and Extra Trees regression models enhanced through meta-heuristic optimization using Sparrow Search and Firefly algorithms to improve predictive performance. Recursive Feature Elimination is applied to identify the most influential variables governing system behavior, while Dempster–Shafer Theory is incorporated to model uncertainty and construct a robust ensemble prediction strategy. The proposed approach is evaluated using a dataset of 2,535 renewable hydrogen system records with spatial attributes derived from documented geographical coordinates. Experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in predictive accuracy, with a 12% increase in R² and a 15% reduction in MAE compared to baseline approaches. Sensitivity analysis indicates that photovoltaic power generation and electrolysis efficiency are the most influential factors affecting hydrogen system performance. Beyond improved prediction accuracy, the framework provides interpretable insights that can support infrastructure development, investment planning, and energy policy design. The proposed methodology demonstrates how hybrid predictive modeling combined with uncertainty quantification can enhance decision-making processes in renewable hydrogen systems and contribute to more reliable low-carbon energy transitions.

Article.Title: Assessing the impacts of solid waste management in the context of corporate social responsibility and the circular economy
Article.Authors: Iqbal S.; Sanjrani M.; Khan K.; Khoso W.; Abrar S.; Umali M.
Article.Abstract: Growing solid waste generation creates public health and environmental challenges, highlighting the need for integrated waste management approaches that support a clean environment and society. This study assesses and develops a framework describing how solid waste management methods influence environmental sustainability and public health outcomes, while observing the role of corporate social responsibility (CSR). This study adopted a quantitative research design to evaluate the relations among solid waste management practices, environmental impacts, health outcomes, circular economy and CSR using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Data collection was completed through a structured questionnaire administered to 200 respondents. The questionnaire was developed based on the theoretical foundations of waste hierarchy, circular economy, and sustainable waste management. Considering the importance of the waste hierarchy and circular economy parameters, this study categorizes solid waste management as segregation, recycling, composting, and disposal methods. The analysis of the conducted study advocates the impact of the environment as an indicator to connect waste management practices and health outcomes. The results show that solid waste management methods meaningfully improve environmental sustainability when the strategies such as segregation, recycling, and composting are followed, as they contribute to current resource recovery and waste reduction. The finding further proposes that sustainable waste management aids to the quality of life and public health by reducing environmental hazards. Furthermore, it envisioned corporate social responsibility as a better tool to implement waste management approaches, with the enhanced stakeholder’s engagement and organizational responsibility. This study further elaborates to investigate sustainability by incorporating CSR, circular economy, waste hierarchy, public health, and environmental quality within an integrated analytical framework. The practical solutions are recommended to organizations and policymakers for developing and implementing sustainable waste governance.

Article.Title: Probabilistic vibration characteristics of bi-directional functionally graded plates with various boundary conditions
Article.Authors: Karsh P.; Hirwani C.; Abderrahmani S.; Alok A.; Tiwari S.; Kumar R.
Article.Abstract: The present work examines the free vibration response of bi-directional functionally graded (Bi-FGM) plates considering both deterministic and probabilistic analyses under four boundary conditions: CFFF, CFCF, SSSS, and CCCC. The material properties vary continuously in the two in-plane directions and are described using a two-parameter power-law distribution. The governing equations are formulated according to First-Order Shear Deformation Theory (FSDT) and solved using an eight-node finite element model. Uncertainty in material parameters is introduced through Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) to determine the first three natural frequencies. The parametric investigation indicates that the NFs decrease as the geometry ratio, material gradation index, and temperature increase, whereas an increase in plate thickness leads to higher frequencies. Among the boundary conditions considered, the fully clamped plate (CCCC) exhibits the highest frequencies, while the cantilever configuration (CFFF) shows the lowest values, with CFCF and SSSS lying between these two extremes. Probability analysis also reveals that the frequency distribution is broader for plates with weaker edge constraints, indicating greater sensitivity to variations in material properties.

Article.Title: Outage probability modelling of multi-user downlink IRS-NOMA network over α-κ-µ and α-κ-µ shadowed faded channels
Article.Authors: Syed N.; Shaik T.; Ayanampudi H.; Kadha V.; Kamireddy R.; Dhuli R.
Article.Abstract: The next generation wireless networks demand innovative approaches to deliver reliable and high-capacity communication service to the users. However, achieving consistent performance remains challenging, especially in complex indoor environments where signal degradation occurs due to obstacles, multi-path propagation and structural attenuation. To overcome these challenges, this work explores the intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), two emerging technologies that enhance signal propagation and spectral efficiency. This work presents a comprehensive outage probability analysis of a multi-user downlink IRS-NOMA system operating under the generalized fading environments: (i) α-κ-µ fading model and (ii) α-κ-µ shadowed fading model. The proposed work provide a flexible framework under diverse propagation conditions, including line-of-sight conditions, multi-path clustering, nonlinearity effects and shadowing effects. The analysis incorporates practical impairments such as imperfect channel state information (CSI) and residual errors in successive interference cancellation (SIC). To provide deeper insight, the derived outage expressions are specialized to several classical and composite fading models, including Nakagami- m , Rician, Rayleigh, κ-µ , η-µ , α-µ , and α-η-µ models. The impact of impairments and channel parameters on outage behaviour is thoroughly investigated through analytical derivations and validated via extensive Monte Carlo simulations.

Article.Title: Adsorptive removal of benzo(ghi)perylene from vehicle-wash wastewater using eucalyptus wood waste-derived biochar
Article.Authors: Hasan M.
Article.Abstract: This study reports the preparation of eucalyptus waste-derived biochar (EWB) and its application in the sustainable removal of benzo[ghi]perylene (B[ghi]P) from vehicle wash wastewater (VWW). The EWB was prepared by pyrolysis under a nitrogen atmosphere, followed by activation with 1 M HCl to improve its adsorption performance. The prepared EWB was characterized by surface area analysis (SAA), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Batch adsorption experiments were conducted to evaluate the effects of initial B[ghi]P concentration, contact time, pH, temperature, and adsorbent dosage on the adsorption process. The optimal adsorption conditions were: initial B[ghi]P concentration of 40 mg L -1 , contact time of 120 min, temperature of 60 °C, adsorbent dosage of 0.8 g, and pH of 6. Under these conditions, the maximum removal efficiency of EWB reached 98%. The adsorption process best fits the pseudo-second-order kinetic model, while the Langmuir isotherm model provides the best statistical fit for the equilibrium adsorption data. Furthermore, the EWB maintained an initial adsorption efficiency of over 84% after six consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles, indicating its potential for reusability. The observed adsorption efficiency and reusability suggest that the EWB may have the potential to treat wastewater contaminated with PAHs. However, further research is needed to determine its practical and sustainable applications, addressing issues such as energy requirements, production costs, environmental impact, and scalability.

Article.Title: Microbial community responses to ceramic amendment in coastal sediments of a seasonally hypoxic bay
Article.Authors: Kosaka T.; Iqbal M.; Nishikawa M.; Nishihara G.
Article.Abstract: Eutrophication-driven sediment deterioration is a critical issue in enclosed coastal bays. A ceramic material composed of humic organic acids and calcium carbonate mesoscopic crystals has been developed for in-situ sediment remediation, generating high-alkaline environments that promote oxidative degradation of organic matter. Although its physicochemical effects have been verified through the Environmental Technology Verification (ETV) program, its influence on sediment microbial communities remains unknown. This study investigated the impact of ceramic treatment on bacterial community structure in coastal sediments of Omura Bay, Japan, a seasonally hypoxic enclosed bay, through comparison with untreated control sediments using 16 S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. A significant increase in alpha diversity was observed in ceramic-treated sediments relative to controls, and PERMANOVA indicated significant differences in microbial community composition between the two areas. Ceramic-treated sediments were enriched in aerobic to facultatively anaerobic organic matter–degrading genera (e.g., Lutimonas , Actibacter , Aureibaculum , Saccharicrinis ) together with the concurrent enrichment of the sulfate reducer Desulfofustis and the sulfur oxidizer Thiolapillus . The concurrent enrichment of these metabolically distinct groups suggests the potential coexistence of oxidative and reductive processes within heterogeneous sediment microenvironments. In contrast, control sediments were characterized by the denitrifier Nitrogeniibacter and several uncultivated GTDB MAG-derived lineages. PICRUSt2-based functional prediction indicated higher predicted relative functional potential for sulfur metabolism, environmental sensing, and biofilm formation pathways in ceramic-treated sediments, whereas control sediments showed greater representation of central carbon metabolism pathways. These findings indicate that ceramic-treated sediments support a more diverse microbial community with distinct taxonomic and predicted functional profiles, including microbial groups associated with both oxidative and reductive processes, providing insights into the potential of ceramic materials for sediment remediation.

Article.Title: Quantum authentication framework for digital twin–driven satellite networks
Article.Authors: Rana A.; Bhangalia P.; K V.; Kumar P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The integration of digital twin technology into large-scale Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations introduces critical security challenges, particularly under emerging quantum threats. This paper proposes a quantum-assisted multi-layer authentication framework for satellite–digital twin communication that combines entanglement-based verification with hardware-rooted identity using Quantum Physical Unclonable Functions (QPUFs). The protocol employs Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen (EPR) pair-based key establishment and decoy-state mechanisms to detect entangle-and-measure (EMA) and intercept-and-resend (IRA) attacks, where the induced disturbance attains 0.25 per decoy qubit under a maximally informative attack. The probability of undetected attacks decreases exponentially as $$(3/4)^u$$ , rapidly approaching zero for moderate decoy lengths. Cabello’s qubit efficiency of the scheme is derived as $$\beta = \frac{k}{6n + 2u}$$ . Experimental validation using Qiskit simulation confirms entanglement correlation preservation across mutually unbiased bases and demonstrates QPUF response uniformity of 0.588, a stabilized majority-based reliability of $$100\%$$ under noiseless simulation, and a response uniqueness of 0.508. The results establish the feasibility of integrating quantum authentication and hardware-root security within digital twin–assisted satellite networks.

Article.Title: Apparent ecological network expansion masks structural reorganization and corridor vulnerability in the Central Plains Urban Agglomeration
Article.Authors: Yang H.; Wu T.; Xu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization is reorganizing landscape connectivity, yet whether increases in ecological sources or corridors actually represent stronger regional networks remains unclear. Using three representative time slices (2013, 2018, and 2023) in the Central Plains Urban Agglomeration, China, we integrated InVEST–MSPA, Conefor, circuit theory, complex-network analysis, Louvain community detection, and edge collective influence (ECI) to examine stage-specific network reorganization and corridor vulnerability. Source numbers increased from 70 to 90 and then declined to 82, whereas total source area continuously decreased from 22,589.53 to 20,510.21 km². Corridor numbers changed from 122 to 165 to 154, while mean corridor length and the intercity-corridor share declined continuously. Cross-period source matching showed that the 2018 peak included retained, newly identified, and locally subdivided source patches. All complete annual networks remained connected, but their mesoscale organization changed: Louvain communities decreased from 13 to 10 while modularity remained close to 0.79. ECI and edge betweenness identified largely different high-value corridor sets, and fixed-removal experiments revealed distinct modes of structural vulnerability. Random-removal distributions further showed that large one-step connectivity losses can occur at different removal steps, providing a common uncertainty benchmark for targeted strategies. These results indicate that apparent network expansion can coexist with contraction of the ecological base, connection reconfiguration, and multiple forms of corridor dependence.

Article.Title: Integrating domain knowledge and user requirements in kitchen layout optimization
Article.Authors: Nádudvari Z.; Gyöngyössy N.; Botzheim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Layout design data sources exhibit a fundamental asymmetry: the challenge lies in processing structured, high-quality domain knowledge alongside task-specific natural language user requirements. To address this, we propose a hybrid evaluation framework for evolutionary algorithms (EAs) that quantifies constraint violations as virtual displacement costs. The framework is evaluated in the present study on four kitchen-layout optimization scenarios with task-specific user requirements and component sets. By integrating hard-coded domain rules with a fuzzy-logic-driven Abstract Syntax Tree (AST), the system enables a flexible yet explainable scoring mechanism. This approach allows for a granular penalty system for individuals, while also guiding local search heuristics through component-level diagnostic logging. The implementation of the AST results in a marginal reduction in convergence cost while reducing the relative dispersion of the algorithms. Within this kitchen-layout benchmark, the evolutionary algorithms achieved lower execution times and aggregate penalty scores than the selected LLM chat applications. The three non-expert human-generated layouts were included only as an exploratory reference because of the small and demographically homogeneous participant sample.

Article.Title: A lightweight privacy-aware federated vision transformer for tomato leaf disease classification
Article.Authors: Ram D.; Gyanchandani M.; Rasool A.; Kushwaha M.
Article.Abstract: Smart farming increasingly depends on intelligent disease diagnosis systems to improve crop productivity while protecting the privacy of agricultural data distributed across farms, research institutions, and edge devices. Conventional centralized deep learning approaches require collecting large volumes of data at a central location, raising concerns about data privacy, ownership, and communication overhead. To address these challenges, this study proposes FedVRT, a lightweight privacy-aware federated learning framework for tomato leaf disease classification. The proposed framework combines a Vision Transformer (ViT) with a lightweight ResNet26 architecture within the Federated Averaging (FedAvg) framework, enabling collaborative model training without exchanging raw agricultural images. The Vision Transformer captures global contextual relationships among disease symptoms, while the ResNet26 branch extracts fine-grained local lesion and texture features. Their complementary feature representations are fused to improve disease classification under heterogeneous non-IID data distributions commonly encountered in real-world agricultural environments. The proposed framework was evaluated on a dataset of 11,108 tomato leaf images across six disease categories in federated settings with 3, 12, 24, and 36 distributed clients. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), confusion matrix analysis, confidence intervals, and statistical significance tests. FedVRT achieved a classification accuracy of 98.50%, with precision 98.42%, recall 98.35%, F1-score 98.38%, and an AUC of 0.997 across 36 participating clients. Comparative experiments further demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms established federated optimization methods, including FedSGD, FedProx, FedNova, SCAFFOLD, FedOpt, and FedDyn, while maintaining lower communication overhead and faster convergence. Unlike existing federated Vision Transformer-based approaches that primarily focus on classification accuracy, FedVRT integrates lightweight hybrid feature extraction, comprehensive statistical validation, scalability analysis, and communication efficiency evaluation within a unified framework. These characteristics demonstrate the effectiveness of FedVRT as a scalable, privacy-aware, and practically deployable solution for intelligent tomato leaf disease diagnosis in next-generation smart farming environments.

Article.Title: Grey wolf optimization-driven convolutional neural network for robust cardiac MRI-based heart disease classification under class imbalance
Article.Authors: Asha M.; Prasath S.; Kesavulu D.; Lakshmi S.
Article.Abstract: Heart disease diagnosis through Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a vital clinical diagnostic technique that enables the non-invasive evaluation of cardiac structure and identification of cardiovascular diseases. Nevertheless, the automation of such a task using deep learning faces some critical problems in terms of limited data size, class imbalance, and manual tuning of hyperparameters, which might hinder the accuracy and reliability of the process. Therefore, this paper introduces a novel algorithm called GWO-CNN for heart disease classification based on cardiac MRI. In this algorithm, structured pre-processing, contrast enhancement, augmenting-based class balancing, CNN-based spatial features extraction, and GWO-based hyperparameters selection will be used for the classification process. Cardiac MRIs are preprocessed through normalization, Gaussian filtering, contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization, cropping, and resizing improve anatomical clarity and generate standardized image inputs. Moreover, the classifier model consists of a CNN model to identify between normal and abnormal heart MRIs and Grey Wolf Optimization algorithm to find optimal values of hyperparameters (learning rate, dropout rate, batch size, configuration of convolutional filters, and dense layer size). Experimental results, obtained via patient-level five-fold cross-validation repeated across five random seeds (25 runs in total), demonstrated that the GWO-CNN framework attained a mean accuracy of 98.30% ± 0.42% (95% CI: 98.13–98.47%), a mean F1-score of 97.50% ± 0.46%, and a mean AUC of 98.60% ± 0.39%, with a representative single-fold configuration reaching 98.42% accuracy, 97.86% precision, 97.31% recall, a 97.58% F1-score, a specificity of 98.91%, a Dice score of 97.52%, a Jaccard similarity index of 95.23%, a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 96.41%, and an area under the curve (AUC) of 98.74%. Paired statistical testing (t-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank, p < 0.001) confirmed that the improvements attributable to preprocessing, GAN-based augmentation, and GWO-based tuning, as well as the improvement over baseline CNN, ResNet-based, and transfer-learning-based comparators, are each statistically significant. The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed GAN-assisted GWO-CNN framework for cardiac MRI classification under limited and class-imbalanced data conditions. A preliminary external evaluation on the independent ACDC dataset, performed without any retraining, yielded 92.00% accuracy, a moderate decrease from the internal cross-validated mean consistent with real but non-catastrophic distributional shift. However, because the primary evaluation is based on a relatively small single public dataset and external validation was limited to one additional cohort assessed once, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary proof-of-concept evidence rather than confirmation of clinical applicability. Further validation using larger and independent multi-center cardiac MRI cohorts is required before the proposed framework can be considered for clinical deployment.

Article.Title: Adverse childhood experiences are associated with intimate partner violence-related head and neck injuries and symptom burden among adult women
Article.Authors: Astridge A.; Mu E.; Copas C.; Hannon O.; Martins B.; Padgett C.; Spitz G.; Makovec Knight J.; McDonald S.; Edwards E.; Meyer S.; Shultz S.; Symons G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are a well-established risk factor for adult intimate partner violence (IPV) victimisation and traumatic brain injuries (TBI), but their relationship with IPV-related brain injury remains unclear. This retrospective cross-sectional study examined the associations between ACEs and subtypes (physical/sexual abuse, emotional abuse/neglect, family adversities, and witnessing domestic violence) on IPV-related head and neck injuries (mild TBI, head impacts, and non-fatal strangulation; NFS), as well as brain injury symptom burden among 170 community-dwelling women (aged 18–75 years). Participants completed the ACE questionnaire, Composite Abuse Scale, Brain Injury Screening Questionnaire (IPV module), and the Rivermead Post-concussion Questionnaire. Family adversities (59%) and emotional abuse/ neglect (54%) were the most prevalent ACE subtypes. Over 40% reported an IPV-related head impact, 27% reported IPV-related mild TBI, and 28% reported NFS experiences. Higher ACE scores increased the odds of IPV-related mild TBI, head impacts, NFS, and NFS-related brain injury (ORs 1.22–1.32). Associations between ACEs and symptom severity were no longer significant after controlling for PTSD, depression, and IPV recency, with a substantial amount of the variance accounted for by co-occurring PTSD. These findings highlight ACEs as an important upstream risk factor for IPV injury, which is critical for prevention, early identification, and policy.

Article.Title: Postural stability and shooting performance in adult and junior elite Brazilian recurve archers
Article.Authors: Ely M.; Schons P.; Clemente F.; de Barros Rodenbusch C.; Trybulski R.; Kawczyński A.; de Oliveira H.; Preissler A.
Article.Abstract: Postural stability is considered a crucial factor for performance in Olympic recurve archery. However, the extent to which it distinguishes athletes from different competitive categories remains unclear. This study aimed to compare postural stability and shooting performance between adult and junior athletes from the Brazilian national archery teams. A cross-sectional, comparative study was conducted with 20 elite athletes: 13 adults (28.00 ± 5.97 years) and 7 juniors (17.43 ± 0.79 years). Participants performed 18 shots at the official competition distance of 70 m while standing on a force platform (Vald Performance, 500 Hz). Center of pressure (COP) displacement variables in the lateral and anteroposterior directions were analyzed for dominant and non-dominant legs. Shot scores were recorded to assess performance. Data normality and homogeneity of variances were assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk and Levene tests, respectively. Independent t-tests were used for normally distributed variables, whereas Mann-Whitney U tests were applied to non-normally distributed variables (age and years of practice). Complementary ANCOVA models adjusted for body mass and years of practice were also performed. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in any stabilometric variable ( p > 0.05). However, adult athletes achieved significantly higher unadjusted average scores (8.67 ± 0.34) than junior athletes (7.85 ± 0.91; p = 0.009; Cohen’s d = 1.382). Age, body mass, and years of practice also differed significantly between groups ( p < 0.05). After adjustment, no significant group effect was observed for stabilometric variables, and the group effect for shooting score was attenuated (adjusted difference = 0.79, 95% CI − 0.01 to 1.58; p = 0.052; ηp² = 0.217). Although no statistically significant differences in postural stability were detected between groups, adult athletes achieved higher unadjusted shooting scores, with this group effect attenuated after adjustment for body mass and years of practice. Therefore, the stabilometric results should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between groups. These findings suggest that, within this elite Brazilian sample, shooting performance differed between groups in the unadjusted analysis, whereas the stabilometric variables did not show statistically significant differences, including after adjustment.

Article.Title: Efficacy and safety of a cetuximab biosimilar compared with Erbitux in patients with RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Rezvani H.; Rezvani A.; Allahyari A.; Ghadiany M.; Esfahani A.; Mortazavizadeh S.; Mehrzad V.; Khodakarim N.; Gorji M.; Sharifi M.; Mohammad Doost H.; Hosseinzadeh M.; Bari A.; Nejati B.; Sadeghi A.; Chavoshi S.; Nekouee A.; Razavi M.; Hajigholami A.; Kalantari B.; Khosravi A.; Darakhshandeh A.; Ataei Azimi S.; Abrishami A.; Tavakkoli Shiraji S.
Article.Abstract: Cetuximab, an epidermal growth factor receptor monoclonal antibody, is a key therapy for RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), commonly used with folinic acid, 5-fluorouracil, and irinotecan (FOLFIRI). In Iran, the rising burden of mCRC and the high cost of imported cetuximab underscore the urgent need for a cost-effective, locally manufactured biosimilar to improve treatment accessibility and sustainability within the healthcare system. The objective of this study is to compare the efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity of cetuximab (manufactured by CinnaGen Co.) versus reference cetuximab (Erbitux; manufactured by Merck) in patients with RAS wild-type mCRC. This phase III, double-blind, randomized, multi-center, active-controlled trial enrolled adult patients (n = 211) with RAS wild-type mCRC. Participants were allocated 2:1 to cetuximab (CinnaGen) plus FOLFIRI (n = 141) or Erbitux plus FOLFIRI (n = 70) for up to 48 weeks. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), time to treatment failure (TTF), objective response rate (ORR), safety, and immunogenicity. The results show that cetuximab (CinnaGen) was comparable to Erbitux for PFS in both PP (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.95; 90% confidence interval [CI]: 0.62–1.45) and ITT (HR = 0.82; 90% CI: 0.55–1.24) analyses, with upper CIs below the non-inferiority margin (1.51). No significant differences were observed in OS (HR = 0.85; 95% CI: 0.45–1.58), TTF (HR = 1.07; 95% CI: 0.77–1.48), or ORR (43.3% vs 45.7%; P-value = 0.77). The majority of patients experienced adverse events, with anemia, neutropenia, and hypomagnesemia being among the most frequently reported. The frequency of serious adverse events was considered clinically acceptable, and immunogenicity analyses revealed no detectable anti-cetuximab antibodies in either treatment group. In conclusion, this study demonstrated that cetuximab (CinnaGen) is non-inferior to Erbitux (Merck) in terms of PFS, with comparable efficacy across other endpoints. The safety profiles of both products were acceptable and consistent with known data for cetuximab-based regimens in mCRC.

Article.Title: Surface ground-motion characteristics and path-corrected PGV prediction for mining-induced seismicity: a case study
Article.Authors: Chen H.; Zhang Q.; Zou J.; Jiao Y.; Ouyang L.; Jiang Y.
Article.Abstract: Strong mining-induced earthquakes in deep mines threaten surface infrastructure, yet their surface vibration fields are difficult to predict because propagation paths cross goafs, fractured overburden, and variable Quaternary cover. This study used a dense surface monitoring array at the Dongtan Coal Mine to characterize the time–frequency evolution and spatial attenuation of typical mining-induced seismic events. Goaf-path length and Quaternary cover thickness were incorporated into a conventional distance-attenuation relationship to build an improved peak ground velocity (PGV) prediction model. The results show that surface waveforms change from short, high-amplitude near-field pulses to multi-peaked coda wave trains in the mid-to-far field. This evolution is marked by envelope broadening, delayed peak arrival, spectral migration to lower frequencies, narrowed bandwidth, and increased spectral decay. Propagation through fractured goaf zones and thick shallow cover accelerates high-frequency attenuation and produces strong azimuthal differences in PGV. Compared with the distance-only model, the path-corrected model improved the coefficient of determination from 0.79 to 0.87 and reduced RMSE and MAPE from 0.38 cm/s and 24.0% to 0.09 cm/s and 21%, respectively. The model is empirical, but it illustrates how path and site effects shape mining-induced surface vibration. The representative M L 1.9 event remained below safety-control thresholds for major surface structures. The proposed framework supports rapid post-event assessment and refined risk zoning in deep mining areas.

Article.Title: Zonal instability identification and full-sequence hierarchical control strategies for surrounding rock in composite-roof coal roadway
Article.Authors: Yang S.; Yang L.; Chen D.; Yin J.; Zhao L.
Article.Abstract: Composite roof coal roadways suffer from developed bedding planes, low cementation strength and delayed staged surrounding rock instability, and conventional one-step support methods poorly adapt to these complex geological conditions. Taking the 1211(1) transportation roadway of Guqiao Coal Mine as the engineering background, this study adopts full-section real-time bolt stress monitoring to explore the temporal and spatial distribution of support stress, identify critical instability zones, and develop a graded, phased differentiated surrounding rock control system with optimized excavation and construction schemes. The results reveal that bolt axial force experiences three evolutionary stages: rapid growth, decelerated growth and stable fluctuation. Surrounding rock stress and support bearing capacity show distinct spatial heterogeneity, with the bearing capacity ordered as central roof > upper rib > lateral roof > lower rib. The central roof and upper rib are high-risk instability zones with severe stress concentration and sensitive bolt stress response, while other zones maintain sufficient support redundancy and good rock stability. Based on the staged deformation and stress redistribution mechanism of surrounding rock, a full-cycle closed-loop control system integrating advance pre-control, early intensive support, transitional stabilization and late cable reinforcement is established. A zonal differentiated support strategy is formulated, implementing intensive reinforcement in key hazardous zones and conventional support in stable areas. Combined with delayed cable support technology, a three-dimensional coupled stress field of shallow bolts and deep cables is constructed, which effectively remedies the defects of traditional support, such as uncoordinated stress adaptation, insufficient deep support and late structural failure. Three phased support modes with matched temporal and spatial parameters are determined, and construction processes are optimized for efficient parallel operation. Field applications verify that the optimized scheme ensures reliable stability and safety of composite roof roadways. After implementation, the daily excavation circulation increases from 6 to 15 ~ 18 cycles, and the daily advance footage rises from 6.0 m to 15 ~ 18 m, significantly improving excavation safety and construction efficiency.

Article.Title: G2T: Gate guided transformer for medical image segmentation
Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Shokouhmand S.; Rahman S.; Bhatt S.; Mirbozorgi S.; Faezipour M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inspired by the human cognitive process and memory capabilities, we present a novel vision transformer (ViT) in this paper, called G ate G uided T ransformer (G2T) for medical image segmentation. G2T addresses a key limitation of cascaded decoder blocks in vision transformers; that is their difficulty in retaining and propagating important information from earlier stages, which often leads to suboptimal feature decoding in later blocks. Our proposed G2T has (i) a novel feature-aware decoder (FAD) consisting of three convolutional gates named Refine, Expand, and Produce (REP), which deal with forgetting irrelevant features, remembering relevant features, and generating the output features, respectively; (ii) a novel attention mixing module called LH-RAAM (Low to High-Resolution Attention Accumulation Module) that accumulates attentions computed in the encoder blocks from low-level features to high-level features, and aggregates them with the attentions computed in the decoder blocks to emphasize similar features during both the encoding and decoding stages. Evaluated on six medical imaging datasets, G2T consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art models by 1-3%, achieving a 94.67% mean Dice score ±0.01 standard deviation on the ACDC dataset and 92.90% ±0.02 on the Synapse dataset. Ablation studies additionally justify the utility of each component of G2T along with strong generalizability outside the medical domain.

Article.Title: Multidimensional spatiotemporal differentiation and driving mechanisms of soil erosion in a mountainous small watershed: an ST-TransUNet-R framework
Article.Authors: Miao H.; Zhang H.; Deng Z.; Hao N.; Zhu W.; Zou J.
Article.Abstract: Soil erosion threatens ecological security and water conservation in mountainous small watersheds. To improve pixel-level assessment under complex terrain and incomplete multi-source raster inputs, we developed ST-TransUNet-R, a deep-learning framework that integrates a ResNet-50 encoder, a Transformer module, a joint-validity mask, and masked mean squared error loss. The framework was applied to the Xikouwai Small Watershed upstream of the Miyun Reservoir for five assessment years between 2005 and 2020 and achieved R² = 0.87, RMSE = 2.08, MAE = 1.15, and PBIAS = − 3.13%. Multidimensional analysis showed that the 600–900 m elevation band contained 48.0% of the eroded area, whereas zones above 1100 m produced disproportionately high soil loss per unit area. Slopes > 35°, vegetation cover < 30%, unused land, and skeletal soils were consistently erosion-sensitive. SHAP analysis identified slope as the dominant predictor, followed by slope length and vegetation cover, indicating that terrain-controlled runoff concentration and surface protection jointly shaped spatial erosion heterogeneity. These findings provide a high-resolution basis for prioritizing erosion-control measures in mountainous water-source protection areas.

Article.Title: Longitudinal single-cell RNA-seq profiling of lung cell phenotypes, signaling, and cross-talk during fibrosis resolution
Article.Authors: Speth J.; Wong V.; Guzman S.; Walker N.; Liu Y.; Zemans R.; Blackwell T.; Aguilar C.; Peters-Golden M.; Fortier S.
Article.Abstract: Resolution of fibrosis following lung injury is distinguished from persistent/progressive parenchymal scarring through the timely clearance of aberrant cell types, removal of excess collagens, and regeneration of alveolar structure. The requisite signaling pathways, cellular cross-talk, and phenotypic shifts associated with, and required for, resolution of established lung fibrosis have not been well characterized. To address this critical knowledge gap, we performed longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing of whole mouse lung digests obtained during spontaneously resolving fibrosis. We observed a fibrosis-associated macrophage and an ECM-secreting Csmd1+ fibroblast population emerging during peak fibrosis and undergoing partial clearance during resolution. Our study also revealed conspicuous shifts in well-established pathways associated with tissue repair and fibrosis among immune, mesenchymal, and epithelial cells during spontaneous resolution. In addition to a decline in pro-fibrotic driver pathways, the putative anti-fibrotic pathways cAMP, HGF/MET, and TWEAK were enriched in several cell types during spontaneous resolution. CellChat analysis was used to predict the cellular senders and recipients of each pathway and characterize their longitudinal changes. Our characterization of the cellular and molecular dynamics in whole lungs during spontaneous fibrosis resolution provides a foundation for the identification of endogenous pathways that might be leveraged to treat pulmonary fibrosis.

Article.Title: Comparative phyto-biochemical profiling, antibacterial efficacy, and culturable rhizosphere bacterial dynamics of turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) variants from eastern India
Article.Authors: Mohapatra A.; Sahoo J.; Mohanty A.; Samal P.; Sahoo L.; Mahapatra S.; Hossain S.; Hossain S.
Article.Abstract: Different turmeric variants possess distinct medicinal and ecological attributes, yet a comprehensive comparative analysis of their phyto-biochemical profiles and associated culturable rhizobacterial profiles is lacking. To resolve this, the current study evaluated yellow, black, and white turmeric variants, revealing distinct phyto-biochemical constituent profiles characterized by peak phenolics in white turmeric (121.63 mg GAE/g), maximum flavonoids (49.85 mg QE/g) and proteins (9.65%) in black turmeric, and primary carbohydrate (63.52%) and carotenoid (35.44 µg/g) reserves in yellow turmeric. Multivariate analysis established marked negative correlations between protein and carotenoid content ( r = − 0.991), and total phenolics and carbohydrates ( r = − 0.970), with a two-component PCA model accounting for 100% total variance (PC1 = 59.42%, PC2 = 40.58%). Antibacterial evaluation against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli demonstrated the highest inhibitory activity in the ethanolic extract of yellow turmeric compared to the other tested variants; however, this activity remained significantly lower than that of ampicillin. In contrast, white turmeric extracts exhibited no antibacterial activity. Phylogenetic model selection based on the lowest Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) designated the Jukes–Cantor model with invariant sites (JC + I; BIC = 5,279.42) as the best fit for Bacillus sp. AKU 5 (putative Bacillus thuringiensis affinity), whereas the Tamura 3-parameter model (T92; BIC = 9,815.55) was optimal for Bacillus sp. AM 1 (putative B. cereus affinity). Maximum likelihood analyses revealed contrasting evolutionary patterns, with B. thuringiensis exhibiting a highly constrained substitution rate (α = 0.04; Log Likelihood = − 2006.341) and pronounced C→A substitution bias, whereas B. cereus showed a more uniform rate distribution (α = 30.23; Log Likelihood = − 4234.930) characterized by symmetric A↔G and T↔C transition biases, emphasizing preliminary nucleotide substitution variations within the turmeric rhizosphere. In-silico thermodynamic profiling of 16S rRNA amplicon secondary structures revealed distinct computational folding stabilities between B. thuringiensis AKU 5 (minimum free energy (MFE) = − 511.90 kcal/mol) and B. cereus AM 1 (MFE = − 506.50 kcal/mol). These baseline structural disparities reflect inherent differences in sequence length and GC-rich base-pairing density rather than in vivo physiological adaptations within the turmeric rhizosphere. Collectively, these findings establish an in-silico sequence modeling rather than verified genome-wide host-driven evolution, providing insights into preliminary turmeric chemotype-culturable rhizobacterial associations. Future research should focus on high-throughput metagenomic profiling to unravel whole-community dynamics, isolation of specific bioactive compounds, and exploiting target rhizosphere strains for agricultural biofertilizer or therapeutic formulations.

Article.Title: Perivascular injection of a pH-responsive and protease-degradable hydrogel with rapamycin-loaded liposomes inhibits neointimal hyperplasia after carotid wire injury in mice
Article.Authors: Wu M.; Zhang L.; Li X.; Li R.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Neointimal hyperplasia is a major cause of restenosis and graft failure after vascular interventions. Perivascular drug delivery offers a potential solution, but achieving sustained and condition-dependent release at injured sites remains challenging. Here, we developed an injectable hydrogel with pH-sensitive and protease-susceptible characteristics (OHA-CS/GelMA) encapsulating rapamycin-loaded liposomes (Rapa-Lipo@Gel). The Schiff-base network enabled pH-triggered degradation, while GelMA provided mechanical stability and intrinsic susceptibility to protease-mediated degradation. The hydrogel degraded faster and released more rapamycin at pH 6.5 than at pH 7.4 in vitro, with further enhancement by protease. Liposomes suppressed burst release. In PDGF-BB-stimulated VSMCs, Rapa-Lipo@Gel inhibited proliferation, migration, and phenotypic switching (α-SMA↑, OPN↓). In a mouse carotid wire injury model, perivascular application of Rapa-Lipo@Gel at day 14 significantly reduced neointimal area and intima-to-media ratio compared to controls. Mechanistically, treatment reduced Ki67⁺ proliferating cells, decreased CD68⁺ macrophage infiltration, reduced overall α-SMA burden, increased MYH11 expression in the neointima, and did not reduce CD31⁺ endothelial coverage. Collectively, this pH-responsive and protease-susceptible hydrogel with liposomal rapamycin provides a promising platform with preliminary safety evidence for local treatment of neointimal hyperplasia, with potential for preventing restenosis.

Article.Title: Force-based design of a novel self-centring concentrically braced steel frame validated by nonlinear time-history analysis
Article.Authors: Alwahsh H.; Salawdeh S.; Jiang Y.; Goggins J.
Article.Abstract: Self-centring concentrically braced frames (SC-CBFs) are intended to limit residual deformation after strong earthquakes, but practical code-oriented procedures for their design remain limited. This study presents a force-based design (FBD) procedure for a horizontally post-tensioned SC-CBF consistent with Eurocode 8 and Eurocode 3. The procedure defines the seismic base shear, brace sizing, allocation of shear resistance between the concentrically braced frame and post-tensioning system, and capacity checks for beams, columns, braces, and strands. A regular four-storey archetype was designed using q = 4 as a case-study assumption and evaluated using nonlinear time-history analyses in OpenSees under 12 spectrum-matched earthquake records. The first-mode period obtained numerically (0.356 s) was close to the Eurocode estimate (0.34 s). Record-specific peak responses and the suite mean were examined; mean peak floor displacements and inter-storey drifts remained within the FBD design profiles, residual drifts were substantially below the adopted tolerance, and post-tensioning forces remained below the specified design capacity. Within the scope of this single archetype, these findings support the proposed FBD procedure as a practical basis for preliminary design of the investigated SC-CBF configuration. The adopted q value and the final 60:40 CBF-to-PT shear allocation are case-study-specific and require further evaluation across other structural and seismic conditions.
