Article.Authors: Byeon H.
Article.Abstract: Attention modules may improve fundus-image classification by reweighting informative channels and spatial regions. The model also had a reported inference time of 28 ms, a 35.2 MB file size, and 1.8 billion floating-point operations. These results support the feasibility of a compact attention-enhanced classifier in this controlled image-level evaluation. They do not establish full clinical effectiveness because the study used one public dataset and one archived split, lacked external validation and component-wise ablation, and did not retain paired lesion-level explanation outputs.

Article.Title: Evidence-based clinical question answering using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and open-source large language models
Article.Authors: Qasim A.; Escobar J.; Maldonado-Sifuentes C.; Akhtar Z.; Qasim S.; Calvo H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are being investigated for clinical decision support tools, but can produce unreliable outputs, including hallucinated information, overgeneralized answers, and responses not clearly derived from authoritative medical sources. To ground responses in high-quality medical texts, researchers developed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). In this work, we show that, within a structured, single-textbook corpus, embedding model choice has significantly greater impact on RAG system reliability and performance than chunking strategy. The system compares twelve embedding models—general-purpose and biomedical-specific—under token-level and character-level chunking, prompting the LLM to answer from retrieved snippets. We evaluate retrieval effectiveness using rank-based metrics and generation quality using standard measures across 232 questions. General-purpose embeddings, particularly Jina-Embeddings-v3 and BGE-base-en-v1.5, outperformed biomedical-specific encoders in both retrieval and generation. Across both strategies, higher retrieval precision translated directly into improved lexical and semantic alignment with gold references. Under our operational definition requiring explicit evidence spans, 35.6% of answered questions lacked supporting evidence; our best configuration (BGE-base-en-v1.5, token-level) achieved the lowest rate at 26.1%—an evidence-grounding measure, not a guarantee of correctness. These findings highlight the central role of retrieval quality in clinical RAG systems, showing that open-source, evidence-driven architectures offer a transparent alternative for textbook-based clinical QA settings.

Article.Title: Structured information extraction from geoscientific literature with GeoExtractor
Article.Authors: Peng Z.; Song Z.; Ye Y.; Li S.; Xiang Z.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Earth science research increasingly depends on the integration of large volumes of heterogeneous data distributed across publications. A substantial amount of quantitative information remains embedded in unstructured literature, making large-scale data compilation labor-intensive and difficult to maintain. Here, we introduce GeoExtractor, a large language model (LLM)-powered multi-agent framework designed to automatically extract structured information from geoscience literature. GeoExtractor employs a hierarchical extraction strategy that combines an iterative decision–retrieval–generation workflow with a two-stage retrieval mechanism, enabling the recovery of complex multi-instance scientific records from heterogeneous document sources. We evaluate the framework on four benchmark datasets spanning diverse geoscience sub-disciplines, using three LLMs and repeated runs to quantify variability. GeoExtractor generally performs better than the comparison methods on multi-record and multi-field tasks, while its limitations on single-record datasets are also characterized. To demonstrate its practical utility, we compiled a literature-derived database containing 2,259 zircon analyses from 179 publications of the Central Asian Orogenic Belt (CAOB), and the resulting dataset reproduces previously recognized tectonic patterns in the region. These results demonstrate that LLM-based multi-agent systems can facilitate the transformation of unstructured geoscientific literature into structured knowledge resources, substantially reducing the effort required for database construction and accelerating data-driven research across Earth science disciplines.

Article.Title: Sickle cell disease classification using Medav-Gaussian filter and Pyramid Shepard CNN
Article.Authors: Ponnada S.; Majji R.; Rout A.; Selvaraju S.
Article.Abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) poses serious health risks and requires accurate classification for effective treatment. In SCD, red blood cells (RBCs) mutate into a sickle shape due to a haemoglobin gene mutation, impairing oxygen delivery and causing blockages in blood vessels. However, accurate SCD classification from blood-smear images remains challenging due to image noise, variations in RBC morphology and overlapping cells. To address these challenges, this study introduces a deep learning (DL)- based approach named Pyramid Shepard convolutional neural network (PShCN-Net) for classifying SCD using blood smear images. The process begins with image denoising using the Medav-Gaussian (MG) filter, followed by cell segmentation with Tsallis entropy-based thresholding. Image augmentation is applied to enhance model robustness, and geometric and first-order statistical features are extracted. Classification is then performed using the proposed PShCN-Net, which combines the PyramidNet and Shephard convolutional neural network architectures for improved accuracy. PShCN-Net attains 91.945% accuracy, 93.235% true positive rate, 92.345% true negative rate, 91.437% precision, 92.327% F1-score, 7.655% false positive rate and 6.765% false negative rate when tested on 90% of the training data. Future work will focus on validating the PShCN-Net using larger and diverse multi-center blood-smear datasets to further assess its generalizability and clinical applicability.

Article.Title: The methylation of the RANKL/OPG system is involved in fluorosis, and the effect of betaine supplementation
Article.Authors: Wu W.; Chen T.; Tao N.; Li P.; Gao M.; Wang M.; Zhang X.; Tang L.; Liu M.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aims to explore the role of DNA methylation in the promoter region of the RANKL/OPG on fluorosis and the effect of betaine supplementation. A case-control study of 82 paired cases and controls was conducted among residents in coal-burning fluorosis areas in Guizhou Province, China. RANKL and OPG levels in serum of particpants were measured using ELISA. In addition, 60 SD rats were randomly divided into five groups ( n = 12): control group, model group, low-dose betaine group, medium-dose betaine group, and high-dose betaine group. 20 pairs case-control were randomly selected from 82 matched pairs to assess gene-specific DNA methylation. The methylation levels of RANKL/OPG in the human and rat whole blood were determined using targeted bisulfite sequencing (TBS). The expression of RANKL and OPG proteins in the femur tissues of rats was detected by Western blotting. The serum RANKL and OPG levels, and their ratios were elevated in the fluorosis patients compared with healthy individuals. A CpG site (pos651) in the OPG promoter exhibited hypomethylation in fluorosis patients, but this did not retain statistical significance after FDR correction( q > 0.05). Furthermore, betaine supplementation produced a dose-dependent reduction in dental fluorosis. Notably, dental fluorosis was present in 100% of the fluoride-exposed model group. Moreover, DNA methylation of CpG sites at pos1262, pos1289, pos1293, and pos1295 in the OPG gene of rat was reduced in the model group compared with the control group, and the methylation level was significantly restored in the betaine intervention group ( P < 0.05). Additionally, long-term fluoride exposure upregulated the expression of RANKL and OPG proteins in bone tissues of the rats however, whereas betaine supplementation could reverse these changes dose-dependently ( P < 0.05). Fluorosis may be associated with aberrant methylation of CpG sites in the OPG promoter. And betaine may potentially alleviate fluoride-induced bone changes, potentially through the regulation of the OPG/RANKL axis via epigenetic mechanisms.

Article.Title: Thirty-five years of urban expansion and thermal transformation: Integrating LULC change climate variability and population growth
Article.Authors: Li R.; Yuan Y.; Tahir Z.; Haseeb M.; Mahmoood S.; Tariq A.; Faqeih K.; Alamri S.; Alamery E.; Kemal B.; Kucher D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rapid urban expansion can alter surface thermal conditions, yet these changes are often evaluated without accounting for climatic variability, demographic pressures, and uncertainty. This study investigated long-term land-use/land-cover (LULC) and thermal dynamics in Jhang District, Pakistan, for 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020, and 2025 using Landsat-based LULC classification, land surface temperature (LST), surface urban heat island (SUHI), Urban Thermal Field Variance Index (UTFVI), spectral indices, Getis–Ord Gi* hotspot analysis, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression (MLR). Landsat-derived LST was independently compared with MODIS, while ERA5-Land, CHIRPS, and GHS-POP were used to characterize climatic and demographic context. Urban land expanded from 62.67 km² (0.98%) to 341.36 km² (5.37%), with 219.53 km² of Vegetated Land converted to Urban land. Maximum LST increased from 49.09 °C to 55.01 °C, while 99% confidence hot spots expanded from 856.42 to 1,041.31 km². LST was negatively correlated with NDVI and NDMI and positively correlated with NDBI and NDBaI. MLR models explained 54.2–83.1% of spatial LST variability. MODIS comparison showed strong spatial correspondence (R 2 = 0.752–0.843) despite systematic absolute-temperature differences. Air temperature increased significantly by 0.199 °C decade⁻¹, while population rose from 1.58 to 3.44 million. The findings demonstrate that Jhang’s thermal evolution reflects interacting land-cover, climatic, and demographic pressures rather than urban growth alone.

Article.Title: Loneliness and quality of life among older adults in Poland: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Domosławska-Żylińska K.; Partyka O.; Kwiatkowska K.; Malewska-Niemyjska K.; Łopatek M.; Olejniczak D.
Article.Abstract: Rapid population aging is reshaping demographic structures and public health challenges. Loneliness among older adults is associated with poorer mental and physical health, higher mortality, and reduced quality of life. This study assessed loneliness and its sociodemographic, social, and health-related correlates among adults aged ≥ 60 years in Poland. A cross-sectional survey was conducted using computer-assisted telephone interviews (CATI) from September to November 2025 among 1,090 adults aged ≥ 60 years. Loneliness was measured using the Revised UCLA Loneliness Scale (R-UCLA), and quality of life using the WHOQOL-BREF. Analyses included parametric and non-parametric tests, Pearson correlations, and hierarchical multivariable linear regression ( p < 0.05). Higher loneliness was associated with lower quality of life across all WHOQOL-BREF domains (all p < 0.001). The highest loneliness was observed among participants aged ≥ 85 years, those with severe functional limitations, living alone, and not participating in local social or educational activities (all p < 0.001). Lower loneliness was associated with marriage, economic activity, and sufficient financial resources (all p < 0.001). The final model explained 45.4% of variance, with relationship satisfaction, face-to-face family contact, age, and financial adequacy remaining significant. Findings highlight the need to strengthen social contact and meaningful relationships, particularly among the oldest adults and residents of large cities.

Article.Title: Short-term changes in HIV-related knowledge, attitudes, and self-reported practices following empowerment-based health education among Chinese college students: a single-group pilot study
Article.Authors: Yang H.; Wang X.; Guan Y.; Peng W.; Wan L.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: This pilot study described short-term within-participant changes in HIV/AIDS-related knowledge, attitudes, and self-reported practices following an empowerment-based program among college students in Sichuan, China. We purposively recruited 153 students to a five-week, six-module program comprising lectures, flipped classrooms, case discussion, role-play, condom-use demonstration, peer education, and reflection. A single-group pretest-posttest design was used. Identical nonidentifying study codes linked assessments. Paired t tests and item-level absolute Cohen’s dz described within-participant change Immediately after the program, knowledge and attitude scores were higher than at baseline, with the largest changes involving misconceptions about non-transmission routes and stigmatizing attitudes toward people living with HIV/AIDS (all P < 0.05). Changes in self-reported practice were smaller: the item concerning prevention of sexually transmitted diseases and sexual morality changed ( P = 0.011), whereas the item concerning personal hygiene and drug avoidance did not reach statistical significance ( P = 0.096). In this single-group pilot study, higher post-program knowledge and attitude scores were observed within participants, whereas changes in the two self-reported practice items were limited. These findings are preliminary associations and do not establish that the program caused the observed changes. Controlled, multicenter studies using validated behavioral measures and longer follow-up are needed. Interactive empowerment-based HIV education warrants further evaluation as a university health-education approach. Future randomized or controlled longitudinal studies should identify active pedagogical components and determine whether short-term changes in knowledge and attitudes are followed by sustained, objectively assessed preventive behaviors.

Article.Title: Mechanisms of aquifer protection and surface subsidence control induced by gangue-paste collaborative backfilling in deep coal mining
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Wu G.; Ma P.; Yu W.; Han T.; Chen B.; Qin J.
Article.Abstract: Mining-induced overburden deformation and surface subsidence pose significant threats to groundwater systems and ecological environments in deep coal mining areas. Developing effective backfilling technologies to control strata movement has therefore become critical for sustainable mining. Based on the deep high-mining-height working face of Pingmei No.11 Mine, this study investigates the influence mechanism of gangue–paste collaborative backfill technology on overlying strata evolution. A collaborative technical system integrating fully mechanized paste backfill behind supports with in-situ gangue backfill is proposed, and a volumetric strain–grading index–confining pressure coupling model and a backfill–surrounding rock–coal pillar collaborative bearing model are established. The evolution characteristics of stress and displacement fields are comparatively analyzed via FLAC3D numerical simulation, and field monitoring verifies the engineering effectiveness. Laboratory results show that continuously graded gangue with a grading index of 0.5 reduces volumetric strain by 38% compared with randomly graded gangue. Numerical simulations reveal that collaborative backfill reduces maximum roof displacement to 139.5 mm and expands the stress plateau zone by 25%. Field monitoring confirms that maximum surface subsidence is only 20 mm, with building crack widths controlled at 1–2 mm, fully meeting Class I protection standards. The proposed system forms a three-in-one control mechanism of mechanical compaction–paste roof contact–spatiotemporal coordination, and reveals the power-law relationship between backfill compression modulus and strata subsidence rate. These findings provide a theoretical basis and engineering paradigm for green mining of deep coal seams.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: aquifer protection; deep coal mining; surface subsidence control; mine backfill

Article.Title: Reproducible smoker’s paradox in COVID-19 - comparative evidence from Swedish and Norwegian cohorts
Article.Authors: Kirui B.; Vikjord S.; Li H.; Vanfleteren L.; Nyberg F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Literature on the impact of smoking on COVID-19 has been inconsistent, and the association remains incompletely understood. To assess the effect of smoking on COVID-19 outcomes using different data sources. We analyzed two cohorts with detailed smoking information linked to COVID-19: a cohort defined from Swedish chronic disease registers (airway disease, heart failure, cardiac disease, and diabetes) and a general population cohort from Norway. Participants with smoking information from 2019 (registers) or 2017–2019 (general population) were included and classified as never, former or current smokers. Adjusted Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for COVID-19 outcomes from January 2020 to December 2022. The chronic disease register cohort included 506,745 individuals, and the general population cohort 155,333. Current smokers were the smallest group (13% and 11%), and never-smokers the largest (55% and 46%), in the two cohorts, respectively. Compared with never-smokers, current smokers had lower hazards of non-fatal COVID-19 events. For COVID-19 infection, HRs were 0.75 [CI: 0.73–0.77] in the chronic disease register cohort and for diagnosis 0.93 [0.91–0.96] in the general population cohort; for hospitalization, the HR was 0.88 [0.84–0.93] in the chronic disease register cohort. However, current smokers had higher hazards of COVID-19 death in both cohorts, although CIs included the null. Former smokers had clearly elevated hazards for most outcomes across both cohorts. While paradoxical inverse associations were observed for COVID-19 infection and hospitalization, current smokers consistently exhibited higher HR estimates for COVID-19 death across cohorts, although the confidence intervals were wide and included the null value.

Article.Title: Blood and saliva provide complementary but non-redundant host transcriptomic responses to cancer
Article.Authors: Koduru S.; Kidd M.; Halim A.
Article.Abstract: Blood and saliva are two of the most accessible biofluids for non-invasive molecular profiling, yet it remains unclear whether they report the same biological response to cancer. Using matched whole-blood and saliva transcriptomic profiling from patients with multiple malignancies (27 samples from six cancers [prostate, lung, breast, pancreatic, colon, or melanoma]) and 9 healthy controls, we evaluated the extent to which these compartments share or diverge in their cancer-associated responses. Although the majority of expressed genes were shared between blood and saliva (about 25,400 detected in blood and 24,100 in saliva, with 86% of salivary genes detectable in blood), global transcriptomic analyses demonstrated that biofluid identity was the dominant source of variation. Cancer-associated transcriptional changes exhibited weak cross-biofluid concordance ( r = 0.01–0.28), which may indicate that the two compartments respond to malignancy through distinct biological mechanisms. Blood-derived signatures were enriched for systemic immune, inflammatory, hematopoietic, and host-defense pathways, whereas salivary signatures emphasized epithelial, secretory, metabolic, and microbial-associated processes. Saliva additionally contained a rich microbial transcriptome absent from blood. These findings demonstrate that blood and saliva provide complementary rather than interchangeable information regarding host responses to cancer and support integrated multi-biofluid approaches for future cancer detection and disease monitoring. Because the cohort is small and heterogeneous, with only three to seven patients per malignancy, all per-cancer findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than generalizable; the principal conclusion concerns the global relationship between the two biofluids.

Article.Title: Efficient training-free query routing framework for federated retrieval-augmented generation
Article.Authors: Eoo H.; Yoo Y.; Yang G.
Article.Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances large language models (LLMs) by grounding responses in external documents retrieved at inference time. In federated RAG (FedRAG), documents are distributed across multiple autonomous corpora that cannot be centrally aggregated due to privacy, regulatory, or organizational constraints. A key challenge in FedRAG is query routing: selecting a subset of relevant corpora for each query without broadcasting to all participants. Existing routing approaches rely on supervised learning, requiring a uniform retrieval embedding model across corpora and costly retraining whenever the federation changes. These assumptions violate corpus autonomy and limit scalability in dynamic federated environments. We propose RAGSpot , a training-free query routing framework that enables efficient corpus selection without requiring a shared local retrieval embedding model. RAGSpot represents each corpus using compact cluster-level metadata derived from its vector index and estimates corpus relevance via query-to-cluster matching. In addition, it introduces a rank-based fusion strategy that jointly leverages document-level and corpus-level rankings to support robust aggregation across heterogeneous embedding models. Experiments with corpora from the BEIR benchmark show that RAGSpot improves retrieval accuracy over the strongest training-based router by 1.23– \(1.48\times\) in nDCG and 1.28– \(1.66\times\) in Recall, and over the strongest LLM-based router by 1.63– \(2.01\times\) in nDCG and 1.93– \(2.34\times\) in Recall, without any further training. Also, RAGSpot achieves query latency that is comparable to, or even lower than, that of SOTA methods on average.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: reciprocal rank fusion; query routing; K-means clustering

Article.Title: Human adipocytes support the proliferation and migration of colorectal cancer cells with concomitant modulation of their glycolysis rate and lipid metabolism
Article.Authors: Pietraszek-Gremplewicz K.; Domagalski M.; Olszańska J.; Skoniecka A.; Tymińska A.; Pikuła M.; Nowak D.
Article.Abstract: Adipose tissue plays a pivotal role in the development and formation of colorectal cancer (CRC). Its primary cellular component, adipocytes, contributes significantly to this process. In the presence of cancer cells, adipocytes convert into cancer-associated adipocytes, which acquire features that promote tumor progression. Thus, the main objective of this study was to investigate how cancer-associated adipocytes stimulate the aggressiveness of CRC cells. Using an indirect co-culture model, we characterized the functional, molecular, and metabolic modifications of CRC cells induced by primary human adipocytes. Our results demonstrate that adipocytes promote an aggressive CRC cell phenotype. Adipocytes stimulated hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal transition of CRC cells with concomitant modification in the expression profile of stem cell markers. Moreover, upon co-culture with adipocytes, the metabolic reprogramming of cancer cells favoring fatty acid oxidation as well as glycolysis linked with cholesterol accumulation was noted. Interestingly, adipocytes also modulated the level of lipases and the lipolysis rate in CRC cells. The results underline the substantial influence of adipocytes on CRC cell behavior, highlighting the presence of several simultaneous mechanisms possibly controlling the tumor expansion in the adipocyte-rich niche.

Article.Title: Pre-disaster preventive dispatch for urban power grids considering frequency support from hydrogen energy systems
Article.Authors: Li D.; Li Z.; Qin H.; He C.; Lin X.; Tang H.
Article.Abstract: With the increasing frequency of extreme weather disasters, urban power grids are vulnerable to topology disruptions and to the frequency-security risks associated with weather-induced line outages and post-contingency operating disturbances. To enhance frequency support in pre-disaster preventive dispatch, this paper proposes a method for pre-disaster preventive dispatch in urban power grids considering frequency support from hydrogen energy systems. First, considering the virtual inertia control and primary frequency regulation characteristics of fuel cells and electrolyzers, a system frequency dynamic response model is constructed, and constraints on the maximum rate of change of frequency, maximum frequency deviation, and quasi-steady-state frequency deviation are established. Second, with the objective of minimizing the cost of pre-disaster preventive dispatch and the expected load-shedding loss under fault scenarios, an optimization model is developed by considering generator output adjustments, hydrogen energy system operation, preventive load shedding, and frequency-regulation reserve allocation. Finally, the problem is formulated as a Markov decision process and solved using the Soft Actor–Critic (SAC) algorithm. Case studies on the modified IEEE 39-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems show that the proposed method can reduce load-shedding loss, improve online decision speed and promote compliance with the prescribed frequency-security limits under the investigated scenarios and evaluation protocol.

Article.Title: Mechanism and field application of CO₂ phase‑change fracturing for gas extraction in low‑permeability coal seams
Article.Authors: Deng C.; Li P.; Zheng C.; Xu M.
Article.Abstract: To address the inefficient gas extraction problem of high‑gas low‑permeability coal seams in Guizhou Province, this study investigates the permeability‑enhancing mechanism and field performance of liquid CO₂ phase‑change fracturing, taking local anthracite and bituminous coal as research objects. Relying on the special thermophysical properties of liquid CO₂, phase‑change shock loading creates multi‑zone fracturing in coal mass; meanwhile, CO₂ can displace adsorbed methane to improve seam permeability. Energy equivalence calculation indicates that 1.4 kg liquid CO₂ releases phase‑transition energy equivalent to 243 g TNT, proving good safety and controllability of this technology. Field tests show that gas production of fractured boreholes follows negative‑exponential attenuation with fitting R² of 0.85‑0.99. The effective gas drainage radius expands rapidly within 10‑30 days after fracturing and finally increases by 1.9‑2.5 times compared with original coal seams. Under consistent fracturing construction parameters, despite inherent disparities in baseline geological properties between the two test coal seams, bituminous coal achieves better pressure‑relief and permeability‑enhancement performance than anthracite. Further analysis reveals the coal‑rank‑dependent differential response mechanism: dense‑matrix anthracite dissipates most impact energy near boreholes and limits fracture propagation, whereas well‑cleated bituminous coal develops long‑range connected fracture networks for efficient gas seepage. This study clarifies the lithology‑controlled differential mechanism of liquid CO₂ phase‑change fracturing and forms targeted gas‑control technology for Guizhou coal mines. The findings provide theoretical support and engineering references for efficient coalbed methane exploitation in high‑gas low‑permeability coal seams of Southwest China.

Article.Title: Synergistic in situ upgrading and heat storage in intermittent SAGD enabled by a bifunctional nanocatalyst
Article.Authors: Zhao R.; Zhou D.; Xu W.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The efficient development of heavy oil and oil sands resources faces critical challenges, particularly the high energy consumption and lack of in-situ upgrading capabilities of Steam-Assisted Gravity Drainage (SAGD) technology. This study proposes a bifunctional nanocatalyst-assisted intermittent SAGD (CNF-I-SAGD) technology to achieve in-situ heavy oil upgrading and efficient thermal energy management. The core innovation is a Ni-Mo/Al₂O₃@Al-Sn-Si core-shell nanocatalyst, where the Al-Sn-Si ternary eutectic alloy acts as a phase-change material (PCM) for thermal energy storage, and the Ni-Mo/Al₂O₃ shell catalyzes hydrothermal cracking.Physical simulation experiments demonstrate that CNF-I-SAGD achieves a final recovery factor of 72.5%, 7.9% higher than conventional I-SAGD. Crucially, during intermittent steam shut-in, the PCM core releases latent heat, maintaining a temperature plateau near 225 °C for up to 8 min, extending the catalyst’s effective high-temperature operating time by 18.5%. This reduces the instantaneous steam-oil ratio (SOR) to 3.56 and improves energy efficiency by 18.7%. Oil analysis reveals that the produced oil exhibits an API gravity increased to 15.2°, a viscosity reduction of 71.7%, and a significant 58% decrease in asphaltene content. This research presents an integrated approach coupling PCM-based thermal energy storage with nanocatalytic in-situ upgrading, offering a promising strategy for green and efficient heavy oil resource development.

Article.Title: TMS timed to interictal epileptiform discharges
Article.Authors: Makkonen M.; Kahilakoski O.; Menchaca M.; Zubarev I.; Siljamo O.; Hassan U.; She X.; Qi W.; Mutanen T.; Ilmoniemi R.; Lioumis P.; Baumer F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) are pathological hypersynchronous bursts of electrical brain activity that occur between seizures in patients with epilepsy. IEDs are caused by transient brain states that are difficult to predict, making them a challenging neurophysiological and technological case for brain-state-dependent stimulation. Administering stimulation at IED onset may provide insight into the epileptic network and optimize neurostimulation therapies. Here, we assessed the feasibility of IED-triggered transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in two children with self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), a common pediatric epilepsy in which IEDs emerge from the motor cortex. A convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained on the participants’ pre-recorded electroencephalography (EEG) data with IEDs annotated by an epileptologist. The CNN was integrated into an EEG-processing pipeline that classified EEG segments as “IED” or “non-IED” in real time. With this pipeline, TMS pulses were administered during IED or non-IED periods in an interleaved, randomized design. We stimulated both the motor cortex generating the IEDs and the contralateral motor cortex and tested the impact of IEDs on TMS-evoked potentials (TEPs). Our study demonstrated that TMS can be timed to IEDs and that there is a site-specific increase in TEP amplitude when stimulating during IEDs. Out of the TMS pulses aimed at an IED, 19% and 39% were successfully delivered during an IED for the two participants, respectively. For future research, we propose ways to address the methodological challenges of IED-timed TMS, enabling brain-state-dependent TMS for epilepsy research and treatment.

Article.Title: Air pollution and rice crop health: evidence from Vietnam’s Mekong Delta
Article.Authors: Go E.; Iddawela Y.; Le S.; Tan E.
Article.Abstract: Ambient air pollution is a growing concern in Southeast Asia, yet its effects on crop performance remain less understood than its effects on human health. Here, we examine whether fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure is associated with rice crop health in Vietnam’s Mekong Delta, a major global rice-producing region. Our main contribution lies in developing a scalable methodology for data-scarce settings using remote-sensing indicators of crop condition with satellite-derived PM2.5, weather data, night-time lights, and fire activity from 2017 to 2022. Panel fixed effects estimates suggest a non-linear relationship between PM2.5 and crop health during the reproductive stage, with damages starting at 16.5 \(\upmu \) g/ \(\hbox {m}^3\) , below the average levels of concentration in the area. The negative impacts of PM2.5 are consistent with the reduction of fraction of photosynthetically active radiation. To address potential endogeneity in local pollution exposure, we instrument PM2.5 using episodic transboundary fire activity outside the Mekong Delta. The instrumental variable estimates also indicate a negative effect of haze-related pollution on crop condition. Together, these findings suggest that air pollution could impose agricultural costs in major rice producing areas, and should be considered in regional food-security and environmental policy discussions.

Article.Title: Post-weaning DHA or EPA supplementation attenuates depressive-like behavior and myelination deficits induced by maternal high-fat diet in rat offspring
Article.Authors: Śliwa M.; Frankowska M.; Jastrzębska J.; Wesołowska J.; Filip M.; Smaga I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Depression affects younger populations, while imbalanced diet may contribute to disease development, with myelin abnormalities representing one possible underlying mechanism. We previously showed that maternal high-fat diet (HFD; 60% energy from fat) during pregnancy and lactation induces depressive-like behavior and myelin-related alterations in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) of rat offspring. We investigated whether post-weaning docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)- or eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)-enriched diets until adulthood could reverse these abnormalities. Depressive-like behavior was assessed in the forced swimming test (FST), while myelin-related changes were analyzed using RT-qPCR, ELISA, and immunofluorescence staining. Both DHA and EPA-enriched diets normalized increased immobility time in adult offspring. In male offspring, both diets normalized the mRNA levels of genes encoding myelin-oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG), 2′,3′-cyclic nucleotide 3′-phosphodiesterase (CNPase), and transferrin, whereas only EPA additionally restored the mRNA levels of genes encoding myelin and lymphocyte protein (MAL) and kallikrein 6 (KLK6). At the protein level, DHA normalized only MOG, while EPA restored MOG, MAL, and CNPase levels. In females, both DHA and EPA increased Mog mRNA levels, whereas DHA additionally increased Klk6 mRNA expression compared to offspring exposed to maternal HFD and post-weaning SD. At the cellular level, DHA and EPA produced sex-specific effects, with broader restoration of oligodendrocytes and myelin intensity in males. Maternal HFD also decreased brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) levels in male offspring (mRNA and protein level), while post-weaning DHA and EPA supplementation restored Bdnf mRNA expression. Overall, post-weaning DHA and EPA alleviated maternal HFD-induced FST-assessed depressive-like behavior and partially restored myelin-related abnormalities in the PFC, with EPA exerting broader molecular and cellular effects than DHA.

Article.Title: Self-reported pain, depressive symptoms and risk for cardiovascular diseases
Article.Authors: Mu X.; Zheng X.; Cao M.
Article.Abstract: Previous studies have found that both pain and depressive symptoms are deleteriously associated with cardiovascular diseases (CVD). The aim of current study was to investigate the joint association of pain and depressive symptoms with CVD risk. A total of 13,184 participants aged 45 years or older from the China Health and Retirement longitudinal study were included in current study. Participants were divided into 4 groups according to self-reported pain and depressive symptoms status. Cox proportional hazards regression model was used to explore the associations between self-reported pain/depressive symptoms and new-onset CVD, stroke and cardiac events. During the 9-year follow-up, a total of 2,834 individuals experienced CVD (including 965 stroke and 2,168 cardiac events). Both self-reported pain and depressive symptoms were independently associated with increased risk of CVD. Self-reported pain and depressive symptoms had additive and multiplicative interactions on CVD risk. Compared to individuals without self-reported pain/depressive symptoms, the adjusted hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) were 1.23 (1.11–1.37) for those with depressive symptoms alone, 1.33 (1.19–1.49) with self-reported pain alone, and 1.59 (1.44–1.76) for those with both self-reported pain and depressive symptoms. Similarly, individuals with both self-reported pain and depressive symptoms were also with highest risk of stroke and cardiac events. Both self-reported pain and depressive symptoms were associated with increasing risk of CVD, individually. Those with pain and depressive symptoms had the highest risk of CVD, suggesting likely synergistic effects. Our findings support the need to target both pain and depressive symptoms in research and clinical practice.

Article.Title: Shared household environment structures the gut microbiota in a large family cohort with central areolar choroidal dystrophy
Article.Authors: Garcia-Gutierrez E.; Ponsero A.; Delgado J.; Crispie F.; Cotter P.; Cuenca N.; Lax P.
Article.Abstract: Central areolar choroidal dystrophy (CACD) is a rare monogenic hereditary retinal dystrophy characterised by progressive retinal pigment epithelium and choriocapillaris atrophy, photoreceptor loss, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiota can modulate systemic inflammatory responses and may influence ocular health through the gut-eye axis. However, the contribution of the gut microbiota to CACD remains unexplored. In this pilot study, we investigated the gut microbiota composition of members of a large Spanish family carrying the PRPH2 Arg195Leu mutation associated with CACD. Faecal samples from 33 mutation carriers and 24 non-carrier household members were analysed using whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing. Taxonomic composition and bacterial diversity were compared adjusting for sequencing depth, age, and sex, accounting for shared household environment through paired and mixed-effects analyses. The findings suggest that gut microbiota variation in this CACD cohort is primarily driven by shared environmental factors rather than disease status at this depth of sequencing. Our study highlights the critical importance of accounting for household effects in microbiome studies of familial and rare genetic diseases and provides a robust framework for future investigations into the gut-eye axis using longitudinal or interventional designs.

Article.Title: 3D numerical study of race-tracking and air entrapment phenomena in polymer filling process
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Liu Q.; Jiang C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The race-tracking effect and air entrapment are two important phenomena that restrict the quality and performance of injection molded parts. This study considers two types of parts with different wall-thickness distributions. Through numerical simulations combined with experimental observations, the race-tracking effect and air entrapment phenomena during polymer melt filling in 3D cavities are investigated, with particular emphasis on the influence of the thin-to-thick wall-thickness ratio. A two-phase flow model is developed by coupling the Navier–Stokes equations with the level set equation, and is discretized using a collocated grid finite volume method and the SIMPLE algorithm is employed for pressure–velocity coupling. The results show that the proposed model can accurately predict melt front evolution in complex cavities and effectively capture the race-tracking effect and air entrapment phenomena during filling. Furthermore, the thin-to-thick wall-thickness ratio plays a crucial role in both phenomena: decreasing this ratio intensifies the race-tracking effect, and for circular cavities, also increases the trapped air area.

Article.Title: High tacrolimus intrapatient variability is associated with graft loss after kidney transplantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Chienwichai K.; Mongkolrattanakul P.; Chang A.
Article.Abstract: Tacrolimus intrapatient variability (IPV) has been proposed as a predictor of adverse outcomes after kidney transplantation, but the magnitude and consistency of this association across IPV measurement methods remain unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies evaluating the association between tacrolimus IPV and clinical outcomes in adult kidney transplant recipients. MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception through October 2025. The primary outcome was death-censored graft loss (DCGL). Random-effects meta-analyses used a three-level model to account for dependence among multiple effect sizes within studies. Ten studies involving 11,647 patients were included. High tacrolimus IPV was associated with increased risk of DCGL (HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.37–3.32; I2 = 69.3%) and rejection (HR 2.05, 95% CI 1.24–3.41; I2 = 0.0%). Point estimates were similar across IPV calculation methods, geographic regions, and assessment timeframes, although subgroup analyses were exploratory and imprecise. The reported prevalence of high IPV ranged from 11 to 69%, reflecting differences in the variability metric, threshold, and measurement window. Taken together, high tacrolimus IPV is associated with graft loss and rejection after kidney transplantation. Whether IPV can serve as a clinical monitoring tool will require standardized measurement, validated thresholds, and prospective evidence.

Article.Title: Development and preliminary psychometric evaluation of the postpartum sexual and reproductive health questionnaire (PSRHQ) in Iranian women
Article.Authors: Rezaei N.; Namazi M.; Sharifi N.; Moghadam Z.; Tahmasebi A.; Taheri S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The postpartum period is a critical phase in a woman’s life. This study aimed to develop and psychometrically evaluate a questionnaire designed to assess sexual and reproductive health among postpartum women. This exploratory sequential mixed-method study was conducted in three phases. In the qualitative phase, 17 mothers, 5 husbands, and 6 midwives participated in semi-structured interviews. Based on the findings, an item pool was developed. In the psychometric phase, content validity, face validity, construct validity and reliability were examined. A total of 98 initial items were generated. After content and face validity assessments, followed by construct validity assessment, the initial 98-item pool was reduced to a final 26-item questionnaire. The exploratory factor analysis (EFA) extracted four factors: spouse abuse, postpartum care, marital problems, and psychological-emotional problems. The total Cronbach’s alpha coefficient was 0.899, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) was 0.846, providing evidence of satisfactory internal consistency and test–retest reliability. The PSRHQ demonstrated preliminary evidence of validity and satisfactory reliability for assessing multiple dimensions of postpartum sexual and reproductive health. Further validation, including confirmatory factor analysis and evaluation of criterion-related, longitudinal, and cross-cultural measurement properties, is needed before broader application.

Article.Title: A single-switch quadratic DC–DC converter with ultra-high voltage gain and low voltage stress on semiconductors
Article.Authors: Gozali M.; Aghaei H.; Babaei E.; Sabahi M.
Article.Abstract: This study offers a single-switch ultra-high step-up DC–DC converter based on the quadratic configuration. In the proposed topology, the quadratic structure is integrated with an auxiliary circuit employing a three-winding coupled inductor. The converter obtains an enhanced voltage gain while simultaneously decreasing the voltage stress imposed on the power switch by incorporating switched capacitor and voltage multiplier methods. As a result, a low on-resistance switch can be utilized, which significantly improves the overall efficiency of the converter. A shared ground between the source and output sides is another notable feature of the proposed converter, enhancing its suitability for a wide range of practical applications. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that, relative to conventional DC–DC boost converters, the proposed design attains a superior voltage conversion ratio. Additionally, it requires a smaller input inductance to supply the load with minimal input current ripple, which contributes to lower power losses. Experimental results obtained from a 200 W laboratory-scale hardware implementation with a 25 V input and a 400 V output validate the effectiveness and performance of the suggested topology.

Article.Title: Clinical significance of intramammary lymph nodes in female primary breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Zhao Z.; Wang X.; Zhang W.; Zhang L.; Pei S.; Yang Y.; Qu Z.; Li Z.; Lu J.; Fang Y.; Wang J.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Intramammary lymph nodes (IntraMLNs), located within the breast parenchyma or axillary tail, are uncommon, and their clinical significance in primary breast cancer remains unclear. This meta-analysis evaluated the association between IntraMLN and axillary lymph node (ALN) status, together with incidence, metastatic rate, diagnostic performance, risk factors, and prognosis. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched without language or date restrictions. Eligible studies included adult women with primary breast cancer and pathologically confirmed IntraMLNs. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed independently. Pooled proportions, odds ratios (ORs), and diagnostic test accuracy indices were estimated using fixed- or random-effects models. Publication bias was assessed using Egger’s or Deeks’ test. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251137541). Twenty-four studies involving 1,482 patients were included. The pooled incidence of pathologically detected IntraMLNs was 0.03 (95% CI, 0.01–0.08), and the metastatic rate was 0.32 (95% CI, 0.27–0.37). IntraMLN positivity was significantly associated with ALN involvement (pooled OR, 4.96; 95% CI, 3.55–6.93). Pooled sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, PLR, NLR, and DOR were 0.505, 0.813, 0.674, 0.711, 2.738, 0.635, and 4.961, respectively. Lymphovascular invasion, tumor size/T stage, and histological grade were commonly associated with IntraMLN metastasis. Prognostic findings were inconsistent. IntraMLN metastasis is strongly associated with ALN involvement and indicates increased axillary metastatic risk. However, its diagnostic accuracy is insufficient to replace standard axillary staging, and its independent prognostic value remains inconclusive.

Article.Title: Comparative phytochemical characterization and in vitro biological activities of coffee (Coffea arabica) and loquat (Eriobotrya japonica) seed extracts
Article.Authors: Al-Rajhi A.; Alsalamah S.; Almotayri A.; Almimoni N.; Zeleei R.; Al Abboud M.; Shater A.; Mashraqi A.; Sahagi E.; Masmali I.; Abdelghany T.
Article.Abstract: The growing demand for natural bioactive compounds has intensified research into plant-derived extracts as plant-derived extracts as sources of bioactive compounds. Coffee ( Coffea arabica ) and loquat ( Eriobotrya japonica ) seeds represent underutilized sources of phytochemicals with potential health benefits, yet a direct comparative evaluation of their multi-target bioactivities remain limited . The objectives were to comparatively assess the phytochemical profiles with antidiabetic, antioxidant, butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) inhibitory activity, antimicrobial, and cytotoxic potentials of coffee and loquat seed ethanol extracts against Caco-2 colorectal cancer cells. Total phenolics, flavonoids, alkaloids, and terpenes were quantified by colorimetric assays, while different phenolic ingredients were examined by HPLC. Antioxidant activity was evaluated using DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging assays. α-Glucosidase and α-amylase inhibition assays were utilized for antidiabetic action, while butyrylcholinesterase inhibition assay was utilized for the extract. Antimicrobial and anti-biofilm activities were tested against pathogenic bacteria and Candida albicans ; and cytotoxicity was assessed on Caco-2 (cancer) and Wi38 (normal) cells. Coffee seed extract contained significantly higher levels of total phenolics (172.46 ± 7.17 mg GAE/g), flavonoids (157.36 ± 3.34 mg QuE/g), and chlorogenic acid (63,681.37 ± 1,245.6 µg/g). It exhibited stronger antioxidant (DPPH IC₅₀ 0.66 ± 0.03 µg/mL; ABTS IC₅₀ 0.42 ± 0.02 µg/mL), antidiabetic (α-glucosidase IC₅₀ 10.20 ± 0.15 µg/mL), anti-Alzheimer (BChE IC₅₀ 3.20 ± 0.08 µg/mL), activity against the tested reference strains (MIC 7.8 µg/mL against S. aureus ), and differential cytotoxicity against Caco-2 cancer cells (IC₅₀ 78.5 ± 0.2 µg/mL) with lower toxicity to normal Wi38 fibroblasts (IC₅₀ 181.3 ± 2.2 µg/mL) under the conditions tested. This resulted in a preliminary selectivity index of 2.31, suggesting differential cytotoxicity that warrants further investigation. Loquat extract showed moderate but noteworthy activity, particularly against C. albicans (94.12 ± 0.8% biofilm biomass reduction (%) at 75% MBC). Coffee seeds show promising multifunctional bioactivities in vitro, warranting further investigation. Loquat seeds demonstrate moderate but noteworthy anti-Candida activity, suggesting potential for further fractionation and characterization.

Article.Title: Impulsivity, cognitive inflexibility, and brain network dysregulation in etomidate use disorder: A clinical and EEG microstate study
Article.Authors: Liao Z.; Huang Q.; Chen X.; Le J.; Wang X.; Wang X.; Tang Y.; Shen H.
Article.Abstract: Etomidate, a short-acting GABA_A receptor modulator and emerging novel psychoactive substance, is increasingly abused non-medically. Despite rising clinical concern, the neuropsychological profiles of etomidate use disorder (EUD) remain poorly characterized, prompting this systematic investigation of its clinical and neurophysiological features. 152 individuals with EUD and 67 age-matched healthy controls (HC) were recruited. Participants completed a series of standardized assessments measuring craving, impulsivity, inhibitory control, and habitual behavior. Resting-state EEG data were analyzed using microstate analysis to characterize the temporal organization of large-scale brain activity, and a multidimensional feature-based support vector machine (SVM) model was built to distinguish EUD from HC. The EUD group exhibited significantly higher craving and impulsivity, and poorer performance on stop-signal and reversal learning tasks. Microstate analysis revealed significantly longer durations of microstates B, C, and D and reduced occurrence of microstate A in the EUD group. SVM classification achieved an AUC of 0.777. This is the first comprehensive characterization of EUD, demonstrating distinct clinical features and alterations in the temporal organization of large-scale brain activity. These findings characterize cross-sectional clinical and neurophysiological features associated with EUD and highlight the potential value of EEG microstate analysis to probe such brain network temporal changes.

Article.Title: A novel hourly PM2.5 concentration prediction model using IMSTL-FVMD-HLDT hybrid architecture with Adam optimized by Schrödinger search strategy
Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Qiao P.; Li H.; Yang S.; Shi Q.; Qin Q.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: PM 2.5 concentration time series are characterized by obvious chaotic behavior, mutually superimposed multi-period components and notable temporal fluctuations, which pose considerable difficulties to the high-precision prediction of PM 2.5 concentration. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel hybrid predictive framework, namely IMSTL-FVMD- HLDT-SRAdam. This framework first employs IMSTL decomposition algorithm to separate the original PM 2.5 series into a trend component, multiple seasonal sub-components, and a residual component, and further splits the residual component into multiple residual sub-components via FVMD decomposition strategy for full extraction of its valid information. Subsequently, these three types of components are taken as input features and separately fed into the LSTM, DLinear and TimesNet sub-models to implement independent modeling and prediction for the trend component, total seasonal components and total residual components. During the model training phase, the SRA meta-heuristic optimization strategy is adopted to strengthen the global search ability of the Adam optimizer and reduce the prediction errors of DLinear and TimesNet sub-models via optimizing their output layer parameters. Finally, the PM 2.5 concentration prediction is obtained through additive reconstruction of the predicted results of each component. Experimental results show that the deep learning predictive framework proposed in this paper achieves favorable prediction accuracy and generalization performance for PM 2.5 , and it possesses certain application value in air pollution early warning and governance.

Article.Title: Structural diagnosis and evolution of urban resilience in dryland oasis urban agglomerations from an eco-immunological perspective
Article.Authors: Hou Y.; Hu Q.; Halik Ü.
Article.Abstract: Dryland oasis urban agglomerations face increasing drought risk, but gains in long-term adaptive capacity may not translate into stronger structural resilience because additive indices allow strong dimensions to offset weak ones. This study developed a partially non-compensatory four-dimensional super-trapezoid resilience model (TE4) integrating resistance, recovery, adaptive capacity, and institutional learning and preparedness, and applied it to ten city- and county-level units on the Northern Slope of the Tianshan Mountains during 2014–2024. The traditional composite index increased by 5.09% and adaptive capacity by 29.38% between the 2014 and 2024 endpoints, whereas the TE4 endpoint value in 2024 was 1.32% lower than that in 2014; however, its downward temporal trend was not statistically significant. Potential resilience rose by 9.28%, recovery capacity fell by 8.03%, and the unrealized resilience gap widened by 15.67%, indicating a modeled recovery-related conversion deficit. Removing NDVI-derived indicators barely altered TE4 rankings (Spearman’s ρ = 0.983). Panel models did not show short-term NPP buffering by higher TE4 under stronger drought, while pre-event recovery capacity showed the strongest positive but statistically inconclusive association with post-drought NPP recovery. TE4 is therefore a structural diagnostic tool for identifying capacity deficits and prioritizing recovery-oriented disaster risk reduction rather than a direct predictor of annual ecosystem productivity.

Article.Title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel 4,5-diaryl-1,2,3-thiadiazole derivatives: anticancer activity and molecular docking studies
Article.Authors: Ghasemi M.; Ghadbeigi S.; Ostad S.; Kalhor H.; Amini M.
Article.Abstract: Malignancies remain a major global health challenge. Microtubule-targeting agents (MTAs) have emerged as a significant therapeutic class, effectively suppressing cancer cell proliferation by interfering with the normal dynamics of microtubules. Combretastatin, particularly combretastatin A-4, is a natural compound with anti-angiogenic and anticancer properties that interacts with the colchicine-binding site at the α/β-tubulin interface. A new series of 4,5-diaryl-1,2,3-thiadiazole analogues, based on the SAR of combretastatin A-4, were designed and synthesized. The anticancer activity of the synthesized derivatives was assessed on human gastric adenocarcinoma (AGS), human colorectal adenocarcinoma (HT-29), human breast adenocarcinoma (MCF-7), and mouse embryo fibroblast (NIH3T3) cell lines by MTT assay, along with known drugs (paclitaxel and doxorubicin) as references. Among the synthesized compounds, compound 5g demonstrated the highest cytotoxic activity in most of the tested cell lines and exhibited superior cytotoxic effects against AGS and HT-29 cells compared with paclitaxel. Doxorubicin remained the most potent compound across all tested cell lines. Particularly, compounds 5d , 5f , and 5h exhibited high safety toward normal NIH-3T3 cells (IC₅₀ > 600 µM), with selective activity against some cancer cell lines. Docking studies showed that all compounds were predicted to bind within the colchicine-binding site of tubulin with more favorable predicted scores than combretastatin A-4. Molecular dynamics supported complex stability, with 5i showing greater stability than 5d . Compound 5g emerged as a promising potential tubulin inhibitor, requiring further experimental and in vivo validation.

Article.Authors: Azmal M.; Paul J.; Shohan M.; Haque A.; Mrinmoy M.; Talukder O.; Mishu M.; Mia M.; Ghosh A.
Article.Abstract: The global emergence of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) poses a major health challenge due to its resistance to carbapenem antibiotics, such as imipenem and meropenem, primarily mediated by β-lactamases, including NDM and KPC carbapenemases. Quercetin, eriodictyol, and luteolin showed favorable docking scores of − 9.1, − 8.32, and − 8.66 kcal/mol against KPC-2 and − 8.74, − 8.72, and − 8.73 kcal/mol against NDM-1, respectively. Molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate the conformational behavior of the quercetin–NDM-1 and quercetin–KPC-2 complexes. In vitro assays showed that quercetin, at 2 µg/µL, enhanced the antibacterial activity of carbapenems against a CRKP isolate carrying both bla NDM-1 and bla KPC-2. However, these assays did not directly assess β-lactamase inhibition. These findings support the preliminary potential of quercetin as a carbapenem adjuvant, while the mechanism underlying the observed potentiation requires biochemical confirmation.

Article.Title: Reservoir eutrophication prediction with explainable framework integrating temporal convolutional networks and bidirectional sequence modeling
Article.Authors: Sharafi M.; Behmanesh J.; Rezaverdinejad V.; Samadianfard S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of total nitrogen (TN) concentration in dam reservoirs is recognized as one of the significant challenges in water resources management. In this regard, the present study, to develop an intelligent and robust modeling framework, introduced the integrated model, which consists of the combination of the improved variational mode decomposition algorithm (IVMD), the attention mechanism-based temporal convolutional neural network (AttTCN), the bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU), and the grasshopper optimization algorithm (GOA), which is used to predict the total nitrogen of Mahabad Dam. The results of this study suggest that the proposed framework has a significant advantage over conventional models, as the analysis of the indices indicated that, with each layer of complexity added to the model, prediction accuracy improved significantly. The 80% reduction in the mean absolute error value from the basic BiGRU model to the final IVMD-GOA-AttTCN-BiGRU model, along with the improvement of Willmott’s index of agreement from 0.75 to 0.99, confirms the superiority of the proposed integrated approach. This significant improvement in accuracy demonstrated that the intelligent combination of data preprocessing, an attention mechanism, and hyperparameter optimization can yield models with greater reliability in water quality prediction. The use of interaction terms such as turbidity × pH corrected the systematic bias of the model, which is hydrologically justified. In summary, the proposed framework shows promise as an accurate prediction tool and provides a useful analytical basis for better understanding water quality dynamics in the Mahabad reservoir, subject to further validation with larger datasets.

Article.Title: Adipose tissue-derived stromal vascular fraction and xanthosine independently promote canine surgical wound healing
Article.Authors: Grewal N.; Sharma V.; Sharma P.; Sethi R.; Kumar A.; Nameirakpam U.; Sherley J.; Choudhary R.
Article.Abstract: Adipose tissue-derived stromal vascular fraction (SVF) and cultured stem cells have been applied in the treatment of wound healing and many other diseases of dogs. However, these cells are difficult to obtain in large amounts for therapy. Xanthosine (Xs) is a nucleoside that has been shown to increase stem cell numbers when used in vivo. This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of SVF along with xanthosine (Xs) on surgical wounds in dogs. Randomly, but age-matched, 24 dogs were allocated into four groups: a control group and three treatment groups (SVF, Xs, and SVF + Xs). The therapeutic effects of treatments on wound healing were assessed at days 7 and 14 by gross observation, photographs, and by measuring levels of angiogenic (VEGF) and inflammatory (TGFB1) markers. Results showed that SVF enhanced hair regrowth by day 7 and maintained its effects at day 14 (p ≤ 0.05). Compared to control, wound redness was visibly low in Xs, SVF, and SVF + Xs groups on day 7, and further reduced on day 14 (p ≤ 0.05) in the Xs group. VEGF expression peaked at day 7 in the SVF group (p ≤ 0.001), whereas the Xs group showed delayed elevation at day 14 (p ≤ 0.01). TGFB1 was mildly upregulated in SVF at day 14 (p ≤ 0.001) and strongly upregulated ( p < 0.001) in the Xs group. A combination of SVF and Xs demonstrated improved wound healing, maintaining a controlled range of TGFB1, which facilitates enhanced tissue regeneration. In conclusion, both SVF and Xs can independently promote wound healing. Furthermore, the combined SVF + Xs therapy was shown to modulate the surgical wound healing process in dogs.

Article.Title: A longitudinal study of perceived employability and psychological health among Chinese college students
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Liu B.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: The decline in psychological well-being among students in higher education has been increasingly documented. Despite growing recognition of perceived employability as consequential for employees’ well-being in the labor market, less is known regarding its specific association with psychological health among college students approaching the school-to-work transition. This study examined the association between perceived employability and psychological distress among Chinese college students and further explored the variation of this association by gender and family economic condition. Data were from three consecutive waves of the Panel Survey of Chinese University Students (PSCUS, 2020–2022), tracking 2552 students from their first to their third year. Fixed-effects models were employed to account for unobserved time-invariant characteristics. Interaction models were used to investigate how gender and family economic condition would shape the relationship between perceived employability and psychological distress. Results showed that higher perceived employability was significantly associated with lower psychological distress. Interaction models further indicated that the association was primarily driven by female and economically disadvantaged students. These findings highlight the need for policymakers to develop career-related programs that enhance students’ perceived employability as a vital means of promoting the psychological well‑being of college students, with particular attention to vulnerable socioeconomic and gender groups.

Article.Title: Integrative chemometric profiling of biochemical composition, fatty acids, minerals, organic acids, and carbohydrates in wild olive (Olea europaea L. subsp. oleaster) genotypes for quality-oriented selection
Article.Authors: Tunç Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the compositional diversity of wild olive ( Olea europaea L. subsp. oleaster ) genotypes through an integrated analysis of biochemical traits, fatty acid composition, mineral elements, organic acids, and carbohydrates, and to identify superior genotypes using chemometric approaches. A total of 150 genotypes collected from the Eastern Mediterranean region were analyzed, revealing significant genotypic variation across all evaluated traits ( p < 0.05). Wild olive genotypes exhibited striking biochemical diversity, with up to 2.4-fold variation in total phenolics, 20-fold variation in flavonoids, and substantial differences in fatty acid profiles (oleic acid: 55–83%). Genotype-specific differences in antioxidant capacity, tocopherol content, and primary metabolites were also observed. Multivariate analysis identified ‘Oleaster-39’, ‘Oleaster-133’, and ‘Oleaster-140’ as promising genotypes based on their favorable oil quality- and stability-related compositional profiles. Overall, the findings reveal extensive biochemical and metabolic diversity within wild olive germplasm and demonstrate the value of integrated compositional profiling and chemometric analysis for identifying promising genotypes with desirable quality attributes. However, the identified superior genotypes should be further validated across different environments, growing seasons, maturity stages, and clonal propagation trials before their large-scale utilization in breeding programs. The selected genotypes may serve as promising germplasm resources for future breeding and conservation efforts targeting improved oil quality, nutritional value, and functional properties, pending further genetic and multi-environment validation.

Article.Title: A multifunctional Tb3+–salicylic acid hydrazide phosphor for anti-counterfeiting, forensic fingerprint visualization, and biological applications
Article.Authors: Nasser H.; Abdelrhman E.; Saif M.; Kamal R.; Shebl M.; Fouad R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A novel terbium(III) complex, Tb(SAH) , derived from salicylic acid hydrazide ( SAH ), was successfully synthesized and fully characterized. Stoichiometric analysis confirmed a 1:2 metal-to-ligand ratio. X-ray diffraction and microscopic studies revealed a polycrystalline structure with micro- and nanodomain features. Photoluminescence investigations demonstrated intense monochromatic emissions: blue for SAH and green for Tb(SAH) , with relatively long excited-state lifetimes in dimethylformamide (DMF), solid state, and polymeric matrices (PVA (polyvinyl alcohol), PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate), and silica xerogel). An efficient ligand-to-metal energy transfer mechanism under ultraviolet (UV) excitation was confirmed, indicating a strong antenna effect responsible for enhanced luminescence. Both SAH and Tb(SAH) were successfully applied in latent fingerprint visualization, clearly resolving level I–III ridge details on diverse porous, non-porous, and multicolored substrates. Additionally, transparent luminescent security inks prepared from the compounds exhibited excellent storage stability and humidity resistance, highlighting their suitability for anti-counterfeiting applications. Biological evaluation revealed that Tb(SAH) exhibits significantly greater in vitro cytotoxicity against the hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG-2) cell line than the free ligand. Significant antioxidant activity was observed for SAH and Tb(SAH) (IC 50 = 0.38 and 0.78 μM, respectively), surpassing ascorbic acid. The Tb(SAH) complex also exhibited improved antidiabetic activity (IC 50 = 14 μg/mL) compared with SAH (IC 50 = 44 μg/mL), with potency comparable to that of acarbose (IC 50 = 35 μg/mL). Antimicrobial studies indicated marked enhancement upon Tb 3 ⁺ coordination, particularly against Staphylococcus aureus . Molecular docking against DNA gyrase B (PDB ID: 6TCK) supported strong binding interactions, corroborating the experimental antimicrobial findings.

Article.Title: Hybrid rank fusion of a group-token transformer with gradient boosting improves detection of evasive and novel-family malware
Article.Authors: Tawfik M.; Al-sellami B.; Heshmat M.; Fathi I.; Shaban W.
Article.Abstract: Static machine-learning malware detectors report near-perfect closed-set accuracy, but the malware that matters operationally is the malware that slips past detection and the malware that belongs to families never seen in training. We study both on three longitudinal benchmarks: EMBER2024 (3.2 M Windows, .NET, APK, ELF and PDF files, 52 training weeks and 12 test weeks, plus a challenge set of 6,315 files that evaded every antivirus engine at first sight), LAMDA (1.0 M Android applications, 2013–2025, with an IID/NEAR/FAR drift protocol) and BODMAS (134 K PE files, 2019–2020, monthly evaluation). We make five contributions. First, an operational evaluation protocol: true-positive rate at 1% and 0.1% false-positive rate, challenge-set detection at fixed FPR, novel-family, singleton and low-consensus strata, week-by-week and year-by-year drift, thresholds calibrated on time-aware validation data, and paired-bootstrap confidence intervals. Second, three new deep architectures for static feature vectors, trained jointly across formats: GT-Former, a Group-Token Transformer over the semantic feature groups, whose hyper-parameters are tuned with Optuna on a time-aware validation window and which is evaluated with five seeds on every benchmark; FR-MoE, a format-routed mixture of experts; and ProtoCon-Net, a prototype classifier with family-aware supervised-contrastive training. Third, three metadata-driven objectives that use antivirus consensus and family labels at training time only (a consensus-aware margin loss, a consensus-regression head and a family-adversarial gradient-reversal head), with full ablations. Fourth, explainability with SHAP and CLS attention. Fifth, benchmark-hygiene findings, including that the public EMBER2024 release lists every record twice. The results are sobering and useful: the EMBER2024 LightGBM benchmark remains the strongest single model at strict operating points (Win32: 90.0% TPR at 0.1% FPR versus \(88.1 \pm 0.4\) % for the tuned GT-Former over five seeds), and the metadata-driven objectives do not pay for themselves: on LAMDA, with five seeds per variant, no objective activated on its own is distinguishable from the plain model, and only their combination degrades the strictest operating point (NEAR TPR at 0.1% FPR falls from \(10.1 \pm 2.3\) % to \(4.4 \pm 3.7\) %). The seed spread on this benchmark is large enough that single-seed ablations are unreliable, which we regard as a methodological finding in itself. The deep models are nevertheless complementary to gradient boosting: a rank average of the tuned GT-Former and LightGBM raises Win32 challenge-set detection from 63.2% to 68.8% at 1% FPR (95% CI \(+4.7\) to \(+6.6\) points), novel-family detection from 89.1% to 91.8% (CI \(+1.5\) to \(+3.9\) ) and test TPR at 1% FPR from 96.8% to 97.3%, with significant challenge-set gains also on .NET ( \(+1.6\) ) and APK ( \(+3.9\) ); on LAMDA a rank average of an MLP and LightGBM raises far-future (2018–2025) detection from 40.5% to 54.4% at 1% FPR (CI \(+13.7\) to \(+14.0\) ) and singleton-family detection from 34.6% to 53.3% when the threshold is calibrated on the benign files of the test region ; under a threshold fixed on validation data and applied unchanged, twelve years of drift move both models far below their nominal budget and the advantage falls to 0.1 points (Section Retrospective and deployment operating points), which we regard as the honest deployment figure; and on BODMAS the tuned GT-Former/LightGBM fusion matches LightGBM at 1% FPR (99.85%) and improves detection at 0.1% FPR (98.9% to 99.5%) and novel-family detection at 0.1% FPR (94.7% to 97.1%). SHAP shows why the benchmark misses evasive files: its strongest evidence is structural sloppiness (suspicious section flags, missing signatures), and evasive malware is exactly the malware that avoids it. Code, de-duplication masks, models and all score files are released.

Article.Title: Effects of a hand sanitizer formulation on upper respiratory symptoms and work restrictions: a double-blind household cluster-randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Yamanaka N.; Mizukoshi K.; Asaoka K.; Morikawa T.; Nakashima Y.; Hayase A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Conventional hand sanitizers provide immediate but short-lived bactericidal and virucidal effects, necessitating their frequent use to reduce contact transmission. This double-blind, parallel-group, cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluated the effect of repeated use of the study formulation. Healthy employees and their cohabiting family members (clusters) were assigned to use either the study formulation or a commercially available 79.7% ethanol-based sanitizer 5–10 times daily for 72 days (December 2023–February 2024). The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of upper respiratory symptoms, defined as fever ≥ 37.8 °C with cough, sore throat, and/or nasal discharge. Among the 568 participants (study-formulation group, 285; ethanol-based sanitizer group, 283) across 417 clusters, upper respiratory symptoms occurred in 35 and 58 participants, respectively. The study-formulation group showed significantly lower risk (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.37–0.89, P = 0.013; approximately 40% lower cumulative incidence), with fewer illness-related work restrictions. Adverse events were infrequent and unrelated to the study interventions. Repeated use of the study formulation was well tolerated and associated with fewer upper respiratory symptoms and work restrictions than ethanol-based sanitizers.

Article.Title: Biomechanical comparison of stand-alone interbody bone grafting versus cage implantation in ULIF: a finite element analysis
Article.Authors: Xu C.; Wu Y.; Tang J.
Article.Abstract: The biomechanical differences between stand-alone interbody bone grafting and cage implantation in unilateral biportal endoscopic lumbar interbody fusion (ULIF) remain unclear. This study compared the two strategies in a patient-specific finite element model and assessed model credibility using geometric reconstruction, published range-of-motion (ROM) data, and mesh convergence analysis. A subject-specific L4-L5 finite element model with residual Grade I spondylolisthesis was used to compare bilateral pedicle-screw fixation with stand-alone interbody impaction bone grafting versus porous titanium cage implantation. A 500-N axial preload and a 7.5-N m pure moment were applied independently in six directions. Segmental ROM, model-reported stiffness, and von Mises stresses in the interbody constructs, screw-rod system, and endplates were evaluated. ROM was calculated from the relative rotation of L4 with respect to L5. In addition to comparison with published cadaveric ROM, five characteristic mesh sizes (4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 2.5, and 2.0 mm) were assessed under identical model settings. Cage implantation reduced ROM by 30.4%-37.3% across the six loading directions and produced higher model-reported stiffness than stand-alone bone grafting. The cage model also generated higher localized stresses in the interbody construct and screw-rod system; during right lateral bending, screw and rod stresses increased by 556.6% and 361.2%, respectively. Endplate effects were direction- and level-dependent, including a 326.7% increase at the L4 inferior endplate during right lateral bending. In the mesh study, the monitored von Mises stresses for 4.0-, 3.5-, 3.0-, 2.5-, and 2.0-mm meshes were 6.820, 11.499, 9.849, 9.865, and 9.840 MPa, respectively; the maximum pairwise difference among meshes of 3.0 mm or finer was 0.25%. Within the prescribed loading, material, contact, and mesh assumptions of this single patient-specific model, cage implantation provided greater immediate segmental restraint but generated a less favorable localized stress environment in selected implant and endplate regions. Stand-alone bone grafting produced greater motion but a more diffuse load-transfer pattern. The mesh convergence results support numerical stability of the reported stress solution but do not constitute independent biological validation. These computational findings are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as proof of clinical superiority, long-term safety, or a direct basis for patient selection.

Article.Title: Research on the mechanical properties of loess solidified via enzyme induced calcium carbonate precipitation (EICP)
Article.Authors: Chen S.; Liu J.; Li G.; Chen C.
Article.Abstract: Loess has a special structure that usually leads to collapse, disintegration and dissolution, and easily triggers slope instability, foundation settlement, and ground fissure. As a recently developed soil stabilization method, high efficiency is widely recognized as a fundamental characteristic of Enzyme-induced calcium carbonate precipitation (EICP). Cost-effectiveness and environmental friendliness render it a proper method for fine-grained soil solidification. Based on the orthogonal test method, the role of enzyme concentration within the generalization processes was assessed via specifically designed enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (EICP) tests. The experiments mandated precise regulation of cementing solution and skim milk powder concentrations, pH value, standing time on the CaCO 3 content, and determining the optimal mineralization condition. Furthermore, to quantify the mechanical performance, the unconfined compressive strength (UCS) tests were conducted to considering the effect of dry density ( ρ d ), cementing solution content (CSC), enzyme to cementation solution ratio (ECSR), and Na-Mt content ( C N ). The test results indicated that the optimal EICP mineralization condition was that the soybean powder concentration was 200 g/L, cementing solution concentration was 1.50 mol/L, skimmed milk powder concentration was 2 g/L, pH was 7, and standing time was 120 h. For the EICP treated loess, the stress-strain curve is divisible into a slow ascending stage, a fast-growing stage, a slow growth stage, and an attenuation decrease stage. A maximum UCS was achieved at the dry density of 1.55 g/cm 3 with 4% Na-Mt content, following a trend of increasing strength concurrent with rises in both initial dry density and Na-Mt concentration. The UCS exhibited the trend of increased firstly and decreased subsequently with the increase of CSC and decreasing of ECSR, it reaches the maximum when the CSC was 14% and the ECSR was 2:3. The research results can promote the practical implementation of EICP method in foundation treatment.
