Article.Title: p300 exacerbates lung injury following cardiopulmonary bypass in AnxA1-deficient rats
Article.Authors: Han M.; Zhang H.; Zhou Y.; Dou X.; Zhuang Y.; Chen S.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) following cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is one of the most common postoperative complications, significantly impairing postoperative recovery and, in severe cases, endangering patient survival. CPB-induced ALI is predominantly associated with systemic inflammatory responses, although multiple factors contribute to this inflammation. Annexin A1 (AnxA1), a potent anti-inflammatory protein, is widely expressed in various organs and has been shown to mitigate lung injury by suppressing inflammatory responses in ALI. In contrast, p300, a histone acetyltransferase, promotes inflammation by enhancing the expression of pro-inflammatory mediators in ALI. These opposing roles suggest a critical regulatory interplay between AnxA1 and p300 in modulating pulmonary inflammation. This study establishes a clinically relevant cardiopulmonary bypass combined left lung ischemia-reperfusion (CPB-I/R) acute lung injury (ALI) rat model, distinct from widely used LPS-induced ALI models, to dissect the interactive regulatory relationship between AnxA1 and p300 in perioperative lung injury for the first time. CPB triggers systemic inflammatory priming, while unilateral left lung ischemia-reperfusion imposes localized pulmonary endothelial damage; the two insults together produce synergistic severe lung injury, which closely mimics clinical cardiac surgery-related perioperative lung dysfunction. In this study, we established CPB-induced ALI models in both wild-type (WT) and AnxA1-knockout rats. We observed upregulated p300 expression and exacerbated inflammatory responses in AnxA1-knockout rats compared to WT controls. Furthermore, co-expression and potential protein complex formation between AnxA1 and p300 were detected in WT animals; however, the current co-immunoprecipitation assay lacks critical IgG negative controls and reciprocal pull-down validation, limiting definitive confirmation of specific bidirectional protein binding.Notably, pharmacological inhibition of p300 with C646 partially alleviated lung injury in the CPB-induced ALI model. Intriguingly, C646 treatment reduced total p300 protein abundance in lung tissue despite functioning as a catalytic activity inhibitor, which we further interpret via potential transcriptional feedback and protein stability mechanisms. Our findings provide novel mechanistic insights into the pathogenesis of CPB-related ALI and highlight the AnxA1-p300 axis as a promising potential therapeutic target, offering a theoretical foundation for future clinical interventions.

Article.Title: Bacillus velezensis UTB96 mitigates saffron fusarium corm rot and promotes plant growth and phytochemical quality
Article.Authors: Kolahderazi N.; Hosseini S.; Ahmadzadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Saffron corm rot, predominantly associated with Fusarium species, is a major constraint to saffron production and may adversely affect both yield and spice quality. In this study, the causal agents of saffron corm rot were isolated from diseased corms collected in Iran, and identified based on morphological characteristics and pathogenicity tests. Three pathogenic isolates were characterized as Fusarium oxysporum , F. solani , and F. culmorum . The biocontrol potential of Bacillus velezensis strain UTB96 was subsequently evaluated through dual-culture and volatile organic compound assays, greenhouse experiments, and a field trial. Under in vitro conditions, UTB96 significantly inhibited the mycelial growth of all three Fusarium isolates, with the greatest inhibition in the dual-culture assay observed against F. solani (68.35%). Volatile compounds produced by UTB96 also suppressed fungal growth, with inhibition rates of 59.28, 66.00, and 73.00% against F. oxysporum , F. culmorum , and F. solani , respectively. In planta experiments, corm treatment with UTB96 significantly reduced disease severity caused by all three pathogens compared with infected controls, with the highest reduction recorded against F. solani (70.74%). In addition, UTB96 significantly enhanced leaf length, leaf number, sprouts number, root length, and corm number, whereas daughter-corm weight was not significantly affected. Field application of UTB96 improved important yield-related traits, including stigma length, stigma weight, and flower weight. Moreover, according to ISO3632-based measurements, the treatment significantly increased crocin and picrocrocin contents at P < 0.01 and safranal content at P < 0.05. Correlation analysis revealed strong positive associations between agronomic traits and crocin and picrocrocin, while safranal was significantly correlated with the other quality indices but not with the measured yield traits. Overall, B. velezensis strain UTB96 demonstrated substantial antifungal, disease-suppressive, and plant growth-promoting activities, highlighting its promise as a multifunctional bioinoculant for sustainable saffron production.

Article.Title: Secretome-dependent antimicrobial and immunomodulatory activity of Lactobacillus johnsonii against multidrug-resistant Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli
Article.Authors: Vasamsetti S.; Ligory M.; Khaderbad Y.; Gupta A.; Morampudi V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) is a leading cause of persistent diarrhea in children in low- and middle-income countries, and the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains necessitates non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies. This study evaluated Lactobacillus johnsonii , previously characterized by our group, as a probiotic candidate against a clinically confirmed MDR EAEC isolate resistant to ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, azithromycin, amoxicillin, and gentamicin. Probiotic properties of L. johnsonii were assessed through gastrointestinal stress tolerance, cell surface hydrophobicity, phenol tolerance, and autoaggregation assays. Antimicrobial and anti-biofilm activity against MDR EAEC were evaluated using agar overlay and crystal violet biofilm assays. Epithelial interaction was assessed through adherence and protection assays on HCT-116 intestinal epithelial cells. Gas production suppression, macrophage nitric oxide modulation in RAW 264.7 cells, and nutrient competition were examined as mechanistic endpoints. The L. johnsonii cell-free supernatant was fractionated by fast protein liquid chromatography (FPLC) and active fractions confirmed by Gram staining. Statistical analyses were performed using unpaired Student’s t-test, one-way ANOVA, or two-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple comparisons test. L. johnsonii demonstrated robust gastrointestinal resilience, high cell surface hydrophobicity, and rapid autoaggregation reaching 80.4 ± 2.3% by 4 h, collectively supporting mucosal colonization potential. It produced zones of inhibition against MDR EAEC substantially exceeding those of gentamicin, reduced viable biofilm-associated EAEC by over 80%, and displaced pre-adhered EAEC from intestinal epithelial cells in a time-dependent manner requiring prior epithelial establishment. L. johnsonii attenuated EAEC-induced gas production and reduced macrophage nitric oxide levels by 67.7%. Inhibition was predominantly secretome-dependent, as nutrient competition did not contribute to pathogen suppression. FPLC fractionation identified fractions S5 and S6 as the principal bioactive components with sustained bactericidal activity at 6 h, with S6 exhibiting greater killing potency than S5. L. johnsonii exhibited potent secretome-dependent antimicrobial activity against MDR EAEC in vitro and significantly suppressed macrophage nitric oxide production, indicating its potential to modulate inflammatory responses. These findings support its potential as a non-antibiotic biotherapeutic strategy for antibiotic-resistant enteric infections. However, further in vivo validation and molecular characterization of the active antimicrobial components are required before clinical translation.

Article.Title: Data-driven optimization and multiscale characterization of sustainable epoxy-benzoxazine hybrid composites for high-performance structural applications
Article.Authors: Vinod B.; Ebenezer N.; Venkataramana P.; Mohammed Z.; Bellary S.; Tamboli S.
Article.Abstract: The polymer composites with enhanced mechanical, thermal, and tribological properties are increasingly important for advanced structural applications. In this study, hybrid composites based on an epoxy-benzoxazine matrix reinforced with basalt fibers (BF), waste cotton textile fibers (WCTF), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) were developed. Optimization of BF content, WCTF content, GNP loading, and curing temperature for tensile strength, flexural strength, impact strength, and Shore D was performed using a Taguchi L9 experimental design. The optimized composite (30% BF, 10% WCTF, 1% GNPs, and a curing temperature of 160 °C) achieved a tensile strength of 138 MPa, flexural strength of 208 MPa, impact strength of 42 kJ m⁻², and Shore D hardness of 87. In addition, the optimized composite exhibited a storage modulus of 5.2 GPa and a glass transition temperature (Tg) of 132 °C. FTIR, AFM, FESEM with EDS, DMA, DSC, TGA, and wear analyses supported enhanced matrix-reinforcement interactions, improved interfacial adhesion, and favorable thermomechanical and tribological performance. Random Forest and XGBoost machine learning models were created for predicting the composite properties, and XGBoost yielded the highest prediction accuracy (R² = 0.9870–0.993). The proposed experimental, statistical, and machine learning strategy is effective for the design of high-performance epoxy–benzoxazine hybrid composites for applications in structural engineering.

Article.Title: Fixed-qubit CVaR-VQE and quantum-inspired QUBO sampling for static and dynamic restricted vertex multicut in telecom resilience
Article.Authors: Abbassi A.; Dujardin Y.; Gourdin E.; Lacomme P.; Prodhon C.
Article.Abstract: A central question in hybrid quantum–classical optimization is how to assign the classical and quantum components according to the structure of the problem, rather than attempting to transfer the full optimization model to a quantum device. We investigate this question on static and finite-horizon dynamic restricted vertex minimum multicut, an NP-hard network-isolation problem with exponentially many path constraints. A classical row-generation layer handles graph separation, feasibility verification, and constraint generation, while quantum or quantum-inspired samplers are used only for the current restricted optimization problem. We develop two such algorithms: an exact-slack QUBO formulation sampled by simulated annealing, and a fixed-register CVaR-VQE formulation in which generated constraints modify a classical loss without enlarging the static quantum register. Exact MILP row generation provides the certifying reference. Experiments on SNDlib-derived telecom instances show that both approaches can be integrated consistently within this workflow, while classical-sampler controls do not establish a quantum-specific performance advantage. The dynamic study further shows how temporal coupling creates a distinct resource bottleneck, motivating decomposed formulations for larger horizons.

Article.Title: Longitudinal proxy pack benchmark generation for remaining useful life assessment of light electric vehicle battery packs in swapping systems
Article.Authors: Zhu L.; Zheng W.; Zhang F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Battery swapping enables rapid energy replenishment for light electric vehicles (LEVs), but high-turnover pack circulation requires reliable pack-level health and remaining useful life ( RUL ) assessment. Publicly reusable longitudinal ageing datasets for complete LEV packs remain scarce. We develop a proxy-pack data-generation and learning framework that organizes independently tested cell-ageing records into fixed-member trajectories representing a 48 V-class 16-series configuration. Each trajectory retains 16 physical-cell identities over their common-cycle sequence. Cycle-level member states are aggregated into pack features for predicting a conservative minimum-member proxy RUL, with test barcodes isolated before combinatorial augmentation. Across ten barcode-level splits in each of three source cohorts, same-source tests with endpoints within the augmented training lifetime range achieved a median R² of 0.909 and a median Spearman correlation of 0.997. Tests beyond this range retained strong degradation ordering but showed larger absolute errors. A secondary mixed-source audit of 80 held-out trajectories achieved a median R² of 0.714 and a median Spearman correlation of 0.992. A matched composition-control analysis yielded a median R² by change of -0.015 after balancing barcode reuse and limiting composition overlap, indicating limited sensitivity to training-composition sampling. A complementary physical audit using one fixed 12S3P pack confirmed cell-to-branch-to-pack electrical closure and revealed persistent voltage limitation and migration of the maximum-temperature location. Proxy-pack generation therefore provides a reproducible approach for constructing longitudinal member-aware benchmarks from cell-ageing records and evaluating pack-health and RUL models across varied compositions and lifetime conditions.

Article.Title: Multi-year dynamics of soil quality and sorghum yield under conservation tillage in Northern Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Kebede M.
Article.Abstract: Global dry land agricultural systems face intensifying structural and climatic pressures, demanding innovative soil management paradigms to sustain crop productivity and preserve scarce hydrological and nutritional resources. Conventional tillage (CT) practices, characterized by intensive mechanical soil inversion, accelerate the oxidation of soil organic matter, disrupt macro-pore continuity, and generate high subsoil bulk density that limits water permeability and exacerbates terminal drought vulnerability. To address these systemic challenges, A five-year field study (2016–2020) was conducted at the Shire-May-Tsebri Agricultural Research Center in northern Ethiopia to assess the long-term impact of five tillage systems Zero Tillage (ZT), Mulch Tillage (MT), Reduced Tillage (RT), Strip Tillage (ST), and Conventional Tillage (CT) on topsoil properties and sorghum productivity. While the 2016 baseline season exhibited uniform initial soil parameters, progressive multi-year divergence established distinct structural equilibria over time. By 2020, continuous conservation management led to highly significant modifications in topsoil infrastructure ( P < 0.001). MT and ST maximized soil organic carbon accumulation to 2.34% and 1.89%, respectively, and drastically reduced bulk density down to 0.23 g/cm 3 and 0.42 g/cm 3 compared to the relatively higher BD under CT (0.89 g/cm 3 ). Two-way split-plot ANOVA confirmed that ST significantly preserved late-season soil profile moisture during terminal post-monsoonal drying phases, retaining a substantial hydrological reserve of 38.98% by November 2020. Agronomical, intensive mechanical inversion under CT optimized initial stand counts and functional heads but compromised the root microenvironment. Conversely, ST effectively bypassed early crop establishment barriers, achieving a stable intermediate plant population and unlocking an overwhelming 63.13% grain yield improvement over CT by the final 2020 season (51.99 kg/ha vs. 31.87 kg/ha). Pearson correlation analysis confirmed that final grain yield was profoundly coupled with late-season moisture retention ( r = 0.79) and organic carbon buildup ( r = 0.74). Ultimately, continuous Strip Tillage progressively rehabilitates dryland soil infrastructure, steadily elevating terminal water-use efficiency and providing a resilient climate-adaptation paradigm for dryland agricultural systems.

Article.Title: Measurement and calibration method of dynamic stress in rock mass based on PDV technology
Article.Authors: Shi Y.; Xing Y.; Huang X.; Li Z.; Jiao X.; Ba Z.; Song S.; Zhang L.; Zhang G.
Article.Abstract: To address the challenge of measuring the dynamic stress of engineering rock mass structures under blast loading, a rock mass dynamic stress measurement and calibration method based on Photonic Doppler Velocimetry (PDV) was developed. Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) loading tests were conducted under different wave impedance and coupling conditions to investigate the stress wave transmission effect and to verify the accuracy of the proposed measurement method. The experimental results show that the SHPB-based calibration method for the rock mass dynamic stress measurement system is accurate and reliable. Under the conditions of identical wave impedance and coupling fixation with a thin adhesive layer, the feasibility of the PDV-based dynamic stress measurement method for engineering rock masses is preliminarily verified, providing a feasible technical approach for measuring dynamic response parameters such as stress and strain of structures under blast loading.

Article.Title: Regional nerve blocks are associated with greater early analgesia for femoral neck fractures in the emergency department
Article.Authors: Uysal Ş.; Akçay G.; Sönmez B.; Çevik H.; Akkaya Ö.; Güner N.; Şirin İ.
Article.Abstract: Femoral neck fractures are highly painful emergency department (ED) presentations, particularly among older adults, and early analgesia is essential for imaging, positioning, and surgical preparation. This prospective, comparative, non-randomized ED study compared intravenous (IV) paracetamol, IV tramadol, ultrasound-guided femoral nerve block (FNB), and ultrasound-guided pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block in adults with isolated femoral fractures, particularly femoral neck fractures. The primary outcome was maximum pain reduction during the 240-minute follow-up. Because baseline pain scores differed between groups, maximum pain reduction was compared using analysis of covariance adjusted for age, fracture type, and baseline pain score. Among 125 patients, 113 (90.4%) had femoral neck fractures. Among 125 patients, 113 (90.4%) had femoral neck fractures. Ultrasound-guided regional blocks were associated with faster and greater pain reduction than systemic analgesics across visual analog, numeric rating, and facial pain scales. The largest early reductions occurred within the first 15 min after the FNB and PENG block. Effect sizes for maximum pain reduction were large on both the visual analog and numeric rating scales. Rescue analgesia was rarely required after regional blocks, whereas adverse events occurred mainly in the opioid group. These findings suggest that ultrasound-guided regional blocks may provide effective early analgesia in similar ED fracture analgesia settings where trained clinicians are available.

Article.Title: Selection signatures in Apis mellifera jemenitica suggest candidate genes potentially involved in energy metabolism, proteostasis, reproduction, and cellular regulation
Article.Authors: Hedayat N.; Khalkhali-Evrigh R.; Seyedsharifi R.; Khanzadeh H.; Pourasad K.; Tanveer H.
Article.Abstract: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) help pollinate plants, support biodiversity, and make a significant contribution to food production. Among their subspecies, A. m. jemenitica (JEM) inhabits desert and semi-desert regions, representing a valuable model for understanding genomic adaptation to extreme environmental conditions. We performed a comparative whole-genome resequencing analysis between JEM and A. m. mellifera (MEL) to identify genetic variants and selection signatures underlying adaptation to arid environments. A total of more than 2.9 million single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were identified and analyzed for population structure, linkage disequilibrium (LD), and genome-wide scans for selection signals using FST, XP-EHH, and π-ratio approaches. Population analyses revealed distinct clustering patterns and clear genetic differentiation between JEM and MEL, accompanied by faster LD decay in JEM, which is consistent with the larger effective population size in JEM (Ne = 2523) compared to MEL (Ne = 952). Through the combined selection scans, we identified 222 overlapping candidate genes that appear to be under positive selection. Many of these genes are involved in diverse biological processes, including energy metabolism, cellular regulation, protein homeostasis, stress response, genome maintenance, and cellular communication, with several having documented roles in heat tolerance, oxidative stress response, circadian regulation, and reproduction. Notable examples include LpR , inositol monophosphatase 1 , AcCoAS , enolase , BAG6 , alpha-Man-Ia , JHE , nocte , CRH-BP , and Est-6 , highlighting potential roles in osmotic and thermal stress tolerance, energy hemostasis, protein quality control, circadian regulation, and reproductive biology. These findings enhance our understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying environmental adaptation in honey bees. Nevertheless, further multi-omics investigations, including transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, as well as functional assays are needed to validate the adaptive relevance of the candidate genes and pathways identified in this study.

Article.Title: Associations of physical function and multimorbidity with cognitive impairment in community-dwelling Chinese octogenarians
Article.Authors: Bian S.; Tong C.; Meng F.; Tian X.; Luo X.; Zhou X.; Wang P.; Gao Q.
Article.Abstract: China’s rapidly aging population has intensified concerns about cognitive impairment and chronic disease burdens among older adults. Despite this, research on the interplay between physical function, multimorbidity, and their associations with cognitive impairment in community-dwelling octogenarians remains limited. This study investigates the associations between physical function, chronic disease prevalence, and cognitive impairment among home-dwelling adults aged ≥ 80 years in China, with a focus on demographic and clinical predictors of cognitive decline. A cross-sectional analysis of 13,027 octogenarians assessed physical function using the Barthel Index (BI) and cognitive status via the Mini-Cog. Logistic regression models evaluated the impact of demographic factors (age, gender, occupation), chronic diseases (hypertension, stroke), and psychosocial factors (aggression, depression) on cognitive impairment severity. Of the participants, 37.88% exhibited high functional independence (BI = 100). Cognitive impairment was significantly influenced by age, gender, and multimorbidity ( p < 0.01). Depression (OR 11.335; 95% CI 8.853–14.514) and aggression (OR 1.93; 95% CI 1.161–3.217) were strongly associated with cognitive impairment severity. Hypertension was moderately correlated with mild cognitive impairment (OR 1.495; 95% CI 1.285–1.739), while stroke tripled the odds of mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment (OR 3.301; 95% CI 2.131–5.113). Reduced self-care ability was associated with nearly fourfold higher odds of cognitive impairment ( p < 0.01). Age, occupation, and lifestyle factors synergistically are associated with chronic disease burden and cognitive impairment in China’s oldest-old population. These findings underscore the urgency of personalized healthcare strategies to preserve independence and mitigate cognitive decline in high-risk octogenarians.

Article.Title: Association of PROMIS Profile-29 based quality of life with heart failure in asymptomatic patients (HERZCHECK)
Article.Authors: Nolden A.; Thiede G.; Beyer R.; Müller M.; Wieditz J.; Kentenich H.; Graja D.; Sehlen S.; Steen H.; Remppis B.; Huppertz A.; Landmesser U.; Falk V.; Frey N.; Stock S.; Fischer F.; Friede T.; Kelle S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heart failure is often diagnosed only when symptoms become acute, but early detection could help prevent disease progression. As patient-reported quality of life is strongly associated with heart failure outcomes, it may also serve as an additional correlate with the disease before symptoms occur. This cross-sectional study investigates the associations of quality of life and asymptomatic heart failure and was conducted as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis. It was based on data of 4,509 asymptomatic patients aged 40 to 69 years with at least one cardiovascular risk factor and without known heart failure at the time of quality of life assessment, whose heart failure status was determined during the baseline evaluation. The quality of life of patients with and without asymptomatic heart failure was compared, using logistic regression. Lower Physical Function was associated with higher odds of asymptomatic heart failure in females generally. Among females with hypercholesterolemia, lower physical function and lower pain interference were associated with asymptomatic heart failure, while in females who smoke, lower physical function was associated with asymptomatic heart failure. In males generally, lower Pain Interference and higher Pain Intensity were associated with higher odds of pre-HF, with additional associations of lower Pain Interference in males with diabetes, higher Depression and higher Pain Intensity in males with hypercholesterolemia, and lower Pain Interference and higher Pain Intensity in males who smoke. This study highlights the association between patient-reported physical health domains and asymptomatic heart failure. The findings provide hypothesis-generating insights into the relationship between quality of life and asymptomatic heart failure and highlight the need for longitudinal research.

Article.Title: Domain adaptation affects adversarial robustness in autonomous steering models
Article.Authors: Mehraban Z.; Glaser S.; Milford M.; Schroeter R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Domain adaptation is commonly used to transfer autonomous steering models across regions with different road configurations, such as from right-hand to left-hand traffic. While prior work has largely evaluated adaptation using clean target-domain steering accuracy, its effect on adversarial robustness remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluates two steering architectures, PilotNet and ResNet-18, under four adaptation strategies: U.S.-trained, flipped U.S.-trained, U.S.-trained + fine-tuned, and flipped U.S.-trained + fine-tuned. Robustness is assessed under FGSM and PGD attacks across multiple perturbation levels using normalized robustness scores and absolute steering-error metrics. Results show that domain adaptation improves clean target-domain accuracy but affects adversarial robustness in a metric-dependent manner. Fine-tuned models often show degraded normalized adversarial robustness, especially after flipped pretraining, indicating larger relative sensitivity to adversarial perturbations compared with their clean baselines. However, absolute adversarial errors show that fine-tuned models are not always worse than pretrained baselines under attack. These results show that, after domain adaptation, clean accuracy and normalized robustness can diverge, and RS may rank robustness differently from absolute steering-error metrics when clean baselines differ. The contribution of this study is to show that metric choice materially affects robustness conclusions for domain-adapted steering models; therefore, RS remains useful for measuring relative degradation, but should be interpreted alongside absolute steering-error metrics and statistical uncertainty.

Article.Title: Two-stage classification of glioma subtypes using a hybrid CNN-ViT model
Article.Authors: Aboelenin S.; Eltoukhy M.; Mohammed M.; Hosny K.
Article.Abstract: Gliomas are among the most serious brain tumor types due to their aggressive behavior. Recent advances in automated methods for early brain tumor detection that analyze whole-slide images of brain tissue enable rapid and precise diagnosis. Therefore, we propose a hybrid approach combining a convolutional neural network and a vision transformer for deep analysis of whole-slide patches. This hybrid model employs a two-stage classification strategy to address highly imbalanced class distributions. The first stage uses a binary-label classifier to label patches as either normal or abnormal. The second stage employs a multi-label classifier to classify abnormal patches into their corresponding glioma subtypes. We evaluated the two-stage hybrid model on an imbalanced test set, achieving the highest balanced accuracy (95.31%), macro-averaged precision (96.08%), and macro-averaged F1-score (95.51%). The two-stage classification approach addressed class imbalance. Furthermore, the hybrid model, which combines a convolutional neural network and a vision transformer, captured deeper features, achieving superior performance and outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

Article.Title: 4-Methoxydalbergione triggers ferroptosis in bladder cancer by suppressing the AKT/mTOR/GPX4 axis
Article.Authors: Li R.; Luo T.; Tao T.; Li X.; Zhou H.; Su T.; Xu C.; Xia L.; Du H.
Article.Abstract: Due to its high recurrence and pronounced metastatic potential, bladder cancer (BC) remains a significant and persistent clinical challenge. Here, we investigate the anti-tumour effects of 4-Methoxydalbergione (4MOD), a naturally occurring flavonoid obtained from Dalbergia sissoo Roxb. In T24 human and MBT2 mouse BC cell lines, 4MOD dose-dependently suppressed proliferation, migration, and invasion; colony formation was additionally suppressed in T24 cells. These effects were associated with a reversal of the epithelial- mesenchymal transition (EMT) process, as evidenced by elevated E‑cadherin and reduced N‑cadherin and vimentin expression. Moreover, 4MOD induced both apoptotic cell death and ferroptosis. The induction of ferroptosis was evidenced by mitochondrial shrinkage, accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and the decreased levels of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4). Caspase and ferroptosis inhibition experiments demonstrated that ferroptosis is the predominant driver of 4MOD‑induced cell death. Mechanistically, 4MOD inhibited AKT and mTOR signaling, as shown by reduced p‑AKT and p‑mTOR levels. Ferroptosis‑specific rescue with Ferrostatin‑1 (Fer‑1) and functional rescue with the AKT activator SC79 indicated that AKT/mTOR inhibition is causally linked to GPX4 downregulation and ferroptosis induction. In a BALB/c‑nu mouse xenograft model, 4MOD markedly suppressed tumour growth without causing significant body weight loss or histopathological abnormalities in liver and kidney tissues, correlating with reduced GPX4, elevated E‑cadherin, decreased vimentin, increased malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and reduced Ki‑67 positivity in tumour tissues. Notably, 4MOD synergized with the ferroptosis inducer erastin to enhance ferroptosis, apoptosis, and anti‑proliferative activity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 4MOD induces ferroptosis via the AKT/mTOR‑GPX4 axis, highlighting its therapeutic potential for bladder cancer.

Article.Title: A study on user continuance intention for children’s intelligent companion robots based on BERTopic-PLS-SEM-fsQCA
Article.Authors: Fan L.; Wu F.; Lai S.; Cheng C.
Article.Abstract: The children’s intelligent companion robot market faces the industry-wide challenge of “high initial adoption yet low sustained retention.” Existing research has predominantly relied on single-method approaches, leaving the psychological mechanisms and configurational pathways driving user continuance intention insufficiently understood. This study constructs a sequential multi-method research framework integrating “BERTopic thematic mining—PLS-SEM linear validation—fsQCA configurational analysis.” Drawing on 6,405 valid online reviews from JD.com and 440 valid questionnaire responses, the study adopts an integrated theoretical framework combining the Expectation Confirmation Model (ECM) and the Value-based Adoption Model (VAM). BERTopic thematic mining identified six core demand dimensions from consumer reviews: perceived usefulness, perceived enjoyment, visual aesthetics, social/gifting value, technical reliability, and expectation confirmation. PLS-SEM analysis reveals that satisfaction is the strongest predictor of continuance intention ( β = 0.705, p < 0.001), explaining 50.3% of its variance ( R ² = 0.503). Perceived value ( R ² = 0.571) is jointly driven by expectation confirmation ( β = 0.230), perceived usefulness ( β = 0.197), technical reliability ( β = 0.163), social/gifting value ( β = 0.141), visual aesthetics ( β = 0.106), and perceived enjoyment ( β = 0.104). Notably, perceived enjoyment exhibits a distinctive dual-pathway mechanism, influencing continuance intention both indirectly through perceived value and directly through satisfaction ( β = 0.232, p < 0.001). Further fsQCA configuration analysis identified four configurations of high continuance intention (with a solution consistency rate of 0.811 and a coverage rate of 0.469), which can be grouped into three broader patterns based on their theoretical coherence: the “expectation confirmation-dominated” pattern (Configurations 1 and 2, with consistency rates of 0.855 and 0.839, respectively), the “full-dimensional attribute-driven” pattern (Configuration 3, consistency rate of 0.814), and the “Social-Hedonic Compensation” pattern (Configuration 4, consistency rate of 0.836), indicating substantial heterogeneity in continuance intention logic across different segments. Theoretically, this study extends the ECM-VAM framework to the context of children’s embodied intelligent products by introducing visual aesthetics and technical reliability as context-specific antecedents of perceived value, demonstrates that unstructured online review texts can serve as a valid source for the contextualized operationalization of theoretical constructs, and qualifies the linear assumptions of conventional net-effect models through a configurational perspective.

Article.Title: Petrographic and magnetic fabric evidence for magmatic emplacement and hydrothermal alteration in the Shadan Au porphyry deposit, Eastern Iran
Article.Authors: Sheibi M.; Yun S.; Raeisi D.; Lotfi M.; Chang C.
Article.Abstract: Magmatic processes and subsequent hydrothermal alterations within porphyry deposits are well-documented through the analysis of mineral chemistry and the magnetic fabrics of their host intrusions. This study integrates structurs, petrography, mineral chemistry, and anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS) data to investigate the evolution of magmatic and hydrothermal fabrics in the Shadan porphyry Au-rich deposit, located in northeastern Iran. Fresh quartz monzodioritic intrusions exhibit primary magmatic fabrics characterized by oblate AMS ellipsoids, predominantly aligned with magnetite. Progressive hydrothermal alteration—including potassic, phyllic, propylitic, and argillic zones—systematically modifies these fabrics. These alterations are associated with the destruction of magmatic magnetite, hematitization, the replacement of biotite by sericite, and Fe–Mg re-equilibration in amphibole, biotite, and chlorite. Quartz–carbonate and late argillic zones exhibit very weak magnetic susceptibility due to the oxidation and obliteration of primary magnetic minerals. AMS fabrics are controlled by both ferromagnetic (magnetite) and paramagnetic silicate minerals and indicate a predominantly compressional brittle–ductile deformation regime, locally overprinted by late-stage extensional structures. The spatial distribution of magnetic fabrics further highlights the influence of regional and local structural controls on fluid pathways and alteration development within the deposit. The findings indicate that AMS effectively records the superimposed magmatic and hydrothermal processes, providing quantitative insights into the physicochemical evolution, alteration zoning, and mineralogical transformations in porphyry gold systems.

Article.Title: Profiling forward playing styles in big five European football leagues through PCA and cluster analysis
Article.Authors: Xia C.; Cao D.; Ye J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Attacking contributions in elite football are multi-dimensional, and broad forward-line labels often obscure functional variation within nominally homogeneous groups. This exploratory study mapped the technical-function space of forward-line players in Europe’s Big Five leagues using principal component analysis (PCA) and clustering, and evaluated the extent to which the data support discrete categories versus continuous variation.Publicly available FBref player-season data for the 2021–2022 and 2022–2023 seasons were analysed for 381 attacking player-season observations from 331 players with at least 900 league minutes. Sixteen technical process indicators were reduced using PCA, and three retained, standardised component scores were used for clustering (K-means, K = 2–5), with additional fuzzy c-means and archetypal analyses to assess profile distinctness.Three PCA components explained 62.7% of the variance and were interpretable as ball-carrying progression, creative playmaking and penalty-area presence; parallel analysis supported retention of these three components. The primary finding across multiple validation approaches is that the technical-function data among forward-line players were more consistent with continuous variation than with sharply separated, temporally stable clusters. K = 2 had the highest silhouette coefficient, whereas a five-region descriptive summary provided a more differentiated heuristic framework. However, fuzzy c-means showed that the median maximum membership across the five regions was 0.505, with 68.5% of player-seasons below 0.60, indicating substantial overlap. Cross-season centroid replication for the five-region solution was markedly weaker than for smaller-K solutions, further supporting the view that the data were more consistent with continuous variation than with temporally stable categories.The five regions were associated with descriptive differences in npxG + xA, npxG/Shot and G + A, but these associations reflect differences in chance access and shot quality and are not independent validation of the regions as distinct player types. Non-penalty goals relative to non-penalty expected goals did not differ significantly across regions.These findings indicate that technical tendencies within forward-line players are more consistent with continuous variation in chance access and contribution than with fixed, discrete roles. The three PCA dimensions offer a more stable framework for describing functional variation among forwards. The five-region heuristic summary is an exploratory, communication-oriented device for navigating this continuous space, not a validated player taxonomy.

Article.Title: Multimodal spatiotemporal knowledge graph construction for conflict-event analysis: an integrated framework with geographic entity-map association
Article.Authors: Guo L.; Zhang W.; Jia N.; Wang C.
Article.Abstract: Heterogeneous conflict-event information is distributed across textual reports, web images, and scanned maps, making it difficult to represent entities, events, geographic locations, temporal attributes, and multimedia evidence within a unified knowledge graph. This study proposes an integrated framework for constructing multimodal spatiotemporal knowledge graphs from event-oriented heterogeneous data. The framework combines textual entity, relation, and event extraction; visual object detection; scanned-map coordinate recognition; geographic entity grounding; cross-modal entity fusion; provenance-aware storage; and graph visualization. A cascaded YOLOv5-PaddleOCR procedure first detects and crops coordinate annotation regions from scanned maps and then reconstructs the map extent from the recognized coordinates. Textual place entities are geocoded using GeoNames and linked to relevant maps through point-polygon spatial intersection. Quantitative experiments showed F1-scores of 0.76-0.84 for the evaluated text extraction tasks. For aircraft, ship, and general web-image detection, YOLOv8 obtained mAP@0.5 values of 0.935, 0.890, and 0.922, respectively. On the 287-map scanned-map dataset, YOLOv5 achieved a region-detection F1-score of 0.977. In the 278-map paired out-of-fold OCR evaluation, complete map-coordinate recognition increased from 64.03% with direct PaddleOCR to 87.05% with the cascaded procedure, and the paired difference was statistically significant (exact McNemar test, p < 0.001). Under an event- and source-document-grouped evaluation protocol, the complete constrained cross-modal entity-fusion method achieved an F1-score of 0.884. A conflict-event case study further demonstrates the practical applicability of the framework.

Article.Title: A cross-sectional study on the mental health status and influencing factors of medical staff in northwestern China
Article.Authors: Niu Z.; Zhang Z.; Yang X.; Pei H.; Pan L.
Article.Abstract: Healthcare workers in Northwest China face heavy workloads and limited resources, yet region-specific evidence on their health is scarce. In this multicentre cross-sectional study, 1143 doctors, nurses and other clinical staff from 151 public hospitals in Northwest China were surveyed in November–December 2023 using a questionnaire compiled from existing Chinese instruments that assessed occupational stressors, mental health, chronic physical diseases and body image. Nearly 60% of participants worked more than five days per week. Longer daily working hours and more weekly working days were independently associated with greater psychological distress, although the model explained only a small proportion of the variance. Staff in secondary hospitals and non-provincial capital cities reported greater psychological distress than those in tertiary hospitals and provincial capitals. Physical diseases were more common among men, emergency department staff and those working longer hours. Physical exertion was the most prominent stressor, followed by psychological and economic stress, and doctors reported higher stress levels than nurses. These findings suggest that workload management, mental health support and occupational health policies targeting high-risk groups may help to protect the well-being of healthcare workers in this region.

Article.Title: Simultaneous methanol recovery and CO2 capture in a single rotating packed bed (RPB) reactor
Article.Authors: Hamidi A.; Eini S.; Ahmadian M.; Farzaneh E.
Article.Abstract: Waste gas streams from methanol production contain recoverable methanol together with a significant amount of CO 2 . Conventional treatment relies on large multi-stage packed columns. In this study, a process-intensified strategy is experimentally demonstrated for simultaneous methanol recovery and CO 2 capture within a single rotating packed bed (RPB) reactor under various operating conditions (gas flow rate, solvent flow rate, and rotational speed). A lab-scale RPB was operated using a synthetic waste gas mixture (air, CO 2 , and methanol) and 30 wt% aqueous monoethanolamine as the solvent. At a representative operating condition (gas flow rate of 30 L/min, solvent flow rate of 0.3 L/min, and rotational speed of 600 rpm), the RPB achieved approximately 80% CO 2 absorption and 93% methanol recovery. To benchmark performance, equivalent separation configurations using conventional fixed packed columns were evaluated through simulation. Accordingly, the RPB provides a volumetric intensification factor of at least 15.2 relative to the conventional configurations. These results demonstrate that a single RPB can simultaneously recover methanol and capture CO 2 with a substantially reduced equipment footprint, offering a compact and high-throughput alternative for waste stream valorization.

Article.Title: Automated whole slide Allred score estimation for estrogen receptor assessment in breast cancer
Article.Authors: Wadood A.; Fauzi M.; Wong L.; Rehman Z.; Nabi M.; Lee J.; Khor S.; Looi L.
Article.Abstract: Accurate assessment of estrogen receptor (ER) status is critical in breast cancer diagnosis and treatment planning, as it directly determines eligibility for endocrine therapy. ER expression is routinely evaluated on immunohistochemistry (IHC) slides using the semi-quantitative Allred scoring system, which combines the proportion of ER-positive tumor nuclei with staining intensity into a composite score of 0–8. However, manual Allred scoring is labor-intensive, subjective, and prone to inter- and intra-observer variability, particularly in cases that are borderline. In this work, we present a whole-slide image (WSI)-level Allred score estimation pipeline built around MOSAIC, our previously developed multi-scale, orientation-aware nuclei analysis network. The pipeline incorporates a patch-based WSI inference strategy that requires only nucleus-level annotations for training; a centroid-guided instance separation and majority-voting scheme that converts pixel-level segmentation outputs into clinically interpretable proportion scores and intensity scores; and a systematic aggregation protocol that derives the final Allred score without requiring slide-level supervision. MOSAIC integrates multi-scale context extraction to handle nuclear size variability, rotation-enhanced fusion to improve robustness to arbitrary nuclear orientation, and a transformer-inspired multi-scale integration hub to model long-range contextual dependencies across heterogeneous tissue regions. Experimental evaluation on an institutional ER-IHC cohort comprising 37 WSIs from different patients demonstrated strong pixel-level segmentation accuracy, robust instance-level nuclei detection, and improved stability in borderline ER cases. At the WSI level, the pipeline achieved the highest concordance with pathologist-assigned hormonal therapy decisions (89.2%) among all compared approaches, requiring an average of 3.5 minutes to analyze the pathologist-defined tumor regions of each WSI, compared with 11 minutes to 2 hours for the baseline methods evaluated under the present experimental protocol.

Article.Title: Loss of nono impairs cardiac morphogenesis and excitation–contraction coupling via the PI3K/Akt pathway in zebrafish
Article.Authors: Zhang Q.; Yan C.; Liu H.; Zhao H.; Sun K.; Peng X.; Lin Y.; Wang X.; Lei Y.; Cao H.
Article.Abstract: Pathogenic variants in NONO are clinically linked to congenital heart disease (CHD), but in vivo mechanisms and gene-targeted interventions remain poorly explored. Using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing and morpholino silencing, we established knockout (KO) and knockdown (KD) zebrafish models to study nono in cardiogenesis. Adult KO hearts displayed severe structural remodeling, characterized by ventricular distortion, disorganized sarcomeres, and myocardial fibrosis. High-speed optical mapping and calcium imaging revealed reduced conduction velocity, increased dispersion, and spatial heterogeneity in action potential and Ca 2+ transients, disrupting excitation–contraction coupling. In larvae, nono deficiency downregulated core transcription factors ( nkx2.5, gata4 ), suppressed the PI3K/Akt pathway, and triggered myocardial apoptosis. Exogenous delivery of nono mRNA (Rescue) restored PI3K/Akt signaling, mitigating embryonic cardiovascular defects and functional failure. Collectively, our dual-model system demonstrates that NONO is required for structural integrity and electrophysiological homeostasis. This study provides vital in vivo functional validation of nono as a molecular target for myocardial dysfunction, offering a proof-of-concept for gene-based therapeutic restoration in NONO -associated CHD.

Article.Title: Fine-tuned U-Net and time-weighted bi-directional LSTM for low-latency cardiopulmonary monitoring in WBSN data
Article.Authors: Rubia R.; Sasikala S.
Article.Abstract: The evolution of Wireless Body Sensor Networks (WBSNs) has dramatically changed the Smart Emergency Monitoring (SEM) landscape, enabling continuous and non-invasive monitoring of vital signs such as blood pressure, SpO 2 , respiratory rate, and even CO 2 levels. However, the timely and precise detection of transient yet clinically significant events remain an enormous statistical challenge owing to the lower sensitivity and specificity offered by traditional deep learning methods. Such salient experimental alerts usually go with a higher error in prediction rate, hence generalizing poorly with sub-average temporal context modeling from U-Net architectures combined with LSTM layers. To defeat such weaknesses, it proposed a statistically refined hybrid approach, followed by the fine-tuned U-Net framework for spatial feature extraction, interfaced with a Time-Weighted Multi-Task Bi-Directional LSTM (TW-MT-BiLSTM) for temporal sequence modeling. Three enhancements are considered statistically significant, such as: (1) attention-based temporal weighting limiting higher consideration to important time segments, (2) bidirectional LSTM giving better inference capitalizing on past and future contexts, and (3) multi-task learning simultaneously predicting the variables of blood pressure, SpO 2 , and respiratory rate, which decreases variance and enhances the robustness of overall prediction. An extensive set of experiments on benchmark datasets such as Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-III) and PhysioNet is compared in terms of statistical performance metrics, including Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square, and the superiority of the proposed methods was revealed over existing methods.

Article.Abstract: Auxetic structures, with a negative Poisson’s ratio, have gained significant attention for aerospace and automotive applications due to their superior mechanical performance. They were designed and fabricated with the use of Stereolithography (SLA) Additive Manufacturing with the use of Standard Photopolymer Resin Material. The mechanical Behaviour was investigated with the help of compression testing according to ASTM D695 Standards using a Universal Testing Machine (UTM). These findings confirm that Auxetic geometry strongly influences mechanical behaviour and performance. The namely Re–entrant Hexagon (A) Geometry is better suited for Flexible and cushioning applications, such as biomedical devices used in implants, ergonomic materials, shoe soles, and soft protective paddings, while the Re- entrant Star triangular (B) geometry is suitable for applications requiring High Strength and Impact Resistance, such as aerospace Sandwich Structures, automotive crash absorbers, and protective equipment.

Article.Title: Smart rubber sensor repeatability and between-system agreement for peak plantar pressure in healthy and older adults during standing and walking
Article.Authors: Yoshikawa Y.; Matsushita C.; Yamaguchi A.; Ma X.; Maeshige N.
Article.Abstract: Smart Rubber technology enables a low-cost, platform-based approach to clinical plantar pressure monitoring, yet its metrological properties relative to established in-shoe sensors remain uncharacterised. We evaluated the within-session repeatability of a Smart Rubber platform sensor (SR Soft Vision) and its agreement with an established in-shoe resistive sensor array (F-Scan) during quiet standing and walking in 20 healthy adults and 10 ambulatory older adults receiving low-level long-term care support. Repeatability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients [ICC(A,1) and ICC(A, k)] with 95% confidence intervals, standard error of measurement (SEM), minimal detectable change (MDC95), and coefficient of variation. Between-system agreement was evaluated using Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland–Altman analysis, while Pearson’s r was additionally reported as an index of linear association. Between-system agreement was task- and region-dependent: forefoot walking peak plantar pressure (PPP) showed near-zero concordance (CCC = 0.04) with large systematic bias (− 497 to − 528 kPa), persisting after exclusion of ceiling-attainment cases (sensitivity analysis). These findings demonstrate high within-session repeatability of SR Soft Vision and support its potential use for repeated within-device assessment under a consistent protocol, while indicating that absolute PPP values are not interchangeable with F-Scan during dynamic forefoot loading.

Article.Title: REDD1 regulates the cGAS-STING signaling pathway in adipocytes
Article.Authors: Clary R.; Dumas K.; Gilleron J.; Lacas-Gervais S.; Peraldi P.; Jager J.; Britto F.; Favier F.; Ollendorff V.; Cormont M.; Tanti J.; Giorgetti-Peraldi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mitochondria are regulators at the interface between metabolism and immunity in adipocytes. In addition to maintaining metabolic homeostasis, mitochondria control immune responses through the activation of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling pathway. This pathway is a central component of the innate immune system for detecting cytosolic DNA and initiating immune responses. The stress-response protein REDD1 (Regulated in Development and DNA damage response 1) has been described as a regulator of mitochondria-associated membranes and may modulate mitochondrial functions. However, the role of REDD1 in controlling mitochondrial integrity and cGAS–STING signaling in adipocytes remains unclear. We showed that REDD1 expression knockdown increased the ER-mitochondria contacts, mitochondrial enlargement and cytosolic mitochondrial DNA release in 3T3-L1 adipocytes. The downregulation of REDD1 expression increased cGAS and STING protein levels through oxidative stress- and mTORC1 dependent pathways. However, increase in cGAS/STING protein expression is uncoupled from canonical inflammatory and autophagy pathways. Instead, decrease in REDD1 expression reduced fatty acid desaturase 2 (FADS2) expression, a key enzyme in polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism in a STING-dependent manner. In conclusion, our study identifies REDD1 as a novel regulator of mitochondrial homeostasis and cGAS-STING signaling in adipocytes, potentially linking mitochondrial stress to FADS2 protein expression.

These partitions yield closed forms for the selected topological indices and for the Shannon entropies obtained by normalizing their edge contributions. These findings identify mitochondrial impairment and network remodeling as early, quantifiable hallmarks of PRYMCE-induced cytotoxicity and provide mechanistic insight into how P. parvum blooms may damage aquatic organisms.

These numbers are remarkably higher than the current state-of-the-art carbon supercapacitor findings. Furthermore, it retains 83.3% of its initial discharge capacity after 2000 galvanostatic charge-discharge cycles at 10 A/g. Finally, the DSAC electrode performance is slightly enhanced with increasing the KOH concentration from 1 M to 3 M.

Article.Title: An integrated explainable machine learning framework for prediction explanation and audit in high stakes binary classification
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Shi M.; Huang J.; He C.
Article.Abstract: Machine learning classifiers are increasingly deployed in high-stakes decision systems, yet their opacity creates governance risks that undermine accountability and trust. This study proposes an integrated framework unifying predictive modelling, explainability, and model auditing, evaluated on a primary public tabular dataset (Lending Club) and an independent benchmark dataset (Give Me Some Credit) drawn from the consumer-credit domain. The framework enforces a strict decision-time feature-availability policy under which all post-origination repayment variables are excluded, defines default over a fixed 24-month outcome horizon, and combines class-imbalance handling, seven benchmark classifiers (including a traditional scorecard), probability-calibration assessment, global and local explainability analysis with quantified SHAP–LIME agreement, and a six-dimension audit covering performance stability, feature reasonableness, error structure, subgroup fairness screening, threshold policy, and robustness to missing inputs. On the temporally held-out Lending Club test set, LightGBM achieved the strongest discrimination, with an AUC-ROC of 0.8451 (95% CI 0.8421–0.8481), AUC-PR of 0.6118, F1-score of 0.6097, and KS statistic of 0.5127; its advantage over CatBoost was not statistically significant, whereas both exceeded the non-boosting baselines. A similar ordering was observed on the independent benchmark, where severe class imbalance made AUC-PR more informative than accuracy. SHAP explanations identified interest rate, loan grade, revolving utilization, debt-to-income ratio, credit-history length, and income as the dominant predictors, and SHAP–LIME attributions agreed strongly across a systematic evaluation sample (mean Spearman correlation 0.84). The audit revealed stable cross-validation performance, mild temporal drift, adequate post-calibration reliability, and elevated false-positive rates for low-income and short-credit-history subgroups; because the datasets contain no directly observed protected attributes, these results constitute socioeconomic subgroup screening rather than a demonstration of demographic fairness. The study shows that predictive performance, interpretability, calibration, and auditability can be jointly evaluated in a single reproducible workflow, providing an operational technical-audit template that complements, but does not replace, legal and institutional review.

Article.Authors: Fadakar M.; Abdollahi A.; Rasouli A.; Doosalivand H.; Mohammadi P.
Article.Abstract: Sleep disturbances are highly prevalent among patients with gastrointestinal (GI) disorders, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying this vulnerability remain poorly understood. Attachment theory offers a valuable framework for examining how early relational patterns, through cognitive-affective pathways involving self-compassion and rumination, ultimately influence sleep outcomes. This study investigated the mediating roles of self-compassion and rumination in the relationship between attachment styles and sleep quality in patients with GI disease. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 348 adult patients diagnosed with GI disorders at a tertiary referral center in Tehran, Iran. Participants completed validated self-report measures, including the Adult Attachment Scale (AAS), the Self-Compassion Scale (SCS), the Ruminative Response Scale (RRS), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Structural equation modeling with bias-corrected bootstrapping (5000 resamples) was used to test mediation hypotheses. Secure attachment was positively associated with sleep quality, while insecure attachment showed a negative association. Both mediation models demonstrated good fit to the data. Self-compassion and rumination each significantly and partially mediated the relationship between attachment styles, both secure and insecure, and sleep quality. Attachment styles influence sleep quality in GI patients through cognitive-affective pathways involving self-compassion and rumination. These findings highlight the clinical utility of attachment-informed, psychologically integrated interventions, targeting rumination and self-compassion, to improve sleep outcomes in this population.

Article.Title: Conventional diversity metrics underestimate gut microbiome disruption under florfenicol exposure in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
Article.Authors: Streb L.; Assane I.; de Souza G.; Pilarski F.; Queiroga A.; Walch S.; Rath S.; Schloter M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome is an integral component of fish health and growth performance and therefore represents an important production factor in aquaculture. Antibiotics are a major stressor, not only by disturbing microbial diversity, but also by altering microbial interactions involved in digestion, colonization resistance and functional redundancy. Current risk assessments, however, rely largely on diversity-based evaluations and rarely consider changes in network topology. Here, we investigated the impact of florfenicol on the gut microbiome of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) using 16S rRNA sequencing, combining conventional diversity metrics with microbial co-occurrence network modelling. While the microbial community remained overall stable at the diversity level, with treatment explaining only a minor proportion of the observed variation, network analysis revealed substantial fragmentation and a less robust network structure. Network connectivity was significantly reduced, with a near-complete turnover of central hub taxa in the florfenicol network. Our findings demonstrate that diversity-based assessments alone may substantially underestimate the extent of antibiotic-induced microbiome disturbance, with network analysis capturing changes within the community that are highly relevant for microbiome stability and would otherwise remain undetected when evaluations are restricted to diversity metrics.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: Oreochromis niloticus; gut microbiota; florfenicol; microbial co-occurrence networks; microbiome stability; antibiotic exposure; aquaculture; network topology; hub taxa; fish health

Article.Title: Formation and preservation mechanisms of ultra-deep microbialite-dominated reservoirs in the ediacaran dengying formation from the central to Northern Sichuan Basin, SW China
Article.Authors: Xu Z.; Li W.; Qiao Z.; Jin Y.; Zhou J.; Fu X.; Lan C.; Yang D.; Zhu X.; Li M.; Long H.; Jin D.
Article.Abstract: The microbialites in the Ediacaran Dengying Formation of the Sichuan Basin exhibit significant hydrocarbon potential. Investigating the formation and preservation mechanisms of ultra-deep microbialite-dominated reservoirs is critical for expanding exploration domains. Based on observations of 374 samples from outcrops and cores, thin-section quantification, porosity and permeability testing, and diagenetic sequence reconstruction, this study systematically analyzes reservoir characteristics under different burial conditions and establishes an evolution model for microbialite-dominated reservoirs. The reservoir rocks are dominated by stromatolites and thrombolites, with an average porosity of 4.52% and a geometric mean permeability of 0.127 mD. The deposition of microbialite provided high initial porosity. Penecontemporaneous dissolution expanded along primary pores, forming fabric-selective vugs. Regional exposure karst of the Tongwan period further created non-fabric-selective dissolution cavities and fractures, preferentially affecting high-porosity zones. Cementation and hydrothermal activity during the middle to deep burial realm caused limited porosity reduction, and hydrocarbon charging may have helped to preserve pore space. Comparative analysis of Well PS6 (~ 8 km burial depth), Well MX9 (~ 5 km), and the Hujiaba section (outcrop exposure) reveals that the second member of the Dengying Formation reservoirs are primarily influenced by meteoric fluid dissolution during the Tongwan Movement. In contrast, the key diagenetic processes affecting the fourth member reservoirs predominantly occurred during the near-surface to shallow burial stages. This indicates that microbialite-dominated reservoirs in ultra-deep settings retain moderate porosity despite strong heterogeneity. Therefore, reservoir quality is essentially determined during the near-surface to shallow burial stage, where early dolomitization and hydrocarbon charging are critical for porosity preservation in deep to ultra-deep settings. The results provide a theoretical reference for predicting ultra-deep microbialite reservoirs and guiding global exploration of analogous systems.

Article.Title: An explainable machine learning model based on ultrasound and clinical features for impacted gallstone
Article.Authors: Gong Z.; Hu Z.; Xue R.; Liu Z.; Fu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Impacted gallstones present a severe form of gallstones. Although positional adjustment during ultrasound examination has well-established clinical utility for evaluating stone impaction, there are still differences between the preoperative diagnosis results and the intraoperative findings. Machine-learning model may help accurate diagnosis prior to surgery. This retrospective cohort study included 1119 patients with gallbladder neck or duct stone. They underwent cholecystectomy to verify the stones were impacted or not. Fifteen candidate variables were evaluated, encompassing ultrasound features and clinical indicators. Six supervised algorithms were constructed with tenfold cross validation. Model performance was evaluated by discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis, and interpretability was assessed with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Nine variables were retained, including C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, Alkaline phosphatase, γ-glutamyltranspeptidase, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, gallbladder’s length and Length/Width, wall thickness, stone Length/Width. The GBM model exhibited the best performance with an AUC of 0.951 (95% CI: 0.930–0.973), and the lowest Brier score (0.1561) in the internal validation set. A proof-of-concept web calculator was developed to explore individualized risk assessment. The GBM model shows promise in identifying impacted gallstones preoperatively. Pending external validation, this tool may assist clinicians in making more precise decisions.

Article.Title: Fed-SecureCvT: optimized federated learning with cryptographic protection and transformer-based intrusion detection for HER
Article.Authors: Gokila S.; Suresh Babu A.
Article.Abstract: Digital healthcare technologies have transformed the sharing of medical information and collaborative clinical decision-making while raising critical concerns about privacy leakage, unauthorized data manipulation, and cyber risks in remote healthcare settings. Current methods generally focus on collaborative learning, cryptographic security, and network security as separate functions, which reduces their potential to offer an all-round solution in an integrated framework and leaves a key gap in research for the context of secure multi-institutional healthcare systems. To address these challenges, this work presents a multilayer secure collaborative framework that combines intelligent learning, optimized cryptography, integrity assurance, and intrusion detection in a seamless coordinated platform for secured EHR management. The proposed approach is Federated Learning and Federated Dynamics optimization (FL–FedDyn), which could support decentralized medical prediction across multiple hospitals without sharing raw patient data, thus protecting privacy and enhancing the generalization performance of the medical prediction model under heterogeneous data distributions. A Decentralized Multi-Authority Attribute-Based Encryption (DMA-ABE) mechanism is embedded to promote fine-grained access control, with each authority independently providing credentials and eliminating the single-point trust dependency. The Mandrill Optimization Algorithm (MOA) is used to generate optimized keys, which maximizes the entropy and minimizes the computational cost to enhance the cryptographic robustness and efficiency. The Merkle Directed Acyclic Graph (Merkle-DAG) structure is used to link encrypted records via hash relationships for efficient tamper detection and secure storage. Moreover, an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) based on a Convolutional Vision Transformer (CvT) is incorporated to constantly monitor the traffic in a healthcare network and identify known and unknown threats through hybrid feature learning of spatial and attention features. The modules are executed in a streamlined process that includes data preprocessing, collaborative training, encryption, secure storage, integrity validation, and real-time threat monitoring, all of which work together to provide holistic protection over multiple layers of security. Experimental evaluation conducted on the EHR and CIC-IDS2017 datasets demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves superior performance with a prediction accuracy of 99.31%, convergence time of 118.42 s using only 36 communication rounds, privacy preservation level of 98.74%, encryption time of 5.26 ms, integrity verification time of 11.38 ms, and intrusion detection accuracy of 99.31% with a false alarm rate of 1.38%. The framework also demonstrates efficient resource utilization with a reduced CPU consumption of 54.18% and energy usage of 0.196 mJ compared with existing techniques. These results confirm that the proposed multilayer approach provides an effective, scalable, and secure solution for collaborative healthcare data management in distributed medical infrastructures.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: federated learning; cryptographic protection

Article.Title: Fluoride enrichment, hydrogeochemical processes, and health risks from groundwater ingestion in the Zabzugu District, Ghana
Article.Authors: Sunkari E.; Cobbiah M.; Okyere M.; Ambushe A.
Article.Abstract: Groundwater quality in the Zabzugu District, Northern Ghana, is increasingly affected by geogenic processes and anthropogenic activities, particularly agriculture. This study examined the hydrogeochemical characteristics, controlling mechanisms, and health implications of groundwater in the district. Groundwater samples from thirteen (13) locations were analysed using physicochemical measurements, hydrogeochemical modelling, and multivariate statistical techniques, including correlation, factor, and cluster analyses. Groundwater was generally neutral to slightly alkaline (pH 7.01–8.22) and predominantly fresh, with total dissolved solids and electrical conductivity largely within WHO and Ghana Standards Authority (GSA) permissible limits. The dominant cations and anions followed the order Mg²⁺ > Ca²⁺ > Na⁺ > K⁺ and HCO₃⁻ > Cl⁻ > SO₄²⁻, respectively, with Mg–K–HCO₃ identified as the principal water type. Hydrogeochemical evolution was mainly controlled by rock–water interaction, mineral dissolution, and ion exchange, with additional anthropogenic influences from agricultural activities. Fluoride concentrations ranged from 0.231 to 6.90 mg/L, with over 76% of samples exceeding the WHO guideline value of 1.5 mg/L. Higher fluoride concentrations occurred mainly in the northwestern and north-central areas, attributed predominantly to geogenic processes, including carbonate mineral dissolution and ion exchange. Health-risk assessment using estimated daily intake and hazard quotient indicated that children were the most vulnerable, with HQ values exceeding 1 in several communities. The findings support targeted monitoring, groundwater treatment, public health interventions, low-cost defluoridation technologies, and improved agricultural practices to safeguard groundwater quality and public health in Zabzugu District.

Article.Title: Soil parameters associated with Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense incidence and their integration into an IoT-based monitoring system for banana plantations
Article.Authors: Uwamahoro B.; Kuradusenge M.; Bakari A.; Gatera O.; Gaidashova S.; Mtonga K.
Article.Abstract: Fusarium wilt, caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (Foc) , is a major soil-borne threat to banana production and food security in economies such as Rwanda. Although soil physicochemical conditions are known to influence pathogen persistence, the precise relationships between specific soil parameters and disease severity along with the potential for real-time field monitoring to replace laboratory testing remain insufficiently studied. This study collected soil samples from healthy and Fusarium-contaminated plots at three banana plantation sites in Rwanda namely Huye-Rusatira, Kamonyi-Gacurabwenge, and Ruhango-Byimana), analyzing nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, pH, and electrical conductivity in the laboratory. Independent-samples t-tests and Pearson correlation analysis compared healthy and contaminated soils and quantified parameter–severity associations, while a paired t-test evaluated agreement between laboratory and IoT-based real-time measurements. Results showed that contaminated soils were consistently more acidic, nitrogen-depleted, and lower in EC than healthy soils ( p < 0.001 at nearly all sites). pH ( r = − 0.922), nitrogen ( r = − 0.777), and EC ( r = − 0.536) exhibited the strongest negative correlations with disease severity, whereas potassium and phosphorus showed weak associations. These findings identify pH, nitrogen, and EC as reliable indicators of Fusarium wilt risk, supporting their integration into IoT-enabled monitoring systems, with future research aimed at developing AIoT-based predictive models combining soil and climatic data for proactive disease forecasting.

Article.Title: Adjudicator sensitivity of safety estimates in large language models for open-ended cardiovascular reasoning: a blinded multi-adjudicator benchmark study running title: adjudicator variability in LLM safety
Article.Authors: Çelik A.; Kiris T.; Kocabas U.; Karaca M.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated for safety-critical clinical reasoning, but safety estimates in open-ended tasks may depend on expert adjudication thresholds. We evaluated 300 blinded responses generated by three API-accessed LLM configurations across 100 cardiovascular scenarios. Two cardiologists independently scored all responses, and the original workflow used predefined triggers for safety adjudication. First-adjudicator ascertainment was subsequently completed for all responses, after which a separate non-author cardiologist independently re-adjudicated all 300 responses while blinded to model identity, reviewer information, and prior decisions; 53 discordant classifications were then assessed by a third blinded cardiologist using a majority-resolution rule fixed before receipt of the third-adjudicator results. Continuous quality-score reliability was poor (ICC 0.028). The first adjudicator classified 53/300 responses (17.7%) as safety-positive, whereas the independent second adjudicator classified 0/300. First–second crude agreement was 82.3%, but positive agreement was 0%. Third-adjudicator resolution yielded 8/300 majority-classified safety-relevant errors (2.7%, 95% CI 1.4–5.2%). Safety estimates in open-ended cardiovascular LLM benchmarks were highly adjudicator-sensitive. Multi-rater reliability and transparent resolution procedures should accompany numerical safety estimates, which should not be interpreted as real-world clinical error prevalence.
Article.Topic: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

Article.Title: A literature-weighted composite index for integrating reproductive dysfunction and cancer-associated molecular features: a reproducible computational pipeline
Article.Authors: Dashti Z.
Article.Abstract: To construct a literature-weighted composite Disease Activity Index (DAI) integrating gene-expression and DNA-methylation features associated with reproductive dysfunction and cancer, and to establish a reproducible computational pipeline for calculating the index from gene-level data. A hybrid dataset comprising 120 gene-level profiles was assembled from 50 literature-derived profiles seeded from 17 peer-reviewed sources and 70 synthetically augmented profiles. For each gene, DAI was calculated deterministically from cancer- and infertility-associated Log2FC values and a literature-derived weight according to a pre-specified formula, within a general mathematical framework that additionally specifies methylation main and interaction terms. The computational pipeline was implemented to reproduce the index and characterize its distribution. K-means clustering (k = 3) with principal component analysis (PCA) was used descriptively to characterize groupings within the resulting feature space. The pipeline reproduced the pre-specified DAI calculation, and the resulting scores showed three descriptive groupings with mean DAI values of 1.62, 1.17, and 0.91. The groupings reflected variation in the standardized molecular features used to construct the index rather than independently derived biological or clinical risk categories. This study provides a transparent, literature-weighted composite index and a reproducible computational framework for integrating gene-expression and DNA-methylation features at the intersection of reproductive dysfunction and cancer. Because DAI is derived directly from its input features and the dataset includes synthetic augmentation, the present findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Independent evaluation using patient-derived molecular measurements and clinically observed outcomes is required before clinical or diagnostic interpretation.

Article.Title: Optimized piezoelectric energy harvester for hydrogen generation from automotive vibration
Article.Authors: Ehab N.; Kouritem S.; Elmaghlany W.; Harraz E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents the design and optimization of a piezoelectric vibration energy harvesting system integrated with electrolysis-based hydrogen production. The suggested harvester is integrated into an automotive engine block and designed as a bimorph cantilever beam, experiencing authentic low-frequency vibrations from the engine at primary working frequencies of 37 Hz and 52 Hz. Finite element analysis (FEA) is performed in COMSOL Multiphysics 6.1 to assess the electromechanical response of the system under dynamic excitation conditions. Three piezoelectric materials PZT-5 H, PVDF, and improved PVDF (PVDF-E) are comparably analyzed under uniform working circumstances to assess their viability for automobile vibration energy harvesting applications. Structural optimization is conducted with BOBYQA and Monte Carlo techniques to enhance harvested electrical output while adhering to geometric and frequency limitations. The numerical model is evaluated against experimental data from the literature, exhibiting a maximum error of 4.47%, hence affirming its trustworthiness. The results suggest that both material characteristics and frequency adjustment substantially influence electromechanical performance. Among the examined materials, PZT-5H obtains the maximum output power of 1.2507 mW at an ideal load resistance of 10 kΩ due to its better piezoelectric coupling coefficient. PVDF and PVDF-E demonstrate reduced power output but greater mechanical flexibility and durability, making them more appropriate for high-stress and flexible applications, whereas PZT-5 H is chosen for low-stress, high-power-density systems. The captured electrical energy is immediately utilized for hydrogen synthesis using a simplified post-processing electrochemical estimate derived from Faraday’s law, as opposed to a fully integrated Multiphysics electrochemical simulation. Over an operational duration of 600 s, the system generates roughly $$\:1.5123\times\:{10}^{-6}\:\:$$ mol of hydrogen, equating to an energy content of 0.363 J and an equivalent gasoline volume of $$\:1.134\times\:10{-}^{11}$$ L. This study reveals a unique hybrid piezoelectric–electrochemical energy conversion framework that permits direct translation of ambient vibration energy into storable chemical energy, giving a scalable approach for self-powered automobile and hybrid energy systems.
